options.label: Target Score
options.description: Score needed to goal

options.label: Death Link
options.description:
When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too. If you enter a group name, you are only linked to the people in the same group.

This can be adjusted later in the client, unless race mode is enabled.

options.label: Include Tech Skills, Weapon Skills, Stats, and Psi
options.description: Include Technical Skills, Weapon Skills, Statistics, Psi Tier unlocks, and Psi ability unlocks.

options.label: Include OSUpgrades
options.description: Include OSUpgrades.

options.label: Remove duplicate locations
options.description:
Drastically reduces the amount of locations by removing extra locations with the same name and locations close together.
Does not affect chemicals if that option is on.  Removes all unneccesary audio logs, reduces amount of some weapons, and compresses consumables.

options.label: Randomize Code Art
options.description:
Randomize where to find the art code for the transmitter.  All 4 pieces of the code need to be seen to activate the transmitter. Unchecked art that could have part of the code have an icon on the map.
If this option is off the 4 locations are: 2 in Rec A, 1 near the safe behind the reception desk, 1 in a crew quarters room on the 2nd floor.
1 in Rec B in the pool room.  1 in Rec C in the artechnology store.  If this option is set to recreation the 7 extra locations are:  2 in Rec A inside crew quarters rooms on the 2nd floor.
1 in Rec B in the dining room where the lights turn off.  4 in Rec C in the artechnology store.  If this option is set to anywhere there are 9 more locations in medsci 2,
1 more in eng a, 1 more in hydro b/c, 15 more in ops b.

options.label: Include chemicals
options.description: Include chemicals and manifests.

options.label: Include starting wrench
options.description: Include the wrench found on the first body in medsci.

options.label: Victory Condition
options.description: Victory condition, options are: defeat Shodan(default), defeat The Many, get to the many level, or get to the rickenbacker level.

options.label: Randomize Enemies
options.description:
Randomizes enemies.  It is recommended to stay on as this mod's balance is different from vanilla's.
If turned off the early game will be much more difficult, especially if the starting wrench is randomized, and the mid-late game will be too easy.

options.label: Elite Enemies
options.description: Enemies can potentially be elite, having increased health and various buffs and effects along with bonus loot. Only works if Randomize Enemies is on.

options.label: Randomize Replicators
options.description: Randomizes contents and prices of replicators.  Forces a Psi hypo to be in the MedSci Xerxes room replicator.  Intended to stay on but not integral.

options.label: Mode
options.description:
Select the randomizer mode.
These differ only slightly from the original game:

* In `normal` mode, the gorilla woods tracker will be in your inventory
  when the game begins rather than in an extra bubble.
* Items which do not belong in specific locations due to bugs in the
  game are forbidden from those locations rather than treated as
  requirements for those locations.
* There is an additional `fruit_salad` mode which includes _all_ of the
  bubbles. This WILL NOT WORK with the current version of the mod, and
  is only included for testing purposes.

options.label: grass Randomizer
options.description: Turns over 200+ blades of grass and bushes in the game into checks.

options.label: Magic
Enemies
options.description: Whether to turn on/off enemies

options.label: Prioritize Houses
options.description: Makes all houses priority locations

options.label: ExtraMagic
options.description: Amount of extra magic in the pool, only if grass sanity

options.label: Parcel type
options.description: Wether to use specific parcel types or progressive parcels

options.label: Monster Encounter Rate (%)
options.description:
Random-encounter rate as a percent.

0 = no random encounters at all, 100 = vanilla rate, 500 = x5.

This setting can be changed mid-game from the Boost tab.

options.label: XP Boost (%)
options.description:
Experience rewarded from battles, as a percent of vanilla.

100 = vanilla, 200 = double XP, 10 = one-tenth.

This setting can be changed mid-game from the Boost tab.

options.label: Gil Boost (%)
options.description:
💰 Gil dropped by battles, as a percent of vanilla.

100 = vanilla, 0 = no gil ever drops, 500 = x5.

This setting can be changed mid-game from the Boost tab.

options.label: Starting Gil
options.description: 💰 Gil the party starts a new game with. 500 = vanilla.

options.label: Boss Difficulty (%)
options.description:
🏋🏻‍♂️ Boss strength, as a percent of vanilla.

100 = vanilla. 10 = pushover bosses (10% stats). 200 = twice as difficult
(200% HP and offense, plus massive defense), a huge jump.

Expect to grind a lot for any value above 200, and around 300 most
bosses one-shot your party members.

This setting can be changed mid-game from the Boost tab.

options.label: Monster Power (%)
options.description:
🏋🏻‍♂️ Regular monster strength, as a percent of vanilla. Applies to
every enemy that is not a boss (bosses use Boss Difficulty instead).

100 = vanilla. 10 = pushover mobs (10% stats). 200 = twice as difficult.
Scales HP, offense and defenses.

Spells that have a chance to miss (Sleep, Dark, Death, Warp...) get less
reliable as this rises, roughly half as likely to land at 200%.

This setting can be changed mid-game from the Boost tab.

options.label: Starting Party Members
options.description:
👥 How many of the 4 party members you begin the game with.
The rest go MISSING, fully removed from the party, and enter the multiworld
item pool as items named for their job (e.g. "Warrior"). A joining member
rapidly gains levels at their first battle victory. Logic knows your party
is short, so a 1-member start does not get asked to do 4-member things.

A missing member's Starting Job cannot be 'choose_at_game_start'
(generation fails).

options.label: Starting Job — Member 1
options.description:
Job for party member 1 (top of the menu).
random_job picks a random job for the party member,
adhering to Party Diversity (below) if enabled.

options.label: Starting Job — Member 2
options.description:
Job for party member 2.
random_job picks a random job for the party member,
adhering to Party Diversity (below) if enabled.

options.label: Starting Job — Member 3
options.description:
Job for party member 3.
random_job picks a random job for the party member,
adhering to Party Diversity (below) if enabled.

options.label: Starting Job — Member 4
options.description:
Job for party member 4 (bottom of the menu).
random_job picks a random job for the party member,
adhering to Party Diversity (below) if enabled.

options.label: Party Diversity
options.description:
☯️ When on, random jobs avoid stacking the same job: never
3 or more of one job; never two separate pairs. So it will not roll
2 White Mages + 2 Warriors, or 3 Thieves.

Jobs you picked yourself aren't changed.

options.label: White And Black Magics
options.description:
☯️ When on, random jobs avoid stacking all one magic color.
There will be at least one white magic user and at least one black magic user.
White: White Mage, Warrior, Monk (only if dabble in magic is on)
Black: Black Mage, Thief
Both: Red Mage

Jobs you picked yourself aren't changed.

options.label: Naked Monks
options.description:
🥋 A Monk's defense actually goes up with their starting Clothes
removed, so with this on, starting Monks auto-sell their Clothes and
Staff. Nothing stops you re-arming a Monk later.

options.label: Shop Item Pool
options.description:
❔💰 Which weapons, armor and items get shuffled into shops. Each level
is a strict superset of the one below:

  unshuffled  (0) -- shops keep their vanilla inventories (no shuffle).
  mundane     (1) -- shuffle, but only ordinary stock: what vanilla town
                     shops sell (Nunchaku, Rapier, Potion, Knight's Armor)
                     plus plain treasure gear (Flame Sword, Ice Brand,
                     Diamond Armor, etc.). No exotic gear.
  exotic      (2) -- also exotic weapons, armor and items (Duel Rapier,
                     Genji gear, Curtains, Emergency Exit, etc.), but not
                     activatable weapons and priceless gear (like Black Robe).
  activatable (3) -- also exotic weapons that cast a free spell when used
                     (Wizard's Staff, Thor's Hammer, Healing Staff, etc.) plus
                     fangs (White/Red/Blue/Vampire Fang, Cockatrice Claw).
                     This equipment costs an extra x1.5.
  all         (4) -- also priceless gear and consumables (Ultima, Barbarian
                     Sword, Excalibur, Stat Pills, Apples, etc.). Priceless
                     items cost an extra x2.

(Magic shops are covered by Shuffle Magic Shops instead.)

options.label: Shuffle Magic Shops
options.description:
🔮 Shuffle which spells each magic shop sells. Gil and MP costs are
still based on vanilla prices.

Each class learns the same number of spells from each shop as vanilla, so
the White Mage learns all 4 spells in Cornelia's white shop, the Red Mage
learns 2 of them, and later the Red Wizard learns those 2 plus 1 more.

options.label: Randomize Prices
options.description: Randomize gil prices (items, weapons, armor, spells).

options.label: Item Price Range — Low (%)
options.description:
🪙🧤 Low bound (percent of vanilla) for randomized item, weapon and
armor prices. So 25 here means an item can randomly cost as little as a
quarter of its vanilla price (never below 5 gil).
Needs Randomize Prices on.

options.label: Item Price Range — High (%)
options.description:
🪙🧤 High bound (percent of vanilla) for randomized item, weapon and
armor prices. So 200 here means an item can randomly cost as much as 2
times its vanilla price.
Needs Randomize Prices on.

options.label: Spell Gil Price Range — Low (%)
options.description:
🪙🔮 Low bound (percent of vanilla) for randomized spell gil prices.
So 25 here means a spell can randomly cost as little as a quarter of its
vanilla gil price.
Independent from item prices. Needs Randomize Prices on.

options.label: Spell Gil Price Range — High (%)
options.description:
🪙🔮 High bound (percent of vanilla) for randomized spell gil prices.
So 200 here means a spell can randomly cost as much as 2 times its vanilla
gil price.
Independent from item prices. Needs Randomize Prices on.

options.label: Slot Magic
options.description:
🪄 Replace the MP pool with NES/Pixel-Remaster-style spell slots.

Each spell level has its own pool of charges.

This setting is not balanced around Shuffle Magic Shops. Flare could land
as a level 1 spell with this vancian system.

options.label: Slot Magic Battle Display
options.description:
🪄 With Slot Magic on: show a compact list of per-level spell charges
for every party member in battle.

Needs Slot Magic on; does nothing without it.

options.label: Spells Hit Low HP Enemies
options.description:
🎯 Your spells that can miss hit more on low health enemies.
Soften up enemies to more reliably land spells like Break or Sleep.

options.label: Randomize Spell Mana Costs
options.description: 🪄 Randomize each spell's MP cost.

options.label: Costly Best Spells
options.description:
🪄 Best spells cost more mana.

With Randomize Spell Mana Costs on, these roll their MP cost over the upper
half of the mana-cost range instead of the whole range, so a lucky roll
can't make them dirt cheap.

For Slot Magic, these are instead more likely to cost higher-level
spell slots.

options.label: Spell Mana Cost Range — Low (%)
options.description:
🪄 Low bound (percent of vanilla) for randomized spell MP costs.
So 50 here means a spell can randomly cost as little as half its vanilla
MP cost.
Needs Randomize Spell Mana Costs on.

options.label: Spell Mana Cost Range — High (%)
options.description:
🪄 High bound (percent of vanilla) for randomized spell MP costs.
So 250 here means a spell can randomly cost as much as 2.5 times its
vanilla MP cost (capped at 99 MP).
Needs Randomize Spell Mana Costs on.

options.label: Shuffle Who Equips What
options.description:
🧤 Randomize which jobs can equip which weapons and armor.

This keeps the overall distribution intact: Ninja can still equip
nearly everything, Monk still almost nothing.

options.label: Harder Overworld Encounters
options.description:
👹 Overworld zones throw a harder, hand-picked pool of monsters
at you.

options.label: Harder Dungeon Encounters
options.description:
🐲 Dungeons are much tougher, on a deliberately rising curve. Most roll
from the next dungeon's difficulty tier; several use hand-picked pools
instead.

options.label: Dangerous Forests
options.description:
🌳 Watch out for forest tiles! Random encounters in forests are
significantly harder than the surrounding overworld encounters.
These encounters are carefully hand-picked per overworld zone.

options.label: Boss Minions
options.description:
👥 Bosses bring friends.

off       -- vanilla; bosses fight alone.
light     -- +1 minor minion.
difficult -- +3 minor minions.
absurd    -- +3 minor minions and 1 elite minion.

options.label: Encounters on Chaos' Floor
options.description:
👑 Random encounters on Chaos' floor. In the vanilla game, there are
no encounters on the last floor of the Chaos Shrine, just before Chaos.
Turn this off to leave that floor quiet.

options.label: Regional Ocean Encounters
options.description:
🌊 The sea has regions. The world's four ocean quadrants get their own
encounter pools. The starting sea around Cornelia is left vanilla. Sail
into the open ocean and the monsters get harder to match where you are.

Pairs well with Northern Docks.

options.label: Northern River Encounters
options.description:
🛶 Northern rivers get their own encounter pool.

With this on, the rivers of the northern continent draw from a separate,
harder, themed pool of monsters.

options.label: Bestiarysanity Percent
options.description:
📖 Monsters hold AP items. This is the percentage of the seed's
huntable monsters that hold a check.

50 makes half of viable monsters hold checks; 100 puts every
huntable monster in this seed into the pool.
Use the AP client's Bestiary tab for tracking.

options.label: Bestiary Progression
options.description:
📖 Allow progression items on bestiary checks (bestiarysanity only).
If on, any item can hide behind a monster hunt, so a required item
may sit on a bestiary check.

Off by default (user call 2026-09-01): a monster hunt is a long tail, and
hiding a required item behind one can stall a run for hours.

options.label: Blood Magic (activatable equipment HP cost)
options.description:
🩸 Activating equipment (spell-on-use gear like Thor's Hammer, Judgment
Staff, Healing Staff, Black Robe) costs the user 10% of their max HP.

Activatable gear stops being a free infinite spell.

(Equipment Runes Required gates whether you can activate at all. This
governs what it costs once you can.)

options.label: Monk & Thief Dabble in Magic
options.description:
✨ Monk and Thief can learn a little magic. They each learn only 1 spell
per spell level, and they gain max MP very slowly.

The Thief can learn spells like Sleep and Confuse; the Monk can learn
spells like Protect and NulBlaze. (With Shuffle Magic Shops on, those will
be other random spells instead.)

This changes these classes from having zero options in battle
(always attack) to having 1 or 2 things they can do per long rest.

options.label: Thieves Steal
options.description:
🎁 Thieves (and Ninja) scavenge after battle. If a thief spots an
item to take, there is a sound effect and an extra sprite shows up briefly
next to your thief.

The chance is based on Agility, and Luck gives an extra chance to find
lower-tier loot. More thieves means more chances at extra loot.

options.label: Thief Extra Crit
options.description:
🗡️ Thieves (and Ninja) get an extra chance to land a critical
hit, based on their Agility.

When your thief scores an extra crit from this, there's an extra
sound effect.

options.label: Job Scroll Boosts
options.description:
📜 Adds Job Scrolls to the item pool, one for each job in your party.
Each grants a permanent boost to the matching party member.

- 🩸⚔️ Blood Knight Scroll: gain lifesteal and armor penetration with
  physical attacks. Undead enemies have no blood to drain, so hitting
  them heals nothing.
- 🥷🎁 Stealth Ninja Scroll: much better steals (needs Thieves Steal on;
  without it, this half of the scroll does nothing). Damaging floors
  also deal less damage. With more Stealth Thieves or Ninja, damaging
  floors actually heal you and restore mana each step.
- 🥋💪 Grand Master Scroll: as they take damage, they gain attack and max
  HP, and heal.
- 🎩🩸 Crimson Wizard Scroll: restore mana based on damage taken, and heal
  based on mana spent.
- 🪄☀️ White Cleric Scroll: Dia spells hurt all bosses. Also, casting a
  Dia-family spell heals the caster and grants temporary INT.
- ☠️🔮 Necrocaster Scroll: instant-kill spells are far more reliable
  (Death/Quake/Scourge/Warp/Kill hit more often), and spells deal damage
  instead of nothing when they miss. Kill deals a little more
  damage than Flare.

options.label: Max Extra Items Per Shop
options.description:
🏪 Max number of EXTRA normal items added to each shop, on top of the
stock it would carry anyway.

options.label: AP Offers Per Shop
options.description: 🛒 Max number of Archipelago items for sale in each shop.

options.label: Max Hints Per Gear Shop
options.description:
🔮 Max number of HINTS for sale in each shop.

Sold at Weapon and Armor shops, purchased hints reveal the AP item at
a location or a set of locations within your world.

options.label: Exotic Loot Amount
options.description:
💍 How much exotic or high-end equipment (Genji set, Sun Blade,
Thor's Hammer, Elven Cloak, Black Robe, etc.) to shuffle into the
multiworld, on a scale from 0 (none) to 10 (the entire exotic pool).

Mundane loot (Flame Sword, Diamond Armor, Aegis Shield, etc.) fills
in the loot pool gaps.

options.label: Priceless Loot Amount
options.description:
💎 How much priceless equipment (Ultima, Excalibur, Masamune, Rune Axe,
Judgment Staff, Ragnarok, Ribbon, etc.) to shuffle into the multiworld, on a
scale from 0 (none) to 10 (the entire priceless pool). By default, there
are restrictions on who can equip priceless gear (see Only Advanced Jobs
Equip Priceless Gear).

options.label: Only Advanced Jobs Equip Priceless Gear
options.description:
🛡️ Lock priceless gear (the same gear Priceless Loot Amount and
Shop Item Pool call priceless) so only promoted jobs can equip it. A
Warrior cannot wield the Barbarian Sword until they class-change into a Knight,
and nobody wears a Ribbon pre-promotion.

Off: Priceless gear keeps whatever equip permissions it would otherwise
have in vanilla (Ribbon = anyone, Barbarian Sword = Warrior, Knight, Red Mage,
Red Wizard).

options.label: Auto-Sell Unusable Items
options.description:
💰 When you get equipment that NOBODY in your party can ever equip,
you are paid its shop sell value.

Never sold: consumables, anything you bought in a store, your starting
inventory, and activatable gear.

options.label: Open Progression
options.description:
⛰️ How much of the world opens up early on foot/canoe:

off      (0)  -- vanilla routing. The southern continent needs the Ship.
early    (1)  -- carves a foot trail from Cornelia to Mount Duergar, and
                 a Canoe river linking the Crescent Lake water system to
                 the Cavern of Ice rivers. The Canoe opens up the entire
                 southern continent.
extended (2)  -- also adds a foot trail from Mount Duergar to the
                 Western Keep, and a new Canoe river linking Mount Duergar
                 to Melmond. The whole Cornelia/Marsh section is sphere 1
                 and the Earth crystal is reachable with only the Canoe.

options.label: Northern Docks
options.description:
⚓ Adds two ship docks to the northern continents: one south of Onrac,
one south of the Mirage Tower desert. Much more of the map becomes
reachable by ship, well before you get the airship.

Pairs well with Regional Ocean Encounters.

options.label: Unlockable Northern Foot Trails
options.description:
🌉 Adds three AP items that reshape the northern map. 
• Lufenian Bridge: bridges Pravoka to the Lufenian landmass
• Lufenian Nitro Powder: blasts the boulder between Lufenia and Gaia
• Gaian Nitro Powder: blasts the boulder between Gaia and Mirage Desert

options.label: Mount Gulg Key
options.description: 🌋 Seals Mount Gulg's entrance until you find the Mount Gulg Key.

options.label: Loot in Normally Empty Chests
options.description:
📦 Puts real loot in the chests that are empty in vanilla.

These empty chests are in Marsh Cave, Mount Gulg, and Citadel of Trials.

Turn this off to leave those chests empty.

options.label: Exclude Bonus Dungeons
options.description:
🚫 Keep all Soul-of-Chaos bonus-dungeon content out of the item pool.
This includes all dynamic and static chests from Earthgift Shrine,
Hellfire Chasm, Lifespring Grotto, and Whisperwind Cove.

Turn this on to skip all those bonus dungeons.

options.label: Earthgift Shrine AP Locations
options.description:
🏔️ Number of procedural chests in Earthgift Shrine (5 floors) that
become AP locations. After you open this many chests here, additional
chests work like vanilla chests.

0 = none, and this dungeon's static boss-chamber chest is also dropped.
Forced to 0 by Exclude Bonus Dungeons.

options.label: Hellfire Chasm AP Locations
options.description:
🌋 Number of procedural chests in Hellfire Chasm (10 floors) that
become AP locations. After you open this many chests here, additional
chests work like vanilla chests.

0 = none, and this dungeon's static boss-chamber chest is also dropped.
Forced to 0 by Exclude Bonus Dungeons.

options.label: Lifespring Grotto AP Locations
options.description:
🌊 Number of procedural chests in Lifespring Grotto (20 floors) that
become AP locations. After you open this many chests here, additional
chests work like vanilla chests.

0 = none, and this dungeon's static boss-chamber chest is also dropped.
Forced to 0 by Exclude Bonus Dungeons.

options.label: Whisperwind Cove AP Locations
options.description:
💨 Number of procedural chests in Whisperwind Cove (40 floors) that
become AP locations. After you open this many chests here, additional
chests work like vanilla chests.

0 = none, and this dungeon's static boss-chamber chest is also dropped.
Forced to 0 by Exclude Bonus Dungeons.

options.label: Crystals Needed
options.description:
💠 How many of the four Crystals (defeated Fiends) you need before the
Black Orb in the Chaos Shrine will shatter, opening the way to Chaos.
0 = the orb opens right away.

See Lute Tablets Required for the other key required to win.

options.label: Bonus Dungeon Crystals
options.description:
💠 Move crystal activation from the four Fiends to the Soul of Chaos bonus
dungeons. When ON, defeating a Fiend still opens its bonus dungeon, but the
matching Crystal only activates once you beat one of that dungeon's end bosses.
Any of a dungeon's end bosses counts.

options.label: Lute Tablets Required
options.description:
🪕 How many Lute Tablets you need to collect to reach the very end of
the game. The Lute is broken into pieces; collect this many to win.
0 = off (the Lute is a single randomized item).

See Crystals Needed for the other key required to win.

options.label: Lute Tablets Percentage
options.description:
🪕 How many Lute Tablet pieces exist in the whole multiworld, as a percent
of Lute Tablets Required (Lute Tablets Extra is then added on top). 100 =
exactly Required, 150 = 50% extra tablets. Extra tablets found above
Required don't do anything.

options.label: Lute Tablets Extra
options.description:
🪕 How many extra Lute Tablet pieces exist on top of
Lute Tablets Percentage (a flat count, not a percent).

options.label: Levistone Shards Required
options.description:
🪨 Set this above 0 to break the Levistone into shards. Collect this
many Levistone Shards to assemble the Levistone and raise the airship.
0 = off (the Levistone is a single randomized item).

options.label: Levistone Shards Percentage
options.description:
🪨 How many Levistone Shard pieces exist in the whole multiworld, as a
percent of Levistone Shards Required (Levistone Shards Extra is then added
on top). 100 = exactly Required, 150 = 50% extra shards. Extra shards found
above Required don't do anything.

options.label: Levistone Shards Extra
options.description:
🪨 How many extra Levistone Shard pieces exist on top of
Levistone Shards Percentage (a flat count, not a percent).

options.label: Equipment Runes Required
options.description:
🗝️ Set this above 0 to lock equipment activation (Healing Helm, Thor's
Hammer, White/Black Robe, etc.) behind Equipment Runes. Collect this
many to earn the Equipment Rune Key, which unlocks activation for good.
0 = off, so equipment activates normally.

Related: Blood Magic sets what activating costs. Shop Item Pool's
"activatable" level decides whether shops stock this gear.

options.label: Equipment Runes Percentage
options.description:
🗝️ How many Equipment Rune pieces exist in the whole multiworld, as a
percent of Equipment Runes Required (Equipment Runes Extra is then added on
top). 100 = exactly Required, 150 = 50% extra runes. Extra runes found
above Required don't do anything.

options.label: Equipment Runes Extra
options.description:
🗝️ How many extra Equipment Rune pieces exist on top of
Equipment Runes Percentage (a flat count, not a percent).

options.label: Spell Tomes
options.description:
📙 Adds Spell Tomes to the item pool. A tome is a consumable item
that teaches its spell to a party member that can
learn it. Shops still sell spells normally.

options.label: Auto Dash
options.description:
🏃 Start with the Config "Dash" setting on, so the party
auto-runs without you holding the dash button.

Super Dash is always available in every seed: with Config "Dash" on,
hold the Dash button to move at double speed anywhere. Towns, dungeons,
the overworld, the ship, the canoe and the airship.

Off = Config "Dash" starts off, and you can turn it on any time from
the in-game Config menu to get both auto dash and Super Dash.

options.label: Message Speed
options.description:
💬 Starting value for the Config "Message Speed" setting.

This only sets the default at new game.

options.label: Cursor
options.description:
🖐️ Starting value for the Config "Cursor" setting.

  default -- menu cursors start at the top every time you open a menu.
  memory  -- menus remember where the cursor was and put it back.

This only sets the default at new game.
Change Cursor in the Config menu whenever you like.

options.label: Spell Chance Colors
options.description:
🎨 Color the battle "miss!!" text by the odds the spell actually had of
landing on that target, so a near-miss looks different from a cast that
never had a chance.

  white  -- 0% chance; the target was immune.
  yellow -- 1% to 15%; small chance, but possible.
  red    -- over 15%; it had a real chance of working.

This even covers spells sent at your party!
It will show you how close Quake was to killing your whole party.

options.label: Trap Percentage
options.description:
💣 Chance for each filler item in your pool to be replaced with a
trap instead. Traps trigger at the start of the next combat and can
be dodged and resisted like any other hostile ability.

options.label: Death Link
options.description:
💀 When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the
reverse is true too.

For FF1 PSP, "dying" means a total party wipe (every party member KO'd).
Receiving a death kills Death Link Severity of your living party members
(see that option).

options.label: Death Link Severity
options.description: 💀 How many party members are killed when a death link is received.

options.label: Gem Shop
options.description:
Enable the Gem Shop.

When enabled: beating scenarios earns Gems (currency). Spend them in the shop to receive items and hints.
Gem Shop is accessible from the AoM AP Launcher window.

When disabled: victories award random multiworld items instead of Gems and you can't enter the shop.

options.label: Wins to Open Shop
options.description:
Number of scenario victories required to open each additional shop tier (only used when Gem Shop is enabled).
Shop A is always open. Shop B opens after this many wins. Shop C opens after 2x wins. Shop D opens after 3x wins.
Set to 0 to open all shops immediately.

options.label: Max Progression Items In Each Shop
options.description:
Maximum number of progression items allowed in each non-first shop (Shop B, Shop C, Shop D).

Set to 0 to forbid progression items in shops entirely (recommended). Set to 15 to allow every slot in those 3 shops to hold any item.

Careful setting this too high as you can't grind gems. If you spend your gems unwisely, you could softlock the seed. (If that happens you can use JUNK FOOD NIGHT to cheat)

options.label: FotT Greek Campaign
options.description:
Include the Fall of the Trident: Greek campaign (scenarios 1-10).
When disabled, those 10 scenarios are unplayable and are removed from the pool.

options.label: FotT Egyptian Campaign
options.description:
Include the Fall of the Trident: Egyptian campaign (scenarios 11-20).
When disabled, those 10 scenarios are unplayable and are removed from the pool.

options.label: FotT Norse Campaign
options.description:
Include the Fall of the Trident: Norse campaign (scenarios 21-30).
When disabled, those 10 scenarios are unplayable and are removed from the pool.

options.label: New Atlantis Campaign
options.description:
Include The New Atlantis campaign.
When disabled, those 12 scenarios are unplayable and are removed from the pool.

options.label: Golden Gift Campaign
options.description:
Include The Golden Gift campaign.
When disabled, those 4 scenarios are unplayable and are removed from the pool.

options.label: Pillars of The Gods Campaign
options.description:
Include The Pillars of The Gods campaign.
When disabled, those 9 scenarios are unplayable and are removed from the pool.

options.label: Relicsanity
options.description:
Include Relicsanity locations in the pool.

When enabled, every relic in the campaigns becomes its own check — garrisoning a relic in a Temple sends a check to the multiworld.
Roughly doubles locations and items in your world.

options.label: Optional Objectives Are Locations
options.description: Turn each scenario's optional (secondary) objectives into Archipelago locations.

options.label: Exclude 30. All Is Not Lost
options.description:
Exclude scenario 30, "All Is Not Lost", from the world.

When enabled, all locations in scenario 30 are filler.

options.label: Gems As Filler
options.description:
Allow Gems to be used as filler items.

Normally Gems are awarded only by Victory locations. When enabled, the world may also pad filler slots with Gems.
Has no effect when the Gem Shop is disabled.

options.label: Max Keys on Keyrings
options.description:
Maximum number of Scenario Keys carried by a Key Ring item.

When more than 0, every scenario is locked behind a Scenario Key and one or more Scenario Keys are found on Key Ring items.
When you or any other player in the multiworld finds a Key Ring, every Scenario Key on that ring is delivered to you.

You begin with one starter Key Ring which includes at least one scenario you can attempt immediately. The remaining rings are shuffled into the item pool.

To Turn this Off:
0 — feature disabled; scenarios are not locked behind keys at all. Unlocking a campaign gives you access to all the scenarios in that branch.

options.label: Starting Scenarios
options.description:
Which civilization block is unlocked at the start? All other enabled campaigns start locked.

greek:        Scenarios 1-10 (Fall of the Trident: Greek)
egyptian:     Scenarios 11-20 (Fall of the Trident: Egyptian)
norse:        Scenarios 21-30 (Fall of the Trident: Norse)
new_atlantis: Start with the New Atlantis Campaign.

Starting with the Greek block is the easiest.

options.label: Final Scenarios
options.description:
What unlocks the Final scenario block (scenarios 31-32)?

beat_x_scenarios (recommended):
Beat the chosen number of scenarios (set via x_scenarios below) to receive the Atlantis Key and open the Final section.

always_open:
The Final section is available from the start. This can result in a much shorter experience.

atlantis_key:
The Atlantis Key is shuffled randomly into the item pool. Finding it anywhere opens the Final section.

options.label: X Scenarios
options.description:
If Final Scenarios (above) is set to beat_x_scenarios, this is how many scenarios must be completed before you receive the Atlantis Key.

You may beat any combination of scenarios from any activated campaigns. 
(46 requires beats all 30 Fall of the Trident, all 12 New Atlantis, and all 4 Golden Gift scenarios)
****Updated to 54 max for PoTG

options.label: Random Major gods
options.description:
Randomize the major god for each scenario at generation time. The assigned god determines which techs and minor gods are available.
Think on your feet with this turned on.

options.label: Force Different Major god
options.description:
When random_major_gods is enabled, forces the random god to never be the vanilla major god for that scenario and makes it more likely to play a civilization different from the vanilla.
(e.g. 1. Omens is normally Poseidon, so you'll never play Poseidon on that mission with this on, and Zeus, Hades, and Demeter are much less likely)

options.label: Shuffle Greek Major gods
options.description:
Include Greek major gods in the random major god pool. Turn this off to never play as the Greeks.
Only applies when Random Major gods is enabled.

options.label: Shuffle Egyptian Major gods
options.description:
Include Egyptian major gods in the random major god pool. Turn this off to never play as the Egyptians.
Only applies when Random Major gods is enabled.

options.label: Shuffle Norse Major gods
options.description:
Include Norse major gods in the random major god pool. Turn this off to never play as the Norse.
Only applies when Random Major gods is enabled.

options.label: Shuffle Atlantean Major gods
options.description:
Include Atlantean major gods in the random major god pool. Turn this off to never play as the Atlanteans.
Only applies when Random Major gods is enabled.

options.label: Shuffle Chinese Major gods
options.description:
Include Chinese major gods in the random major god pool. Turn this off to never play as the Chinese.
If you don't have the Chinese DLC, Favored Land won't work for you and some graphics may look wrong. Buy the Chinese DLC for best results, but you can still play as them even if you don't have the DLC.
Only applies when Random Major gods is enabled.

options.label: Shuffle Japanese Major gods
options.description:
Include Japanese major gods in the random major god pool. Turn this off to never play as the Japanese.
If you don't have the Japanese DLC, Japanese Experience Points won't work for you and some graphics may look wrong. Buy the Japanese DLC for best results, but you can still play as them even if you don't have the DLC.
Only applies when Random Major gods is enabled.

options.label: Shuffle Aztec Major gods
options.description:
Include Aztec major gods in the random major god pool. Turn this off to never play as the Aztecs.
If you don't have the Aztec DLC, Aztec Tonalli favor won't work for you and some graphics may look wrong. Buy the Aztec DLC for best results, but you can still play as them even if you don't have the DLC. 
Only applies when Random Major gods is enabled.

options.label: Disable Demeter and Freyr
options.description:
Remove Demeter and Freyr from the random major god pool.

Only applies when Random Major Gods is enabled.

options.label: Extra Final Mission Age Unlocks
options.description:
Scenario 32 normally requires 3 Age Unlock items to reach the Mythic Age and build the Wonder. 
This adds extra copies of whichever civilization's Age Unlock corresponds to the god assigned to scenario 32 (Greek by default, or randomized if Random Major gods is enabled).

At the default of 1, there are 4 total copies of that unlock in the pool.

options.label: Hero Abilities
options.description:
Include custom hero special ability items in the item pool?

enabled (true):
Recommended setting for an exciting, hero-focused campaign.
The following items are included:

Arkantos:
  - Arkantos Lifesteal         (Arkantos' melee attacks heal him)
  - Arkantos Petrifying Shout  (shout ability petrifies and damages nearby enemies)
  - Arkantos is a House        (Arkantos provides +10 population capacity)
  - Arkantos Attack Speed      (increases melee attack speed)

Ajax:
  - Ajax Stunning Blow         (shield bash stuns the target for 10 seconds)
  - Ajax Smiting Strikes       (melee attacks temporarily reduce target's max HP)
  - Ajax Shield Bash AOE       (shield bash hits a wide area)

Chiron:
  - Chiron Poison Arrow        (arrows apply a poison damage over time)
  - Chiron Crippling Fire      (arrows slow the target's attack rate significantly)
  - Chiron Shotgun Special     (special shot fires a ton of extra arrows)

Amanra:
  - Amanra Whirlwind Throw     (leap attack sends targets flying)
  - Amanra Army of the Dead    (enemies slain by Amanra are reincarnated as allied minions)
  - Amanra Divine Smite        (melee attacks deal +5 divine damage)

Odysseus:
  - Odysseus Entangling Shot   (special shot snares the targets' movement for 10 seconds)
  - Odysseus Swift Escape      (ranged attacks cripple the target's speed)
  - Odysseus Perfect Accuracy  (ranged attacks never miss)

Reginleif:
  - Reginleif Frost Strike     (javelins progressively freeze the target)
  - Reginleif +1 Projectile    (fire an additional javelin)

Kastor (only in pool when New Atlantis campaign is enabled):
  - Kastor Undermines with Attacks  (melee attacks deal large damage over time to buildings)
  - Kastor Can Summon Soldiers      (Kastor can train Hoplites, Spearmen, Berserks, Murmillos, Yari Spearmen, Tlamanih Spearmen, Dao Swordsmen, Prodromos, War Elephants, Jarls, Destroyers, Samurai, Shorn Ones, and Tiger Cavalry)
  - Kastor is a Manor               (Kastor provides +20 population capacity)

disabled (false):
All above hero ability items are removed from the pool and replaced with
filler. Removing these makes the game much harder and less hero-focused.

options.label: Local Filler Frequency
options.description:
Percentage of filler items that will be placed locally in your own world instead of the shared multiworld pool.
0 = all filler goes into the shared pool (default, fully multiworld).
75 = up to 75% of filler items are guaranteed to stay in your own game.
Has no effect in single-player games (all items are local anyway).

options.label: Trap Percentage
options.description:
Percentage of filler items to replace with traps (0 = no traps, 100 = all filler becomes traps).
Traps fire randomly during scenarios. Only filler items are replaced; useful items are never swapped for traps.

options.label: Victory Goal Logic
options.description:
Which victory should be achievable before the game is considered beatable?

Note that this solely affects progression logic. You can still beat the game earlier than expected or pursue a
different victory if you so choose.

Domination and Time victories are not included here as Domination can be achieved at any moment and Time has no
requirements.

options.label: Era Goal Logic
options.description:
Which era must be unlocked before the game is considered beatable?

This is in addition to the value given for "Victory Goal Logic".
Similarly, this solely affects progression logic.

options.label: Embarking Goal Logic
options.description:
Add Optics and Astronomy as requirements before the game is considered beatable.

Similarly to other goal logic options, this solely affects progression logic.

options.label: Policy Cost Modifier
options.description: Multiplies the base cost of adopting social policies with the given percentage.

options.label: Tech Cost Modifier
options.description: Multiplies the base cost of researching technologies with the given percentage.

options.label: Progressive Techs
options.description:
Use progressive technologies.

Progressive technologies divides all 79 technologies (excl. Agriculture) into 11 categories.
This makes the unlocking of technologies feel less chaotic and more streamlined compared to true random
technologies. It also makes it far less likely to not have important early-era buildings in the mid to late game.

options.label: Item Hints
options.description:
Enable item hints for all locations.

Options are:
- full: Locations state their exact item.
- classification: Locations state the classification of their item (progression; useful; filler; trap).
- none: Locations do not state their item.

options.label: Disguise Traps
options.description:
Item classification hints will classify traps as progression items.

Keep in mind that if item hints are set to 'full', the name of the trap is still visible and could potentially spoil
you of the true nature of the item.

Has no effect if item hints are set to 'none'.

options.label: Satellites Meets All
options.description: Receiving the Satellites technology will also meet all civilizations and city-states.

options.label: Super Palace
options.description:
Replaces the default Palace with a version that has much higher yields:
- Gold/Science/Production: 3 -> 15
- Culture: 1 -> 5
- Happiness/Faith/Food: 0 -> 5

This makes the early game easier without your usual base technologies.

options.label: Building Sanity
options.description:
Add most standard buildings to the location pool.

This adds 53 buildings to the location pool in total.

Buildings that will not be added:
- Palace
- Courthouse
- Any religious building (Cathedral; Monastery; Mosque; and Pagoda)
- Any civilization-unique building (they count as the building they replace instead)
- Any National Wonder (see National Wonder Sanity instead)
- Any World Wonder (see World Wonder Sanity instead)

options.label: National Wonder Sanity
options.description:
Add all national wonders to the location pool.

This adds the 11 national wonders and the 3 guilds to the location pool.

options.label: World Wonder Sanity
options.description:
Add all world wonders to the location pool.

This adds the 47 world wonders to the location pool, including the 3 ideology world wonders.

WARNING: This option is NOT suitable for syncs.

options.label: Unit Sanity
options.description:
Add most standard units to the location pool.

This adds 66 units to the location pool in total.

Units that will not be added:
- Foreign Legion
- Any religious unit (Inquisitor and Missionary)
- Any civilization-unique unit (they count as the unit they replace instead)
- Any Great Person
- Any Spaceship unit (SS Booster; SS Cockpit; SS Engine; and SS Stasis Chamber)

options.label: Settler Sanity
options.description:
Adds Settlers to the item and location pools, with the amount being determined by the Settler Sanity Amount option.

When enabled, Settlers can only be obtained as a progressive item. Training them counts as a location, up to the
amount, after which they can no longer be trained. When receiving a Settler as an item, they spawn near the capital
(or a different city if you happen to not have one).

Enabling this option will remove the Settler from the Unit Sanity location pool, if it is enabled.

options.label: Settler Sanity Amount
options.description:
Number of Settlers to put in the item and location pools.

Progression logic will expect you to be able to get the following number of Settlers per era:
- Ancient: 1
- Classical; Medieval; and Renaissance: 2
- Industrial; Modern; and Atomic: 3
- Information: 4

Has no effect if Settler Sanity is not enabled.

NOTE: The lower limit being 0 is not a mistake. If you want to be Venice as a different civilization, be my guest.

options.label: Promotion Sanity
options.description:
Add all earnable unit promotions (excl. Heal Instantly) to the item and location pools.

This adds 83 promotions to the item and location pools in total.

WARNING: This option can cause situations where you need to level up many units types to find logical progression.

options.label: Enable Traps
options.description: Add traps to the filler item pool.

options.label: Trap Filler Chance
options.description:
The percent chance for a filler item to be a trap instead.

Has no effect if traps are not enabled.

options.label: Death Link Trigger
options.description:
What triggers a death link to be sent?

Has no effect if death link is disabled.

Possible triggers:
- Unit killed: When any of your units gets killed.
- City captured: When any of your cities gets captured.
- Capital captured: When your capital gets captured.
- Game lost: When you lose a game.

options.label: Goal area
options.description:
The game will goal upon entering Aftermath.
- bossfight: Unlock and complete the Boss Fight level to unlock Aftermath
- aftermath: Quadcopter Pieces directly unlock Aftermath

options.label: Total pieces
options.description:
How many Quadcopter Pieces to add to the item pool.
There may be fewer than this depending on the number of free locations.

options.label: % pieces required
options.description: Percentage of total Quadcopter Pieces that need to be collected to unlock the goal area.

options.label: Levels
options.description: Require items to be able to access each level. Automatically gives you one level to start (19-20 items)

options.label: Hole effects
options.description:
- off: Hole contents always have effects.
- global: Require an item to have effects from hole contents. (1 item)
- split: Require items to have effects from each individual type of hole contents. (5 items)

options.label: Catapult
options.description:
- off: Catapult is always available.
- global: Require an item to use the catapult. (1 item, 1 location)
- split: Require items to launch specific kinds of object. (11 items, 1 location)

options.label: Texting
options.description: Require an item to be able to send text messages. (1 item)

options.label: Trash souls
options.description:
Require an item to unlock physics on each type of trash. Has no effect if `trashsanity` is `off`. (113 items)
"It's like the Dark Souls of trash"

options.label: Achievements
options.description: Location for each non-postgame achievement. (16 locations)

options.label: Snake danger
options.description: Ranger Station snake danger is randomized. (4 locations, 4 items)

options.label: Salt & pepper
options.description: Cat Soup shakers will give locations, Progressive Salt & Pepper unlock progression. (5 locations, 5 items)

options.label: Trashsanity
options.description:
- off: Trash gives no checks
- types: Collecting each type of trash is a location (113 locations)
- all: Collecting each individual piece of trash is a location (1274 locations)

options.label: Weapon Restriction Type
options.description:
Choose the restriction behavior:
Cannot Equip - Nothing will allow you to use the selected weapon types during this run
Require Multiworld Item - You will need to acquire an item from the multiworld to use the selected weapon types during this run

options.label: Restrict Pistols
options.description: Restrict pistols according to Weapon Restriction Type.

options.label: Restrict Melee
options.description: Restrict melee weapons according to Weapon Restriction Type.

options.label: Restrict Rifle
options.description: Restrict rifles according to Weapon Restriction Type.

options.label: Restrict Sniper Rifles
options.description: Restrict sniper rifles according to Weapon Restriction Type.

options.label: Restrict LMG
options.description: Restrict LMGs according to Weapon Restriction Type.

options.label: Restrict Shotgun
options.description: Restrict shotguns according to Weapon Restriction Type.

options.label: Restrict SMG
options.description: Restrict SMGs according to Weapon Restriction Type.

options.label: Weapon Passes from Other Worlds
options.description:
When weapon pass mode is active and this is enabled in a multiworld,
active weapon passes are added to non_local_items and cannot be placed
on your own checks.

No effect when weapon restriction type is not Require Multiworld Item,
or in solo seeds.

options.label: Completion Goal
options.description:
Choose what counts as completing the world:
- Complete Any Ending: reach Ending Reached (default behavior).
- Complete Any Ending W/ All Side Quests: reach Ending Reached and have
  logical access to every included SIDE_QUEST / DLC_SIDE location.
- Complete Only Phantom Liberty Questline: complete PL's main questline.
  This mode implies Phantom Liberty DLC for world generation and disables
  district token restrictions to keep the pool aligned to PL checks.

choices.label: Complete Any Ending W All Side Quests

options.label: District Restriction Type
options.description:
Choose the major-district restriction behavior:
- None: District tokens are not placed and the client will not enforce district locks.
- Require District Token: Selected districts require their access token.

Defaults to None: gating every major district behind its own always-required
Access Token can leave too few always-reachable locations to place all of
those tokens, causing generation failures. Opt in (and consider disabling
a few districts below) once you've verified generation succeeds for your
other settings.

options.label: Restrict Westbrook
options.description: Gate Westbrook behind its Access Token when District Restriction Type is Require District Token.

options.label: Restrict City Center
options.description: Gate City Center behind its Access Token when District Restriction Type is Require District Token.

options.label: Restrict Heywood
options.description: Gate Heywood behind its Access Token when District Restriction Type is Require District Token.

options.label: Restrict Santo Domingo
options.description: Gate Santo Domingo behind its Access Token when District Restriction Type is Require District Token.

options.label: Restrict Pacifica
options.description: Gate Pacifica behind its Access Token when District Restriction Type is Require District Token.

options.label: Restrict Badlands
options.description: Gate Badlands behind its Access Token when District Restriction Type is Require District Token.

options.label: Restrict Dogtown
options.description:
Gate Dogtown behind its Access Token when District Restriction Type is
Require District Token and Phantom Liberty is enabled.

options.label: Restrict by Sub District
options.description:
Restrict access to subdistricts
When enabled, players will only be able to access subdistricts by aquiring access tokens from the multiworld.
**Restrict by Major District must be enabled for this option to work.**

options.label: District Tokens from Other Worlds
options.description:
When district restrictions are active and this is enabled in a multiworld,
active district and subdistrict access tokens are added to non_local_items
and cannot be placed on your own checks.

No effect when district restriction type is None, in solo seeds, or when
the PL-only completion goal disables district restrictions.

options.label: Include Phantom Liberty DLC
options.description: Include Phantom Liberty DLC content (Dogtown and its questline) in generation.

options.label: Death Link
options.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

options.label: Death Link Amnesty
options.description: Deaths forgiven before sending a DeathLink. 0 means every death sends.

options.label: Include Gigs
options.description: Include gig checks in the location pool.

options.label: Include Tarot
options.description: Include tarot card checks in the location pool.

options.label: Include Cyber Psycho Sighting
options.description: Include cyberpsycho sighting checks in the location pool.

options.label: Quick Hacks as Items
options.description: Put progressive quickhack items into the multiworld

options.label: Include NCPD Hustles
options.description: Temporarily disabled: client detection is unreliable. Set via YAML to test.

options.label: Include Minor Quests
options.description: Include minor quest checks in the location pool.

options.label: Vendor Sanity
options.description: Turn vendor stock slots into checks. Individual vendor categories are toggled below.

options.label: Include Ripperdocs
options.description: Include ripperdoc vendor checks when Vendor Sanity is enabled.

options.label: Include Weapon Vendors
options.description: Include weapon vendor checks when Vendor Sanity is enabled.

options.label: Include Clothing Vendors
options.description: Include clothing vendor checks when Vendor Sanity is enabled.

options.label: Include Melee Vendors
options.description: Include melee weapon vendor checks when Vendor Sanity is enabled.

options.label: Include Netrunners
options.description: Include netrunner vendor checks when Vendor Sanity is enabled.

options.label: Enable Traps
options.description: Include trap items in the item pool.

options.label: Trap Items per Trap
options.description: How many trap items to add to the pool for each trap type, when Enable Traps is on.

options.label: Oops! All Traps!
options.description: Replaces all Useful and Filler items with traps

options.label: Character
options.description:
Which playable character this run uses.

Yunica, Hugo, and Toal climb the same tower with different skills/POV. The
vertical slice targets **Hugo**; Yunica/Toal come once their routes are
mapped.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
What finishing the seed requires.

defeat_darm: finish your character's story. Toal's ends with Darm; Yunica's
and Hugo's end with Dalles, so for them this means beating Dalles.
defeat_all_bosses: the same, after also defeating all six floor bosses
(Velagunder, Nygtilger, Gelaldy, Khonsclard, Pictimos and Zava). Useful with
warps, which can otherwise skip a boss.

options.label: Statue checks
options.description: Add a check for activating each goddess statue / save point (~22).

options.label: Blessing checks
options.description: Add a check for buying each Divine Blessing (~24, filler-only for now).

options.label: Boss checks
options.description:
Add a check for defeating each boss / mid-boss (~12). Sent when the fight
is won, and it can hold any item.

options.label: Floor checks
options.description: Add a check for reaching each tower floor (~21).

options.label: Room checks (sanity)
options.description:
Add a check for entering each tower room (~140). Big. A room check can hold
any item, like a chest.

options.label: Statue warp locks
options.description:
Lock the goddess statues. Each statue starts wrapped in darkness and stays
fully inactive — no warp, healing, saving, or blessings — until you receive
its unlock item (one per statue, shuffled into the multiworld). One statue is
unlocked from the start so you can always save (see Random start). Unlock
items are bonus convenience and don't affect logic (everything stays
reachable on foot).

options.label: Random start statue
options.description:
Start a New Game at a RANDOM goddess statue anywhere in the tower instead
of 1F. Requires Statue warp locks. The mod skips the entire intro (movies +
cutscenes, all characters) and warps you straight to the spawn statue with a
floor-appropriate level + weapon loadout so you're playable wherever you land;
reachability uses a bidirectional warp-network logic so the seed stays
beatable from any spawn. (Normal, non-random seeds are unchanged.)

options.label: Random start max floor
options.description:
Highest tower floor a Random start may spawn you on. Random start picks a
goddess statue uniformly at random, and the deep statues (a 25F spawn) drop you
into brutal rooms with no gear history behind you. This caps the draw to statues
on floor <= this value, so New Game always begins somewhere survivable while
still landing you *somewhere* rather than 1F. Only affects ``random_start``;
lower = gentler openings, raise it (up to 25 = the summit) for more variety.
Ignored when ``random_start`` is off. If no statue exists at or below the cap,
the lowest-floor statue is used. Default 5 keeps openings in the early tower
(1F/4F/5F statues) so a fresh, low-level, starter-weapon run stays fair.

options.label: Max warp floors skipped
options.description:
How many tower floors ahead of your current reach a warp may jump, in the
random-spawn warp network. With 0 the warp network is unrestricted (a single
received unlock can send you 15 floors up into rooms you have no business in
yet). With N > 0 the generator only puts a statue's warp in logic once you can
already reach a floor within N of it — so progress climbs in steps of at most N
floors instead of one lucky unlock teleporting you across the tower. Everything
still stays reachable on foot; this only paces the warp shortcuts. Only affects
``random_start``; 0 = unlimited (old behaviour).

options.label: Starting items
options.description:
Items to grant at the start of every New Game, as a floor (they're simply
marked owned — good for key items). Defaults to the two warp Crystals the
opening cutscene normally hands you (Crystal, and Toal's Dark Crystal), so a
Random start — which skips that intro — still begins with them. Add any item
names here (e.g. ``Mask of Eyes``) to start with them; unknown names are
ignored. Names must match the game's item names exactly.

options.label: Starting level
options.description:
Character level to start every New Game at, applied as a floor (only ever
raises you — never below your real level). Default 1 = vanilla. Raise it for a
gentler opening, especially with Random start dropping you on a higher floor.
Stacks with catch-up level scaling: you end up at the higher of this and the
floor's expected level.

options.label: Starting weapon level
options.description:
Displayed weapon level (1-6) to start every New Game with, applied as a
floor. Default 1 = the vanilla starter weapon. The in-game mod owns the weapon
(it upgrades on Cleria Ore and re-applies the floor-appropriate weapon on a
Random-start spawn), so this raises the *minimum*: you begin with at least this
level, and Cleria Ore / floor-appropriate gear can take you higher.

options.label: Level scaling
options.description:
Catch-up leveling so the statue warp network never means a grind wall.
Compares your level to the floor you're on (per the game's own level curve):

- ``off``            : vanilla leveling.
- ``level_floor``    : entering a floor far above your level bumps you up to
                       (floor level - margin); only ever raises you.
- ``exp_multiplier`` : boosted EXP only — no instant bump. A flat always-on
                       multiplier (default) so you level naturally but fast;
                       raise the catch-up option for extra EXP while behind.
                       This is the DEFAULT: with a low ``max_starting_floor``
                       you begin near-vanilla and just gain levels quicker,
                       rather than being teleported up in power.
- ``both``           : the bump gets you most of the way, the EXP boost
                       finishes it through play — for high warp-ahead starts.

options.label: Level scaling margin
options.description:
How many levels under a floor's expected level you may be before Level
scaling kicks in (also the gap the level-floor bump leaves for you to earn).
Default 0: with the corrected floor-level curve and a floor-appropriate
weapon, the level floor brings you to exactly the floor's expected level
(live-tuned at 18F: expected 27 + weapon Lv4 = the right difficulty). Raise it
if you want more challenge (you'll be that many levels under); too high and
combat clamps to 1 damage on warped-ahead floors.

options.label: Base EXP multiplier
options.description:
Flat EXP multiplier applied everywhere while EXP scaling is on (the
``exp_multiplier`` / ``both`` modes). Default 20x: a rando run zig-zags the
tower out of order and the mod's own EXP hook only reaches kills once fixed,
so a strong flat boost keeps leveling brisk. 1 = vanilla rate. A kill never
gives less than half the multiplier, however far below your level the
monster is.

options.label: Catch-up EXP multiplier
options.description:
EXP multiplier while you're CATCHING UP: your level is at or under the
expected level of the deepest floor you've visited, plus the margin below.
Replaces the base multiplier whenever the condition holds, so falling behind
your furthest progress levels you back fast wherever you choose to fight.
Default 60, three times the base: the floor curve climbs steeply from 18F
(27 -> 44 over five floors), and at the base rate a player who was on curve
at 17F fell a dozen levels behind by 20F. Set it equal to the base for a
single flat multiplier with no catch-up.

options.label: Catch-up margin (levels)
options.description:
How many levels ABOVE the deepest-visited floor's expected level still
count as catching up (the catch-up multiplier applies while
your level <= expected + this). Default 5.

options.label: EXP multiplier max (deprecated)
options.description:
DEPRECATED (v1.6.0): the single EXP cap was replaced by the
``exp_multiplier_base`` / ``exp_multiplier_catchup`` pair. Kept as an accepted
no-op so yamls written for v1.3.0-1.5.0 still generate without error; the
value is ignored. Set the two replacement options instead.

options.label: Progressive armor & boots
options.description:
Make defensive gear progressive. Ys Origin has two gear slots — Armor and
Boots — each a strict tier ladder per character. When on, every gear chest
puts a "Progressive Armor" / "Progressive Boots" in the pool instead of a
specific piece: receiving one grants your character's NEXT tier, so you can't
get the 22F armor before the 7F one (pickups never skip ahead). Off = raw
pieces are shuffled as-is (you can find endgame armor first).

options.label: Blessing effects in the item pool
options.description:
Shuffle the divine-blessing EFFECTS into the item pool.

Off (default): buying a blessing at a goddess statue sends the check AND
gives you that blessing, as it does today.

On: the statue sells checks only — the purchase reports the location and
the blessing itself does nothing. The 24 effects become real items that can
land anywhere in the multiworld, so someone else's chest might hand you
"Increase SP gain".

The purchase is detected at the grant opcode rather than by watching the
effect bit, so a bought slot still reads as bought and cannot be re-bought.

options.label: Progressive elemental skills
options.description:
Make the three elemental skills progressive.

Each element is an artifact plus three gems. Shuffled independently you can
collect three Emeralds and still not have the Wind skill, which they only
upgrade. On, each element becomes one chain of four: the first grants the
skill, the rest raise its level.

ALWAYS ON since 2.0: hidden, and forced on in generate_early. Kept as an
accepted no-op so older yamls still generate.

options.label: Progressive blessing tiers
options.description:
Make the tiered blessings progressive (LV1 -> LV2 -> LV3).

Seven blessings come in levels. Shuffled independently you can be handed LV3
before LV1, which is both nonsense and a balance jump. On, each family is one
chain granted in order.

Only does anything together with "Blessing effects in the item pool" — the
effects have to BE items before they can be made progressive.

options.label: Blessing shop hints
options.description:
Show what each Divine Blessing purchase actually gives (the multiworld
item scouted at that shop slot) on the in-game overlay while you're at a
goddess statue. Off = blessings are blind buys.

options.label: Blessing costs
options.description:
Blessing shop economy. ``vanilla`` = buy from the game's own statue menu
at its normal prices. ``shuffled`` = the mod's OWN shop overlay (F5) sells
the blessings at seed-randomized SP prices (between the min/max below) — the
vanilla menu still works at vanilla prices, but the overlay shop is where
the deals (and ripoffs) are. Purchases either way grant the blessing effect
AND the multiworld check. (The value can't be called ``random`` — that's a
reserved yaml keyword for Choice options in Archipelago.)

options.label: Blessing cost min
options.description:
Price of the CHEAPEST blessing slot (SP).

The shop is priced on a geometric ladder from this value up to
``blessing_cost_max``, so the early slots sit near this number and only the
last few approach the maximum.

options.label: Blessing cost max
options.description:
Price of the most EXPENSIVE blessing slot (SP).

The default spans 100 -> 100,000: early slots land in the low hundreds, the
midgame in the low thousands, and only the last couple are a real endgame
investment. The old 800 ceiling made every blessing trivially affordable by
the midgame. Expensive slots are also gated in logic behind the tower depth
their price implies, so a five-figure slot can never hold a sphere-1 item.

options.label: Blessing shop unlock
options.description:
How the overlay shop's inventory unlocks. ``all`` = every blessing is
purchasable from the start. ``one_per_floor`` = one more shop slot (cheapest
first) unlocks for each distinct tower floor you visit — pace your power to
your exploration.

options.label: Weapon requirements
options.description:
Gate each tower zone behind enough Cleria Ore (= weapon upgrades) to fight
there, so the warp network can't strand you somewhere your weapon can't dent.
When on, the generator guarantees the **vanilla weapon level for each floor**
is obtainable (by you, or friends in a multiworld) before that zone is in
logic, and Cleria Ore becomes progression.
Off = no weapon gating (Cleria Ore is filler). Either way, receiving a
Cleria Ore upgrades your weapon on the spot.

options.label: Fire skill crosses gaps (Toal)
options.description:
Count Toal's fire skill as a way across gaps the logic otherwise wants the
wind skill or the double jump for: the 2F Path 2 gap, and the 22F Path 2
chest (which otherwise needs both). His fire skill is a forward dash and
carries him over; the other two characters' fire skills do not, so the
option does nothing for them.
Off (the default) = those need the wind skill and / or the Gold Bracelet.

options.label: Item classification overrides
options.description:
Retune how individual items are classified for THIS seed (advanced).

Map item names to a tier — ``filler``, ``useful``, ``progression`` or
``trap`` — to override the apworld's built-in classification. The tier
controls how the fill algorithm treats the item: only ``progression`` items
are guaranteed to land somewhere reachable, ``useful`` are placed with mild
priority, ``filler`` anywhere. Empty (the default) = use the built-in tiers.

Applied LAST, so it wins over every default (including the automatic
Cleria-Ore / statue-warp promotions). Unknown item names and invalid tiers
are ignored with a log warning — a typo never aborts generation.

Use it to stop *minor* progression items from eating your priority
locations, e.g. ``{"Mask of Eyes": useful}``. You may also DOWNGRADE a
default-progression item to ``filler`` when you know a skip makes it
non-essential — that's allowed on purpose. Caveat: if you demote an item the
logic actually requires, generation fails loudly (a broken seed is never
produced), so only downgrade items you're sure are skippable.

The current default tiers are listed in the yaml template comment; anything
not listed there is ``filler``.

options.label: Trap count
options.description:
How many filler slots to replace with TRAP items, shuffled into the
multiworld — you'll send them to other players and receive them yourself.
Traps: **EXP Leech** (drops a chunk of your EXP), **Chaos Warp** (yanks you to
a random unlocked statue), **Butterfingers** (weapon reverts to Lv1 for a few
seconds), **Blinding Fog** (screen hazes over briefly). 0 = no traps.

options.label: Tasks Reward DP
options.description:
Should tasks reward the normal DP amount upon completion.
If off, some filler DP items are replaced with larger
sums of DP to replace the missing task rewards.

options.label: Starting DP Balance
options.description:
Starting DP Balance. The vanilla value is 2500.
This is not exact; you will start with a balance *near* the selected value.

options.label: Additional DP in Itempool
options.description:
How much DP should be in the itempool? Note, currently the only filler
item is small amounts of DP, so there will be more than just this much
in the item pool. This option allows you to force the addition of larger
DP items to the pool. If 'Tasks Reward DP' is off, some larger DP amounts
will have already been added. We recommend at least some additional DP,
since you may receive expensive Species before having a lot of DP earn per minute.

options.label: Include Size Checks
options.description: Adds checks for breeding species of size 1.10 and 1.20.

options.label: Free Evolution
options.description:
Removes the DP cost from evolution. Other requirements
still must be fulfilled.

options.label: Goal
options.description: Completion condition

worlds.game: The Magical Quest Starring Mickey Mouse

options.label: Game Mode
options.description:
How the Stages open up.

Map Fragments: You start with one Stage, and each Stage is locked behind an AP Item called "Map Fragment", shuffled into the multiworld.
You are guaranteed to always start with a Map Fragment. Recommended for playing alongside other games.

Open World: All Stages are available from the beginning: Treetops, Dark Forest, Fire Grotto, Pete's Peak and Snowy Valley.
Only the Pete's Castle Map Fragment has to be found in the multiworld. Recommended for synchronous play.

Linear: You start in Treetops. Clearing a Stage unlocks the next one, in the vanilla game's order.
(Treetops -> Dark Forest -> Fire Grotto -> Pete's Peak -> Snowy Valley -> Pete's Castle).

Vanilla Progression: Like Linear, but each Costume is also on its vanilla Stage
(Wizard in Dark Forest, Firefighter in Fire Grotto, Mountaineer in Pete's Peak).
Costumes are received on Stage entry. You will likely end before other Players.

options.label: Starting Stage
options.description:
The Stage you start in. 
This only applies to the Map Fragments Game Mode.
Recommended: Random.

options.label: Starting Max Health
options.description:
The number of Big Hearts Mickey starts with (1 to 10). The rest of the Big Hearts are placed in the pool.
The vanilla game starts with 3 on Normal and 2 on Hard. Only choose 1 if you hate your own guts.

options.label: Hard-only Box Holds Filler
options.description:
Treetops 1-2 has a Treasure Box that can only be reached when the game is played on Hard difficulty.
Turn this is on so that Location only holds filler items. Turn it off if you plan to play on Hard: it becomes a normal Location.
You choose the difficulty in the game's own options menu.

options.label: Store Hints
options.description:
When you enter a Store, the client sends hints for what you would get from it: the two Upgrades in every Store,
and the two Big Hearts in their respective Stores. Everyone in the multiworld sees them, whichever game
the item belongs to. Turn this off if you would rather find out what the Store holds by buying it.

Simple - Wind Scroll jump maybe required in areas that need double jump height and are easy to do

options.label: Starter Pack
options.description:
This provides a set of stages and puzzles to start with.
If you're doing Stage Clear only and you don't start in Round 6, the Last Stage will be in Round 6.
Starting with only one Stage Clear round has all 5 stages in that round unlocked.
Starting with only one Puzzle level has all 10 puzzles in that level unlocked.
If there are only extra puzzles and no regular puzzles, the starter level is corrected as such.
Vs Two Stages gives stages 1 and 2.

options.label: Stage Clear Goal
options.description:
This makes Stage Clear Last Stage Clear one of the goals (you will need to complete all goals for the seed).
If multiple modes need to be cleared, each will provide a final item and auto-hint the other win conditions.
Note that if you don't start in round 6, the Last Stage unlock will be in Stage Clear Round 6 Clear.

options.label: Puzzle Goal
options.description:
This makes Puzzle and/or Extra Puzzle Round 6 Clear one of the goals (you will need to complete all goals for the seed).
If multiple modes need to be cleared, each will provide a final item and auto-hint the other win conditions.

options.label: Versus Goal
options.description:
This makes Versus one of the goals (you will need to complete all goals for the seed).
If multiple modes need to be cleared, each will provide a final item and auto-hint the other win conditions.
Note that harder difficulties will be forced to end at the goal difficulty's final stage.
If Easy Bowser is enabled for Easy or Normal, the goal becomes Stage 12 at that difficulty.
Stages that come after the goal stage will be extra unlocks and checks.

options.label: Stage Clear Inclusion
options.description:
This adds Stage Clear to the randomizer, even if they are not part of the goal.
Note that if the Last Stage is a goal, this won't have any effect.

options.label: Puzzle Inclusion
options.description:
This adds Puzzles to the randomizer, even if they are not part of the goal.
Note that if (Extra) Puzzle Round 6 Clear is a goal, this won't have any effect unless the other set is not a goal.

options.label: Versus Inclusion
options.description:
This adds Versus to the randomizer, even if they are not part of the goal.
Note that if clearing Versus is a goal, this won't have any effect.

options.label: Stage Clear Mode
options.description:
Determines how progression works in Stage Clear.
Whole Rounds puts each round as one item.
Individual Stages puts each round as 5 progressive items. All 5 are needed to start a round.
Incremental puts each round as 5 progressive items with optional gate.
Skippable puts each round as 5 or 6 items. You can start a round with some stages locked, but all 5 stages are needed for the Round Clear.

options.label: Stage Clear Filler
options.description:
If enabled, the game will maximize the number of locations (aside from additional Special Stages) and add more filler items to the pool.
Note that there are situations where filler is forced, otherwise the logic would be too tight and lead to unbeatable seeds.

options.label: Stage Clear Saves
options.description: If enabled, Stage Clear will let you resume rounds at the first unchecked stage or the stage after the last cleared one, whichever is earlier

options.label: Special Stage Trap Count
options.description:
Adds extra locations to certain Stage Clear stages such as Round 3 Clear, but as a consequence adds the Special Stage trap.
When tripped, you must either win or lose the Special Stage before you can continue.
Requires Stage Clear to be included or as a goal.

options.label: Special Stage Hp Multiplier
options.description: Changes Bowser's HP to this times 100 in the Special Stage traps. Default (vanilla) is 6 (x100).

options.label: Last Stage Hp Multiplier
options.description:
Changes Bowser's HP to this times 100 at the Last Stage. Default (vanilla) is 6 (x100).
For reference, a x2 Chain does 50 damage while a x6 Chain does a total of 980 damage.

options.label: Shock Panel Checks
options.description:
Number of items to add to the item pool locked behind clearing shock panels (gray ! panels) in Stage Clear.
Multiply by the panels per check for the total panel count in your slot.
For reference, one panel will spawn per row but will step up to two panels per row if you fall behind.

options.label: Shock Panels Per Check
options.description:
Number of shock panels required to unlock each check.
This also determines the number of panels you get each time you receive the item.

options.label: Puzzle Mode
options.description:
Determines how progression works in Puzzle.
Whole Levels puts each level as one item.
Individual Stages puts each level as 10 progressive items. All 10 are needed to start a level.
Incremental puts each level as 10 progressive items with optional gate.
Skippable puts each level as 10 or 11 items. You can start a level with some puzzles locked, but all 10 puzzles are needed for the Round Clear.

options.label: Puzzle Filler
options.description:
If enabled, the game will maximize the number of locations and add more filler items to the pool.
Note that there are situations where filler is forced, otherwise the logic would be too tight and lead to unbeatable seeds.

options.label: Versus Mode
options.description:
Determines how difficulty levels are handled and which ones have locations.
Minimum puts locations on the minimum difficulty level required for each stage except for the last stage.
For example, if the goal is to beat Vs on Hard, stages 1 to 10 will still give checks on Easy.
If filler is included, higher difficulties for early stages are considered non-priority.
Minimum progressive is the same as above, but adds one set of unlocks as progressive from 1 to 10/11/12.
Goal puts locations on the goal difficulty level only, and also forces the game to that difficulty.
Goal progressive is the same as above, but adds one set of unlocks as progressive from 1 to 10/11/12.

options.label: Versus Easy Bowser
options.description:
When enabled, Kamek can be fought on Easy, and Bowser can be fought on Easy and Normal.
This also changes the goal stage number for Easy and Normal goals.

options.label: Music Filter
options.description: Pick the categories of music you want to disable. Menu music also includes the title screen.

Asylum Brain Tank and Brain Hunt: Find the required amount of Camper Brains, AND defeat the Coach Oleander Brain Tank.
