options.label: Item pool
options.description:
Which spots hold items from the multiworld. The others keep their vanilla item (or get shuffled, with
randomize_other_items).
key_items: only the spots that hold key items in the vanilla game.
guarded: those, plus most items guarded by bosses.
equipment: those, plus most of the equipment lying around.
everything: every item spot in the castle.

options.label: Shuffle the other items
options.description: The vanilla items of the spots that aren't in the item pool are shuffled among those spots.

options.label: Powerful items
options.description:
Puts the game's most powerful items in: Duplicator, Crissaegrim, Ring of varda, Mablung sword, Masamune,
Marsil and Yasutsuna, each in place of another item (in the item pool, or with randomize_other_items at one
of the other spots).

options.label: Boss drops
options.description:
The items the 13 bosses drop when beaten are checks. Your own key items are never put there: a drop you
leave behind is gone for good.

options.label: Enemysanity
options.description:
Each kind of enemy is a check the first time it gets into your enemy list (141 checks). What fills them
depends on difficulty:
easy: a second copy of every key item, plus 50 vessels and 50 pieces of equipment.
normal: a second Gold ring, Silver ring, Spike breaker and Holy glasses, plus 35 vessels and 35 pieces of
equipment.
hard: 15 vessels and 15 pieces of equipment.
very_hard: nothing extra.
The rest is filler (fruit).

options.label: Enemysanity needs the Faerie scroll
options.description:
Enemysanity checks only count once you have the Faerie scroll (enemies met before then count once you
get it).

options.label: Caverns back door
options.description:
The back door between the Castle Entrance and the Underground Caverns.
closed: closed, as in the vanilla game (opened from the Caverns side).
open_after_alchemy_lab: open once you've been to the Alchemy Laboratory.
open_from_start: open from the start, so you can get to it before meeting Death at the entrance.

options.label: Colosseum back door
options.description: The back door between the Royal Chapel and the Colosseum is open from the start.

options.label: Open shortcuts
options.description:
The castle's shortcuts are open from the start: from the Castle Entrance to the Underground Caverns, to the
Marble Gallery and to its warp room, from Olrox's Quarters and from the Colosseum to the Royal Chapel, and the
one in the inverted castle's Entrance. The logic doesn't count on them.

options.label: Starting area
options.description:
After the first Warg at the entrance, you're taken to a random room and play on from there.
vanilla: you aren't; the game goes on from the entrance.
random_castle: a room in the castle.
random_inverted_castle: a room in the inverted castle (Leap stone and Gravity boots work there until you
reach the castle).
random_anywhere: a room in either.
The logic doesn't take the new start into account.

options.label: Library card to the inverted castle
options.description:
Hold down while using a Library card to go to the inverted castle's library instead (once Richter is
saved).

options.label: Skip the Clock Tower puzzle
options.description: No gear puzzle in the Clock Tower: hitting any of the gears once opens the secret door.

options.label: No logic
options.description: Items go anywhere, without logic: the seed can need glitches, or be unbeatable.

options.label: Difficulty
options.description:
easy: enemies have half their HP, attack and defence and always drop their items; the shop costs 50-75%.
normal: the vanilla game.
hard: enemies have 1.5 times their HP, attack and defence; the shop costs 100-125%.
very_hard: enemies have twice their HP, attack and defence; the shop costs 125-150%.

options.label: Enemy strength
options.description:
Enemy HP, attack and defence as a percentage of the vanilla values (25-200), instead of what difficulty
sets. use_difficulty: leave it to difficulty.

options.label: Random enemy stats
options.description:
Each enemy gets random HP, attack and defence (25-200% of the vanilla values; difficulty or
enemy_strength replaces this part with its own scaling), and a random attack element, weaknesses and
resistances.

options.label: Drop rate
options.description:
How often enemies drop their items.
normal: as difficulty sets (the vanilla rates, or always on easy).
increased: more often.
abundant: more often still.
guaranteed: every enemy that has a drop always drops; with the Ring of arcana, its rare one.

options.label: Enemy drops
options.description:
What enemies drop.
vanilla: the vanilla drops.
shuffled: the vanilla drops, shuffled between enemies.
same_type: each drop is a random item of the same kind (a weapon for a weapon, a potion for a potion...).
any_item: each drop is any random item.

options.label: Enemy drops: hearts and gold too
options.description: With enemy_drops, the hearts, gold and other small drops any enemy can leave change too.

options.label: Enemy drops: can be key items
options.description:
With enemy_drops same_type or any_item, a drop can be a Gold ring, Silver ring, Spike breaker or Holy
glasses: extra copies, outside the logic.

options.label: Candle drops
options.description:
What candles drop (not the ones with the Stopwatch).
vanilla: the vanilla items.
shuffled: the vanilla items, shuffled between candles.
same_type: each is a random item of the same kind, never a key item.
any_item: each is any random item, never a key item.
any_item_with_key_items: any random item, including the Gold ring, Silver ring, Spike breaker and Holy
glasses (extra copies, outside the logic).

options.label: Shop stock
options.description:
What the Librarian sells.
vanilla: the vanilla stock.
random_items: random items, which can be key items (extra copies, outside the logic).
random_non_key_items: random items, never a key item.

options.label: Shop sells the Library card
options.description: With random items in shop_stock, the Librarian still sells the Library card.

options.label: Random shop prices
options.description: Shop prices are random, 50-150% of the vanilla prices, instead of what difficulty sets.

options.label: Random starting equipment
options.description: Alucard starts with a random weapon, shield, helmet, armour, cloak and accessory, never a key item.

options.label: Death doesn't take your equipment
options.description: Death doesn't take Alucard's equipment at the entrance.

options.label: Skip the prologue
options.description: A new game starts with Alucard, without Richter's fight with Dracula.

options.label: Infinite wing smash
options.description: Wing smash keeps going until you hit a wall or run out of MP (leave bat form to stop it).

options.label: Magic vessels
options.description: Heart Vessels also raise max MP by 3 and refill MP.

options.label: No screen freezes
options.description: The game doesn't pause when you level up or pick up a relic or a vessel.

options.label: Fast warp
options.description: Faster animation when using a warp room.

options.label: Heal at save rooms
options.description: Entering a save room restores HP and MP.

options.label: DeathLink
options.description: When you die, everyone else with DeathLink on dies too, and the other way round.

options.label: Map colour
options.description: Colour of the map (the pause map, and the mod's map window).

options.label: Alucard's colours
options.description: Alucard's colours.

options.label: Cape lining
options.description: Colour of the lining of Alucard's cape.

options.label: Random colours
options.description:
Random colours for Alucard's cape, the Gravity boots trail, Hydro storm, wing smash, Richter, Dracula's
cape and Maria.

options.label: Relic surprise
options.description: Every relic looks the same: you only find out which one it is when you pick it up.

options.label: Random music
options.description: Each area plays a random song.

traps: Black Marble Gallery - Corridor to Entrance Item on Spike Trap

worlds.game: Jak and Daxter: The Precursor Legacy

options.label: Enable Move Randomizer
options.description:
Include movement options as items in the randomizer. Until you find his other moves, Jak is limited to
running, swimming, single-jumping, and shooting yellow eco through his goggles.

This adds 11 items to the pool.

options.label: Enable Orbsanity
options.description:
Include bundles of Precursor Orbs as checks. Every time you collect the chosen number of orbs, you will trigger
another check.

**Per Level:** bundles are for each level in the game.

**Global:** bundles carry over level to level.

This adds a number of Items and Locations to the pool inversely proportional to the size of the bundle.
For example, if your bundle size is 20 orbs, you will add 100 items to the pool. If your bundle size is 250 orbs,
you will add 8 items to the pool.

options.label: Global Orbsanity Bundle Size
options.description:
The orb bundle size for Global Orbsanity. This only applies if "Enable Orbsanity" is set to "Global."
There are 2000 orbs in the game, so your bundle size must be a factor of 2000.

This value is restricted to safe minimum and maximum values to ensure valid singleplayer games and
non-disruptive multiplayer games, but the host can remove this restriction by turning off enforce_friendly_options
in host.yaml.

options.label: Per Level Orbsanity Bundle Size
options.description:
The orb bundle size for Per Level Orbsanity. This only applies if "Enable Orbsanity" is set to "Per Level."
There are 50, 150, or 200 orbs per level, so your bundle size must be a factor of 50.

This value is restricted to safe minimum and maximum values to ensure valid singleplayer games and
non-disruptive multiplayer games, but the host can remove this restriction by turning off enforce_friendly_options
in host.yaml.

options.label: Enable Ordered Cell Counts
options.description:
Reorder the Cell Count requirements for vehicle sections to be in ascending order.

For example, if Fire Canyon Cell Count, Mountain Pass Cell Count, and Lava Tube Cell Count are 60, 30, and 40
respectively, they will be reordered to 30, 40, and 60.

options.label: Require Punch For Klaww
options.description:
Force the Punch move to come before Klaww.

Disabling this setting may require Jak to fight Klaww and Gol and Maia by shooting yellow eco through his goggles.

This only applies if "Enable Move Randomizer" is ON.

options.label: Filler Power Cells Replaced With Traps
options.description:
The number of filler power cells that will be replaced with traps. This does not affect the number of progression
power cells.

If this value is greater than the number of filler power cells, then they will all be replaced with traps.

options.label: Filler Orb Bundles Replaced With Traps
options.description:
The number of filler orb bundles that will be replaced with traps. This does not affect the number of progression
orb bundles. This only applies if "Enable Orbsanity" is set to "Per Level" or "Global."

If this value is greater than the number of filler orb bundles, then they will all be replaced with traps.

options.label: Trap Effect Duration
options.description:
The length of time, in seconds, that a trap effect lasts. If set to 0, trap items will still be created to replace
filler items, but they will have no effect ingame.

options.label: Boosted and Extended Uppercuts
options.description:
Create alternate paths to some areas with advanced movement.

Enabling this setting may require Jak to use boosted and extended uppercuts as opposed to regular movement options.

It may also require Jak to use uneven geometry, or missing collision boxes to reach unintended locations.

This only applies if "Enable Move Randomizer" is ON.

options.label: Punch Uppercut Scout Flies
options.description:
Treat *Punch Uppercut* as a valid move to break scout fly boxes.

Enabling this setting may require Jak to break scout fly boxes using only *Punch Uppercut*, even in confined spaces.

This only applies if "Enable Move Randomizer" is ON.

options.label: Geyser Rock Cliff Climb
options.description:
Remove the movement requirement for the Geyser Rock Cliff.

Enabling this setting may require Jak to use uneven terrain to reach the cliff with only *Single Jump*.

This only applies if "Enable Move Randomizer" is ON.

options.label: Sentinel Beach Cannon Tower Climb
options.description:
Create an alternate path to the Sentinel Beach Cannon Tower.

Enabling this setting may require Jak to use uneven geometry to reach the cannon tower without having the
*Blue Eco Switch* unlocked.

**Medium:** Tower is climbable with only *Double Jump*.

**Hard:** Tower is climbable with only *Jump Kick* or only *Double Jump*.

This only applies if "Enable Move Randomizer" is ON.

options.label: Snowy Mountain Entrance Climb
options.description:
Create an alternate path into Snowy Mountain.

Enabling this setting may require Jak to use uneven geometry to reach Snowy Mountain's main area with fewer move
options.

**Medium:** only *Double Jump* or *Crouch Jump*

**Hard:** only *Single Jump*

This only applies if "Enable Move Randomizer" is ON.

options.label: Boggy Swamp Flut Flut Escape
options.description:
Create an alternate path into the Boggy Swamp Ambush.

Enabling this setting may require Jak to get Flut Flut into the ambush arena instead of using attacking moves.

This only applies if "Enable Move Randomizer" is ON.

options.label: Snowy Mountain Flut Flut Escape
options.description:
Changes Snowy Mountain to rely on Flut Flut for movement.

Enabling this setting may require Jak to get Flut Flut over an invisible barrier to access all of Snowy Mountain.

options.label: Snowy Mountain Flut Flut Skip
options.description:
Create an alternative path to the end of the Flut Flut course in Snowy Mountain.

Enabling this setting may require Jak to use advanced movement tricks to reach the Fort Gate Button with only
*Single Jump* and no *Flut Flut*.

options.label: Sandover Village Orb Cache Climb
options.description:
Create an alternative path to the Sandover Village orb cache on the cliff.

Enabling this setting may require Jak to use precise jumps to reach the orb cache (and the blue eco next to it) with
only *Single Jump*.

This only applies if "Enable Move Randomizer" is ON.

options.label: Attackless Lurker Cannons
options.description:
Remove the attack requirement for lurker cannon power cells in Sentinel Beach and Misty Island.

Enabling this setting may require Jak to defeat the lurkers next to the cannon without any attacking moves.

This only applies if "Enable Move Randomizer" is ON.

options.label: Sentinel Beach Attackless Pelican
options.description:
Create an alternative path to the Pelican power cell in Sentinel Beach.

Enabling this setting may require Jak to  use other unlocks to acquire the power cell without any attacking moves.

This only applies if "Enable Move Randomizer" is ON.

options.label: Attack with Roll Jump
options.description:
Treat *Roll Jump* as a valid attack move for some power cells.

Enabling this setting may require Jak to use *Roll Jump* to destroy objects and acquire these power cells.

This only applies if "Enable Move Randomizer" is ON.

options.label: Forbidden Jungle Attackless Spiral Stumps Scout Fly
options.description:
Create an alternative path to the Scout Fly "On Spiral Of Stumps" in Forbidden Jungle.

Enabling this setting may require Jak to use precise movement to collect this scout fly without attack moves.

This only applies if "Enable Move Randomizer" is ON.

options.label: Forbidden Jungle Elevator Skip
options.description:
Create an alternative path to the temple interior in Forbidden Jungle without having *Jungle Elevator* unlocked.

Enabling this setting may require Jak to get inside the temple with only *Jump Kick*.

options.label: Misty Island Single Jump Far Side Orb Cache
options.description:
Create an alternative path to the Far Side Orb Cache in Misty Island.

Enabling this setting may require Jak to reach the orb cache with blue eco with only *Single Jump*.

This only applies if "Enable Move Randomizer" is ON.

options.label: Misty Island Attackless Scout Flies
options.description:
Remove attack requirements to the scout flies "Barrel Ramps", "Ledge Near Arena Entrance", "Near Arena Door",
"Overlooking Entrance" in Misty Island.

Enabling this setting may require Jak to break these scout fly boxes with precise blue eco movement or clever use
of game mechanics.

This only applies if "Enable Move Randomizer" is ON.

options.label: Misty Island Arena Fight Skip
options.description:
Create an alternative path to the power cell "Return To The Dark Eco Pool" in Misty Island.

Enabling this setting may require Jak to reach this power cell with only *Single Jump*.

This only applies if "Enable Move Randomizer" is ON.

options.label: Misty Island Far Side Cliff Seesaw Skip
options.description:
Create an alternative path to the far side cliff (with scout fly "Scout Fly On Ledge Near Arena Exit") in Misty
Island.

Enabling this setting may require Jak to use uneven terrain to find an alternative way to the cliff, using
only *Single Jump*.

This only applies if "Enable Move Randomizer" is ON.

options.label: Rock Village Single Jump Orb Cache
options.description:
Remove requirements from the orb cache in Rock Village.

Enabling this setting may require Jak to use precise movement to reach the orb cache with only *Single Jump*.

This only applies if "Enable Move Randomizer" is ON.

options.label: Rock Village Pontoon Skip
options.description:
Create alternative paths to Boggy Swamp and Klaww Cliff in Rock Village.

Enabling this setting may require Jak to use precise movement to reach these locations without having the
*Warrior's Pontoons* unlocked.

This only applies if "Enable Move Randomizer" is ON.

options.label: Klaww Cliff Climb
options.description:
Create an alternative path to get up to Klaww from Rock Village.

Enabling this setting may require Jak to use glitches and uneven terrain to reach Klaww with only *Single Jump*.

This only applies if "Enable Move Randomizer" is ON.

options.label: Klaww Boulder Skip
options.description:
Create an alternative path to Klaww without having enough power cells.

Enabling this setting may require Jak to use glitches to reach Klaww even if the boulder is not lifted.

This may drastically increase the amount of reachable locations when Rock Village is reachable.

This only applies if "Enable Move Randomizer" is ON.

options.label: Boggy Swamp Precise Movement
options.description:
Create an alternative path through Boggy Swamp.

Enabling this setting may require Jak to traverse through the whole Boggy Swamp with only *Single Jump* using
precise movement, invincibility after taking damage, and respawns.

This only applies if "Enable Move Randomizer" is ON.

options.label: Boggy Swamp Attackless Ambush
options.description:
Remove the attack requirement from the Boggy Swamp ambush.

Enabling this setting may require Jak to defeat the lurkers by only shooting yellow Eco through his goggles.

This only applies if "Enable Move Randomizer" is ON.

options.label: Boggy Swamp Flut Flut Skip
options.description:
Create an alternative path through the Flut Flut course in Boggy Swamp without having *Flut Flut* unlocked.

Enabling this setting may require Jak to complete the whole course with only *Roll Jump*, and reach the scout fly
"Overlooking Flut Flut" with only *Double Jump* or *Jump Kick*.

options.label: Lost Precursor City Single Jump Slide Tube Climb
options.description:
Create an alternative path through the helix with the rising dark eco in Lost Precursor City.

Enabling this setting may require Jak to use precise movement to reach the power cell at the bottom of Lost
Precursor City and escape the rising dark eco with only *Single Jump*.

This only applies if "Enable Move Randomizer" is ON.

options.label: Snowy Mountain Fort Gate Skip
options.description:
Create an alternative path into the Snowy Mountain Fort Gate without having *Snowy Fort Gate* unlocked.

Enabling this setting may require Jak to use uneven geometry and precise movement, or *Flut Flut* to enter the Fort
in Snowy Mountain.

**On Foot**: Fort is reachable after many movement options are unlocked.

**Flut Flut**: Fort is reachable after *Flut Flut* is unlocked.

options.label: Sentinel Beach Blue Eco Switch Skip
options.description:
Create an alternative path to the blue eco jump pad in Sentinel Beach without having *Blue Eco Switch* unlocked.

Enabling this setting may require Jak to use precise movement to reach the jump pad with enough blue eco, using
only *Punch* or only *Roll Jump*.

options.label: Completion Condition
options.description: Set the goal for completing the game.

options.label: Hide Spoiler Names
options.description: Replace character and some area names with spoiler free name.

options.label: Victory Condition
options.description:
Determine the victory condition

- Chapter 1: Beat Chapter 1 Boss
- Chapter 2: Beat Chapter 2 Boss

options.label: Treasure Chests Items
options.description:
Determine the treasure chest item pool

- Vanilla Shuffle: Shuffle the vanilla chest items into the item pool.
- Completely Random: Generate new item pool.

options.label: Randomize Starting Characters
options.description:
Randomize who you start the game with.

- Vanilla: Start the game with Kevin and Ries
- Set: Start the game with specific character(s)
- Completely Random: Start the game with completely random characters

options.label: First Starting Characters
options.description:
Pick the first character to start the game with.
Only used when Randomize Starting Character is set to Set.

options.label: Second Starting Characters
options.description:
Pick the second character to start the game with.
Only used when Randomize Starting Character is set to Set.
If the same character from the previous option is picked, it will be treated as random.

options.label: Sealing Stone Characters Unlock
options.description:
Randomize what you get from interacting with a sealing stone.

- Vanilla: Sealing Stones will unlock their respective character. Will be replace with Kevin and Ries if the character is selected as a starting character.
- Shuffle: Sealing Stones will unlock random characters.
- Charactersanity: Sealing Stones will give random items. Characters are in the general item pool.

options.label: Character Starting Quartz
options.description:
Determine the character starting quartz pool. They are obtained by interacting with the respective character's sealing stone.

- Vanilla: Character Sealing Stone will give out the default quartz loadout for that character.
- Vanilla Shuffle: The default starting quartz will be added to the general item pool. Character Sealing Stone will give out a completely random item for each starting quartz the character has in vanilla.
- Random Quartz: Character Sealing Stone will give out a random quartz for each starting quartz the character has in vanilla.
- Completely Random: Character Sealing Stone will give out a completely random item for each starting quartz the character has in vanilla.

options.label: Craft Shuffle
options.description:
If enabled, characters crafts may differ from their default crafts.
E.g. Estelle may get Joshua's Dual Strike instead of Hurricane.

options.label: Craft Placement
options.description:
Shuffle craft unlocks into the item pool.

Default: Crafts are placed in the default locations.
Crafts: Craft unlock locations will always unlock a craft, but it will be for a random character.
Anywhere: Crafts can be anywhere in the item pool.

options.label: Weapon Shuffle
options.description:
Shuffle Weapon unlocks into the item pool.
Weapon unlocks are progressive based on weapon type.

options.label: Craft Level Offset
options.description:
Level offset applied to craft unlocks. For example, if set to -2, you will receive
all crafts 2 levels earlier that you would otherwise. This reduces grinding.

Modifying this option to extreme amounts may lead to out of logic location checks.
This is because logic assumes that you will get crafts at their default level.

options.label: Goal Type
options.description:
How game completion is determined.

- **Unique Characters:** Win with N different characters.
- **Total Wins:** Win N matches total.
- **Spirits:** Collect N Spirits (MacGuffin) to win.
- **Win with Character:** Collect X Spirits to unlock your chosen final character, then win one match with that character.

options.label: Unique Characters to Win
options.description: Number of unique characters you must win with to finish (1-38).

options.label: Total Wins to Win
options.description: Number of total match wins you must achieve to finish.

options.label: Spirits to Win
options.description: Number of Spirits (MacGuffin) you must collect to finish. Max depends on game mode (Standard: 162, Street Brawl: 143).

options.label: Spirits to Unlock Final Character
options.description:
Number of Spirits (MacGuffin) you must collect to unlock your final character (Win with Character goal).

The world caps this below the usual Spirits max by three: the final hero's three win checks require
this many Spirits first and may themselves contain Spirits, so the threshold must be reachable using
other locations only.

options.label: Game Mode
options.description: Which game mode locations are included. Only checks for the selected mode exist in the seed.

options.label: Exclude Hard Locations
options.description: When enabled, locations marked as hard (MVP/Key Player, high kills, fast rounds, etc.) are removed from the seed.

options.label: Goal: Number of Levels
options.description:
If the goal is 'Complete Some Levels', 'Complete Random Levels', or 'Complete Some And Specific Levels',
this is how many levels must be completed.

options.label: Goal: Specific Levels
options.description:
If the goal is 'Complete Specific Levels', or 'Complete Some And Specific Levels',
all levels chosen here must be completed.

options.label: Added Ammo - Bullets
options.description: Set how much capacity for Bullets will be added when a capacity upgrade is obtained.

options.label: Added Ammo - Shells
options.description: Set how much capacity for Shells will be added when a capacity upgrade is obtained.

options.label: Added Ammo - Energy Cells
options.description: Set how much capacity for Energy Cells will be added when a capacity upgrade is obtained.

options.label: Added Ammo - Rockets
options.description: Set how much capacity for Rockets will be added when a capacity upgrade is obtained.

options.label: Energy Link
options.description:
Enables using the server's EnergyLink pool to obtain powerups.

When enabled, items sent to you that would have no mechanical effect are instead converted into energy.
You can then spend that energy at any later time to refill your ammo or give yourself powerups.

Optionally, you can set this option to an arbitrary string.
This will restict your EnergyLink pool to only other players that use the same string.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Choose the goal of the game.

- **Complete All Levels**: Complete every level to win.
- **Complete Some Levels**: Complete some number of total levels to win.
- **Complete Random Levels**: Complete a set of randomly chosen levels to win.
- **Complete Specific Levels**: Complete a specific set of levels to win.
- **Complete Some And Specific Levels**: Complete some number of total levels, as well as specifically chosen ones, to win.

options.label: Difficulty
options.description:
Choose the game difficulty (skill level).

- **Baby**: (I'm too young to die.) - Damage taken is halved. Ammo received from pickups is doubled.
- **Easy**: (Hey, not too rough.) - Lesser number or strength of monsters, and more pickups.
- **Medium**: (Hurt me plenty.) - The default skill. Balanced monsters and pickups.
- **Hard**: (Ultra-Violence.) - Greater number or strength of monsters, and less pickups.
- **Nightmare**: (Nightmare!) - Monsters are faster, more aggressive, and respawn.

options.label: Reset Level on Death
options.description:
If enabled, when the player dies, the level is reset, respawning all pickups and monsters.

Turning this setting off is considered easy mode. Good for new players that don't know the levels well.
Note that regardless of this setting, your inventory and checks made are never lost on death.

options.label: Random Monsters
options.description:
Choose how monsters are randomized.

- **Off**: Monsters are left unchanged.
- **Shuffle**: Monsters in the level are shuffled around.
- **Same Type**: Each "small" monster in the level is replaced with a different "small" monster; same for "medium" and "big" monsters.
- **Balanced**: All monsters in the level are randomized. The ratio of "small", "medium", and "big" monsters in the level will be preserved.
- **Chaotic**: All monsters in the level are completely randomized. This can make levels *significantly* harder!

options.label: Random Pickups
options.description:
Choose how pickups (medkits, ammo, etc.) are randomized.

- **Off**: Pickups are left unchanged.
- **Shuffle**: Pickups in the level are shuffled around.
- **Same Type**: Each "small" pickup in the level is replaced with a different "small" pickup; same for "medium" and "big" pickups.
- **Balanced**: All pickups in the level are randomized. The ratio of "small", "medium", and "big" pickups in the level will be preserved.
- **Chaotic**: All pickups in the level are completely randomized.

options.label: Random Music
options.description:
Choose how music will be randomized.

- **Off**: The music tracks will be left unchanged.
- **Shuffle Selected**: All music tracks within the episodes you have selected will be shuffled together.
- **Shuffle Game**: All music in the entire game will be shuffled together.

options.label: Flip Levels
options.description:
Choose if levels should be randomly flipped (mirrored).

- **Off**: Levels won't be flipped.
- **On**: All levels will be flipped.
- **Random Mix**: Each level has a random chance of being flipped.

options.label: Allow Death Logic
options.description:
Allow or disallow death logic locations and tricks.

Some locations can only be attempted once, and can become unreachable if the player fails to get them. Once this has happened, the player must die or otherwise reset the level to attempt to reach the location again.
If death logic is disabled, these locations will never contain any progression items.

On higher trick difficulty settings, this setting may also enable some tricks that put the player in a position where they are stuck and must die/reset the map afterwards.

options.label: Trick Difficulty
options.description:
Choose which tricks, if any, can be logically expected.

- **None**: Assumes vanilla progression through levels.
- **Basic**: Some minor unintended strategies may be required.
- **Pro**: More advanced speedrunning strategies like wallruns, SR40/SR50 straferunning, and exploiting the Z axis may be required.
- **Extreme**: If it's feasible in real time, it's in logic. Includes tricks that require enabling vertical mouse movement, tricks that punish failure with death, or out-of-bounds movement.

options.label: Tombola Victory Count
options.description:
Sets the amount of Tombola needed to goal the game.
(Default: 3)

options.label: Milestone Victory Count
options.description:
Sets the amount of Milestones needed to goal the game.
(Default: 9)

options.label: Card Generation Criteria
options.description:
Determines what Card generation type will be used.
- Classic: The normal Card generation criteria. the following Tombola rules will be followed:
  (1-9 in first column, 10-19 in second column, ..., 80-90 in last column)
  (All columns will have at least one number)
  (Numbers in the same column are ordered in ascending order)

- Order: Numbers will be distributed into card in order.
  (1 in Card 1, 2 in Card 2, ..., 6 in Card 6, 7 in Card 1, 8 in Card 2, ...)

- Chaos: Numbers will not respect the Tombola rules respected by the Classic option.
  (e.g. 1 may appear in any column, 54 may appear before 22 in a column)
(Default: Classic)

options.label: Prevent Other Meta-Game Items
options.description:
When enabled, prevents locations in the game from having items from other Meta-Games, such as APBingo.

Note: Progression Items from AP Tombola slots will never be placed in an AP Tombola slot, even if this option is disabled.
(Default: Enabled)

options.label: Automatic Number Hints
options.description:
When enabled, all Numbers will be automatically hinted. Highly recommended.
(Default: Enabled)

options.label: Cardsanity
options.description:
If Cardsanity is set to a value other than zero, than that many Cards' Unlocks will be sent to the Multiworld,
instead of being automatically given at the start of the game.
(Default: 0)

options.label: Additional Card Unlocks
options.description:
If Cardsanity and this option are enabled, an additional copy of "Card X Unlock" is created for each locked Card.
(Default: Enabled)

options.label: Rowsanity
options.description:
If Rowsanity is enabled, for each row of a Card and for each score type other than Tombola,
a location will be created that will require that specific row's numbers to be checked.
In the case of a Decina, each combination of 2 rows will be a location.
Note: Despite being classified as a Sanity Option, this option enhances the Tombola Experience and is thus recommended.
(Default: Enabled)

options.label: Marksanity
options.description:
If Marksanity is enabled a location is created for each number.
Marking a number will check the corresponding location.
(Default: Disabled)

options.label: Deprioritize Numbers
options.description:
When enabled, will set the "deprioritize" flag on all Numbers.
This means that if other slots have set locations to be Priority Locations,
Numbers from this slot will not land on said Priority Locations
(Unless *all* other progression items have already been placed on Priority Locations)

(Default: Enabled)

options.label: Start Hints
options.description: Start with these item's locations prefilled into the ``!hint`` command.

options.label: Easy Item Links
options.description:
Link your items with other players that have enabled this function!
Add the name for each kind of item you want to link.
This option accounts for players having different options, thus differing amount of items,
automatically creating links to have the highest amount of items linked without impacting player options*

*if any linked player for Unlocks has Additional Card Unlocks enabled, all linked players will have the extra unlock

Valid Keys are: "Numbers", "Unlocks", "Free Marks", "Free Location Hints", "Traps & Shields"

(Default: None)

options.label: Randomize maps (Wm)
options.description:
NOT IMPLEMENTED YET: Individual maps are randomized. For now this is only a subset of possible maps. A randomized
map will have all the same features (exits, chests, NPCs, etc) except things are moved around.

options.label: Shuffle areas (Wa)
options.description: Shuffles some or all area connections.

options.label: Shuffle house entrances (Wh)
options.description:
Shuffles all the house entrances, as well as a handful of other things, like the
palace/fortress-type entrances at the top of several towns, and standalone houses.

options.label: Randomize trade-in items (Wt)
options.description:
Items expected by various NPCs will be shuffled: specifically, Statue of Onyx, Kirisa Plant, Love Pendant, Ivory
Statue, and Fog Lamp. Rage will expect a random sword, and Tornel will expect a random bracelet.

options.label: Unidentified key items (Wu)
options.description: Item names will be generic and effects will be shuffled. This includes keys, flutes, lamps, and statues.

options.label: Randomize elements to break walls (We)
options.description:
Walls will require a randomized element to break. Normal rock and ice walls will indicate the required element by
the color (light grey or yellow for wind, blue for fire, bright orange ("embers") for water, or dark grey ("steel")
for thunder. The element to break these walls is the same throughout an area. Iron walls require a one-off random
element, with no visual cue, and two walls in the same area may have different requirements.

options.label: Shuffle Goa fortress floors (Wg)
options.description: The four areas of Goa fortress will appear in a random order.

options.label: Randomize sprite colors (Ws)
options.description: Monsters and NPCs will have different colors.

options.label: Randomize wild warp (Ww)
options.description: Wild warp will go to Mezame Shrine and 15 other random locations. These locations will be considered in-logic.

options.label: Story Mode (Rs)
options.description: Draygon 2 won't spawn unless you have all four swords and have defeated all major bosses of the tetrarchy.

options.label: No Bow mode (Rb)
options.description:
No items are required to finish the game. An exit is added from Mezame shrine directly to the Draygon 2 fight
(and the normal entrance is removed). Draygon 2 spawns automatically with no Bow of Truth.

options.label: Orbs not required to break walls (Ro)
options.description: If true, walls can be broken and bridges formed with level 1 shots.

options.label: Sword of Thunder warp
options.description:
Determines where the player is warped to when receiving the Sword of Thunder.
Shuffled: The Sword of Thunder will warp you to a random town.
None: The Sword of Thunder won't warp you. (Rt)
<town name>: The Sword of Thunder will warp you to the chosen town.

options.label: Vanilla Dolphin interactions (Rd)
options.description:
By default, the randomizer changes a number of dolphin and boat interactions: (1) healing the dolphin and having
the Shell Flute is no longer required before the fisherman spawns: instead, he will spawn as soon as you have the
item he wants; (2) talking to Kensu in the beach cabin is no longer required for the Shell Flute to work: instead,
the Shell Flute will always work, and Kensu will spawn after the Fog Lamp is turned in and will give a key item
check. This flag restores the vanilla interaction where healing and shell flute are required, and Kensu no longer
drops an item.

options.label: Fake flight (Gf)
options.description:
Fake flight allows using Dolphin and Rabbit Boots to fly up the waterfalls in the Angry Sea (without calming the
whirlpools). This is done by swimming up to a diagonal beach and jumping in a different direction immediately before
 disembarking.  Note: Fake flight cannot be disabled. The available options are in_logic or out_of_logic.

options.label: Statue glitch (Gs)
options.description:
Statue glitch allows getting behind statues that block certain entrances: the guards in Portoa, Amazones, Oak,
Goa, and Shyron, as well as the statues in the Waterfall Cave. It is done by approaching the statue from the top
right and holding down and left on the controller while mashing B.

options.label: Mt Sabre requirements skip (Gn)
options.description:
Entering Mt Sabre North normally requires (1) having Teleport, and (2) talking to the rabbit in Leaf after the
abduction (via Telepathy). Both of these requirements can be skipped: first by flying over the river in Cordel plain
rather than crossing the bridge, and then by threading the needle between the hitboxes in Mt Sabre North.

options.label: Statue gauntlet skip (Gg)
options.description:
The shooting statues in front of Goa and Stxy normally require Barrier to pass safely. With this flag, Flight can
also be used by flying around the edge of the statue.

options.label: Sword charge glitch (Gc)
options.description:
Sword charge glitch allows charging one sword to the level of another sword by equipping the higher-level sword,
re-entering the menu, changing to the lower-level sword without exiting the menu, creating a hard save, resetting,
and then continuing.

options.label: Trigger skip (Gt)
options.description:
A wide variety of triggers and exit squares can be skipped by using an invalid item every frame while walking.
This allows bypassing both Mt Sabre North entrance triggers, the Evil Spirit Island entrance trigger, triggers for
guards to move, slopes, damage tiles, and seamless map transitions.

options.label: Rage skip (Gr)
options.description:
Rage can be skipped by damage-boosting diagonally into the Lime Tree Lake screen. This provides access to the
area beyond the lake if flight or bridges are available. For simplicity, the logic only assumes this is possible if
there's a flyer.

options.label: Randomize background music (Am/As)
options.description: Randomizes or disables the background music.

options.label: Randomize map colors (Ac)
options.description: Randomizes the palettes of the background tiles.

options.label: Randomize monster weaknesses (Me)
options.description: Monster and boss elemental weaknesses are shuffled.

options.label: Replace all chests with mimics (Mg)
options.description:
Every chest is now a mimic, and killing the mimic will drop the real item chest. Careful when killing the mimic,
if it drops the chest out of reach you'll need to reset the room!

options.label: Shuffle tower robots (Mt)
options.description: Tower robots will be shuffled into the normal pool.

options.label: Don't shuffle mimics (Et)
options.description: Mimics will be in their vanilla locations.

options.label: Keep unique items and consumables separate (Eu)
options.description:
Normally all items and mimics are shuffled into a single pool and distributed from there. If this flag is set,
unique items (specifically, anything that cannot be sold) will only be found in either (a) checks that held unique
items in vanilla, or (b) boss drops. Chests containing consumables in vanilla may be safely ignored, but chests
containing unique items in vanilla may still end up with non-unique items because of bosses like Vampire 2 that drop
consumables. If mimics are shuffled, they will only be in consumable locations. These locations are tracked by the
multiworld, so they will still count against your hint points, but they will only contain your non-unique items.

options.label: Decrease enemy damage (Ed)
options.description:
Enemy attack power will be significantly decreased in the early game (by a factor of 3). The gap will narrow in
the mid-game and eventually phase out at scaling level 40.

options.label: Guarantee starting sword (Es)
options.description:
The Leaf elder is guaranteed to give a sword. It will not be required to deal with any enemies before finding the
first sword.

options.label: Guarantee refresh (Er)
options.description: Guarantees the Refresh spell will be available before fighting Tetrarchs.

options.label: Experience scales faster (Ex)
options.description: Less grinding will be required to "keep up" with the game difficulty.

options.label: No community jokes (Ec)
options.description:
Skip community jokes, such as funny/misspelled item, monster, or character names. This will make it easier to
look up information in guides/FAQs if necessary.

options.label: Battle magic not guaranteed (Nw)
options.description:
Normally, the logic will guarantee that level 3 sword charges are available before fighting the tetrarchs (with
the exception of Karmine, who only requires level 2). This disables that check.

options.label: Matching sword not guaranteed ("Tink Mode") (Ns)
options.description:
Enables "tink strats", where wrong-element swords will still do a single damage per hit. Player may be required
to fight monsters (including bosses) with tinks.

options.label: Barrier not guaranteed (Nb)
options.description:
Normally, the logic will guarantee Barrier before entering Stxy, the Fortress, or fighting Karmine. This puts
those locations in logic with any sword (to farm money) and one of Shield Ring, Refresh, or a place to buy Medical
Herbs.

options.label: Gas mask not guaranteed (Ng)
options.description:
The logic will not guarantee gas mask before needing to enter the swamp, nor will leather boots (or hazmat suit)
be guaranteed to cross long stretches of spikes. Gas mask is still guaranteed to kill the insect.

options.label: Don't buff medical herb or fruit of power (Hm)
options.description:
If this is set to true, Medical Herb is not buffed to heal 80 damage, which is helpful to make up for cases where
Refresh is unavailable early. Fruit of Power is not buffed to restore 56 MP.

options.label: Max scaling level in tower (Ht)
options.description: Enemies in the tower spawn at max scaling level.

options.label: Experience scales slower (Hx)
options.description: More grinding will be required to "keep up" with the difficulty.

options.label: Charge shots only (Hc)
options.description: Stabbing is completely ineffective. Only charged shots work.

options.label: Blackout (Hz)
options.description: All caves and fortresses are permanently dark.

options.label: Permadeath (Hh)
options.description: Hardcore mode: checkpoints and saves are removed.

options.label: Don't buff Dyna (Vd)
options.description:
By default, we make the Dyna fight a bit more of a challenge. Side pods will fire significantly more. The safe
spot has been removed. The revenge beams pass through barrier. Side pods can now be killed. This flag prevents that
change.

options.label: Don't buff bonus items (Vb)
options.description:
Leather Boots are changed to Speed Boots, which increase player walking speed (this allows climbing up the slope
to access the Tornado Bracelet chest, which is taken into consideration by the logic). Deo's pendant restores MP
while moving. Rabbit boots enable sword charging up to level 2 while walking (level 3 still requires being
stationary, so as to prevent wasting tons of magic). Turning this on removes all these changes.

options.label: Vanilla maps (Vm)
options.description:
Normally the randomizer adds a new "East Cave" to Valley of Wind, borrowed from the GBC version of the game. This
cave contains two chests (one considered a key item) on the upper floor and exits to two random areas (chosen
between Lime Tree Valley, Cordel Plain, Goa Valley, or Desert 2), one unblocked on the lower floor, and one down
the stairs and behind a rock wall from the upper floor. This flag prevents adding that cave. If set as "Lime
Passage" then a direct path will instead be added between Valley of Wind and Lime Tree Valley.

options.label: Vanilla shops (Vs)
options.description:
By default, we disable shop glitch, shuffle shop contents, and tie the prices to the scaling level (item shops
and inns increase by a factor of 2 every 10 scaling levels, armor shops decrease by a factor of 2 every 12 scaling
levels). This flag prevents all of these changes, restoring shops to be completely vanilla.

options.label: Vanilla wild warp (Vw)
options.description:
By default, Wild Warp is nerfed to only return to Mezame Shrine. This flag restores it to work like normal. Note
that this will put all wild warp locations in logic unless the flag is set as "Out Of Logic".

options.label: Vanilla HUD (Vh)
options.description:
By default, the blue status bar (HUD) at the bottom of the screen is reorganized a bit, including displaying
enemies' names and HP. This disables those changes.

options.label: Don't automatically equip orbs and bracelets (Qa)
options.description:
Prevents adding a quality-of-life improvement to automatically equip the corresponding orb/bracelet whenever
changing swords.

options.label: Disable controller shortcuts (Qc)
options.description:
By default, we disable second controller input and instead enable some new shortcuts on controller 1: Start+A+B
for wild warp, and Select+B to quickly change swords. To support this, the action of the start and select buttons is
changed slightly. This flag disables this change and retains normal behavior.

options.label: Audible wall cues (Qw)
options.description:
Provide an audible cue when failing to break a non-iron wall. The intended way to determine which sword is
required for normal cave walls is by looking at the color. This causes the level 3 sword sound of the required
element to play when the wall fails to break. Note that fortress walls (iron in vanilla) do not give this hint,
since there is no visual cue for them, either.

options.label: Boss Weakness Plando
options.description:
Allows defining what elements the bosses of the game are vulnerable to. Note that for Vampire 2 and Giant Insect,
this element corresponds to what element the boss is immune to, while for the Tetrarchs, this element corresponds
to the element the boss is weak to. If a boss is not specified in the list, then its weakness is chosen randomly,
as it normally would be. This option only does anything when randomize_monster_weaknesses is set to true.

options.label: Wall Element Plando
options.description:
Allows defining what elements the walls of the game are vulnerable to. If a wall is not specified in the list,
then its weakness is chosen randomly, as it normally would be. This option only does anything when
randomize_wall_elements is set to true. Generate a spoiler log with randomize_wall_elements on for a list of valid
wall names, or see WALL_NAMES in types.py in the GitHub repository.

options.label: Trade In Plando
options.description:
Allows defining what NPC accepts what item. If one of the trade-in NPCs is not specified, it is randomized as
normal from among the non-plandoed options. Format is "NPC Name": "Trade-in Name". Valid NPC names are Akahana,
Aryllis, Fisherman, Kensu, and Slimed Kensu. Valid item names are Statue of Onyx, Fog Lamp, Love Pendant, Kirisa
Plant, and Ivory Statue. Does nothing if randomize_tradeins is false.

options.label: Key Item Name Plando
options.description:
Allows defining names of unidentified key items, within the limits of the datapackage. Format is "Original
Name": "New Name". Works on Bows, Keys, Lamps, Statues, and Flutes. Does nothing if unidentified_key_items is set
to false.

options.label: Shop Inventory Plando
options.description:
Allows defining what each item shop has available for purchase. Format is "<town name> Item Shop": ["<item
name 1>", "<item name 2>", ...]. Does nothing if vanilla_shops is true. Shops you plando will sell exactly the
items you specify. Other shops will be shuffled among themselves. At least one non-Shyron shop must sell Medical
Herbs, and at least one non-Shyron shop must sell Warp Boots.

options.label: Wild Warp Plando
options.description:
Allows defining what screens can be wild warped to, along with how many wild warps are available. The list may
be anywhere from 1 to 15 entries long, where each entry is either a screen name or "Any". Any means that slot will
be randomly filled in from among the valid remaining screens. If left empty, wild warps will be completely random,
as usual. Only does something if randomize_wild_warp is true and vanilla_wild_warp is disabled. For a full list of
screen names, look at worlds/crystalis/types.py for SCREEN_NAMES_TO_IDS.

options.label: Progressive Stat Caps

options.label: Random starter digimon
options.description:
Randomise the 2 starter digimon options
Vanilla = Agumon and Gabumon are the starters
All = Any digimon can be a starter
Rookie = Only rookie digimon can be a starter

options.label: Random techniques
options.description:
Randomise the techniques that digimon learn
Vanilla = Digimon techniques are unchanged
Enabled = Techniques are randomised

options.label: Fast Drimogemon
options.description: Makes Drimogen dig in 1 day instead of 10

options.label: Easy Monochromon
options.description: Always win the Monochromon Minigame

options.label: Randomize Adjudicators
options.description: Randomizes Adjudicators in the game, changing their required weapon type

options.description:
Set the max style rank for randomized adjudicators.

Leave at default to not change them (I can't recommend SS or SSS)

options.description: Set your starting melee weapon

options.label: Starting Second Melee
options.description: Set your second starting melee weapon

options.label: Starting Gun
options.description: Set your starting gun

options.label: Starting Second Gun
options.description: Set your starting gun

options.label: Randomize Skills
options.description: Should weapon skills be items?

options.label: Randomize Gun Levels
options.description: Should gun levels be items?

options.label: Death Link
options.description:
**DeathLink**: Standard DeathLink behavior.

**HurtLink**: Sends DeathLink messages out when you die. But any received DeathLink's will cause (Difficulty Dependent) damage rather than insta kill.

**None**: No death link features will be enabled

options.label: Randomize Styles
options.description: Add Dante's styles into the world as progressive upgrades. The starting style will be chosen at random unless one is specified via start inventory

options.label: Purple Orb Mode
options.description:
On: 10 Purple orbs will be added to the item pool (DT Item will be worth 0 runes if it is in the item pool)

Off: 7 Purple orbs will be added to the item pool as well as the Devil Trigger Item (Worth 3 DT Runes)

options.label: Devil Trigger Mode
options.description:
**On**: Devil Trigger item will be needed to access Devil Trigger (DT Item will be added to the item pool)

**Off**: Devil Trigger will be accessible upon reaching 3 runes

options.label: Minimum Mission Clear Rank
options.description:
What minimum rank is needed to give a mission's completed check.

**D** will be any and all ranks

**C, B, A, S** are self-explanatory

**SS** is a perfect S rank, all sub ranks must be S as well. (Only choose this if you are confident in your abilities)

options.label: Minimum Required Mission Clear Difficulty
options.description: What minimum difficulty is needed to give a mission's completed check.

options.label: Initially Unlocked Difficulties
options.description: What difficulties are unlocked when starting a new game (Normal is unlocked by default)

options.label: Enable SS Rank Checks
options.description: If the SS Rank checks are added to the multiworld

options.label: Useful SS Rank Goodies
options.description: Allow excluded SS Rank Mission Clears to have useful items and not just filler

options.label: SS Ranks Check Minimum Difficulty
options.description: If SS Rank checks also check to see if you are on the minimum difficulty

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Which goal setting to use:

**Standard**: Beat M20 in linear order M1-M20

**All**: Beat all missions, all are unlocked at start

**Random Order**: Beat all missions in a random linear order

options.label: Mission Order Setting
options.description:
**Grouped**: All 20 missions are divided into blocks of N missions. The order of these blocks is then randomized

**Pure RNG**: Leave it all up to chance. You may get Mission #1 as your first, or you may get Mission #20.
Not recommended for Synchronous games.

**Weighted**: Mission order is based on the provided weights

options.label: Mission Order Group Count
options.description:
Used for the "Grouped" Mission order setting

Set's how many mission "groups" there are

I.e 20/N where N is number of groups.

options.label: Exclude Locations
options.description: Prevent these locations from having an important item.

options.label: Orb Checks
options.description:
Add checks to the store.

This includes both Blue and Purple Orbs

options.label: Gun Store Checks
options.description:
Purchasing gun levels will send out checks

You will need the specific gun for the checks

options.label: Auto Orb Hints
options.description:
What types of hints should be automatically created

* All will auto hint all orb purchases
* None will result in no hints

options.label: Auto Gun Hints
options.description:
Gun Level Auto hinting behavior

* All: All gun level checks will be auto-hinted
* Obtained: Hint all levels when the gun is obtained
* None: No automatic hinting

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Choose your goal for the multiworld
- Home: Defeat the final boss and equip the Home shell
- Roland: Defeat Roland on the Pinbarge
- Voltai: Defeat Voltai in Scuttleport
- Magista: Defeat Magista in Slacktide

options.label: Fork Location
options.description:
Choose where the Fork(weapon) location is set. Does nothing if [Allow Forkless] option is enabled.
- Shuffled Early Local: Forces Fork location to be somewhere early in your own game.
- Shuffled Early Global: Forces Fork location to be somewhere early in any game.
- Vanilla Location: Forces Fork to be placed at its intended location.

options.label: Allow Forkless
options.description:
If enabled, allows for the Fork to not be required early on, meaning you may have to play some amount of the game without it. Ignores [Fork Location] option and shuffles Fork into item pool if enabled.
- Disabled: Fork is required to fight early bosses, meaning that it will be placed early in your run.
- Forkless Easy: Ensures that the intended forkless strategy is not too advanced (Includes logic for adaptation and shellspell focused builds)
- Forkless Hard: Allows for the possibility of more advanced forkless strategies to be necessary (Includes logic for rolling attack and summon focused builds)

options.label: Logic Rules
options.description:
Set the preferred logic rules for your game
- Vanilla: Standard logic, no skips/glitches required to complete the goal.
- Glitchless: Allows for the following parkour-based skips (list of glitchless rules here) to be required to complete the goal.
- Restricted: In addition to the list under glitchless, allows for (list of easy glitches/skips here) to be required to complete the goal.
- Unrestricted: In addition to the lists under both glitchless and restricted, allows for (list of hard glitches/skips here) to be required to complete the goal.

options.label: Shelleport Location
options.description:
Choose where the Shelleport (fast travel) skill location is set
- Shuffled: Shelleport is placed into the item pool.
- Shuffled Early Local: Forces Shelleport location to be somewhere early in your own game.
- Shuffled Early Global: Forces Shelleport location to somewhere early in any game.
- Starting Items: Places Shelleport in your starting inventory.
- Vanilla Location: Forces Shelleport to be placed at its intended location

options.label: Fishing Line Location
options.description:
Choose where the Fishing Line (grapple) location is set
- Shuffled: Fishing Line is placed into item pool.
- Vanilla Location: Forces Fishing Line to be placed at its intended location

options.label: Random Shells
options.description: Choose whether or not shells will be randomized. Only randomizes shells within other shell locations.

options.label: Random Fuse
options.description: Choose if the location of the Plug Fuse shell is randomized when using the shell randomizer. Does nothing if [RandomShells] is set to false

options.label: Remove Costumes
options.description: Choose whether or not to include Costumes in the item pool. Set to true to remove them.

options.label: Microplastic Multiplier
options.description: Multiplies the amount of microplastics received from all sources. Only supports integer values.

options.label: Trap Amount
options.description:
Defines a percentage of the filler items to be replaced with trap items
Set to 0 to not include any traps

options.label: Death Link
options.description: Enables Death Link

options.label: NG+ Bosses
options.description:
Replaces all bosses with their NG+ variants.
This can make runs signifigantly more difficult, especially early on.
NOT COMPLETE, USE AT OWN RISK

options.label: NG+ Stowaways
options.description:
Adds New Game+ stowaways to the item pool.
NOT COMPLETE, USE AT OWN RISK

options.label: NG+ Stowaway Capacity
options.description:
Determines stowaway capacity and slots
False = NG (3 Stowaways, 9 Slot Max)
True = NG+ (4 Stowaways, 12 Slot Max)
NOT COMPLETE, USE AT OWN RISK

options.label: Pellys Required
options.description: Choose how many Pellys will be required for victory.

options.label: Level Quota
options.description: Choose how many levels must be completed for your goal, in addition to gathering enough Pellys.

options.label: Valuable Hunt
options.description: Determines if extracting all valuables (excluding pellys) is required for your goal.

options.label: Monster Hunt
options.description: Determines if extracting all monster souls is required for your goal.

options.label: Combat Logic
options.description:
Determines what items are logically required to fight monsters.
Easy: Guns or Explosives
Medium: Strength Upgrades + Stun Items, Melee Weapons, Guns, or Explosives
Hard: No combat logic. Player may have to kill monsters with valuables found in levels.

options.label: Progressive Shop Stock Amount
options.description: Choose how many Archipelago Shop Items are unlocked with each Progressive Shop Stock.

options.label: Total Shop Upgrade Locations
options.description: Choose how many Archipelago Items show up in the Upgrades section of the Shop.

options.label: Shop Upgrade Locations in Logic
options.description:
Choose how many shop upgrades will potentially be logically relevant.
Items past this number will not have progression items.
This number gets set to the Total Shop Upgrade Locations if it is greater.

options.label: Starting Level Type
options.description: Choose which level type to start with.

options.label: Filler Item Weights
options.description:
Choose the weights for adding filler and traps to the item pool.
Each upgrade item will spawn one upgrade of that type in the truck.
Each small health pack spawns one small health pack (25hp) in the truck.
Traps:
    Extra Monster Trap - Spawns an extra enemy (or enemy group) from the tier 3 enemy pool.
    Audit Trap - Takes half of your money the next time you visit a shop.
    Monster Lure Trap - Lures monsters to your location for two minutes.
    Progressive Moon Phase Trap - Increases the moon phase by one stage FOR THE REST OF THE MULTIWORLD.

options.label: Audit Trap Money Lost
options.description: The percentage of the player's money that an Audit Trap will take when triggered.

options.label: Win Condition
options.description:
**Evilizer**: Beat the final boss

**Badges**: Get X merit badges earned

options.label: Badges Required
options.description: For the Badges win con, how many badges are needed

options.label: Difficulty
options.description: Difficulty Setting

options.label: Long Checks
options.description:
**Excluded**: Remove 100%, 39 badges, swampdog to 50, witch to lvl 9 spells, 5000 gems,
the monster point badges, a true hero

Does nothing if badges are already set to none

options.label: Multiple Saves
options.description:
**Disabled**: Remove badges that require using certain characters/terror mode in adventure mode,
removes all "takes effect on new game" cheats

options.label: Remix
options.description: **Excluded**: Remix mode not included

options.label: Overpowered Cheats
options.description:

Also disables Brawlin' as a location, since it requires Touch of Death

options.label: Badges
options.description:
**Full**: All badges and their cheats are in logic

**Vanilla**: Badges aren't randomized, but are in logic

**None**: Badges aren't in logic

options.label: Monster Dolls
options.description:
**Full**: Monsters can drop randomized items, monster dolls can be found at locations

**Vanilla**: Monsters drop their normal monster doll

**None**: Dolls aren't in logic, the collection quest gives nothing

options.label: Entrance Randomization WIP
options.description: **Enabled**: Randomize where all loading zones go, but put the opposite direction to the same place

options.label: Player Goal
options.description:
What the player should achieve to reach their goal.
Heartstopper: Vanilla ending, fulfill Bit's final request
Altitude Loss: Labyrinths ending, any
Veteran: Break into a super secret node
VIP: Complete every Entropy and CSEC mission
Completionist: All of the above. Recommended for asyncs

options.label: Exclude Project Junebug
options.description:
If enabled, Project Junebug will not be marked as a location.
If "Admin Access as Checks" is enabled, this will also not mark Project Junebug nodes.
Recommended for those easily triggered by sensitive topics.
If enabled while Shuffle Executables is disabled, KBTPortTest can be found in finale nodes.

options.label: Shuffle Labyrinths
options.description:
Whether or not to shuffle Labyrinths content (missions, executables, etc.)
If player goal is set to Altitude Loss, Veteran, or Completionist, generation will throw an error if this is disabled.

options.label: Shuffle Limits
options.description:
Whether or not to set limits on in-game mechanics, shuffling progressive limits into the item pool.
Enable All: Set limits for shells (defaults to 1) and RAM.
Shells: Restricts how many shells you can have open at once. (Defaults to 1)
Shells Zero: Same as shells, but defaults to 0 instead of 1 shell. (Meaning, you can't open ANY shells from the start)
RAM: Restricts your RAM to 300mb from the get-go. Progressive RAM adds 50mb each time it's received.
Disabled: (Default) Don't set any limits.

options.label: Shuffle Steam Achievements
options.description:
If enabled, actions that usually unlock Steam achievements will be added as location checks.
("Rude" is excluded, as the player is automatically put onto the /el Sec path after defeating Naix.)
(If the player misses Quickdraw, they can get it again by starting a new save file.)

options.label: Admin Access as Checks
options.description:
Admin Access as Checks

Adds admin access for EVERY ACCESSIBLE NODE as a check. This adds a LOT of locations.
(~140 with DLC enabled) Recommended for asyncs.
Respects "Shuffle Labyrinths" and "Exclude Project Junebug"

options.label: Shuffle PointClicker Upgrades
options.description:
Adds PointClicker upgrades as checks and items.
PointClicker upgrades only send a check the first time they're bought.
This adds ~51 location checks.

Block Upgrades: Every PointClicker upgrade is a check, but won't do anything when the player buys it.
This forces the player to rely on PointClicker Passive items being sent to them.
Only Checks: Every PointClicker upgrade is a check, and will actually upgrade when the player buys it.
Disabled: (Default) Don't shuffle PointClicker, at all.

options.label: Max. Amount of Mission Skips
options.description:
The maximum amount of mission skips that should be shuffled into the item pool.
Mission skips allow you to skip any current mission.
Mission skips cannot be used on transition missions.
Mission skips cannot be used on finale missions.
If set to 0, no mission skips will be shuffled into the item pool.

options.label: Max. Amount of ForceHacks
options.description:
The maximum amount of forcehacks that should be shuffled into the item pool.
ForceHacks allow you to instantly gain admin access to most nodes. (With a few exceptions...)
If set to 0, no forcehacks will be shuffled into the item pool.

options.label: Shuffle Executables
options.description:
Shuffles executables into the item pool. The player can't do ANYTHING without these, pretty much.
Any executable not shuffled can be found and downloaded in its vanilla location.

Shuffle All: Shuffle EVERY executable. Even the useless ones.
Progression And Useful: Only shuffle progression and useful executables. (e.g., OpShell, ThemeChanger)
Progression Only: Only shuffle progression executables. (e.g., FTPBounce, WebServerWorm)
Disabled: Don't shuffle executables.

The finale sequencer executable is never shuffled.

options.label: FTPSprint Replaces FTPBounce
options.description:
Completely removes FTPBounce from the item pool, replacing it with FTPSprint.
If disabled, FTPBounce and FTPSprint will be two different items in the item pool.
This ignores Shuffle Labyrinths.
If Shuffle Executables is set to Disabled, this does nothing.

options.label: Start with FTP & SSH Crushers
options.description: When shuffling executables, add FTPBounce and SSHCrack to starting inventory automatically.

options.label: Executable Grouping
options.description:
When shuffling executables, how should they be grouped?
If set to a value other than Individually, all executables will be shuffled, regardless of classification.

Individually: (Default) Every executable is its own item.
Regional: Executables are grouped by region. (e.g., "Labyrinths Executables" is TorrentStreamInjector, SSLTrojan, etc.)
Practicality: Executables are grouped by what they're used for. (e.g., Portcrushers, Aesthetics, etc.) Good for quick syncs.

options.label: Shuffle Faction Access
options.description:
If enabled, the player must first receive the respective Access for the faction before they can do missions for it. (Entropy, CSEC, Kaguya Trials)
Good for asyncs!

Starting Hints: Automatically hints access for each faction from the start of the run.

options.label: Trap Percentage (%)
options.description: What percentage of filler items should be traps. If set to 0, no traps will be shuffled into the item pool.

options.label: Enable ETAS Traps
options.description:
If traps are enabled, shuffle ETAS traps. Automatically causes an ETAS to trigger.
These can be REALLY annoying, so they're off by default. Enable them if you like a challenge!

options.label: Enable DeathLink
options.description:
If enabled: whenever you are traced back or your in-game computer crashes, a deathlink is sent.
DeathLinks are not sent for the crash caused by Striker. (But they are for Naix)

A DeathLink in Hacknet will crash the player's (in-game) computer. If an ETAS is currently active, then the DeathLink is discarded.

options.label: DeathLink Method
options.description:
Changes what happens when you receive a DeathLink. This does nothing if DeathLink is disabled.

Crash: Classic, bluescreen and crash your in-game PC
ETAS: Activates the Emergency Trace Aversion Sequence

options.label: Death Link
options.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

options.label: Ring Link
options.description: Enable Ring Link for use with games that support it. Incoming rings are converted to the current level's Hit counter.

options.label: Victory Condition
options.description:
Choose your victory condition.
Andross or Robot Andross - Defeat either Andross or Robot Andross
Andross and Robot Andross - Defeat both Andross and Robot Andross
Andross - Defeat Andross in Venom 2

options.label: Required Medals
options.description:
Require a certain number of medals before you can enter Venom 2.
The same requirment will apply for Venom 1 if your victory condition is 'Andross or Robot Andross'

options.label: Level Access
options.description:
Completing a level a certain way will give a random item.
Choose what type of level access item gets added to the pool.

Shuffle Levels - You will receive levels as items which will allow you to select that level at any time.
Shuffle Paths - You will receive paths as items which will allow you to take that path to other levels.

options.label: Shuffle Starting Level
options.description:
If Level Access is 'Shuffle Levels', shuffle which level you start with.
You normally start with Corneria.

options.label: Shuffle Medals
options.description:
Shuffle the medals awarded by reaching a certain number of Hits in each level.
Earning a medal will give a random item, and you will visually see the medal on the map to indicate that you've completed the check.

Note: Medals are very challenging in vanilla.
Unless you know what you're doing, it is recommended to lower the score needed for each level using their options.

options.label: Shuffle Checkpoints
options.description:
Shuffle checkpoints rings for the levels that have them.
You will not be able to use the checkpoint ring in a level until you receive the item for it.

options.label: Accomplished Sends Complete
options.description: Getting 'Mission Accomplished' on any level will also count as getting 'Mission Complete' for that level.

options.label: Radio Rando
options.description: Randomize the radio dialog.

options.label: Engine Glow
options.description: Set the color of your engine's glow.

options.label: Default Lives
options.description: Set the number of lives (Arwings) you start with and reset to after a game over.

options.label: Medal Corneria
options.description: Set the score required to earn the medal on Corneria.

options.label: Medal Meteo
options.description: Set the score required to earn the medal on Meteo.

options.label: Medal Sector Y
options.description: Set the score required to earn the medal on Sector Y.

options.label: Medal Katina
options.description: Set the score required to earn the medal on Katina.

options.label: Medal Fortuna
options.description: Set the score required to earn the medal on Fortuna.

options.label: Medal Aquas
options.description: Set the score required to earn the medal on Aquas.

options.label: Medal Solar
options.description: Set the score required to earn the medal on Solar.

options.label: Medal Sector X
options.description: Set the score required to earn the medal on Sector X.

options.label: Medal Zoness
options.description: Set the score required to earn the medal on Zoness.

options.label: Medal Titania
options.description: Set the score required to earn the medal on Titania.

options.label: Medal Sector Z
options.description: Set the score required to earn the medal on Sector Z.

options.label: Medal Macbeth
options.description: Set the score required to earn the medal on Macbeth.

options.label: Medal Area 6
options.description: Set the score required to earn the medal on Area 6.

options.label: Medal Bolse
options.description: Set the score required to earn the medal on Bolse.

options.label: Medal Venom
options.description: Set the score required to earn the medal on Venom.

options.label: Force local first abilitiy
options.description: If enabled, forces an ability that can deal damage into your world as the first location you can check (where Trowzer teaches you Tail Twirl). Otherwise, it will be filled into any location that is reachable from the beginning of any game.

options.label: Prevent Tropics BK
options.description: If enabled, forces either Reptile Roll or Flappy Flight into your world in a location accessible before Tribalstack Tropics. If disabled, these abilities may be placed anywhere.

options.label: Flappy Flight Location
options.description: Choose where Flappy Flight is put. Flappy Flight opens up many checks and effectively invalidates some abilities like Lizard Leap. "Early" refers to one of the earlygame checks before entering Tribalstack Tropics.

options.label: Pagies Required for Capital B
options.description: The amount of pagies required to face Capital B. Note that this does NOT guarantee you will be able to access Capital B's office at a particular time, as there are still ability requirements to progress up to Capital B's office in the first place. There are a total of 145 pagies in the game.

options.label: Randomize Grand Tome World Order
options.description: If enabled, randomizes the order of the Grand Tome worlds. This does not change the location of the Grand Tomes within Hivory Towers or the cost of the Grand Tomes, only the world you go to when entering a Grand Tome. Galleon Galaxy will never be randomized in place of Tribalstack Tropics.

options.label: Disable Quizzes
options.description: If enabled, causes the quizzes to be completely skipped.

options.label: Goal Unlock Method
options.description:
Determines how Stargazer Colosseum (your goal) will be unlocked.

Badge Hunt: Stargazer Colosseum will be unlocked once you get a certain number of Pokétopia Badges (macguffin item).
Colosseum Clears: Stargazer Colosseum will be unlocked once you beat a certain number of Colosseums.
Both: Both of the above requirements will need to be met before Stargazer Colosseum can be unlocked.

options.label: Required Badge Amount
options.description:
The number of Pokétopia Badges required to unlock Stargazer Colosseum.
This option only matters if Goal Unlock Method is set to either Badge Hunt or Both.

options.label: Total Badge Amount
options.description:
The total number of Pokétopia Badges in the item pool.
If this option is set to a lower number than Required Badge Amount, then it will be increased to match.
This option only matters if Goal Unlock Method is set to either Badge Hunt or Both.

options.label: Colosseum Clear Count
options.description:
The number of Colosseums needed to be cleared to unlock Stargazer Colosseum.
This option only matters if Goal Unlock Method is set to either Colosseum Clears or Both.

options.label: Starting Colosseum Amount
options.description:
The number of random Colosseums you will start with.
Set to Vanilla to begin with the vanilla starter Colosseums (Gateway and Main Street Colosseums).

options.label: Starting Colosseum Pool
options.description:
The Colosseums that can be chosen for you to start with.
If the number of Colosseums set in this option is lower than the Starting Colosseum Amount,
then random ones will be added to the pool until the number matches.

options.label: Randomize Rental Passes
options.description:
Whether Rental Passes should be added to the item pool.
Getting new Rental Passes from Gateway Colosseum will give you checks.

options.label: Starting Rental Pass
options.description:
The Rental Pass that you will start with.
This option only matters if Randomize Rental Passes is turned on.

options.label: End Goals
options.description:
Select the End Goals of a run.
You must achieve all selected goals for the run to be completed.
Goal checks are excluded from progression placement and contain only non-progression rewards.
Goals that are not selected are controlled by the 'Persistent Goals' option.

'Reverberation Ensemble' - Defeat X out of 10 Ensemble battles. X can be set in the 'Reverberation Ensemble Goal Receptions' setting.
'Black Silence' - Complete Reception of The Black Silence.
'Keter Realization' - Realize the Floor of General Works.
'Distorted Ensemble' - Complete Reception of The Reverberation Ensemble Distorted.

options.label: Persistent Goals
options.description:
Select goals that should appear in the regular stage tree when they are not selected as End Goals.
A goal selected in both options remains in the goal section and is not added to the regular tree.

options.label: Reverberation Ensemble Goal Receptions
options.description:
Select the number of Reverberation Ensemble receptions required for the
'Reverberation Ensemble' goal to be considered completed.

This option only applies when Reverberation Ensemble is selected as an End Goal.

options.label: Endgoals Always Unlocked
options.description: If 'true', selected End Goals can be accessed without completing Oliver's reception.

options.label: Lock Floors
options.description: If 'true', every floor except one (Random or preset) is locked at the start of the run and must be unlocked via respective items.

options.label: Starting Floor
options.description: If "Lock Floors" is 'true', select which floor will be unlocked at the start of the run.

options.label: Progression Mode
options.description:
Battle Graph - Battles are gated by the battle graph and require books.

Layered - Burning books unlocks new battle layers. Entering the next chapter
             also requires clearing the configured percentage of the current chapter.
             Books of Everything provides max stacks of pages in a little mixed chapter-by-chapter order,
             while Booster Packs provide a few mostly random pages.

Compared to Battle Graph, Layered mode gives the player a little more freedom to
