Determines how the rando will close off parts of the adventure field.
Emblems (0): Areas are gated based on the number of emblems collected.
KeyItems (1): Areas are gated based on key items like the Train or Station Key

options.label: Send Death Link Chance
options.description: When dying, the chance of sending a death link to another player.

options.label: Receive Death Link Chance
options.description: When receiving a death link, the chance of dying.

options.label: Ring Link
options.description:
Whether your in-level ring gain/loss is linked to other players.
Disabled (0): Ring Link is disabled.
Enabled (1): Rings are sent and received in normal situations.
Enabled Casinopolis (2): Rings are sent and received in most situations, plus while playing Sonic's Casinopolis.
Enabled Hard (3): Rings are sent and received when including finishing a level and during the Perfect Chaos fight.

options.label: Ring Loss
options.description:
How taking damage is handled.
Classic (0): You lose all of your rings when hit.
Modern (1): You lose 20 rings when hit.
One Hit K.O. (2): You die immediately when hit.
One Hit K.O. No Shields (3): You die immediately when hit, and you can't use shields or invincibility power ups.

choices.label: One Hit K O No Shields

options.label: Trap Link
options.description: Whether your received traps are linked to other players

options.label: Playable Sonic
options.description: Determines whether Sonic is playable.

options.label: Playable Tails
options.description: Determines whether Tails is playable.

options.label: Playable Knuckles
options.description: Determines whether Knuckles is playable.

options.label: Playable Amy
options.description: Determines whether Amy is playable.

options.label: Playable Big
options.description: Determines whether Big is playable.

options.label: Playable Gamma
options.description: Determines whether Gamma is playable.

options.label: Sonic's Action Stage Missions
options.description: Choose what action stage missions will be a location check for Sonic.

options.label: Tails' Action Stage Missions
options.description: Choose what action stage missions will be a location check for Tails.

options.label: Knuckles' Action Stage Missions
options.description: Choose what action stage missions will be a location check for Knuckles.

options.label: Amy's Action Stage Missions
options.description: Choose what action stage missions will be a location check for Amy.

options.label: Big's Action Stage Missions
options.description: Choose what action stage missions will be a location check for Big.

options.label: Gamma's Action Stage Missions
options.description: Choose what action stage missions will be a location check for Gamma.

options.label: MusicSource
options.description:
Selects the source of the game's music.

You can mix and match music from SADX, SA2B, and custom tracks.
Custom songs are mapped to the Sonic Heroes soundtrack by default,
but you're free to replace them with any songs you prefer.

Choose between: SADX (0), SA2B (1), Custom (2), SADX + SA2B (3), SADX + Custom (4), SA2B + Custom (5),
or SADX + SA2B + Custom (6).

NOTE: You must own SA2B and/or Sonic Heroes on PC to use their music.

options.label: Music Shuffle
options.description:
Controls how music is randomized in the game.

Disabled (0 - default): Use original tracks without randomization.
Curated (1): Randomize music using a hand-picked list that fits the original tone.
By Type (2): Randomize songs within the same category (e.g., levels, bosses).
Full (3): Randomize across the entire pool of available tracks.
Singularity (4): Replace every song with the same single track.

Options 1 and 2 are recommended for the most coherent experience.

options.label: Music Shuffle Consistency
options.description:
Defines how frequently music changes during gameplay.

Static (0 - default): Music remains the same for the seed/slot.
On Restart (1): Music is reshuffled every time the game is restarted.
Per Play (2): Music changes every time it starts playing.

Note: Shuffling is handled on the client side, using the seed and song.json file.

options.label: Life Capsules Change Songs
options.description:
If enabled, collecting a Life Capsule will trigger a music change, based on your current Music Shuffle settings.
Only available if Music Shuffle is consistency is set to Per Play (2).

options.label: Randomize Everyone's Upgrades
options.description: Determines whether upgrades are randomized and sent to the item pool.

options.label: Boss Checks
options.description: Determines whether beating a boss grants a check (15 Locations).

options.label: Unify Chaos 4
options.description: Determines whether the Chaos 4 fight counts as a single location or three (Sonic, Tails, and Knuckles).

options.label: Unify Chaos 6
options.description: Determines whether the Chaos 6 fight counts as a single location or three (Sonic, Big, and Knuckles).

options.label: Unify Egg Hornet
options.description: Determines whether the Egg Hornet fight counts as a single location or two (Sonic, Tails).

options.label: Field Emblems Checks
options.description: Determines whether collecting field emblems grants checks (12 Locations).

options.label: Secret Chao Egg Checks
options.description: Determines whether getting the 3 secret chao eggs grants checks (3 Locations).

options.label: Chao Races Checks
options.description: Determines whether winning the chao races grants checks (5 Locations).

options.label: Level Access Percentage for Chao Races
options.description:
Percentage of the available levels accessible for the chao races to be in logic.
Higher values means races are required later in the game.

options.label: Enable Mission Checks
options.description: Determines whether completing missions grants checks (60 Locations).

options.label: Auto Start Missions
options.description: Determines whether missions will start already activated.

options.label: Mission Blacklist
options.description:
Determines what missions are blacklisted. The default are:
Mission 49 (Flags in the Kart section of Twinkle Park).
Mission 53 (Triple Jump in the Snowboard section of Ice Cap).
Mission 54 (Flags in the Snowboard section of Ice Cap).
Mission 58 (Flags in the rolling bounce section of Lost World).
Also, you can blacklist all the missions by using the character names. i.e. ['Big', 'Sonic']

options.label: Twinkle Circuit Check
options.description:
Determines whether beating Twinkle Circuit grants a checks
Disabled (0): Twinkle Circuit disabled.
Enabled (1): Twinkle Circuit enabled (1 location).
Enabled Multiple (2): Enable a different track for each character as well (+5 locations).

options.label: Sand Hill Check
options.description:
Determines whether beating Sand Hill grants a check:
Disabled (0): Sand Hill disabled.
Enabled (1): Sand Hill enabled (1 location).
Enabled Hard (2): Harder (points-based) Sand Hill mission enabled (+1 location).

options.label: Sky Chase Checks
options.description:
Determines whether beating Sky Chase grants a check:
Disabled (0): Sky Chase disabled.
Enabled (1): Sky Chase Act 1 and 2 enabled (2 locations).
Enabled Hard (2): Harder (points-based) Sky Chase missions enabled (+2 locations).

options.label: Enemy Sanity
options.description:
Determines whether destroying enemies grants checks (710 Locations).
You need to enable enemy-sanity for some characters for it to work.

options.label: EnemySanityList
options.description:
Determines which enemies are included in enemy-sanity.
Character names are used as values

options.label: Include Missable Enemies
options.description:
Determines whether enemies in missable locations grant checks. This includes:
- Enemies in the Casinopolis Sewers (Sonic and Tails)
- Enemies in the Kart section of Sonic's Twinkle Park

options.label: Capsule Sanity
options.description:
Determines whether destroying capsules grants checks (692 Locations).
You need to enable capsule-sanity for some characters and some types for it to work.

options.label: CapsuleSanityList
options.description:
Determines which capsules are included in capsule-sanity.
You can use Character name plus capsule type as values.
X-Life, X-Shield, X-PowerUp, and X-Ring with X being the character name (i.e. 'Sonic-PowerUp')

options.label: Include Missable Capsules
options.description:
Determines whether capsules in missable locations grant checks. This includes:
- Capsules in the Casinopolis Sewers (Sonic and Tails)
- Capsules in the Kart section of Sonic's Twinkle Park
- Capsules in the 'Going Down?' section of Sonic's Speed Highway
- Capsules in the Boulder section of Sonic's Lost World

options.label: Include Pinball's Capsules
options.description: Determines whether pinball's capsules grant checks (5 Locations).

options.label: Fish Sanity
options.description: Determines whether catching every type of fish grants checks (23 Locations).

options.label: Lazy Fishing
options.description:
Enabling Lazy Fishing grants infinite tension during fishing if you have the Power Rod upgrade.
Depending on your option, the Power Rod will be a logic requirement or not for your locations:
0: Disabled (default).
1: Enabled, no requirements (Power Rod is not a logic requirement for any location check).
2: Enabled, fishsanity (Power Rod is a logic requirement for fish-sanity only).
3: Enabled, all (Power Rod is a logic requirement for fish-sanity, B/A/S ranks and every "Keeper" mission for Big).

options.label: Junk Fill Percentage
options.description: Replace a percentage of non-required emblems in the item pool with random junk items.

options.label: Trap Fill Percentage
options.description: Replace a percentage of junk items in the item pool with random traps.

options.label: Ice Trap Weight
options.description: Likelihood of receiving a trap that freezes the player in place.

options.label: Spring Trap Weight
options.description: Likelihood of receiving a trap that spawns a spring that sends the player flying in the opposite direction.

options.label: Police Trap Weight
options.description: Likelihood of receiving a trap that spawns a lot of Cop Speeder enemies.

options.label: Buyon Trap Weight
options.description: Likelihood of receiving a trap that spawns a lot of Buyon enemies.

options.label: Reverse Controls Trap Weight
options.description: Likelihood of receiving a trap that reverses your controls.

options.label: Gravity Trap Weight
options.description: Likelihood of receiving a trap that increments your gravity.

options.label: Reverse Control Trap Duration
options.description: How many seconds the reverse control trap will last. If set to 0, the trap will last until you die or change level.

options.label: Traps and filler on Adventure Fields
options.description: If enabled, traps and filler can activate in the adventure field.

options.label: Traps and filler on Boss Fights
options.description: If enabled, traps and filler can activate during boss fights.

options.label: Traps and filler on Perfect Chaos Fight
options.description:
If enabled, traps and filler can activate during the Perfect Chaos fight.
Keep in mind that enemy traps will subtract rings from the player.

worlds.game: A Dance of Fire and Ice

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Determines what must be done to complete the game.
[Creator] Ascend Vermillion Tower and fight the Creator.
[Monkey] Ascend the Grand Krys'kajo and defeat the Son of the East.
[Observatory] Complete all five A Promise is a Promise quests and uncover the secret of the Observatory.
[Di'orbis] Descend Ku'lero temple and defeat the Gods of Shape. Requires DLC to be enabled.

options.label: Enable DLC
options.description: If enabled, DLC areas will be placed in logic. Requires that you have the DLC installed.

options.label: Circuit Overrides
options.description: Number of circuit overrides to shuffle into the pool.

options.label: Vermillion Tower Shade Lock
options.description:
If set to a non-None value, creates an in-game barrier at the entrance of Vermillion Tower to prevent extremely
quick playthroughs.
[Bosses] Vermillion Tower only opens when the bosses at the end of the first four dungeons have been beaten.
[Shades] Vermillion Tower only opens when the four shades acquired at the end of the first four dungeons have been
         acquired.
[Bosses and Shades] Vermillion Tower opens when both of the other conditions have been satisfied.

options.label: Vermillion Wasteland Meteor Passage
options.description: If enabled, places a gate between Sapphire Ridge and Vermillion Wasteland unlockable with the meteor shade,

options.label: Skip Vermillion Tower
options.description:
If enabled, Vermillion Tower will not need to be completed; instead, the player will skip through it to the final
boss.

options.label: Closed Gaia
options.description:
If set to a non-None value, adds barriers to each side of Gaia's Garden to decrease the amount of immediate checks
when unlocking the area, openable with East and West Gaia Pass obtained from Apollo duel encounter.
[Minimal] Adds barriers to Left and Right side of Gaia (includes dungeons).
[Full] Besides the Left and Right barriers, also adds gates in Grove and Infested areas which require the dungeon shades.

options.label: Quest Randomization
options.description: If enabled, all quest rewards will be added to the location list.

options.label: Botanics Completion Amount
options.description: The number of plants required to turn in the quest "Crocus Pocus".

options.label: Show Hidden Quest Rewards
options.description:
Some quests hide their rewards until they are completed.
[Vanilla] Behavior is unchanged from the base game.
[Show All] Show all rewards regardless of whether they're hidden in the base game.
[Hide All] Hide all rewards regardless of whether they're hidden in the base game.

options.label: Hidden Quest Obfuscation Level
options.description:
For quests with hidden rewards, this option controls the level to which rewards are obscured.
[Hide Item] Only hides the item name. The icon and receiving player are still accurate.
[Hide Text] Obscures item name and receiving player. The icon will still be accurate.
[Hide All] The item name and receiving player will all be hidden and the icon will be replaced with a generic
           Archipelago logo.

options.label: Quest Dialog Hints
options.description:
If enabled, upon viewing the quest dialog for a quest with rewards that are not hidden, hints are sent to the
Archipelago server for all non-filler quest rewards.

options.label: Shop Randomization
options.description: If enabled, all shops will be added to the location list.

options.label: Shop Dialog Hints
options.description:
If enabled, upon opening the dialog for a shop, corresponding hints are sent to the Archipelago server for all
non-filler shop items.

options.label: Shop Send Mode
options.description:
Controls what exactly counts as a check when shop randomization is enabled.
[Per Item Type] A check is added for each type of item (for example, Sandwich). Therefore, purchasing a sandwich
from any shop in the game clears the same check.
[Per Slot] A check is added for each item slot in each shop. Therefore, purchasing a Sandwich in Rookie Harbor
clears a separate check than purchasing a Sandwich in Bergen Village.

options.label: Shop Receive Mode
options.description:
Controls how shops are unlocked when shop randomization is enabled.
[None] All shop slots are able to be purchased as soon as the player can access the shop.
[Per Item Type] A check is added for each type of item (for example, Sandwich) which unlocks the ability to purchase
that item from any shop.
[Per Shop] A check is added for each shop (for example, Rookie Harbor Items) which unlocks the ability to purchase
items from that shop.
[Per Slot] A check is added for each item slot in each shop which unlocks the ability to purchase that item from
that shop (this may lead to tedious playthroughs).

options.label: Botanics Randomization
options.description: If enabled, acquiring all the information about each plant by collecting drops is a location.

options.label: Start with Green Leaf Shade
options.description:
If enabled, the player will start with the green leaf shade, unlocking Autumn's Fall. This makes the early game far
more open.

options.label: Start with Chest Detector
options.description: If enabled, the player will start with the chest detector item, which will notify them of the chests in the room.

options.label: Start with Discs
options.description:
If set to a value other than "none", the player will start with the corresponding disc items.
Disc of Insight unlocks the records menu.
Disc of Flora unlocks the botany menu, allowing the player to start collecting plant samples from the beginning.

options.label: Start with Pet
options.description: If enabled, the player will start with a random pet. This is just for fun.

options.label: Rhombus Hub Unlock
options.description:
If enabled, allows traveling to areas out of order from the hub in Rhombus Square. Allows skipping areas such as
Autumn's Fall if you are missing the Red Flame Shade, but have the Green Seed Shade / Star Shade.

options.label: Progressive Area Unlocks
options.description:
If enabled, the items that unlock overworld areas and dungeons (including shades and some passes) will be made
progressive.
[None] no areas are unlocked progressively.
[Dungeons] dungeons are unlocked progressively; overworld areas are not.
[Overworld] overworld areas are unlocked progressively; dungeons are not.
[Split] both dungeons and overworld areas are unlocked progressively in separate progressive chains.
[Combined] both dungeons and overworld areas are unlocked progressively from the same progressive chain.

options.label: Progressive Equipment
options.description:
If enabled, equipment will be progressive, sorted into different categories according to playstyle depending on
which of the other location-adding options are enabled.

options.label: Keyrings
options.description: If enabled, all keys for each dungeon will be replaced with a singular item that unlocks every door in that dungeon.

options.label: Allow Booster Grinding
options.description:
If enabled, some locations may require grinding enemies with boosters on for gem drops.
If disabled, alternative methods for obtaining required items will be made available.

options.label: Chest Reveal
options.description:
If enabled, shows the category of all chests without having to reach the room chests are in first.
If disabled, the player must reach the room with chests to know what category the chests are.

options.label: Shade Shuffle
options.description: Where shades will appear.

options.label: Element Shuffle
options.description: Where elements will appear.

options.label: Small Key Shuffle
options.description: Where small keys will appear.

options.label: Master Key Shuffle
options.description: Where master keys will appear.

options.label: Chest Key Shuffle
options.description:
Where the Thief's Key, White Key, and Radiant Key (the keys that open bronze, silver, and gold chests, respectively)
may appear.

options.label: Chest Lock Randomization
options.description: If enabled, the lock on all chests (Bronze, Silver, Gold, or None) will be randomized.

options.label: Unlocked Chest Weight
options.description: Controls the likelihood of giving a chest no lock (if chest lock randomization is enabled).

options.label: Bronze Chest Lock Weight
options.description: Controls the likelihood of giving a chest bronze lock, requiring Thief's Key to open (if chest lock randomization is enabled).

options.label: Silver Chest Lock Weight
options.description: Controls the likelihood of giving a chest silver lock, requiring White Key to open (if chest lock randomization is enabled).

options.label: Gold Chest Lock Weight
options.description: Controls the likelihood of giving a chest gild lock, requiring Radiant Key to open (if chest lock randomization is enabled).

options.label: Exclude Always Quests
options.description:
Certain quests are always in the location pool because they hold progression items when playing vanilla CrossCode.
If this option is selected (and quest rando is disabled), this option will ensure that none of those locations are
populated with progression or useful items. It will also prohibit items from being placed on NPC interactions that
give progression items but require working through part of a questline to get to.

options.label: Common Pool Weight
options.description: Controls the likelihood of choosing a common filler item when filling the world.

options.label: Rare Pool Weight
options.description: Controls the likelihood of choosing a rare filler item when filling the world.

options.label: Epic Pool Weight
options.description: Controls the likelihood of choosing a epic filler item when filling the world.

options.label: Legendary Pool Weight
options.description: Controls the likelihood of choosing a legendary filler item when filling the world.

options.label: Consumable Weight
options.description: Controls the likelihood of choosing a consumable item (as opposed to a drop).

options.label: Drop Weight
options.description: Controls the likelihood of choosing a drop item (as opposed to a consumable).

options.label: Balanced Rapid Fire
options.description:
Makes the upgrade power of Rapid Fire more evenly distributed, and gives a slightly faster starting speed.

True: 10/8/6/4/2/1 frames per shot.
False: 12/5/4/3/2/1 frames per shot (vanilla behavior).

options.label: Item Distribution
options.description:
Determines how many copies of items and upgrades exist in the item pool. 
Note that vanilla maximums still apply, the extra copies only make it more likely to max out earlier.
Filler items (EEs and Energy Packs) are distributed based on intended relative difficulty.

Vanilla: Uses the vanilla item distribution, where possible. Some items have extra copies, some don't.
Exact: Only the exact number of items needed to max out stats and subweapons is provided.
Reduced: Reduced maximum for stats and subweapons. This will make the game much harder!
Extra: Some extra copies of all items are added to the pool. This will make the game slightly easier.

(Developer note: Extra is recommended for Sync games, Exact for Async. Reduced may result in brutal difficulty!)

options.label: Area Gating Strength
options.description:
Determines how much offensive and defensive power is needed before putting each Area in logic. 
Higher settings will be easier but more likely to follow the vanilla game Area order.

Totals required for Area 10 - 
Low: 7 Defense, 9 Offense
Normal: 9 Defense, 12 Offense
High: 12 Defense, 16 Offense

(Developer notes: In the Offense totals, Attack Up counts as double.
High is recommended for most players, as lower gating can result in having to do late-game areas 
 while severely underpowered.)

options.label: Corridor 11-20 Hints
options.description:
The rooms that normally explain how to open Corridor 1-10 will instead have hints for
the classification of items in Corridor 11-20. Choose how many Corridors receive hints.
(If less than 10 is chosen, hinted corridors will be randomly selected.)

options.label: Enable Map Randomization
options.description:
Randomizes the layout of the walking sections of Naju.
Areas will still branch off from central Area 0 but the layouts will be different.
Item distributions will be the same as vanilla, but the original coordinates no longer apply.
Randomization algorithm adapted from Fireball87: https://github.com/fireball87/GuardianLegendRando

options.label: Progression Lock Difficulty
options.description: Determines how high the progressive check locks are for each sphere. (Completion by Diff LeafLover=10%, Normal=25%, Hard=33%, Lethal=50%, Karl=75%)

options.label: Starting Stats
options.description: Determine how hard your starting stats are. this also affects your maximum stats reached

options.label: Goal of the Run
options.description: Set The Current Run Goal [Working Options = kill_caretaker (default) [Long], goldrush [Medium], hunter (beta) [Medium], gauntlet (beta) [Short]

options.label: Goal Gold for Gold Rush
options.description: Set The Current Gold Rush Gold needed (GoldRush Goal) [Must be Multiple of 10 and >5000]

options.label: Gold Increment for Checks for Gold Rush
options.description: Set The Amount of Gold Needed per Check (GoldRush Goal) [Must be Multiple of 10 and >30]

options.label: Should Deathlink Kill All Players?
options.description: Sets whether deathlink will kill all palyers, or just a single dwarf at random (in multiplayer)

options.label: Should Deathlink Only Send On Mission Failure?
options.description: Sets whether deathlink will send only on Mission Failure (instead of dwarf death)

options.label: Chosen Starting Class
options.description: Set you starting class

options.label: Enable / Set Weapon Randomization
options.description: Set Weapons randomization Style (Fully Random disables Starting Weapon Choices)

options.label: Chosen Starting Primary Weapon
options.description: Set you starting primary weapon. (Make sure its for your starting class)

options.label: Chosen Starting Secondary Weapon
options.description: Set you starting secondary weapon. (Make sure its for your starting class)

options.label: Error Cube Checks
options.description: Sets the number of checks to be Error cubes (Defaults to 10)

options.label: Enable Traps
options.description: Turns on/off Trap Items

options.label: Enable Minigame Locations
options.description: Turns on/off Jetty Boot as a location

options.label: Minigame Num
options.description: Sets the high score needed for all the Minigame Locations (in increments of 5)

options.label: Enable Machine Event Locations
options.description: Turns on/off Machine Events as a location

options.label: Average Coin Shop Prices
options.description: Set the avg coin shop price. This will determine the cost of APCoin Shop Items in game.

options.label: Gold to APCoin Conversion Rate
options.description: Set the value of Gold Gathered to APCoin Conversion Rate. For example setting this to 100 would mean 100x gathered gold gets you 1x APCoin.

options.label: Beer Materials to APCoin Conversion Rate
options.description: Set the value of Beer Materials to APCoin Conversion Rate. For example setting this to 5 would mean 5x gathered beer materials gets you 1x APCoin.

options.label: AP Coin Shop Item Count
options.description: Set the amount of items to be in the APCoin Shop.

options.label: Set Max Hazard for All Objectives
options.description: Determines how high the highest generated hazard level will be for objectives. (If Playing Gauntlet Goal, this is your Chosen Hazard Level)

options.label: Trophy Hunter Normal Amount
options.description: Set The Current Hunter Trophies Needed per enemy (Hunter Goal)

options.label: Valid Hunter Targets for Hunter Goal
options.description: Determines what counts for the Hunter Goal (Hunter Goal)

options.label: How Many Boss Trophies Finished To Win?
options.description: Determines how many Boss Hunter Goals you must meet to win (Hunter Goal)

options.label: Trophy Hunter Boss Amount
options.description: Set The Current Hunter Trophies Needed per Boss enemy (Hunter Goal)

options.label: Should Start with Sprinting Unlocked?
options.description: Sets whether sprinting should be possible from the start (removes some base movespeed checks)

options.label: Starting Biome for Kill Caretaker
options.description: Determines what Biome you start with unlocked (Kill Caretaker Goal) [Unlocks all but End Biome]

options.label: Biome for Final Boss in Kill Caretaker
options.description: Determines what Biome you end with (Kill Caretaker Goal)

options.label: Gauntlet Goal Stages to Victory Mission
options.description: Set The number of Stages to complete the Gauntlet (Gauntlet Goal)

options.label: Gauntlet Mission Generation Seed
options.description: Set a Mission Generation Seed for the Gauntlet (Gauntlet Goal)

options.label: Gauntlet Goal Stages to Start With
options.description: Set The number of Stages you start with unlocked (Gauntlet Goal)

options.label: Enable Gauntlet Starter Kit (Balanced Starting Stats)
options.description: Adds some additional starting stats in Gauntlet Mode to Balance the early game (Gauntlet Goal). Turn this off for added difficulty.

options.label: Biome Blacklist
options.description: Prevents certain biomes from being included in generation. (Only affects Kill Caretaker)

options.label: Objective Blacklist
options.description: Prevents certain objectives from being included in generation. (Only affects Kill Caretaker)

options.label: Secondary Blacklist
options.description: Prevents certain objectives from being included in generation. (Affects Most Goals)

options.label: Warning Blacklist
options.description: Prevents certain objectives from being included in generation. (Affects Most Goals)

options.label: Trap Link
options.description: When your friends receive a trap, you get it too! Of course the same is true the other direction. Works with compatible games.

options.label: Randomize Park Values
options.description: Randomizes values such as starting cash, starting bank loan amount, and the max bank loan

options.label: Base Land Price
options.description: Sets the base price of land. Setting this to 201 will keep the default land price in the scenario, which will then be randomized based on randomization range. Monopoly mode overrides this setting.

options.label: Base Construction Rights Price
options.description: Sets the base price of construction rights. Setting this to 201 will keep the default construction rights price in the scenario, which will then be randomized based on randomization range. Monopoly mode overrides this setting.

options.label: Ignore Ride Stat Changes
options.description: Disables changes to base ride stats. If enabled, rides will always behave like they do in the base game.

options.label: Guest Objective
options.description: Choose how many guests are required to win the scenario

options.label: Park Value Objective
options.description: If enabled, choose what park value (In USD) is required to win the scenario.

options.label: Roller Coaster Objective
options.description: If enabled, choose how many coasters, and what prerequisites they need to beat the scenario.

options.label: Excitement Requirement
options.description: Select the minimum excitement 😀 for a coaster to count towards your objective. 0 will disable a minimum excitement rating.

options.label: Intensity Requirement
options.description: Select the minimum intensity 😬 for a coaster to count towards your objective. 0 will disable a minimum intensity rating.

options.label: Nausea Requirement
options.description: Select the minimum nausea 🤢 for a coaster to count towards your objective. 0 will disable a minimum nausea rating.

options.label: Unique Ride Requirement
options.description:
Requires specific rides to be built before scenario completion is awarded. These will tend to appear in the later half of the game.
It's highly recommended to have this set to at least 1!

options.label: Include Shops for Goal
options.description: Select whether shops and stalls should elligible to be included in the required rides list for completion.

options.label: Park Rating Objective
options.description: If enabled, choose the minimum park rating needed to beat the scenario.

options.label: Pay Off Loan
options.description: Require Loan to be paid off before scenario completion is awarded. Multiple objectives can be enabled!

options.label: Monopoly Mode
options.description: Monopoly Mode is a new objective type. Every unowned tile will be set to purchasable (Or purchasable construction rights for any unowned tile with a grounded path. Elevated paths will not be purchasable). To complete the objective, all tiles on the map must be purchased. Multiple Objectives can be enabled!

options.label: Fireworks
options.description: Have an explosive firework display on victory! Strongly discouraged if you intend to keep playing after victory or if you expect to have a huge park.

options.label: Balance Guest Counts
options.description:
Attempts to balance the minimum guest requirements to the ride they're attached to. Low throughput rides
like Spiral Slides will tend towards the minimum, while high throughput rides like roller coasters will 
tend towards the maximum.

options.label: Exclude Safest Park Award
options.description: Exclude the Safest Park Award from having a check. This may be useful depending on deathlink settings.

options.label: Minimum Shop Excitement Requirement
options.description:
If the shop determines you need a ride with a minimum excitement, this value will be the lowest it can ask for.
If this value is higher than the maximum, the generator will assume it is a mistake and set it to 0.

options.label: Maximum Shop Excitement Requirement
options.description: If the shop determines you need a ride with a minimum excitement, this value will be the highest it can ask for.

options.label: Minimum Shop Intensity Requirement
options.description:
If the shop determines you need a ride with a minimum intensity, this value will be the lowest it can ask for.
If this value is higher than the maximum, the generator will assume it is a mistake and set it to 0.

options.label: Maximum Shop Intensity Requirement
options.description: If the shop determines you need a ride with a minimum intensity, this value will be the highest it can ask for.

options.label: Minimum Shop Nausea Requirement
options.description:
If the shop determines you need a ride with a minimum nausea, this value will be the lowest it can ask for.
If this value is higher than the maximum, the generator will assume it is a mistake and set it to 0.

options.label: Maximum Shop Nausea Requirement
options.description: If the shop determines you need a ride with a minimum nausea, this value will be the highest it can ask for.

options.label: Minimum Shop Length Requirement
options.description:
If the shop determines you need a ride with a minimum length (In Meters), this value in meters will 
be the lowest it can ask for. If this value is higher than the maximum, the generator will assume it is a 
mistake and set it to 0.

options.label: Maximum Shop Length Requirement
options.description:
If the shop determines you need a ride with a minimum length (In Meters), 
this value will be the highest it can ask for.

options.label: Minimum Shop Customers Requirement
options.description:
If the shop determines you need a ride with a minimum total number of customers, this value will be the 
lowest it can ask for. If this value is higher than the maximum, the generator will assume it is a mistake and 
set it to 0.

options.label: Maximum Shop Total Customers Requirement
options.description:
If the shop determines you need a ride with a minimum total number of customers, this value will be the 
highest it can ask for.

options.label: Maximum Roller Coasters Required
options.description:
When the shop requires multiple roller coasters, sets the maximum 
it can ask for. The default is the reccomended value.

options.label: Maximum Tracked Rides Required
options.description:
When the shop requires multiple tracked rides, sets the maximum 
it can ask for. The default is the reccomended value.

options.label: Maximum Specific Rides (Early) Required
options.description:
When the shop requires a specific, trackless ride 
early in the game, sets the maximum it can ask for. The 
default is the reccomended value.

options.label: Maximum Specific Rides Required
options.description:
When the shop requires a specific, trackless ride 
later in the game, sets the maximum it can ask for. 
The default is the reccomended value.

options.label: Maximum Transport/Water Rides Required
options.description:
When the shop requires transport rides, water rides, 
and unwieldy roller coasters, sets the maximum it can ask 
for. The default is the reccomended value.

options.label: Maximum Stalls Required
options.description:
When the shop requires shops and stalls, sets the 
maximum it can ask for. The default is the 
reccomended value.

options.label: Maximum Other Rides Required
options.description:
When the shop requires other rides and categories, 
(Mostly flat rides) sets the maximum it can ask for. 
The default is the reccomended value.

options.label: Filler
options.description: How many extra filler items to add to the mix as a percentage. This includes cash bonuses, weather events, and guest spawns.

options.label: Include ATM
options.description: Includes an ATM in the item list, regardless of whether it normally appears in the chosen scenario.

options.label: Include First Aid Room
options.description: Includes a First Aid Room in the item list, regardless of whether it normally appears in the chosen scenario.

options.label: Include Gamespeed Items
options.description: If included, the ability to use the speed toggle will be restricted behind an item. 4 items total will be added, each progressively unlocking a faster speed.

options.label: Skips
options.description:
By default, every game starts with a single skip to ignore a shop requirement. This will add additional skips to 
be found in the item pool.

options.label: Land Discounts
options.description: Adds Land Discounts to the pool. 0 means no discounts will be included in the pool. More discounts will make individual discounts easier to find, but less effective. Monopoly mode will raise the minimum to 20.

options.label: Construction Rights Discounts
options.description: Adds Construction Rights Discounts to the pool. 0 means no discounts will be included in the pool. More discounts will make individual discounts easier to find, but less effective. Monopoly mode will raise the minimum to 20.

options.label: Furry Convention Traps
options.description: When found, instantly hosts a furry convention in your park! Adding traps will increase the total number of items in the world.

options.label: Bathroom Traps
options.description: When found, instantly maxes out the bathroom stat of every guest! Adding traps will increase the total number of items in the world.

options.label: Spam Traps
options.description: When found, spams ads all over the screen! Adding traps will increase the total number of items in the world.

options.label: Loan Shark Traps
options.description: When found, increases your loan! Adding traps will increase the total number of items in the world.

options.label: Food poisoning Traps
options.description: When found, gives everybody with food in the park Norovirus! Adding traps will increase the total number of items in the world.

options.label: Include All Rides and Scenery (Base Game)
options.description: Adds every ride and scenery pack in the base game to the item pool. This will make for a significantly longer scenario.

options.label: Include All Rides and Scenery (Expansion Packs)
options.description:
Adds every ride and scenery pack in the RCT2 Expansion Packs to the item pool. If this is true the base game rides and 
scenery will also be included. This will make for a significantly longer scenario.

options.label: Logic Complexity
options.description:
Simple: Smiler warps (Bee statues) will not be factored into logical progression.
        Interface manipulation will also not be factored into logic with the following exceptions:
            Traversing DIS
            Reaching B000
            Reaching Cif's brand room
        Simple Logic is not compatible with the following options:
            (Nothing yet)

Full:   Smiler warps and interface manipulation are factored into logic.
            (Using the HP value is still not logically required)
        All settings are compatible.

options.label: Idolsanity
options.description:
When enabled, the Lover, Smiler, and Killer statues are eggs until their respective items are received.
While eggs, the statues will not perform any of their functions.

options.label: Shortcutsanity
options.description:
Access to each of Mon's five shortcuts are now items.
Speaking to Mon at his five hint locations will each send a check.
Only shortcuts 3, 4, and 5 have logical implications currently.

options.label: Include Dead End
options.description:
Adds all nine accessible empty chests from the voided ending sequence as checks.
Also adds the "It's your brand" mural as a check.
You can now reach this area from B225 without being VOID.

options.label: Include White Void
options.description:
When enabled, spawns five chests at the end of the White Void area after interacting with the statue.
Regardless of this option, the statue no longer deletes your save file.
Short: Limit the dungeon to a random 12 screens before the final room.
Full: All 28 rooms are required to traverse before the final room.

options.label: Include Beehole
options.description:
When enabled, moves the "Slay the Lord of Sloth" check to the end of the Beehole dungeon.
To access, you must first show Gor the Void Rod, and then find the entrance room (Normally past the secret exit on B144).
Also includes the two chests in the entrance room, and adds two additional chests to the end of the area.

options.label: Include Greedzone
options.description:
When enabled, includes the 15 chests at the end of Mon's Funhouse as checks.
A set amount of Greed Coins are added as items and are required to access the dungeon.
This will be revamped in v0.12.0

options.label: DIS Length
options.description:
How long the final dungeon, DIS, should be.
Short chooses a random 12 rooms
Full is the normal vanilla length.

options.label: Greed Coin Amount
options.description:
Sets the amount of Greed Coins in the pool.
Only works if the Greed Zone is enabled. Valid range is 1-30.

options.label: Skip Cutscenes
options.description:
When enabled, the final cutscene at the end of the game is skipped, stepping onto the elevator brings you
 instantly to controlling Lily in the final room.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Victory condition for the seed.
- beat_the_game: Defeat the Ninth Child and escape (default, vanilla goal).
- beat_the_dlc: Defeat the final boss in the in the Tower of Oannes DLC.
  Requires Oannesanity.
- glossary_hunt: Collect a set number of AP shuffled Glossary entries. 
  You will start off with the Ruins Encyclopedia which tracks your progress.
  Requires at least one Glossanity category to be enabled.
If the chosen goal's prerequisites aren't met, falls back to beat_the_game.

options.label: Glossary Hunt Count
options.description:
Number of Glossary entries required to win when the goal is glossary_hunt.
The maximum value is automatically lowered to the number of Glossary entries
shuffled based on the enabled Glossanity options (and Oannesanity, for DLC glossary).
Any surplus beyond the required count is set as filler (will still count).

options.label: Starting Area
options.description:
Starting area for the player.
Some areas require specific entrance randomizer options to be enabled. If the chosen area's
prerequisites aren't met, a uniform re-roll is performed across the remaining valid areas
(a warning is logged); if no valid options remain, falls back to Village of Departure.

Requires non-original shops: annwfn, immortal_battlefield.
Requires vertical_entrances: icefire_treetop.
Requires gate_entrances: divine_fortress, shrine_of_the_frost_giants, takamagahara_shrine,
valhalla, dark_star_lords_mausoleum, ancient_chaos, hall_of_malice.

options.label: Starting Weapon
options.description: Starting weapon for the player.

options.label: Random Grail
options.description: Randomize the Holy Grail.

options.label: Random Scanner
options.description: Randomize the Hand Scanner.

options.label: Random Codices
options.description: Randomize the Codices.

options.label: Random FDC
options.description: Randomize the Future Development Company software.

options.label: Random Ring
options.description: Randomize the Ring.

options.label: Random Shell Horn
options.description: Randomize the Shell Horn.

options.label: Random Maps & Mapping Software
options.description: Randomize Maps & Mapping Software.

options.label: Mantra Placement
options.description:
random: Mantras can be anywhere.
only_murals: Mantras are restricted to mural locations.
original: Mantras stay in their vanilla mural locations.

options.label: Shop Placement
options.description:
random: All shop items are shuffled.
at_least_one: Each shop is guaranteed at least one non-ammo/weight item.
original: Shops keep vanilla items.
Note: If [original] is selected, FDC, Codices and Hand Scanner cannot not be randomized.

options.label: Include Expensive Item in Shop
options.description:
Put one random shop slot at a 1000 coin price tag.
Buying it is logically gated behind either the Harp which discounts the item,
or Ganesha's Talisman plus Money Fairy access to farm the coins required.

options.label: Random Research
options.description:
Add all Kosugi Research Papers into the AP item pool.
If disabled, they will be static untracked locations in-game.

options.label: Remove Research Notes
options.description:
Remove Kosugi Research Notes from the item pool.
Any remaining research item will be converted to filler.

options.label: Research to Sacred Orbs
options.description:
Replace X Kosugi Research Papers with additional Sacred Orbs (max. 10)
Requires Random Research to be enabled (otherwise research isn't in the pool)
The remaining research items stay in the pool as normal.
Remove Research Notes will not remove Sacred Orbs; only remaining research items.

options.label: Remove Maps
options.description:
Removes maps from the item pool.
This means that 16 filler items will take their place.

options.label: Nibiru Dissonance Skulls
options.description: Number of Crystal Skulls required for Nibiru Dissonance.

options.label: Remove Skulls
options.description: Remove Excess Crystal Skulls from the item pool.

options.label: Random Dissonance
options.description:
All 6 dissonance locations are converted into chests and turns the Beherit into 7 progressive items.
If true, sealing the Corridor of Blood requires all 7 Progressive Beherit in addition to the set GuardianKills.
If false, sealing the Corridor of Blood requires beating Anu and absorbing all dissonance from their original locations.
(Effectively requires beating at least Vritra, Aten-Ra, Anu, Echidna and Hel based on just this flag).

options.label: Costumesanity
options.description:
Add the costume chests (4+1) and their correlating costumes into the pool.
At the start of the seed you will not have your costumes available.
The chests are openable by default and do not require a key.
This option will impact logic relating to glitches and DLC. 
Note: DLC Item is only shuffled if Oannesanity is turned on.

options.label: Potsanity - Low Value Pots
options.description:
Potsanity: add Low Value item pots as checks. (144 pots)
39 x 1 Weight Pots
74 x 10 Coins Pots
31 x 30 Coins Pots

options.label: Potsanity - High Value Pots
options.description:
Potsanity: add High Value item pots as checks. (24 pots)
8 x 50 Coins Pots
7 x 80 Coins Pots
9 x 100 Coins Pots

options.label: Potsanity - Shuriken Pots
options.description: Potsanity: add all Shuriken ammo pots as checks. (23 pots)

options.label: Potsanity - Rolling Shuriken Pots
options.description: Potsanity: add all Rolling Shuriken ammo pots as checks. (16 pots)

options.label: Potsanity - Earth Spear Pots
options.description: Potsanity: add all Earth Spear ammo pots as checks. (23 pots)

options.label: Potsanity - Flare Pots
options.description: Potsanity: add all Flare ammo pots as checks. (24 pots)

options.label: Potsanity - Caltrops Pots
options.description: Potsanity: add all Caltrops ammo pots as checks. (17 pots)

options.label: Potsanity - Chakram Pots
options.description: Potsanity: add all Chakram ammo pots as checks. (10 pots)

options.label: Potsanity - Bomb Pots
options.description: Potsanity: add all Bomb ammo pots as checks. (26 pots)

options.label: Local Potsanity Percentage
options.description:
The percentage of Potsanity pot filler forced into your own world.
0% - no items are pre-filled, pot filler can be anywhere (including own world)
100% - all pot filler items are forced into own world.

options.label: Glossanity - Freestanding
options.description:
Glossanity: add all Freestanding Glossary entries. (50+5 entries)
Note: DLC Glossary is only shuffled if Oannesanity is turned on.

options.label: Glossanity - Scannable
options.description: Glossanity: add all Scannable Glossary entries that require Hand Scanner. (27 entries)

options.label: Glossanity - NPC
options.description: Glossanity: add all NPC Glossary entries as checks. (78 entries)

options.label: Glossanity - Enemy
options.description:
Glossanity: add all Enemy Glossary entries as checks. (77+7 entries)
Note: DLC Glossary is only shuffled if Oannesanity is turned on.

options.label: Local Glossanity Percentage
options.description:
The percentage of Glossanity entries forced into your own world.
0% - no items are pre-filled, glossary can be anywhere (including own world)
100% - all glossary chips are forced into own world.

options.label: Oannesanity
options.description:
DLC Required. Enabling this may add the following checks based off of other options:
- Beat the DLC goal
- 1 Item Chest (Comes with this option)
- 5 Freestanding Glossary (Glossanity - Freestanding Required)
- 7 Enemy Glossary (Glossanity - Enemy Required)
- 1 Costume Chest (Costumesanity Required)
- 12 Entrance Pairs (Include DLC Entrances Required)

options.label: Required Guardian Kills
options.description:
Only applies if RandomDissonance is on.
Number of Guardians required to be defeated to seal the Corridor of Blood.
Note: the Spiral Boat soul gate value will be adjusted to be at or below this value.
This way, you will always be able to reach the final area without requiring additional guardians.

options.label: Guardian Specific Ankh Jewels
options.description: Makes Ankhs only usable at their designated bosses.

options.label: Logic Difficulty
options.description:
Logic difficulty setting.
- normal: intuitive logic - certain HP / damage thresholds required for (mini-)bosses.
- tricky: includes some shenanigans such as precise jumps, janky hitboxes or damage boosting.
- minimal: in addition to tricky logic, sets minimal melee requirements for (mini-)bosses.

options.label: Game Difficulty
options.description:
In-game difficulty.
- normal: default game difficulty.
- hard: difficulty level +3 (normally toggled by scanning a specific tablet twice).
Note: Logic is unaffected — this is a QoL (?) feature for those wanting to play on Hard Mode.

options.label: Echidna Difficulty
options.description: The Boss Echidna phase difficulty.

options.label: Costume Clip
options.description:
Logically require using a glitch called Costume Clip.
Costume Clip: jump and pause on the same frame.
Once you hear the jump SFX as you open the menu, switch costumes.
This allows you to clip into objects like pots which can push you through walls.

options.label: Future Development Company in Logic
options.description:
Logically require Future Development Company for accessing backside regions.
(This does not include Icefire Treetop or Immortal Battlefield).

options.label: DLC Item Logic
options.description:
Logically require making use of the DLC reward.
When enabled, the DLC item is assumed as collected from the start, unless it is
randomized by Costumesanity, in which case it must be obtained first.
When disabled, the DLC item is never considered in logic.

options.label: Life Sigil to Awaken HoM
options.description:
Logically require Life Sigil to Awaken Hall of Malice.
If enabled, will consider access to the grail point in logic.

options.label: Remove Icefire Treetop Statue
options.description: Remove Icefire Treetop Statue for more accessibility.

options.label: Random Cursed Chests
options.description:
Randomize Cursed Chests
Vanilla:
- FlameTorcChest (Surtr)
- GiantsFluteChest (Echidna)
- DestinyTabletChest (Anzu)
- PowerBandChest (Belial)

options.label: Cursed Chests
options.description:
Number of Cursed Chests to randomize (only used when Random Cursed Chests is on).
Base game has 86 regular chests, boosted to 92 through various sanity settings.
The max is automatically clamped down if set to higher than the actual amount of chests.

options.label: Horizontal Entrances
options.description: Shuffle horizontal entrances.

options.label: Vertical Entrances
options.description: Shuffle vertical entrances.

options.label: Gate Entrances
options.description: Shuffle gate entrances.

options.label: Unique Transitions
options.description:
Shuffle unique transitions.
(e.g. Annwfn -> Immortal Battlefield / Takamagahara Shrine -> Heaven's Labyrinth)

options.label: Full Random Entrances
options.description: Mix the enabled randomized entrances across area types.

options.label: Include DLC Entrances
options.description:
Requires Oannesanity toggled on. Include DLC entrances in the entrance pool.
Note: Combat logic to survive in the DLC areas is still minimal.

options.label: Prevent Area Loops
options.description:
Prevent entrance randomization from pairing exits within the same area.
May increase fill success rate if you're having issues with generation.

options.label: Soul Gate Entrances
options.description:
Shuffle [1,2,3,5] soul gate entrances with each other.
Note: does not mix with regular the above regular entrances and transitions.

options.label: Include Nine Soul Gates
options.description:
Include the two [9] soul gates (HoM to IB Boat) in the Soul Gate pool.
Can work with Soul Gate Entrances and Random Soul Gate Values separately.
Note: [9] soul gate is floored to be reachable depending on player set
RequiredGuardians value if RandomDissonance is enabled.

options.label: Random Soul Gate Value
options.description:
How the soul gate costs are handed out.
Standard: every gate keeps its vanilla cost. (Only applies to Soul Gate ER off)
Shuffled: vanilla costs are shuffled between the Soul Gates.
Randomized: each gate pair independently rolls any of [1,2,3,5,9].

options.label: Auto Scan Tablets
options.description:
Automatically scan tablets when read.
Requires Hand Scanner in logic if disabled.

options.label: Auto Place Skulls
options.description: Auto-Place Crystal Skulls in Nibiru.

options.label: Greedy Charon
options.description:
AP coin grants can be sent by another player at any point, 
which may not be ideal in synced playthroughs. 
Turning this on will make Charon take all your coins as payment, 
so you don't get bricked with additional coins while trying to get to Charon.

options.label: Persistent Inventory
options.description:
Keep everything you have locally collected after a death or a save load.
Normally only AP items get regranted upon loading; this option extends to ALL items.
In other words, turning this on keeps your inventory fully synced with AP's CollectionState.
Own world items are silently recovered and checked locations remain checked.
Note: Puzzle progression flags will not persist.

options.label: Starting Money
options.description: Starting money amount.

options.label: Starting Weights
options.description: Starting weights amount.

options.label: Item Chest Color
options.description: Color for item chests.

options.label: Filler Chest Color
options.description: Color for filler chests.

options.label: AP Chest Color
options.description: Color for AP chests.

options.label: Write Seed File.
options.description:
Writes seed.lm2r (standalone compatible) and a seed.lm2ap
For those who wish to play solo seeds outside of AP.
AP generated seeds require both files to play the seed solo offline.
Standalone generated seeds can also be played (will use the original
filler and ankh jewel system).
Seed files need to be placed in La-Mulana 2/LaMulana2Randomizer/Seed

options.label: Taste of Adventures
options.description: Taste of Adventures DLC

options.label: Booms and Blooms
options.description: Booms and Blooms DLC

options.label: Dinos and Dynasties
options.description: Dinos and Dynasties DLC

options.label: Utility Buildings
options.description: Adding all 4 Utility Buildings to the pool.

options.label: Decorations
options.description:
Adding all 11 Decoration Themes to the pool.
(9 Items if not having DLC "Dinos and Dynasties DLC")

options.label: Statistics
options.description: Adding all 31 Statistics to the pool, if possible.

options.label: Guaranteed unlocked Starter
options.description: An Attraction or Shop is guaranteed as starter.

options.label: Early Toilets

options.description: Early Training Room (If "UtilityBuildings" are enabled!).

options.description: Choose how many guests are required to win the scenario

options.label: Money Goal
options.description: Choose how much money is required to win the scenario

options.label: Roller Coaster Goal
options.description: Choose how many coasters are required to win the scenario

options.label: Excitement Rating
options.description:
Select the minimum excitement 😀 for a coaster to count towards your objective.
0 will disable a minimum excitement rating.

options.label: Intensity Rating
options.description:
Select the minimum intensity 😬 for a coaster to count towards your objective.
0 will disable a minimum intensity rating.

options.label: Ride Profit Goal
options.description: Choose how much profit you need from all rides to win the scenario

options.label: Park Tickets Goal
options.description: Choose how many park tickets has to be sold to win the scenario

options.label: Shops Goal
options.description: Choose how many shops are required to win the scenario

options.label: Shop Profit Goal
options.description: Choose how much profit you need from shops to win the scenario

options.label: Challenge: Max Customers
options.description:
If a challenge determines you need a ride or shop with a maximum amount of customers, this value will be the lowest it can ask for.
If this value is higher than the maximum, the generator will assume it is a mistake and set it to 0.

options.label: Challenge: Max Excitement
options.description:
If a challenge determines you need a rollercoaster with a maximum excitement, this value will be the lowest it can ask for.
If this value is higher than the maximum, the generator will assume it is a mistake and set it to 0.

options.label: Challenge: Max Intensity
options.description:
If a challenge determines you need a rollercoaster with a maximum intensity, this value will be the lowest it can ask for.
If this value is higher than the maximum, the generator will assume it is a mistake and set it to 0.

options.label: Challenge: Max Nausea
options.description:
If a challenge determines you need a rollercoaster with a maximum nausea, this value will be the lowest it can ask for.
If this value is higher than the maximum, the generator will assume it is a mistake and set it to 0.

options.label: Challenge: Max Satisfaction
options.description:
If a challenge determines you need a rollercoaster with a maximum satisfaction, this value will be the lowest it can ask for.
If this value is higher than the maximum, the generator will assume it is a mistake and set it to 0.

options.label: Challenge: Max Coaster Revenue
options.description:
If a challenge determines you need a ride with a total revenue, this value will be the lowest it can ask for.
If this value is higher than the maximum, the generator will assume it is a mistake and set it to 0.

options.label: Challenge: Max Ride Revenue
options.description:
If a challenge determines you need a ride with a total revenue, this value will be the lowest it can ask for.
If this value is higher than the maximum, the generator will assume it is a mistake and set it to 0.

options.label: Challenge: Max Shop Revenue
options.description:
If a challenge determines you need a shop with a total revenue, this value will be the lowest it can ask for.
If this value is higher than the maximum, the generator will assume it is a mistake and set it to 0.

options.label: Challenge: Max Ride Profit
options.description:
If a challenge determines you need a ride with a total profit, this value will be the lowest it can ask for.
If this value is higher than the maximum, the generator will assume it is a mistake and set it to 0.

options.label: Challenge: Max Shop Profit
options.description:
If a challenge determines you need a shop with a total revenue, this value will be the lowest it can ask for.
If this value is higher than the maximum, the generator will assume it is a mistake and set it to 0.

options.label: Challenge: Deco Rating
options.description:
Determines if a challenge need an Attraction with a specific Decoration rating.
Difficulty depending on the value.

options.label: Challenge: Max Photos
options.description:
If a challenge determines you need a Rollercoaster with sold photos, this value will be the lowest it can ask for.
If this value is higher than the maximum, the generator will assume it is a mistake and set it to 0.

options.label: Challenge: Max Ride Vouchers
options.description:
If a challenge determines you need a ride with redeemed vouchers, this value will be the lowest it can ask for.
If this value is higher than the maximum, the generator will assume it is a mistake and set it to 0.

options.label: Challenge: Max Shop Vouchers
options.description:
If a challenge determines you need a shop with redeemed vouchers, this value will be the lowest it can ask for.
If this value is higher than the maximum, the generator will assume it is a mistake and set it to 0.

options.label: Challenge: Park Guests
options.description: Adding Challenge with "Have X amount of Guests in your Park""

options.label: Challenge: Employee
options.description:
Adding Challenge with "Have X amount of Employees""
Difficulty depends on the Experience Level an Employee must have

options.label: Challenge: Pay Money
options.description:
Adding Challenge with "Pay X amount of Money""
Depending on the Difficulty and if "goal_money" is set

options.label: Skips
options.description:
by default, every game start with 5 skips to, well, skip a challenge.
This will add additional skips to be found in the item pool.

options.label: Player Money Trap
options.description:
When found, little Money is added to your Bank Account!
Adding traps will increase the total number of items in the world.

options.label: Attraction Breakdown Trap
options.description:
When found, instantly break specific amount of Attraction/s!
Adding traps will increase the total number of items in the world.

options.label: Attraction Voucher Trap
options.description:
When found, certain Guests will receive an Attraction Voucher in your Park!
Adding traps will increase the total number of items in the world.

options.label: Shop Ingredients Trap
options.description:
When found, ProductShops ingredients needs to be restocked!
Adding traps will increase the total number of items in the world.

options.label: Shop Cleaning Trap
options.description:
When found, Shops needs to be cleaned!
Adding traps will increase the total number of items in the world.

options.label: Shop Voucher Trap
options.description:
When found, some Guests will receive a Shop Voucher in your Park!
Adding traps will increase the total number of items in the world.

options.label: Employee Hiring Trap
options.description:
When found, instantly Hire randomly picked Employees in your park!
Adding traps will increase the total number of items in the world.
The difficulty decides how many of them will be hired!

options.label: Employee Training Trap
options.description:
When found, instantly send randomly picked Employees to the training room!
Adding traps will increase the total number of items in the world.
The difficulty decides how many of them will be training!

options.label: Employee Tiredness Trap
options.description:
When found, instantly raise Employees tiredness!
Adding traps will increase the total number of items in the world.
The difficulty decides how many of them will be tired!

options.label: Weather Trap
options.description:
When found, "Rainy", "Cloudy", "Sunny" or "Stormy Weather" is coming over!
Adding traps will increase the total number of items in the world.

options.label: Guest Spawn Trap
options.description:
When found, a wave of certain Guests appears in your Scenario!
Adding traps will increase the total number of items in the world.

options.label: Guest Kill Trap
options.description:
When found, certain Guests will disappear in your Scenario!
Adding traps will increase the total number of items in the world.

options.label: Guest Money Trap
options.description:
When found, certain Guests will receive or lose their Money in your Park!
Adding traps will increase the total number of items in the world.

options.label: Guest Hunger Trap
options.description:
When found, Guests will be hungry!
Adding traps will increase the total number of items in the world.

options.label: Guest Thirst Trap
options.description:
When found, Guests will be thirsty!
Adding traps will increase the total number of items in the world.

options.label: Guest Bathroom Trap
options.description:
When found, alot of Guests will be running to the next toilet!
Adding traps will increase the total number of items in the world.

options.label: Guest Vomiting Trap
options.description:
When found, Too many Guests will try to find the next First-Aid room or Trashcan!
Adding traps will increase the total number of items in the world.

options.label: Guest Happiness Trap
options.description:
When found, certain Guests will just be happy!
Adding traps will increase the total number of items in the world.

options.label: Guest Tiredness Trap
options.description:
When found, certain Guests will just be tired!
Adding traps will increase the total number of items in the world.

options.label: Guest Vandal Trap
options.description:
When found, certain Guests become a Vandal!
Adding traps will increase the total number of items in the world.
The difficulty decides how many Guests vandalizing your Park!

options.label: Research Trap
options.description: When found, certain Decoration (Path Attachments included) Theme, Attraction/s or Shop/s have to be researched again.

options.label: Trap Link
options.description:
When a player found a Trap, it will spread to everyone that has TrapLink enabled!

You're able to change TrapLink with commands while playing (case-insensitive):
- !!toggleTrapLink = Toggle the TrapLink
- !!joinTrapLink = Join the TrapLink
- !!leaveTrapLink = Leave the TrapLink

options.label: Guest Money Flux
options.description:
(If "Guest Money Trap" is enabled!)
Decides if the Guest receive or/and lose money.

options.label: Progressive Speedups
options.description:
If included, the ability to use the speedups at the window will be restricted behind an item.
6 items total will be added, each progressively unlocking a faster speed.
Game Speedups (0x, 1x, 2x, 3x) are always usable.

options.label: Release Mode
options.description:
Checks/Challenges will *not* be removed when Park Goal completed.
Bigger Async profits from this option when it is 'false'.

Note: When "Release Mode" is enabled, all Challenges/Checks are removed.

You're able to change it with commands while playing (case-insensitive):
- !!toggleReleaseMode = Toggle the Release Mode
- !!disableReleaseMode = Disable Release Mode
- !!enableReleaseMode = Enable Release Mode

options.label: Parkitect Mods
options.description:
Enable or disable individual Parkitect mods below.
Steam Collection: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3647109901

You can ignore this setting. It is always on.

options.label: Game Mode
options.description:
Game mode to generate for (RANDOMIZED PP IS NOT YET IMPLEMENTED, PLEASE TEST OTHER MODES FIRST AND REPORT ANY ISSUES YOU FIND!)

randomizedPP: Randomly generates a list of ranked songs, separated by style (Speed, Tech, etc). 
    Checks are gated behind dynamic pp thresholds (one check every X pp, with X going down as you get more checks). 
    Your pp is weighted on both a map curve and a pool curve, meaning as you clear more maps, 
    the amount of pp you get every new clear goes down. Works with OST and DLC maps (thanks to BeatLeader).
    Win condition: Pass a certain pp threshold (e.g., 1000pp).
    This is the recommended mode, as it provides a more balanced experience.

randomizedAccuracy: Randomly generates a list of curated/ranked songs, separated by style (Speed, Tech, etc).
    Checks are gated behind per-difficulty accuracy thresholds (e.g getting A or above on Expert+, an S on Expert, etc).
    Maximum difficulty for songs is based on selected star rating, and the difficulty to play each map is always the highest available.
    Win condition: A random 'goal map' is selected as the hardest map from the randomly generated pool, and you need to meet the accuracy threshold on that map to win.
    The goal map is locked until you have a certain number of Bloq Keys (10 by default).

randomizedPass: Randomly generates a list of curated/ranked songs, separated by style (Speed, Tech, etc).
    Similar to randomizedAccuracy, but checks are gated behind simply passing the song at each difficulty.
    Win condition: Same as randomizedAccuracy, but you just need to pass the goal map instead of meeting an accuracy threshold.
    Can lead to similarly unbalanced experiences as randomizedAccuracy,
    but is more accessible for players who may struggle with accing certain songs/difficulties but can still pass them.

presetAccuracy:Uses the preset song list under the "Songs" option, and gates checks behind accuracy thresholds (e.g getting A or above on Expert+, an S on Expert, etc).
    Win condition: can either be a preselected goal map, or just pass the hardest accuracy threshold of your final map.

presetPass: Uses the preset song list under the "Songs" option, and gates checks behind simply passing the song at each difficulty.
    Win condition: can either be a preselected goal map, or just pass the final song in the playlist. (currently only the latter is implemented)

options.label: Songs
options.description:
Songs that may occur in the custom playlist if a preset game mode is selected. Ignored otherwise.

For custom maps:
- Specify the levelid from beatsaver (in the url, /maps/<id>)
- Set is_official to False

For official Beat Saber maps:
- Use the levelID (e.g., "100Bills", "AngelVoices", etc. Typically just the song name in PascalCase and no special characters)
- Set is_official to True

All songs need difficulty (0-4) and characteristic (usually "Standard")
Currently, difficulty and characteristic are not utilized for anything, but they are required for future compatibility with potential logic that may want to differentiate between them.

options.label: Max Stars
options.description:
Maximum star rating for maps to be included in the pool, if using randomized map pools.
Some reference points, for those unfamiliar with star ratings:
Beat Saber Normal is 2.25 stars
Country Rounds Hard is 3.3 stars
Crab Rave Expert is 6.7 stars
$100 Bills Expert+ is 8.2 stars
Ghost Expert+ on the Camellia OST is 11.3 stars
Power of the Saber Blade Expert+ is 12.6 stars
Ov Sacrament Expert+ is 12.9 stars
The highest rated map on BeatLeader as of February 2025 is Unwelcome School at 15.9 stars

options.label: Song Sorting

Difficulty count means single difficulties go first and full spread maps go last. Difficulty sorting is ascending by default (easiest to hardest). Descending would be the opposite (hardest maps go first)

A Cheap is completing a song with less than a Standard clear.

options.label: Goal Mode
options.description:

Leeks: The original mode where you collect Leeks from the item pool.
Percent: Reach a percentage of checks done. More room in the item pool for other things.

options.label: Leek Percentage
options.description:
If Goal Mode is Leeks, the percentage of Leeks to add to the pool based on the total number of Starting and Additional Songs.
A higher available Leek percentage leads to more consistent game lengths, but individual Leeks will be less important.

Example: (5 Starting + 40 Additional Songs) * 20% Leeks Total = 9 Leeks will be available

Recommended values are between 10 and 40.
WARNING: Higher values, especially 100, are more suited for solo seeds to replicate the console progression experience.

options.label: Leek Percentage Needed to Win
options.description:
If Goal Mode is Leeks, the percentage of available Leeks in the item pool that are needed to unlock the Goal Song.

Example: (5 Starting + 40 Additional Songs) * 20% Leeks Total * 80% Leeks Needed = 7 out of 9 Leeks needed to goal

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Choose which goal should count as completing your game. For a first
playthrough, we recommend *Main Quest 7* which marks the end of the
original Outward story line with one of the *Peacemaker* quests or the
*A House Divided* quest.
- **Main Quest N:** Complete the *n*-th main quest in Outward: Definitive
Edition. *Main quest 7* is the end of the original story line, and *Main
quest 12* is the end of the Definitive Edition story line. These could be
different quests depending on which faction you choose, but all factions
have the same number of quests.
- **Blood Under the Sun Quest:** Complete the parallel quest *Blood Under
the Sun* by finding the culprit behind the assassination of Prince Jaden.
- **Purifier Quest:** Complete the parallel quest *Purifier* by
investigating rumors of trouble in the *Hallowed Marsh*.
- **Vendavel Quest:** Complete the parallel quest *Vendavel Quest* by
preventing the destruction of *Cierzo*.
- **Rust and Vengeance:** Complete the parallel quest *Rust and Vengeance*
by foiling the *Rust Lich*'s plans to destroy Harmattan.

options.label: Difficulty
options.description:
What tricks will be factored into the game's logic.
Intended means that if an item makes a level easier in any way, it is required for logic.
Simple means that easily skippable items will not be required for logic.
Advanced means that any skippable items will not be required for logic.
Glitched means that any skippable items including glitches will not be required for logic.

options.label: Open World
options.description:
How open the world is.
Closed means each level is unlocked individually.
Partial means standard exits are unlocked at the start.
Boss and Secret exits still need to be unlocked.
Open means that everything besides boss exits are unlocked at the start.
The Scenic Route's exit is also an exception.
Full means that all exits are unlocked at the start.

options.label: Paths
options.description:
How are Paths between levels unlocked.
Vanilla means that beating a level will unlock its corresponding path.
Randomized means that each level path will be an item in the pool.
Progressive means that progressive path items will be added to the pool.
While normal paths will be unlocked with Progressive Paths, 
paths to and from secret levels will be unlocked with Progressive Secret Paths.

options.label: Door Rando

Two way doors are always excluded from door rando.
Full means that any door can lead to any other door.
Balanced means that any door can lead to any other door,
but levels will always have the same number of rooms as they had originaly.
Restricted means that doors can lead to any other door in the same level.
Disabled means that doors will not be randomized.

options.label: Default Item Groups
options.description:
How items will be grouped together by default.
To use Pop Blocks as an example:
Separated item groups means Standard Pop Blocks and Galactic Pop Blocks will be added to the pool.
Collecting each one will unlock its corresponding item.
Progressive item groups means two Progressive Pop Blocks will be added to the pool.
Collecting the first will unlock Standard Pop Blocks, and the second will unlock Galactic Pop Blocks.
Grouped item groups means Pop Blocks will be added to the pool.
Collecting it will unlock both Standard Pop Blocks and Galactic Pop Blocks.
Precollected item groups means no items will be added to the pool.
Both Standard Pop Blocks and Galactic Pop Blocks will be unlocked from the start.

options.label: Default Extra Items
options.description:
Whether extra items are included by default.
How these extra items are added is dependent on the item's grouping.
To use Skull Rings as an example:
Separated item groups will have two Yellow Skull Rings, and two Blue Skull Rings in the pool.
Collecting the first of each will let you stop the corresponding Skull Ring from moving.
Collecting the second of each will neutralize the corresponding Skull Ring.
Progressive item groups will add a third additional Progressive Skull Ring to the pool.
Collecting the third Progressive Skull Ring will neutralize both types of Skull Rings.
Grouped item groups will add a second additional Skull Rings to the pool.
Collecting the second Skull Rings will neutralize both types of Skull Rings.
Precollected item groups means no items will be added to the pool.
Both types of Skull Rings will be neutralized from the start.

options.label: Enabled DLCs
options.description:
List of enabled DLCs. Per default, all DLCs except for docklands are enabled.

Valid keys: 'sunken-treasures', 'botanica', 'the-passage', 'seat-of-power', 'bright-harvest', 'land-of-lions',
