options.label: Enable Docklands Logic
options.description:
Per default, docklands outputs will not be included in the randomizer logic. Turn this on to include them.
Leads to short and simple randomizers since docklands can supply pretty much everything before skyscrapers and
artistas.
Has no effect unless the Docklands DLC is enabled.

options.label: Enforce Cape Trelawney
options.description:
Select whether Cape Trelawney should be enforced at a certain point in the game or not.
Has no effect unless the Sunken Treasures DLC is enabled.

Off: Cape Trelawney is fully optional. You might never reach it.

By Artisans: The Cape Trelawney expedition will be completable before you require artisans.

By Engineers: The Cape Trelawney expedition will be completable before you require engineers.

By Investors: The Cape Trelawney expedition will be completable before you require investors.

options.label: Enable Progressive Unlocks
options.description:
Per default, all upgradable buildings and monuments are found as progressive unlocks, meaning there are multiple of
the same item that progressively unlock the upgrade levels / stages.
When this is turned off, it is common that an early upgrade level is placed late in the game while later upgrades
are placed early, meaning you can often only upgrade later, but then all at once.
For non-tiered residences, this normally will progress the regular upgrade path (e.g. Engineer -> Investor).
For tiered residences, this normally will progress the tiered upgrade path (e.g. Skyscraper Level 1 -> Level 2).

options.label: Hint Mode
options.description:
Determines the kind of hints Anno 1800 will send out. Hints will be shown for all items for which the game would
usually display an unlock requirement - that means visible, but not unlocked buildings in the build menu as well as
upgrades to any buildings.
Per default, send hints about local items only since those are shown ingame anyways.

Off: Don't send any hints

Local: Send hints only for items that are available to unlock in Anno 1800.

Global: Send hints for all items that are visible, but not unlocked.

options.label: Start with Flagship
options.description:
Per default, the starting flagship will not be included in the randomizer logic. If you intend to start with a
flagship, turn this on to tell the randomizer you have a decent expedition ship from the start.

If you start with one of the fleets, you will have some out-of-logic ships.

options.label: Start with Trading Post
options.description:
Per default, the randomizer assumes you start with a trading post. If you intend to start without one, turn this
off. Important: DO NOT settle on an island without a clay and an iron deposit or you may get stuck.

options.label: Required Street for Settling
options.description:
Sets which level of street must be availablee for the randomizer to assume ability to settle. Only affects the
New World.

Basic: The dirt road must be available.

Upgraded: The dirt road or the paved street must be available. Often requires shipping many bricks to the New World.

Hacienda: The dirt road or any of the two hacienda streets must be available. Hacienda streets are limited to 999
squares, which makes settling very restrictive and likely makes settling multiple islands required. Same as Basic
unless the Seeds of Change DLC is enabled.

Hacienda and Upgraded: The dirt road, paved street or any of the two hacienda streets must be available. Same as
Upgraded unless the Seeds of Change DLC is enabled.

options.label: Allow Hacienda Residences upon Unlock
options.description:
Per default, Hacienda residences must not only be unlocked, but their corresponding regular residence also has to be
built at least once first. By turning this on, they will be buildable as soon as they are unlocked. This often
results in skipping most of the New World goods as these residences allow the randomizer to progress without
fulfilling the needs of the New World populations.

options.label: Incident Difficulty
options.description:
Select how challenging incidents (fire, riots, illness) should be. Can be combined independently with the ingame
setting to adjust difficulty to your liking. If you intend to disable incidents, use the brutal option below to
remove the responder buildings from logic alltogether.

Easy: Incidents unlock once you have unlocked the responder building and had enough materials to build them in 
storage at least once. They are guaranteed to be available before upgrading to the tier of population after the
one they would unlock with in vanilla.

Normal: Incidents unlock once you have unlocked the responder building. They are guaranteed to be available before
upgrading to the tier of population after the one they would unlock with in vanilla.

Challenging: Incidents unlock once you reach the local incident requirement. They are guaranteed to be available
before upgrading to the tier of population after the one they would unlock with in vanilla.

Brutal: Incidents unlock once you reach the local incident requirement. There are no guarantees about ever
unlocking the responder building.

options.label: Free Goods and Ships
options.description:
Determines what goods and ships and how many you receive for free at game start and when entering sessions for the
first time.

Minimal: Close to the minimum required to beat the game (only game start wood and Enbesa starting goods)

In Logic: Only receive goods and ships that are in logic. If you started with a flagship and didn't unlock any ships
yet, you may end up empty-handed. Otherwise, unavailable goods are replace with timber and ships are downgraded to
the next-largest option available (min. Schooner for Enbesa).

In Logic Generous: As 'In Logic', but with more goods and ships.

Vanilla: No change to vanilla Anno 1800. May allow skipping some logic.

Generous: As 'Vanilla', but with more goods and ships.

options.label: Required Monuments
options.description:
Each of the monuments in this list must be built to win the randomizer.
Monuments that are not available in the DLCs selected in 'Enabled DLCs' will be ignored.
Find the Skyline Tower under 'Required Skyscrapers' instead as it is also a residence.

Valid keys: 'worlds-fair', 'research-institute', 'arctic-airship-hangar', 'the-iron-tower',
'ow-rigid-airship-hangar', 'nw-rigid-airship-hangar', 'dam', 'grand-stadium'

options.label: Enable Mine Slot Unification (Taludas)
options.description:
Enables support for the mod 'Mine Slot Unification (Taludas)'.

Removes the requirement for settling other islands from mines in the Old World.

options.label: Exclude Locations
options.description: Prevent these locations from having an important item.
default: (Build 1 OW: Cafe) THEN (Have 1 Elephant Enclosure (Zoo, Eastern Elephant or Elephant)) (OW: Cafe: Palmier Biscuit)

(Build 1 OW: The Iron Tower) THEN (Hidden quest: Complete the set 'Polar Circle' in an OW: Zoo (Arctic Fox, Great Auk, Narwhal, Polar Bear, Ringed Seal, Walrus)) (OW: The Iron Tower: Age of Exploration)
(Build 1 OW: The Iron Tower) THEN (Hidden quest: Socket a 'Lobsterman' in a Harbourmaster's Office in Enbesa) (OW: The Iron Tower: Homard Lit de Terroir)
(Build 1 OW: Furniture Store) THEN (Complete the set 'Eastern Jungle' in an OW: Zoo (Eastern Elephant, Chital, Eastern Water Buffalo, Crocodile, Peacock, Tiger)) (OW: Furniture Store: Vanity Screens)
(Build 1 OW: Drug Store) THEN (Complete the set 'Icebound' in an OW: Museum (Collection Of Lost Expedition Relics, Frozen Woolly Mammoth, Wolf Pup Mummy)) (OW: Drug Store: Face Cream)
Build 25 OW: Investor Skyscraper: Level 5 (OW: Skyline Tower: Foundations)
Build 40 OW: Investor Skyscraper: Level 5 (OW: Skyline Tower: Superstructure)
Build 55 OW: Investor Skyscraper: Level 5 (OW: Skyline Tower: Glazing)
Build 75 OW: Investor Skyscraper: Level 5 (OW: Skyline Tower)
(Build 1 OW: Drug Store) THEN (Build 40 OW: Investor Skyscraper: Level 5) (OW: Drug Store: Detergent)

options.label: Pickupsanity
options.description: Whether collecting freestanding 1ups, HP and Weapon Energy capsules will grant a check.

options.label: Character
options.description:
Choose which character you'd like to play as during your seed
NOTE: If Zero, certain locations are excluded to prevent unbeatable seeds.

options.label: Damage Link
options.description: Share damage with other players through DamageLink.

options.label: Energy Link
options.description: Enable EnergyLink support. When enabled, the client can spend EnergyLink to restore current HP.

options.label: DeathLink Amnesty
options.description:
Number of lives to restore after sending or receiving a DeathLink.
This prevents DeathLink from immediately causing repeated game overs.
Receiving the EX Tank will increase this by 2.

options.label: Energy Link Auto Heal
options.description: Automatically spend EnergyLink to heal missing HP during gameplay.

options.label: Energy Link Cost Per HP
options.description: EnergyLink cost for each HP point restored by auto heal.

options.label: Infinite Nova Strike
options.description:
Lock Nova Strike / Giga Attack energy to full while in-game.
This writes 0x30 to the Nova Strike energy RAM value every client tick.

options.label: Enable Boss Item Requirements
options.description: Whether to enable item requirements for bosses

options.label: Web Spider Requirement
options.description:
A list of items required in logic to beat Web Spider
for example: { Twin Slasher: 1, Heart Tank: 2 }

options.label: Cyber Peacock Requirement
options.description:
A list of items required in logic to beat Cyber Peacock
for example: { Soul Body: 1, Heart Tank: 2 }

options.label: Storm Owl Requirement
options.description:
A list of items required in logic to beat Storm Owl
for example: { Aiming Laser: 1, Heart Tank: 2 }

options.label: Magma Dragoon Requirement
options.description:
A list of items required in logic to beat Magma Dragoon
for example: { Double Cyclone: 1, Heart Tank: 2 }

options.label: Jet Stingray Requirement
options.description:
A list of items required in logic to beat Jet Stingray
for example: { Frost Tower: 1, Heart Tank: 2 }

options.label: Split Mushroom Requirement
options.description:
A list of items required in logic to beat Split Mushroom
for example: { Lightning Web: 1, Heart Tank: 2 }

options.label: Slash Beast Requirement
options.description:
A list of items required in logic to beat Slash Beast
for example: { Ground Hunter: 1, Heart Tank: 2 }

options.label: Frost Walrus Requirement
options.description:
A list of items required in logic to beat Frost Walrus
for example: { Rising Fire: 1, Heart Tank: 2 }

options.label: Double/Iris Requirement
options.description:
A list of items required in logic to beat Double/Iris
for example: { Rising Fire: 1, Heart Tank: 4 }

options.label: General Requirement
options.description:
A list of items required in logic to beat General
for example: { Soul Body: 1, Heart Tank: 4 }

options.label: Sigma Requirement
Trap Chance
options.description:
Percentage chance for non-progression item slots to contain traps.
Set to 0 to disable traps entirely.

options.label: Trap Types
options.description: Which categories of trap may appear in your item pool. Has no effect unless "Trap Chance" is above 0.

options.label: Allowed Item Types
options.description:
Which categories of optional (non-progression) give items may appear in your item pool. Removing a
category keeps all of its items out of your pool.

Defaults to "Permanent Patches" only; add the others to put their gives in your pool.

Valid categories are:
- "Permanent Patches"
- "City Trial Item Gives"
- "City Trial Event Gives"
- "Copy Ability Gives"
- "Top Ride Item Gives"

options.label: Trap Link
options.description:
When on, traps you receive in-game are broadcast to other TrapLink players and you receive theirs.
Independent of "Trap Chance".

options.label: Spawn Rate Min
options.description:
Starting item spawn rate percent. The rate climbs from here as "Spawn Rate Up" items are received
(+10% each); set it equal to "Spawn Rate Max" for a flat rate with no such items.

options.label: Spawn Rate Max
options.description:
Item spawn rate ceiling percent, reached after collecting every "Spawn Rate Up" item; the pool
contains (max - min) / 10 of them. Snapped to the nearest multiple of 10. Applies to City Trial
and Top Ride.

options.label: Energy Link
options.description:
Enables EnergyLink: collecting patches or destroying objects in City Trial sends energy to the
Multiworld's shared pool, which you can spend on patches or other items.

options.label: Checklist Rewards
options.description:
Which categories of the game's vanilla checklist rewards (red boxes) are placed as items into the
multiworld. Valid categories are:

- "Sound Test": sound test entries
- "Music": course and stadium music tracks
- "Filler Boxes": boxes awarding a checkbox filler
- "Endings": the ending movie for each mode
- "Gameplay Extras": Top Ride extra rules, Air Ride's Special Machine Intros, City Trial's pause-screen
  power-up display

Only categories you specify are added to the pool. Others are left out, and automatically unlocked in-game
from the start. In-game checklists will not contain these items.

Other reward categories are gated by other options. This option only covers the categories above.

options.label: Non-Progression Checkboxes
options.description:
What happens to a checkbox whose category is not selected in its mode's "Progression" option.

- Excluded: it stays a location but only ever holds filler. You can still fill it in-game and it
  still sends its check.
- Removed: it is not a location at all. Nothing is placed there and filling it in-game sends
  nothing. It still counts toward "fill in N checklist blocks" goals.

Boxes named in a "checklist_list" goal are always kept, even when their category is unselected.

options.label: City Trial Goal
options.description:
Sets the goal for City Trial.

- 100 Checklist Blocks: Get the checkbox for getting 100 checkboxes in the City Trial Checklist
- N Checklist Blocks: Get the specified number of checkboxes
- Hydra and Dragoon: Get the checkbox for assembling Hydra and Dragoon in a single CT run
- Beat King DeDeDe: Get the checkbox for defeating King DeDeDe in under a minute
- Checklist List: Specify a custom list of City Trial checkboxes (locations) to complete
- Max Stats in One Run: Get max stats for every patch in one CT run

Select "None" to disable City Trial.

options.label: Number of Checklist Boxes for City Trial
options.description: This sets the number of checklist boxes for the 'Fill in N Checklist blocks!' goal for City Trial.

options.label: City Trial Goal Locations
options.description:
The specific checklist locations required for the "checklist_list" goal in City Trial.
Only used when City Trial Goal is set to "checklist_list". Supports location group names.

options.label: City Trial Progression Categories
options.description:
Which extra categories of City Trial checkboxes may hold progression items.

- "High Effort": long grinds or high difficulty, such as breaking 1000 boxes
- "Multiplayer": boxes that need a second player
- "Free Run": Free Run boxes
- "Bust Vehicle on Vehicle": busting one machine with another
- "RNG: Events": City Trial events
- "RNG: Food": getting X food items in one run
- "RNG: Copy Chance Wheel": copy abilities from the wheel

Categories you leave out are excluded from progression, or removed from your world completely,
decided by the "Non-Progression Checkboxes".

options.label: City Trial Checkbox Fillers
options.description:
Number of "checkbox filler" items added to pool for the City Trial Checklist.
Set to 0 to disable.

options.label: City Trial Reveal Checklist
options.description:
If enabled, the City Trial checklist starts off completely revealed.
Revealing is visual only: it does not complete or unlock anything.

options.label: Patch Cap Min
options.description:
Per-stat patch cap the player starts with (18 = vanilla). The cap climbs from here as "Patch Cap
Increase" items are received (+1 each); set it equal to "Patch Cap Max" for a flat cap with none.

options.label: Patch Cap Max
options.description:
Per-stat patch cap ceiling (18 = vanilla), reached after collecting every "Patch Cap Increase"
item; the pool contains (max - min) of them. Also the per-stat threshold for the
"max_stats_in_one_run" goal.

options.label: City Trial Stadiums Gated
options.description:
When enabled, City Trial stadiums are locked and must be unlocked by finding their
corresponding Unlock Stadium items.

When disabled, every stadium is available from the start and no Unlock Stadium items are added to the
pool.

options.label: Starting Stadium
options.description:
The City Trial stadium unlocked from the start.

Only applies when City Trial is enabled and "City Trial Stadiums Gated" is on; otherwise ignored.
VS. KING DEDEDE cannot be picked when it is your City Trial goal.

options.label: AP Patches
options.description:
Number of AP Patches in the seed. AP Patches drop from Archipelago boxes in City Trial.
Every AP patch collected is a check, and any rider can collect one, even CPUs.

Use this to add more locations to the world that can hold items.

Set to 0 to disable AP patches.

options.label: AP Patch Placement
options.description:
Whether AP Patch locations can hold progression.

- Default: treated like any other location.
- Excluded: filler only.

options.label: Air Ride Goal
options.description:
Sets the goal for Air Ride.

- 100 Checklist Blocks: Get the checkbox for getting 100 checkboxes in the Air Ride Checklist
- N Checklist Blocks: Get the specified number of checkboxes
- Checklist List: Specify a custom list of Air Ride checkboxes (locations) to complete

Select "None" to disable Air Ride.

options.label: Number of Checklist Boxes for Air Ride
options.description: This sets the number of checklist boxes for the 'Fill in N Checklist blocks!' goal for Air Ride.

options.label: Air Ride Goal Locations
options.description:
The specific checklist locations required for the "checklist_list" goal in Air Ride.
Only used when Air Ride Goal is set to "checklist_list". Supports location group names.

options.label: Air Ride Progression Categories
options.description:
Which extra categories of Air Ride checkboxes may hold progression items.

- "High Effort": long grinds or high difficulty, such as gliding for an hour or racing 300 laps
- "Free Run": Free Run boxes
- "Time Attack": Time Attack boxes
- "RNG: Rivals": boxes that depend on what your rivals happen to do

Categories you leave out are excluded from progression, or removed from your world completely,
decided by the "Non-Progression Checkboxes".

options.label: Air Ride Checkbox Fillers
options.description:
Number of "checkbox filler" items added to the pool for the Air Ride Checklist.
Set to 0 to disable.

options.label: Air Ride Reveal Checklist
options.description:
If enabled, the Air Ride checklist starts off completely revealed.
Revealing is visual only: it does not complete or unlock anything.

options.label: Top Ride Goal
options.description:
Sets the goal for Top Ride.

- 100 Checklist Blocks: Get the checkbox for getting 100 checkboxes in the Top Ride Checklist
- N Checklist Blocks: Get the specified number of checkboxes
- Checklist List: Specify a custom list of Top Ride checkboxes (locations) to complete

Select "None" to disable Top Ride.

options.label: Number of Checklist Boxes for Top Ride
options.description: This sets the number of checklist boxes for the 'Fill in N Checklist blocks!' goal for Top Ride.

options.label: Top Ride Goal Locations
options.description:
The specific checklist locations required for the "checklist_list" goal in Top Ride.
Only used when Top Ride Goal is set to "checklist_list". Supports location group names.

options.label: Top Ride Progression Categories
options.description:
Which extra categories of Top Ride checkboxes may hold progression items.

- "High Effort": long grinds or high difficulty, such as racing 300 laps
- "Free Run": Free Run boxes
- "Time Attack": Time Attack boxes
- "Multiplayer": boxes that need multiple players

Categories you leave out are excluded from progression, or removed from your world completely,
decided by the "Non-Progression Checkboxes".

options.label: Top Ride Checkbox Fillers
options.description:
Number of "checkbox filler" items added to the pool for the Top Ride Checklist.
Set to 0 to disable.

options.label: Top Ride Reveal Checklist
options.description:
If enabled, the Top Ride checklist starts off completely revealed instead of filling in around
the squares you complete. Revealing is visual only: it does not complete or unlock anything.

options.label: Archipelago Checklist Goal
options.description:
EXPERIMENTAL - ONLY USE IF YOU WANT TO TEST - SOME CHECKS LIKELY BROKEN
Sets the goal for the Archipelago checklist.

- N Checklist Blocks: Get the specified number of checkboxes in the Archipelago Checklist
- Checklist List: Specify a custom list of Archipelago checkboxes (locations) to complete
- Assemble Archipelago Star: Assemble the Archipelago Star Legendary Machine in one CT run
- Assemble All Three Legendaries in One Run: Assemble all 3 legendary machines in one CT run

Select "None" to exclude archipelago checklist locations completely.

choices.label: All Three Legendaries In One Run

options.label: Number of Checklist Boxes for Archipelago
options.description:
This sets the number of checklist boxes for the 'Fill in N Checklist blocks!' goal for the
Archipelago checklist.

The Archipelago checklist holds fewer boxes than the other modes, so the range stops at what
the checklist actually has rather than the grid's 120 cells.

options.label: Archipelago Goal Locations
options.description:
The specific checklist locations required for the "checklist_list" goal on the Archipelago
checklist. Only used when Archipelago Checklist Goal is set to "checklist_list". Supports location
group names.

options.label: Archipelago Progression Categories
options.description:
Which extra categories of Archipelago checklist checkboxes may hold progression items.

- "High Effort": long grinds or high difficulty, such as assembling all three legendary machines
- "RNG: Food": get x food items in one run boxes
- "RNG: Copy Chance Wheel": copy abilities from the wheel
- "RNG: Rivals": boxes that depend on what your rivals happen to do

Categories you leave out are excluded from progression, or removed from your world completely,
decided by the "Non-Progression Checkboxes".

options.label: Archipelago Checkbox Fillers
options.description:
Number of "checkbox filler" items added to the pool for the Archipelago checklist.
Set to 0 to disable.

options.label: Archipelago Reveal Checklist
options.description:
If enabled, the Archipelago checklist starts off completely revealed.
Revealing is visual only: it does not complete or unlock anything.

options.label: City Trial Events Gated
options.description:
When enabled, City Trial events (Dyna Blade, Meteor, Tac, etc.) are locked and must be
unlocked by finding their corresponding items.

When disabled, all events are available from the start and no event unlock items are added to
the pool.

options.label: Copy Abilities Gated
options.description:
When enabled, copy abilities (Fire, Sword, Bomb, etc.) are locked and must be unlocked
by finding their corresponding items.

When disabled, all copy abilities are available from the start and no ability unlock items are
added to the pool.

options.label: Base Abilities Gated
options.description:
When enabled, base abilities - inhale, quick spin, and machine charge - start locked and must
each be unlocked by finding their item.

When disabled, all three moves are available from the start and no base ability unlock items are
added to the pool.

options.label: City Trial Patch Types Gated
options.description:
When enabled, patch stat types (Boost, Top Speed, Offense, etc.) are locked and must be
unlocked by finding their corresponding items.

When disabled, all patch stat types are available from the start and no patch type unlock items
are added to the pool.

options.label: City Trial Items Gated
options.description:
When enabled, City Trial items (All Up, Speed Max, Candy, food, legendary parts, etc.)
are locked and must be unlocked by finding their corresponding items.

When disabled, all game items are available from the start and no item unlock items are added to
the pool.

options.label: Machines Gated
options.description:
When enabled, air ride machines are locked and must be unlocked by finding their
corresponding items. Applies to all modes.

When disabled, all machines are available from the start and no machine unlock items are added
to the pool.

options.label: Starting Machine
options.description:
The machine unlocked unlocked from the start.

Only applies when "Machines Gated" is on and City Trial or Air Ride is enabled; otherwise ignored.

With "Base Abilities Gated" on, Bulk, Slick and Turbo Star cannot be picked.

options.label: Starting Top Ride Machine
options.description:
The Top Ride machine unlocked from the start.

Only applies when "Machines Gated" is on and Top Ride is enabled; otherwise ignored.

options.label: City Trial Boxes Gated
options.description:
When enabled, box types (Blue, Green, Red) are locked and must be unlocked by finding
their corresponding items.

Boxes will still not spawn if none of their containing items are unlocked yet.

When disabled, all box types are available from the start and no box unlock items are added to
the pool.

options.label: Air Ride Courses Gated
options.description:
When enabled, Air Ride courses are locked and must be unlocked by finding their
corresponding items.

When disabled, all Air Ride courses are available from the start and no course unlock items are
added to the pool.

options.label: Starting Air Ride Course
options.description:
The Air Ride course unlocked from the start.

Only applies when Air Ride is enabled and "Air Ride Courses Gated" is on; otherwise ignored.

options.label: Kirby Colors Gated
options.description:
When enabled, Kirby colors are locked and must be unlocked by finding their corresponding
items.

When disabled, all Kirby colors are available from the start and no color unlock items are added
to the pool.

options.label: Starting Kirby Color
options.description:
The Kirby color unlocked from the start.

Only applies when "Kirby Colors Gated" is on; otherwise ignored.

options.label: Top Ride Courses Gated
options.description:
When enabled, Top Ride courses are locked and must be unlocked by finding their
corresponding items.

When disabled, all Top Ride courses are available from the start and no course unlock items are
added to the pool.

options.label: Starting Top Ride Course
options.description:
The Top Ride course unlocked from the start.

Only applies when Top Ride is enabled and "Top Ride Courses Gated" is on; otherwise ignored.

options.label: Top Ride Items Gated
options.description:
When enabled, Top Ride items are locked and must be unlocked by finding their
corresponding items.

The four items tied to copy abilities (Freeze Fan, Fire, Bomb, Walky) are additionally unlocked
by the copy ability unlock items.

When disabled, all Top Ride items are available from the start and no item unlock items are added
to the pool.

options.label: Deathlink
options.description: When you die (whole party wipes), everyone dies. And vice versa

options.label: Goal Type
options.description: normal: win game on normal difficulty. pearls: collect N pearls. brutal_orchestra: get achievement Brutal Orchestra (100%).

options.label: Pearl Count
options.description: Pearl amount to win

options.label: Long Locations
options.description: Enable long locations (Winstreak, Quests Bronzo/Mordrake/Director, 100%).

options.label: Ability Sanity
options.description: Randomize amount of slots in the pool. 2 Progressive Ability per charachter.

options.label: Far Shore Battles
options.description: Number of regular battles in Far Shore.

options.label: Orpheum Battles
options.description: Number of regular battles in Orpheum.

options.label: Far Shore Money Chests
options.description: Number of money chests in Far Shore.

options.label: Orpheum Money Chests
options.description: Number of money chests in Orpheum.

options.label: Far Shore Artifact Chests
options.description: Number of artifact chests in Far Shore.

options.label: Orpheum Artifact Chests
options.description: Number of artifact chests in Orpheum.

options.label: Far Shore Shop Checks
options.description: Number of shop checks in Far Shore.

options.label: Orpheum Shop Checks
options.description: Number of shop checks in Orpheum.

options.label: Buy Fool Count
options.description: Number of Fool shop locations.

options.label: Hardmode
options.description: Enable hardmode (Garden) locations and items.

options.label: Garden Battles
options.description: Number of battles in the Garden.

options.label: Garden Money Chests
options.description: Number of money chests in the Garden.

options.label: Garden Artifact Chests
options.description: Number of artifact chests in the Garden.

options.label: Progressive Start Money items
options.description: Number of Progressive Start Money items in the pool. Each adds +10 starting coins.

options.label: Starting Soul Color
options.description: Determines which soul color the player will be when the run is started. If combined with Door Keys, the starting route's key will be given to you.

options.label: Door Keys
options.description: Blocks the ability to enter doors without the corresponding key. Adds additional checks for completing routes for these door.

options.label: Dragon's Power Gem Requirement
options.description: Determines the percentage of gems required to beat the dragon.

options.label: Cosmetics
options.description: Add cosmetics and their locations to the pool.

options.label: Battle Rewards
options.description:
Chooses what battles will be added to the randomization. Their Battles and xps will be added.
- Major Battles: Unique Battles which are fought on the main path of any route.
- Unique Battles: Battles which feature a unique character.
- All Battles: All non-spaceship battles.

options.label: Include Hillbert Hotel
options.description:
Whether to include the Hillbert Hotel and its rooms, keys, battles and items to the pool.

If Battle Rewards is enabled, Hillbert Hotel battles will be included.

options.label: Randomise Color Reflects
options.description:
Determines if you can reflect all colors of projectiles, or whether you need to get an item first.
- Off: Can reflect any projectile back to enemies.
- Single: Reflecting a color requires only a Soul Piece of that color.
- Multiple: Color requirements scale based on which hub the fight is connected to. Cosmic Hub = 1, Time Hub = 2, Infinity Hub = 3

options.label: Prevent Dragon 3
options.description: When enabled, Dragon 3 will no longer appear if you fight the dragon after completing only a single starting zone.

options.label: Health Multiplier Percentage
options.description: Multiplies the Health of *ALL* enemies.

options.label: Completion Condition
options.description:
Chooses the completion condition of the game.
- Dragon is the final multi-phase fight of the Cosmic Hub
- Judge Creation is the final fight of the Time Hub
- Riley is the final fight of the game.
- Cat Gods Hairball is the final fight of the colloseum.

options.label: Mission Reward Multiplier
options.description:
How many item checks each mission/arena/rank objective awards.
At 4x the seed uses nearly the entire part catalogue, leaving little
variety between seeds. Lower values give more rotation per seed.

options.label: Run Mode
options.description:
How many New Game cycles the run spans, and whether each cycle has its
own set of checks.

single:             one playthrough, any ending completes the goal.

options.label: Shop Checks
options.description:
Add shop purchases as check locations. Shop slots absorb any remaining
parts after mission/arena/rank locations are filled, up to 300 slots
across 4 chapters. Slot mapping is sent via slot_data; no per-seed files
are needed. Shop checks are cycle-agnostic and fire exactly once.

options.label: Mercenary Rank Checks
options.description:
How many mercenary rank checks to include (0-15).
Order: 1 -> 2 -> ... -> 15. Set to 0 to disable.

NOTE: some of the Combat Logs that feed Mercenary Rank are locked to
NG+/NG++ mission variants, so rank 15 cannot be reached in a single
playthrough. Defaulted to 0 until the real single-run cap is confirmed;
raise it at your own risk of an uncompletable seed.

options.label: Arena Checks
options.description:
How many arena checks to include (0-7).
Order: 1=F -> 2=E -> 3=D -> 4=C -> 5=B -> 6=A -> 7=S
Set to 0 to disable.

NOTE: the Alpha, Beta, and Gamma Simulator fights are NG++-only and are
disabled for now (single-run only). They'll return once multi-cycle
support does.

options.label: Goal
options.description: The victory condition for your run

options.label: Shuffle characters
options.description: Shuffles characters into the item pool.

options.label: Shuffle Free Aim
options.description: Shuffles the ability to shoot outside of battle into the pool.

options.label: Exclude Endgame Locations
options.description:
Determines how to handle locations higher level than the set goal, if the goal is Paintress or Curator.
Excluded: Locations won't be added to the pool.
Filler: Locations will only contain filler items.
Included: All locations are included.

options.label: Exclude Endless Tower
options.description:
Determines how to handle Endless Tower locations.
Excluded: Locations won't be added to the pool.
Filler: Locations will only contain filler items.
Included: All locations are included.

options.label: Exclude Superbosses
options.description:
Determines how to handle Superbosses (the four in the Endless Tower).
Excluded: Locations won't be added to the pool.
Filler: Locations will only contain filler items.
Included: All locations are included.

options.label: Shuffle Lost Gestrals
options.description: Shuffles the lost gestrals into the item pool.

options.label: Starting character
options.description: Determines which character you start with. Does nothing if Shuffle Characters is set to false.

options.label: Gear Scaling
options.description:
How the levels of pictos and weapons you receive are determined.
Sphere placement: Roughly scales pictos/weapons by the logical sphere they're placed in.
Order received: As you receive more pictos/weapons, the levels of the next ones you receive will go up.
Balanced random: Pictos/weapons have random levels assigned in an even spread.
Full random: Exaclty what it says. There's no guarantee that you'll get high-level pictos... but you probably will.

options.label: Max Equipment Level
options.description:
What level pictos and weapons received though Archipelago will go up to. Weapons can still be upgraded past this.
Highest Included Location: The highest level equipment will match the gear you would normally get from the most
difficult location included in the pool. With endgame locations excluded, this will be 15 with Paintress as your
goal, 16 for Curator, 28 for Clea, or 33 for Simon or Painted Love.
Custom: Set a specific level.

options.label: Custom Max Equipment Level
options.description: What level pictos and weapons received through Archipelago will go up to if Max Equip Level is set to Custom.

options.label: Area logic
options.description:
Determines how many major area unlock items will be placed how early.
Normal: Act 1 major areas won't be placed past Act 1; Forgotten Battlefield and Old Lumiere won't be placed behind
Visages/Sirene; Visages and Sirene won't be placed behind The Monolith.
Hard: Only half of the major areas will be placed in those segments.
No Logic: Areas could be anywhere. You may need to grind world map enemies for a long time.

options.label: Trap Chance
options.description:
The chance for any filler item to be replaced with a trap.
Currently, the only implemented trap is the Feet Trap.
Feet Trap: plays the "My, what lovely feet" voice line and shows you some feet pics. Are you sure about this....?

options.label: Chroma pack type
options.description:
Random fixed range: Choses ONE random number between range option. The Chroma pack will always be this value
Random range: The client chose one random value between the range option. If you rerun the same seed, the client can give different value.

options.label: Min Chroma Pack
options.description: How much the filler: "Chroma Pack" can give chroma at minimum. If you have Shopsanity, i suggest to have a high range of chroma pack.

options.label: Max Chroma Pack
options.description: How much the filler: "Chroma Pack" can give chroma at maximum. If you have Shopsanity, i suggest to have a high range of chroma pack.

options.label: Shop Sanity
options.description: Add shop items to location pool.

options.label: Location Per Shop
options.description: How many locations are in each shop. Does nothing if Shopsanity is disabled.

options.label: Fighting Merchant
options.description:
If enabled, fighting merchant gives a check. Otherwise it will unlock extra items in shop like in vanilla.
Also, if enabled, you need to find your merchant unlock in the pool to unlock extra items in shop

options.label: Extra Location Per Shop
options.description: How many locations are in each extra shop (when fighting/having the extra shop item).

options.label: Minimum Price Shop
options.description: How much the price of location shop is at minimum

options.label: Maximum Price Shop
options.description: How much the price of location shop is at maximum. If it's below the minimum, the max price will be equals to the minimum price

options.label: Show Shop Items
options.description:
Show clearly what the item in shop location is (progressive, item for which player).
Extra shop locations are hidden until your have the corresponding item to unlock them.

options.label: Create Hint Automatically
options.description:
Create a hint for shop items. If the Show shop items is disabled, it will also create hint.
To create hint for extra shop locations, it's an another option

options.label: Create Hint Automatically for Extra items
options.description: Create a hint for extra shop items. Can be useful to know what's behind them

options.label: Start Inventory
options.description: Start with these items

worlds.game: The Legend of Zelda - Oracle of Seasons

options.label: Goal
options.description:
The goal to accomplish in order to complete the seed.
- Beat Onox: beat the usual final boss (same as vanilla)
- Beat Ganon: teleport to the Room of Rites after beating Onox, then beat Ganon (same as linked game)

options.label: Logic Difficulty
options.description:
The difficulty of the logic used to generate the seed.
- Casual: expects you to know what you would know when playing the game for the first time
- Medium: expects you to know well the alternatives on how to do basic things, but won't expect any trick
- Hard: expects you to know difficult tricks such as bomb jumps
- Hell: expects you to use tricks and glitches that span over more than a few inputs

options.label: Death Link
options.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

options.label: Open Advance Shop
options.description:
In the vanilla game, there is a house northwest of Horon Village hosting the secret "Advance Shop" that can only
be accessed if the game is being played on a Game Boy Advance console.
If enabled, this option makes this shop always open, adding 3 shop locations to the game (and some rupees to the
item pool to compensate for the extra purchases that might be required)

options.label: Rupee Old Men
options.description:
Determine how the Old Men which give or take rupees are handled by the randomizer.
- Vanilla: Each Old Man gives/takes the amount of rupees it usually does in the base game
- Shuffled Values: The amount of given/taken rupees are shuffled between Old Men
- Random Values: Each Old Man will give or take a random amount of rupees
- Random Positive Values: Each Old Man will give a random amount of rupees, but never make you pay
- Turn Into Locations: Each Old Man becomes a randomized check, and the total amount of rupees they usually give
  in vanilla is shuffled into the item pool

options.label: Shuffle Business Scrubs
options.description:
This option adds the 4 accessible business scrubs (Spool Swamp, Samasa Desert, D2, D4) to the pool of randomized
locations. Just like any other shop, they ask for rupees in exchange of the randomized item,
which can only be purchased once.
Please note that scrubs inside dungeons can hold dungeon items, such as keys.

options.label: Shuffle Golden Ore Spots
options.description:
This option adds the 7 hidden digging spots in Subrosia (containing 50 Ore Chunks each) to the pool
of randomized locations.

options.label: Deterministic Gasha Locations
options.description:
When set to a non-zero value, planting a Gasha tree on a unique soil gives a deterministic item which is taken
into account by logic. Once an item has been obtained this way, the soil disappears forever to avoid any chance
of softlocking by wasting several Gasha Seeds on the same soil.
The value of this option is the number of items that can be obtained that way, the maximum value expecting you
to plant a tree on each one of the 16 Gasha spots in the game.

options.label: Secret Locations
options.description: When enabled, add the linked game secrets to the list of locations

options.label: Linked Hero's Cave
options.description:
Sets whether and how the link version of the hero's cave is placed in the world.
- Samasa: an entrance is placed in the Samasa desert, below the oasis
- Hero's cave: a warp is placed at the entrance of d0

options.label: Required Essences
options.description:
The amount of essences that need to be obtained in order to get the Maku Seed from the Maku Tree and be able
to fight Onox in his castle

options.label: Shuffle Essences
options.description:
If enabled, essences will be shuffled anywhere in the multiworld instead of being guaranteed to be found
at the end their respective dungeons.

options.label: Placed Essences
options.description:
The amount of essences that will be placed in the world. Removed essences are replaced by filler items instead, and
if essences are not shuffled, those filler items will be placed on the pedestal where the essence would have been.
If the value for "Placed Essences" is lower than "Required Essences" (which can happen when using random values
for both), a new random value is automatically picked in the valid range.

options.label: Exclude Dungeons Without Essence
options.description:
If enabled, all dungeons whose essence has been removed because of the "Placed Essences" option will be excluded,
which means you can safely ignore them since they cannot contain an item that is required to complete the seed.
If "Shuffle Essences" is enabled, this option has no effect.
Hero's Cave is not considered to be a dungeon for this option, and therefore is never excluded.

options.label: Show Dungeons With Map
options.description: If enabled, dungeons will indicate where they are once their corresponding map is obtained

options.label: Show Dungeons With Essence
options.description:
Determines the condition required to highlight dungeons having an essence on their end pedestal
(with a sparkle on the in-game map).
This is especially useful when using "Exclude Dungeons Without Essence" to know which dungeons you can ignore.
If "Shuffle Essences" is enabled, this option has no effect.
- Disabled: Dungeons with an essence are never shown on the map
- With Compass: Dungeons with an essence can only be highlighted after obtaining their Compass
- Always: Dungeons with an essence are always shown on the map

options.label: Default Seasons
options.description:
The world of Holodrum is split in regions, each one having its own default season being forced when entering it.
This options gives several ways of manipulating those default seasons.
- Vanilla: default seasons for each region are the ones from the original game
- Randomized: each region has its own random default season picked at generation time
- Random Singularity: a single season is randomly picked and put as default season in every region in the game
- Specific Singularity: the given season is put as default season in every region in the game

options.label: Normalize Horon Village Season
options.description:
In the vanilla game, Horon Village default season is chaotic: every time you enter it, it sets a random season.
This nullifies every condition where a season is required inside Horon Village, since you can leave and re-enter
again and again until you get the season that suits you.
Enabling this option disables that behavior and makes Horon Village behave like any other region in the game.
This means it will have a default season picked at generation time that follows the global behavior defined
in the "Default Seasons" option.

options.label: Animal Companion
options.description:
Determines which animal companion you can summon using the Flute, as well as the layout of the Natzu region.
- Ricky: the kangaroo with boxing skills
- Dimitri: the swimming dinosaur who can eat anything
- Moosh: the flying blue bear with a passion for Spring Bananas

options.label: Shuffle Subrosia Portals
options.description:
- Vanilla: pairs of portals are the same as in the original game
- Shuffle Outwards: each portal is connected to a random portal in the opposite dimension picked at generation time
- Shuffle: each portal is connected to a random portal, which might be in the same dimension (with the guarantee of
  having at least one portal going across dimensions)

options.label: Shuffle Dungeons
options.description:
If enabled, each dungeon entrance will lead to a random dungeon picked at generation time.
Otherwise, all dungeon entrances lead to their dungeon as intended.

options.label: Remove Hero's Cave Alt. Entrance
options.description:
If enabled, remove the hole acting as an alternate entrance to Hero’s Cave. Stairs will be added inside the dungeon to make the chest reachable.
This is especially useful when shuffling dungeons, since only main dungeon entrances are shuffled.
If this option is not set in such a case, you could potentially have two distant entrances leading to the same dungeon.

options.label: Remove D2 Alt. Entrance
options.description:
If enabled, remove both stairs acting as alternate entrances to Snake’s Remains and connect them together inside the dungeon.
This is especially useful when shuffling dungeons, since only main dungeon entrances are shuffled.
If this option is not set in such a case, you could potentially have two distant entrances leading to the same dungeon.

options.label: Default Seed Type
options.description:
Determines which of the 5 seed types will be the "default seed type", which is given:
- when obtaining Seed Satchel
- when obtaining Slingshot
- by Horon Seed Tree

options.label: Duplicate Seed Tree
options.description:
The game contains 6 seed trees but only 5 seed types, which means two trees
must contain the same seed type. This option enables choosing which tree will
always contain a duplicate of one of the other 5 trees.
It is strongly advised to set this to "Tarm Ruins Tree" since it's by far the hardest tree to reach
(and being locked out of a useful seed type can lead to very frustrating situations).

options.label: Master Keys
options.description:
- Disabled: All dungeon keys must be obtained individually, just like in vanilla
- All Small Keys: Small Keys are replaced by a single Master Key for each dungeon which is capable of opening
  every small keydoor for that dungeon
- All Dungeon Keys: the Master Key for each dungeon is also capable of opening the boss keydoor,
  removing Boss Keys from the item pool
Master Keys placement is determined following the "Keysanity (Small Keys)" option.

options.label: Keysanity (Small Keys)
options.description: If enabled, dungeon Small Keys can be found anywhere instead of being confined in their dungeon of origin.

options.label: Keysanity (Boss Keys)
options.description: If enabled, dungeon Boss Keys can be found anywhere instead of being confined in their dungeon of origin.

options.label: Maps & Compasses Outside Dungeon
options.description: If enabled, Dungeon Maps and Compasses can be found anywhere instead of being confined in their dungeon of origin.

options.label: Start with Dungeon Maps & Compasses
options.description:
When enabled, you will start the game with maps and compasses for every dungeon in the game.
This makes navigation easier and removes those items for the pool, which are replaced with random filler items.

options.label: Treehouse Old Man Requirement
options.description: The amount of essences that you need to bring to the treehouse old man for him to give his item.

options.label: Tarm Ruins Gate Required Jewels
options.description: The number of jewels that you need to bring to Tarm Ruins gate to be able to open it.

options.label: Golden Beasts Requirement
options.description:
The amount of golden beasts that need to be beaten for the golden old man to give his item.
Golden beasts are 4 unique enemies that appear at specific spots on specific seasons, and beating all four of them
requires all seasons and having access to most of the overworld.

options.label: Sign Guy Requirement
options.description:
In Subrosia, a NPC will "punish" you if you break more than 100 signs in the vanilla game by giving you an item.
This option lets you configure how many signs are required to obtain that item, since breaking 100 signs is not
everyone's cup of tea.

options.label: Gasha Nut Requirement
options.description:
This option lets you configure how many kills are required to make a gasha tree grow.
Using a gasha ring halves this number.

options.label: Randomize Puzzles
options.description:
If enabled, randomize some puzzles and mini-games.
Puzzles relying on owls will not have their logic affected, and puzzles will not require additional items.

options.label: Randomize Lost Woods Item Sequence
options.description:
If enabled, the secret sequence leading to the Noble Sword pedestal will be randomized (both directions to
take and seasons to use).
To know the randomized combination, you will need to bring the Phonograph to the Deku Scrub near the stump, just
like in the vanilla game.

options.label: Randomize Lost Woods Main Sequence
options.description:
If enabled, the secret sequence leading to D6 sector will be randomized (both directions to take and
seasons to use).
To know the randomized combination, you will need to stun the Deku Scrub near the jewel gate using a shield, just
like in the vanilla game.

options.label: Randomize Samasa Desert Gate Code
options.description:
This option defines if the secret combination which opens the gate to Samasa Desert should be randomized.
You can then configure the length of the sequence with the next option.

options.label: Samasa Desert Gate Code Length
options.description:
The length of the randomized combination for Samasa Desert gate.
This option has no effect if "Randomize Samasa Desert Gate Code" is disabled.

options.label: Quick Flute
options.description: When enabled, playing the flute will immobilize you during a very small amount of time compared to vanilla game.

options.label: Rosa Quick Unlock
options.description: When enabled, Rosa will instantly unlock all subrosia locks when given the Ribbon

options.label: Shop Prices
options.description:
Determine the cost of items found in shops of all sorts (including Subrosian Market and Business Scrubs):
- Vanilla: shop items have the same cost as in the base game
- Free: all shop items can be obtained for free
- Cheap: shop prices are randomized with an average cost of 50 Rupees
- Reasonable: shop prices are randomized with an average cost of 100 Rupees
- Expensive: shop prices are randomized with an average cost of 200 Rupees
- Outrageous: shop prices are randomized with an average cost of 350 Rupees

options.label: Enforce Potion in Shop
options.description: When enabled, you are guaranteed to have a renewable Potion for 300 rupees inside Horon shop

options.label: Required Rings
options.description:
Forces a specified set of rings to appear somewhere in the seed.
Adding too many rings to this list can cause generation failures.
List of ring names can be found here: https://zeldawiki.wiki/wiki/Magic_Ring

options.label: Excluded Rings
options.description:
Forces a specified set of rings to not appear in the seed.
List of ring names can be found here: https://zeldawiki.wiki/wiki/Magic_Ring

options.label: Fool's Ore
options.description:
In the vanilla game, the Fool's Ore is the item "given" by the strange brothers in "exchange" for your feather.
The way the vanilla game is done means you never get to use it, but it's by far the strongest weapon in the game
(dealing 4 times more damage than an L-2 sword!)
- Vanilla: Fool's Ore appears in the item pool with its stats unchanged
- Balanced: Fool's Ore appears in the item pool but its stats are lowered to become comparable to an L-2 sword
- Excluded: Fool's Ore doesn't appear in the item pool at all. Problem solved!

options.label: Cross Items
options.description:
When enabled, adds the Cane of Somaria, the Switch Hook and the Seed Shooter to the item pool
⚠ Requires the Oracles of Ages US ROM on patch, you won't be able to play without

options.label: Combat Difficulty
options.description:
Modifies the damage taken during combat to make this aspect of the game easier or harder depending on the
type of experience you want to have

options.label: Bird Hint
options.description:
Disabled: The Owls and Know-it-all birds say their vanilla text when talked to
Know-it-all: Enable region hints from the birds in the house next to the advance shop
Owl: Enable owls to give hints about items from your world

options.label: Randomize AI
options.description:
When enabled, enemy AI will be randomized.
This option is only visible on yamls generated in April.

⚠ This option may cause logic issues or unbeatable seeds due to some untested combos caused
by the high number of possibilities. Some graphical oddities are also to be expected.
⚠ Required golden beasts is 0 because you are not guaranteed to get an enemy
with a golden beast AI that would be counted for the old man

options.label: Randomize AI
options.description:
When enabled, movement will be linked between games that enabled this option.
This option is only visible on yamls generated in April.

⚠ This option may easily cause softlocks and may cause some issues. Some graphical oddities are also to be expected.

options.label: Remove Items from Pool
options.description:
Removes specified amount of given items from the item pool, replacing them with random filler items.
This option has significant chances to break generation if used carelessly, so test your preset several times
before using it on long generations. Use at your own risk!

options.label: starting green star seeds

shop items after the number set will be excluded from having progression items in them. will do nothing if set higher than the number of shop items, 
NOTE will cause world generation to fail if number is set too low as there will be not enough location slots for progression items

options.label: hide shop item details
options.description: hide shop item id and item progression category

options.label: shop food min

options.label: shop arch max
options.description: set max value for Arch shop items. MUST BE HIGHER OR EQUAL TO shop_arch_min

options.label: goal start
options.description: Starting affection goal for date puzzles

options.label: goal addition
options.description: affection added to the starting goal based on how many pairs you have taken on dates

options.label: goal boss
options.description: affection goal for boss puzzles

options.label: puzzle moves
options.description: moves you start a puzzle with (EASY MODE=30, NORMAL MODE=25, HARD MODE=20) NOTE: boss fight will start with 4x this number caped at 999

options.label: filler item
options.description:
how the filler item is handled by making them all either:
nothing: nothing items,
seed: random seed items,
date: random date gifts
mixed: all of above

options.label: goal
options.description:
set the goal
panties: give kyu all available girls panties
sex: have sex with all available girls

options.label: filler item
options.description:
how the filler item is handled by making them all either:
nothing: "nothing" items,
filler: random non progression items (date gifts, food, drink) + "nothing" items

options.label: deathlink
options.description:
enables/disables deathlink

"disable": disable deathlink
"send": send deathlink on date fails but don't receive deaths
"limited": send deathlink on date fails and receive deaths but do nothing if death is received outside a date
"full": send deathlink on date fails and receive deaths, if death is received outside a date it will wait until you are in a date then kill you

full: will randomize the gifts each girl want

make dates/sleeping with girls require a progressive date item (Date Pass) to access

options.description: Sets Character Gender in Game NOTE: you can change this by interacting the wardrobe in the house in oakwood village

options.label: Char Hairstyle

options.label: Char Hair Color
options.description:
Sets Character Hair Color in Game NOTE: you can change this by interacting the wardrobe in the house in oakwood village
NOTE 2: Male Chars only have 3 hair colors so if option 3 is selected it will be changed to option 2

options.label: Char Outfit
options.description: Sets Character Outfit in Game NOTE: you can change this by interacting the wardrobe in the house in oakwood village

options.label: map rando option
options.description:
sets what the goal is
mission = complete all main missions
catch = catch all spirits
rare = catch all rare spirits
affection = catch and get Lv5 affection with all spirits

options.label: Randomise Spawns
options.description: randomise the spawns in the grass/water NOTE will also randomise what spirit is obtained through the "Simulated Scuffle" and "Gold Plated" side quests

options.label: Grass Slots
options.description: number of spirit slots in the grass

options.label: Water Slots
options.description: number of spirit slots in the water

options.label: Randomise Enemies
options.description: randomise the enemies team of spirits

options.label: Enemy Vision
options.description: Enable/Disable Enemy Vision

options.label: Enemy Spin
options.description: Sets whether Enemy's will stand sill, spin in a circle or randomly rotate

options.label: Randomise Spirit Moves
options.description: randomise moves learned by spirits

options.label: Random Spirit Moves Amount
options.description: number of move to randomise on to spirits

options.label: Randomise Spirit Evo
options.description: randomise Evolution for spirits

options.label: Randomise Spirit Type
options.description: randomise Type for spirits

options.label: Randomise Spirit Stats
options.description: randomise stats for spirits

options.label: Goal Type
options.description:
What must you accomplish to win the game?

Survival: Survive a number of days to win. Chose the amount in "Days to Survive" option.

Bosses (Any): Defeat any boss selected in "Boss Defeat Requirement" to win.

Bosses (All): Defeat all bosses selected in "Boss Defeat Requirement" to win.

options.label: Days to Survive
options.description:
Only applies for the survival goal. The number of days your character must survive for the survival goal.

Each day would last 8 real life minutes on default settings. Being a ghost pauses your timer. Regenerating the world or dying in Wilderness mode resets your timer.

options.label: Boss Defeat Requirement
options.description:
Only applies for boss goal types. Which boss(es) are required to be defeated to beat the game?

Make sure correct regions, seasons, and day phases are enabled for your goal boss to be in logic.

"Random" chooses a random boss. If bosses are chosen along with it, it'll choose a random boss within your selection.

Valid Bosses:
Deerclops - Winter
Moose/Goose - Spring
Bearger - Autumn
Ancient Guardian - Cave (Full)
Antlion - Summer
Dragonfly
Bee Queen
Klaus - Winter
Toadstool - Cave
Malbatross - Ocean
Crab King - Ocean
Frostjaw - Ocean
Eye Of Terror - Night
Retinazor - Night
Spazmatism - Night
Nightmare Werepig - Cave (Full)
Scrappy Werepig - Cave (Full)
Ancient Fuelweaver - Cave (Full), Night
Celestial Champion - Ocean (Full)

Example: ['Deerclops', 'Moose/Goose', 'Bearger']

options.label: Crafting Mode
options.description:
Change the crafting behavior?

Vanilla: Crafting behavior is vanilla.

Journey: Once you craft an item once, you can craft it again freely.

Free Samples: Once you unlock a recipe, you can craft one for free.

Free-Build: Once you unlock a recipe, you can always craft it.

Locked Ingredients: You cannot craft items that use one of your missing items as an ingredient.

options.label: Cave Regions
options.description:
How far into the cave will your items and checks be shuffled?

None: No cave. Choose this if you're making a no-cave world!

Auto: Choose minimum regions based on your goal. (Survival goal will default to None. For boss goals, check the tooltip for "Boss Defeat Requirement".)

Light: Shuffle caves without ruins and archive.

Full: Shuffle caves, ruins, and archive.

options.label: Ocean Regions
options.description:
How far into the ocean will your items and checks be shuffled?

None: No ocean checks.

Auto: Choose minimum regions based on your goal. (Survival goal will default to None. For boss goals, check the tooltip for "Boss Defeat Requirement".)

Light: Shuffle ocean without moonstorm.

Full: Shuffle ocean and moonstorm. Requires either Boss Locations to be "all" or Celestial Champion as your goal.

options.label: Seasons
options.description:
Which seasons will be enabled in your world?

This is not automatic. If changed from default, seasons will need to be set manually in your world settings!

options.label: Starting Season
options.description:
Which season do you start with in your world?

This is not automatic. If not autumn, starting season will need to be set manually in your world settings!

options.label: Day Phases
options.description:
Which day phases will be enabled in your world?

This is not automatic. If changed from default, day phases will need to be set manually in your world settings!

Set to Night only if you plan to play on a Lights Out world.

options.label: Creature Locations
options.description:
Are non-boss creatures checks, by killing or non-violent interactions?

None: Creatures are not checks. (Disabling will remove a lot of checks. Excess items will be moved into your start inventory.)

All: All creatures are checks.

Peaceful: Only creatures that have a peaceful interaction are checks. Killing still also grants the check.

options.label: Boss Locations
options.description:
Are boss defeats checks, other than ones listed in your goal condition?

None: No boss checks other than ones on your goal path.

Easy: Only easier bosses. These can be defeated even if playing solo with default difficulty.

All: Includes raid bosses. These are intended for multiplayer sessions, but can still be soloed with enough damage bonuses or creative strategies.

options.label: Cooking Locations
options.description:
Have checks for cooking different foods in the crock pot? Your checks and example recipes are in the in-game tracker.
The wiki is also a good resource: https://dontstarve.wiki.gg/wiki/Dishes

None: No checks from cooking. (This will remove a lot of checks. Excess items will be moved into your start inventory.)

Regular: Get checks for cooking in the crock pot, excluding Warly's exclusives. (Up to 70 checks)

Warly Enabled: All crock pot recipes are checks, including Warly's exclusives.
Logic will expect you to have the ability to use the Portable Crock Pot. (Up to 81 checks)

Veggie Only: All recipes except meat and Warly exclusives. (Up to 32 checks)

Meat Only: All recipes except veggie and Warly exclusives. (Up to 48 checks)

options.label: Farming Locations
options.description: Have checks for harvesting giant crops?

options.label: Shuffle Starting Recipes
options.description:
Turn your basic starting recipes into Archipelago items?

This may leave you vulnerable to darkness on your first night! If you're not okay with this, you may want to add {Torch: 1} to your start inventory.

Sphere 1 will also be small, making generation more restrictive when generating alone, and is prone to fail if "Creature Locations" are off!

options.label: Shuffle Ancient and Celestial Recipes
options.description: Turn crafting recipes from the Ancient Pseudoscience Station and Celestial Altars into Archipelago items?

options.label: Chess Piece Sketch Items
options.description:
Include Knight, Bishop, and Rook Figure Sketches as items?

This bypasses the need to assemble the marble sculptures for Shadow Pieces, while preventing specific progression-locking scenarios.

options.label: Farm Plant Seed Items
options.description: Turn farm plant seeds into Archipelago items? When enabled, generic seeds can only grow weeds.

options.label: Extra Damage Against Bosses
options.description:
This adds "Extra Damage Against Bosses" buffs as Archipelago items. High is recommended if planning to take on raid bosses solo.

Each stack of this buff gives all damage sources a permanent +10% damage against easier bosses and +25% damage against tougher ones.

This is exponential. With 10 stacks, this turns into x2.6 and x9.3 damage multipiers respectively. Multipliers can be configured in the mod configuration in the game's menu.

This amount is separate from any prefilled through "Boss Fill Items" setting.

options.label: Damage Bonuses
options.description:
This adds "Damage Bonus" buffs as Archipelago items.

Each stack of this buff gives the player a permanent +10% damage against all mobs. It only affects a player's direct damage.

This is exponential. With 10 stacks, this turns into a x2.6 multipier. Multiplier can be configured in the mod configuration in the game's menu.

This amount is separate from any prefilled through "Boss Fill Items" setting.

options.label: Boss Fill Items
options.description: Choose what type of items a boss check can grant. Requires Boss Locations to be enabled.

options.label: Junk Item Amount
options.description:
Number of junk (stat change) and trap items to add to the item pool

If set too high, junk will leave no space for regular items, and overflow them into your starting inventory.

options.label: Trap Item Chance (Percentage)
options.description: Chance percentage junk items can be regular traps. These do not change the season. If combined with Season Traps Items, the percentage is split.

options.label: Season Trap Item Chance (Percentage)
options.description:
Chance percentage junk items can be season-changing traps. These can only be seasons that are enabled. If combined with Traps Items, the percentage is split.

Season traps trigger a cooldown for player-controlled season changes. The length is configurable in the mod options (default 1 day).

options.label: Season Flow
options.description:
How do seasons progress in your world?

Normal: Seasons progress as default. Logic attempts to prepare you for seasons in time, but not guaranteed. Seasonal checks may not have progression items.

Unlockable: Season-changing items are progression. Seasonal checks may have progression items. Can optionally play with long seasons.

Unlockable Shuffled: Same as unlockable, except seasons are logically shuffled within the spheres. Can optionally play with long seasons.

options.label: Logic Difficulty
options.description:
What skill level should be considered for randomizer logic?

Easy: Adds useful items in logic and avoids harder solutions.

Advanced: Expects the player to be familiar with game mechanics.

Expert: Expects the player survive in riskier conditions, have minimal items, and know advanced tricks.

Abilities that are allowed to be in the item pool

options.label: Line Clear Leniency
options.description:
How many lines worth of extra blocks are needed for line clears to be considered in logic.

If zero, lines require the exact number of blocks it takes to clear them and all lines before.
This is not as strict as it sounds since stacking and clearing higher lines out-of-logic is still possible.

If you rely on trackers, it's recommended to set higher than zero.

options.label: Max Stacking Height
options.description:
How high logic expects you to stack blocks to reach coins. This is NOT relevant to line clear locations.

If set to board height (currently 20), what's possible is in logic. Setting it lower makes logic more lenient.
If you rely on trackers, it's recommended to set it lower otherwise it will create unneeded pressure.

Warning! Setting this higher than your board height can make the game more difficult or even impossible!
Only do this if you accept the risk and want to challenge yourself in a solo game.

options.description: Ratio of traps to all shapes

options.label: Tutorials
options.description: How many times do you need to see the tutorial?

options.description: When you receive a trap, everyone who enabled trap link receives a trap. Of course, the reverse is true too.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
How the seed is won.
grand_goal: collect Required Fragments, then find the answer to the Grand Goal question.
realm_master: clear the last round of every branch / Realm. Needs Branch Count of at least 1;
Knowledge Fragments and the Grand Goal are not generated.

options.label: Required Fragments
options.description:
Knowledge Fragments needed to reveal and clear the Grand Goal.
Landing on the answer page finishes the slot.
Capped at Round Count: a higher value needs (and puts in the pool) only Round Count fragments.

options.label: Additional Fragments In Pool
options.description: Extra Knowledge Fragments placed in the item pool beyond required_fragments (goal still needs only the required count).

options.label: Round Count
options.description:
Number of Start→Target rounds (checks) generated for your slot (10–999).
Generation still fails if the enabled article pool is too small.

options.label: Start Rounds Unlocked
options.description:
How many Start→Target rounds are playable immediately at seed start (1–999).
High relative to Round Count feels more open early; low means waiting more on Round Access.

options.label: Rounds Per Round Access
options.description: How many additional rounds each Round Access item unlocks (1–999).

options.label: Branch Count
options.description:
How many main-road rounds are crossroads (never round 1). Branch N needs N keys plus that finished crossroad
(either order). 0 disables the whole branch system. All unlocked branches stay live at once.

options.label: Branch Length
options.description: Rounds in each unlocked side branch chain (1–20).

options.label: Topic Portals
options.description:
Topic Realms. Every branch becomes a Realm with its own topic (History, Music, ...) and
is opened by that topic's Portal item instead of generic Branch Keys, so Realms open in any order.
Each Realm needs a distinct enabled category with at least Branch Length unused articles.
Additional Branch Keys is ignored when this is on.

options.label: Additional Branch Keys
options.description: Extra Branch Key items in the pool beyond branch_count. Still progression; extras do not open more branches.

options.label: Back Depth Start
options.description: Starting Back depth per round (0 = Back locked until Progressive Back items are found).

options.label: Back Depth Unlocks
options.description: Number of Progressive Back items in the pool (each raises per-round Back depth by 1).

options.label: Target Rerolls Start
options.description:
Starting target rerolls available each round. Alternatives come from leftover articles in the same seed pool.
The Grand Goal article itself cannot be rerolled.

options.label: Target Reroll Unlocks
options.description: Number of Progressive Reroll items in the pool (each raises per-round reroll max by 1).

options.label: Letter Pair Bingo
options.description:
When enabled, add letter-pair bingo board(s) with row/column/diagonal/full-card checks.
Stamp pairs from page titles. Bingo on with start 0 and unlocks 0 is rejected (no boards).

options.label: Letter Pair Bingo Grid Size
options.description:
Bingo grid size N (N×N cells). Weighted sample from the slot language's Scrabble letter-pair frequencies (3-20).
Letter pairs use Scrabble alphabets (e.g. pl keeps Ą/Ć/Ł…; fr folds é→E; de keeps Ä/Ö/Ü, ß→SS).

options.label: Bingo Cards Start
options.description: How many letter-pair bingo boards are unlocked from the start (0 = all boards locked behind Progressive Bingo Card).

options.label: Bingo Card Unlocks
options.description: Number of Progressive Bingo Card items in the pool (extra boards beyond Bingo Cards Start). Combined boards capped at 40.

options.label: Bingo Stamp Unlocks
options.description: Number of Progressive Bingo Stamp items in the pool (each stamps one empty cell on one unlocked board, once per seed).

Enabling lenses (even one) can make routing much harder; stacking several increases difficulty sharply.

options.label: Randomize References
options.description:
When enabled, footnotes/references stay hidden until Reference Lens is received.
Enabling lenses (even one) can make routing much harder; stacking several increases difficulty sharply.

options.label: Deaths
options.description:
When enabled, revisiting a page already visited this round causes a death
(jump to a random Wikipedia page). Local only unless Death Link is also on.
Peaceful when off.

options.label: Death Link
options.description: When enabled, join Archipelago DeathLink (send and receive).

options.label: Link Bombs
options.description:
When enabled (and Deaths is on), random links on each page may be bombs that cause a death.
Target and Grand Goal links are never bombs.

options.label: Link Bomb Density
options.description:
How many bomb links to try to place per page (capped at half the eligible links). Requires Deaths and Link Bombs.

options.label: Trap Count
options.description:
Number of trap items (Foggy Links / Missing Links / Wrong Wiki) added to the pool before Footnote filler.
Counts toward the mandatory item budget — generation fails if too many.

options.label: Trap Type
options.description:
Which trap items to generate and accept from Trap Link.

``all`` includes Foggy Links, Missing Links, and Wrong Wiki.

options.label: Trap Link
options.description: When enabled, share traps with other Trap Link players (send and receive). Independent of Trap Count.

options.label: Endings
options.description: How many endings are required to be completed to win the game.

options.description: If the gem unlocks should be randomized

options.label: Gems in Pool
options.description: How many Gems are in the pool

options.label: Gems Required
options.description: What percentage of available gems (rounded down) is required to open the door

options.label: RequireFailableJumps
options.description: This includes jumps in logic that are difficult and result in death if missed

options.label: RequireHardCombat
options.description: This adds ending 49 into logic without shield

options.label: AddTreasureSword
options.description: This adds the sword in the treasure room into the sword progression

options.label: NonStopMode
options.description:
This turns on non-stop mode, which allows continuing after getting certain endings.
If set to canonical, it will only allow continuing after endings that "make sense". E.g. endings where Lonk does not die canonically.
If set to logical, it will allow continuing after any ending that does not break logic.
If set to everything, it will allow continuing after any ending. This will allow you to break logic because you can e.g. walk in lava.

options.label: UseExperimentalRegionGraph
options.description: This turns on the experimental region graph. This options is still bugged and likely to slow down generation or produce unbeatable seeds. Turn on at your own risk.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
The victory condition for your run. Please specify a valid location which can be found in archi_defs or archi_data.
You can specify one value or many. If you specify multiple values, you win once you complete all of them.

Deletes your character's gear on first connection, avoids granting checks immediately for Skyrocket, Gearbox guns, etc.
(Please be careful to back up your saves and load the correct character)

options.description:
Gear Licenses will be added to the item pool as receivable items. (Ex. Uncommon Pistol)

disabled = Exclude from Item Pool, ability to equip things is always unlocked.
exclude_glitch = Glitch rarity are excluded
all = All licenses are added to the pool

options.label: Gear Receive Type
options.description:
When receiving gear licenses from the item pool, does it spawn for you or do you only get the ability to equip the ones you find.
This option does nothing if gear_licenses is disabled
equip_only = do not spawn gear when receiving a license
receive = spawn gear when receiving a license

options.label: Filler Gear
options.description:

unique = Unique items (Legendaries, Seraphs, etc. but as filler)
rarity_groups = Common, Uncommon, etc. as filler
both = Both unique and non-unique gear

options.label: Filler Item Rotation
options.description:
What items should be added to fill out the rest of the filler item pool.
Filler items will be added to the item pool in a round-robin fashion, so any item in this list will be added many times.
Include more instances of an item type by including it multiple times. Items will be added in the same ratio as they appear in this list.
You can find item names in archi_data.py. Examples of items to use: 
"3 Skill Points", "$100", "10 Moonstones", "10% Exp", "Filler Gear: Glitch Pistol", "Filler Gear: Smasher", "Trap Spawn: Opha"
You can also include "gear" and "sdu"
"gear" will cycle through gear based on the choice in filler_gear.
"sdu" will cycle through backpack and ammo upgrades up to the vanilla max levels.
"3 Skill Points" is handled specially and will stop being added once you can reach 120 skill points.
Note: 1 instance of every filler item aside from "Filler Gear" is included regardless of what you put in this list, and "3 Skill Points" is automatically included enough times to reach 27 skill points.
Quest rewards are added separately from this rotation list (see quest_reward_items)
Trap spawns are added separately from this rotation list (see spawn_traps), but you can add more here if you're crazy.

options.label: Game Mode
options.description:
Determines how to advance through the game. Cups is closest to the vanilla game.

Cups: Courses are raced in sets of four, place 4th or better to advance each race. Unlock each cup progressively.
The Cups victory condition is beating the Special Cup on 150cc.

Courses (NOT YET SUPPORTED): Each course is run individually. Unlock the final courses progressively to reach the
final race. The Courses victory condition is winning 1st place on the last course.

(NOT YET SUPPORTED)
