    'Chaotix CheckpointSanity 1 Set',
    'Chaotix CheckpointSanity Both Acts',
    
    'Super Hard Mode',
    'Super Hard CheckpointSanity',
]

options.label: Unlock Type
options.description:
How should the entire run be structured?
Ability Character Unlocks has all levels open from the start and locks characters and abilities behind items.
Legacy Gates has all abilities and characters unlocked from the start and instead locks level access behind level gates (like SA2).

options.label: Ability Unlocks
options.description:
How should Ability Unlocks be Handled (if enabled)?
Entire Story will make there be a "Homing Attack" item for each Team that unlocks Homing Attack on all levels for that team.
All Regions Separate will have 7 sets of ability items (Per Team) that unlock the ability for that respective region. (A Region is a set of levels that follow the same theme)
For example, Seaside Hill and Ocean Palace are both in the Ocean Region

Dev Note: All Regions Separate can cause significant BK in syncs (depending on speed of other games)
Recommended for asyncs only (or with proper consideration)

options.label: Legacy Number Of Level Gates
options.description:
How many Level Gates should there be?
This option is ignored if set to Ability and Character Unlocks.

This will result in this many groups of levels locked behind emblems and boss completions and 1 additional group unlocked from the start.

options.label: Legacy Level Gates Allowed Bosses
options.description:
Which Bosses should be allowed to be level gate bosses?
This option is ignored if set to Ability and Character Unlocks.
This needs to be equal to the number of level gates or larger.

Valid Choices:

    - 'Egg Hawk'
    - 'Team Fight 1'
    - 'Robot Carnival'
    - 'Egg Albatross'
    - 'Team Fight 2'
    - 'Robot Storm'
    - 'Egg Emperor'

options.label: Required Rank
options.description:
What Minimum Rank should be required to send level complete checks?
This option is ignored when Ability and Character Unlocks is enabled.
This also affects Bonus/Emerald stage unlocking as well.

options.label: Final Boss
options.description:
What should the final boss be?
Metal Madness requires both Metal Madness and Metal Overlord (in one go).
This is accessed from Metal Overlord in level select regardless of choice.
Sea Gate is the scariest final boss of all time.

options.label: Goal Unlock Conditions
options.description:
How should Metal Madness/Overlord be unlocked?
Adding Multiple will require all of them.

Valid Choices:
    - 'Emblems'
    - 'Emeralds'
    - 'Level Completions All Teams'
    - 'Level Completions Per Story'


Note: All Characters are required to be unlocked if Unlock Type is Ability Character Unlocks as well.
Note: There are no Emblems added to the item pool if Unlock Type is Ability Character Unlocks

options.label: Goal Level Completions
options.description:
How Many Level Completions are needed across all Stories to unlock Metal Madness/Overlord?
Completing Both Acts of a level will not count as a second Completion.
This Requires Level Completion Goal Unlock Condition.
This is capped to 14 * the number of stories enabled.
This is in addition to Goal Unlock Conditions Per Story.

options.label: Goal Level Completions Per Story
options.description:
How Many Level Completions are needed per Story to unlock Metal Madness/Overlord?
This Requires Level Completion Per Story Goal Unlock Condition.
Each Story will require at least this many completed levels.
This is in addition to Goal Level Completions.

options.label: Sonic Story Starting Character
options.description:
If Ability and Character Unlocks are enabled, which Character should be unlocked for Sonic Story from the Start?
Knuckles has the largest sphere 1
Sonic and Tails are even though Tails is slightly more restrictive logically

options.label: Dark Sanity
options.description:
How many enemies are needed for a sanity check?
Requires Mission B and Dark ObjSanity to be enabled
1 results in 1400 checks
20 results in 70 checks

options.label: Dark Story Starting Character
options.description: If Ability and Character Unlocks are enabled, which Character should be unlocked for Dark Story from the Start?

options.label: Rose Sanity
options.description:
How many rings are needed for a sanity check?
Requires Mission B and Rose ObjSanity to be enabled
1 results in 2800 checks
20 results in 140 checks

options.label: Rose Story Starting Character
options.description: If Ability and Character Unlocks are enabled, which Character should be unlocked for Rose Story from the Start?

options.label: Chaotix Sanity
options.description:
Should Chaotix Sanity be enabled, and if so, how many rings are needed for a check on Casino Park? (All non-Casino Park levels are the same if enabled)
Mission A only Check Count: 223 + 200 / value (if enabled)
Mission B only Check Count: 266 + 500 / value (if enabled)
Both Missions Check Count: 489 + 700 / value (if enabled)

options.label: Chaotix Story Starting Character
options.description: If Ability and Character Unlocks are enabled, which Character should be unlocked for Chaotix Story from the Start?

options.label: Super Hard Mode Starting Character
options.description: If Ability and Character Unlocks are enabled, which Character should be unlocked for Super Hard Mode from the Start?

options.label: Remove Casino Park VIP Table Laser Gate
options.description:
This Option will Remove the Laser Gate in front of the ramp before the VIP Table in Casino Park.
This allows access to the Bonus Key there and the VIP table without having to get the switch on the pinball table before.

options.label: Trap Fill
options.description: What percent of filler items should be replaced with trap items?

options.label: Stealth Trap Weight
options.description:
Determines the weight (not percent) for Stealth Trap.
Traps must be enabled for this to have any effect.

options.label: Freeze Trap Weight
options.description:
Determines the weight (not percent) for Freeze Trap.
Traps must be enabled for this to have any effect.

options.label: No Swap Trap Weight
options.description:
Determines the weight (not percent) for No Swap Trap.
Traps must be enabled for this to have any effect.

options.label: Ring Trap Weight
options.description:
Determines the weight (not percent) for Ring Trap.
Traps must be enabled for this to have any effect.

options.label: Charmy Trap Weight
options.description:
Determines the weight (not percent) for Charmy Trap.
Traps must be enabled for this to have any effect.

options.label: Mission Amount
options.description: Amount of levels required to complete goal

options.label: Randomize Starting Tools
options.description: If enabled, the starting tools will be randomized.

options.label: Randomize Starting Level
options.description: If enabled, the starting level is randomized, if not it is Old Building Problem.

options.label: Max Animatronics Appearing
options.description: Max amount of Animatronics that will appear at once.

options.label: Catalogue Rando
options.description: Turns catalogue unlocks into checks.

options.label: Night Mode Difficulty
options.description:
Alters mechanics in the Night Mode to make it easier or harder.

Easy Mode:
Makes the Motion Detector always show where the animatronics are located.

Normal Mode:
Mechanics are unchanged.

options.label: Speed Upgrade Rando
options.description: Turns the speed upgrades for the tasks into checks.

options.label: Easier Money Grinding
options.description:
Gives you unlimited playtests to allow easier money grinding.
LOGIC EXPECTS THIS TO BE ENABLED

options.label: Wallet-sanity
options.description: Limits how much money you can have based on how many Wallet Capacity Increases you have obtained.

options.label: Full Wallet
options.description:
Makes when you receive a Wallet Capacity Increase, it gives you money equivalent to your new maximum.
(Requires Wallet Sanity to be enabled.)

options.label: Day-sanity
options.description: You need to receive the corresponding day item to go to the specific day.

options.label: Skip-able Night
options.description: Makes it where you can immediately finish the office section if you have not received any animatronics.

options.label: Ending Goal
options.description: Which ending do you want to be the goal.

options.label: Initial Characters
options.description: Decides your starting characters

options.label: Vanilla Halloween Land
options.description: Makes the Halloween Land minigames give the vanilla stuff

options.label: Vanilla Lasers
options.description: Makes the laser switches always be found in their vanilla locations

options.label: Vanilla Pearl
options.description: Makes the pearl always be found in its vanilla location

options.label: Logic Difficulty
options.description:
Decides how difficult the logic is:
Easy: Every Boss requires a strong Animatronic, Late Game checks are only in logic with certain characters (Garuntees good characters early on)
Normal (recommended): Late Game requires certain characters and/or attacks (Higher chance of good characters earlier)
Hard: Only certain Bosses require characters with Neon Wall or Gift Boxes
Insane: Everything is expected to be done without any strong characters, including every Bosses

options.label: Cheaper Shop Prices
options.description: Halves the price of every Item in every Shop

options.label: Require Find Char
options.description:
Makes every character location logically require the Find Characters chip
This means you can still find characters, but they are not logically intended to be found yet.

options.label: Progressive Animatronics
options.description: Makes you get animatronics in a randomized set order, but with stronger animatronics later in the order

options.label: Progressive Bytes
options.description: Makes you get bytes in a randomized set order, but with stronger bytes later in the order

options.label: Progressive Chips
options.description: Makes you get chips in a randomized set order, but with stronger chips later in the order (Some chips may be excluded)

options.label: Progressive Areas
options.description:
Makes you get areas in randomized set order, but with more progression into one direction of the map.
e.g.:
Choppy's Woods -> Dusting Fields 
Lilygear Lake -> Blacktomb Yard -> Pinwheel Circus
Halloween Land -> Geist Lair

options.label: Warp Access
options.description:
How do the warp buttons function?
visit_area: You have to trigger the warp the same way as vanilla.
always: You only need the Access Switch/Access item for that area to warp there.
warp_item: Similar to always, but you need an additional item for warping.

options.label: Randomized Fazcoin Chests
options.description: How many Fazcoin chests per area will be give out Checks

options.label: Halloween Minigame Lock
options.description:
If the minigames from Update 2 in Halloween Land should be shuffled into the pool:
true: Randomizes the Accesses for the Minigames into the pool, you'll need an Item for each Minigame
false: Minigames are Accessible as soon as you can enter Halloween Land

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Select the goal you need to reach to win.
Raft Quest: Collect eight Raft Pieces and escape the island.
Queen of Adventure: Collect eight Raft Pieces, defeat Simulacrum and get the Big Ol' Bag Of Loot, and escape the island.
Queen of Dreams: Complete all five Dreamworld dungeons, which will let you escape the island, then do so.
In Queen of Dreams, only one Raft Piece is in the pool, Grand Library is forced open, and you cannot set Dungeon Rewards Setting.
Potion Hunt: Collect a specified number of potions, which will allow you to escape the island.
In Potion Hunt, only the number of Raft Pieces you need to get all randomized checks will be in the pool.

options.label: Required Number of Potions (Potion Hunt)
options.description:
(Potion Hunt goal only) How many potions are required to get off the island?
Recommended to use keysey/keyrings and reduced shard settings to have room in the pool.

options.label: Extra Potions (Potion Hunt)
options.description:
(Potion Hunt goal only) How many extra potions should be in the pool?
Recommended to use keysey/keyrings and reduced shard settings to have room in the pool.

options.label: Dungeon Rewards Setting
options.description:
Select what will be at the reward location in dungeons. In Dreamworld dungeons, the middle card is the reward.
This can produce more dungeon-heavy seeds, as the randomizer generally tries to avoid putting items deep in dungeons.
Anything: The reward can be anything
Priority: The reward can have any item marked progression in the multiworld
Rewards: The reward can be either a Raft Piece or a Forbidden Key (if Open Tomb of Simulacrum is off).
If there are more dungeon rewards locations in the pool than available reward items, the rest will be priority locations.
Tomb of Simulacrum can never have its reward set with this. If you want to require Tomb, use the Queen of Adventure goal.
Quietus will also never be required.
Incompatible with Queen of Dreams Goal (this setting will be ignored if that goal is set)
If the goal is Potion Hunt and this is set to Rewards, dungeon rewards will be set to potions before they start being
filled with Raft Pieces and Forbidden Keys.

options.label: Dungeon Rewards Count
options.description:
How many dungeons should have their rewards set as per the Dungeon Rewards Setting?
Note that this will only set the reward locations for dungeons that are randomized in the pool,
so if you set this higher than the number of randomized dungeons, it will be the number of dungeons instead.

options.label: Progressive Items
options.description:
If on, there are three Force Wands, Dynamites, Ice Rings, and Chains in the pool (vanilla behavior).
If off, there are only one of each, and there are two upgrades available of each which will only apply
once you've obtained the base item.
This makes it harder to get these items.

options.label: Include Portal Worlds
options.description: Randomizes any chests in Portal Worlds. Excludes the Super Secret Portal Worlds.

options.label: Include Secret Dungeons
options.description:
Randomizes any chests in the three shard dungeons and Tomb of Simulacrum.
Even if this is off, Tomb of Simulacrum will be included if Queen of Adventure is the goal

options.label: Include Dream Dungeons
options.description:
Randomizes any chests and cards in the five Dreamworld dungeons.
This will automatically be turned on if the goal is Queen of Dreams.

options.label: Include Super Secrets
options.description:
Randomizes a secret item in the Dreamworld, LUDDC, and a secret with NAAQ BLX.
If you know, you know. If you don't, leave this off.
(This option removes the need to be as healthy or waste your time.)

options.label: Include Secret Signs
options.description:
The four incomplete signs and the Super Hint signs give you an item when they're read.
The number and letter signs are included if Super Secrets are on.

options.label: Region Connection Blockades
options.description:
Adds 14 area connection items which are required to travel between areas. For example, you need the
"Connection - Fluffy Fields To Sweetwater Coast" to be able to enter Sweetwater Coast from Fluffy Fields.
Connections are two-way, so that also allows you to enter Fluffy Fields from Sweetwater Coast.
This is not compatible with and will disable Start With All Warps.

options.label: Open Grand Library
options.description:
Opens the entrance to Grand Library, removing the need to collect seven Raft Pieces.
This setting is forced on if you have the Queen of Dreams goal.

options.label: Open Tomb of Simulacrum
options.description: Opens the entrance to Tomb of Simulacrum and removes the Forbidden Keys from the pool.

options.label: Open Dreamworld Dungeons
options.description:
Opens the entrance the first four Dreamworld dungeons.
This does not remove the need for a Raft Piece,
but it does make it so you do not need items to enter the dungeons themselves.

options.label: Dream Dungeons Do Not Change Items
options.description: Dreamworld dungeons no longer restrict your items, but will also not give you the items expected to beat them.

options.label: Key_Settings
options.description:
How should dungeon keys be treated by the randomizer? Forbidden Keys are not affected by this setting.
Keys for dungeons not randomized will not be included.
Default: Keys are individual items.
Keyrings: All keys are removed and keyrings for each dungeon are placed in the pool instead,
granting all the keys you need at once
Keysey: All keys and locks are removed

options.label: Secret Shard Requirements
options.description:
Open: Secret Shards are not required to access any of the secret dungeons.
Shards are removed from the pool and Extra Shards is ignored.
Half: Sunken Labyrinth needs 4 Shards to enter, Machine Fortress needs 8, and Dark Hypostyle needs 12.
Vanilla: Secret dungeons require their normal amount of shards to enter.
Lockdown: Sunken Labyrinth needs 12 Shards to enter, Machine Fortress needs 24, and Dark Hypostyle needs 36.
If Include Secret Dungeons is off, shards will not be in the pool.

options.label: Extra Shards
options.description:
Adds extra Secret Shards to the pool. Once you have obtained enough to open Dark Hypostyle,
Secret Shards will give you a random heart instead.
If Include Secret Dungeons is off, shards will not be in the pool.

options.label: Start Without Stick
options.description:
Start without Ittle's stick and places an additional Progressive Melee into the pool.
You will be unable to attack or open chests, so this severely limits your initial available locations.

options.label: Start Without Roll
options.description: Start without the ability to roll and places a Roll item into the pool.

options.label: Roll Opens Chests
options.description: Rolling can be used to open chests. Can be used to make Start Without Stick more viable.

options.label: Early Weapon Choice
options.description:
Force a specific weapon to be in Sphere 1.
Since the randomizer will usually pick stick to be your earliest weapon if Randomize Stick is on, this setting
can be used to try to force something else.
Ice Ring is the easiest, Force Wand is the most limited, and Dynamite is the most difficult.
Note that this setting will generally be completely ineffective if you don't Randomize Stick.
Keeping the setting off lets Archipelago determine your earliest weapon, and may not put it in sphere 1.

options.label: Major Dungeon Skips
options.description:
Allows the following tricks:
Early Grand Library
Grand Library Skip
Early Tomb of Simulacrum
Quietus Boss without breaking the crystals
You can keep this setting off to allow phasing in logic without it being too powerful.

options.label: Allow Phasing
options.description:
ID2 has a glitch called "Phasing" which allows you to clip over gaps and through objects.
There are different types of phases, and this setting allows them being required in logic.
Gap Phases: Allows phasing over pits and through loading zones (phasing through door transitions requires rolling).
Object Phases: Allows phasing through collision to objects, including Ice Ring blocks. Also allows Gap Phases.
Ice Dynamite Clips: Allows clipping through walls using Ice and Dynamite Clips. Also allows Gap and Object Phases.
ALL PHASING EXPECTS A CONTROLLER.

options.label: Allow Enemy Phases
options.description:
This allows the use of Enemy phases in logic, which can be used to clip through walls wherever there is an enemy.
Turning this setting on also enables Object Phasing.
ALL PHASING EXPECTS A CONTROLLER.

options.label: Allow Difficult phases
options.description:
This allows difficult, precise, or annoying phases to be in logic, depending on your other phasing settings.
For example, you can now be expected to have to phase through room transitions without roll.
ALL PHASING EXPECTS A CONTROLLER.

options.label: Start With Tracker 3
options.description:
Start with Tracker 3 (and removes all Progressive Trackers from the pool),
allowing you to know where all locations in dungeons are.

options.label: Start With All Warps Unlocked
options.description:
Start with all the warps in the Warp Garden unlocked for convenience.
This will be disabled if Region Connection Blockades is on.

options.label: Lockpicks In Pool
options.description: Number of lockpicks to place in the pool. Lockpicks are not logically considered.

options.label: Crayons In Pool
options.description: Number of crayons to place in the pool.

options.label: Remove Cards From Pool
options.description:
Due to the limited pool size, you can turn this on to remove cards from the item pool if you're having errors
due to not having enough locations. This will only help if Include Dreamworld Dungeons is on as cards are not
items in the pool otherwise.

options.label: Normal Trap Percentage
options.description:
Percentage of filler items replaced with the following traps:
Bee Trap
Random Debuff Trap
Meteor Shower Trap

options.label: Debilitating Trap Percentage
options.description:
Percentage of filler items replaced with the following particularly debilitating traps:
Bee Onslaught
Matriarch Trap

options.label: Randomize Piano Puzzle
options.description:
Randomizes the Syncope piano puzzle.
The solution to the puzzle can be found in the room with the three knights.
Off: The solution will be the vanilla "DEAD"
Words: The solution will be a real word, 3-7 characters long, consisting of only white keys.
Black Keys: Same as Words, but some white keys are randomly replaced by black keys.
Full Random: The solution is a completely random string, 3-7 characters long, including white and black keys.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Sets the goal.
- Yu Yevon: Defeat Yu Yevon.
- Nemesis: Defeat Nemesis.

options.label: Goal Requirement
options.description:
Sets the requirement to start the final battles. Defeating Yu Yevon is always the goal.
- None: No requirements.
- Party Members: Requires unlocking a number of party members (not counting Aeons).
- Party Members and Aeons: Requires unlocking a number of party members (including Aeons).
- Pilgrimage: Complete all required temples, and defeat the boss in Zanarkand Ruins.
- Nemesis: Requires defeating Nemesis in the Monster Arena. To enable this option Capture Sanity must be enabled, and Creation Rewards & Arena Bosses must be set to Original Creations

options.label: Required Party Members
options.description:
Sets how many party members are required if goal_requirement is set to party_members or party_members_and_aeons.
Default is 7. Max is 8 for party_members, 16 for party_members_and_aeons.

options.label: Required Al Bhed Primers
options.description:
Set how many Al Bhed Primers are required to allow access to the goal.
This is in addition to the regular goal_requirement, meaning that for example, both Party Members & Primers may be required.

options.label: Ability Point Multiplier
options.description:
Sets the AP (Ability Point) multiplier.
Setting the multiplier to 0 will disable any AP gain (Effectively NSG - No Sphere Grid)
Default is 2.

options.label: Blitzball
options.description:
Sets whether Blitzball is included.
If off it will only have filler items.
This includes:
- Luca Story Blitzball win
- World Champion
- Wakka's Overdrives
- Jupiter Sigil

options.label: Macalania Butterflies
options.description:
Sets whether the Macalania Butterflies are included.
If off they will only have filler items.

options.label: Lightning Dodging
options.description:
Sets whether the Thunder Plains Lightning Dodging is included.
If off it will only have filler items.

options.label: Cactuar Village
options.description:
Sets whether the Bikanel Cactuar Village sidequest is included.
If off it will only have filler items.

options.label: Chocobo Training
options.description:
Sets whether the Calm Lands Chocobo Training minigames are included.
If off they will only have filler items.

options.label: Remiem Chocobo Race
options.description:
Sets whether the Remiem Temple Chocobo Race minigames are included.
If off they will only have filler items.

options.label: Recruit Sanity
options.description:
Sets whether Blitzball Free Agents are included or not. If off they will only have filler items.
There are 24 Free Agents throughout Spira. There are 59 total players throughout Spira.
Default is off.

options.label: Capture Sanity
options.description:
Sets whether Fiend Captures are included or not. If off they will only have filler items.
A check is included for the first capture of each of the 102 unique capturable fiends
Default is off.

options.label: Monster Arena Access
options.description:
The Monster Arena will be accessible directly from the Airship menu, instead of via the Calm Lands.
This option sets how the 'Region: Monster Arena' item will be placed in the multiworld.
- Normal: The Monster Arena region item will be placed in the multiworld, and captures will come into logic per region once the arena is accessible
- Early: The Monster Arena region item will be placed globally in sphere 1. Otherwise, the same as 'Normal'
- Always: Start with the Monster Arena region item, and captures will be in logic immediately per region.
Default is off.

options.label: Creation Rewards
options.description:
** Requires Capture Sanity **
Sets whether Monster Arena Creation Rewards are included or not. If off they will only have filler.
These rewards can be gained from the Monster Arena after completing any Area or Species Conquest, or unlocking an Original Creation
- Off: All arena rewards will be filler.
- Area: Only Area Conquest rewards will be in logic. Other rewards will only have filler.
- Species: Both Area & Species Conquest rewards will be in logic. Other rewards will only have filler.
- Original: All rewards will be in logic. This can require up to 10 captures of every fiend.
Default is off.

options.label: Arena Bosses
options.description:
** Requires Capture Sanity **
Sets whether Monster Arena boss locations are included or not. If off they will only have filler items.
Monster Arena bosses include all Area & Species Conquests, as well as the Original Creations.
- Off: All arena bosses will have filler.
- Area: Area Conquest bosses will be in logic. Other arena bosses will have filler.
- Species: Area & Species Conquest bosses will be in logic. Other arena bosses will have filler.
- Original: All arena bosses will be in logic, up to & including Nemesis.
Default is off.

options.label: Encounter Weighting
options.description:
** Requires Capture Sanity **
Sets how much more likely enemy formations are to appear in encounters
when they contain fiends that need to be captured.
- Disabled: No weighting will be done. This is the default option.
- Low: Remaining formations will be weighted a little.
- Comfortable: Remaining formations will be weighted a noticeable amount.
- Extreme: Remaining formations will be heavily weighted.

options.label: Super Bosses
options.description:
Sets whether Super Boss locations are included or not. If off they will only have filler items.
- Omega Weapon: Enables the Omega Weapon boss fight in Omega Ruins.
- Dark Aeons: Enables the Dark Aeon checks around Spira, as well as the above.
Default is off.

options.label: Jecht Spheres
options.description:
Sets whether Jecht Sphere locations are included or not. If off they will only have filler items.
Includes all 8 Jecht Spheres, as well as the Auron & Braska Sphere
Default is off.

options.label: Tidus's Overdrives
options.description:
Sets whether Tidus's Overdrive locations are included or not. If off they will only have filler items.
Default is off.

options.label: Tidus's Early Overdrive Access
options.description:
This option can provide early access to a random one of Tidus's overdrives, to allow for earlier logical access to his overdrive locations.
Tidus requires at least one of his overdrives to be able to begin grinding towards his others.
- Off: Tidus begins with zero overdrives, and his overdrive locations will only be in logic once he has access to at least one, as well as an appropriate number of combat regions.
- Early: A random one of Tidus's overdrives will be placed globally in sphere 1. Otherwise, the same as 'Off'.
- Start With: Tidus will start with one random overdrive. His overdrive locations will be in logic immediately depending on the number of combat regions available.
Default is off.

options.label: Kimahri's Ronso Rages
options.description:
Sets whether Kimahri's Ronso Rage locations are included or not. If off they will only have filler items.
Default is off.

options.label: Overdrive Modes
options.description:
Sets whether you will start with all overdrive modes enabled for each chararcter.
Default is off.

options.label: Traps Enabled
options.description:
Sets the percentage of non-progression items that will be traps.
Default is 0.

options.label: Logic Difficulty
options.description:
Sets how strict the logic is for region access. Higher is harder / less restrictive.
Default is 3.

options.label: Early Party Members
options.description:
Sets how many additional party members will be placed globally in sphere 1.
This will allow players to have access to more characters earlier.
This value does **NOT** include the starting character
Default is 0.

options.label: Always Sensor
options.description:
Sets whether to always have the Sensor ability active, regardless of equipped weapon abilities
Default is off.

options.label: Always Capture
options.description:
Sets whether to always have the Capture ability active, regardless of equipped weapon abilities
Default is off.

options.label: Capture Damage
options.description:
Sets which damage type(s) will trigger a capture attempt, assuming that you have a capture weapon or 'Always Capture' is enabled.
- Physical: Only physical damage originating from a party member (base game rules).
- All Direct: Any damage directly caused by a party member (or Aeon if 'Always Capture' is enabled). This includes items, magical damage and overdrives.
- All: Any damage caused by a party member (or Aeon if 'Always Capture' is enabled). This includes status effects.
  - Behaves the same as 'All Direct' when 'Always Capture' is disabled.
Default is Physical.

options.label: Skip Contest Of Aeons
options.description:
Sets whether to skip Contest of Aeons before fighting Yu Yevon.
Default is off.

options.label: Hardcore Dream's End
options.description:
Sets whether eternal auto-life is removed from the Contest of Aeons and Yu Yevon battles.
Default is off.

options.label: Customization Recipes
options.description:
Sets whether gear 
- Gear Customization items are required to be able to customize gear with their respective auto-abilities.
- Aeon Customization items are required to be able to teach aeons their respective abilities.

- Off:
    Customizations are always available. Gear/Aeon Customization items make one free.
- On:
    Customizations are only available after receiving the respective Gear/Aeon Customization item.
    Afterwards, the first customization is free.
- Always Free:
    Customizations are only available after receiving the respective Gear/Aeon Customization item.
    From then on, they are always free.
Default is off.

options.label: Deathlink
options.description:
Sets whether deathlink is enabled when you start a new game.
Default is off.

options.label: Deathlink Send Type
options.description:
Sets when a deathlink should be sent.
- Game Over: A deathlink will be sent when you game over.
- KO: A deathlink will be sent whenever a party member or aeon is KO'd.
Default is Game Over.

options.label: Deathlink Receive Type
options.description:
Sets what effect should occur at the start of the next battle after receiving a deathlink.
- Doom (Strict): All characters will start with a doom counter set to 1.
- Doom (Lenient): All characters will start with a doom counter set to 3.
- Grave HP: All characters will have their HP set to a random single-digit number.
- Bad Breath: All characters will start poisoned, silenced, blinded, and slowed.
- Random Type: A random effect will be applied for each deathlink received.
Default is Doom (Strict).

options.label: Sphere Grid Randomization
options.description:
Sets whether the Sphere Grid is randomized.
Default is off.

options.label: Starting Mainhand Weapon
options.description:
Sets your starting mainhand weapon.

none: Do not start with a mainhand weapon. Only valid if you select an offhand.  Some offhand weapons are difficult
    to do damage with, so be careful with this option.
random/random_proficient: Selects a mainhand or two-handed weapon your character is proficient with.
random_proficient_one_handed: Selects a one-handed weapon that your profession is proficient with.
random_proficient_two_handed: Selects a two-handed weapon that your profession is proficient with.

options.label: Starting Offhand Weapon
options.description:
Sets your starting offhand weapon.
This will be ignored if a two-handed weapon was selected for starting_mainhand_weapon

none: Do not start with an offhand weapon. Only valid if you select a mainhand.
random/random_proficient: Selects an offhand weapon your character is proficient with.

options.label: Group Content
options.description:
Sets what kind of group content you are interested in. Please be respectful of other players and do not join
pugs doing difficult content if you do not have the unlocks to contribute (Don't try to fight Dhuum naked)

none: Limits game to open world, story, and WvW (if competitive is selected)
five_man: Also allows fractals, dungeons, and PvP (if competitive is selected)
ten_man: Also allows raids and strikes

options.label: Include Competitive
options.description: Allows PvP and WvW achievements to be included

options.label: Achievement Weight
options.description: The probability weight of any location being an achievement

options.label: Quest Weight
options.description: The probability weight of any location being a quest

options.label: Max Quests
options.description:
The maximum number of quest locations to generate. The number of quests in each storyline are as follows:

Core => 49,
Season1 => 30,
Season2 => 32,
HeartOfThorns => 16,
Season3 => 36,
PathOfFire => 16,
Season4 => 30,
IcebroodSaga => 41,
EndOfDragons => 27,
SecretsOfTheObscure => 20,

options.label: Training Weight
options.description: The probability weight of any location being a skill/trait unlock

options.label: Max Training
options.description:
The maximum number of training locations to generate. The number of training in each storyline are as follows:

Core => 49,
Season1 => 0,
Season2 => 0,
HeartOfThorns => 16,
Season3 => 0,
PathOfFire => 16,
Season4 => 0,
IcebroodSaga => 0,
EndOfDragons => 27,
SecretsOfTheObscure => 0,

options.label: World Boss Weight
options.description: The probability weight of any location being a world boss

options.label: Unique Item Weight
options.description: The probability weight of any location being a purchase from a heart vendor (or similar for maps without hearts)

options.label: Poi Weight
options.description: The probability weight of any location being a point of interest (includes waypoints, vistas, and hero points)

options.label: Mist Fragments Required
options.description: The number of "Mist Fragment" items required to complete this world

options.label: Extra Mist Fragment Percent
options.description:
Multiplier to determine how many extra Mist Fragments to create. For example if mist_fragments_required is 20
and this is value is 50, there will be 30 Mist Fragments in the multi-world,
but only 20 will be required to finish.

options.label: Heal Skill
options.description: A random core heal skill could be placed early or given to the player as a starting skill

options.label: Gear Slots
options.description: Gear slots could be placed early or given to the player at the start

options.label: Storyline Items
options.description:
Which skills, traits, and weapons do you want shuffled into the item pool
all: all skills, traits, and weapons
core: only core skills, traits, and weapons
storyline: limit to core items plus those from the selected storyline. Living World storylines include the items
    from their associated expansion
storyline_plus: all items from the selected storyline and all preceding storylines.

options.label: Episode 1
options.description: Include Episode 1: The Foothills.

options.label: Episode 2
options.description: Include Episode 2: The Facilities.

options.label: Episode 3
options.description: Include Episode 3: The Nameless City.

options.label: Secret Levels
options.description: Include each included episode's secret level (E1MS, E2MS, E3MS). Their access is an item like any other level.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
bosses: finish the final level of every included episode (E1M10, E2M10, E3M10).
all_levels: finish every included level.

options.label: Randomize Weapons
options.description:
Weapon pickups (Pistol, Shotgun, Super Shotgun, Assault Rifle, Hunting Rifle, Crossbow, Mortar, Riveter, Sword)
become checks, and the weapons themselves are shuffled into the multiworld. ~270 checks.

options.label: Randomize Keys
options.description: Red/Blue/Yellow key pickups become checks, and each level's keys become items. ~90 checks.

options.label: Randomize Powerups
options.description:
Hallowed Health, Fast Fire Totem, Serum of Blistering Heat, Flashlight and Backpack pickups become checks.
Thermal Suits are never randomized. ~105 checks.

options.label: Randomize Secrets
options.description: Discovering a secret area is a check. ~165 checks.

options.label: Randomize Treasure Chests
options.description: Opening a treasure chest is a check. 16 checks.

options.label: Randomize Health
options.description: Medical kits, small medical kits and magic potions become checks. ~525 checks.

options.label: Randomize Morale (Armor)
options.description: Morale pickups (gold coins, bags of gems, diamonds) become checks. ~580 checks.

options.label: Randomize Ammo
options.description: Every ammo pickup becomes a check. ~1440 checks; this makes for a very long seed.

options.label: Combat Logic
options.description:
Only matters when weapons are randomized. How many distinct firearms (weapons other than the starting sickles
and the sword) the logic expects before a level is considered in logic. More required firearms means you arrive
better armed. Each episode's first level never needs any; secret levels need as many as the end of their episode.
exorcist: for testing. Every check outside E1M1 needs all 10 weapons (both Progressive Pistols, both Progressive
          Shotguns and the other six; not the Sword), so all 10 are placed in E1M1. If Episode 1 is off, the
          first included episode's first level takes E1M1's place.
easy: Episode 1 needs 1 from E1M3 and 2 from E1M6; Episode 2 needs 2 from E2M2 and 3 from E2M6; Episode 3
      needs 3 from E3M2 and 4 from E3M6.
normal: Episode 1 needs 1 from E1M6; Episode 2 needs 1 from E2M2 and 2 from E2M6; Episode 3 needs 2 from E3M2
        and 3 from E3M6.
unhinged: no combat logic. Sickles are enough for everything; you may play a long time with only them.

options.label: Victory Locations
options.description: How many checks are sent per level completed.

options.label: Objective Locations
options.description: How many checks are sent per side objective completed.

options.label: Income Boost
options.description: How much extra income the player gets per turn per boost received.

options.label: Commander Defense Boost
options.description: How much extra defense the player's commander gets per boost received.

options.label: Groove Boost
options.description: How much extra groove the player's commander gets per boost received.

options.label: Level Shuffle Seed
options.description: What seed to use for level shuffling. 0 uses the world seed.

options.label: Commander Choice
options.description:
How the player's commander is selected for missions.

- Locked Random: The player's commander is randomly predetermined for each level.

- Unlockable Factions: The player starts with Mercival and can unlock playable factions.

- Random Starting Faction:  The player starts with a random starting faction and can unlock the rest.

When playing with unlockable factions, faction items are added to the pool.

options.label: Enabled Commanders
options.description:
The commanders available to the player and the AI.
If no commanders are enabled, Mercival will be the only available commander.

Format as a comma-separated list of commander names: ["Mercia", "Valder"]

options.label: FinalLevels
options.description: How many final levels to beat before victory is achieved.

options.label: Player Sacrifice Limit
options.description:
How many times the player can sacrifice a unit at the Stronghold per level attempt.
Sacrificed units are stored in the multiworld for other players to summon.

options.label: Player Summon Limit
options.description:
How many times the player can summon a unit at the Stronghold per level attempt.
Summoned units are from the multiworld which were sacrificed by other players.

options.label: AI Sacrifice Limit
options.description:
How many times the AI can sacrifice a unit at the Stronghold per level attempt.
Sacrificed units are stored in the multiworld for other AIs to summon.

options.label: AI Summon Limit
options.description:
How many times the AI can summon a unit at the Stronghold per level attempt.
Summoned units are from the multiworld which were sacrificed by other AIs.
If a level becomes impossible, use /sacrifice_summon in the client to toggle sacrifices and summons on and off.

options.label: Player Barracks Early Sphere Cost
options.description:
The cost multiplier of units purchased from the player's barracks in earlier spheres.
The map's victory item determines the sphere number.
If a level becomes impossible, use /toggle_costs in the client to toggle dynamic unit costs on and off.
