Incorporates Astral Codec story mod content into the randomizer with an additional 1 item and 21 locations.
If logsanity is enabled, that will add another 39 locations, for a total of 60 AC locations.

If randomize_warp_platforms is true, this option will ensure there's a warp from the Hourglass Twins to Timber Hearth.

options.label: Enable Hearth's Neighbor 2: Magistarium Story Mod
options.description:
Incorporates Hearth's Neighbor 2: Magistarium story mod content into the randomizer with an additional 4 items and 18 locations.
If logsanity is enabled, that will add another 30 locations, for a total of 48 HN2 locations.

options.label: Enable Fret's Quest Story Mod
options.description:
Incorporates Fret's Quest story mod content into the randomizer with an additional 1 item and 20 locations.
If logsanity is enabled, that will add another 38 locations, for a total of 58 FQ locations.

options.label: Enable Forgotten Castaways Story Mod
options.description:
Incorporates Forgotten Castaways story mod content into the randomizer with an additional 13 items and 54 locations.
If logsanity is enabled, that will add another 118 locations, for a total of 172 FC locations.

options.label: Enable Echo Hike Story Mod
options.description:
Incorporates Echo Hike story mod content into the randomizer with an additional 1 item and 3 locations.
If logsanity is enabled, that will add another 8 locations, for a total of 11 EH locations.
The main appeal of this mod is the unique "Threader" item, which is a grapple beam/hook that works on any
surface in the game.
When this is enabled, using the Threader will be in-logic for multiple base game, DLC and story mod
locations outside of Echo Hike itself, and receiving the "Threader" AP item will spawn Threaders
on all the base game, DLC and story mod planets/areas where you might need one.

options.label: Enable Heliostudy Story Mod
options.description:
Incorporates Heliostudy story mod content into the randomizer with an additional 5 items and 20 locations.
If logsanity is enabled, that will add another 28 locations, for a total of 48 HS locations.

options.label: DLC
options.description: Set whether or not to use Delicious Last Course content (Requires owning the DLC).

options.label: Mode
options.description:
Set the mode of the randomizer which includes goal.
NOTE: If DLC is not enabled, picking DLC modes will pick a random mode from the base game instead.

options.label: Logic
options.description:
-HARD LOGIC WORKS, BUT IS INCOMPLETE-
Set the logic mode.
Hard: Use more difficult logic that may require more skillful actions without specific items.

options.label: Expert Mode
options.description: Set the boss difficulty to expert.

options.label: Start Weapon
options.description:
Choose weapon to start with.
NOTE: If DLC is not enabled, picking DLC weapons will pick a random base game weapon instead.

options.label: Weapon Mode
options.description:
Set how the weapons are shuffled in the pool.
Options:
- Normal: EX is part of the weapon you receive (vanilla behavior).
- Progressive: turns the weapons in the pool into progressive weapons (plane has a separate EX item).
- EX Separate makes each weapon's EX ability a separate item.
- ... Except Start: makes the start weapon have normal behavior.
Notes:
- "Progressive" means that weapon EX is unlocked from having two of the same weapon.
- A weapon EX item without the base weapon will give you a weapon that only can do EX shots.

options.label: Starting Max Health
options.description:
Set starting max health.
NOTE: Health cannot be any higher than 9, so health charms would be less useful at higher health amounts.

options.label: Starting Max Health
options.description:
Set starting max health for Player 2. Set to 0 to use Player 1's max health.
NOTE: Health cannot be any higher than 9, so health charms would be less useful at higher health amounts.

options.label: Contract Requirements
options.description:
Set the amount of contracts needed to confront King Dice and, ultimately, the devil.
The required contracts for the die houses are evenly distributed.

options.label: [DLC] Ingredient Requirements
options.description:
-DLC ONLY-
Set the amount of ingredients needed to confront Saltbaker.

options.label: Contract Goal Requirements
options.description:
Set the amount of contracts needed for goal.
Note: Cannot be lower than Contract Requirements

options.label: [DLC] Ingredient Goal Requirements
options.description:
-DLC ONLY-
Set the amount of ingredients needed for goal.
Note: Cannot be lower than Ingredient Requirements

options.label: Level Shuffle
options.description:
Shuffle the Boss and Run n' Gun levels.
Bosses and Run n' Guns are shuffled within their own group.
Note: Be careful with this option! This can easily break generation if used with plando.

options.label: Shuffle King Dice Bosses
options.description:
Shuffle the King Dice mini-bosses.
This option is independent of Level Shuffle.

options.label: Level Placements
options.description:
Define which levels will be placed in which spots when shuffling the levels.
Note: Some levels cannot be shuffled, and some levels cannot be placed in specific spots.
Key: original, Value: new

options.label: Free Move Isles
options.description: Allow all the levels on each island to be freely accessible without completing a previous level first.

options.label: Death Link
options.description:
Enable DeathLink. When you die, everyone dies. Of course the reverse is true too.
In Cuphead, this only applies while you are in a level.

options.label: Death Link Mode
options.description:
-REQUIRES DEATHLINK-
Set DeathLink Mode.

Modes:
- Lose: Both players dying triggers DeathLink. Same in reverse.
- Per Player: Each player's death will trigger DeathLink. Receiving a DeathLink will kill a random player.

NOTE: Per Player will behave like Lose if playing singleplayer.

This option is ignored on older clients that don't support this feature

options.label: Death Link Grace Count
options.description:
-REQUIRES DEATHLINK-
Set DeathLink Grace Count. Each "Grace" grants you a free Death without triggering DeathLink.

options.label: Randomize Abilities
options.description: Randomize essential abilities like Crouch, Parry, Dash, etc.

options.label: Boss Secret Checks
options.description:
Also include beating the secret phases that certain bosses have as checks.
The boss levels include: Botanic Panic, Pyramid Peril, Dramatic Fanatic, and Doggone Dogfight (DLC).
The secret phases are generally more difficult than the normal fight.

options.label: Boss Grade Checks
options.description:
Enable grade checks for Boss Levels.
NOTE: S Grade option will be treated as A+ Grade if Expert Mode is disabled.

options.label: Run n' Gun Grade Checks
options.description:
Enable grade checks for Run n' Gun levels.
Pacifist: Beat the level without killing any monsters (not easy).

options.label: King Dice BossSanity
options.description:
---NOT YET IMPLEMENTED---
Enable checks for beating the King Dice mini-bosses.
There is an indicator for which mini-bosses you defeated.

options.label: [DLC] Boss Chalice Checks
options.description:
-DLC ONLY-
-REQUIRES CHALICE-
Enable checks for defeating each boss as Ms. Chalice.
Separate makes Chalice checks separate from level completion checks.
Grade Required has the set grade check requirement for bosses.

options.label: [DLC] Run n' Gun Chalice Checks
options.description:
-DLC ONLY-
-REQUIRES CHALICE-
Enable checks for completing each run n' gun as Ms. Chalice.
Separate makes Chalice checks separate from level completion checks.
Grade Required has the set grade check requirement for run n' guns.

options.label: [DLC] King Dice Chalice Checks
options.description:
--NOT YET IMPLEMENTED--
-DLC ONLY-
-REQUIRES CHALICE-
-REQUIRES KING DICE BOSSSANITY-
Enable checks for completing King Dice Bossanity checks as Ms. Chalice.

options.label: [DLC] Chess Chalice Checks
options.description:
-DLC ONLY-
-REQUIRES CHALICE-
-REQUIRES THE KING'S LEAP-
Enable checks for completing The King's Leap checks as Ms. Chalice.

options.label: Silverworth Quest
options.description:
Enable the Silverworth Quest check.
This means that you will have to beat 15 levels with at least an A- Grade in order to get this check.

options.label: Pacifist Quest
options.description:
Enable the Pacifist Quest check.
This means that you will have to beat all 6 Run n' Gun levels without beating any enemies (not easy).

options.label: [DLC] Ms. Chalice
options.description:
-DLC ONLY-
Enable Ms. Chalice and the Astral Cookie.
Options:
- Disabled: The cookie is disabled and cannot be obtained (Ms. Chalice is disabled).
- Start: The cookie is available at the start of the game.
- Vanilla: The cookie is obtained at the start of the DLC (Vanilla Behavior).
- Randomized: The cookie is in the item pool. Starting the DLC is a check.

options.label: [DLC] Chalice Items Separate
options.description:
---NOT YET IMPLEMENTED---
-DLC ONLY-
Make certain items seperate for when playing as Ms. Chalice.
Options:
- Core Items: Core items like plane and supers.
- Abilities: Abilities including parry.

With parry for Ms. Chalice, the Parry item is replaced with Progressive Dash.
Progressive Dash has two levels: 1. Dash only, 2. Dash with Parry.

Note: Chalice Double Jump is randomized regardless of this option if Randomize Abilities is on.

options.label: [DLC] The King's Leap
options.description:
-DLC ONLY-
Choose how to handle the locations of The King's Leap.
Gauntlet is the run where you have to defeat all the King's Leap bosses in succession.

options.label: [DLC] The King's Leap P. Sugar
options.description:
-DLC ONLY-
-REQUIRES THE KING'S LEAP-
Allow P. Sugar to be used in the King's Leap levels. Vanilla behavior only allows Parry.

options.label: [DLC] Cactus Girl Quest
options.description:
-DLC ONLY-
-REQUIRES CHALICE-
Enable the Cactus Girl Quest (aka Ms. Chalice Quest) check.
This means that you will have to beat EVERY boss as Ms. Chalice (tedious) for a single check.
You can talk to the Cactus Girl to know which bosses you need to defeat still.

options.label: [DLC] Curse Mode
options.description:
-DLC ONLY-
Set how the cursed and devine relic is handled.

Modes:
- Off: Broken Relic is removed from the game
- Vanilla: Broken Relic is in pool. The graveyard and getting the devine relic is excluded from logic.

options.label: Early Parry
options.description:
Make Parry be placed early in the multiworld.
This may prevent early BK.
NOTE: This is on regardless in single player multiworlds.

options.label: Extra Coins
options.description: Set extra coins in the item pool.

options.label: Max Health Upgrades
options.description:
Set number of max health upgrades in the pool.
NOTE: Health cannot be any higher than 9, so health charms would be less useful at higher health amounts.

options.label: Minimum Filler Items
options.description:
Set the minimum amount of filler items that should exist in this world.
NOTE: If there are not enough locations, some coins will be compressed into packs of 2 or 3 to make space.

options.label: Traps
options.description:
---NOT YET IMPLEMENTED ON CLIENT---
Set Trap percentage for filler items.

options.label: Extra Health Weight
options.description:
Set Extra Health weight. Higher weight means it will more likely appear compared to other filler items.
Set to 0 to disable this item.

options.label: Super Recharge Weight
options.description:
Set Super Recharge weight. Higher weight means it will more likely appear compared to other filler items.
Set to 0 to disable this item.

options.label: Fast Fire Weight
options.description:
Set Fast Fire weight. Higher weight means it will more likely appear compared to other filler items.
Set to 0 to disable this item.

options.label: Loadout Mixup Any Item
options.description:
For Loadout Mixup Trap:
Allow Loadout Mixup to use any item including ones you do not currently have.

options.label: Finger Jam Trap Weight
options.description:
Set Finger Jam Trap weight. Higher weight means it will more likely appear compared to other traps.
Set to 0 to disable this trap.

options.label: Slow Fire Trap Weight
options.description:
Set Slow Fire Trap weight. Higher weight means it will more likely appear compared to other traps.
Set to 0 to disable this trap.

options.label: Super Drain Trap Weight
options.description:
Set Super Drain Trap weight. Higher weight means it will more likely appear compared to other traps.
Set to 0 to disable this trap.

options.label: Loadout Mixup Trap Weight
options.description:
Set Loadout Mixup Trap weight. Higher weight means it will more likely appear compared to other traps.
Set to 0 to disable this trap.

options.label: Music Shuffle
options.description:
---NOT YET IMPLEMENTED ON CLIENT---
Enable Shuffling Music.
NOTE: This option will do nothing until the client is updated

options.label: DuckLock PlatDrop
options.description:
Allow the dropping-down-platforms-without-duck-by-using-aim-lock exploit.
This option re-enables that bug that the mod had before alpha02.
This "feature" is purely client-side and does not affect logic.

options.label: Contract Requirements Isle2
options.description:
Internal. Set during generation.
Amount of contracts needed to access Inkwell Isle II

options.label: Contract Requirements Isle3
options.description:
Internal. Set during generation.
Amount of contracts needed to access Inkwell Isle III

options.label: Starting Characters
options.description: Number of randomly selected non-GBA golfers available when the seed starts.

options.label: Shuffle Progressive Characters
options.description: Shuffle two progressive copies per golfer: base first, then star.

options.label: Shuffle Progressive Star Stages
options.description: Compatibility partner for Shuffle Characters; both values must match.

options.label: Club Distribution
options.description:
Choose how the thirteen standard non-putter clubs are distributed.

Global Club Unlocks and Unique Character Bags use Starting Clubs. Balanced
Character Bags always gives every golfer one wood, one iron, and one wedge.

options.label: Starting Clubs
options.description:
Number of starting clubs for Global or Unique Character Bags.

Global Club Unlocks gives the same selected clubs to every golfer. Unique
Character Bags selects this many clubs independently for every golfer.
Vanilla and Balanced Character Bags ignore this setting.

options.label: Shuffle Advance Tour Custom Club Sets
options.description: Shuffle all 15 club sets transferable from Mario Golf: Advance Tour.

options.label: Shuffle Advance Tour Golfers (Neil and Ella)
options.description: Shuffle one item that adds default Neil and Ella transfer profiles.

options.label: Advance Tour Golfer Stats
options.description: Choose the driving-distance profile for AP-created Neil and Ella.

options.label: Shuffle Tournaments
options.description: Shuffle the six physical courses used by both Tournament menus.

options.label: Starting Regular Courses
options.description:
Number of random regular courses available at seed start.

A course item grants that course in regular Tournament, Star Tournament,
Stroke Play, Speed Golf, and Character Match. Ring Attack retains its
vanilla sequential course progression. At least one physical course is
always available at seed start.

options.label: Shuffle Modes
options.description: Shuffle game-mode access, including Putting Practice.

options.label: Starting Modes
options.description:
Number of modes available when mode shuffling is on.

The starting selection always includes Tournament or Ring Attack.

options.label: Shuffle Power Shot Capacity
options.description: Shuffle Tournament and Stroke Play Power Shot capacity above the start.

options.label: Starting Power Shot Capacity
options.description: Tournament and Stroke Play starting capacity when capacity is shuffled.

options.label: Shuffle Putter Ranges and Approach Shot
options.description: Start with one putter range; shuffle the other ranges and Approach Shot.

options.label: Putter Range Unlock Scope
options.description: Choose whether shuffled putter lengths are global or owned per golfer.

options.label: Approach Shot Unlock Scope
options.description: Choose whether Approach Shot is global or unlocked for each golfer.

options.label: Shuffle Putting Practice Difficulties
options.description: Shuffle Novice, Intermediate, and Expert Putting Practice access.

options.label: Spin Unlocks
options.description: Choose whether spin inputs are vanilla, globally shuffled, or per golfer.

options.label: Tournament Win Per Character Checks
options.description: Add one check for winning any tournament with each of the 16 golfers.

options.label: Character Match Win Per Course Checks
options.description:
Add one check for winning a Character Match on each regular course.

These six locations require a human Pro-difficulty victory and a verified
course result. They can be disabled for a smaller location pool.

options.label: Character Match Pro Challenge Checks
options.description:
Add two global Pro-difficulty Character Match checks.

Win five consecutive holes in one match (a tie or loss breaks the streak),
and win a match by at least seven holes. Only the human player's results
count. These checks do not change the Pro opponent goal requirements.
These demanding checks contain only non-progression rewards.

options.label: Character Match Course Access
options.description:
Choose whether regular Character Match courses start open.

Toadstool Tour uses the same six availability bits for Character Match and
regular Tournament courses. The default links both menus to the shuffled
regular Tournament items. The compatibility choice exposes all six in both
modes and therefore precollects all six regular Tournament access items.

options.label: Ring Attack Player Counts
options.description: Choose which Ring Attack player-count checks are included.

options.label: Individual Best Badge Checks (108)
options.description: Add one local check for birdie-or-better on each regular course hole.

options.label: Coin Attack Checks
options.description: Add per-golfer cumulative and per-hole Coin Attack checks.

options.label: Speed Golf Time Checks
options.description:
Add ten Speed Golf checks: each full course under 10 minutes, a full
round under 15 minutes while under par, any hole under 15 seconds,
a par 4 under 30 seconds, and a par 5 under 40 seconds.
Time thresholds are strict: exactly 30/40 seconds does not qualify.

options.label: Practice and Birdie Challenge Clear Checks
options.description: Add supported Practice clears and Birdie Challenge Front 9.

options.label: Congo Canopy Stroke Play Score Checks
options.description: Add the supported Congo Canopy Front 9 Stroke Play score check.

options.label: Congo Canopy Required Score to Par
options.description: Required score relative to par for each enabled Congo Canopy check.

options.label: Near-Pin Aggregate Distance Target (Feet)
options.description: Maximum saved total distance for the aggregate Near-Pin check.

options.label: Deferred Special-Mode Checks (Unavailable)
options.description: Reserved compatibility option; Part D checks are deferred and never generated.

options.label: 300-Yard Drive Check (Experimental)
options.description:
Experimental: add Drive 300 Yards for P1's first tee shot (non-putter).

Counts final distance including roll, using the retail yardage display's
data. The client must be connected before the tee shot. CPU shots, later
strokes, imported saves and in-flight peaks do not count. This optional
check has passed live testing but cannot hold progression items.

options.label: Cumulative Driving and Putting Checks (Experimental)
options.description:
Experimental slot-wide checks: drive 100,000 yards and sink over 1,000
feet of putts. Counts completed P1 tee shots including roll, and holed
putts only, shared across all your golfers. CPU shots and missed putts do
not count. Totals and unsent credits are journaled across client restarts.
Stay connected before each shot; one gameplay client per slot. Neither
location can hold progression. The final 100,000-yard threshold and the
cumulative putting check still need end-to-end playtesting.

options.label: Native In-Game Unlock Messages
options.description:
Choose client-only text or experimental serialized in-game notices.

One AP notice is allocated through the game's text system at a time. It
retires after about three seconds or a detected transition; waiting notices
stay queued. Native game dialogs are not replaced. Requires the matching
release patch. Recent live tests passed, but wider transition coverage is
still needed. Client-only remains the conservative default.

options.label: Gale Force Winds Trap Count
options.description: Number of Gale Force Winds traps placed into the multiworld item pool.

options.label: Gale Force Winds Speed (MPH)
options.description:
Wind speed applied to the next eligible hole by Gale Force Winds.

Defaults to 99 MPH, which has passed live testing. Choose 20–99 MPH
for a gentler or stronger trap. Direction stays random. This does
nothing when there are no trap receipts; trap count defaults to zero.

options.label: Visual Gate Indicators
options.description:
Dim unowned native portraits and main-mode icons.

Only the 16 native portraits are covered. Selected
owned golfers retain retail's selected shading. Hidden portraits stay
hidden. Main-mode icons follow each player count's actual retail menu.
This does not change selection permissions. Advance Tour portraits and
child/difficulty screens are not covered.

options.label: Multiplayer Ring Attack Bags (Experimental)
options.description:
Experimental P2-P4 standard-club restrictions in Ring Attack.

Assigned Native Bags uses each native golfer's own received club items,
or the global bag in Global Club Unlocks. P1 is unchanged; CPUs and other
modes are untouched. Transfer golfers and P2-P4 putter lengths/techniques
retain retail behavior. Requires the matching 1.1.0 patch, including the
automatic-club selection fix. Keep the default for retail P2-P4 bags.

options.label: Enable Development Debug Commands
options.description: Allow server-backed item and location cheat commands for testing.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Choose the accomplishments that complete this Archipelago slot.

Best Badge goals require 50 or 100 distinct course-hole badges. They
automatically enable individual Best Badge checks so Archipelago retains
progress across reconnects and retail save resets. Repeating a birdie on
the same hole does not add another badge.

Win Bowser Star Championship requires first place in that Star tournament.
Owning Bowser Badlands, a top-three finish, or its regular tournament win
does not complete this goal.

options.label: Viral Sensation Goal
options.description:
Reach 1,000,000 views in a single quota.
Fired by the client when the threshold is crossed in-game.

options.label: Views Goal
options.description:
Reach the configurable lifetime view target (Views Goal Target).
Requires Views Checks to be enabled — if Views Checks is off, this
goal is treated as off.

options.label: Views Checks
options.description:
When enabled, lifetime-view milestone locations are part of the pool.
Disable to remove all view threshold locations from generation.
If off, views_goal is invalid.

options.label: Views Goal Target
options.description:
When Views Goal is enabled, the lifetime view total required to win.
The world uses the nearest lifetime-view milestone at or above this value.
Maximum 33,739,000 — the highest reachable lifetime total at the maximum
quota count (day 63).

options.label: Quota Goal
options.description:
Reach and complete the configured number of quotas.
Requires Quota Requirement to be enabled — if Quota Requirement is off,
this goal is treated as off.

options.label: Quota Requirement
options.description:
When enabled, quota checks are included in the location pool and
completing quotas can be part of the goal.
When disabled, all quota-related checks are removed from the pool.
If turned off, the Quota Goal will be invalid.

options.label: Quota Count
options.description:
The number of quotas to play through.  Drives the active count of
Quota / Day Extraction / Sponsorship locations and (if Quota Goal is on)
the number required to win.
Each quota is 3 days, so day-extraction checks run from day 1 to
QuotaCount * 3.  Sponsorship checks run from 1 to QuotaCount - 1
(capped at 20).

options.label: Monster Hunter Goal
options.description:
Film a configurable number of distinct monsters (Monster Hunter Count)
to win.

options.label: Monster Hunter Count
options.description:
When Monster Hunter is enabled, the number of distinct monsters that
must be filmed to win.  Minimum 5, maximum 33.
Note: an average 5-quota run encounters 15-20 monsters.

options.label: Monster Tiers
options.description:
When enabled, each non-difficult filmable monster gains two additional
filming location checks (2nd and 3rd sightings).  Adds up to 42 extra
location checks across non-difficult monsters and artifacts.  No new
logic is added beyond the dungeon-depth rules of the base check.

options.label: Filler Multi-Sightings
options.description:
When enabled, all 2nd / 3rd sighting locations created by Monster
Tiers hold filler items only — no progression items spawn there.
Disable to let real items spawn behind multi-sighting checks at the
cost of more required dives.  No effect when Monster Tiers is off.

options.label: Difficult Monsters Have Real Items
options.description:
When enabled, difficult/rare monsters (Flicker, Cam Creep, Infiltrator,
Black Hole Bot, Ear, Snail Spawner, Big Slap, Ultra Knifo, Weeping)
can have real (non-filler) items behind their base filming checks.
Tier 2 / Tier 3 of difficult monsters always remain filler regardless
of this option.

options.label: Hat Collector Goal
options.description: Purchase a configurable number of hats (Hat Collector Count) to win.

options.label: Hat Collector Count
options.description:
When Hat Collector is enabled, the number of hats that must be
purchased to win.  Minimum 5, maximum 31 (total hats available).

options.label: Include Sponsorships
options.description:
When enabled, sponsorship checks are included in the pool.
Each completed sponsorship grants the next sponsorship check in
order; the active count per seed is QuotaCount - 1, capped at 20.

options.label: Sponsor Filler
options.description:
When enabled (default), all sponsor locations contain filler items.
Sponsorships are RNG-dependent and can be hard to complete; this keeps
progression away from them by default.  Disable to let progression items
spawn at sponsor locations.

options.label: Multiplayer Mode
options.description:
Enable if this game is played in multiplayer (more than one player).
When enabled, multiplayer-only monster locations (Weeping) are added to
the world and can receive real items.
When disabled (default / solo play), those locations are completely
omitted from generation — the player would never be able to film them
without other players in the lobby.

options.label: Death Link
options.description:
Enable Death Link. When enabled, if any player in the Death Link group
dies in their respective game, all players in that group will die.
Content Warning counts as dead when the entire team wipes. If the team is not in the old world
when another player dies they will not be affected by Death Link until they return to the old world.

options.label: Board Expansion Amount
options.description:
How much a Board Expansion item will increase the card limit by.
If <Board Expansion Mode> option is 'Vanilla' then this setting will be ignored.

NOTE: The card limit for your run will be capped at 20 + (Expansion Amount * Expansion Count).
      The lower you set Expansion Amount and Expansion Count, the more challenging resource management will be.
      Physical board size will still be capped at the largest vanilla size (without Lighthouses).

options.label: Board Expansion Count
options.description:
How many 'Board Expansion' items are added to the item pool for each compatible board (Mainland & Island).
If <Board Expansion Mode> option is 'Vanilla' then this setting will be ignored.

NOTE: The card limit for your run will be capped at 20 + (Expansion Amount * Expansion Count).
      The lower you set Expansion Amount and Expansion Count, the more challenging resource management will be.
      Physical board size will still be capped at the largest vanilla size (without Lighthouses).

options.label: Enable Pausing
options.description:
The player keeps the ability to be able to pause time.
If disabled, time will only be paused by cutscenes and end-of-moon routines.

options.label: Equipmentsanity
options.description:
Add checks for crafting one of each Equipment card. (E.g. Club, Sword, Blunderbuss etc.)
Will only add checks for Equipment that are reachable on the boards selected in the <Boards> option.

This will add 16 checks to Mainland and 6 checks to The Island.

options.label: Foodsanity
options.description:
Add checks for cooking one of each Food card. (E.g. Stew, Fruit Salad, Tamago Sushi etc.)
Will only add checks for Foods that are reachable on the boards selected in the <Boards> option.

This will add 3 checks to Mainland and 3 checks to The Island.

options.label: Locationsanity
options.description:
Add checks for exploring one of each Location card. (E.g. Mountain, Old Village, Jungle etc.)
Will only add checks for Locations that are reachable on the boards selected in the <Boards> option.

This will add 4 checks to Mainland and 2 checks to The Island.

options.label: Mobsanity
options.description:
Add checks for killing one of each Mob card. (E.g. Elf, Giant Snail, Tiger etc.)
Will only add checks for Mobs that are reachable on the boards selected in the <Boards> option.

This will add 18 checks to Mainland, 3 checks to The Dark Forest and 9 checks to The Island.

options.label: Mobsanity Balancing
options.description:
Greatly increases chance for all Packs / Strange Portals / Dark Forest Waves to spawn reachable Mobs that you have not yet killed.

It is recommended to set this to 'true' to prevent relying on RNG to reach all Mobsanity checks.
If set to 'false' you will be at the mercy of RNG to spawn all Mob types to reach all Mobsanity checks.

This setting is ignored if the <Mobsanity> option is 'false'.

options.label: Structuresanity
options.description:
Add checks for building one of each reachable Structure card. (E.g Garden, Market, Distillery etc.)
Will only add checks for Structures that are reachable on the boards selected in the <Boards> option.

This will add 16 checks to Mainland and 10 checks to The Island.

options.label: Trap Fill Percentage
options.description:
The percentage of the filler item pool that should be populated with trap items.

0   -> No trap items will be included in the filler item pool
25  -> Approximately 25% of the filler item pool will be trap items
50  -> Approximately 50% of the filler item pool will be trap items
etc.

options.label: Feed Villagers Trap Weighting
options.description:
The weighting of Feed Villagers Trap in the trap pool.
The higher this number relative to the other trap weightings, the more often it is likely to appear.

Feed Villager Trap will force all villagers on the current board to be fed - villagers not fed will die.

If <Trap Fill> is 0 then this setting will be ignored.

options.label: Mob Trap Weighting
options.description:
The weighting of Mob Traps in the trap pool.
The higher this number relative to the other trap weightings, the more often it is likely to appear.

Mob Traps will spawn a random, basic enemy to the current board - killing mobs from Mob Traps will not count towards Mobsanity checks.

If <Trap Fill> is 0 then this setting will be ignored.

options.label: Sell Cards Trap Weighting
options.description:
The weighting of Sell Cards Trap in the trap pool
The higher this number relative to the other trap weightings, the more often it is likely to appear.

Sell Cards Trap forces you to immediately sell <Sell Cards Trap Amount> of cards from the current board.

If <Trap Fill> is 0 then this setting will be ignored.

options.label: Sell Cards Trap Amount
options.description:
How many cards a Sell Cards Trap will force you to sell.

You will be forced to sell this amount of all sellable cards when you receive this trap. If you have fewer than
this amount, you will instead be forced to sell all remaining sellable cards.

If <Trap Fill> is 0 or <Sell Cards Trap Weight> is 0 then this setting will be ignored.

options.label: Strange Portal Trap Weighting
options.description:
The weighting of Strange Portal Trap items in the trap pool.
The higher this number relative to the other trap weightings, the more often it is likely to appear.

Strange Portal Traps will spawn a Strange Portal to the current board.
Portals from these traps cannot be used to travel to The Dark Forest and killing enemies spawned from these Portals will not count towards Mobsanity checks.

If <Trap Fill> is 0 then this setting will be ignored.

options.label: Characters
options.description:
Select the character(s) to include.

To include all supported characters, set to [ "All" ] or [].
To select specific characters, set to a list of supported character names.

NOTE: Currently only supports Rodman, Nina Nix, Hayley Bayles, Sam Gambit, Bones the Dog and Octacles.
      Additional characters will be supported in a future update.

options.label: Starting Character
options.description:
Select the character (from the <Characters> option) to start with.

To select a random character from the <Characters> option, set to [ "Random" ] or []
To select a random character from a specific set, set to a list of one or more names from the <Characters> option.

Names in the list that do not match those selected from <Characters> are ignored.

options.label: Required Sticker Synergies
options.description:
Each character logically requires 5 Stickers that synergise to 'reasonably' beat Stage 5.

To use the preset synergy, leave a character as [ "Default" ] or [].
To use a custom synergy, set a character to a list of exactly 5 Sticker names.

Stickers in the synergy will be guaranteed in the item pool and treated as progression items.

options.label: Required Stamp Synergies
options.description:
Each character logically requires 5 Stamps that synergise to 'reasonably' beat Stage 5.

To use the preset synergy, leave a character as [ "Default" ] or [].
To use a custom synergy, set a character to a list of exactly 5 Stamp names.

Stamps in the synergy will be guaranteed in the item pool and treated as progression items.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Select the condition that the character(s) must reach to achieve the goal.

Runs    -> All <Goal Characters> must successfully beat at least one run.
Michael -> All <Goal Characters> must successfully beat Michael at least once.
Crowns  -> All <Goal Characters> must beat the highest <Crowns> tier at least once.

Michael goal requires <Michael> = 'True' and will be automatically adjusted if prerequisite not met.
Crowns goal requires <Crowns> = 'Purple' (or higher) and will be automatically adjusted to 'Purple' if prerequisite not met.

options.label: Goal Characters
options.description:
Select the <Characters> that are required to complete the <Goal> condition to reach the goal.

To select all characters from the <Characters> option, set to [ "All" ] or []
To select characters from a specific set, set to a list of one or more names from the <Characters> option.

Names in the list that do not match those selected from <Characters> are ignored.

options.label: Include Michael
options.description:
Include locations for obtaining 5 Fairies and beating Michael for all selected <Characters>.

NOTE: The earliest Michael can be reached is via a Purple Crown run so if <Crowns> = 'None', it will be automatically adjusted to 'Purple' to ensure generation succeeds.
      This means each of your selected <Characters> will need to receive one '{Character}: Progressive Crown' to reach Michael.

WARNING: This setting will add (<Characters> count * 8) locations to your location pool.

options.label: Include Crowns
options.description:
Include locations for clearing all stages up to a maximum Crown tier for all selected <Characters>.

Crown Tiers are unlocked by receiving '{Character}: Progressive Crown' items which make the next Crown Tier reachable for each selected <Characters>.
The selected Crown tier will include ALL CROWN TIERS BELOW IT because crown progression remains as per vanilla (you must beat Purple before you can move on to Yellow etc).

EXAMPLES:
None    -> Does not include any Crown tiers.
Yellow  -> Includes Purple and Yellow Crown tiers.
Green   -> Includes Purple, Yellow, Orange, Pink and Green tiers.

NOTE: If <Goal> = 'Crowns' and this setting is 'None', it will be automatically adjusted to 'Purple' to ensure generation succeeds.

WARNING: This setting will add (<Characters> count * <Crowns> count * 15) locations to your location pool.

options.label: Money Earned Locations
options.description:
Sets the highest 'Money Earned' amount to include as locations from a pre-defined scaling curve.
Value is clamped to the closest location value (equal to or less than) in the curve - e.g. 387 is clamped to 350.

Locations are checked when the total money gained during a single run is equal to or greater than the required amount.

DIFFICULTY GUIDE:
The higher the value, the less 'guarantee' there is of being able to check the locations, so please choose carefully.
0 - 9       -> Excludes these locations entirely (minimum location is 10)
10 - 200    -> Comfortably reachable
201 - 350   -> May be trickier
351 - 500   -> Likely quite challenging

options.label: Word Length Locations
options.description:
Sets the highest 'Word Length' amount to include as locations.

Locations are checked when a submitted Word's tile length exactly matches the required amount.

DIFFICULTY GUIDE:
The higher the value, the less 'guarantee' there is of being able to check the locations, so please choose carefully.
0       -> Excludes these locations entirely
1 - 10  -> Comfortably reachable
11 - 15 -> May be trickier
16 - 20 -> Likely quite challenging

options.label: Word Score Locations
options.description:
Sets the highest 'Word Score' amount to include as locations from a pre-defined scaling curve.
Value is clamped to the closest location value (equal to or less than) in the curve - e.g. 1689 is clamped to 1500.

Locations are checked when a submitted Word's score is equal to or greater than the required amount.

DIFFICULTY GUIDE:
The higher the value, the less 'guarantee' there is of being able to check the locations, so please choose carefully.
0 - 4           -> Excludes these locations entirely (minimum location is 5)
5 - 2500        -> Comfortably reachable
2501 - 5000     -> May be trickier
5001 - 10000    -> Likely quite challenging

options.label: Shuffle Grid Size
options.description:
Grid are reduced to 3x3 Tiles.
2x 'Progressive Grid Size' items are added to the item pool which increase the grid size to 4x4 and then 5x5.

options.label: Shuffle Inventory Slots
options.description:
Your inventory starts with all Sticker and Stamp Slots locked.
5x 'Progressive Sticker Slot' and 5x 'Progressive Stamp Slot' items are added to the item pool, each unlocking one respective slot.

options.label: Shuffle Item Rarities
options.description:
The shop only stocks items of 'Common' rarity.
2x 'Progressive Item Rarity' items are added to the item pool which allow 'Rare' and then 'Legendary' items to be stocked.

options.label: Shuffle Locked Tile Positions
options.description:
Grids have 10 fixed tile positions removed, making them un-usable.
10x 'Progressive Tile Position' items are added to the item pool, each unlocking a tile position.

NOTE: The 10 positions are selected and balanced across the entire potential 5x5 grid size, meaning that
      any reduced grid sizes (from bosses or the <ShuffleGridSize> option) are still playable.

options.label: Boss-sanity
options.description:
Add locations for defeating each "standard" boss type (Axolotl, Badger, Bat etc.)

WARNING: This setting will add 15 locations to your location pool.

options.label: Pinsanity
options.description:
Add locations for upgrading the Left and Right sides of each <Characters> Pin

WARNING: This setting will add (<Characters> count * 8) locations to your location pool.

NOTE: Does not currently support pin upgrade locations for the Michael stage.
      Support may be added in a future update

options.label: Shopsanity
options.description:
Add custom shopsanity items to the shop which can be purchased as locations.

NOTE: Locations are split as evenly as possible across both the Stickers and the Stamps sections of the shop.
      Shopsanity items have a 33% chance to appear in the first slot of each section resoectively.

options.label: Shopsanity Limit
options.description:
Choose how many <Shopsanity> items will be added to the shop (and adds this many locations to your location pool).

NOTE: If <Shopsanity> = 'False' then this setting will be ignored.

options.label: Shopsanity Cost
options.description:
How much each <Shopsanity> item will cost to purchase.

NOTE: If <Shopsanity> = 'False' then this setting will be ignored.

options.label: Tilesanity
options.description:
Add locations for both Buying and Submitting each Tile Colour and Glyph Type.

WARNING: This setting will add 26 locations to your location pool.

NOTE: Does not currently support the Purple, White, Gold, Pink, Green, Cactus and Glitch colours.
      Does not currently support the Item glyph type.
      Support may be added in a future update.

options.label: Trap Percentage
options.description:
Customise percentage of Filler items in the item pool that are replaced with Trap items.

0       -> Will not include trap items in the item pool.
1 - 100 -> Will replace XX% of filler items in the item pool with trap items.

E.g. If your seed contains 20 Filler items and this value is set to '25', then 4 (25% of 20)
     filler items will be replaced with trap items.

options.label: Trap Weighting
options.description:
Customise how often each Trap item can appear in the item pool, relative to the other Trap items.
This setting will be ignored if <Trap Percentage> = '0'

Higher numbers appear more often, lower numbers appear less often, '0' will exclude it entirely.
Items removed from the list will default to '1'.

At least one item must have a value greater than '0'.

E.g: { "$1": 3, "Consumable Tile": 1, "Extra Re-Roll": 0 }
     Makes '$1' three times more likely to appear than 'Consumable Tile' and 'Extra-Re-Roll' is excluded entirely.
     All unlisted items will be equally as likely to appear as 'Consumable Tile'.

options.label: Filler Weighting
options.description:
Customise how often each Filler item can appear in the item pool, relative to the other Filler items.

Higher numbers appear more often, lower numbers appear less often, '0' will exclude it entirely.
Items removed from the list will default to '1'.

At least one item must have a value greater than '0'.

E.g: { "$1": 3, "Consumable Tile": 1, "Extra Re-Roll": 0 }
     Makes '$1' three times more likely to appear than 'Consumable Tile' and 'Extra-Re-Roll' is excluded entirely.
     All unlisted items will be equally as likely to appear as 'Consumable Tile'.

options.label: Select your Goals
options.description:
What will be your goal(s)?
Configure them further with other options.

Possible values are:

- **Space Elevator Tier**
- **AWESOME Sink Points (total)**
- **AWESOME Sink Points (per minute)**
- **Exploration Collectables**
- **Erect a FICSMAS Tree**

options.label: Goal Requirements
options.description: Of the goals selected in *Select your Goals*, how many must be reached to complete your slot?

options.label: Final Space Elevator Phase in logic
options.description:
Put the milestones accessible BEFORE this Space Elevator Phase in logic.
Milestones after the selected Phase are empty and contain nothing.
If your goal selection contains *Space Elevator Phase* then submitting this Phase's elevator package completes that goal.
If the goal is not enabled, this setting simply limits the included HUB and MAM content.

Estimated in-game completion times:

- **Phase 1 (Tiers 1-2)**: ~3 Hours
- **Phase 2 (Tiers 1-4)**: ~8 Hours
- **Phase 3 (Tiers 1-6)**: ~50 Hours
- **Phase 4 (Tiers 1-8)**: ~100 Hours
- **Phase 5 (Tiers 1-9)**: ~140 Hours

options.label: AWESOME Sink points total
options.description:
Does nothing if *AWESOME Sink Points (total)* goal is not enabled.

Sink an amount of items totalling this amount of points to finish.
This setting is a *point count*, not a *coupon* count!

In the base game, it takes 347 coupons to unlock every non-repeatable purchase, or 1895 coupons to purchase every non-producible item.

Use the **TFIT - Ficsit Information Tool** mod or the Satisfactory wiki to find out how many points items are worth.

If you have *Free Samples* enabled, consider setting this higher so that you can't reach the goal just by sinking your Free Samples.

options.label: AWESOME Sink points per minute
options.description:
Does nothing if *AWESOME Sink Points (per minute)* goal is not enabled.

Sink items to maintain a sink points per minute of the chosen amount for 10 minutes to finish.
This setting is in *points per minute* on the orange track, so DNA Capsules don't count.
This option's presets are example production thresholds - you don't have to sink exactly those specific items.

Use the **TFIT - Ficsit Information Tool** mod or the Satisfactory wiki to find out how many points items are worth.

options.label: Exploration Collectables
options.description:
Does nothing if *Exploration Collectables* goal is not enabled.

Collect this amount of Mercer Spheres, Somersloops, Hard Drives, Paleberries, Beryl Nuts, and Bacon Agarics each to finish.

- The amount of **Mercer Spheres** is **2x** the selected amount
- The amount of **Somersloops** is **1x** the selected amount
- The amount of **Hard Drives** is **1/5th** the selected amount
- The amount of **Paleberries** is **10x** the selected amount
- The amount of **Beryl Nuts** is **20x** the selected amount
- The amount of **Bacon Agarics** is **1x** the selected amount

options.label: Hard Drive Progression Items
options.description:
How many Hard Drives can contain progression items.
Hard Drives above this count cannot contain progression, but can still be Useful.

There are 118 total hard drives in the world and the current implementation supports up to 100 progression hard drives.

options.label: Free Samples: Equipment
options.description:
How many free sample Equipment items are given when they are unlocked.

(ex. Jetpack, Rifle)

options.label: Free Samples: Buildings
options.description:
How many copies of a Building's construction cost are given as a free sample when they are unlocked.
Space Elevator is always excluded.

(ex. Packager, Constructor, Smelter)

options.label: Free Samples: Parts
options.description:
How many general crafting component free samples are given when their recipe is unlocked.
Space Elevator Project Parts are always excluded.

Negative numbers mean that fraction of a full stack.

(ex. Iron Plate, Packaged Turbofuel, Reinforced Modular Frame)

options.label: Free Samples: Radioactive
options.description:
Allow free samples to include radioactive parts.
Remember, they are delivered directly to your player inventory.

options.label: Milestone cost multiplier %
options.description:
Multiplies the amount of resources needed to unlock a Milestone by this factor.

The value is a percentage:

- **50** = half cost
- **100** = normal milestone cost
- **200** = double the cost

options.label: Trap Chance
options.description:
Chance of traps in the item pool.
Traps will only replace filler items such as parts and resources.

- **0:** No traps will be present
- **100:** Every filler item will be a trap.

options.label: Trap Override
options.description:
Precise list of traps that may be in the item pool to find.
If you select anything with this option it will be used instead of the *Trap Presets* setting.

options.label: EnergyLink
options.description:
Allow transferring energy to and from other worlds using the Power Storage building.
Some energy is lost when depositing it in the multiworld network.

options.label: Randomize Default Part Recipes
options.description:
Randomizes what recipes you use to craft the default unlocked parts:
Iron Ingot, Iron Plate, Iron Rod, Copper Ingot, Wire, Concrete, Screw, Reinforced Iron Plate

- Could require usage of Foundries or Assemblers (which get unlocked by default if needed, at reduced build costs)
- Could require other ores to be mixed in via alt recipes (which will become hand-craftable if needed)

options.label: Maps
options.description:
Which ARK map(s) your server runs. Any supported map can be played ON ITS OWN - you are
never forced to pair maps.

List more than one for a CLUSTER (maps linked by obelisk/transmitter travel under a single AP
slot), which pools all their content together:
    maps:
      - the_island
      - scorched_earth

Anything not listed is filtered out, so a check you cannot reach never appears - and the goal
only ever asks for bosses your maps actually have.

Smaller maps have fewer locations than the Island but receive the same craftable-everywhere
engrams, so engram grouping is raised automatically when a slot needs it (as if you had set
engrams_per_item yourself). Supported today: the_island, scorched_earth, ragnarok, the_center,
valguero, fjordur.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Which bosses you must defeat to win (any difficulty - Gamma, Beta, or Alpha).

Defaults to the Island's four. List exactly the bosses you want instead, in any combination,
across any of your enabled maps:
    goal: [broodmother, manticore, fenrisulfr]

Use `all_bosses` (or an empty list) to mean "every boss my enabled maps have", which adapts on
its own - handy on a map whose bosses are not the Island's (Scorched alone would be the
Manticore), and on a cluster it means every boss across all of them:
    goal: [all_bosses]

Valid names:
  broodmother | megapithecus | dragon | overseer      (the Island four)
  manticore                                            (Scorched / Ragnarok / Valguero)
  beyla | hati_and_skoll | steinbjorn | fenrisulfr     (Fjordur)

Every boss you name must exist on a map you enabled, or generation stops with an error naming
the ones that are missing - rather than handing you a seed that can never be won.

options.label: Lock Taming
options.description: Lock dino taming behind an Archipelago item.

options.label: Lock Supply Crates
options.description: Lock supply crate (care package) access behind an Archipelago item.

options.label: Bundle Saddles
options.description:
Bundle each rideable dino's saddle with its tame unlock. When on, unlocking
'Tame: X' also grants X's saddle engram, and those saddle engrams are removed
from the item pool (the freed slots become filler). Off = saddles are separate items.

options.label: Free Starter Engrams
options.description:
Early-help option: grant the basic starter engrams (campfire, cloth armor, spear,
thatch building, storage, etc.) for FREE at the start, and remove them from the item
pool so no one finds them in the multiworld. The set is engrams.json 'starter_engrams'.

options.label: Trap Percentage
options.description:
Of the filler items, what percent are traps (e.g. spawning wild dinos near you)
vs neutral 'Bonus Resources'. 0 = no traps. Only affects filler slots, not real items.

options.label: Early Dino Checks
options.description:
Cross-game starter help / lockout prevention. When on, the ONLY sphere-1 (start-reachable)
ARK checks are the 8 weak early-dino first-kills (Dodo, Parasaur, Trike, Dilo, Phiomia,
Lystrosaurus, Compy, Dimorphodon, marked PRIORITY) plus low levels (Reach Level 5-40). A
global-early item (e.g. Dark Souls III 'early_banner: early_global') can therefore only land
there -> no player gets locked out. Explorer notes still hold later progression but are moved to
a sphere-2 region gated behind receiving any early-dino tame, so they never catch the early item;
every other slow/late check (other kills, tames, Reach Level 45+, bosses) is EXCLUDED to filler.
Keep dossier_checks at/above default.

options.label: Progression Tiers
options.description:
Tech-tree progression (RECOMMENDED - default ON). Splits every check into 4 tier REGIONS you
open in order: Menu -> Tier 0 -> Tier 1 -> Tier 2 -> Tier 3, each unlocked by receiving the prior
tier's crafting-station engram(s). This is what gives the seed a real sphere-by-sphere climb;
with it OFF almost everything is reachable from the start and the playthrough collapses into one
or two spheres.
  Tier 0 (start): weak dinos, Reach Level <= 40
  Tier 1: opens on Engram: Forge + Engram: Mortar And Pestle - mid dinos, Level 45-80
  Tier 2: opens on Engram: Anvil Bench (the Smithy - it costs metal ingots, so it needs the
          Forge first) - strong/water dinos, Level 85-120; explorer NOTES open here
  Tier 3: opens on Engram: Fabricator - apex/deep-ocean dinos, bosses, Level 125-150
The gate engrams are ordinary pool items classified PROGRESSION, so the fill guarantees each is
reachable before its tier opens (no hard-placement, no waiting on another player). Explorer notes
sit behind Tier 2 (two gates deep), so ARK's sphere-0 set is just Tier 0 kills + low levels -
another game's early-forced item can only land there. Supersedes early_dino_checks. The
tame/kill/cave access rules still apply ON TOP, within each tier.

options.label: Station Engram Placement
options.description:
How the 3 tier-gate station engrams (Refining Forge, Smithy/Anvil Bench, Fabricator) are
placed when progression_tiers is on:
  tiered       - (default) hard-placed on YOUR OWN active checks, staggered by tier: Forge in
                 Tier 0, Smithy in Tier 1, Fabricator in Tier 2. The classic staged ARK climb.
  local_early  - forced into an early sphere of YOUR world (like DS3 'early_local'). All three
                 surface quickly on your own early checks, so tiers open sooner.
  global_early - forced into an early sphere ANYWHERE in the multiworld (like DS3 'early_global').
                 A friend may find your stations for you. Only meaningful in a multiworld.
Ignored when progression_tiers is off.

options.label: Extra Early Items
options.description:
Force specific items early, the same way station_placement handles the tier gates. List exact
item names (engrams like "Engram: Bow", or tames like "Tame: Rex"), quoted:
    extra_early_items:
      - "Engram: Bow"
      - "Tame: Raptor"
Routing follows station_placement: global_early -> forced early ANYWHERE in the multiworld;
anything else (local_early / tiered) -> forced early in YOUR world. Works with or without
progression_tiers. Names that aren't real items are ignored.

options.label: Tier 0 Add
options.description:
(progression_tiers only) Creatures to FORCE into Tier 0. Their kill + tame checks become
sphere-0, so they join the pool that can host the T0 station gates. Use exact creature names,
quoted, e.g.:
    tier0_add:
      - Carno
      - Sabertooth
Names that don't match a creature are ignored.

options.label: Tier 0 Remove
options.description:
(progression_tiers only) Creatures to REMOVE from Tier 0 (bumped to Tier 1), so their kills
are no longer sphere-0 / eligible to host the T0 station gates. Only affects creatures that are
Tier 0 by default. Use exact creature names, quoted.

options.label: Dossier Checks
options.description:
How many explorer-note locations to include as checks.

Counted per SLOT, from the notes your maps actually have - the Island has 232, Scorched Earth
adds 137, and a value above your total harmlessly caps there. Ragnarok has none of its own.
Keep near the maximum unless you know what you're doing: ARK's big pool needs most of the notes
plus the other locations to fit, and generation fails if too low.

options.label: Food Sanity
options.description:
Percent of the food 'hold N in inventory' checks (Citronal, Cooked Meat, Jerky, Honey,
Rare Flower, etc - 14 total) included as locations. Which ones are picked is random per seed.
0 = no food checks.

options.label: Tame Sanity
options.description:
Percent of the per-species 'Tamed: X' checks included as locations - lower = fewer tames
REQUIRED to finish. Which species are picked is random per seed. Every 'Tame: X' unlock item
stays in the pool regardless, so everything remains tameable (with lock_taming).
NOTE: low values remove many locations; if generation errors about item count, raise this,
or turn on bundle_structures / bundle_saddles to shrink the item pool to match.

options.label: Death Sanity
options.description:
Percent of the cause-of-death checks included as locations - the 10 'Die to a carnivore /
to cold / to drowning / from fall damage / to starvation ...' checks. Which ones are picked is
random per seed. 0 = no death checks at all, for anyone who would rather not be nudged into
dying on purpose.

Note these checks CAN hold progression - every cause is reachable (you can always starve or
drown), so nothing gets stranded, but it does mean a seed may want you to die deliberately. Set
this to 0 if that is not for you.

options.label: Death Milestones
options.description:
Include the cumulative death-count milestones (die once, 5, 10, 25, 40 times).

Separate from death_sanity because they are a different kind of ask: the cause-of-death checks
are things that happen while you play, whereas the count milestones reward dying repeatedly.
Turning this off leaves the individual death checks alone.

options.label: Bundle Structures
options.description:
Bundle building-structure engrams by material: ALL Wood structures unlock from one
'Bundle: Wood Structures' item (same for Stone, Metal, Greenhouse). Tools/weapons like the
Metal Pick stay individual. Shrinks the item pool by ~100 items (backfilled with filler).

options.label: Engrams Per Item
options.description:
Group engram unlocks so one AP item unlocks SEVERAL engrams at once.
1 = off (one item = one engram, the classic behavior)
2-4 = fold engrams into groups of that size, in PROGRESSION order (early engrams grouped
      with early, late with late), so the pool carries far fewer engram items (the freed
      slots become filler). The tame-logic access rules follow automatically, and the plugin
      unlocks every engram in a received group. Handy for shrinking a huge engram pool so it
      fits the location count. Structure-bundled / starter / auto-granted engrams are never
      grouped (they're already handled).

options.label: Tames Per Item
options.description:
Group taming unlocks so one AP item unlocks SEVERAL 'Tame: X' at once.
1 = off
2-4 = fold tames into groups of that size WITHIN each progression tier (never mixing an
      early creature with an endgame one), so receiving one item unlocks the ability to tame
      several species. Shrinks the item pool; with lock_taming the group item gates every
      species it covers. 'Tame N Species' milestones become filler-only when this is above 1
      (you still tame the species in-game; they just stop hosting progression).

options.label: Randomize Dino Spawns
options.description:
FULLY randomize which species live in which biome: every species is dealt across the
map's spawn zones, and each biome's spawn roster is completely REPLACED by its seeded hand
(via Game.ini spawn-container overrides the connector writes; one server start applies).
Every species is guaranteed to spawn SOMEWHERE, so all checks stay obtainable.
  off     - normal spawns
  grouped - land+air species dealt across land biomes, water species across water zones,
            with predators down-weighted (apex rare, mid uncommon) so zones stay livable
  chaos   - everything dealt across everything at EQUAL weight (beached mosas, ocean rexes,
            predator-saturated beaches... the full experience)
Bosses, alphas, tek variants, cave interiors, and specialty spawners (Giga, Quetz, beaver
dams...) are never touched.

options.label: Mod IDs
options.description:
Steam Workshop mod IDs to include. Their engrams become AP items. ONLY the mods below are
supported (an unknown ID is a generation error - the apworld can't know an arbitrary mod's
engrams). Supported:
    731604991 / 1999447172  Structures Plus / Super Structures  (building - needs bundle_structures: true)
    1565015734              Kraken's Better Dinos
    821530042               Upgrade Station
    2594067220              Super Spyglass Plus
    1609138312              Dino Storage v2
    889745138               Awesome Teleporters
    1631378184              Explorer Note Tracker
    1404697612              Awesome SpyGlass
    1967741708              Lethal's Reusables
Structures Plus and Super Structures are forks of one mod - list whichever you run, not both.
Accepts a yaml list OR a comma-separated string, quotes optional:
    mod_ids: 731604991, 1631378184, 2594067220, 821530042, 1609138312, 1565015734, 1404697612, 889745138
    mod_ids: [1609138312, 889745138]

options.label: Goal
options.description:
The level you must survive in to complete your goal.
Cannot be the same as your starting level. If it is the same, the goal level will be changed to the next available level.

options.label: Goal Time
options.description:
The amount of time you are expected to survive in order to goal on your goal level.
Will round to the nearest 10 seconds, if its not set to a multiple of 10.

options.label: Starting Level
options.description:
The level you start on. This is the first level you will play, and the first level you will have to survive in.
Cannot be the same as your goal level. If it is the same, your goal will be moved instead (see the Goal option).

options.label: Disable Hyper Levels
options.description:
Choose which Hyper levels to remove from the game. Disabled levels are fully removed from the game and not playable, and have no checks.
A disabled level cannot be your goal or starting level. If a level is set as a goal or starting level, it will be removed from this list.
Valid options: "Hyper Hexagon", "Hyper Hexagoner", "Hyper Hexagonest"

options.label: Hexagon Survival Time
options.description:
The amount of time you are expected to survive the Hexagon level. This adjusts the check count, with every 10 seconds sending a check.
Will round to the nearest 10 seconds, if its not set to a multiple of 10.

options.label: Hexagoner Survival Time
options.description:
The amount of time you are expected to survive the Hexagoner level. This adjusts the check count, with every 10 seconds sending a check.
Will round to the nearest 10 seconds, if its not set to a multiple of 10.

options.label: Hexagonest Survival Time
options.description:
The amount of time you are expected to survive the Hexagonest level. This adjusts the check count, with every 10 seconds sending a check.
Will round to the nearest 10 seconds, if its not set to a multiple of 10.

options.label: Hyper Hexagon Survival Time
options.description:
The amount of time you are expected to survive the Hyper Hexagon level. This adjusts the check count, with every 10 seconds sending a check.
Will round to the nearest 10 seconds, if its not set to a multiple of 10.
This option is ignored if this level is disabled.

options.label: Hyper Hexagoner Survival Time
options.description:
The amount of time you are expected to survive the Hyper Hexagoner level. This adjusts the check count, with every 10 seconds sending a check.
Will round to the nearest 10 seconds, if its not set to a multiple of 10.
This option is ignored if this level is disabled.

options.label: Hyper Hexagonest Survival Time
options.description:
The amount of time you are expected to survive the Hyper Hexagonest level. This adjusts the check count, with every 10 seconds sending a check.
Will round to the nearest 10 seconds, if its not set to a multiple of 10.
This option is ignored if this level is disabled.

options.label: Levels Beat Required
options.description:
Number of levels (excluding goal) you need to have beaten before unlocking your goal level.
A level is beaten when you survive for your set maximum survival time.
0 requires no levels beaten, allowing you to goal when you receive your goal level.

options.label: Hexagon Fragments
options.description:
The number of fragment items you need to collect to unlock the goal level.
If set to 0, you will not need any hexagon fragments, and none will be added into the pool.

options.label: Deathlink Amnesty
options.description:
The amount of deaths it takes for a deathlink to count.
Can be adjusted in the client after this is set.

options.label: Coinsanity
options.description:
Adds every freestanding coin in the world as a location check.
When enabled, Coins are added to the item pool as progression items,
and shop purchases logically require receiving Coins.

options.label: Co-op Levels
options.description:
Adds the Piku & Niku co-op levels to the randomizer.
A "Co-op Level Access" item is added to the item pool, which is required
to access the co-op level completion checks and the Piku & Niku trophies.

CURRENTLY UNIMPLEMENTED, DO NOT SELECT

options.label: Early Pencil Hat
options.description:
Determines how the Pencil Hat is placed.

- Early Local: Placed in an early sphere in your own world.
- Early Global: Placed in an early sphere any world in the multiworld. (Default)
- Shuffled: Placed anywhere in the multiworld. This will make you get stuck quickly.

options.label: Piku Color
options.description:
Randomizes Piku's color scheme.

Accepts one of the named modes below, or a 6-digit hex color code
(e.g. "#FF0000" or "FF0000") to force Piku to always use that exact color.

- Off: Piku keeps its normal color. (Default)
- Random Per Screen: Piku is given a new random color every time you enter a screen.
- Random Per Seed: Piku is given a single random color for the entire seed.

options.label: Death Link Amnesty
options.description:
How many deaths it takes to send a DeathLink. DeathLinks only apply during the
platforming challenges or bossfights.

options.label: Exclude Locations
options.description: Prevent these locations from having an important item.

options.label: Eurosanity
options.description: Include the scattered Euro collectibles as randomizer locations.

options.label: Jewelsanity
options.description:
Include the Mystical Jewels locations as randomizer checks.
Automatically enabled if is the Lugh goal is selected.

options.label: Hatsanity
options.description: Include the hat locations as randomizer checks.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Select one or more goals you will have to complete to win the run.
orb: Act 4 access, the Orb, 3 Progressive Cooling Rods. Throw the orb in the pot.
museum: Act 4 access, 100 dumpster items, the Belgium Waffle, 4 Progressive Mystical Dumbbells, 3 Progressive Cooling Rods. Throw the Belgium Waffle in the pot.
fellowship: Act 4 access, the GREENISH ABOMINATION, the Priestess, 3 Progressive Cooling Rods. Throw the GREENISH ABOMINATION in the pot.
lugh: Act 4 access, and all 4 Progressive Mystical Jewels. Jump into Lugh's hands at the Gully.

options.label: Lugh Quest Locking
options.description: When enabled, Lugh will not accept items you bring to him unless you have been sent that specific item.

options.label: Trap Toggle
options.description:
When enabled, trap items (Police Trap, Phone Ratio Trap) may appear in the item pool
as filler, replacing some Euro drops.

options.label: Museum Threshold
options.description:
Number of dumpster items required to unlock the Museum.
NOTE: Changing these can sometimes lead to weird generation problems, but usually does not. If you run into problems, try generating with slightly different values.
If you DO run into generation problems, let Jeff know.

options.label: Act 2 Threshold
options.description:
Number of dumpster items required to unlock Act 2 (Beenie HQ cluster).'
NOTE: Changing these can sometimes lead to weird generation problems, but usually does not. If you run into problems, try generating with slightly different values.
If you DO run into generation problems, let Jeff know.

options.label: Act 3 Threshold
options.description:
Number of dumpster items required to unlock Act 3 (Driving Test/Blimbo City, contains the Kei Truck).
NOTE: Changing these can sometimes lead to weird generation problems, but usually does not. If you run into problems, try generating with slightly different values.
If you DO run into generation problems, let Jeff know.

options.label: Act 4 Threshold
options.description:
Number of dumpster items required to unlock Act 4 (post-apocalypse areas, also requires the Kei Truck).
NOTE: Changing these can sometimes lead to weird generation problems, but usually does not. If you run into problems, try generating with slightly different values.
If you DO run into generation problems, let Jeff know.

options.label: Raccoon Color Randomization
options.description: When enabled, the color of Raccoon will be randomized every time you enter a new area.

options.label: Dark Quartz Multiplier
options.description: Multiplier increase to the amount of dark quartz you get from all sources.

options.label: Required Room Count
options.description: How many rooms must be cleared per area.

options.label: Shrine Check Count
options.description: Total number of shrine checks to generate across the game.

options.label: De-Skull Trap Weight
options.description: Percentage chance for a filler item to be a De-Skull Trap. Set to 0 to disable traps entirely.

options.label: Goal Level
options.description:
Set what goal level you want to do have as your final level.
This level is removed from the multiworld, if selected, and will not be an item sent.
Levels from World 5 or World P will force enable those worlds if selected, and the worlds aren't enabled
4-18 is a level with no gameplay or uncanny cat, so is provided as an option if you want to just win when you are at go mode.

options.label: Goal Level Prism Amount
options.description:
How many in game rank prisms are required to be obtained in total before your goal level unlocks.
Requirement may be forcefully lowered to account for disabled levels or peak checks being disabled.
You can always view the required amount you need in game to reference it.

Does nothing if macguffin goal is enabled.

options.label: Macguffin Goal
options.description:
Sets your goal to require a specified amount of "Cannium Prism" items instead of a specific requirement.
This is a macguffin item that unlocks the goal level when reaching the specified amount.

options.label: Goal Level Macguffin Amount
options.description:
How many macguffin "Cannium Prism" items are added into the multiworld.
Does nothing if macguffin goal is disabled.
May be automatically lowered depending on settings and excluded levels.

options.label: Macguffin Required Percentage
options.description:
What percentage "Cannium Prism" items are required to be obtained in total before your goal level unlocks.
Does nothing if macguffin goal is disabled.

options.label: Gimmick Locking
options.description: Lock level gimmicks such as wormholes, dogs, toggle switches, etc. behind items in the multiworld.

options.label: Level Unlock Style
options.description:
How level unlocks are handled.

Individual: All level unlocks are individual items you must be sent
World: Worlds are unlocks that you must be sent, you get access to all levels after being sent that world

options.label: Minigames
options.description: Enable minigames as checks, such as Bort Bash, UNCANNY_DASH, Meowls, etc.

options.label: World 5 Levels
options.description: Include World 5 (Elysian Fields) levels as checks.

options.label: World P Levels
options.description: Include World P (Cosmic Championship) levels as checks. These are a big step up in difficulty, so be warned

options.label: World E Levels
options.description: Include World E levels as checks, which are exclusive levels from the Endless Shuffle.

options.label: Peak Checks
options.description: Add a check for gaining a "PEAK" rank in a level. These can be really difficult.

options.label: Coinsanity
options.description:
Add checks for every coin found in the levels.

If you set this to All, it may be beneficial to make Uncanny Cat Spray a local item, to prevent bloating
the multiworld with a huge amount of filler from your game. Please be cautious when using this setting
without other people being aware of it, as this adds over 1000 locations into the game.

Off: Coins are not checks.
All: Adds checks for every individual coin.
Full Clear: Adds checks for fully clearing all coins in a level, but leaves out individual coin checks.

options.label: Excluded Levels
options.description:
Remove levels from the multiworld completely. This removes all locations related to that level, and the level unlock item.
Name levels by their id, e.g. "1-4, P-14, 5-3".

Excluding a level also removes the prisms from that level in logic, so your goal prism amount
may be forcefully lowered to a still-obtainable number.

World 0 cannot be excluded at all (why would you want to?)

options.label: Excluded Minigames
options.description:
Remove specific minigames from the multiworld completely. This removes all locations related to that minigame, and the minigame unlock item.
Valid options are "Bort Bash", "UNCANNY_DASH", and "Meowls"

options.label: Goal Rank Requirement
options.description:
Which in-game rank is required to unlock the goal.

Any: Any rank is allowed to unlock the goal.
OK: An "OK" (3 prism) rank or better is required.
Good: A "GOOD" (4 prism) rank or better is required.
Peak: A "PEAK" (5 prism) rank or better is required.

options.label: Rank Check Difficulty
options.description:
Which in-game rank sends the per-level rank check.

OK: An "OK" (3 prism) rank or better sends the check.
Good: A "GOOD" (4 prism) rank or better is required.

Every level always has a rank check. This only sets how hard it is to send one.
This also determines how many levels are required to goal your game for logic.

options.label: Temporary Modifiers
options.description:
Adds temporary modifier items based on the existing modifiers, some of which are traps and some are useful. These last until you complete a level.
If you find these too difficult, you can always go back to 0-1 to cycle through them, as that level will always be available.

When enabled, these make up 50% of the filler in your world, or 30% of it with Coinsanity on (the rest is Uncanny Cat Spray, which prevents you from dying to the Uncanny Cat one time per item).
When disabled, that filler is all Uncanny Cat Spray instead (besides the costumes and other one off fillers)

options.label: Buff Uncanny Cat Spray
options.description:
Buffs the Uncanny Cat Spray item from doing nothing to giving you a one time protection against the Uncanny Cat.
It is used up the moment you touch the Uncanny Cat, and doesn't come back upon restarting a level.

options.label: Chill Mode
options.description:
Enable the "Chill Mode" modifier that removes the Uncanny Cat entirely. This makes the game significantly easier.
This can be disabled/enabled in the mod config.

options.label: Panic Mode
options.description:
Enable the "Panic Mode" modifier that speeds up the Uncanny Cat quite a bit. This makes the game significantly harder, and may
result in unbeatable seeds depending on your skill levels. BE WARNED.

DO NOT ENABLE THIS IF YOU AREN'T PREPARED FOR WHAT IT ENTAILS.

Automatically disabled if "Chill Mode" is enabled.
This can be disabled/enabled in the mod config.

options.label: Mayor Only
options.description:
In Mayor only mode, you will win purely by becoming mayor with a single character.
This is an option meant for new players or short Archipelago games.

options.label: Become Mayor
options.description:
Requires you to become mayor at least once.
Only used if "Mayor Only" is disabled.

options.label: Big Quests Completed
options.description:
How many big quests to compelete.
Only used if "Mayor Only" is disabled.

options.label: Achievements Completed
options.description:
How many achievements to completed.
Only used if "Mayor Only" is disabled.

options.label: Random Characters
options.description:
How many random characters do you want to start with?
Only used if "Gorilla Mode" is disabled.

options.label: Starting Characters
options.description:
Which characters must you start with? I recommend none, but a new player may want an easier character to start with, such as Vampire or Cannibal.
These are in addition to how many random characters you picked.
If you chose 2 random characters and select Alien and Vampire, you will start with Alien and Vampire plus two random characters.
Only used if "Gorilla Mode" is disabled.

options.label: DLC Enabled
options.description: Enabled DLC in streets of rogue. Requires DLC purchase (well worth it!)

options.label: Enable Purple Coin Stars
options.description: Add Purple Coin star location. Only one of these is normally available outside of post game

options.label: Stars to finish
options.description:
This will set the number of stars required to reach the center of the universe.
This will be capped at 104 stars if extra locations are not enabled in a single world multiworld.

options.label: Mario Colors
options.description:
Choose new colors for part of Mario's Outfit! (These will also be applied to Luigi)
4 pieces are changeable: 'Hat' , 'Overalls', 'Shoes', 'Gloves'

The following predetermined colors are available:
"Red", "Orange", "Yellow", "Green", "Blue", "Purple", "Black", "Brown", "White", "Pink", "Gray"

Putting Random with any color will set all 4 pieces to a random color. If a piece of clothing is missing from the option,
a random color will be chosen for it. (example Random: Green)
If a given piece of clothing does not have a valid value or is not included at all, one will be chosen for you.
Invalid colors other than the ones above will turn into a random color.

options.label: Dome Shuffle
options.description: Shuffle Dome entrances

options.label: Galaxy Shuffle
options.description:
Determine what kinds of galaxies should be added to the shuffle pool. Leave empty to disable shuffling

Full: Any galaxy in any galaxy position

Dome Majors: Add Major galaxies to shuffle pool

Dome Minors: Add Minor galaxies to shuffle pool

Observatory Specials: Add Direct from Observatory galaxies to shuffle pool, such as Trials or Hungry Luma galaxies

Bosses: Add Boss galaxies to shuffle pool

options.label: Galaxy Shuffle Type
options.description:
Choose how galaxies are shuffled between slots. Does nothing if no galaxies are randomized

By Type - Galaxies will only be shuffled between slots of the same kind. Major galaxies on major galaxies,
Boss galaxies on Boss galaxies, Observatory Galaxies on observatory galaxies

Major Separately - Major galaxies will only be shuffled among themselves, but all other galaxies can go anywhere

Full - Any galaxy can go on any Galaxy slot

options.label: Hide Galaxy
options.description:
Choose Galaxy visibility in domes

Visible - All galaxies will have a shadow silhouette represent the galaxy present and show star count required to open

Hide Minors - Minor Galaxies will appear as question mark blocks until opened for the first time. Majors will still
    show a galaxy silhouette but minors will not show the star count required to open them.
