Hide All - All Galaxies will appear as question mark blocks until opened for the first time. Neither will show how
    many stars are required to open the galaxy.

options.label: Star Colors
options.description:
If this option is enabled, each star in the Star Select screen will be colored according to the classification of
the item on that star location. After it has been collected, the star will be clear

If the option is disabled, all stars will start clear and become colored according to item classification after
clearing the stage.

options.label: Tutorial skip
options.description: Remove the need to complete the tutorial and unlock tutorial related tech. Grant a free launch for every selected planet.

options.label: Campaign choice
options.description: Select Serpulo, Erekir or both for the randomized campaign.

options.label: Goal
options.description: The goal for the multiworld

options.label: Disable invasions
options.description: Disable invasions and prevent losing progress.

options.label: Faster production
options.description: Enable faster production and harvesting of resources.

options.label: Faster unit production
options.description: Enable faster unit production.

options.label: Faster conveyor
options.description: Enable faster conveyor.

options.label: Death link
options.description: Enable death link.

options.label: Death link mode
options.description: Select the death link mode.

options.label: Military level tracking
options.description: Ensure the player has enough military power to clear sectors. If turned off, the logic will consider that the player can clear every sector once they have the minimal requirement to land on that sector.

options.label: Randomize core units weapon
options.description: Will randomize core units weapon. Erekir core unit will be made vulnerable and be given an ability instead.

options.label: Logistic distribution
options.description: Change how logistics research are distributed.

options.label: Progressive Drills
options.description: Makes Drills progressive.

options.label: Progressive Generators
options.description: Makes Generators progressive.

options.label: Progressive Pumps
options.description: Makes Pumps progressive.

options.label: Make early roadblocks local
options.description: Make items that could block the player early on local.

options.label: Amount of resources required
options.description: The amount of resources required to complete the 'Every resources collection' goal.

options.label: Core Russian Roulette Chambers
options.description: The number of chambers for the Core Russian roulette option. If you select X amount of chambers, you will have 1 in a X chance of having your cores destroyed

options.label: Factory malfunction trap
options.description: Add the Factory malfunction trap to the filler pool

options.label: Launch wave trap
options.description: Add the Launch wave trap to the filler pool (Only work for serpulo campaign)

options.label: Construction speed buffs
options.description: Add the Construction speed buffs to the filler pool

options.label: Research discount buffs
options.description: Add the Research discount buffs to the filler pool

options.label: Add sectors as locations
options.description: Add selected campaign(s) sectors as locations in the research tech tree.

options.label: Add resources as locations
options.description: Add selected campaign(s) resources as locations in the research tech tree.

options.label: Difficulty
options.description:
The difficulty of the randomizer's logic.
Standard: Logic only requires tricks at a similar level of difficulty to the base game
Hard: Logic requires some advanced tech and more difficult execution compared to the base game
Expert: Logic requires glitches and extremely difficult execution

options.label: Shine Count
options.description:
How many Shine Sprite items appear in the item pool
If this number of shines is less than the availiable locations, it will be adjusted to the number of availible locations

options.label: Goal Level Shines
options.description:
How many Shine Sprites are required to access level 12-8.
If less than this number of Shines exist in the pool, it will be adjusted to the total Shine count.

options.label: Shine Sanity
options.description:
Enables Shine Sprites in the location pool. 
Note that if Blue Coin Sanity is also disabled, this will be forcefully enabled

options.label: Blue Coin Sanity
options.description:
Enables Blue Coins in the location pool. 
Note that if this is the only location option selected, you may find yourself saving and qutting the game regularly to exit levels

options.label: Shuffle Bubble Nozzle
options.description:
Includes the Underwater Hover Nozzle from Noki Bay (called the Bubble Nozzle for brevity) in the item pool.
When obtained, you can switch to it with D-Pad Up.

options.label: Shuffle Long Jump
options.description:
Includes the Long Jump move in the item pool.
Use it by holding Z and pressing A while moving.

options.label: Shuffle Fruit Gummies
options.description:
Includes the Fruit Gummies in the item pool.
Fruit Gummies allow Yoshi eggs to be hatched without bringing them fruit.
However, Yoshi will not be able to spray juice without eating an actual fruit.

options.label: Shuffle Dive Helmet
options.description: Includes the Dive Helmet in the item pool.

options.label: Shuffle Sunglasses
options.description: Includes the Suglasses in the item pool.

options.label: Shuffle Shine Shirt
options.description: Includes the Shine Shirt in the item pool.

options.label: Shuffle Cap
options.description:
Strips Mario's Cap and includes it in the item pool.
This is only a visual change

options.label: Level Access
options.description:
If on "vanilla", the main levels are accessed in the way they are in the base game (e.g. Ricco Harbor is accessible after collecting 3 Shine Sprites).
If on "tickets", each level has a ticket item that must be acquired to access the level.
To reduce generation failures in testing, you'll automatically receive one free ticket at the start.

options.label: Enable 100 Coin Shines
options.description:
Turn off to ignore the 100 coin Shine Sprites, which removes 8 Shine Sprites from the pool.
You can still collect them, but they don't do anything.

options.label: Corona Mountain Shines
options.description:
How many Shine Sprites are required to access Corona Mountain and the Delfino Airstrip revisit.
If this is more than the locations available, This will be automatically adjusted to 90-80% of locations available
after all other progression items are created / accounted for.

options.label: Extra Shines
options.description:
How many extra shine sprites you want added to the pool. This is a percentage so it ranges from 0 to 90
If more shines would be added than locations possible it will add as many as it can

options.label: Enable Nozzle Boxes
options.description: Enables Nozzle Boxes as a location.

options.label: All Shines Selectable
options.description:
Enables you to select every shine without having to complete each in order.
You will still need access to each hub (Gelato Beach, Noki Bay, Pinna Park, etc.)

options.label: Blue Coinsanity
options.description:
Full shuffle: adds Blue Coins to the pool and makes Blue Coins locations.
Trade Shines Only: Adds the trade shines from the boathouse. Will NOT add the blue coin locations though.

options.label: Blue Coin Maximum
options.description:
How many Blue Coins to include in the pool if Blue Coinsanity is on.
Does nothing if Blue Coinsanity full_shuffle is off.
Corresponding trade shines will be removed from locations.
Removed Blue Coins will be replaced by other items in the pool, such as filler, to fill the
    remaining Blue Coin locations.
Example: You only want 220 of the 240 possible blue coins, the other 20 spots will be filled by other items.

options.label: Trade Shine Maximum
options.description:
The number of Shines from the boathouse trades that will be shuffled. If the Blue Coin Maximum is not enough
to obtain this amount, it will decrease automatically.
Keep in mind that if this value is too high, there is a chance you will have to nearly 100% the game.

options.label: Starting Nozzle
options.description:
If on, you will start with no Spray Nozzle, and in fact, no FLUDD at all. (Still in non-enforce mode)
You will skip directly to Delfino Plaza, and the first Airstrip mission will be removed from locations.
In this early version of this setting, you are expected to spray unusual things with Hover.

options.label: Difficulty
options.description:
This enables difficulty settings. Higher difficulty settings will include checks in logic that normally
are not possible without doing difficult or unintended things. This includes spraying things with different
nozzles, doing difficult platforming, and executing glitches.

options.label: Logic Level
options.description:
The level of logic to use when determining what locations in your world are accessible.

**Normal:** Can require damage boosts, but otherwise approachable for someone who has beaten the game.

**Hard:** Expects more knowledge and tighter execution.
Has leashing, normal clips and much tighter d-boosting in logic.

options.label: Shuffle Mega Time Shards
options.description: Whether mega shards should be item locations.

options.label: Shuffle Elemental Skylands Generators
options.description:
Whether the elemental skylands generators should be locations.

With this setting, all four Progressive Generator Shutdown are required to open the final door in the Fire Generator room.

options.label: Limited Movement
options.description: Removes either rope dart or wingsuit from the itempool. Forces logic to at least hard and accessibility to minimal.

options.label: Early Meditation
options.description: Guarantees meditation will be found early

options.label: Available Starting Portals
options.description:
Number of portals that are available from the start. Autumn Hills, Howling Grotto, and Glacial Peak are always
available. If portal outputs are not randomized, Searing Crags will also be available.

options.label: Shuffle Portal Outputs
options.description:
Whether the portals lead to random places.
Entering a portal from its vanilla area will always lead to HQ, and will unlock it if relevant.
Supports plando.

**None:** Portals will take you where they're supposed to.

**Shops:** Portals can lead to any area except Music Box and Elemental Skylands, with each portal output guaranteed
to not overlap with another portal's. Will only put you at a portal or a shop.

**Checkpoints:** Like Shops except checkpoints without shops are also valid drop points.

**Anywhere:** Like Checkpoints except it's possible for multiple portals to output to the same map.

options.label: Shuffle Level Transitions
options.description:
Whether the transitions between the levels should be randomized.
Supports plando.

**None:** Level transitions lead where they should.

**Coupled:** Returning through a transition will take you from whence you came.

**Decoupled:** Any level transition can take you to any other level transition.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Requirement to finish the game.
To win with the power seal hunt goal, you must enter the Music Box through the shop chest.

options.label: Music Box Gauntlet
options.description: Whether the music box gauntlet needs to be done.

options.label: Notes Needed
options.description:
How many notes need to be found in order to access the Music Box.
6 are always needed to enter, so this places the others in your start inventory.

options.label: Total Power Seals
options.description: Number of power seals that exist in the item pool when power seal hunt is the goal.

options.label: Percent Seals Required
options.description: Percentage of total seals required to open the shop chest.

options.label: Include Traps
options.description: Whether traps should be included in the itempool.

options.label: Shop Prices Modifier
options.description: Percentage modifier for shuffled item prices in shops

options.label: Shop Price Plando
options.description: Plan specific prices on shop slots. Supports weighting

options.label: Episode Select
options.description:
Which episodes should be included in the seed.
ck4 = Episode 4
ck5 = Episode 5
both = Episode 4 & Episode 5

options.label: Enable Gemsets
options.description:
Whether gemsets should be enabled in the seed.
With this option on, you will receive all level gem items for a specific level at the same time.
With this option off, you will receive each level gem individually.

options.label: Enable Keen 4 Secret Level
options.description:
Whether the Keen 4 secret level, the Pyramid of the Forbidden, is included.
With this option on, it becomes an unlockable level with its own location
checks and unlock items. It is optional — not required for the Keen 4
(BWB Megarocket) goal.

It is harder to reach than the regular levels: its hidden entrance sits
behind the Pyramid of the Moons. Only applies when Keen 4 is in the seed.
Off by default.

options.label: Enable Keen 5 Secret Level
options.description:
Whether the Keen 5 secret level, Korath III Base, is included.
With this option on, it becomes an unlockable level with its own location
check and unlock item. It is optional — not required for the Keen 5
(QED) goal.

It is harder to reach than the regular levels: it is only reached via the
Impossible Pogo Trick (pogo + stunner) inside the Gravitational Damping
Hub. Only applies when Keen 5 is in the seed. Off by default.

options.label: Additional Starting Levels
options.description:
How many additional levels should be randomly unlocked at the start of the game.
By default, Border Village and Slug Village in Keen 4 and Ion Ventilation System and
Security Center in Keen 5 are always unlocked. Additionally, the gems and keycards
needed to complete these levels are also unlocked from the start.

options.label: Enable Conesanity
options.description:
Whether to enable conesanity (Keen 4 only).
With this option on, every reachable Ice Cream Cone in Keen 4 (the
5000-point pickup) becomes its own AP location check. Lower point
tiers (100/200/500/1000/2000) are NOT included; the omnispeak-ap
engine currently only emits checks for the 5000-pt class.

options.label: Enable Sugarsanity
options.description:
Whether to enable sugarsanity (Keen 5 only).
With this option on, every reachable Bag O' Sugar in Keen 5 (the
5000-point pickup) becomes its own AP location check. Lower point
tiers (100/200/500/1000/2000) are NOT included; the omnispeak-ap
engine currently only emits checks for the 5000-pt class.

options.label: Enable Flasksanity
options.description:
Whether to enable flasksanity (Keen 4 only).
With this option on, every accessible Lifewater Flask in Keen 4 becomes
its own AP location check. Lifewater Flasks are the extra-life pickups
(no points; every 100 collected grants an extra life). Flasks known to
be unreachable in the original maps are excluded automatically.

options.label: Enable Kegsanity
options.description:
Whether to enable kegsanity (Keen 5 only).
With this option on, every Vitalin Keg in Keen 5 becomes its own AP
location check. Vitalin Kegs are the extra-life pickups (no points;
every 100 collected grants an extra life).

options.label: Randomize Pogo
options.description:
Whether the pogo stick should be randomized.
startwith = Start the game with the ability to use the pogo stick. This is vanilla behavior.
early = The pogo stick will be placed early in the seed.
randomize = The pogo stick can appear anywhere in the seed.

options.label: Randomize Stunner
options.description:
Whether the neural stunner should be randomized.
startwith = Start the game with the ability to use the stunner. This is vanilla behavior.
early = The stunner will be placed early in the seed.
randomize = The stunner can appear anywhere in the seed.

options.label: Randomize Wetsuit
options.description:
Whether the wetsuit should be randomized.
startwith = Start the game with the ability to use the wetsuit.
early = The wetsuit will be placed early in the seed.
randomize = The wetsuit can appear anywhere in the seed.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Free Duel mode means progression will be made through the Free Duel menu
culminating in a fight against Yami Yugi.
Your game will be longer per duelist you set to play against.
You do not enter tournaments in this mode.

Tournament mode means progression will be made in Tournaments with the
goal being completing The Last Judgement in the Dark Tournament Division.
24 - 72 duel wins required, depending on checks you receive.

options.label: Tournament Rewards
options.description:
This option only matters when your Progression mode is Tournament.

Choose whether you will be awarded one, two or three checks every time
you complete a Tournament.

options.label: Free Duel Rewards
options.description:
This option only matters when your Progression mode is Free Duel.

Choose whether you will be awarded one or two checks every time
a duelist is defeated in Free Duel.

options.label: Starting Duelists
options.description:
This option only matters when your Progression mode is Free Duel.
 
The number of Duelists to start with unlocked.

options.label: Free Duel Goal
options.description:
This option only matters when your Progression mode is Free Duel.

The number of duelists defeated required to unlock your goal duel (against Yami Yugi).
A higher number leads to a longer game.

options.label: Free Duel Pool
options.description:
This option only matters when your Progression mode is Free Duel.

Set the number of duelists that locations will be created for
in Free Duel progression mode.
Lowering your location count allows you to send out fewer items
if you set and achieve an early goal.

If this number is set below FreeDuelGoal,
it will be raised to match it.

options.label: Dice Stats
options.description:
The double option changes all dice crest faces to have
double their normal value. This can reduce the amount of time
spent rolling for necessary crests in battle and can give
AI opponents a little more bite than normal.
Normal leaves crest faces as they are in vanilla gameplay.

options.label: Randomize Starting Dice
options.description:
In the base game your starting pool is lightly randomized to begin with,
but this setting takes off the guardrails and generates you with any
15 dice from the game (no duplicates).

It is impossible to generate a starting pool with only items and no creatures to summon.

With this option active you have to select all of your new dice from your collection
before the first duel begins.

options.label: Set Starting Dice
options.description:
If RandomizeStartingDice is True, you can set some or all of the dice
you'd like to start with here.

Leave this empty if you'd like all random starting dice.
You can specify up to 15 Dice, any entries
after the 15th will be ignored, if you don't provide
enough the rest will be random.
You can include multiples of the same dice.
Dice names are case sensitive, invalid names should
raise an exception on game Generation.

Example Syntax for a Harpie Lady Sisters and two Lord of D.'s
["Harpie Lady Sisters", "Lord of D.", "Lord of D."]

options.label: Bonus Item Mode
options.description:
Decide what you would like to receive from filler checks.

Random Dice will reward any random die from the game.
In Tournament Progression mode, Grandpa's Shop can still progress
although it is quite slow. Approximately 3-6 Tournament wins per shop level.

Shop Progress makes collecting Dice locations. You may be required
to buy dice from Grandpa's Shop to progress. This mode will divide the 
number of filler checks between Shop Levels and Gold items.
This will halt normal shop progression if you have chosen Tournament mode.

options.label: Gold Reward Amount
options.description:
This option only matters when your Bonus Item Mode option is Shop Progress.

The amount of gold you will receive from Gold filler checks.

options.label: Set Free Duel Opponents
options.description:
This option only matters when your Progression mode is Free Duel.

You can write in names of Duelists you'd like to gaurantee
appearing in your free duel pool.

Leave this empty if you'd like all opponents to be random.
You can specify as many duelists up to the size of your pool,
any additional entries will be ignored, if you don't provide
enough the rest will be random.
Duelist names are case sensitive, invalid names should
raise an exception on game Generation.

Yami Yugi and Yugi Moto always appear, they are invalid
entries for this option.

Example Syntax for Mai Valentine and Joey Wheeler
["Mai Valentine", "Joey Wheeler"]

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Choose what you want your goal to be.
In missionsanity all missions are individually added to the pool of checks,
you set the number of missions that you must complete in order to complete your goal.
In progressive missions you receive 'progressive mission' items that unlock groups of
5 missions at a time. Your goal is completing Destroy Floating Mines after collecting
all 'progressive mission' items.

options.label: Missionsanity Goal Requirement
options.description:
This option only matters if your Goal is Missionsanity.
Select how many missions it takes to complete your goal.
Does not include the tutorial mission.

options.label: Include Human+ Filler
options.description:
If this option is on, three "Progressive Human+"
Enhancement levels will be added as filler to the item pool.

options.label: Shopsanity
options.description:
Shopsanity turns all parts listings in the shop into locations,
and all parts that you don't start with are shuffled into the multiworld.

options.label: Shopsanity Listings Per Mission
options.description:
Define how many shop listings open up per mission completion.
Higher numbers may require more grinding. Includes Raven Test.

options.label: Randomize Starting Mech
options.description:
Your starting AC Parts will be randomized but still
adhere to weight and energy limits.

options.label: Credit Check Amount
options.description: Define how much you earn from Credit Filler checks you receieve.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Choose which Boss will be the goal for your game.
The requirements for each boss is the same as the base game
plus the required warp room to reach them.

options.label: Trophy Rounds
options.description:
How many rounds you must win to beat a Trophy Challenge.
In the base game, this number is 3.

options.label: Include Gold Relics
options.description:
Gold Relic challenges will become locations,
as well as the Splash Dash, Dante's Dash and Mallet Mash minigames
which are otherwise excluded because you can't reach them.
Gold Relics will be shuffled into the multiworld.

options.label: Include Platinum Relics
options.description:
PLEASE NOTE this option is not yet implemented.
Activating this option has no effect on the game currently.

Platinum Relic challenges will become locations.
Platinum Relics will be shuffled into the multiworld.

options.label: Remove From Item Pool
options.description:
Allows customizing the item pool by removing unwanted items from it.

Note: Items in starting inventory are automatically removed from the pool; you don't need to remove them here too.

options.label: Enable Tyrian 2000 support
options.description:
Use data from Tyrian 2000 instead of Tyrian 2.1.

Turning this on is mandatory if you want to do anything with Episode 5. All of Tyrian 2000's weapons and new items will also be added to the item pool.

options.label: Episode 1
options.description:
Add Episode 1 (Escape) levels to the pool. Adds 93 locations across 16 levels.

If "goal" is chosen, you'll need to complete "ASSASSIN" (in addition to other episode goals) to win.

options.label: Episode 2
options.description:
Add Episode 2 (Treachery) levels to the pool. Adds 75 locations across 12 levels.

If "goal" is chosen, you'll need to complete "GRYPHON" (in addition to other episode goals) to win.

options.label: Episode 3
options.description:
Add Episode 3 (Mission: Suicide) levels to the pool. Adds 81 locations across 12 levels.

If "goal" is chosen, you'll need to complete "FLEET" (in addition to other episode goals) to win.

options.label: Episode 4
options.description:
Add Episode 4 (An End to Fate) levels to the pool. Adds 100 locations across 18 levels.

If "goal" is chosen, you'll need to complete "NOSE DRIP" (in addition to other episode goals) to win.

options.label: Episode 5
options.description:
Add Episode 5 (Hazudra Fodder) levels to the pool. Adds 56 locations across 7 levels.

This setting requires enabling Tyrian 2000 support to have any effect.
If "goal" is chosen, you'll need to complete "FRUIT" (in addition to other episode goals) to win.

options.label: Data Cube Hunt
options.description:
If enabled, goal levels will not be in the item pool, but will be locked behind collecting a given amount of "Data Cube" items.

See data_cubes_required, data_cubes_total_percent, and data_cubes_total for more information.

options.label: Data Cubes Required
options.description: The amount of data cubes that must be collected to access goal levels in Data Cube Hunt mode.

options.label: Data Cubes Total
options.description:
How many data cubes should be added to the pool in Data Cube Hunt mode, as an absolute amount.

You may specify 'percentage' to use the value from data_cubes_total_percent instead.

options.label: Data Cubes Total %
options.description:
How many data cubes should be added to the pool in Data Cube Hunt mode, as a percentage of the required amount.

100 adds in exactly the number of data cubes required, 200 adds in twice that amount, etc.

options.label: Game Difficulty
options.description:
Select the base difficulty of the game.

Anything beyond Impossible (4) is VERY STRONGLY not recommended unless you know what you're doing.

options.label: Contact Bypasses Shields
options.description:
Direct contact with an enemy or anything else will completely power down your shields and deal armor damage.

Note that this makes the game significantly harder. Additional "Enemy approaching from behind" callouts will be given throughout the game if this is enabled.

options.label: Allow Excess Armor
options.description:
Twiddles, pickups, etc. can cause your ship to have more armor than its maximum armor rating.

Enabling this is vanilla behavior.
If disabled, a red line over the Armor meter will show the maximum armor level that you are allowed to attain, if not already at maximum armor.

options.label: Logic Difficulty
options.description:
Select how difficult the logic will be.

If 'beginner', most secret locations will be excluded by default, and additional leeway will be provided when calculating damage to ensure you can destroy things required to obtain checks.
If 'standard', only a few incredibly obscure locations will be excluded by default. There will always logically be a weapon loadout you can use to obtain checks that your current generator can handle (shields notwithstanding).
If 'expert', almost all locations will be in logic, and it will be expected that you can manage a weapon loadout that creates a power drain on your current generator.
If 'master', all locations will always be in logic, and you will also be expected to know technical things like specific triggers for secrets and other minute details. You will be expected to use twiddles if available, and little to no leeway will be provided with damage calculation.
If 'no_logic', all locations within a level will be assumed attainable if you can access that level at all, with zero regard for loadout or anything else. This is *extremely* dangerous and should be used with caution.

options.label: Boss Timeout in Logic
options.description: If enabled, bosses that can be timed out may logically require you to do so; requiring you to dodge them until the level automatically completes to obtain items from a shop afterward.

options.label: Local Level %
options.description:
Set some percentage of levels, chosen randomly, to be local to your own world.

Increasing this may reduce the chance of being in BK mode (having no checks available), but may also result in less interaction with other worlds.

options.label: Add Bonus Games
options.description:
Add the three bonus games into the item pool as additional filler.

If 'off', these bonus games will be available by default.
If 'on', the items for each bonus game will need to be obtained to play them, just like any other level.

options.label: Progressive Items
options.description:
How items with multiple tiers (in this game, only generators) should be rewarded.

If 'off', each item can be independently picked up, letting you skip tiers. Picking up an item of a lower tier after an item of a higher tier does nothing.
If 'on', each "Progressive" item will move you up to the next tier, regardless of which one you find.

options.label: Specials
options.description:
Enable or disable specials (extra behaviors when starting to fire).

If 'on', your ship will have a random special from the start.
If 'as_items', specials will be added to the item pool, and can be freely chosen once acquired.
If 'off', specials won't be available at all.

options.label: Twiddles
options.description:
Enable or disable twiddles (Street Fighter-esque button combinations).

If 'on', your ship will have up to three random twiddles. Their button combinations will be the same as in the original game; as will their use costs.
If 'off', no twiddles will be available.

The following option is not currently available but is planned in the future:
If 'chaos', your ship will have up to three random twiddles with new inputs. They may have new, unique behaviors; and they may have different use costs.

options.label: Random Starting Weapon
options.description:
Choose whether you start with the default Pulse-Cannon, or some other random weapon.

The weapon you receive depends on logic difficulty settings, among other things. In particular, adding generators to your start inventory may result in a better selection for lower logic difficulties.

Note: If your start inventory contains a front weapon, you will not receive another starting weapon (and therefore, this option will be ignored).

options.label: Starting Maximum Power Level
options.description:
Change the maximum power level you're allowed to upgrade weapons to when you start the seed.

Increasing this can result in more varied seeds, and/or easier starts.

options.label: Starting Money
options.description: Change the amount of money you start the seed with.

options.label: Shop Mode
options.description:
Determine if shops exist and how they behave.

If 'none', shops will not exist; credits will only be used to upgrade weapons.
If 'standard', each level will contain a shop that is accessible after clearing it. The shop will contain anywhere from 1 to 5 additional checks for the multiworld.
If 'hidden', shops will behave as above, but will not tell you what you're buying until after you spend credits.
If 'shops_only', shops will be the only location checks available; items within levels will only contain varying amounts of money for yourself. Note that this mode is designed for "no logic", and is extremely restrictive; you may need to tweak your logic difficulty settings when playing solo.

options.label: Shop Item Count
options.description:
The number of shop location checks that will be added.

All levels are guaranteed to have at least one shop item if there's more shop location checks than levels.
You may also specify 'always_one', 'always_two', 'always_three', 'always_four', or 'always_five' to guarantee that shops will have exactly that many items.

options.label: Money Pool Scaling
options.description:
Change the amount of money in the pool, as a percentage.

At 100 (100%), the total amount of money in the pool will be equal to the cost of upgrading the most expensive front weapon to the maximum level, plus the cost of purchasing all items from every shop.

Note that this does not take into account money that you earn while playing levels, so it is safe to set this to a relatively low value.

options.label: Base Weapon Cost
options.description:
Change the amount that weapons (and, in turn, weapon power upgrades) cost.

If 'original', weapons will cost the same amount that they do in the original game.
If 'balanced', prices will be changed around such that generally more powerful and typically used weapons (Laser, etc.) will cost more.
If 'randomized', weapons will have random prices.

You may also input a positive integer to force all base weapon prices to that amount.

options.label: Force Game Speed
options.description: Force the game to stay at a specific speed setting, or "off" to allow it to be freely chosen.

options.label: Christmas Mode
options.description: Use the Christmas set of graphics and sound effects.

options.label: Death Link
options.description:
When you die, everyone else with DeathLink enabled also dies. The reverse is also true.

Can be toggled off in the Options menu, if enabled.

options.label: MRS Full Story
options.description: Adds a few extra locations in My Roommate Sonic, capturing the full story.

options.label: SMM Sanity
options.description: Adds multiple checks to various tasks in Sonic Movie Maker (Photosanity/Foodsanity/Birthsanity).

options.label: Eggysanity (SMM)
options.description: Adds checks to hidden Eggy NPCs in Sonic Movie Maker.

options.label: Eggysanity (EO)
options.description: Adds checks to hidden Eggy NPCs in Eggman Origin.

options.label: Ascensions to Goal
options.description: The amount of Ascensions needed to goal. This will increase the amount of items and locations in the pool (7 items and 8 locations per ascension).

options.label: Junk Percentage
options.description: Percentage of non-required Robust Worms to be converted to junk items.

options.label: Goal Type
options.description:
Choose which arc or arcs you need to beat to satisfy the end goal.
To beat an arc, you must beat the final level of the selected chapter. If both arcs are enabled, you must beat the final level of both selected chapters for Ultra Arc and Bonus Arc.

options.label: Ultra Arc Chapters
options.description:
Choose which chapters in the Ultra Arc should be part of your multiworld.
Ultra Arc chapters will require normal Completion Medal items to access, which will be added to the multiworld if this option is enabled.
NOTE: If Ultra Arc is included in the Goal Arc, you must select AT LEAST chapter 3 (Focus On Flow).

options.label: Bonus Arc Chapters
options.description:
Choose which chapters in the Bonus Arc should be part of your multiworld.
Bonus Arc chapters will require Gold Completion Medal items to access, which will be added to the multiworld if this option is enabled.
All other unlock criteria, such as medals available and how many medals per chapter unlock, will be the same as chapters in the Ultra Arc.
NOTE: If Bonus Arc is included in the Goal Arc, you must select AT LEAST chapter 2 (The Way of the Marble).

options.label: Medal Types
options.description:
Choose which types of level completions to count as checks.
NOTE: Unless Treasureboxsanity is enabled, at least two of the four medal checks MUST be enabled.

Available values:
- Bronze
- Silver
- Gold
- Diamond

options.label: Medals Per Chapter
options.description:
Determine how many Completion Medals are needed to unlock each chapter.
(Chapter 2 will always require 5 medals to unlock.)

options.label: Extra Medals
options.description: Determine how many extra Completion Medals per enabled chapter to add to the item pool.

options.label: Treasureboxsanity
options.description:
Enables collecting Treasure Boxes as checks.
NOTE: Some Treasure Boxes require intentional death to collect. Be mindful of this if you are enabling Death Link.

options.label: Enable Blast
options.description:
Allow the ability to Blast behind a useful item.
NOTE: Logic is NOT written with Blast in mind.

options.label: Death Link
options.description: When you die by falling out of bounds or being crushed, everyone dies. The reverse is also true.

options.label: Death Link Amnesty
options.description: How many deaths it takes to send a Death Link.

options.label: Trap Fill Percentage
options.description: Determine a percentage of junk items in the item pool to replace with traps.

options.label: Add Time Trap Weight
options.description: This trap will instantly add 5 seconds to your current time.

options.label: Add Cosmetic Shuffle Weight
options.description: This trap will randomly shuffle what cosmetics your marble is wearing.

options.label: Anomaly Types
options.description: You can choose which type of anomalies you would like to see, including from the base game, Everyday mode, or both.

options.label: Enable Interactive Anomalies
options.description: If enabled, this will add checks tied to interacting with certain special anomalies such as Menya Botan and AZKi's Ice Cream Bar.

options.label: Talentsanity
options.description:
You can choose whether to group anomalies by Hololive gen, or by individual talent.
Generation provides more fluid logic, but introduces a lot of filler.
Talent has less filler, but has very one-to-one logic.

options.label: No Anomaly Percentage
options.description:
Percentage chance to land on a floor with no anomaly.
This does not affect the 2-floor anomaly failsafe.
It is recommended to keep this value low for syncs, and midrange for asyncs.

options.label: Reused Anomaly Percentage
options.description: Percentage chance during floor shuffle to include floors with anomalies that you have already seen.

options.label: Hard Anomalies
options.description:
Enable anomalies that are difficult to spot.
It is recommended to keep this option turned off for syncs.

options.label: Talentsanity Filler
options.description:
When playing on Talentsanity, determine whether or not to first fill the multiworld with talents not in holo8, space permitting.
none: No talents not in holo8 will be added to the item pool.
terminated: Adds terminated female talents.
holostars: Adds active and alumni Holostars talents.
everyone: Adds all historical Hololive talents.

options.label: Death Link
options.description: When you die, everyone dies. The reverse is also true (you will immediately be sent back to Floor 8).

options.label: DeathLink On Wrong Elevator
options.description:
If enabled, will also send a DeathLink if you board the wrong elevator.
Will have no effect if DeathLink is disabled.

options.label: Adaptive Locations
options.description:
Reduces the number of Abnos availiable to be in line with your goal.
For example: MALKUTH SUPRESSION = 28 Abnos items total (25 days + 3)
This massively reduces the amount of locations this game has.

options.description: This sets the amount of Equipment Checks the Gebura supression upgrade adds to each abnormality.

options.label: Goal Type
options.description:
What goal are you trying to reach in this game:
Vanilla: Collect 9 Seeds of Light and Beat Day 50
Dissolution: Reach a certain Dissolutuion percentage
Day and Dissolution: Reach a certain Dissolutuion percentage and complete a certain day
Supression: Clear a certain Core Supression / supress WhiteKnight or apocalypse bird

options.label: Dissolution Goal
options.description:
This sets the amount of Dissolution required to complete your goal.
!Only Observation Checks on non-tool Abnos are counted towards this!
The percentage how close you are to your goal will be dsiplayed at the start of every day.
This option is only applied if Goal Type is 'Dissolution' or 'Day and Dissolution'.
Min : 0
Max : 100

options.label: Day Goal
options.description:
This sets the amount of days required to beat to complete your goal.
This option is only applied if Goal Type is 'Day and Dissolution'.

options.label: Supression Goal
options.description:
This sets the supression required to complete your goal.
This option is only applied if Goal Type is 'Supression'.

options.label: Trap Item Percentage
options.description: Choose the percentage of trap items that will appear when filling the item pool with junk.

options.label: Trap Item Weights
options.description: Choose the odds of each trap item being created when filling the item pool with traps.

options.label: Apocalypse Bird Mode
options.description:
Determines if and how Apocalypse Bird is in your run.
Disabled: The three Birds will not appear in the Item Pool
Excluded: Apocalypse Bird Suppression Locations will not have progression items
Enabled: Apocalypse Bird Suppression Locations might have progression items
Apocalypse: Apocalypse Bird Suppression Locations will have progression items

options.label: Whitenight Mode
options.description:
Determines if and how Whitenight is in your run.
Disabled: Plague Doctor will not appear in the Item Pool
Excluded: Whitenight Suppression Locations will not have progression items
Enabled: Whitennight Suppression Locations might have progression items
DarkDay: Whitennight Suppression Locations will have progression items

options.label: Deathlink
options.description: Determines if Deathlink is enabled or not.

options.label: Deathlink Count
options.description:
Only takes effect if DeathlinkTrigger is 'EmployeeDeath' or 'AgentDeath'
Choose amount of times an Employee can die before a Deathlink is sent.

options.label: Deathlink Grace Period Length
options.description:
After a Deathlink is recieved a timer starts, a grace period.
While this timer is running there are no consequences for triggering a deathlink.
This is to prevent chain deaths. (A deathlink leading to the lobcorp player sending a deathlink at a later date)
Determines how long the grace period is in seconds.

options.label: Deathlink Effect
options.description:
Determines what consequences recieving a deathlink brings:
Button: DontTouchMe will be pressed.
Breakout: Sets all abnos Qlipoth-Counters in a department to 0.
Ordeal: Start the next ordeal after 30 seconds. Should Midnight already be completed, you will have to do it again.
Graze: Calls the Rabbit team to a random Department.
Trap: Triggers a random trap.
Train: Summons the Express Train to Hell.
Random: Randomly picks one from the above options everytime a deathlink is recieved.

options.label: Deathlink Trigger
options.description:
Determines which event counts as a death for Deathlink.
EmployeeDeath: A Deathlink is sent after X clerks and agents die. Counter resets on day end/reset. (X is determined by the DeathlinkCount option)
AgentDeath: A Deathlink is sent after X agent. Counter resets on day end/reset. (X is determined by the DeathlinkCount option)
DepartmentDeath: A Deathlink is sent after a whole department is dead.
Retry: A Deatlink is sent on Retry of a day.

options.label: Goal Stage
options.description:
Which stage should be the final one.
Both require 32 Star Cards, but Weapon's Core also requires 13 Time Capsules.
Selecting Merga as the goal completely removes Time Capsules from the item pool.

options.label: Chapter Unlocks
options.description:
Determines how stages should be unlocked.
Individual = Stages unlock in sets, based on their grouping in the Adventure Mode.
Progressive = Stages unlock in sets in a set order.
Open = Stages unlock individually, without their Star Card requirements.

options.label: Star Card Locks
options.description:
If using the Individual or Progressive Chapter Unlocks, should stages beyond Globe Opera be locked by a Star Card requirement.

Globe Opera and the Persua Episodes require 11 Star Cards, while the Bakunawa Episode requires 23.

options.label: Extra Progression Star Cards
options.description: How many extra Progression Flagged Star Cards should be added to the Item Pool.

options.label: Extra Progression Time Capsules
options.description: How many extra Progression Flagged Time Capsules should be added to the Item Pool.

options.label: Filler Star Cards
options.description: Allow extra Star Cards to be added as Filler Items. Unlike the extra Progression Flagged ones, these can be overwritten with traps.

options.label: Filler Time Capsules
options.description: Allow extra Time Capsules to be added as Filler Items. Unlike the extra Progression Flagged ones, these can be overwritten with traps.

options.label: Enable Rainbow S-Ranks
options.description: Makes getting Rainbow S-Ranks into locations.

options.label: Enable S-Ranks
options.description:
Makes getting S-Ranks into locations.
Obtaining a Rainbow S-Rank will also send the S-Rank location.

options.label: S-Ranks Logically Require Brave Stones
options.description:
Only adds S-Ranks to logic when at least one Brave Stone is acquired.
If disabled, then S-Ranking a stage via completing it without taking damage will be logically expected.

options.label: Enable A-Ranks
options.description:
Makes getting A-Ranks into locations.
Obtaining an S-Rank or Rainbow S-Rank will also send the A-Rank location.

options.label: Enable Item Chests
options.description: Makes opening chests into checks, adding 82 locations.

options.label: Enable Chest Tracers
options.description: Enables the drawing of arrows that point to any unopened chests in the level (can be toggled with F9 or Select).

options.label: Enable Chest Tracer Items
options.description:
Locks each stage's chest tracer behind an item, either globally or per stage.
If enabled, then the chests for each stage will not be logically required without the stage's tracer.

options.label: Strict Chest Locks
options.description: Require a stage's Chest Tracer to be able to open its chests at all.

options.label: Enable Milla's Shop
options.description: Makes buying items from Milla's shop on the level select into checks, adding as many locations as specified in the next option.

options.label: Enable Vinyl Shop
options.description: Makes buying the vinyls from the shop on the level select into checks, adding as many locations as specified in the next option.

options.label: Milla Shop Location Count
options.description: How many locations Milla's shop will have.

options.label: Vinyl Shop Location Count
options.description: How many locations the Vinyl shop will have.

options.label: Milla Shop Price
options.description: The cost that the items in Milla's shop will be set to, in Gold Gems.

options.label: Vinyl Shop Price
options.description: The cost that the items in the Vinyl shop will be set to, in Crystal Shards.

options.label: Gold Gem Crystal Cost
options.description: How many Crystal Shards are required to make a Gold Gem.

options.label: Gold Gem Core Cost
options.description: How many Robot Cores are required to make a Gold Gem.

options.label: Enemy Sanity
options.description: Makes killing each enemy type into checks, adding 72 locations.

options.label: Boss Sanity
options.description: Makes killing each boss type into checks, adding 44 locations.

options.label: Item Box Sanity
options.description:
Adds the various item boxes found in stages to the location pool.
Currently experimental with a severe lack of logic.

options.label: Item Box Sanity (Crystals)
options.description: Include Crystal Item Boxes in the Item Box Sanity.

options.label: Item Box Sanity (Petals)
options.description: Include Petal Item Boxes in the Item Box Sanity.

options.label: Item Box Sanity (Shields)
options.description: Include Shield Item Boxes in the Item Box Sanity.

options.label: Item Box Sanity (Gold Gem)
options.description: Include Gold Gem Item Boxes in the Item Box Sanity.

options.label: Include Extra Item Slots
options.description: Adds the unused extra item/potion slots to the item pool.

options.label: Trap Brave Stones
options.description: Treat negative Brave Stones as traps, allowing the copies specified in Trap Weights (Brave Stones) to be added to the item pool along the always placed ones and auto activating them upon receiving.

options.label: Trap Weights (Brave Stones)
options.description:
How likely it is to receive an extra copy of a negative Brave Stone as a trap. Valid options are:
none
low
medium
high

These will only be added if the Trap Brave Stones option is enabled.
In addition, the Invisibility Cloak, Madstone, Explosive Finale, Idol of Greed and Gravity Boots will only be added if the Potion Seller Mod Compatibility is enabled.

options.label: Trap Weights (Annoyance)
options.description:
How likely it is to receive a trap designed primarly to annoy the player. Valid options are:
none
low
medium
high

options.label: Trap Weights (Gameplay)
options.description:
How likely it is to receive a trap designed to impact gameplay. Valid options are:
none
low
medium
high

options.label: Trap Weights (Mini-Game)
options.description:
How likely it is to receive a trap that forces the player to play a life or death mini-game. Valid options are:
none
low
medium
high

options.label: Dangerous Time Limit
options.description: Make the Time Limit Brave Stone kill the player upon the timer running out.

options.label: Fast Weapon's Core
options.description: Skips the actual stage of Weapon's Core and goes straight to the Bakunawa Fusion fight.

options.label: Trap Chance
options.description: How many fillers will be replaced with traps. 0 means no additional traps, 100 means all fillers are traps.

options.label: Sonic Mod Compatibility
options.description: Adds seven Chaos Emerald items to the item pool. When all seven are collected the Chaos Emeralds item from the Sonic mod will be added to the player's inventory, allowing usage of a character's Super Form.

options.label: Potion Seller Mod Compatibility
options.description: Adds the items from the Potion Seller mod to the item pool.

options.label: Lightning Mod Compatibility
options.description: Adds the Step Booster from the Lightning mod to the item pool.

options.label: DeathLink
options.description:
When you die, everyone dies. Of course the reverse is true too.
If survive is enabled, then you can revive on the spot as normal.

options.label: RingLink
options.description: Whether picking up a crystal shard will also send one to other RingLink players.

options.label: TrapLink
options.description: Whether your received traps are linked to other players.

options.label: DamageLink
options.description:
Any damage you take is also sent to other players with DamageLink enabled.
Of course the reverse is true too.

options.label: Valid Starting Stages
options.description: Stages that the generator can choose to be the starting stage if using the Open Chapters option.

options.label: Valid Starting Bosses
options.description:
Bosses that the generator can choose to be the starting stage if using the Open Chapters option.
Merga is only a valid option if the goal is set to Weapon's Core.

options.label: Level pool
options.description:
The levels the seed plays, keyed by display name. Every level is a valid
key; the default is all of them. A level left out generates no checks and
no access item. With randomize_level_pool on, this is the set the random
draw picks from. The find_bob goal forces the Digsite and the six note
levels into the pool. The Digsite's gate-locked checks (Open the Digsite
Gates, Find Bob, the Red Keycard, the Bolter) only exist when the pool
holds the Digsite and every note level.

options.label: Randomize level pool
options.description:
Play a random subset of level_pool instead of the whole set. Each seed
draws the subset size at random, from the smallest set the goal allows
(goal_amount_levels levels for complete_levels, enough
collectible-holding levels for collect_collectibles, the Bob chain for
find_bob) up to the whole pool. Off by default.

options.label: Milestone step
options.description:
How finely each level's cleanliness is checked. 5 percent gives 20
checks per level; 1 percent gives 100 (a very large world, more still
with above_and_beyond). The 100 percent rung (Employee of the Month)
exists at every step, and steps finer than 5 keep the 5 percent step's
ladder ceiling and logic margins, so no check gets closer to a level's
known maximum than at the 5 percent step.

options.label: Above and beyond
options.description:
Extend each level's milestone ladder past 100 percent (levels overfill
via restorables and bonus points). The ladder tops out a full step under
the level's known maximum cleanliness, so the last rung stays attainable.
Those top rungs lean on the punch-out report, which the
auto_fill_punchout_report option can fill for you. Off by default.

options.label: Speedrunsanity
options.description:
Add a Speedrun check to every level: punch out at least 95 percent clean
within the level's par time. Off by default, so seeds carry no speed
pressure unless asked for.

options.label: Toolsanity
options.description:
Lock each level's tools and machines behind per-level items: hands
(carrying), the laser welder, the shovel, the J-HARM lift, the vendor, and
the incinerator become progression, while the sniffer, broom, and bin
dispenser become useful unlocks. Every level starts with just the mop and
the Slosh-O-Matic, and higher cleanliness milestones need the tools that
can physically reach them. On by default.

options.label: Random starting kit
options.description:
With toolsanity on, each level independently rolls its free starting
pair: mop plus Slosh-O-Matic, or hands plus incinerator (the displaced
pair becomes that level's items). A hands start is the hard way: debris
can burn, but blood waits for the mop. On a hands-start level the
Self-Cleaning Mop counts as the Slosh-O-Matic in logic, since a mop that
never dirties needs no rinse bucket. Off by default (every level starts
mop and Slosh-O-Matic).

options.label: Hard start Squeaky Clean Boots
options.description:
With random_starting_kit on, a level that rolls the hands and
incinerator start also starts with its Squeaky Clean Boots, so the
janitor tracks no bloody footprints while the mop is still locked. That
level's boots item is granted up front instead of entering the pool.
On by default. Does nothing without random_starting_kit.

options.label: Mop start Self-Cleaning Mop
options.description:
With random_starting_kit on, a level that rolls the mop and
Slosh-O-Matic start also starts with its Self-Cleaning Mop, so the mop
never needs rinsing while cleaning the easy way. That level's Self-Cleaning
Mop item is granted up front instead of entering the pool. On by default.
Does nothing without random_starting_kit (a hard-start level's Self-Cleaning
Mop stays in the pool, where it stands in for the itemized Slosh-O-Matic).

options.label: Auto fill punchout report
options.description:
Fill the punch-out report for the janitor. The form's paperwork counts
toward cleanliness, and some of its answers (the causes of death on each
PID, the casing and bullet-hole counts) cannot be known from playing, so
this fills the whole form in: the report fills itself when you first use
the punch clock, and each PID chip fills its own death report when you feed
it into the machine. You still have to find the chips. While this is on the
mod keeps the form filled, so your own writing in it does not stick. Off by
default.

options.label: Trap percentage
options.description:
The share of filler items that become traps: a mess dump near the
janitor, a spilled bucket, thirty seconds of walking at half or double
speed, a magnet pull that yanks everything loose nearby toward the
janitor, or thirty seconds of near-zero gravity. Traps arrive from the
multiworld while cleaning; they are never required by logic. 0 disables
traps.

options.label: Useful percentage
options.description:
The share of filler items that become useful supplies: a bucket of
clean water or an empty bin dropped next to the janitor. Supplies arrive
from the multiworld while cleaning; they are never required by logic. When
trap_percentage and useful_percentage together pass 100, traps take their
share first. 0 disables supplies.

options.label: Death Link
options.description:
When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the
reverse is true too. Either way the whole shift goes down together: every
janitor in the session dies with the first, and the remains are yours to
clean up. A death that arrives while no level is loaded is dropped, never
held. Off by default.

options.label: Trap Link
options.description:
Link trap activations with every other player who enabled trap link:
when a trap fires in your game it also fires in theirs, and their linked
traps arrive here as the closest of this game's traps (one with no close
equivalent is ignored). Linked traps arrive even with trap_percentage 0.
Off by default.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
The win condition.

complete_levels: punch out of `goal_amount_levels` levels.
find_bob: follow the notes and find Bob in the Digsite (needs the six
note levels plus the Digsite).
collect_collectibles: bank `goal_amount_collectibles` collectibles in
the trunk.

options.label: Goal amount levels
options.description:
How many levels the complete_levels goal needs. It must fit the level
pool: asking for more levels than the pool holds fails generation. `all`
is every level. The other goals ignore it.

options.label: Goal amount collectibles
options.description:
How many collectibles the collect_collectibles goal needs. It must fit
the level pool: asking for more collectibles than the pooled levels hold
fails generation. `all` is every collectible. The other goals ignore
it.

options.label: Starting levels
options.description: How many levels are unlocked at the start of the seed.

options.label: Game Mode
options.description:
Which install layout this seed targets.

`vanilla` (default): retail HP2 + M212 patch, the normal story flow.
Whether the 7 story regions gate behind bookcases (the Progressive Level
Key chain plus the Duelling / Quidditch keys) or open immediately is
governed by `vanilla_gate_levels`. The other 7 keys are always
precollected here.

`open_castle`: the HP2 Bingo community pack's distribution maps (every
door unlocked from spawn). All 14 bookcase-blocker keys are AP items
gating each level transition.

Harry's starting spells are set by `starting_spells`, not by this option.

options.label: Starting Spells
options.description:
Spells Harry starts with. Any spell not listed is an AP item instead.

The `vanilla` game mode physically requires Lumos and Flipendo to finish
the Whomping Willow level. If either is missing here in vanilla, they are
added automatically, since the seed would otherwise have nowhere reachable
to place them. Open castle leaves the set untouched.

Valid spells: Lumos, Flipendo, Alohomora, Rictusempra, Skurge, Diffindo, Spongify.

options.label: Allow Running logic
options.description:
How much running the logic assumes. Applies in both game modes.

`off`: no running is expected.
`on`: Running becomes a logic flag and certain regions or locations become
reachable earlier.
`difficult`: everything `on` covers, plus the running tricks with tight
timing or precise positioning, e.g. in Castle Exterior.

Anything above `off` makes sprinting free (no bean cost, and usable at 0
beans), so the running this logic relies on is genuinely always available.

options.label: Allow Glitched logic
options.description:
If true, locations and regions tagged with the `Glitched` logic flag are
treated as reachable via glitches, without the items they would otherwise
need. One umbrella flag covering every glitch shortcut. Applies in both game
modes.

Additive only: a seed solvable with it off stays solvable with it on.
`Glitched` is a logic flag, not an item: when this is on the world
precollects it so any `... | Glitched` clauses in the rule tables pass.
Off by default. The standard logic expects no glitches. Enabling it assumes
the player can perform the glitches the tagged checks rely on.

Hidden from the player YAML template and option UIs (no glitch checks ship
this release). The option stays wired so it still parses if set by hand.

options.label: Vanilla gate levels
options.description:
Vanilla only. If true, the 7 story regions are gated: the mod spawns a
bookcase blocking each region until its key arrives. The 5 level regions
(Bicorn, Boomslang, Goyle, Slytherin Common Room, Forbidden Forest) form a
cumulative chain matching vanilla's linear story order, so they are gated
by 5 copies of one Progressive Level Key item: each copy received unlocks
the next level in that order. Duelling and Quidditch are standalone and
keep their own named keys.

If false, all region keys are precollected instead, so the regions open
immediately and no bookcases spawn (the classic vanilla flow).

options.label: Allow Missable Progression
options.description:
Vanilla-only (ignored in open castle). If true, missable locations in
un-replayable vanilla levels (Willow, Bicorn, Boomslang, Goyle, Slytherin
Common, Forest and Chamber) are allowed to hold progression items. This covers
missable secrets (when `enable_secrets` is true) and, when `containersanity`
is on, the containers in those same one-way regions.

If false, those missable locations are filler-only, which is safer because
the player can't soft-lock by missing a one-way check. Locations in
replayable areas (hubs, the spell challenges) always allow progression
regardless of this setting; this flag only gates the un-replayable subset.

Open castle makes every level infinitely replayable, so nothing is
missable there and this option has no effect.

options.label: Open castle goal: cards
options.description:
Open castle only. Wizard cards needed to open the Great Hall. 0
disables this clause. Counts cards Harry actually owns (including AP-granted).

options.label: Open castle goal: spells
options.description:
Open castle only. Spells needed to open the Great Hall. 0 disables
this clause. (If every open castle goal clause is 0/off, this is forced
to 7.)

options.label: Open castle goal: level objectives
options.description:
Open castle only. Level objectives finished to open the Great Hall. 0
disables. 13 objectives: 3 key-item levels + 2 bosses + 2 story levels
+ 5 challenges + the Gold Card Room.

options.label: Open castle goal: all duels
options.description:
Open castle only. If true, all 10 Duelling Club duels must be won to
open the Great Hall.

options.label: Open castle goal: all Quidditch matches
options.description:
Open castle only. If true, all 6 Quidditch matches must be won to open
the Great Hall.

options.label: Always Goyle in Slytherin Common Room
options.description:
Open castle only. If true, Harry always wears the Goyle disguise inside
the Slytherin Common Room, so the Slytherins there never chase him. The
disguise comes off on leaving the level, and a Polyjuice Potion Trap
received there has no effect.

options.label: Enable Wizard Cards
options.description:
Card shuffle. The 101 wizard cards are always AP locations; this only
chooses how the card items are placed.

true: cards are shuffled into the multiworld pool.
false: each card is locked to its own original spot.

options.label: Enable Secrets
options.description:
If true, the 109 Secrets become AP locations, plus open castle's 9 in
the Gryffindor challenge (118 total in open castle).

options.label: Enable Challenge Stars
options.description:
If true, the Challenge Stars become AP locations:
44 across the 4 spell-challenges (Rictusempra, Skurge, Diffindo, Spongify),
plus 10 in open castle's Gryffindor challenge (54 total in open castle).

options.label: Containersanity
options.description:
If true, ~283 in-world containers (chests without cards, cauldrons,
cigar / jewel / music boxes, decanters, oil cans, plant pots, vases,
knights, ingredient spawners, statues, toilets) each become a location.

options.label: Tradersanity
options.description:
Every non-Weasley card vendor and ingredient vendor sells one AP
location check on its first sale, then permanently reverts to selling its
normal cards or ingredient. The price mode sets what that AP sale costs:

off: vendors sell their normal stock only, no AP checks.

price_vanilla: a normal in-game price. Ingredient vendors keep their real
price; card vendors charge a card-like price.

price_random: a random price per vendor, fixed for the whole seed, from
10 to 250 beans.

price_low: a flat low price of 10 beans for every vendor.

options.label: Enable Quidditch upgrades
options.description:
If true, the Nimbus 2001 from Fred and the Quidditch Armour from George
become locations.

options.label: Tradersanity hint on open
options.description:
If true, opening a Tradersanity vendor's dialogue for the first time
publishes a broadcast hint for that vendor's AP check.
No effect when `tradersanity` is off.

options.label: Skip vendor voices
options.description:
If true, every vendor's in-trade voice cues (sell / transaction-done
/ decline / narrator instruction / Harry's inquiry) are skipped.

options.label: Enable Duelling
options.description: If true, each of the 10 duels at the Duelling Club becomes a location.

options.label: Enable Quidditch matches
options.description: If true, each of the 6 Quidditch matches becomes a location.

options.label: Enable Spell Challenge times
options.description:
If true, beating the replay par time ("Mastered") on each of the 4
spell challenges (Rictusempra, Skurge, Diffindo, Spongify) becomes a
location.

options.label: Traps
options.description:
Which trap types may appear in your item pool. Traps replace a fraction
(set by `trap_fill_percent`) of the filler. Pick any subset.

An empty set means no traps at all.

Valid traps:
Polyjuice Potion Trap (turns Harry into Goyle for the rest of the level)
Engorgio Trap (giant Harry ~30s)
Reducio Trap (tiny Harry ~30s)
Overcompensation Trap (giant wand for the rest of the level)
Levicorpus Trap (Harry hangs upside down ~30s)
Jelly-Legs Jinx Trap (jumping disabled ~20s while Harry jumps at random)
Bean Thief Trap (steals up to 200 beans)
Drowsiness Draught Trap (sleepy slow ~20s)
Confundus Trap (inverted camera look ~20s)
Obliviate Trap (spellbook withheld ~30s)

options.label: Trap fill percent
options.description:
Percentage of filler items replaced with traps when `traps` is non-empty.
Does nothing when `traps` is empty.

options.label: Trap Link
options.description:
If true, every trap you receive is also sent to all other TrapLink
slots in the room, and traps they receive are applied to you. Inbound
traps from another HP2 slot apply by name; a trap from a different game
(whose name HP2 has no effect for) maps to a random HP2 trap, so a linked
player always feels something. Independent of `traps`: you still receive
linked traps even if your own seed generates none. Inbound traps respect
your `traps` selection. A trap you turned off is remapped to one you kept
(unless `traps` is empty, in which case any of the ten can land).

options.label: Ring Link
options.description:
If true, in-game bean pickups and vendor spending are mirrored
to every other RingLink slot in the room, and their currency changes
are applied to yours. AP-granted bean filler and the Bean Thief trap
are not mirrored.

options.label: Ghost Players
options.description:
If true, the other Harry Potter 2 players in the room who are on the
same map appear in your game as translucent ghosts, moving and animating
as they play, and your Harry appears in theirs. Cosmetic only: a ghost has
no collision and cannot be targeted. /ghosts in the client toggles it
mid-run; off also stops sharing your own position.

options.label: Music randomizer
options.description:
If true, every music track is swapped for another from the same pool.
Requires the client to be run in administrator mode if the game files
live inside your program files.

Upon first connect, you need to tell your client where your game files live.

There are 2 music pools:
A long-form background music pool and a shorter pool of jingles.

Music can be reshuffled if needed with the /reroll_music command.
Music can be restored to their original with the /restore_music command.

options.label: Sound randomizer
options.description:
Shuffle the sound effects, deterministically per seed.
Requires the client to be run in administrator mode if the game files
live inside your program files.

Upon first connect, you need to tell your client where your game files live.

`off` (default): sound effects are left alone.
`on`: every sound effect is swapped for another of similar length (sounds
shuffle within their own length band: short / medium / long).
`no_footsteps`: the same, but footstep sounds are left alone, since
randomizing them can be overwhelming.

Sounds can be reshuffled with the /reroll_sounds command.
Sounds can be restored to their original with the /restore_sounds command.

options.label: Dialogue randomizer
options.description:
Shuffle the spoken dialogue / voice lines.
Requires the client to be run in administrator mode if the game files
live inside your program files.

Upon first connect, you need to tell your client where your game files live.

`off` (default): dialogue is left alone.
`within_actor`: each character's lines are shuffled among their own, so every
character keeps their own voice but says the wrong things.
`all_actors`: lines are shuffled across every character, so anyone can speak
anyone's line.

Dialogue can be reshuffled with the /reroll_dialogue command.
Dialogue can be restored to its original with the /restore_dialogue command.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Pick a Goal to finish the game.
Hell Castle is the usual finish of the game, being the last stage to beat.
Volcano and Mountaintop are boss rush stages and are therefore regarded has more difficult stages than Hell Castle.

options.label: Shuffle Books
options.description:
Controls whether buying Books are checks.
At least one of Shuffle Books, Shuffle Enemies or Shop Checks needs to be on.

options.label: Shuffle Enemies
options.description:
Controls whether enemies drop a check.
At least one of Shuffle Books, Shuffle Enemies or Shop Checks needs to be on.

common enemies: Every non-boss enemy has a 5% chance to drop.
boss enemies:   Every boss enemy has a 25% chance to drop.
both:           Both settings are on.

options.label: Shop Checks
options.description:
When enabled, buying each item in a shop for the first time sends a check.

That is 462 checks, one per item the shops stock, wherever you buy it. The
shop shows an Archipelago logo until the check has been collected, and the
normal item afterwards.

options.label: Progressive Shop
options.description:
When enabled, each town's shop stock is unlocked by its own Progressive
Shop items instead of by completing stages.

Every shop has its own track, so opening Island's stock does not open
Town's: 32 Progressive Town Shop, 15 Village, 1 Resort and 33 Island. Town
keeps its first row stocked because that is where you start; Village,
Resort and Island hold nothing at all until their own first item arrives,
and say so.

In the base game only Town's stock grows with the stages you beat; Village,
Resort and Island sell everything the moment you arrive. So this option
replaces Town's gating and adds gating to the other three.

Does nothing unless Shop Checks is on.

options.label: Book Cost Randomizer
options.description:
Randomizes the costs of Books.

vanilla:                  Costs are vanilla (1000*stage number).
random_balanced:          Costs are randomized, but still balanced.
random_extreme:           Costs can range between 1-99999.
random_extreme_expensive: Costs can range between 1-999999. (Not recommended)
vanilla_tenth:            Costs are vanilla divided by 10.

options.label: Class Randomizer
options.description:
When enabled, start with the Class selected in Class Selector, and unlock other Classes via checks.
This also starts you off with the Forget Tree, to switch Classes, and Forget is free.

options.label: Class Selector
options.description: Selects the Class you start with when Class Randomizer is enabled.

options.label: Classes required for Castle
options.description:
Number of Ranger Classes you must have before entering the Castle stage.
Your starting class counts towards this, so 1 means "no extra classes needed".
Ignored unless Class Randomizer is enabled, and raised to match an earlier
boss stage that asks for more.

options.label: Classes required for Submarine Shrine
options.description:
Number of Ranger Classes you must have before entering the Submarine Shrine stage.
Your starting class counts towards this, so 1 means "no extra classes needed".
Ignored unless Class Randomizer is enabled, and raised to match an earlier
boss stage that asks for more.

options.label: Classes required for Pyramid
options.description:
Number of Ranger Classes you must have before entering the Pyramid stage.
Your starting class counts towards this, so 1 means "no extra classes needed".
Ignored unless Class Randomizer is enabled, and raised to match an earlier
boss stage that asks for more.

options.label: Classes required for Ice Castle
options.description:
Number of Ranger Classes you must have before entering the Ice Castle stage.
Your starting class counts towards this, so 1 means "no extra classes needed".
Ignored unless Class Randomizer is enabled, and raised to match an earlier
boss stage that asks for more.

options.label: Classes required for Hell Castle
options.description:
Number of Ranger Classes you must have before entering the Hell Castle stage.
Your starting class counts towards this, so 1 means "no extra classes needed".
Ignored unless Class Randomizer is enabled, and raised to match an earlier
boss stage that asks for more.

options.label: Minimum number of required pre-Castle stages
options.description:
Minimum number of pre-Castle stages you must unlock before entering the Castle stage.
Pre-Castle stages are: Grassland 1-7, Lake, Hill Country 1-3, Forest 1&2, Cavern 1-3 and Castle Gate.

options.label: Maximum number of required pre-Castle stages
options.description:
Maximum number of pre-Castle stages you must unlock before entering the Castle stage.
Pre-Castle stages are: Grassland 1-7, Lake, Hill Country 1-3, Forest 1&2, Cavern 1-3 and Castle Gate.

options.label: Actual number of required pre-Castle stages
options.description:
Actual number of required pre-Castle stages to beat.
Only used for rules and tracking.

options.label: Minimum number of required pre-Submarine Shrine stages
options.description:
Minimum number of pre-Submarine Shrine stages you must unlock before entering the Submarine Shrine stage.
Pre-Submarine Shrine stages are: Seaside 1-4, Submarine 1-4, Mist Grove 1-3 and ???.

options.label: Maximum number of required pre-Submarine Shrine stages
options.description:
Maximum number of pre-Submarine Shrine stages you must unlock before entering the Submarine Shrine stage.
Pre-Submarine Shrine stages are: Seaside 1-4, Submarine 1-4, Mist Grove 1-3 and ???.

options.label: Actual number of required pre-Submarine Shrine stages
options.description:
Actual number of required pre-Submarine Shrine stages to beat.
Only used for rules and tracking.

options.label: Minimum number of required pre-Pyramid stages
options.description:
Minimum number of pre-Pyramid stages you must unlock before entering the Pyramid stage.
Pre-Pyramid stages are: Desert 1-8, Oasis and Beach 1-3.

options.label: Maximum number of required pre-Pyramid stages
options.description:
Maximum number of pre-Pyramid stages you must unlock before entering the Pyramid stage.
Pre-Pyramid stages are: Desert 1-8, Oasis and Beach 1-3.

options.label: Actual number of required pre-Pyramid stages
options.description:
Actual number of required pre-Pyramid stages to beat.
Only used for rules and tracking.

options.label: Minimum number of required pre-Ice Castle stages
options.description:
Minimum number of pre-Ice Castle stages you must unlock before entering the Ice Castle stage.
Pre-Ice Castle stages are: Cavern 4-6, Snowfield 1-8, Mountain 1&2 and Frozen Lake.

options.label: Maximum number of required pre-Ice Castle stages
options.description:
Maximum number of pre-Ice Castle stages you must unlock before entering the Ice Castle stage.
Pre-Ice Castle stages are: Cavern 4-6, Snowfield 1-8, Mountain 1&2 and Frozen Lake.

options.label: Actual number of required pre-Ice Castle stages
options.description:
Actual number of required pre-Ice Castle stages to beat.
Only used for rules and tracking.

options.label: Minimum number of required pre-Hell Castle stages
options.description:
Minimum number of pre-Hell Castle stages you must unlock before entering the Hell Castle stage.
Pre-Hell Castle stages are: Snowfield 9, Beach 4, Forest 3-6, !!!, Hell 1-8,
Inferno 1-3, Blood Lake, Cavern 7&8 and Hell Gate.

options.label: Maximum number of required pre-Hell Castle stages
options.description:
Maximum number of pre-Hell Castle stages you must unlock before entering the Hell Castle stage.
Pre-Hell Castle stages are: Snowfield 9, Beach 4, Forest 3-6, !!!, Hell 1-8,
Inferno 1-3, Blood Lake, Cavern 7&8 and Hell Gate.

options.label: Actual number of required pre-HellCastle stages
options.description:
Actual number of required pre-Hell Castle stages to beat.
Only used for rules and tracking.

options.label: Enforce Logic
options.description:
When enabled, stages that are out of logic cannot be entered at all.

They still show on the map, greyed out, so you can see what you hold. There
is no way to override it mid-run, which is the point: the run cannot be
broken by accident or on purpose.

options.label: Enforce Shop Logic
options.description:
When enabled, a shop item that Archipelago does not consider reachable yet
cannot be bought. It is greyed out until the world has opened far enough.

This is the shop's half of Enforce Logic. Without it the shop still sells
anything it has stocked -- logic simply does not count on you buying it.

Does nothing unless Shop Checks is on.

options.label: Trap Percentage
options.description:
What share of the filler items are Traps, as a percentage.

The share is of the items left once every stage and class unlock is placed,
so at 100 every non-progression check you find is a Trap and Archipelago
never hands you a weapon or a compo.

options.label: Trap Disguise
options.description:
When enabled, a trap waiting in a shop or a book wears the name of some
other item in the room, misspelled: "Unlock Laek", "Progressive Eisland
Shoppe", "Mothwing Cloack".

It reads as a real item at a glance and gives itself away only if you look
properly, in the spirit of Ocarina of Time's ice traps. While it is on the
shops never send a hint for a trap, since the hint would carry its real
name; that quiet is itself a small tell, but a smaller one. Anyone else
scouting the location by other means still sees the trap for what it is.

options.label: Shop Hints
options.description:
What the item shop and the Book shop tell you, and the room, about what
they sell.

off:            a shop item that is still a check reads "AP Item" and shows
                only its price; nothing is hinted.
important_only: you see everything; the room is only sent hints for
                progression and traps, so a 462-item shop does not bury
                everyone else's hints.
all:            you see everything and every item is hinted to the room.

options.label: Gold Multiplier
options.description: Multiplies the gold dropped by enemies.

options.label: XP Multiplier
options.description: Multiplies the XP gained per enemy killed.

options.label: Drop Multiplier
options.description: Multiplies the chance of enemies dropping an item.

options.label: Free Respec
options.description:
When enabled, respeccing at the Forget Tree is always free.
