Everything the merchant sold as gear leaves the buy tab and is shuffled
into the item pool - it can land anywhere, including other players'
worlds: weapons, attachments, the knives, the attache case sizes,
crafting recipes, body armor and the trade tab's stock. The extended
arsenal rides along: the Deluxe weapons and the Separate Ways guns that
work in Leon's campaign (Sentinel Nine, Skull Shaker, the Sawed-off
W-870, the Blast Crossbow and the XM96E1) join the pool too, and so do
the Extra Content weapons (Handcannon, Chicago Sweeper, and the Primal
Knife as the knife ladder's second step); the in-game mod keeps the
game from handing those three out or deleting them, so nothing is
written to your profile. Case sizes and knives arrive as progressive
items, each one the next step up. What stays on his shelf is the
restocked Staples (healing and crafting), tune-ups, selling and the
spinel exchange.

Expect a different power curve: your next gun is a check somewhere out
there, not a purchase. Gear never gates logic, so a seed can always be
finished with what the world hands you.

Pairs naturally with Merchant Shop Checks, so the emptied shelf sells
checks instead of nothing. While either option is on, BioRand's own
Random Merchant is switched off at patch time - one owner per shop.

options.label: Merchant Trade Checks Per Chapter
options.description:
How many Archipelago checks the merchant's TRADE tab releases each
chapter, purchased with Spinel.

The seed total is this number across 15 chapters, so the default 3
gives 45 checks, which is also the cap. Same lever shape as Merchant
Shop Checks Per Chapter, because the two tabs are two halves of one
merchant. Release is round-robin (every chapter gets its first trade
check before any chapter gets a second), and checks rotate through the
tab's seven slots, so any rate works.

Each check has a fixed spinel price by tier; the pool mints exactly
enough Spinel to cover every check, and the game's own Merchant
Request rewards (84 spinel across the campaign) are gravy on top.
Trade checks never refund.

0 turns the AP half of the tab off: it becomes a pure currency
exchange (infinite Velvet Blue plus restocking gems), with the
vanilla trade stock shuffled into the multiworld either way while
Shuffle Merchant Gear is on.

Requires Shuffle Merchant Gear, like the rest of the merchant
takeover.

options.label: Starting Arsenal
options.description:
Start the run already holding this many random weapons from the pool.

The guns are in your case from the campaign's first moment, ammo to
match, exactly like BioRand's own starting loadout - no delivery, no
Storage detour. Each one leaves the item pool (a filler stack takes
its place), so nobody ever finds a second copy of a gun you started
with. Starting Arsenal Types picks which classes the draw may take.

Each gun may bring its attachment along: a scope-fit gun always
starts with a scope (the basic one, never the Biosensor), and every
other gun has a 50% chance of one compatible attachment - a stock,
the Laser Sight. Attachments come from the scattered merchant gear
and leave the pool exactly like the guns do.

Requires Shuffle Merchant Gear: the roll draws from the scattered
arsenal. Without the shuffle this option refuses to generate - use
BioRand's own starting-inventory options on the launcher's options
screen instead, which still work exactly as they always did.

options.label: Starting Arsenal Types
options.description:
Which weapon types the Starting Arsenal may draw.

Mirrors BioRand's own starting-inventory pickers: handgun, shotgun,
smg, rifle, magnum, bolt, arrow, flame. The Rocket Launcher is
deliberately not among them - an infinite-ammo novelty is not an
opening weapon, and it is already kept off the merchant's shelf under
scatter for the same reason.

Bolt Thrower and Arrows are off by default; tick them for a wider
lucky dip. With two starting weapons the draw takes two different
types whenever the filter leaves it a choice.

Only consulted while Starting Arsenal is above zero.

options.label: Weapon Randomization
options.description:
How far BioRand's weapon-upgrade randomization goes, decided by your
settings file.

**off**: the vanilla upgrade system, untouched.

**stats_only**: every weapon's upgrade curve is rerolled - power,
capacity, reload and fire rate can land anywhere from forgettable to
monstrous - but the upgrade tree itself stays vanilla.

**full**: the rerolled curves AND randomized upgrade paths.

The multiworld holds the weapons now, so the choice about their
character rides with them: set here once, applied identically on every
patch, and BioRand's own two switches for this are taken out of your
hands in the launcher. One control because BioRand only supports these
three shapes - upgrade paths without stats is the combination it
refuses, and it broke v0.5.0's release seeds.

Flavor only. The logic never requires any weapon, so a cursed reroll
cannot strand a seed - it can only make you cry.

Old settings files keep working: true means full, false means off.

options.label: Check Guidance
options.description:
Permission ceiling for the in-game world markers that tag unchecked AP locations.

off: no world markers at all - the mod's marker toggle is disabled.
markers: neutral [AP] markers are available; the player can still toggle them
and tune distance/text live in the REFramework script UI.
markers_rarity: additionally unlocks the opt-in marker colours that reveal each
check's scouted item classification (progression/useful/filler) - hint-tier
information, which is why it requires this level.

The section-scoped overlay header (current area name + check counts) is always
on and not affected by this option. Enforcement is client-side, like DeathLink.

options.label: Marker Detail
options.description:
How much your in-game world markers say.

This is the level you start the run with, and it is what you see: pick
locate here and markers read at locate the moment you connect. The
in-game Guidance tab can still change it whenever you like, and once you
change it there your choice sticks for that seed.

It was a ceiling until 2026-08-17, which never made sense: in a
multiworld everyone writes their own settings file, so it only ever
capped the person who set it, and asked the same question twice.

minimal: distance and height only.
basic: also the chapter and the area name.
locate: also the item as it appeared in vanilla, what it is sitting in,
and any note on how to reach it. This says nothing about what the
multiworld actually put there.
identify: also the real item and which player it belongs to. This is a
spoiler, and it is the level a bought hint always shows.
developer: also the location code from the spoiler log. A debug tool.

Markers must be allowed at all (see Check Guidance) for any of this to
matter.

options.label: Unlocked Typewriters
options.description:
Typewriter save points that are unlocked from the start of the run.

Name each typewriter by its name, with or without the "(Save Point)"
tag, or by its stage id: "Farm Typewriter", "Farm Typewriter (Save
Point)" and 43300 all mean the same one. Case does not matter. The
launcher writes stage ids.

options.label: Mode
options.description:
Game mode.

- `hunt_a_thon` (default): hunting a large monster requires its
  license. Licenses are scattered across the multiworld. A random goal monster
  is selected, and hunting that goal monster wins the game.
  
  Monsters are split into three tiers based on difficulty. Accessing a tier of
  monsters is gated by having half of the previous tier unlocked or completed.
  Additionally, the goal monster is gated by having or completing half of the
  highest tier of monsters. 
  
  NOTE: Huntathon requires a save file at HR 100+ with the ability to clear
  Crimson Glow Valstrax for base game, a save file at MR 10+ with the ability
  to clear P. Malzeno and Amatsu if you enable Sunbreak, and a save file at
  MR 180+ with the ability to clear Risen Shagaru Magala for Sunbreak with Risen Elders enabled.

- `quest_rando`: completing a quest requires its unlock item. Unlocks
  are scattered around the multiworld. Clear your way through quests 
  until reaching the goal. MonsterCount is ignored in this mode;
  the rest of the options apply. This option is intended for
  new save files.

options.label: Quest Pool
options.description:
QuestRando Only: Select which pool of quests should be randomized.
- `quest_rando_village` (default): each village quest's boss monster
  is randomly swapped (within per-map compatibility). Clearing a quest
  sends AP checks when the matching `Unlock: <quest>` and — if weapons
  are enabled — the wielded weapon's license are held. Goal =
  clearing the final village urgent "Comeuppance". There are 18 quests
  in this pool.
- `quest_rando_hub`: each low/high rank hub quest's boss monster is
  randomly swapped (within per-map compatibility). Clearing a quest sends
  AP checks when the matching `Unlock: <quest>` and — if weapons
  are enabled — the wielded weapon's license are held. Goal =
  clearing the 7* urgent "Serpent Goddess of Thunder". There are 59 quests
  in this pool.
- `quest_rando_sunbreak`: each hub and master rank quest's boss monster
  is randomly swapped (within per-map compatibility). Clearing a quest
  sends AP checks when the matching `Unlock: <quest>` and — if weapons
  are enabled — the wielded weapon's license are held. Goal =
  clearing the MR6 urgent "Proof of Courage". This option requires 
  Sunbreak, and will default to `quest_rando_hub` if sunbreak is disabled.
  There are 118 quests in this pool.

options.label: Questsanity
options.description:
QuestRando Only: Include optional quests in the QuestRando pool.
This option will add 3 quests to Village QuestRando,
26 quests to Hub QuestRando, and 60 quests to Sunbreak QuestRando

options.label: Include Sunbreak
options.description:
Include Sunbreak monsters (and their subspecies / Risen variants) in
the world. When disabled, only base-game Rise monsters are randomized.

options.label: Include Risen
options.description:
Include Risen elder dragons (Anomaly Investigation endgame —
Risen Kushala Daora, Chameleos, Teostra, Shagaru Magala, Crimson
Glow Valstrax). Default off because they are post-credits / very
high difficulty. Has no effect when Sunbreak is disabled.

options.label: Starting Monsters
options.description:
Huntathon Only: Select which monsters can be the starting monster.
Cannot include elder dragons or rajang to avoid overlap with the goal monster.
See the game info document for a full list of expected monster names.
Leave this option as "Random" to allow any starting monster.

options.label: Goal Monsters
options.description:
Huntathon Only: Select which monsters can be the goal monster.
The goal monster must be an elder dragon or Rajang.
See the game info document for a full list of expected monster names.
Leave this option as "Random" to allow any goal monster

options.label: Include Weapons
options.description:
Add weapon-type licenses to the pool. When enabled, weapon
licenses fill the spare itempool slots; the player needs the
license for their currently-equipped weapon to complete a hunt
(HuntAThon) or send a quest-clear check (QuestRando). One random
weapon license is always precollected. Applies to both modes.

options.label: Weapon Pool
options.description:
Restrict which weapon-type licenses are eligible for the pool
(and for the precollected starter weapon). Defaults to all 14
weapons. To play with a smaller set, list the weapon names you
want — e.g.:

    weapon_pool:
      - Long Sword
      - Bow
      - Switch Axe

Must contain at least one valid weapon name. Empty sets will default
to all weapons. Names are case-sensitive and must match the entries in
`data/weapons.py`. No effect when `include_weapons` is disabled.
Applies to both modes.

options.label: Starting Weapons
options.description:
Restrict which weapon types are eligible to be your starting weapon. One
of the weapons types in this pool will be precollected. Leave the 
option as "Random" to get any weapon from the weapon pool.

Must contain at least one valid weapon name or Random. Empty sets will
default to random selection. Any names not in the weapon pool will be ignored.
No effect when `include_weapons` is disabled. Applies to both modes.

options.label: Randomize Quest Monsters
options.description:
QuestRando only: when enabled (default), every pool quest's
boss monster is randomly swapped (within per-map compatibility).
When disabled, quests keep their vanilla boss — the rando reduces
to gating clear checks on the per-quest `Unlock:` items without
altering the in-game fight. No effect in HuntAThon.

options.label: Excluded Monsters
options.description:
Select any monsters which should be excluded from the pool. Note that
excluding monsters will also reduce the maximum size of the huntathon pool.
If you exclude all monsters in a biome, questrando will use default quest monsters in that biome.
Leave empty to keep the entire monster pool.
You can find a list of monster names as expected by this option in the game's info document.

options.label: Monster Count
options.description:
Number of monsters randomly drawn into the world. Determines how
many hunts are randomized. Clamped to the available pool size at
generation time (max 32 with Sunbreak off, 72 with Sunbreak on).
Min 3 — at N=2 the spare-slot budget is too tight to fit weapon
licenses without overrunning available locations.

options.label: Deathlink
options.description:
Enable or disable deathlink. When enabled,
a faint will count as a death. This setting can be toggled in game.

options.label: Boss Goal
options.description: Select Dungeon from 2-6 to be the goal.

options.label: All Bosses
options.description: Requires defeating every boss up to the goal boss in order to finish the game.

options.label: Required Memory Count
options.description: How many complete pieces of Seda's memory are required for access to the Dark Genie. No effect if boss goal is less than 6.

options.label: Open Dungeon
options.description: Open all dungeon floors as they become logically available.

options.label: Progressive Char Recruitment
options.description:
Makes all character recruitment buildings one progressive item.  Useful for long/large multiworlds.
All Player House pieces will be received, followed by Cacao's House starting at item 8, etc.

options.label: Extra Char Building Pieces
options.description:
Adds an extra of each character recruitment building to the item pool as well as an extra Matataki River
in place of a number of Well parts. What building parts are reflected by the progressive_chars option.
Adds a little extra progression speed to larger multiworlds.

options.label: Better Starting Weapons
options.description: Give each character a Tier 1 weapon in addition to their unbreakable starter.

options.label: Chest Sanity
options.description: Add miracle chests to the item pool.

options.label: Shop Sanity
options.description:
Add 2 items to each shop (excluding Rando).  Gaffer will have 2 items temporarily replaced if the full shop is
unlocked.

options.label: Fish Sanity
options.description:
Catching each fish once is a location.  Adds carrots to Wise Owl Shop inventory for Umadakara.
some_fish is Norune/Matataki/Muska Lacka fish
most_fish adds ocean fish
all_fish includes the Garayan fish as well.  Mardan Garayans require Queens (boss goal 3+) to
purchase poisonous apples and Baron Garayan Muska Lacka (boss goal 4+) for potato cakes.

options.label: Floor Sanity
options.description:
Makes full clearing a floor count as a location.  This requires killing all 15 current enemies without leaving or
going to a back floor.  'all_floors' includes character limited floors.

options.label: Gem Set
options.description: Adds a set of gems to the item pool.  *May require non-atla locations to be enabled to guarantee a full set.*

options.label: Idea
options.description:
It's time for another 'Good Idea, Bad Idea'.  Good Idea: Leave this option alone. Bad Idea: Enable this option.
*Be prepared to release the slot/only use this in MWs where that is accepted. It is not thoroughly tested.*

options.label: ABS Multiplier
options.description: Adjust the ABS gained from enemies.

options.label: Attachment Multiplier
options.description: Adjust the value of attachments. Does not affect attack/speed/magic/endurance received normally in game.

options.label: Attachment Multiplier Config
options.description: Enable attachment multiplier for all attachments, only those from MW, or no attachments.

options.label: Auto Build Buildings
options.description:
Automatically places building pieces as received.
Hundo places buildings for 100% town completion.
Any percent places only buildings with chests clustered similar to how speed runs place them.
Muska only auto builds only Muska Lacka for 100%, robot only the sun giant and muska/robot builds both.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
reach_x_percent: collect the complete_x_percent location, done once
percent_goal % of the other locations are collected.
kill_gobliterator: kill the third phase of the Gobliterator. The
complete_x_percent location is removed from the seed.

Any other value falls back to reach_x_percent.

options.label: Percent Goal
options.description:
Percentage of the other locations that must be done to complete the goal
location (complete_x_percent), which releases the player.
Only used when the goal is reach_x_percent.

options.label: Traps
options.description:
Add monster-spawn trap items to the item pool.

When enabled, traps are filled up to their maximum quantity (in addition to
the single copy seeded by Death Link, if that is also enabled).

options.label: Death Locations
options.description:
Add the death-achievement locations (dying in specific ways: falling,
drowning, fire, projectiles) to the pool.

options.label: Memories
options.description:
Add the memory-collection locations (memories_1 ... memories_150) to the
pool. Use "Maximum Memories" and "Memories Every" to control how many.

options.label: Maximum Memories
options.description:
Highest memory milestone (memories_N) that can become a location.
Only takes effect when Memories is enabled.

options.label: Memories Every
options.description:
Step between included memory milestones. For example a value of 2 includes
memories_1, memories_3, memories_5, ... Only takes effect when Memories is
enabled.

options.label: Regions
options.description:
Add the region-exploration locations (visiting each of the 12 regions) to
the pool.

options.label: Character
options.description:
Determines whether to play as Sora, Riku, or Both
0: Both
1: Sora Only
2: Riku Only

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Win Condition
0: Defeat the Final Boss (Xemnas for Sora and Young Xehanort for Riku
1: Defeat All Superbosses (Secret Portals and Julius)

options.label: Armored Ventus Nightmare
options.description:
If enabled, the win condition for the Final Boss goal is moved to AVN instead of Young Xehanort
This is ignored if the goal is Superbosses or the player chooses Sora as their character

options.label: Recipes Required
options.description:
Number of Recipes needed to beat the game
Meow Wow and Komory Bat recipes are always required

options.label: Recipes in the Item Pool
options.description:
Number of Recipes in the Item Pool
Always includes Meow Wow and Komory Bat recipes

options.label: Starting Worlds
options.description: Number of random worlds to start with

options.label: Superbosses
options.description:
Determines whether Secret Portals and Julius  are checks
This option is ignored if the Goal is Superbosses

options.label: Play Ursula Battle
options.description:
Allows you to play the Ursula battle at the start of the run.
This grants 5 additional checks.
Does nothing if the player chooses Riku as their character.

NOTE: Need to connect to the server before starting a new game
      in order for this to take effect.

options.label: Skip Light Cycle
options.description:
Allows you to skip the Light Cycle section of Riku's Grid.
Skipping will still grant the check for clearing the Light Cycle minigame.
Does nothing if the player chooses Sora as their character.

options.label: Fast Go Mode
options.description:
When enabled, the save point for Young Xehanort is
activated after collecting the necessary key items,
allowing you to do the final fight instantly without
having to play the entirety of The World That Never Was.

Does nothing if the goal is Superbosses or the player
chooses Sora as their character.

options.label: Exp Multiplier
options.description: Determines the multiplier to apply to EXP gained

options.label: Stat Bonus Amount
options.description:
Determines how many points each stat increase grants.
Only applies to Strength, Defense, and Magic increases.

options.label: Strength in Pool
options.description:
Determines how many strength increases per character are in the item pool.
Does nothing if Stats On Levels is enabled.

options.label: Magic in Pool
options.description:
Determines how many magic increases per character are in the item pool.
Does nothing if Stats On Levels is enabled.

options.label: Defense in Pool
options.description:
Determines how many defense increases per character are in the item pool.
Does nothing if Stats On Levels is enabled.

options.label: Randomize Keyblade Stats
options.description: Determines if Keyblade stats should be randomized

options.label: Keyblade Minimum Strength
options.description: Determines the minimum Strength bonus a keyblade can have

options.label: Keyblade Maximum Strength
options.description: Determines the maximum Strength bonus a keyblade can have

options.label: Keyblade Minimum Magic
options.description: Determines the minimum Magic bonus a keyblade can have

options.label: Keyblade Maximum Magic
options.description: Determines the maximum Magic bonus a keyblade can have

options.label: Instant Drop Trap Chance
options.description: Determines the % chance a filler item gets replaced by an instant drop trap.

options.label: Stats On Levels
options.description: Determines whether level checks contain only stat increases.

options.label: Flowmotion is One Item
options.description: If enabled, all flowmotion is obtained as a single item

options.label: Local Item Notifications
options.description:
Determine how received item notifications are handled
0: Display a notification for every received item
1: Display a notification for received progressive items only
2: Do not display received item notifications

options.label: Sent Item Notifications
options.description:
Determine how sent item notifications are handled
0: Display a notification for every sent item
1: Display a notification for sent progressive items only
2: Do not display sent item notifications

options.label: Shuffle Historia Crux
options.description: Allow randomization of the Historia Crux (entrance rando)

options.label: Allow DLC Items
options.description: Allow DLC items in the pool (requires additional DLC Restoration mod)

options.label: Fully Remote Items
options.description: Have Archipelago handle excluded locations instead of filling them locally.

options.label: Allow DLC Locations
options.description: Allow DLC locations to be in scope for Crux randomisation

options.label: Crux fixed start
options.description:
When using Shuffle Historia Crux, whether or not the starting location(s) should
be fixed to be:
- 0: None
- 1: Bodhum 3AF
- 2: Bodhum 3AF -> Bresha 5AF

Note that when Allow DLC Locations is also enabled, the 3 DLC locations will be
randomised and connected to the initial location even if it is fixed here.
This option is recommended if not using enemy/boss randomisation at the point of
converting the AP generated seed data into the rando modpack.

options.label: Win Condition
options.description:
In addition to reaching the end of Academia 500AF, extra conditions can be placed
which will prevent you from accessing the final bosses until they are completed.
- 0: No additional checks
- 1: Fragment Hunt - A minimum number of fragments will be required

options.label: Fragment Hunt Count
options.description:
If the win condition is set to "Fragment Count" this controls how many fragments are required

NOTE: Currently game logic does not take this into account at all, so UT may falsely report
"Go Mode" when you do not have enough fragments. Until more (or at least most) of them are in
the pool this will likely not be resolved. Sorry :)

options.label: Require Final Bosses for victory
options.description:
If disabled, victory will be granted once whatever win condition check is cleared at the end of
Academia 500AF.
If enabled, the final bosses must be defeated to win the seed.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
The goal to win the game.
Bomb Fragments: A MacGuffin item goal. Must recieve all bomb fragments to goal.
networth: Reach a specificed net worth to goal.
missions_: Complete the main story, defeat the cartel to goal
    - 700 Suburbia cartel influence (7 cartel items) is required to defeat the cartel.

options.label: Networth Amount Required
options.description:
The net worth amount required to win the game.
This option is only relevant if the goal includes net worth.

options.label: Number of Bomb Fragments Required
options.description:
The number of bomb fragments required to win the game.
This option is only relevant if the goal includes bomb fragments.
The default value is 5.

options.label: Number of Extra Bomb Fragments
options.description:
The number of extra bomb fragments to include in the item pool.
This option is only relevant if the goal includes bomb fragments.
The default value is 2. Make sure to accomadate for how many required.
Recommended value to have ~25-33% extra fragments.

options.label: Ban Bad Filler Items
options.description: If enabled, bad filler items will not be included in the item pool.

options.label: Ban Progression Skip Filler Items
options.description:
If enabled, filler items that allow for progression skips will not be included in the item pool.
This can add variety to the seed to allow for out of logic skips.

options.label: Trap Chance
options.description: Percentage chance that a filler item will be a trap.

options.label: Number Of Xp Bundles
options.description:
Number of XP bundles to include in the item pool.
min to max xp bundles will be interpolated based on number of bundles.
Meaning there will be 1 min bundle and 1 max bundle and the rest will be evenly distributed in between.
If default min/max are used, 25 bundles give max level xp. 12 gives out about a quarter of that.
16,425 xp is needed to complete the game, but this can be done naturally, bundles speed up process.
If 1 bundle is chosen, only the minimum xp bundle will be in the item pool.

options.label: Amount Of Xp Per Bundle Min
options.description:
Min amount of XP per bundle included in the item pool.
Each bundle is worth the specified amount of XP.
This option is only relevant if NumberOfXpBundles > 0.

options.label: Amount Of Xp Per Bundle Max
options.description:
Max amount of XP per bundle included in the item pool.
Each bundle is worth the specified amount of XP.
This option is only relevant if NumberOfXpBundles > 0.

options.label: Number Of Cash Bundles
options.description:
Number of cash bundles to include in the item pool.
min to max cash bundles will be interpolated based on number of bundles.
Meaning there will be 1 min bundle and 1 max bundle and the rest will be evenly distributed in between.
If 1 bundle is chosen, only the minimum cash bundle will be in the item pool.
Defaults will give out ~87k cash with 20 bundles. 46 bundles gives out ~200k cash.

options.label: Amount Of Cash Per Bundle Min
options.description:
Min amount of cash per bundle included in the item pool.
Each bundle is worth the specified amount of cash.
This option is only relevant if NumberOfCashBundles > 0.

options.label: Amount Of Cash Per Bundle Max
options.description:
Max amount of cash per bundle included in the item pool.
Each bundle is worth the specified amount of cash.
This option is only relevant if NumberOfCashBundles > 0.

options.label: Randomize Level Unlocks
options.description:
Leveling up is always a check regardless of this option.
Block Boss I, 30,350xp, will be the highest checks will go to.
Things you unlock by leveling up will be shuffled into the item pool if this option is enabled.
When this is enabled, you will no longer get level up rewards naturally.

options.label: Randomize Cartel Influence
options.description:
Determines if cartel influence will be randomized into the item pool.
7 Bundles of 100 cartel influence per in-game region that applies.
Every 100 cartel influcence by the player counts as a check regardless of this option.
This option removes the player's ability to earn cartel influence naturally

options.label: Cartel Influence Items Per Region
options.description:
Number of cartel influence Items to include in the item pool per region.
Each item is worth 100 cartel influence.
7 needed to unlock region, recommend to add extra of each region.
Westville has 5 less checks and 5 less cartel influence items
This option is only relevant if Randomize Cartel Influence is enabled.

options.label: Randomize drug making Properties
options.description:
Determines if drug making properties will be added into the item pool.
Purchasing drug making properties become checks, but you do not purchase them.
Realtor will have AP items instead of drug making properties if this is enabled.
This does not include ones you must purchase through missions.

options.label: Randomize business making Properties
options.description:
Determines if business properties will be added into the item pool.
The Realtor will have AP items instead of business properties if this is enabled.

options.label: Randomize Dealers
options.description:
Determines if dealers will be added into the item pool.
Recruiting dealers become checks, but you do not recruit them.
This does not include Benji, who is required for story progression.

options.label: Randomize Customers
options.description:
Determines if customers will be added into the item pool.
Customers are checks regardless if this is toggled on or off
Player can still get successful samples as checks

options.label: Randomize Suppliers
options.description:
Determines if suppliers will be added into the item pool.
If enabled, befriending suppliers no longer become checks.
Albert Hoover is unlocked by default

options.label: Randomize Sewer Key
options.description:
Determines if the Sewer Key will be added into the item pool.
If enabled, Jen Herd will no longer sell sewer key.
Buying the sewer key from Jen Herd is a check no matter if this option is toggled on or off.

options.label: Recipe Checks
options.description:
Number of recipe checks to include in the item pool.
These are recipes per drug type.
10 means 10 weed recipes, 10 meth recipes, etc.

options.label: Cash For Trash
options.description:
Number of checks for each 10 pieces of trash collected
50 = 500 total pieces of trash which is equal to the achiemvement.

options.label: Death Link Options
options.description:
Specify how deathlink will affect you.
traps include: Heat Trap, Slippery Trap, Trash Trap, Pan Trap, TimeScale Trap, Sleep Trap
Death sends players to the hospital (Cash Fee). 
Recommended: Use either random trap or death or both. Sleep trap is okay too. Arrested is especially brutal.
Options:
- sleep trap: Ends day.
- arrested: Player is arrested and loses all illegal items in their inventory.
- random trap: Player will be affected by a random trap.
- death: Player will be sent to the hospital upon death (Cash Fee). The mod does not reset to last save on death.

options.label: Deathlink
options.description:
Whether you want to play with deathlink on
Can always be changed in the client
'Unchanged' means it won't change the setting in the client upon first connection

options.label: Deathlink Amnesty
options.description:
How many deathlinks you need to RECEIVE before you actually die
'Unchanged' (0) means it won't change the setting in the client upon first connection

options.label: Free Disk Vendors
options.description:
Makes all disk vendors free if enabled.
Can always be changed in the client

options.label: Starting Debuffs
options.description: The amount of "Debuff" perks you start with

options.label: Total Buffs
options.description:
The amount of "Progressive Buffs" that will be in the pool
One buff is worth the opposite of a debuff
***WARNING*** If this is set too low for the logic to generate, it will throw an error!

options.label: Starting Trinket Slots
options.description: The amount of trinket slots that you start with

options.label: Total Extra Trinket Slots
options.description: The total amount of progressive trinket slot items that will be in the pool

options.label: Goal Region
options.description: What region you have to reach in order to send the goal

options.label: Include Training Sector
options.description: Adds training sector rooms to the location pool as well as an item check to allow you to enter it

options.label: Include Challenge Modes
options.description:
Makes the individual challenge modes and their medals checks to be completed, 4 per challenge, for 24 total checks
Off: Turns off the challenge modes entirely
Open: Makes all challenges available from the start
Locked: Makes each challenge require a check to be accessible

options.label: Hidden Clamp Total Buffs
options.description: Hidden option specifically for large sync/async creators to prevent gen errors

options.label: Dragun Goal
options.description: Require High Dragun defeat for completion

options.label: Kill The Past Goal
options.description:
Require Past Kills for game completion. 'Standard' is base 4 characters. 'All' adds Robot & Bullet
Mod provides way to use all game characters

options.label: Lich Goal
options.description: Require Lich Goal defeat for completion

options.label: Base Secret Chamber Boss Goal
options.description: Require Blobulord & Old King for completion

options.label: Advanced Gungeon & Draguns Bosses
options.description:
Require bosses from the AG&D Update (Resourceful Rat, Advanced Dragun) for completion.
Do not need to beat Rat at Punch Out

options.label: Farewell To Arms Bosses
options.description:
Require bosses from the Farewell To Arms Update (Cam Clarke AS Agunim) for completion
[Paradox Lich currently WIP]

options.label: Paradox Mode
options.description: Start all runs as Paradox. Other playable characters are Items in randomizer

options.label: Randomize Enemies
options.description: Randomize all basic enemies in the Gungeon.

options.label: Reverse Curse Mode
options.description:
Gain curse at the beginning of every run & add randomizer items to reduce curse.
Standard adds curse after 1 Past is cleared. Hard adds curse immediately

options.label: Gun Pool Items
options.description: Amount of Guns in your item pool

options.label: Passive & Active Pool Items
options.description: Amount of Passive & Active items in your item pool

options.label: Traps
options.description: Amount of Traps in your item pool

options.label: Consumable Items
options.description: Amount of Consumable items in your item pool

options.label: Achievement Locations
options.description: Location checks for accomplishing tasks in Enter the Gungeon

options.label: Ap Item Locations
options.description: Location checks from APItem replacing item in chests, shops, etc.

options.label: Starting Lives
options.description: The number of lives you start with after selecting a level from the title screen.

options.label: Randomize Power Ups?
options.description: Adds power up unlocks into the item pool:

options.label: Randomize Vehicles?
options.description: Adds the vehicles in 2-3 and 4-3 into the item pool

options.label: Bonus Game Checks?
options.description: Adds each end of level bonus game as a location

options.label: Heartsanity
options.description: Adds each 1UP Heart as a location, NOTE: THIS REQUIRES AN EXTRA LUA SCRIPT IN ORDER TO WORK. SEE README FOR MORE INFO

options.label: Early Abilities
options.description:
Determines where the game's early abilities can be placed.

Vanilla: Transforming in the starting room will give you a Progressive Hover and a Progressive Melee Attack.
Local Early: At least one of Melee, Drill, or Saw Blade (to leave the starting room) and one of Wall Jump, Hover,
             or Drill (to make progress in the following room) will be present in the starting room.
Early: The abilities listed in Local Early will be available from the start but may be in another world.
Anywhere: Abilities may be placed in any valid location.

options.label: Goal Condition
options.description:
Choose what you need to do to win.
Defeat Bowser Monsters: Unlock a full team and the day-night cycle, then defeat the Bowser Monsters in a game.
Play Badge: Unlock and win all minigames (including Toy Field).
Friend Badge: Recruit all characters.
Star Badge: Have star status on every character, then defeat the Bowser Monsters in a game.

options.label: Goal Characters
options.description: How many characters you need to have unlocked in order to fight Bowser Jr. and Bowser.

options.label: Starting Captain
options.description: Choose which captain you want to start with.

options.label: Randomize Shops
options.description:
Choose whether shop items are randomized. Logical access to at least one minigame is expected in order to shop.
Full: All shop items are randomized.
Key Items Only: Luigi's Flashlight and the Cruiser Pass are randomized, all other shop items are unchanged.
None: All shop items are in their vanilla locations.

options.label: Randomize Stars
options.description: Adds a check for achieving star status with each character and randomizes the stars into the pool.

options.label: Randomize Error Items
options.description: Start the game with 3 random error items rather than the vanilla Shell, Banana, and Bob-omb.

options.label: Randomize Stats
options.description:
Shuffles stats between different characters. Pitching, batting, fielding, and running stats are shuffled
independently.

options.label: Randomize Puzzles
options.description: Randomizes the lever puzzle in Mario Stadium and the hedge maze in Peach Ice Garden.

options.label: Randomize Quiz
options.description:
Choose which question set(s) to use for Blue Yoshi's quiz.
Valid options are vanilla, sluggers, math, and meme.

options.label: Randomize Music
options.description: Shuffles music between different stadiums, overworld locations, and menus.

options.label: Randomize Text
options.description: Shuffles dialogue throughout the game. Relevant UI/tutorial dialogue is excluded.

options.label: Reduced Cutscenes
options.description: Marks certain one-time cutscenes as already watched to speed up gameplay.

options.label: Progressive Vacuum Tubes
options.description:
Determines whether you get access to main areas progressively.
If enabled, you will receive Whoville, Who Forest, Who Dump, and Who Lake in that order.

options.label: Starting Area
options.description:
Here, you can select which area you'll start the game with.
Whichever one you pick is the region you'll have access to at the start of the Multiworld.
If "progressive_vacuums" is enabled, this is not considered and will always start in Whoville.

options.label: Mission Locations
options.description: Adds individual tasks of a particular mission as locations.

options.label: Environments Excluded
options.description:
Allows entire environments to be entirely removed to ensure you are not
logically required to enter the environment along with any and all checks
that are in that environment too.

Valid keys: "Post Office", "Clock Tower", "City Hall", "Ski Resort",
"Civic Center", "Minefield", "Power Plant", "Generator Building",
"Scout's Hut", "North Shore", "Mayor's Villa", "Submarine World"

options.label: Giftsanity
options.description:
Determines if individual gifts are checks
NOTE: This currently only disables the missions relating to squashing all
gifts for an entire region.

options.label: Supadow Minigames
options.description:
Enables completing minigames through the Supadows in Mount Crumpit as checks.
NOTE: Each difficulty will need to be played separately.
These are not mixed with other difficulties for how locations get checked

options.label: Killsanity
options.description:
Determines whether you consider killing/destroying certain enemies
throughout the games are checks.

"Whos" are considereed as people such as guards, children, and other
humanoid related figures.
"Animals" are considered as non-human species such as Summer beasts,
porcupines, moose, and mosquitoes.
"Robots" are considered mechanical beings that electrocute the player,
specifically the robots you find in Who Dump.

options.label: Progressive Gadgets
options.description: Determines whether you get access to a gadget as the individual blueprint count.

options.label: Randomize Gadgets
options.description:
Determines whether the Grinch's gadgets will be randomized or not.
Disabling this will give you every gadget at the start from gadgets_to_randomize.

options.label: Gadgets Randomized
options.description:
If "gadget_rando" is enabled, gadgets that you add to the dictionary will
be randomized.

options.label: Remove Grinch Copter
options.description:
Tired of getting Grinch Copter? This option ensures Grinch Copter is
entirely taken out from the multiworld.
Note that locations that hard require Grinch Copter will also be removed.

options.label: Randomize Moves
options.description:
Determines whether the Grinch's moves will be randomized or not.
Disabling this will give you every gadget at the start from moves_to_randomize.

options.label: Moves Randomized
options.description: If "move_rando" is enabled, the Grinch's moves that you add to the dictionary will be randomized.

options.label: Unlimited Rotten Eggs
options.description:
Determine if you run out of rotten eggs when you utilize your gadgets.
This will also give 1 nitro egg/thistle per 0.5 seconds if in their respective regions.
NOTE: Attempting to enable this with ringlink will force generation to stop
until either option is disabled.

options.label: Trap Percentage
options.description: Determines how much filler is replaced with traps.

options.label: Ring Link
options.description:
Whenever this is toggled, your ammo is linked with other ringlink-compatible
games that also have this enabled.
Due to instability, ringlink will not give you eggs if you are in either the
Sleigh Ride or any of the minigames in Mount Crumpit.
NOTE: Attempting to enable this with unlimited_eggs will force generation
to stop until either option is enabled.

options.label: Trap Link
options.description:
If a trap is sent from Grinch, traps that are compatible with other games
are triggered as well.

options.label: Advanced Logic
options.description:
Enables logic to allow skips, damage boosts, glitches, game restarts,
excessive egg usage, and various other unintentional ways that beginners
wouldn't grasp on their first playthrough if this is enabled to be considered
logical.

options.label: Miscellaneous Locations
options.description:
Adds locations that aren't specifically categorized and are either random
events or just unnecessarily added locations that don't mean anything.

options.label: Damage Rate
options.description:
How much damage can the Grinch tolerate before death
0 = Invincible
1 = Base game damage rate
78 = Instant death without any Hearts of Stone
88 = Instant death with one Heart of Stone
99 = Instant death with two Hearts of Stone
110 = Instant death with three Hearts of Stone
120 = Instant death

options.label: Goal
options.description:
sleigh_ride: Sleigh parts are placed in their local areas that you must
physically collect them to goal.
missions_completed: You must complete a certain number of missions to
goal.
macguffin_hunt: Same as sleigh_ride, except you must allow the Grinch's
heart to grow just enough to access the Sleigh Room.
supadows_completed: You are required to win every supadow minigame to
goal and obtain access to their minigames to do so.
squashing_all_gifts: You must squash every gift in the entire game to goal.
slaughter: You must kill every Who, every animal, and every robot to goal.

options.label: Mission Goal Count
options.description:
If your goal is missions_completed, set how many missions you want to
complete to goal. If your goal is missions_completed_with_gifts, this option
will be ignored.

options.label: Include Gift Squashing in Missions Completed Goal
options.description:
If your goal is missions_completed, include the squashing all gift missions.
Otherwise, if your goal is not missions_completed, this will do nothing.

options.label: Music Rando
options.description: Randomizes all music in the game

options.label: Reduced Cutscenes
options.description: Certain cutscenes no longer trigger if enabled for a faster experience

options.label: Randomize Mission Specific Items
options.description:
Allows mission specific items to be randomized in the itempool.
NOTE: Excluding Submarine World from `exclude_environments` will still require
you to enter the region to collect the Twin-End Tuba.
NOTE: Disabling this adds the locations and will not add their items to the
item pool. Enabling this removes these locations and adds the items.

options.label: Randomize Sleigh Parts
options.description:
Allows the sleigh parts to be randomized in the itempool.
NOTE: Disabling this adds the locations and will not add their items to the
item pool. Enabling this removes these locations and adds the items.

options.label: Teleport Multibind
options.description:
Enables functionality to directly teleport back to Mount Crumpit on command.
To teleport, you must be in the notebook and hold start followed by L1 + R1

options.label: Death Link Option
options.description:
When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.
NOTE: Due to instability, you will not be able to send or receive deaths if you are in the following areas:

Mount Crumpit, Sleigh Ride, any minigame in Mount Crumpit, Clock Tower, City Hall, and Post Office

options.label: Heart Size Increase Requirement
options.description:
If your goal is macguffin_hunt, set how many Heart Size Increase items you
want to allow access to the Sleigh Room.

options.label: Send Lower Medals
options.description:
When you recieve a medal whether to send lower medals
EX. Recieving Gold sends: Gold, Silver, Bronze

options.label: Use Bronze Medals
options.description:
Whether to use Bronze Medals as possible locations
The more medals you select the more filler/trap is included

options.label: Use Silver Medals
options.description:
Whether to use Silver Medals as possible locations
The more medals you select the more filler/trap is included

options.label: Use Gold Medals
options.description:
Whether to use Gold Medals as possible locations
The more medals you select the more filler/trap is included

options.label: Use Platinum Medals
options.description:
Whether to use Platinum Medals as possible locations
The more medals you select the more filler/trap is included

options.label: Use Developer Medals
options.description:
Whether to use Developer Medals as possible locations
The more medals you select the more filler/trap is included

options.label: Minimum Medal types
options.description:
The minimum amount of medals types to be included
Will never generate with less medals per level than this
The more medals you select the more filler/trap is included
Below 3 it may not be possible to not gen due to lack of locations for items

options.label: Death Link Amnesty
options.description:
Amount of deaths required from you to send out a Death Link to other Players
0  = Only receive Death Links does not send any when you die
1+ = Send a Death Link when you die this amount of times

options.label: Trap Percent
options.description:
Percentage of filler items that are traps
Any items that are not traps(includes traps&anti-traps) are empty items that do nothing

options.label: Clumsy Trap Weight
options.description:
Weight of be Clumsy Trap
Clumsy trap triggers ragdoll every 3 seconds up to 5 times

options.label: Stop Hitting Yourself Trap Weight
options.description:
Weight of Stop Hitting Yourself Trap
Stop Hitting Yourself Trap activates "Brainrot" for 10 seconds

options.label: FIREEE! Trap Weight
options.description:
Weight of FIREEE! Trap
FIREEE! Trap sets you on fire

options.label: FIREEE* Trap Weight
options.description:
Weight of FIREEE* Trap
FIREEE* Trap sets you on fire and extinguishes before death

options.label: Slippery Hands Trap Weight
options.description:
Weight of Slippery Hands Trap
Slippery Hands Trap drops held item

options.label: Whats Under There? Trap Weight
options.description:
Weight of Whats Under There? Trap
Whats Under There? Trap teleports you 5 frames every 0.25 seconds for up to 25 times

options.label: Caught You! Trap Weight
options.description:
Weight of Caught You! Trap
Caught You! Trap puts you in a net

options.label: Duck Season Trap Weight
options.description:
Weight of Duck Season Trap
Duck Season Trap replaces your weapon with the suicide gun

options.label: Hot Potato Trap Weight
options.description:
Weight of Hot Potato Trap
Hot Potato Trap gives you an active grenade

options.label: Whats This? Trap Weight
options.description:
Weight of Whats This? Trap
Whats This? Trap gives you a random weapon/item

options.label: esreveR Trap Weight
options.description:
Weight of esreveR Trap
esreveR Trap reverses your left and right inputs for 10 seconds

options.label: A Gift for you Trap Weight
options.description:
Weight of A Gift for you Trap
A Gift for you Trap is BAD(mostly)/spawns a random Death Crate

options.label: Don't look up Trap Weight
options.description:
Weight of Don't look up Trap
Don't look up Trap spawns a bunch of active grenades on the screen, Look out!

options.label: Prot V Anti-Trap Weight
options.description:
Weight of Prot V Anti-Trap
Prot V Anti-Trap gives you armour

options.label: Make it rain Anti-Trap Weight
options.description:
Weight of Make it rain Anti-Trap
Make it rain Anti-Trap gives you infinite ammo for the weapon you are holding

options.label: Goal
options.description:
The goal you need to reach to beat the randomizer for this world.

Normal Ending: Get the required note percent defined in the other options
    and enter A World Without Gnosia, ending the loop there.
Role Achievements: Get all role-related achievements (Including "Hero")
    Achievements can be excluded by putting them in Excluded Achievements or Excluded Locations.
    You can add role achievements as locations as well, but it's not necessary for this goal to work.

options.label: Required Note Percent
options.description:
The % of Note Items you'll need in order to see the Normal Ending.
Min: 0%, Max: 100%, Default: 80%, Vanilla Game: 100%

options.label: Excluded Achievements
options.description:
Achievements that are put in this list won't be needed for the Role Achievements Goal

Does nothing if the goal is not Role Achievements

options.label: Randomize Character Unlocks
options.description:
Characters will no longer appear outside of tutorial loops unless unlocked.
You will start with at least 4 random ones.
(This option replaces progressive crew max items with specific character unlocks)

options.label: Starting Crew Count
options.description:
The maximum number of characters, including the player, per loop
before any item is received to increase this.
Min: 5, Max: 15

options.label: Priority Starting Characters
options.description:
When picking starting characters, characters from this list will be prioritized

Does nothing if character unlocks are not randomized
or if characters in Start Inventory From Pool already fill the crew count

options.label: Randomize Role Unlocks
options.description:
Roles will need to be found as items before being included in a loop
Also adds 8 locations, one for each time a role is explained during tutorials
or otherwise unlocked (in the case of the Bug Role)

options.label: Randomize Notes
options.description:
Notes will be shuffled into the item pool
This also adds 82 Locations (one for each note)

options.label: Randomize Skills
options.description:
Skills will be shuffled into the item pool
This also adds 17 Locations (one for each skill)

Definite Human and Definite Enemy count as a single skill

options.label: Add Role Achievement Locations
options.description:
Adds a location for each role-related achievement (Plus the Hero Achievement)

Adds 6 locations in total

options.label: Add Win With Character Locations
options.description:
Adds a location for the first time you win with each character
(They must be on the same team you're on)

Adds 14 locations in total

options.label: Add Win Against Character Locations
options.description:
Adds a location for the first time you win against each character
(They must be on any team except the team you're on)

Adds 14 locations in total

options.label: Add Win As Role Locations
options.description:
Adds a location for the first time you win as each role

Adds 8 locations in total

options.label: Add Win Against Role Locations
options.description:
Adds a location for the first time you win against each role
(They must be on any team except the team you're on)

Adds 8 locations in total

options.label: Tutorial Handling
options.description:
How to handle tutorial loops:

Vanilla: Tutorials are not skipped at all.
Skip: The game will start on loop 14, and you will receive all tutorial
    loop locations immediately. The Bug-related Tutorial loops will also be skipped
Skip And Remove Locations: Same as Skip but without receiving any locations.
    Requires adding at least 14 Locations from "Extra Locations"
    Plus an additional 14 locations if randomizing notes
    Plus an additional 8 locations if randomizing roles
    These requirements can be lowered by having a higher starting crew count
    or by using any feature that removes items from the pool (such as Start Inventory From Pool)

options.label: Exp Multiplier
options.description: When ending a loop, the experience gained will be multiplied by this number

options.label: Allow Gender-Specific Logic
options.description:
By default, logic will assume you could have chosen any of the game's three gender options.
As such, events will only be in logic if *all* genders can access the event with the current items.

By activating this option, a patch will be applied to the game that allows you to instead
change the main character's gender mid-game (by talking to Yuriko as the Bug at night)

This allows any gender-specific event or logical path to be accessed in any save file
and logic will account for that (so you may be required to make use of this feature if you enable it)

options.label: Goal
options.description:
How you complete the randomizer. 
Collecting enough of the "Medal" item will unlock a victory map (marked by the archipelago logo)

Default: Beat the victory map on the highest available difficulty in the pool.
Boss: Defeat a random Boss Bloon event on the victory map.
Elite Boss: Defeat a random Elite Boss Bloon event on the victory map. 
            Note: Boss Events are guaranteed to take place on Beginner or Intermediate maps.

options.label: Total Medals
options.description:
The total number of Medal items placed in the item pool.
These are the collectables required to unlock the goal map.

options.label: Medal Requirement Percentage
options.description:
The Percentage of the Total Medals required for you to access the Goal Map

For my own sanity and the randomizers this is hard bottomed at 50% so it can't be cheesed

options.label: Mode Pool
options.description:
Which difficulty/mode checks are eligible to be assigned to maps.
Each included map will randomly draw `modes_per_map` modes from this pool.

Available modes: Easy, Medium, Hard, Impoppable, Chimps,
PrimaryOnly, MilitaryOnly, MagicOnly,
Deflation, Apopalypse, Reverse, DoubleMoabHealth, HalfCash, AlternateBloonsRounds

Note: Completing milestone rounds on higher difficulties will still send checks for
lower difficulties assigned to that map (e.g. round 60 on Impoppable sends Medium
if Medium is in that map's pool).

options.label: Modes Per Map
options.description:
How many modes from the Mode Pool are randomly assigned as checks for each map.
If this exceeds the pool size, it is capped at the pool size and every mode in the pool will be on every map.

options.label: Random Mode Amount Per Map
options.description:
When enabled, each map receives a random number of modes between 1 and Modes Per Map
(capped at the pool size). Every map may have a different count.

options.label: Total Map Count
options.description: The number of maps to be included (not including starting maps).

options.label: Starting Map Count
options.description: The number of maps that will be automatically unlocked at the start.

options.label: Minimum Map Difficulty
options.description:
The Minimum Map Difficulty for selected maps (including starting and goal map)

0 = Beginner
1 = Intermediate
2 = Advanced
3 = Expert

Must be less than or equal to Maximum Map Difficulty.

options.label: Maximum Map Difficulty
options.description:
The Maximum Map Difficulty for selected maps (including starting and goal map)

0 = Beginner
1 = Intermediate
2 = Advanced
3 = Expert

Must be greater than or equal to Minimum Map Difficulty.

options.label: Map Blacklist
options.description:
Maps to never include in this randomizer, entered by display name.
Example: ["Monkey Meadow", "#ouch", "Bloonarius Prime"]
If a map appears in both the blacklist and whitelist, the blacklist wins.

options.label: Map Whitelist
options.description:
Maps that are guaranteed to be included in the pool (starting maps or unlockable maps),
as long as they fall within the selected difficulty range and are not blacklisted.
Other maps outside this list can still fill remaining slots. Entered by display name.
Example: ["Monkey Meadow", "Bloonarius Prime", "Infernal"]

options.label: Category Lock
options.description:
False/Off: Monkeys are unlocked individually as normal.
True/On:  Monkeys are unlocked by category (Primary, Military, Magic, Support).
          You start with one random category and the other three are sent as items.
          When enabled, starting monkeys are always randomized (ignores Random Starting Monkeys option).

options.label: Starting Monkey Amount
options.description:
The number of starting Monkeys you would like.
Only relevant if Category Lock is disabled.

options.label: Starting Monkeys
options.description:
Choose specific starting monkeys by entering their display name, e.g. ["Heli Pilot"].
Only relevant if Category Lock is disabled.

Empty: All starting monkeys are randomized.
Non-empty: Every monkey listed is guaranteed as a starting monkey. If you list fewer
           monkeys than Starting Monkey Amount, the remaining slots are filled randomly.
           If you list more monkeys than Starting Monkey Amount, all of them are still included.

options.label: XP Curve Behaviour
options.description:
The scaling of the XP requirements for Level Up checks.

False/Static: A Configurable Amount of XP is Required to Level Up EACH time.
True/Curved: Uses the default XP Curve from BTD6

options.label: Static XP Requirement
options.description:
Only relevant if "XP Curve Behaviour" is set to false.

Min Req. 500 XP
Max Req. 10,000 XP

options.label: Maximum Level
options.description:
What do you want to be the maximum level of the randomizer?

Levels start at 0, if at 0 they are disabled.

options.label: Knowledge Mode
options.description:
How Monkey Knowledge is handled.

Unlock Checks: Each Monkey Knowledge node is its own item. Once received, click it in the
               Knowledge Tree to send a check. {Adds 134 checks}
Automatic:     Each Monkey Knowledge node is its own item but you don't have to activate them
               in the tree's and have no checks for activating them.
Progressive:   The 134 knowledge items are replaced with 7 "Progressive Knowledge" items.
               Each one activates the next full layer of the Knowledge Tree across all
               branches.

options.label: Progressive Prices
options.description:
False/Off: Tower and upgrade costs behave normally based on the selected difficulty.
True/On:  All tower and upgrade costs start at Impoppable pricing (1.20x).
          Receiving "Progressive Prices" items progressively decreases costs across all difficulties:
          Impoppable (1.20x) -> Hard (1.08x) -> Medium (1.00x) -> Easy (0.85x)

options.label: Progressive Starting Cash
options.description:
The number of "Progressive Starting Cash" items placed in the item pool.
Every game starts with its normal starting cash (650 in most modes),
and each Progressive Starting Cash you receive adds another 150 to it.

options.label: Pop Tier Checks
options.description:
False/Off: Monkey upgrade tiers are not locked behind pop counts.
True/On:  Tier 3, 4, and 5 upgrades for each monkey are locked until that monkey
          has accumulated enough pops. Hitting each threshold sends a check.
          {Adds 72 checks}

options.label: Tier 3 Pop Requirement
options.description:
Number of pops in a single game required with a monkey type to unlock its Tier 3 upgrades and send a check.
Only relevant if Pop Tier Checks is enabled.

options.label: Tier 4 Pop Requirement
options.description:
Number of pops in a single game required with a monkey type to unlock its Tier 4 upgrades and send a check.
Only relevant if Pop Tier Checks is enabled.

options.label: Tier 5 Pop Requirement
options.description:
Number of pops in a single game required with a monkey type to unlock its Tier 5 upgrades and send a check.
Only relevant Pop Tier Checks is enabled.

options.label: Upgrade Sanity
options.description:
False/Off: Monkey upgrade paths are freely available as normal.
True/On:  Each monkey's three upgrade paths (Top, Middle, Bottom) become items
          in the multiworld pool. Receiving e.g. "DartMonkey-MiddlePath" unlocks
          Dart Monkey's tier 4 and 5 upgrades on the middle path.
          Tiers 1-3 remain freely purchasable on all paths.
          {Adds 78 items to the pool}

options.label: Round Sanity
options.description:
Adds location checks for completing rounds on any map.
Set to 0 to disable. Otherwise, a check is sent every N rounds up to round 100.

Examples:
5 = checks at rounds 5, 10, 15, 20, ..., 100 (20 checks per map)
20 = checks at rounds 20, 40, 60, 80, 100 (5 checks per map)
60 = check at round 60 only (1 check per map)

options.label: Custom Round Checks
options.description:
Specify exact rounds to send checks on, if Round Sanity overlaps it counts as 1 check.
Enter round numbers between 1 and 100.
Example: ['98', '95', '93', '78']
If Round Sanity is also set, both sets of checks are included.

options.label: Trap Percentage
options.description: Replace a percentage of filler items in the item pool with random traps.

options.label: Trap Link
options.description:
Whether your received traps are linked to other players

You will also receive any linked traps from other players with Trap Link enabled,
if you have a weight above "0" set for that trap.

options.label: Included Campaigns
options.description: Controls which campaigns will be included in the output world.

options.label: Victory Cache
options.description: Adds additional locations received on mission victory.

options.label: Bonus Mercenary Camps
options.description: Adds mercenary camps to build missions that did not have them in vanilla.

options.label: Mercenary Allocation
options.description:
Specifies what mercenaries can be hired in what missions.
vanilla:      Mercenary camps have their vanilla rosters.
              Non-vanilla camps will have 3-4 fixed tileset-appropriate mercs.
vanilla_plus: Random additional mercs are added to the mercenary camp pools
              in addition to vanilla/tileset rosters.
species:      Mercenary camps will supply mercenaries from 2~3 randomly-selected species.
full_random:  Mercenary camps will supply a random collection of mercenaries.

options.label: Mercenaries Per Camp
options.description:
Specifies the maximum number of mercenaries a single camp can offer.
Will not eliminate fixed/vanilla mercs specified by `vanilla` or `vanilla_plus` allocations.

options.label: Catnip-sanity
options.description: All Catnip Crystals are added to the item pool

options.label: Merge Rando
options.description: Limits merging to items whose recipes are found. The Inventor's recipes become locations.

options.label: DLC: Rise of the Giant
options.description:
Include content from Rise of the Giant DLC.
Adds biomes: Cavern, Giant, Astrolab, Observatory.
Adds items: GiantKiller, SonicCrossbow, BleedAxe, GodAxe,
            ThrowingSpear, MagicSalve, ThunderShield, and more.
Required to access 5BC route via Astrolab.

options.label: DLC: The Bad Seed
options.description:
Include content from The Bad Seed DLC.
Adds biomes: Greenhouse, Swamp, SwampHeart.
Adds items: SmokeBomb, ParryBlade, RhythmicBlade, Blowgun, and more.

options.label: DLC: Fatal Falls
options.description:
Include content from Fatal Falls DLC.
Adds biomes: Tumulus, Cliff, GardenerStage.
Adds items: SnakeFang, GiantStaff, Lantern, LightningRod, and more.

options.label: DLC: The Queen and the Sea
options.description:
Include content from The Queen and the Sea DLC.
Adds biomes: Shipwreck, Lighthouse, QueenArena.
Adds items: Trident, HandHook, Shark, ElbowBlades, ThrowingCards, and more.

options.label: DLC: Return to Castlevania
options.description:
Include content from Return to Castlevania DLC.
Adds biomes: PurpleGarden, DookuCastle, DookuCastleHard, DeathArena, DookuArena.
Adds items: VampireKiller, AdeleScythe, Bible, Cross, BouncingStone, and more.

options.label: Boss Cells Goal
options.description:
The Boss Cell difficulty required to complete the goal.
The player must defeat the Hand of the King (or reach the End region)
at this difficulty level or higher.

0 = No Boss Cells (easiest)
5 = 5 Boss Cells (hardest, requires Rise of the Giant DLC for Astrolab route)

Note: Setting this to 5 without enabling Rise of the Giant DLC will
restrict the 5BC Astrolab route, so the Throne -> End path will be used.

options.label: Trap Percentage
options.description:
Percentage of filler item slots that will be replaced by trap items.
Traps are sent to the Dead Cells player and trigger negative in-game effects
such as curses, elite spawns, gold loss, or inverted controls.

0  = No traps
25 = 25% of fillers are traps (recommended)
100 = All filler slots are traps (very punishing)

options.label: Include Cosmetics in Pool
options.description:
Include cosmetic items (skins and head accessories) in the item pool.
When enabled, skins and head items are added as filler items that can
appear in other players' worlds.
When disabled, only gameplay-relevant items are in the pool, and
extra filler slots are filled with consumables and gems.

Noteably, disabling this will also disable the "Giant Comb" and 
"Sewing Scissors" locations as they depend on cosmetic checks sent, but 
they will still be in the item pool

options.label: Include Aspects in Pool
options.description:
Include the 13 Aspects as locations and items in the pool. 
When enabled, your first 13 deaths will send an AP Item. 
When disabled, you will start with all Aspects as items, and no 
locations will exist for unlocking them.

options.label: Include Starting Weapons in Pool
options.description:
Include base-game weapons that are available from the start
without any blueprint (e.g. Quick Sword, Broad Sword, Dual Daggers).
When disabled, these items are removed from the pool, making the
randomizer more focused on blueprint unlocks.
When enabled, they are added as useful filler items.

options.label: Include Starting Mutations in Pool
options.description:
Include base-game mutations that are available from the start
without any blueprint (e.g. Combo, Support, Necromancy).
When disabled, these items are removed from the pool, making the
randomizer more focused on blueprint unlocks.
When enabled, they are added as useful filler items.

options.label: Death/Curses Link
options.description:
When enabled, dying in Dead Cells sends a death signal to all other
players with Death Link enabled in the multiworld session.
Receiving a death signal will kill your current run when set to 0.
With a positive value, give you that amount in curses instead of killing your run
Negative values disable this option.

options.label: Disable Death Link for Aspects
options.description:
At the start of your game you have 13 aspects to find, and you'll have to die
a lot on purpose. That's a little incompatible with Death Link, so with this
option enabled you won't send Death Link while you still have aspects to check.

options.label: Death Trap
options.description:
Override Death/Curses Link. When enabled, it will send a death link upon death
and will give you a random trap upon receiving a death link.

options.label: Death Trap Link Trigger
options.description:
Sub-option for Death Trap. When enabled, it will send a trap link upon
receiving a death trap.

options.label: Damage Link
options.description:
When enabled, taking damage in Dead Cells sends damage points to all
other players with Damage Link enabled in the multiworld session.
The rate is 16 damage points for 1% health.

options.label: Health Link
options.description:
When enabled, life is shared between all other Dead Cells players with Health
Link enabled in the multiworld session. Taking damage, healing, and recovery are
shared based on percentage. Dying will kill other players.

options.label: Health Curse Link
options.description: Sub-option for Health Link. When enabled, curses too are shared between players.

options.label: Trap Link
options.description:
When enabled, traps are shared with all other Dead Cells players who have Trap
Link enabled in the multiworld session. The same kind of trap is sent to every
other player upon receiving one.

options.label: Respawn Stat Up Scroll
options.description: At the start of each run, every filler stat up scroll will be given again.

options.label: Flawless Boss Scroll
options.description:
Gives you Epic Scrolls of Power the first time you beat a boss without taking
a hit. It's best to use it with the Respawn Stat Up Scroll option enabled.

options.label: Starting Power Item Preset
options.description:
Determines which Power Items are added to the starting inventory.
For fully custom starting Powers, set this to 'None' and use the StartInventoryPool option instead

Full: Start with all Power Items, including Double Dash.
None: Start with no Power Items.
Vanilla: Start with one Thunderbolt and one Dash (default).
Thunderbolt: Start with one Thunderbolt.
Dash: Start with one Dash.
IronTail: Start with one Iron Tail.
Randomize: Start with a random number of each Power Item, including Double Dash.

options.label: Starting Fast Travel Items
options.description:
Determines how many Fast Travel Items are added to the starting inventory.

None: Start with no Fast Travel Items (default).
One: Start with one random Fast Travel Item.
All: Start with all Fast Travel Items.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Determines the goal required to complete the world.

Mew: Complete Mew's Power Competition (default).
Postgame: Complete the postgame Prisma completion, which requires all Friendships.

options.label: Required Battle Win Streak
options.description:
Determines the number of required consecutive Wins to challenge Battle count Pokemon e.g. Scyther

Set this to 0 to remove the consecutive Battle requirement.

options.label: Separate Pokemon Locations by Zone
options.description:
Pokemon that appear in multiple Zones become separate Locations for each Zone.

For example, Bonsly in the Meadow, Cavern, and Magma Zones becomes three separate Locations instead of one shared
Location.

options.label: Remove Battle Power Competition Locations
options.description:
Removes Battle Power Competition Locations. Battles can still be played to gain Berries but will no longer send
Location Checks.

WARNING: Removing too many Location types may leave too few Locations for the required progression Items.

options.label: Remove Chase Power Competition Locations
options.description:
Removes Chase Power Competition Locations. Chases can still be played to gain Berries but will no longer send
Location Checks.

WARNING: Removing too many Location types may leave too few Locations for the required progression Items.

options.label: Remove Quiz Power Competition Locations
options.description:
Removes Quiz Power Competition Locations. Quizzes can still be played to gain Berries but will no longer send
Location Checks.

WARNING: Removing too many Location types may leave too few Locations for the required progression Items.

options.label: Remove Hide-and-Seek Power Competition Locations
options.description:
Removes Hide and Seek Power Competition Locations. Hide and Seek can still be played to gain Berries but will no
longer send Location Checks.

WARNING: Removing too many Location types may leave too few Locations for the required progression Items.

options.label: Remove Errand Locations
options.description:
Removes Errand Locations. Errands can still be completed to gain Berries but will no longer send Location Checks.

WARNING: Removing too many Location types may leave too few Locations for the required progression Items.

options.label: Remove Miscellaneous Friendship Locations
options.description:
Removes miscellaneous Friendship Locations that do not belong to another Power Competition category. These
activities can still be completed to gain Berries but will no longer send Location Checks.

WARNING: Removing too many Location types may leave too few Locations for the required progression Items.

options.label: Remove Legendary Pokemon Locations
options.description:
Removes Legendary Pokemon Power Competition Locations, such as Celebi. These competitions can still be played to
gain Berries but will no longer send Location Checks.

WARNING: Removing too many Location types may leave too few Locations for the required progression Items.

options.label: Remove Power Training Locations
options.description:
Removes Power Training Locations, such as Thunderbolt Training with Electabuzz.

WARNING: Removing too many Location types may leave too few Locations for the required progression Items.

options.label: Remove Attraction Record Locations
options.description:
Removes the individual Pokemon Record Locations from Attractions. Attractions can still be played to gain Berries,
and their Prisma Locations are not removed by this option.

WARNING: Removing too many Location types may leave too few Locations for the required progression Items.

options.label: Remove Attraction Prisma Locations
options.description:
Removes the Prisma Location from each Attraction. Attractions can still be played to gain Berries, and their
individual Pokemon Record Locations are not removed by this option.

WARNING: Removing too many Location types may leave too few Locations for the required progression Items.

options.label: Remove Pokemon Unlock Locations
options.description:
Removes Locations for unlocking Pokemon in the overworld, such as Caterpie's Tree and Shroomish's Crate.

WARNING: Removing too many Location types may leave too few Locations for the required progression Items.

options.label: Skygarden Prisma Requirement
options.description: Determines how many Prisma Shards are required to travel to Skygarden with Piplup in the Treehouse.

options.label: In-Zone Roadblock Items
options.description:
Adds Roadblock Items for obstacles inside the Zones, such as the Beach Zone Bridges.

When disabled, all affected Roadblock Items are added to the starting inventory.

options.label: Randomize Attraction Entrances
options.description: Randomizes Attraction Entrances among themselves. Entering an Attraction may lead to a different Attraction.

options.label: Randomize Fast Travel Routes
options.description:
Randomizes Drifblim Fast Travel Entrances among themselves.

Each Fast Travel route is randomized separately based on its starting Zone and selected destination. For example,
traveling from the Meadow Zone to the Beach Zone may lead somewhere different than traveling from the Cavern Zone
to the Beach Zone.

Enabling this option automatically disables unlocking Fast Travel through Taxi Stops.

options.label: Randomize Treehouse Gates
options.description: Randomizes the Zone Gates in the Treehouse among themselves. Entering a Gate may lead to a different Zone.

options.label: Randomize General Entrances
options.description:
Randomizes general overworld Entrances, such as the connection between the Meadow Zone Main Area and the Venusaur
Area.

options.label: Mix Entrance Randomization Pools
options.description:
Combines all enabled Treehouse Gate, Fast Travel, and General Entrance pools into one randomized pool. Attraction
Entrances remain in their own pool.

options.label: Harder Power Competition AI
options.description:
Pokemon always use their harder AI during Power Competitions. Logic requirements are increased to account for the
additional difficulty, but individual matchups may still be harder depending on player skill and know-how.

options.label: Unlock Fast Travel at Taxi Stops
options.description:
Unlocks Fast Travel to reachable Zones when interacting with the Taxi Stops beside Drifblim.

This option is automatically disabled when Fast Travel Entrances are randomized.

options.label: Death Link
options.description:
Sends a DeathLink when losing a Power Competition. Depending on the game version, the Power Competition's
location, and other circumstances, some losses may not send a DeathLink right now.

DeathLinks from other players can be received anywhere in the game. More information can be found in the
documentation.

options.label: Show Client Messages In-Game
options.description: Displays Archipelago Client messages inside the game. This can also be toggled from the PokePark Client.

options.label: 60 FPS Patch
options.description: Unlocks the frame rate up to 60 FPS.

options.label: Starting Parts

options.label: Chapter Order

options.label: Remove Shop Maps

options.label: Include Achievements
options.description: Include Archipelago locations for in-game achievements.

options.label: Include Minigames
options.description: Include Archipelago locations for completing minigames (Stickers, Cleaning, Tickets, Phone).

options.label: Stickers Per Check
options.description: How many stickers you need to peel off to send an Archipelago check.

options.label: Cleaning Per Check
options.description: How many items you need to clean to send an Archipelago check.

options.label: Tickets Per Check
options.description: How many flight tickets you need to process to send an Archipelago check.

options.label: Phone Calls Per Check
options.description: How many phone calls you need to make to send an Archipelago check.

options.label: Total Item Checks
options.description: The total number of generic Archipelago checks available for returning items.

options.label: Target Debt

options.label: Enable Traps

options.label: Trap Percentage

options.label: Trap Rotation Amount

options.label: Filler Money Amount

options.label: Tea Filler Chance
