Determines if Hell Rock locations and items should be enabled, even if it's not the objective.
Does not include the final location.

options.label: Green Cabinet Items and Locations Enabled

Determines if Green Cabinet locations and items should be enabled, even if it's not the objective.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
The goal required to complete the run in Archipelago.
clear_game: Clear the game as intended by dunking in Terminus.
clear_game_with_fizzies: Same as the previous, but you cannot dunk until you have a minimum amount of Fizzy Ice Creams.
all_checkpoints: Activate every checkpoint to clear the game.

options.label: Fizziesforgoal

The number of Fizzy Ice Cream items needed to complete the Goal state when the option "option_clear_game_with_fizzies"
is enabled. Range between 0 and 20.

options.label: Character Goals
options.description:
Should Goals be tied to specific characters?
any: Any character can beat any goal
single: Each goal can only be beaten by a single character, which is randomly assigned when generating the game.
grouped: Each goal can only be beaten by a group of characters, which is randomly assigned when generating the game. The group size is determined by the Goal Amount.

options.description:
If character_goals is set to single or grouped, you can exclude certain characters from being assigned to goals here.
Valid characters are: ["Isaac", "Magdalene", "Cain", "Judas", "???", "Eve", "Samson", "Azazel", "Lazarus", "Eden", "The Lost",
                       "Lilith", "Keeper", "Apollyon", "The Forgotten", "Bethany", "Jacob & Esau", "Tainted Isaac", 
                       "Tainted Magdalene", "Tainted Cain", "Tainted Judas", "Tainted ???", "Tainted Eve", "Tainted Samson", 
                       "Tainted Azazel", "Tainted Lazarus", "Tainted Eden", "Tainted Lost", "Tainted Lilith", "Tainted Keeper",

Entire areas to exclude from the game. By excluding an area, none of the entrance methods to the area will be able to spawn and no location checks will be placed in those areas.

By enabling this, successfully winning a run unlocks all the room location checks per stage which didn't spawn on all the stages you went through during that run.

any: This room can containy any sort of item

any: This room can containy any sort of item

mild: When death link is triggered, you'll receive 4 hits of damage (= 2 full hearts, or 4 full hearts on Womb+).
normal: When death link is triggered it tries to kill you but invincibility or revives will keep the run alive.

Enable progressive pouch upgrades. When enabled, pouches are a progressive item in the item pool.
When disabled, pouches are added as separate items

When disabled, weapons are added as separate items

options.label: Goal Requirements
options.description:
What you need before the gate to Slither Inc., the final area, opens.

Biometals: own the models chosen in required_models.
Secret Disks: collect an ammount of Secret Disks.
Missions: complete a number of story missions.

options.label: Required Models
options.description:
Models that count for the Biometals goal requirement: 
Model X, Model ZX, Model HX, Model FX, Model LX, Model PX, Model OX.
Only used with Biometals in goal_requirements.

options.label: Required Models Count
options.description:
How many of the models in required_models you need: 6 by default (the six main biometals),
any other number, or all for every model in the list.
A number above the size of the list means all of them.

options.label: Require Full Models
options.description:
For the Biometals goal requirement, a progressive model counts only with both halves
(its level 2 charge). Off: the first half is enough. Ignored without progressive_models.

options.label: Required Secret Disks
options.description:
How many Secret Disks you need for the Secret Disks goal requirement.
Only used with Secret Disks in goal_requirements. Depending on your configuration, generation may fail if the number of required disks is too high

options.label: Total Secret Disks
options.description:
How many Secret Disks go into the pool.
A total below required_secret_disks is raised to match it, and one that does not fit in the pool is lowered.

options.label: Starting Model
options.description: The model you start with

options.label: Progressive Models
options.description:
Biometals H, F, L and P come as two Progressive Model items each: the first half makes
the form usable, the second unlocks its level 2 charged attack. Off: each is a single Model
item that gives the whole biometal at once.

options.label: Human Form (Hu) In Pool
options.description:
The human form (Hu) becomes an item of the pool instead of being always
available. Ignored when starting_model is none.

options.label: Starting Transerver
options.description:
Transerver floor of the hub where a new game starts. Only that area's
Transerver Access is yours from the start; every other destination is an item like the rest.

options.label: Boss Logic
options.description:
Per-boss difficulty, your call: what you must be carrying before the
logic considers you able to beat each story boss.

It only restricts the logic: in game you can fight with whatever you
have. What it guarantees is that the seed never forces you through a boss
you are not equipped for by your own standard.
The eight Pseudoroids are fought twice (their own area and the boss rush
of the D-4 tower, which the game requires before D-5): the requirement
applies to both encounters (unless skip_boss_rush is on).

Bosses: Rayfly (B-2), Model Z (D-2), Hivolt (E-7), Lurerre (F-5),
Fistleo (G-5), Purprill (H-4), Hurricaune (I-3), Leganchor (J-5),
Flammole (K-4), Protectos (L-4), Prometheus (X-3), Pandora (M-3),
Prometheus & Pandora (O-2), Serpent (D-5), Omega Zero (N-1). The room
code works as a key too ("E-7"). Bosses you leave out ask just for any model;
the gate to Serpent's area follows goal_requirements.

Requirements: models (X ZX HX FX LX PX OX; "HX2" or "Model HX (full)" =
both halves of the progressive item, i.e. the level-2 charge), ALL6 (the six main biometals),
"Life Up x2" (or LIFEUP>=2), "Sub Tank x1" (or SUBTANK>=1) and ITEM B chips by name ("Absorber Chip"),
combined with & (and), | (or) and parentheses. A required chip is promoted from useful to progression automatically.

Example:
  boss_logic:
    Hivolt: "HX & Life Up x2"
    Flammole: "Model FX (full) & Absorber Chip"
    Serpent: "ALL6 & Sub Tank x2 & Life Up x4"
    Omega Zero: "OX | (ALL6 & SUBTANK>=2)"

options.label: Skip Boss Rush
options.description:
Skips the boss rush of the Slither Inc. tower: you do not have to beat the 8 Pseudoroids again before Serpent.
As you climb the tower, the rooms of each pair of bosses appear as already cleared.

options.label: Skip Mini-Bosses
options.description:
QoL change so that you don't have to fight the mini bosses in each area every time.
- after_first_defeat: Only have to fight them once. Next time you leave and come back to the area, the boss stays defeated.
- always: all of them count as beaten from the start, so their fights never start.

options.label: Pickup Checks: 1-Ups
options.description:
The 1-Ups placed in the world (7) count as checks: the first time you
pick each one up it sends its location; afterwards it keeps respawning
and giving a life as usual.

options.label: Pickup Checks: Energy Capsules
options.description:
The energy capsules placed in the world (45) count
as checks: the first pickup of each one sends its location; afterwards
they keep respawning and healing.

options.label: Pickup Checks: Weapon Energy
Pickup Checks: E-Crystals
options.description:
The E-Crystal pickups placed in the world (56) count as checks: the
first pickup of each one sends its location; afterwards they keep
respawning and giving crystals.

only; useful: progression and useful; all: also filler (E-Crystals,
1-Up). Can be changed in game with /mmzx_notify.

your checks holds their item): which classes are shown (off,
progression, useful, all). Can be changed in game with /mmzx_notify.

options.label: On-screen Notifications: Style

Format of the on-screen notification. short: a single line of 30
characters (the player name is dropped and the item name cut if it does
not fit). full: the whole text ("Got <item> from <player>") split by
words into pages the same popup shows one after another. Can be changed
in game with /mmzx_notify short|full.

Last Word: They are on Last Word's Spell Cards

Anywhere: They are anywhere in the multiworld

If the Spell Card is excluded, it will do -1 to the spell card until it found a valid one.
Default to the last Spell Card of Kaguya.

Stage 1:   1-13
Stage 2:   14-32
Stage 3:   33-54

What do you need to complete your goal?
Open the city: Complete the game's story by opening Walled City 99.
Recieve all badges: Get all six of the Badges from the multiworld.
Both: Open Walled City 99 after getting all six Badges.
Complete Chapter: Complete a specific chapter, specified by the next option.

4: The Slums Part 1

7: Dead End
8: Sewers
9: Antvillage

options.label: Scratchsanity
options.description:
When enabled, makes each spot where you can scratch an object a location.
It is highly recommended to turn either this and/or Camerasanity on when playing solo.
Adds 43 locations.

options.label: Camerasanity
options.description:
NOT CURRENTLY IMPLIMENTED! THIS OPTION DOES NOTHING!
When enabled, makes meowing at each camera in Dead City and The Flat a location.
It is highly recommended to turn either this and/or Scratchsanity on when playing solo.
Adds 0 locations.

options.label: Outsider Badge Logic
options.description:
How should the Outsider Badge work logically?
This only affects Logic. Nothing in the game actually requires having the Outsider Badge.

False: The Outsider Badge is never logically required for anything.
True: The Outsider Badge is logically required to progress past the start of Dead End.

options.label: Code Logic
options.description:
How should code giving items work logically?
For example, the Sheet Music Safe inside the Slums is supposed to be opened with the Safe's Mysterious Password.
However, if you know the code ahead of time, this can be skipped.
If you would rather do it the intended way, this option makes the code giving items logically required.

This affects...
Unreadable Sheet Music (requires Safe Mysterious Password and Poncho)
Accessing the Nightclub (requries Mysterious Message)

False: Code giving items are never logically required for anything.
True: Code giving items are logically required for things that are behind those codes.

options.label: DeathLink
options.description:
NOT CURRENTLY IMPLIMENTED! THIS OPTION DOES NOTHING!
If the Stray dies :(, everyone else with DeathLink dies.
If someone else with DeathLink dies, the Stray dies too :(

options.label: Scavenger Hunt
options.description:
Adds checks for items hidden around the world.
Adds 10 locations and no items.
***Does nothing in this tech demo***

options.label: Trap Percentage
options.description:
Globally changes how many filler items are replaced with traps. For specific item weights, see the next option.
Treat as a percentage, with 100(%) being all filler items are traps. Set to 0(%) to disable traps.

options.label: Trap Item Weights
options.description: Weights of each trap item. To disable all trap items, see the previous option.

options.label: Goal Requirement
options.description:
Where is the goal placed?
Reach Depth: Reach a chosen depth starting from a random or chosen layer. Depth Extenders allow you to go deeper.
Escape Overgrown Depths: Start in Gravel Lands and goal upon escaping Overgrown Depths. Progressive Layers allow you to go deeper.
Defeat Elder Thornback: Start in a random layer that isn't Overgrown Depths and goal upon killing an Elder Thornback.

options.label: Starting Layer
options.description:
Only has an effect if your goal is Reach Depth or Defeat Elder Thornback.
Determines which layer you'll start with.
You will have to unlock the other layers through the multiworld.
If your goal is Defeat Elder Thornback, your starting layer cannot be Overgrown Depths.

options.label: Goal Depth
options.description:
Only has an effect if your goal is Reach Depth.
How deep do you have to go in one run to goal? Must be a multiple of 100, and will be automatically rounded if it isn't.
Each 300m requires a Depth Extender progression item.
There will be the amount needed +5 in the item pool, unless your goal is 1500m or less, where there will be the exact amount needed.

options.label: Moodlesanity
options.description:
Each possible moodle (status effect) is a check. Does not include Anxious and Deceased, as they are impossible to get.
Disabled: Moodles do not send checks.
Questboard: Adds a new UI that shows 'quests'. You must get the shown moodle to send its check. More moodles and
            questboard slots are unlocked via items. Each "Progressive Quests" item (12 in total) unlocks 15 moodles.
Open: All moodle locations are available in sphere 1 (minus a few). Creates VERY LARGE sphere 1. Use with caution.
With every Moodle enabled, adds 166 locations.

options.label: Moodlesanity Exclusions
options.description:
What Moodlesanity locations will be excluded? Only has an effect if Moodlesanity is on.

The 'Minimal' preset excludes only Last Stand, Tachycardia, and Bradycarda
The 'Deadly' preset excludes locations that will almost always kill Experiment (lung failure, comatose, etc...)
The 'Difficult' preset excludes locations that rely on a specific item (drug overdose, rapid neuron regeneration sickness, etc...)
The 'Deadly and Difficult' preset includes everything from the three presets above
You can specify your own list as well.

options.label: Moodlesanity Questboard Cooldown Time
options.description:
How long should the cooldown between refreshes on the Questboard be? Only has an effect if Moodlesanity is set to Questboard.
Time is in seconds. Set to 0 to disable the cooldown.

options.label: Randomize Minigames
options.description:
Start without the ability to play Minigames (ex: lockpicking, removing shrapnel) until they are received through Archipelago.
Disabled: Minigames are always unlocked.
As One: There is only one item that unlocks all minigames.
Individual: Each of the 9 minigames is an individual item.
Suicide and self harm minigames are never randomized.

options.label: Limb Unlocks
options.description:
Start with Experiment's arms being amputated, with them being unlocked progressively through the multiworld.
Each arm has three progressive items, one for each limb.
There is NO LOGIC applied to this. Use at your own risk, as you will not be able to break tiles without arms.
Adds 6 items.

options.label: Randomize Recipes
options.description:
If Recipes should be randomized.
If enabled, all 132 Recipes become items to recieve.
Blueprints will still spawn, but will only give INT experience (unless Archipelago Items is above 0).

options.label: Free Samples
options.description:
Only has an effect if Randomize Recipes is on.
Receiving recipes spawns a free copy of the item the recipe makes, but only once.
This does not work on items that only exist in liquid form.

options.label: Craftsanity
options.description:
Makes crafting each individual recipe in the game a check.
Will be sphere 1 without additional options like Skillsanity and Randomize Recipes.
Note: **Item qualities required for crafting are not considered in logic.**
Adds 132 locations.

options.label: Skillsanity
options.description:
Each skill level up to level 15 is a location, and up to level 18 is an item.
Adds 45 locations and 54 items.

options.label: Archipelago Items
options.description:
How many Archipelago Items can be found throughout the cave system?
When used, they send a check and give 10 INT Experience.
They are guarenteed to drop from destroying traps, opening containers, and killing enemies.
Each Survivor is also guarenteed to have at least one free Archipelago Item in their trades.

options.label: RingLink Trading
options.description:
Allow depositing and withdrawling RingLink currency for Survivor trading value.
Deposit a positive amount to add to the pool, and deposit a negative amount to withdrawl.
No currency is lost on transfer.
If this and EnergyLink are both enabled, you will be able to pick between them in-game.

options.label: EnergyLink Trading
options.description:
Allow depositing and withdrawling EnergyLink currency for Survivor trading value.
Deposit a positive amount to add to the pool, and deposit a negative amount to withdrawl.
No currency is lost on transfer.
If this and RingLink are both enabled, you will be able to pick between them in-game.

options.label: SleepLink
options.description:
When another player with SleepLink enabled goes to sleep, you will too.
When you go to sleep, all other players with SleepLink also fall asleep.

The only other game that is planning to support this is Stardew Valley's Beta, so this is
mainly meant for servers with more than one Casualties: Unknown game.

options.label: Gifting
options.description:
Allows gifting inventory items between games.
Sending gifts to other Casualties: Unknown games will give that player the exact same item.
Sending gifts to any other game will attempt to translate the gift into something similar.
Most items are supported, but not all of them.

Use the `apgift` command in-game to send gifts to others.

options.label: Trap Percentage
options.description:
Globally changes how many filler items are replaced with traps. For specific item weights, see the next option.
Treat as a percentage, with 100(%) being all filler items are traps. Set to 0(%) to disable traps.

options.label: Trap Item Weights
options.description: Weights of each trap item. To disable all trap items, see the previous option.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Choose the end goal.
Main Quest: Complete the main quest
Questsanity: Complete all quests in the game
Max Level: Reach level 99
Max Level and Main Quest: Complete the main quest and reach level 99
Spellmastery: Get all skills to max level

options.label: Skills Upgrades
options.description:
Choose how skills will be upgraded.
Coins: You upgrade skills in-game using coins. (The vanilla way)
Progressive Skills: Each skill is added to the itempool 10 times.
Upgrades: Each skill is added to the itempool once, allowing usage of that skill. Additionally, 9 upgrades for each skill are added to the itempool, that will be applied once the skill is aquired.
Magic Levels: Each skill is added to the itempool once, allowing usage of that skill. Additionally, 9 magic levels are added to the itempool, that will upgrade all acquired skills.

options.label: Include Temples
options.description: Choose if visiting temples will be included

options.label: Include Monuments
options.description: Choose if visiting monuments will be included

options.label: Include EXP Quest Rewards
options.description: Choose if you want to receive EXP as quest rewards. (Beware, not including this option can cause heavy grind with some options)

options.label: Include Coin Quest Rewards
options.description: Choose if you want to receive coins as quest rewards

options.label: Starting Episode
options.description:
Select Which episode to start with.

Dead Men Tell No Tales requires items to do the first job, meaning you'll
only have ThiefNet locations in logic when starting there.
Flight of Fancy and A Cold Alliance also require items to have even ThiefNet
in logic, so if you start with one of those episodes without the required
items, you will start with no locations in logic.
Flight of Fancy only needs Bentley (the default bonus crew member), so this
is only a problem if you change the bonus crew member away from Bentley.

options.label: Include Mega Jump

options.label: Mega Jump Energy Cost
options.description:
The amount of gadget meter a single Mega Jump consumes. Vanilla is
34 (a full meter allows three jumps).

options.description:
The minimum number of coins you'll receive when you get a "Coins" filler
item.

options.label: Coins Maximum

The maximum number of coins you'll receive when you get a "Coins" filler
item.

options.label: ThiefNet Cost Maximum

options.label: Start with Binocucom
options.description:
Start with the ability to use the binocucom, rather than shuffling it into
the pool.

options.label: Start with Bombs
options.description: Start with Bentley's bombs, rather than shuffling it into the pool.

options.label: Start with Double Jump

Start with Bentley's double jump (one Progressive Hover Pack), rather than
shuffling all three into the pool. This is the vanilla default.

options.label: Permissive Yaml
options.description:
If permissive yaml is on, incompatible yaml options will be changed to more
suitable ones. If turned off, these yaml options will throw an error and
cause generation to halt.

This is intended for yamls with random values. If you're not randomizing
any options, it's recommended that you turn permissive yaml off.

options.label: Ring Link
options.description:
Whether your coin gain/loss is linked to other players. When you gain or
lose coins, ring-linked players gain or lose the same amount, and vice
versa.

options.label: Permissive Yaml
options.description:
If permissive yaml is on, incompatible yaml options will be changed to more
suitable ones. If turned off, these yaml options will throw an error and
cause generation to halt.

This is intended for yamls with random values. If you're not randomizing
any options, it's recommended that you turn permissive yaml off.

options.label: Starting Episode
options.description:
Select Which episode to start with. Starting with Anatomy for disaster
is not compatible with the "first section", "whole episode" and
"progressive sections" options for "Episode 8 Keys".

choices.label: He Who Tames The Iron Horse

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Which boss you must defeat to goal, or Clockwerk Hunt.

Clockwerk Hunt requires you to collect a certain number of Clockwerk
parts/keys to goal. All Vaults requires you to open all 8 vaults.

Pick and Mix lets you combine several victory conditions; configure which
ones with the "Pick and Mix" option.

options.label: Clockwerk Parts in Pool
options.description:
How many Clockwerk parts are added to the pool. If this is lower than the
required number of keys (for either Clockwerk Hunt or Episode 8 unlock),
the generator warns and keeps your values as written, which can make the
goal or Episode 8 impossible, or, with permissive_yaml on, lowers the
requirement to match.

Setting this to values close to 500 requires that you set tasksanity to
true, bottle_location_bundle_size to 1, and bottle_item_bundle_size to at
least 3 (4 if both vault and pickpocket checks are turned off).

options.label: Episode 8 Keys
options.description:
Whether to have Anatomy for Disaster be unlocked with a number of Clockwerk
parts, rather than with a single item like the other episodes.

- First section: Unlock only the first section of Anatomy for Disaster with
  the required amount of Clockwerk Parts.
- Last section: Unlock only the final mission of Anatomy for Disaster with
  the required amount of Clockwerk Parts.
- Whole episode: Unlock every mission in Anatomy for Disaster with the
  required amount of Clockwerk Parts.
- Gradual sections: Unlock the four sections of Anatomy for Disaster one at
  a time, each requiring a larger fraction of the required Clockwerk Parts,
  with the final section requiring the full amount.
- Off: Unlock Anatomy for Disaster with progressive episode items, like the
  other episodes.

options.label: Episode 8 Required Keys
options.description:
How many Clockwerk parts you need to unlock Anatomy for Disaster, if
Episode 8 Keys is turned on.

options.label: Goal Required Keys
options.description: How many Clockwerk parts you need to goal, if goal objective is Clockwerk Hunt

options.label: Include TOM
options.description: Add the TOM ability/gadget to the pool.

options.label: Include Mega Jump
options.description: Add the Mega Jump ability/gadget to the pool.

options.label: Include Time Rush
options.description: Add the Time Rush ability/gadget to the pool.

options.label: Coins Minimum
options.description:
The minimum number of coins you'll receive when you get a "Coins" filler
item.

options.label: Coins Maximum
options.description:
The maximum number of coins you'll receive when you get a "Coins" filler
item.

options.label: Include Vaults
options.description: Whether to include vaults as checks.

options.label: Include Pickpocketing
options.description: Whether to include pickpocketing loot from guards as checks.

options.label: Task Sanity
options.description: Whether to include the individual tasks that make up each job as checks.

options.label: Small Guard Loot Chance
options.description: The chance that any given small guard will have pick-pocketable loot.

options.label: Large Guard Loot Chance
options.description: The chance that any given large guard will have pick-pocketable loot.

options.label: Loot Table Distribution
options.description:
How "evenly" the loot table chances will be distributed. By default, the 6
pieces of loot a guard can carry will be distributed with the chances
(30%/30%/15%/15%/5%/5%). A lower value will make first pieces of loot even
more likely, and a higher value will flatten out the chances.

options.label: Randomize Loot
options.description:
Whether to shuffle all pickpocketing loot locations. A guard could have the
same piece of loot multiple times on their table, so there is no
guaranteeing that each guard will have exactly 6 different pieces of loot.

options.label: Dynamic Loot Tables
options.description:
Whether the pickpocketing loot tables update during play, making loot whose
checks have not been collected more common than loot that has already been
checked.

options.label: Loot Values
options.description:
How much each piece of pickpocketing loot sells for.

- Vanilla: Loot sells for what it does in the base game.
- Shuffled: The vanilla sell values are shuffled between the pieces of loot.
- Randomized: Each piece of loot gets a new sell value, rolled between
  "Loot Value Minimum" and "Loot Value Maximum".

options.label: Loot Value Minimum
options.description:
The lowest a piece of loot can sell for. Only takes effect if loot_values is
set to Randomized.

options.label: Loot Value Maximum
options.description:
The highest a piece of loot can sell for. Only takes effect if loot_values
is set to Randomized.

options.label: Treasure Values
options.description:
How much each treasure sells for.

- Vanilla: Treasures sell for what they do in the base game.
- Shuffled: The vanilla sell values are shuffled between the treasures.
- Randomized: Each treasure gets a new sell value, rolled between "Treasure
  Value Minimum" and "Treasure Value Maximum".

options.label: Treasure Value Minimum
options.description:
The lowest a treasure can sell for. Only takes effect if treasure_values is
set to Randomized.

options.label: Treasure Value Maximum
options.description:
The highest a treasure can sell for. Only takes effect if treasure_values is
set to Randomized.

options.label: ThiefNet Cost Minimum
options.description: The minimum number of coins items on ThiefNet will cost.

options.label: ThiefNet Cost Maximum
options.description: The maximum number of coins items on ThiefNet will cost.

options.label: Bottle Location Bundle Sizes
options.description:
How many bottles you need to collect for each check. Set to 0 to disable
bottles as checks. Both this and bottle_item_bundle_size must be non-zero
for bottles to appear; setting only one is invalid.

options.label: Bottle Item Bundle Sizes
options.description:
How many bottles you receive from an item. Set to 0 to disable bottles
as items. Both this and bottle_location_bundle_size must be non-zero for
bottles to appear; setting only one is invalid.

options.label: Bottlesanity
options.description:
Each bottle is its own check, rather than counting the number of bottles
collected. Only takes effect if bottle_location_bundle_size is 1.

options.label: Scout Thiefnet
options.description: Whether to scout/hint ThiefNet checks. They will still be displayed in game.

options.label: Trap Chance
options.description: The percentage of filler items that are replaced with traps.

options.label: Remote Items
options.description: Indicates you get items sent from your own world. This allows coop play of a world.

options.label: First Item
options.description:
Which movement item if any will apper at Hidden Pipe Heart

None - no guaranteed first item expect to be BK'd until you receive one of the 3 movement items

options.label: Fast Sheol
options.description: Skip most of the final area Sheol (Skips the Junkoids and the "Baby")

options.label: Use Smallmech
options.description:
Includes logic for the Smallmech glitch.
In "Vanilla" difficulty, this will force the Lava Cooled event to be at Cooler.

options.label: Use Watermech
options.description: Includes logic for the Watermech glitch.

options.label: Ventilation Hardlock Bypass
options.description:
WORK IN PROGRESS!
Includes logic for the Ventilation Hardlock bypass.
You need to collect all items after the chase, or reset your file if you don't.

options.label: Gato Tech
options.description:
Difficulty of strategies.

"Medium" is recommended for normal players. You might have to do some tricks done in the Any% speedrun if you enable glitches.

"Hard" includes a bunch of difficult or obscure strategies, which require advanced knowledge.

"Vanilla" is a special difficulty, with a raised difficulty for the very best. It will:
- remove the hotboy crash fixes in heater core (still includes the fix for the mauser fight)
- include the logic for the standard cat vent skip and vent mashing

options.label: Nexus Start
options.description:
Start in the Nexus instead of the Landing Site.
Allows for some logic checks without rocket

options.label: Force Local Start
options.description: Makes the Rocket (or if possible, Spin Jump + Dash) a local drop, preventing an early BK.

options.label: Aqueduct Goal
options.description: Required amount of "Progressive Water Level" required to enter Incubator.

options.label: Heater Core Goal
options.description: Required amount of "Lava Cooled" required to enter Incubator.

options.label: Ventilation Goal
options.description: Required amount of "Progressive Vent Level" required to enter Incubator.

options.label: Loresanity
options.description:
Add lore buttons/terminals as checkable locations.
Includes the main terminal in nexus and the two secret lore spots in nexus.

options.label: Health Filler
options.description:
Makes all Health Upgrades filler.
Use this to allow for extra filler for excluded locations.

options.label: Out-Of-Logic Display
options.description:
Shows out-of-logic check in the universal tracker.
Recommended order is: Medium -> Medium all Glitches -> Hard -> Hard all Glitches -> Vanilla all Glitches -> Vanilla (No Glitches!)
"all_glitches" shows logic with all glitches enabled.
"difficulty" shows logic for a difficulty one level higher.

options.label: Bosssanity
options.description:
Add mauser boss kills as checkable locations.
Do not kill the first 3 bosses with Smallmech since that causes a crash/softlock!

options.label: Starting Zone
options.description:
Determines with zone to start with. 
Leaf Forest through Egg Utopia are valid along with random.

options.label: Starting Character

Determines which character to start with.
Sonic must be available for goal.
If yaml settings cause Sonic to not be available, one character will be replaced with Sonic.

difficulties.

Makes the progression more interesting. It's like gun game, but you unlock them in order up to

Choose the level to start in

Choose level to complete to finish the game

List as many levels as you would like to skip completing

The number of deaths needed to send out a deathlink event

Percentage chance to replace money filler with a Hostile Trap.

options.label: Logic Difficulty

The difficulty of tricks the logic will expect.
Developer Intended: No tricks will be expected. For a room to be possible, you need every mechanic that would normally be required.
Reasonable Skips: Enables skips that are not too difficult, but may require thinking outside the box.

Whether your ring gain/loss is linked to other players.

options.label: Enable Gear 1st Place

options.label: Level Checks
options.description: Number of level-up checks included in the game.

options.label: Quest Goal Tier
options.description: Quest tier completion required to achieve victory. Ten quests are required for each tier.

options.label: Include Advanced Gathering Challenges
options.description:
Include the 10 "Gatherer" challenge locations (large resource-gathering
quotas). These are excluded by default because they are considerably
more grindy than the other challenge checks.

options.label: Include Hunter Challenges
options.description: Include the 10 Hunter challenge locations to hunt wildlife. This can be very time consuming, and relies on the random spawning of wildlife.

options.label: Include Zombie Kill Challenges
options.description: Include challenges that require killing specific zombie types. These can be incredibly grindy, and require rare zombies to appear.

options.label: Additional Rocket Pool
options.description:
Adds a pool to draw items from specifically for the rocket, silo and satellite randomized recipes.
This is to emulate the Vanilla AP factorio space_science_pack setting but for all Maximum Science Packs.
It Doesn't affect the difficulty of the rocket but lowers the difficulty of science packs slightly.

options.label: Percent Items for randomization
options.description:
The percentage of items in the game considered for randomized recipes.
Lowering will cause all ingame recipes to become easier.
If generation fails, try upping this.

options.label: No Earlier Pools
options.description:
When enabled when randomizing recipes, no earlier item pools will be considered for ingredients.
This will drastically increase the difficulty you've been warned.

options.label: Goal
options.description: Goal required to complete the game.

options.label: Technology Tree Layout
options.description:
Selects how the tech tree nodes are interwoven.
Single: No dependencies
Diamonds: Several grid graphs (4/9/16 nodes each)
Pyramids: Several top halves of diamonds (6/10/15 nodes each)
Funnels: Several bottom halves of diamonds (6/10/15 nodes each)
Trees: Several trees
Choices: A single balanced binary tree
Irregular: A single randomly generated technology tree.

options.label: Minimum Science Pack Cost
options.description: The cheapest a Technology can be in Science Packs.

options.label: Maximum Science Pack Cost
options.description: The most expensive a Technology can be in Science Packs.

options.label: Tech Cost Distribution
options.description:
Random distribution of costs of the Science Packs.
Even: any number between min and max is equally likely.
Low: low costs, near the minimum, are more likely.
Middle: medium costs, near the average, are more likely.
High: high costs, near the maximum, are more likely.

options.label: Science Pack Cost Mix
options.description:
Percent chance that a preceding Science Pack is also required.
Chance is rolled per preceding pack.

options.label: Ramping Tech Costs
options.description:
Forces the amount of Science Packs required to ramp up with the highest involved Pack. Average is preserved.
For example:
off: Automation (red)/Logistics (green) sciences can range from 1 to 1000 Science Packs,
on: Automation (red) ranges to ~500 packs and Logistics (green) from ~500 to 1000 Science Packs

options.label: Tech Layer Obscurity
options.description:
Hides technologies based on what science packs you have crafted.
on: If you have crafted Automation (red) science. You can only view technologies that require Automation (red) science.
off: Even if you have crafted only Automation (red) science. You can still see technologies that require Utility (yellow) science.
WARNING: no technology will be visible at the start of the game. You need to craft a red science pack to view any technologies.
If information is Full, then this will also hide the hints.
Works alone or in combination with Depth Obscurity.

options.label: Tech Depth Obscurity
options.description:
Hides technologies based on what you have researched.
The value determines how far you can see.
Tech tree example:
   B   |
   |   |
A  C   |
|\ |  /
D  E
|
F
Only A is researched.
0: disabled. This feature shuts of at 0.
1: You only see sciences that are one step away from what you have researched so far. In the example above. This will be B and D. (Note, E needs C to be researched.)
2: You will see techs that are two steps away from all the tech you have researched. In the example above this is A, B, C, D and F. (E is still not visible.)
If information is Full, then this will also hide the hints.
Works alone or in combination with Layer Obscurity.

options.label: Rocket Silo
options.description: Ingredients to craft rocket silo or auto-place if set to spawn.

options.label: Satellite
options.description: Ingredients to craft satellite.

options.label: Free Samples
options.description: Get free items with your technologies.

options.label: Free Samples Quality
options.description:
If free samples are on, determine the quality of the granted items.
Requires the quality mod, which is part of the Space Age DLC. Without it, normal quality is given.

options.label: Technology Tree Information
options.description:
How much information should be displayed in the tech tree.
None: No indication of what a research unlocks.
Advancement: Indicates if a research unlocks an item that is considered logical advancement, but not who it is for.
Full only hint advancement: Labels with exact names and recipients of unlocked items; only the advancement unlocks are prefilled into the !hint command, or get hinted out by the tech obscurity.
Full: Labels with exact names and recipients of unlocked items; all researches are prefilled into the !hint command, or get hinted out by the tech obscurity.

options.label: Starting Items
options.description: Mapping of Factorio internal item-name to amount granted on start.

options.label: Free Sample Blacklist
options.description: Set of items that should never be granted from Free Samples

options.label: Free Sample Whitelist
options.description: Overrides any free sample blacklist present. This may ruin the balance of the mod, be warned.

options.label: Recipe Time
options.description:
Randomize the time it takes for any recipe to craft, this includes smelting, chemical lab, hand crafting etc.
Fast: 0.25X - 1X
Normal: 0.5X - 2X
Slow: 1X - 4X
Chaos: 0.25X - 4X
New category: ignores vanilla recipe time and rolls new one
New Fast: 0.25 - 2 seconds
New Normal: 0.25 - 10 seconds
New Slow:  5 - 10 seconds

options.label: Random Recipe Ingredients Level
options.description: Select if rocket, or rocket + science pack ingredients should be random.

options.label: Randomized Recipe Ingredients Offset
options.description:
When randomizing ingredients, remove or add this many "slots" of items.
For example, at -1 a randomized Automation Science Pack will only require 1 ingredient, instead of 2.

options.label: Blueprints
options.description: Allow or Disallow Blueprints from outside the current savegame.

options.label: World Generation
options.description:
World gen settings for the factorio world
If you use custom, you must define the logic in custom_world_generation
World Generation settings. Overview of options at https://wiki.factorio.com/Map_generator,
with in-depth documentation at https://lua-api.factorio.com/latest/concepts/MapGenSettings.html
An example for this can be found: https://discord.com/channels/731205301247803413/1426234278462750860/1459637472496586905

options.label: Custom World Generation
options.description:
World Generation settings. Overview of options at https://wiki.factorio.com/Map_generator,
with in-depth documentation at https://lua-api.factorio.com/latest/concepts/MapGenSettings.html

options.label: Progressive Technologies
options.description:
Merges together Technologies like "automation-1" to "automation-3" into 3 copies of "Progressive Automation",
which awards them in order.

options.label: Attack Traps
options.description: Trap items that when received trigger an attack on your base.

options.label: Evolution Traps
options.description: Trap items that when received increase the enemy evolution.

options.label: Evolution Trap %% Effect
options.description:
How much an Evolution Trap increases the enemy evolution.
Increases scale down proportionally to the session's current evolution factor
(40 increase at 0.50 will add 0.20... 40 increase at 0.75 will add 0.10...)

options.label: Teleport Traps
options.description:
Trap items that when received trigger a random teleport.
It is ensured the player can walk back to where they got teleported from.

options.label: Grenade Traps
options.description: Trap items that when received trigger a grenade explosion on each player.

options.label: Cluster Grenade Traps
options.description: Trap items that when received trigger a cluster grenade explosion on each player.

options.label: Artillery Traps
options.description: Trap items that when received trigger an artillery shell on each player.

options.label: Atomic Rocket Traps
options.description:
Trap items that when received trigger an atomic rocket explosion on each player.
Warning: there is no warning. The launch is instantaneous.

options.label: Atomic Cliff Remover Traps
options.description:
Trap items that when received trigger an atomic rocket explosion on a random cliff.
Warning: there is no warning. The launch is instantaneous.

options.label: Inventory Spill Traps
options.description: Trap items that when received trigger dropping your main inventory and trash inventory onto the ground.

options.label: Peek a Tech Traps
options.description: Trap items that when received hide all the technologies on the tech screen. Stopping all science for a short while.

options.label: Tech Reset Traps
options.description: Trap items that when received resets the process of all technologies, does not unresearch.

options.label: Reset Map Info Traps
options.description: Trap items that when received trigger that your map data gets deleted.

options.label: Energy Spiral Traps
options.description: Trap items that when received temporarily increases the energy cost and raises pollution produced of all machines.

options.label: Energy Spiral Type
options.description:
Determine how the Energy Spiral Traps stack.
Intensity: Makes intensity stack, leading to that more traps means even higher energy costs.
Duration: Makes the duration stack, leading to a longer during time in which the energy costs are higher.

options.label: Energy Link
options.description: Allow sending energy to other worlds. 25% of the energy is lost in the transfer.

options.label: Additional logic
options.description:
Add additional logic that can make progression nicer.
If you use custom, you must define the logic in custom_additional_logic
An example for this can be found: https://discord.com/channels/731205301247803413/1426234278462750860/1437568465987829975

options.label: Custom Additional Logic
options.description:
Custom logic: hidden
example found here: https://discord.com/channels/731205301247803413/1426234278462750860/1437568465987829975

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Chooses which of the three possible endings to pursue:
- Our Song: Complete the game's classic ending after collecting five vessels.
- Your New World: Collect five vessels through violent or hostile outcomes and destroy her without outside help.
- Oblivion: Reject the Princess and refuse to enter the cabin, ultimately choosing oblivion.

options.label: Memories Hunt
options.description:
Determines how many gallery images must be collected before the game can be completed.
- 0: No memories are required, just complete the goal.
- 1-439: The specified number of memories must be collected before completion.

options.label: Death Link
options.description:
Determines how DeathLink behaves.
- Nothing: DeathLink is disabled.
- Only Receive: You can receive DeathLinks from other players, but your deaths are never sent.
- On Archipelago Death: Sends a DeathLink when you become stuck because you are missing required progression items.
- On Real Death: Sends a DeathLink whenever the protagonist dies during the story.
- Both: Combines Archipelago Death and Real Death behaviors.

options.label: Chapter Access Rando
options.description:
Determines which items are required to access chapters and shuffles them into the item pool.
- Nothing: No items added, you can enter a chapter just like in the base game.
- Princess: You will only need the princess item to enter a chapter (+23 items)
- Voices: You will only need the voice items to access a chapter (+10 items)
- Both: You will need the princess and voice items to access a chapter (+33 items)

options.label: Pristine Blade Rando
options.description:
Controls how many Pristine Blades are available and shuffles them into the item pool.
- Nothing: Pristine Blade is not randomized
- One Blade: Only one Pristine Blade is available for the entire game (+1 items)
- Chapter Blade: One Pristine Blade per chapter [The fourth one is for the goddess] (+4 items)
- Princess Blade: One Pristine Blade per princess (+23 items)

options.label: Pristine Sword Rando
options.description: Shuffles the pristine sword in the apotheosis chapter into the item pool. (+1 items)

options.label: Narrator Rando
options.description: Shuffles the narrator into the item pool as an item required to talk with him in the mirror in the space between. (+1 items)

options.label: Save Slot Rando
options.description:
Shuffles save slots into the item pool, indicating the number of possible saves
It's just a slot, you can save multiple times to the same slot if you want

Set to -1 so it's not randomized (you will have 5 pages of 6 slots (30 in total) available)
Set to -2 so that all filler items become save slot items (= number of locations - number of items) [max 30]

options.label: Gift Rando
options.description:
Chooses to randomize gifts in the world. (+5 locations/items)
- Nothing: Gifts are not randomized
- Item: Invitations are added as progression items required to complete loops
- Location: Gifts are added as check locations. When you encounter the Shifting Mound for the Xth time during the same save
- Both: Invitations and Gifts are both items and locations

options.label: Memories Sanity
options.description:
Chooses to randomize the memories in the world. (+439 locations/items)
- Nothing: Memories are not randomized
- Location: Memories are added as check locations, but the items are not shuffled.
- Both: Memories are both items and locations

options.label: Chapter Rando
options.description:
Chooses to randomize entering a chapter in the world.
- Nothing: Entering a chapter is not random.
- Chapter: Entering a chapter for the first time is a check locations in the world. (+23 locations)
- Global: Entering a global chapter (2 and 3) for the first time is a check locations in the world. (+2 locations)
- Both: Entering chapter and global chapter are check locations in the world. (+25 locations)

options.label: Voice Rando
options.description: Add the fact that a voice speaks for the first time as check locations in the world. (+10 locations)

options.label: Heart Rando
options.description:
Chooses to randomize hearts in the world.
- Nothing: Hearts are not random.
- Heart: Hearts are check locations in the world. (+29 locations)
- Vessel: For example, for Damsel: "A Gentle Heart" and "A Pliable Heart" are combined into a single location
          Chapter affected: Razor, Prisoner, Damsel, Fury, Dragon, Wild, Grey. (+22 locations)

options.label: Mirror Rando
options.description:
Chooses to randomize facing a mirror in the world.
- Nothing: Mirror are not random.
- Space Between: Add facing the mirror in the end of the 5 loops as check locations in the world. (+5 locations)
- Chapter: Add facing a mirror in a chapter as check locations in the world. (+19 locations)
- Both: Facing the mirror in the space between and in a chapter are check locations in the world. (+24 locations)

options.label: Oblivion Rando
options.description: Add all oblivion steps as check locations in the world. (+6 location)

options.label: White Powerup Item Weight
options.description: When you receive a powerup item, the weight of this powerup being white

options.label: Blue Powerup Item Weight
options.description: When you receive a powerup item, the weight of this powerup being blue

options.label: Orange Powerup Item Weight
options.description: When you receive a powerup item, the weight of this powerup being orange

options.label: Number Of Powerup Logic Region
options.description:
How many regions to create in logic and put powerups pickup locations into
The logic uses multiple regions in order to force late powerups locations (example, White Powerup 87) to be in later spheres (so that one of your friends doesn't need it to enter their sphere 2 for example)
Higher values means that it's less likely for powerups locations you will get pretty late to contain items needed earlier

options.label: Number Of White Powerup Location Per Region
options.description:
How many white powerup pickup location to put in each region
Note that the total ammount of white powerups you will need to pickup to get the whole location pool is Number Of Regions * Number Of Location Per Region
White powerup locations picked up after that won't give you anything

options.label: Number Of Blue Powerup Location Per Region
options.description: Same as above but for the blue powerup locations

options.label: Number Of Orange Powerup Location Per Region
options.description: Same as above but for the orange powerup locations

options.label: Include Exotic Armors
options.description: Wether to add crafting Wolfskin armor and Chunkium armor as locations

options.label: Include Legendary Weapons
options.description:
Wether to add crafting legendary weapons as locations
These are the Wyvern Dagger, Gronk's Sword, Chunky Hammer, Night Blade, Chiefs Spear and Ancient Bow

options.label: Allow Looting Locations
options.description:
Allows you to get the locations for crafting tools/weapons/armors by obtaining them through other means
(Looting chests, buying from woodmen...)

options.label: Logic Difficulty
options.description:
Only used in logic to determine how many powerups/weapons/armors you need to defeat bosses
Will cause generation errors when using a low difficulty and a small item pool

Easy will wait until you have a LOT of powerups and weapons before saying you can fight bosses
None will assume you can beat everything with nothing but a rock
Normal and Hard are in-betweens

It is NOT recommended to play with None

options.label: Deathlink
options.description: Include deathlink

options.label: Starting Weapon
options.description:
What weapon to start with to make the beggining more fun
If you choose None, you might have to farm your first powerup region with just a rock

options.label: Goal
options.description:
mastery: Complete every included check on the goal heroes.
distinct_wins: Win one match with each goal hero.
Goal Hero Count rolls that many from the seed. Goal Heroes adds chosen names in that set.

options.label: Goal Heroes
options.description:
Optional named heroes forced into the goal. Leave empty to use only Goal Hero Count.
Listed heroes must be enabled and stay in the pool.

options.label: Party Mode
options.description:
When enabled, builds the seed for a group. Heroes unlock in waves (Progressive Hero Wave).
Role Passes, Extra Starting Heroes, and Shards are ignored.

Use this option if you have a group of players that want to play the multiworld together.

options.label: Party Size
options.description:
Party Mode only. How many players the seed is built for (2–5).
Each wave unlocks this many heroes together.

options.label: Starting Waves
options.description:
Party Mode only. How many hero waves start already unlocked.
1 = one hero per party size. 2–3 grants that many unlocked waves.

Example: Party Size:3 + Starting Waves:2 will give 6 heroes at the start.

options.label: Role Passes
options.description: When on, each hero needs its unlock item and a role pass (Tank, Bruiser, Support, Melee Assassin, or Ranged Assassin). Healers and utility supports use Support Pass. Ignored when Party Mode is on.

options.label: Extra Starting Heroes
options.description:
Random extra heroes unlocked at start with the starting hero. All extras share one role
pass when Role Passes is on. Up to 4 extras (5 starting heroes total).
Ignored when Party Mode is on (use Starting Waves).

options.label: Shards Per Hero
options.description:
How many shards it takes to unlock a hero.
0 = no shards; every hero is a single unlock item.
1-5 = total shards spread across the multiworld needed to unlock each hero.
Ignored when Party Mode is on.

options.label: Include Timed Win Check
options.description:
When Role Passes is on, add one timed win check per role pass bucket (win in under 18 minutes).
Any currently unlocked hero in that pass can achieve the check.

options.label: Cumulative Checks
options.description:
When on, stat-based hero checks (damage, healing, takedowns, etc.) add up across
games with that hero. Win and reach level 20 still require a single match.

options.label: Remove Level 20 Check
options.description:
When on, the reach level 20 check is removed from every hero.
Also excludes level 20 from random talent checks (if enabled).

options.label: Random Talents Per Hero
options.description:
How many random talent slots are forced on each selected hero.
0 disables random talent checks. Each matching slot is its own check.
See the Talents tab for which slots to pick.

options.label: Daily Quests
options.description:
When on, roll up to 3 cumulative daily quests from check families that have
at least 5 matching heroes in the pool. Examples: Collect 150 regen globes,
Kill 200 minions, Restore 200,000 health, etc..

options.label: Credit Mode
options.description:
Who gets credit from a replay.

me: Only your /name.
team: Unlocked heroes on your team. Empty Credit Names = whole team.
match: Unlocked heroes in the game. Empty Credit Names = everyone.

options.label: Credit Names
options.description:
Use this option to filter specific players when Credit Mode is team or match.
Leave empty to credit everyone that mode allows. Your entire team or match.
Listing names means ONLY those players get credit (include yourself if you want your row).

Use the scoreboard / replay name (usually BattleTag without #1234).

options.label: Include AI
options.description: Also credit computer players allowed by Credit Mode.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Choose your victory condition:

Arena: Complete 21 Arena matches and become Grand Champion
Gatecloser: Close X Oblivion Gates (number set by Gate Count)
Shrine Seeker: Complete X Daedric Shrine quests (number set by Shrine Goal)
Dungeon Delver: Complete all dungeons in your seed. (Regions * Dungeons per Region)
Light the Dragonfires: Complete the Main Quest
Nirnsanity: Collect Nirnroot plants and complete the Seeking Your Roots quest
Treasure Hunter: Collect a specific amount of gold (set by Gold Goal)
Bounty Hunter: Complete all Bounty Contracts in your seed

options.label: Shrine Goal
options.description:
For Shrine Seeker goal: How many Daedric Shrine quests you need to complete for victory.
You can complete any of the available shrines to reach this goal.

Only relevant when Goal is Shrine Seeker. Ignored for other goals.

options.label: Gold Goal
options.description:
For Treasure Hunter goal: How much gold you need to collect for victory.

Gold is tracked in increments with checks along the way.
Your Gold capacity is gated by Progressive Septim Satchels.

Only relevant when Goal is Treasure Hunter. Ignored for other goals.

options.label: Shrine Count
options.description:
Number of Daedric Shrine quests available as location checks. Shrines require Shrine Unlock Tokens to access.

When Goal is Shrine Seeker: This many total shrines are available, complete any X (set by Shrine Goal) to win.
When Goal is NOT Shrine Seeker: This many shrines are available as location checks.

options.label: Gate Count
options.description:
Number of Oblivion Gates available as location checks. Gates require Oblivion Gate Keys to access.

When Goal is Gatecloser: You must close this many gates for victory.
When Goal is NOT Gatecloser: This many gates are available as location checks.
When Goal is Light the Dragonfires: This setting is ignored.

options.label: Arena Matches
options.description:
Number of Arena matches available as location checks. Arena matches require Arena Rank items to access.

When Goal is Arena: This setting is IGNORED - all 21 matches are always available and required for victory.
When Goal is NOT Arena: This many arena matches (1 through X) are available as location checks.

options.label: Nirnroot Harvesting Checks
options.description:
Number of Nirnroot harvesting location checks available in the world.

When Goal is Nirnsanity: You must collect this many Nirnroot for victory. Your Nirnroot 
harvesting limit is gated by Progressive Nirnroot Satchels.

When Goal is NOT Nirnsanity: This many Nirnroot plants are available as location checks. 
All are immediately harvestable with no capacity restrictions.

options.label: Regions per Seed
options.description:
Number of regions that will appear as unlock items.
Only these regions' dungeons and sidequests will be available as location checks.

Set to 0 to disable regional dungeon content entirely (only allowed when Goal is not Dungeon Delver).
Note: When regions > 0, you are granted one region unlock at the start of the game.

options.label: Dungeons per Region
options.description:
Maximum number of dungeons selected from each unlocked region.
If Dungeon Delver is your goal, you will need to complete every dungeon in the selected regions.

Note: If a region has fewer dungeons than this value, all of its dungeons are selected.
Note: This setting is ignored when region_unlocks is set to 0.

options.label: Wealth Sidequest Count
options.description:
Number of wealth-focused sidequests that will be randomly selected and included in the seed.
WARNING: These sidequests require accumulating a significant amount of gold to purchase expensive items.

Note: Most sidequests require specific region access. You may receive less sidequests depending on the value of RegionUnlocks above.

options.label: Exploration Sidequest Count
options.description:
Number of exploration-focused sidequests that will be randomly selected and included in the seed.
These sidequests involve exploration and adventure activities.

Note: Most sidequests require specific region access. You may receive less sidequests depending on the value of RegionUnlocks above.

options.label: Doomstone Checks
options.description:
When true: Birthsign Doomstone checks are included for each unlocked region.
When false: No doomstone location checks are added.

Ignored when regions are disabled.

options.label: Black Market
options.description:
Highest Black Market fencing threshold included in the seed.
Thresholds at or below this value become locations. 0 disables Black Market checks.

Possible checks: 50, 150, 300, 500, 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000

options.label: Bounty Count
options.description:
Number of bounty contracts generated for this seed (0-20).
Bounty contracts assign specific NPCs or enemy types to kill.
The first contract is granted at the start of the game. Each Progressive Bounty Contract unlocks the next.

If Goal is Bounty Hunter: Completing this number of contracts is required for victory.

options.label: Weapon Lock
options.description:
When true: Dungeon, overworld, and Oblivion kill checks only increment if the
kill was made with a licensed weapon type. You start with a Starting Weapon
license; the other licenses must be found in the world.

Does not affect bounty kills.

When false: All weapon types count.

options.label: Starting Weapon
options.description:
Which weapon license you start with when Weapon Lock is on.

Ignored when Weapon Lock is off.

options.label: Dungeon Kill Checks
options.description:
Number of dungeon kill location checks (enemies killed in dungeon or most interior cells).
Set to 0 to disable dungeon kill checks.

When regions are enabled, checks are divided evenly across regions: each region unlock
makes the next batch accessible. For example, 50 kills with 5 regions = 10 kills per
region batch, so you start with 10 accessible and gain 10 more per region unlock.

options.label: Kills per Dungeon Check
options.description: Enemy kills needed to award one Dungeon Kill check.

options.label: Overworld Kill Checks
options.description:
Number of overworld kill location checks (enemies killed in Tamriel).
Set to 0 to disable overworld kill checks.

When regions are enabled, checks are divided evenly across regions: each region unlock
makes the next batch accessible. For example, 40 kills with 5 regions = 8 kills per
region batch, so you start with 8 accessible and gain 8 more per region unlock.

options.label: Kills per Overworld Check
options.description: Enemy kills needed to award one Overworld Kill check.

options.label: Oblivion Kill Checks
options.description:
Number of Oblivion plane kill location checks (enemies killed inside Oblivion Gates).
Set to 0 to disable Oblivion kill checks.

When Gate Count is above 0: batched by Gate Key count. With 5 keys and 50 kills,
checks 1-10 need 1 key, 11-20 need 2 keys, and so on.

When Goal is Light the Dragonfires: checks are batched by region unlocks, same as dungeon
and overworld kills. If regions are disabled, all Oblivion kill checks
are accessible immediately.

Ignored when Gate Count is 0 and Goal is not Light the Dragonfires.

options.label: Kills per Oblivion Check
options.description:
Enemy kills needed to award one Oblivion Kill check.
Ignored when Oblivion Kill Checks is 0.

options.label: Class Selection
options.description:
Choose your character class:

OFF: No class location checks
RANDOM: Randomly select a class from all available classes
[Class Names]: Choose a specific class

When enabled, all associated major skills for the class will be checks.

options.label: Class Level Maximum
options.description:
Maximum class level when Class Selection is enabled.
This number will determine how many Progressive <Class> items are available in the item pool.

Each level provides 14 additional skill checks (2 per class skill).
With the default of 3, this adds 42 checks.

Note: This does not change how you level up in-game. This is for AP checks only.

Ignored when Class Selection is Off.

options.label: Start With Class
options.description:
Where your first Progressive <Class> Level is placed.

Early: Sphere 1, any world's locations.
Local Early: Sphere 1, only on this slot's locations.
Start With: Start with the first class level already unlocked.

Ignored when Class Selection is Off.

options.label: Excluded Skills
options.description:
Exclude specific skills from the class system.

Set a skill to 1 (or any non-zero #) to exclude it (it will not generate checks).

Only affects major skills for your selected class.
Example: If you're an Acrobat and exclude Acrobatics and Sneak, 
you'll only get checks for your remaining 5 major skills.

Ignored when Class Selection is Off.

options.label: Extra Gate Keys
options.description:
Additional Oblivion Gate Keys beyond the base amount needed.

Adds extra Gate Keys to the item pool beyond the base number, which is equal to the number of gates. 
Useful for increased routing flexibility and redundancy in case of hard to reach checks.

options.label: Extra Nirnroot
options.description:
Additional Nirnroot multiworld items beyond the Nirnroot Count setting.

Provides a buffer so you don't need to find every single Nirnroot location check.
This adds extra Nirnroot items to the multiworld item pool.

Only relevant when Goal is Nirnsanity. Ignored for other goals.

options.label: Oblivion Gate Vision
options.description:
Determines how Oblivion Gate map markers are visible:

On: Gate markers are visible immediately
Off: Gate markers must be found (vanilla behavior)
Item: Gate markers become visible when you find the Oblivion Gate Vision item (default)

Ignored when Gate Count is 0.

options.label: Free Shrine Offerings
options.description:
When true: Daedric Shrine offering items are automatically provided when needed.
When false: You must find or obtain shrine offerings yourself in the game.

options.label: Fast Travel Item
options.description:
Locks the fast travel system behind an Archipelago item.

When true: You cannot use fast travel until you receive the "Fast Travel" item from the multiworld.
When false: Fast travel is available from the start (vanilla behavior).

Warning: Fast Travel item can be anywhere in the seed, including late locations.

options.label: Dungeon Marker Mode
options.description:
Controls how dungeon map markers appear on your map.

Reveal and Fast Travel: All selected dungeon locations are revealed on the map immediately and can be fast traveled to (if Fast Travel Item allows).
Reveal Only: Dungeon locations appear as "rumors" (grayed out markers) - you can see them but must physically travel there first.

Note: This setting only affects dungeon map markers, not the overall fast travel system.

options.label: Dungeon Warp
options.description:
Automatically warp the player out to the overworld when completing a seeded dungeon.

Off: No warp (vanilla behavior)
On: All dungeons that provide a check offer a warp-out option upon completion
Item: Warp functionality unlocked when you receive the "Dungeon Warp" item from the multiworld
Early Item: Same as Item, but the Dungeon Warp item is forced into early locations

options.label: Shop Scout Type
options.description:
How shop item scouting displays information.

Off: No shop scouting - shop tab will not display any information
Summary: Shows the receiving player name and item classification (Progression/Useful/Filler) - default
Player Only: Shows only the receiving player name for each shop item
Full Info: Shows the complete item name and receiving player (creates !hint commands)

Note: Trap items are always disguised in Summary mode.

options.label: Fast Arena
options.description:
When true: Skip arena announcer dialogue before matches and fight immediately.
When false: Must wait for announcer dialogue before match begins (default).

options.label: Auto Tracking
options.description:
This feature enables auto-tracking for Nirnroot and Boss Chests.

When true: Guides the player to any nearby Nirnroot or Boss Chest(if included in seed). 
Entering the overworld switches to Nirnroot tracking. Entering a
dungeon switches to Boss Chest tracking.

Note: F11 can be used to manually cycle the mode or disable the feature.

options.label: Silent Auto-Tracking
options.description:
When enabled, auto-tracking updates the in-game quest marker silently -
no guidance via Message is shown. Cuts down on notifications in the Message queue.

When disabled (default), compass direction is shown via Message 
whenever the tracked target changes. 
Note: The polarity of the message is incorrect in some dungeons.

options.label: In-Game AP Tips
options.description:
Enable Archipelago tips? These will provide extra guidance on how to complete checks.
This is recommended if you are unfamiliar with Archipelago or if you prefer a more guided experience.

options.label: Skill Leveling Speed
options.description: Skill XP multiplier. 1 is vanilla. 2 is double speed, 3 is triple speed, etc.

options.label: Trap Percentage
options.description:
Percentage of filler item slots replaced by traps (0-20%). Set to 0 to disable traps entirely.
Trap types and their relative frequency are controlled by the weight settings below.

options.label: Movement Trap Weight
options.description:
Relative weight for Movement Trap. Set to 0 to disable this trap type.
By default, 55% of traps will be Movement Traps.

options.label: Spawn Trap Weight
options.description:
Relative weight for Spawn Trap. Set to 0 to disable this trap type.
By default, 30% of traps will be Spawn Traps.

options.label: Storm Trap Weight
options.description:
Relative weight for Storm Trap. Set to 0 to disable this trap type.
By default, 10% of traps will be Storm Traps.

options.label: Wanted Trap Weight
options.description:
Relative weight for Wanted Trap. Set to 0 to disable this trap type.
By default, 5% of traps will be Wanted Traps.

options.label: Starting Item
options.description:
Randomize what weapon you start the game with.
vanilla: Start with the Bomb Glove.
random_same: Start with a random weapon.
random_item: Start with any random equipable item, weapons or gadgets.

options.label: Shuffle Starting Planet
options.description: Randomize what Planet you start on

options.label: Shuffle Weapons
options.description:
Randomize Weapon locations
vanilla: Weapons are unshuffled.
random_same: Weapons are shuffled to other Weapon locations.
random_item: Weapons are shuffled anywhere, useful items are found at Weapon locations.
unrestricted: Weapons are shuffled anywhere, anything can be found at Weapon locations.

options.label: Shuffle Gadgets
options.description:
Randomize Gadget locations
vanilla: Gadgets are unshuffled.
random_same: Gadgets are shuffled to other Gadget locations.
random_item: Gadgets are shuffled anywhere, useful items are found at Gadget locations.
unrestricted: Gadgets are shuffled anywhere, anything can be found at Gadget locations.

options.label: Shuffle Packs
options.description:
Randomize Pack locations
vanilla: Packs are unshuffled.
random_same: Packs are shuffled to other Pack locations.
random_item: Packs are shuffled anywhere, useful items are found at Pack locations.
unrestricted: Packs are shuffled anywhere, anything can be found at Pack locations.

options.label: Shuffle Helmets
options.description:
Randomize Helmet locations
vanilla: Helmets are unshuffled.
random_same: Helmets are shuffled to other Helmet locations.
random_item: Helmets are shuffled anywhere, useful items are found at Helmet locations.
unrestricted: Helmets are shuffled anywhere, anything can be found at Helmet locations.

options.label: Shuffle Boots
options.description:
Randomize Boot locations
vanilla: Boots are unshuffled.
random_same: Boots are shuffled to other Boot locations.
random_item: Boots are shuffled anywhere, useful items are found at Boot locations.
unrestricted: Boots are shuffled anywhere, anything can be found at Boot locations.

options.label: Shuffle Extra Items
options.description:
Randomize Extra Item locations (Hoverboard, Persuader, etc...)
vanilla: Extra Items are unshuffled.
random_same: Extra Items are shuffled to other Extra Item locations.
random_item: Extra Items are shuffled anywhere, useful items are found at Extra Item locations.
unrestricted: Extra Items are shuffled anywhere, anything can be found at Extra Item locations.

options.label: Shuffle Gold Bolts
options.description: Randomize Gold Bolt locations

options.label: Shuffle Infobots
options.description:
Randomize Infobot locations
vanilla: Infobots are unshuffled.
random_same: Infobots are shuffled to other Infobot locations.
random_item: Infobots are shuffled anywhere, useful items are found at Infobot locations.
WARNING! Using random_same, or random_item with no other pool selected, is likely to fail on solo worlds.
unrestricted: Infobots are shuffled anywhere, anything can be found at Infobot locations.

options.label: Shuffle Gold Weapons
options.description:
Randomize Gold Weapon locations
vanilla: Gold Weapons are unshuffled.
random_same: Gold Weapons are shuffled to other Gold Weapon locations.
random_item: Gold Weapons are shuffled anywhere, useful items are found at Gold Weapon locations.
unrestricted: Gold Weapons are shuffled anywhere, anything can be found at Gold Weapon locations.

options.label: Gold Bolt Pack Size
