options.label: Goal
options.description:
Determines the goal of the slot. Some goals are specific to certain campaigns
Options starting with "Castle" are played in the Castle Hammerwatch campaign, while "Temple" options are played in the Temple of the Sun Campaign
Castle All Bosses: Defeat all the bosses in Castle Hammerwatch. Escaping is NOT required
Castle Escape: Find at least 12 Strange Planks, defeat Worldfire, and escape with your life
Castle Plank Hunt: Find a certain number of Strange Planks in Castle Hammerwatch
Temple All Bosses: Defeat all the bosses in the Temple of the Sun
Temple Plank Hunt: Find a certain number of Strange Planks in the Temple of the Sun
Temple Pyramid of Fear: Unlock and complete the Pyramid of Fear
See the game info page on where to go after collecting all required planks in the Plank Hunt goal modes

options.label: Plank Hunt Requirement
options.description: Determines the amount of Strange Planks required to win the game for the Plank Hunt goals

options.label: Extra Plank Percentage
options.description:
Determines the percentage of extra Strange Planks in the item pool
For the Castle Escape goal, the required planks count is 12
For the Plank Hunt goals, the required planks count is determined by the Plank Hunt Requirement setting

options.label: Difficulty
options.description: What difficulty the game will be played on

options.label: Exit Randomization
options.description:
Randomizes where level exits/portals lead. Use the /t command in-game to return to the start if you get stuck!
No Boss Exits: exits to boss levels will not be shuffled
All: all exits including bosses will be shuffled
WARNING: This option has a moderate chance of causing generation to fail, use at your own risk!

options.label: ER Act Connection Range
options.description:
Determines the maximum number of acts away levels will try to be connected to each other in exit randomization
For example with an act range of 1 Prison exits will mostly only connect to other Prison exits or Armory exits

options.label: Randomize Start Location
options.description:
If Exit Randomization is on, you will start the game at a random exit determined by the Start Location Act option
Use the /t command in game to return if you get stuck!

options.label: Start Location Act
options.description: Determines the act in which you start if Randomize Start Location is on

options.label: Gate Shuffle
options.description: Shuffles whether gates are bronze, silver, or gold

options.label: Shop Location Shuffle
options.description: Shuffles the shops around so that they may be different from their normal locations

options.label: Shuffle Shop Upgrade Categories
options.description:
Shuffles the shop upgrades between different categories of shops
Group: upgrades sharing the same base name (Damage 1, 2, 3, etc.) are shuffled together in the same category
All: upgrades are shuffled amongst all categories, regardless of prerequisites

options.label: Minimum Shop Cost Percent
options.description: The lowest percent each shop upgrade cost can be multiplied by

options.label: Maximum Shop Cost Percent
options.description: The highest percent each shop upgrade cost can be multiplied by

options.label: Shopsanity Player 1 Class
options.description:
Adds shop upgrades of this player's class to the item pool and enables items to appear in their shop
All members of the same class will receive their upgrades together and will have the same items in their shops
WARNING: there is normally not enough gold to purchase all upgrades.
It is strongly recommended to reduce the costs of shop items so you will not have to grind excessively for gold!
WARNING #2: there is no extra logic for shop upgrades!
This means you could get into a situation where you are required to play much of your game with no upgrades.
Consider making shop upgrades local if you're playing in a larger multiworld

options.label: Shopsanity Player 2 Class
options.description:
Adds shop upgrades of this player's class to the item pool and enables items to appear in their shop
All members of the same class will receive their upgrades together and will have the same items in their shops
WARNING: see the warnings in the Shopsanity Player 1 Class option!

options.label: Shopsanity Player 3 Class
options.description:
Adds shop upgrades of this player's class to the item pool and enables items to appear in their shop
All members of the same class will receive their upgrades together and will have the same items in their shops
WARNING: see the warnings in the Shopsanity Player 1 Class option!

options.label: Shopsanity Player 4 Class
options.description:
Adds shop upgrades of this player's class to the item pool and enables items to appear in their shop
All members of the same class will receive their upgrades together and will have the same items in their shops
WARNING: see the warnings in the Shopsanity Player 1 Class option!

options.label: Shopsanity Obfuscation
options.description:
Cause the names and descriptions of trap items in shops to mimic another item in the world of the receiving player
On: trap names/descriptions will mimic another item
Imperfect: trap names/descriptions will mimic another item, but with subtle changes in letters/punctuation
L33T: 7r4p n4m35/d35cr1p710n5 w1ll b3 1n 4ll l3375p34k
OwO: twap names/descwiptions wiww be in aww owo
All Mystery: instead hides ALL item names/descriptions, so none of the items will be known!

options.label: Balance Shopsanity Costs
options.description:
Reduces the costs of items in shops based on their classifications
If the item is not progression it will cost 50% as much, and filler items will cost 10% as much

options.label: Shopsanity Base Upgrade Assist
options.description:
Various methods to make base shop upgrades more accessible
Duplicate Base Upgrades: add an extra copy of each base upgrade to the item pool
Swap Base Upgrades: swap base upgrades with the earliest version of its sub upgrade so you should find base upgrades first
only considers Hammerwatch locations
Swap Base Upgrades Experimental: like Swap Base Upgrades, but will swap with locations in ANY game. This may cause issues with other apworlds!

options.label: Enemy Shuffle Mode
options.description:
Shuffles the locations of enemies, spawners, mini-bosses, and towers in each level
Individual: enemies will be shuffled individually regardless of type, keeping the same ratios as vanilla
Type: converts all enemies of a single type into another. For example all tier 1 bats can become tier 1 beetles
Chaos: enemies will be shuffled individually regardless of type or ratio

options.label: Enemy Shuffle Act Range
options.description:
How many acts away enemies can be shuffled to
When set to 0 only enemies in the same act will be shuffled
When set to 3 enemies can be shuffled to any act

options.label: Enemy Shuffle Keep Tier
options.description: If Enemy Shuffle is on, only shuffles enemies of the same tier amongst each other

options.label: Bonus Level Location Behavior
options.description:
Determines how bonus chest locations in bonus levels are handled
None: Don't include any bonus chest items/locations
Necessary: Include bonus level locations for any extra items in the pool
All: Include all bonus chest items/locations. Extra items will replace filler items as normal

options.label: Randomize Bonus Keys
options.description: Whether bonus keys are shuffled into the pool

options.label: Remove Extra Lives
options.description:
Removes extra lives (Ankhs) from the item pool and replaces them with filler.
Recommended to have enabled when playing with the infinite_lives or no_extra_lives modifiers

options.label: Randomize Recovery Items
options.description: Whether recovery items (such as apples and mana crystals) are shuffled into the pool

options.label: Randomize Temple Random Secrets
options.description: (TotS only) Whether items from random secrets (small rooms with cracked walls in the cave levels) are shuffled into the item pool

options.label: Randomize Peg Puzzles
options.description: Whether items from peg puzzles are shuffled into the item pool

options.label: Randomize Major Enemy Loot
options.description:
Whether items dropped by minibosses and towers are shuffled into the item pool
On: major enemy loot locations will exist using the vanilla loot drop chances
All: forces all major enemy loot locations to exist and have items

options.label: Buttonsanity
options.description:
Whether the effects of buttons and switches are shuffled into the item pool
Normal: button/switch effects are turned into locations, so completing a button sequence or puzzle is one location
Insanity: all buttons/switches will be locations, regardless if the button would do anything by itself or not

options.label: Open Castle Portals
options.description:
(Castle only) Starts the game with the specified number of portals open in the hub
This starts with the prison portal and goes up to the chambers portal

options.label: Key Mode
options.description:
Changes the behavior of how keys interact with gates
Generic: keys can be used anywhere on their respective gates (WARNING: can cause generation failures!)
Act Specific: (castle only) replaces keys with versions that can only be used in a specific act
Floor Master: consolidates keys on a floor into a single item that unlocks all gates of that type on an entire floor

options.label: Extra Keys Percent
options.description: Determines the percentage of extra silver and gold keys (and mirrors in the TotS campaign) that are added to the item pool

options.label: Big Bronze Key Conversion Percent
options.description: (Castle only) What percentage of bronze keys get converted into big bronze keys, which act as 3 bronze keys each

options.label: Enable Castle Shortcut Portal
options.description:
(Castle only) Enables the use of the shortcut portal at the beginning of the game. This allows early access
to Prison Floor 3 before the bronze gate, preventing a potential early BK
A return portal will also be placed so that the first two floors can be fully completed

options.label: Portal Accessibility
options.description:
(TotS only) Ensures rune keys will be placed locally on the floor they would normally appear so that hub portals
are more easily accessible

options.label: Disable Sunbeam Damage
options.description: (TotS only) Disables sunbeam damage, removing much of the long and awkward backtracking inside the temple

options.label: Treasure Shuffle
options.description: Shuffles the locations of minor treasure such as coins, crates, pots, and vegetation

options.label: Pan Fragments
options.description:
(TotS only) If greater than 1 separates the pan into multiple fragments
All fragments must be collected in order to purchase from the consumables merchant

options.label: Split Pumps Lever Mode
options.description:
(TotS only) Determines if/how the pumps lever is split into multiple items
If 0 or 'per_level' the pumps lever will be split into 3 items that only lower the water on a specific cave level
If greater than 1 separates the pumps lever into multiple fragments
All fragments must be collected in order to turn on all the pumps

options.label: Starting Life Count

infinite_lives, hp_regen, double_damage, double_lives, and 5x_mana_regen

options.label: Basic Research Location Count
options.description: The number of basic research locations in the game. These will only require the basic research bench.

options.label: Hi-Tech Research Location Count
options.description: The number of hi-tech research locations in the game. These will only require the hi-tech research bench (which requires Microelectronics.)

options.label: Multi-Analyzer Research Location Count
options.description: The number of multi-analyzer research locations in the game. These will only require the hi-tech research bench and the multi-analyzer (and the research for them.)

options.label: Research Base Cost
options.description: The amount of research points required to research research locations.

options.label: Research Cost Variance
options.description:
The max amount research points will vary by for research locations.
If the base cost is 500 and the variance is 800, every research will cost between 500 and 1300 points.

options.label: Research Cost Increase Per Tier
options.description:
The amount of points that will increase per research tier.
For example, if the base cost is 500, the variance is 800, and the Increase Per Tier is 100, a third-tier (third column) research will be
between 700 and 1500 points.

options.label: Research Max Prerequisites
options.description: The max number of prerequisites for the generated Archipelago research. The higher this is, the more restricted your selection of research will be.

options.label: Craft Location Count
options.description: The number of craft locations in the game. These locations require crafting two random items together.

options.label: Raid Location Count
options.description: The number of raid locations in the game. These locations require defeating a target enemy, one of which will carry a location item in its inventory in each raid.

options.label: Trade Location Count
options.description: The number of trade locations in the game. These locations require trading with a caravan or settlement for a location item.

options.label: Quest Location Count
options.description: The number of quest locations in the game. These locations require completing a quest for a location item.

options.label: Raid Trap Count
options.description: The guaranteed number of raid traps in the game.

options.label: Colonist Item Count
options.description: The number of colonists that will get sent as items in the game. Note: If you wind up with more than ~20 colonists, you may have performance issues.

options.label: Use Player Names for Colonist Items
options.description: If enabled, random player names from the multiworld will be used for colonist nicknames

options.label: Craft Location Count
options.description: The chance random filler will become trap items, like raids.

options.label: Victory Condition
options.description: The way to win. Choosing "any" will ensure one of these is considered "in-logic." They also require a "basic" set of research that isn't strictly required to win, so royalty will consider pianos and noble apparel in logic, while anomaly will consider basic bioferrite research in logic. The monument victory condition will require building a room with special archipelago statues and some number of randomized room conditions.

options.label: Monument Statue Count
options.description: If the monument victory condition is enabled, this specifies how many Archipelago statues will be required to create a monument and win the game.

options.label: Extra Monument Statue Count
options.description: If the monument victory condition is enabled, this specifies how many extra monument statues will be in the pool, allowing the player an easier victory.

options.label: Monument Other Building Requirement Count
options.description: If the monument victory condition is enabled, this specifies how many non-statue building requirements will be required to create a monument and win the game.

options.label: Monumentwealthrequirement

options.label: Royalty Enabled
options.description: Enable the Royalty DLC. If you disable any DLC in yaml and enable it in client, all research will be researchable and excluded from the generator.

options.label: Ideology Enabled
options.description: Enable the Ideology DLC. If you disable any DLC in yaml and enable it in client, all research will be researchable and excluded from the generator.

options.label: Biotech Enabled
options.description: Enable the Biotech DLC. If you disable any DLC in yaml and enable it in client, all research will be researchable and excluded from the generator.

options.label: Anomoly Enabled
options.description: Enable the Anomaly DLC. If you disable any DLC in yaml and enable it in client, all research will be researchable and excluded from the generator.

options.label: Odyssey Enabled
options.description: Enable the Odyssey DLC. If you disable any DLC in yaml and enable it in client, all research will be researchable and excluded from the generator.

options.label: Starting Research Level
options.description: If "none" is selected, the player will have access to NO research, regardless of starting scenario. Tribal and Crashlanded will give the player those starting research (regardless of starting scenario.)

options.label: Bonus Research Items
options.description: How many bonus items will you receive when a research (that unlocks items) is received. For example, if this is set to 2, you may receive a jacket and a flophat when you receive Complex Clothing. If set to -1, you'll receive one of everything, otherwise, you'll receive any number at random (note: This means setting it to higher than 1 may result in getting, say, 5 Harps when you receive Harp.)

options.label: Researchscouttype
options.description: How research project scouting works - this will show you what items research projects will send. "None" will show no information for all research. "Summary" options will show the player name and item type (Chris's progressive item). "Fullitem" options will show player name and item name (Chris's progressive item, Master Sword). "Available" options will show only if the research can be started now. "All" options will hint all research.

options.label: Researchscoutsecrettraps
options.description: If turned on, the game will lie about scouted trap items. If the scout type shows the player and item name, all traps will be replaced by a random progression item from another player (instead of showing Alex's freeze trap, it will show Chris's Master Sword.) If the scout type only shows item type, it will simply show traps as progression items.

options.label: Neolithic Item Weight
options.description: How likely it will be that low/no-tech items are chosen for crafting locations. Higher weights make this category more likely. 0 will exempt it from the list. Note that these categories are slightly different than the vanilla "Tech Level," to help account for how challenging they are to craft.

options.label: Medieval Item Weight
options.description: How likely it will be that low-tech items are chosen for crafting locations. Higher weights make this category more likely. 0 will exempt it from the list. Note that these categories are slightly different than the vanilla "Tech Level," to help account for how challenging they are to craft.

options.label: Industrial Item Weight
options.description: How likely it will be that mid-tech items are chosen for crafting locations. Higher weights make this category more likely. 0 will exempt it from the list. Note that these categories are slightly different than the vanilla "Tech Level," to help account for how challenging they are to craft.

options.label: Spacer Item Weight
options.description: How likely it will be that high-tech items are chosen for crafting locations. Higher weights make this category more likely. 0 will exempt it from the list. Note that these categories are slightly different than the vanilla "Tech Level," to help account for how challenging they are to craft.

options.label: Hard To Make Item Weight
options.description: How likely it will be that complicated items are chosen for crafting locations. These items usually require specific/unique investment, like multiple advanced components and the like. Higher weights make this category more likely. 0 will exempt it from the list. Note that these categories are slightly different than the vanilla "Tech Level," to help account for how challenging they are to craft.

options.label: Anomaly Item Weight
options.description: How likely it will be that Anomaly-specific items are chosen for crafting locations. These items will often require bioferrite, and investment into the anomaly expansion to craft. Higher weights make this category more likely. 0 will exempt it from the list. Note that these categories are slightly different than the vanilla "Tech Level," to help account for how challenging they are to craft.

options.label: Area Unlock Mode
options.description:
In RTA AP, in order to interact with anything in a town (enter houses, talk to cars, etc.), you must unlock the town first.

In **Decorations** mode, you must obtain one of the garage decorations associated with that town to unlock it.
Every town has 2. (A couple of towns lacking garage decorations use wallpapers instead.)

In **Stamps** mode, 100 stamp items are added into the pool. Every 5 stamp items you get unlocks the next town.

options.label: Remove Double-Up Stamps
options.description:
If using Decorations mode, enable this to combine NPC rewards and stamps that are received back-to-back into one location (e.g. Stamp 2, and many many others). 
Applies to roughly half of the stamps in the game.

This cannot be enabled in Stamps mode, as it would bring the number of locations well below the number of items.

options.label: Additional Progressive Part Tracks
options.description:
Add additional progressive part tracks to the item pool. Defaults to 2, one for each of your teammates.

These parts can also be used by you, or just sold for money at the Recycle Shop.

Leaving this at 2 is recommended for Decorations mode.
In Stamps mode, lowering this to 1 is worth considering. When set to 2 in Stamps mode, most cosmetic/filler items (horns, meters, etc.) will have to be removed from the item pool in order to make enough space. (If this is fine, leave at 2.)
Setting to 0 is not recommended, as it makes finding part upgrades a bit rare.

options.label: Prioritize Good Rewards for Races
options.description:
Set the percent chance that a race will be forced to have a Progression item. (Rolled separately for each race.)

Before items are placed, a random number between 1 and 100 is rolled for each race.
If the number is equal to or below the value selected here, the item will be guaranteed to be Progression.
This provides more incentive to complete races, which require more skill and time than most stamps.

Since this is rolled for *each* race, it is not a guarantee that a certain percentage of races will have Progression items - just that on average, they will.

options.label: Prioritize Good Rewards for Minigames
options.description:
Set the percent chance that a minigame will be forced to have a progression item. (Rolled separately for each minigame.)

Works the same way as the setting for races.

Several minigames are not included due to lack of a meaningful challenge (notably Q's Rally, fishing, and the Figure 8 courses, since none of these have time limits).

options.label: License Handling
options.description:
Set how license items/locations should be handled.
Standard: Licenses are awarded via Progressive License items found in the multiworld. License completions are locations.
Vanilla: Force the license unlock items to be in their vanilla locations. (e.g. a Progressive License will always be found at Rank C completion, etc.)
Remove: Start with all licenses. License completions are *not* locations.

options.label: Parts Cost Modifier
options.description:
Set a percentage modifier for the cost of parts.

If set to 0, all parts will be free.

options.label: Parts Cost Maximum
options.description:
Set the maximum cost for a part. 

This maximum is applied *after* the percentage modifier above.

If set to -1 (default), no maximum will be applied.
If set to 0, all parts will be free.

options.label: Auto Unlock Warps
options.description: Automatically unlock the ability to warp to a town's Q's Factory when you gain access to it.

options.label: Randomize Q Coins
options.description:
Randomize the 100 Q Coins into the multiworld.

Picking up a Q Coin will send out a randomized item instead.

options.label: Q Coins Needed Per Coine Reward
options.description:
Set the number of Q coins needed to reach the next reward from Coine in My City.

In the vanilla game, Coine gives one reward per 10 coins. (10 rewards * 10 coins per reward = 100 coins total)

Reduce this number to speed up the process of receiving rewards from Coine, and to lower the total number of coins
needed to collect all rewards.

e.g. If set to 2, Coine will give a reward for every other coin, with a maximum of 20 needed to get all 10 rewards.

If 'Randomize Q Coins' is enabled, all coins beyond those needed to receive all 10 rewards will be classified as Filler.

options.label: Require World Grand Prix
options.description:
Require the World Grand Prix to be completed before the president's mansion can be entered.

Setting this to False will cause the mansion gate to open automatically once all Progressive
Licenses are obtained.

If this option is set to False, and License Handling is set to 'Remove', the mansion can be entered
immediately once Cloud Hill can be accessed.

options.label: Money Filler Amount
options.description:
In Road Trip AP, any additional locations without an item are filled with money.

Set the amount of money received from one of these filler items.

options.label: DeathLink
options.description:
Determines DeathLink behavior.

disabled: Disabled.
Shielded: The Butterfly Jar will protect you from a received DeathLink death, if you have it.
Enabled: Enabled without shielding.

options.label: DeathLink Amnesty
options.description:
If DeathLink is enabled, this option decides how many in-game deaths need to occur before a DeathLink
death is sent out to the multiworld. The game mod tracks your deaths on the pause menu's box labeled "DL:".

options.label: Logging Level
options.description:
Choose how much Spyro AHT generation information should be logged.
The log will contain messages from all levels up to, and including, your choice. For example, "medium" will log low
and medium messages, but not high or maximum messages. **Warning messages stemming from YAML issues are always logged.**

None: No additional logging beyond warnings.
Low: Logs notable generation steps, such as "Checking if any minigames need vanilla rewards forced."
Medium: Logs useful debugging information, such as listing your randomized shop prices. This is the default because
  the information in these messages can be very helpful when making bug reports.
High: Logs messages with extra generation logic, such as "Fire Breath has been placed into Starter Checks: Breath."
Maximum: Logs with extreme detail, such as noting every single item created.

options.label: Auto Corrections
options.description:
Chooses the logging behavior of the generator if YAML issues are encountered. It is recommended to leave this
set to fix_minor, especially if intending to randomize multiple options. Clashes stemming from this (such as having
fireworks_goal on but having firework_checks disabled) are fixed by fix_minor.

halt: Generation will be strictly halted upon any sort of YAML issue.
chaos: The generator will not halt or make changes, even if there is a known problem or high likelihood of generation failing.
fix_minor: Only issues deemed minor will be fixed (such as the above example with fireworks_goal).
fix_major: All issues will be fixed, even if it has a major impact (such as changing your starting realm to avoid an impossible start).

A full, detailed list of every scenario that can lead to a generation issue can be found on the project's wiki,
linked below. auto_corrections is not capable of fixing issues with the base syntax of your YAML.
https://github.com/PhoenixAki/PhoenixAP/wiki/Spyro:-AHT-1.2-%E2%80%90-List-of-auto_corrections-Fixes

options.label: Boss Goals
options.description:
Adds a goal requirement to defeat a number of boss(es). You can enter "Random" to have a random selection
of bosses chosen, even if you also choose a few bosses explicitly alongside "Random".

Note that this + all other goals are based on AHT checks. In specific circumstances, this can result in AHT
registering goals unexpectedly early. See the below project wiki FAQ post for more info.
https://github.com/PhoenixAki/PhoenixAP/wiki/Spyro:-AHT-1-%E2%80%90-Setup-Guide-&-FAQ#i-goaled-early-what-gives 

Valid Options: ["Gnasty Gnorc", "Ineptune", "Red", "Mecha-Red", "Random"]

options.label: Dark Gems Goal
options.description: Adds a goal requirement to complete a number of Dark Gem checks.

options.label: Light Gems Goal
options.description: Adds a goal requirement to complete a number of Light Gem checks.

options.label: Dragon Eggs Goal
options.description: Adds a goal requirement to complete a number of Dragon Egg checks.

options.label: Fireworks Goal

Keep in mind that the first randomized shop item is always free.

options.label: Locked Chests Goal

options.description:
The checks for dragon_eggs_goal and light_gems_goal include locked chests which contain Dragon Eggs/Light Gems.
This option lets you limit them to only Dragon Eggs and Light Gems from non-chest sources.

options.description:
Adds a goal requirement to talk to a number of elder dragons. You can enter "Random" to have a random selection
of elders chosen, even if you also choose a few elders explicitly alongside "Random".

Valid Options: ["Elder Tomas", "Elder Magnus", "Elder Titan", "Elder Astor", "Random"]

options.label: Minigames Goal
options.description:
Adds a goal requirement to complete minigames. Next to each, you can enter any of the following:
- 0-8: complete this many to goal.
- random-on: picks a random number from 1-8.
- random-off: 1/2 chance of 0, 1/2 chance of 1-8.

options.label: Open World Mode
options.description:
In vanilla AHT, you can only teleport to a remote shop pad once you have physically reached it.
open_world_mode lets you choose from a variety of new ways to unlock shop pads through Archipelago items.
Any choice besides 'vanilla' requires enabling "Teleport Across Realms" in time_savers to prevent potential softlock scenarios.

vanilla: Vanilla game behavior.
full: All shop pads are unlocked from the start of the seed.
randomized: Shop pads unlock individually e.g. "Dark Mine - Miner's Drop Shop Unlock".
progressive_levels: Shop pads unlock per-level in vanilla game order e.g. "Progressive Crocovile Swamp Shop Unlock". 
reverse_progressive_levels: Same as progressive_levels, but backwards vanilla order.
full_level: All shop pads in a level will unlock at once e.g. "Sunken Ruins - Shop Unlock".
full_realm: All shop pads in a realm will unlock at once e.g. "Icy Wilderness - Shop Unlock".

options.label: Firework Checks
options.description: Enables 22 checks for flaming fireworks.

options.label: Vanilla Minigame Rewards
options.description:
Places Dragon Egg and Light Gem rewards into minigame checks.

Valid options: ["Sgt. Byrd", "Blink", "Turret", "Sparx"]

options.label: Trap Percentage
options.description: Decides how much of the junk (fillers + traps) item pool will be traps, as a percentage out of 100.

options.label: Filler Items
options.description:
Choose which categories of filler (neutral-to-positive effect) items to enable.

Dragon Eggs: These are filler due to having no logical impact.
Breath Bombs: Fire, Electric, Water, and Ice Bombs. Only usable if their respective breath is unlocked.
Gem Packs: Gives a random amount of gems (400-600, 800-1200 if you have double gems).
    It is advised to disable these if using shop_randomization, as shop logic does not account for gem packs.
Shinies: Items which do nothing, but have humorous names referencing AHT or other games/series.

Valid options: ["Dragon Eggs", "Breath Bombs", "Gem Packs", "Shinies"]

options.label: Trap Items
options.description:
Choose which trap (neutral-to-negative effect) items to enable. Spam Call, Reverse Controls, and Bounce are
queued and triggered sequentially. Traps received while offline will get processed upon next client reconnection.

Spam Call: Random lines of Moneybags dialog + shop music will play for trap_length seconds.
Reverse Controls: Flips the X and Y axis of both control sticks for trap_length seconds.
Damage Sparx: Take 1 hit of damage. Does nothing if Sparxless or if in a Sparx minigame.
Gem Tax: Takes away a random amount of gems (500-1000).
  It is advised to disable these if using shop_randomization, as shop logic does not account for gem taxes.
Bounce: The player character's model will bounce for trap_length seconds. Can negatively affect first-person camera aiming.

Valid options: ["Spam Call", "Reverse Controls", "Damage Sparx", "Gem Tax", "Bounce"]

options.label: Trap Length
options.description: Determines how long Spam Call, Reverse Controls, and Bounce run for, in seconds.

options.label: Starting Breaths
options.description:
Choose which breath(s) you want to start with.

If multiple are listed, one will go into "Starter Checks: Breath", and the rest will go into your start inventory.
"None" will place a random Archipelago item into "Starter Checks: Breath".
If the list is left empty, 1 random breath will be chosen.

Valid Options: ["Fire Breath", "Electric Breath", "Water Breath", "Ice Breath", "None"]

options.label: Movement Randomization
options.description:
Choose whether to randomize each of the 3 base movement abilities (glide, swim, and charge).
If any are randomized, you will start with a random item from Archipelago in their place.

Valid Options: ["Glide", "Swim", "Charge"]

options.label: Starting Realms
options.description:
Choose which realm(s) to start with realm access cards for. 

If the list is left empty, 1 random realm will be chosen.
If using full open_world_mode, you will start with all 4 access cards.
If using non-full open_world_mode, non-starting realms are unlocked via shop unlocks instead of access cards.
    
Starting with only Icy Wilderness, shop_randomization off, and movement_randomization empty is disallowed due to impossible starts.

Valid Options: ["Dragon Kingdom", "Lost Cities", "Icy Wilderness", "Volcanic Isle"]

options.label: Shop Randomization
options.description:
Choose whether to randomize Moneybags' shop. If not randomized, it will function identically to the vanilla game. 

If randomized, vanilla game shop items will be replaced with items from Archipelago. This has a few consequences:
    - Double Gems, if enabled, is permanent once received, as is the Butterfly Jar (it replenishes on death).
    - There is no limit to how many lockpicks or breath bombs you can hold at once.
    - Remote shop pads will not upcharge you for items.

options.label: Key Rings
options.description:
Choose whether your shop will have lockpicks or key rings which open all locked chests in a level.

If shop_randomization is off, they will be placed in the shop. Chests will be in logic as soon as you have access to them.
If shop_randomization is on, they will be placed into the world by Archipelago. Chests will be in logic as you collect each
  key ring, or once you collect all 52 lockpicks.

options.label: Shop Item Count
options.description: Determines how many shop items checks you will have, if shop_randomization is on.

options.label: Shop Logic
options.description:
When using shop_randomization, how many gems you have access to is tracked. This is used to logically spread out shop item purchases.
The formula below is used to calculate a "base shop price", and your choice here determines item prices using that.
The first item is always free, to prevent restrictive starts (Moneybags offers it as a loss-leader).

unordered: items will have equal prices and can be bought in any order. Logic assumes you will buy them in order left -> right.
ordered: items will be free, but get unlocked at a steadily increasing amount of gems, which enforces the logical order.
 
***********************************FORMULA (for the math nerds)***********************************
blink_gems_total = (20,203 - exclusions) * blink_gems%
non_blink_enemies_total = 16,353 * non_blink_enemies%
other_gems_total = (105,357 - exclusions) * other_gems%
  If a minigame check is added to exclude_locations, its gems are excluded from logic.
gem_total = blink_gems_total + non_blink_enemies_total + other_gems_total
base_shop_price = gem_total / (shop_item_count - 1)

If shop_logic is unordered, shop items will all cost base_shop_price, rounded down as needed.
If shop_logic is ordered, shop items will cost base_shop_price * 1, base_shop_price * 2, etc., rounded down as needed.
**************************************************************************************************

options.label: Blink Gems
options.description:
Decides what % of gems from Blink minigames you want to be expected to collect, if shop_randomization is enabled.
For example, a value of 50 means being expected to collect approximately 50% of such gems.

options.label: Non-Blink Enemies
options.description:
Decides what % of gems from enemies you want to be expected to collect, if shop_randomization is enabled.
Only applies to enemies in Spyro & Hunter levels.

options.label: Other Gems
options.description:
Decides what % of gems you want to be expected to collect from gems on the ground, breakable containers, and
Sgt. Byrd + Sparx minigames, if shop_randomization is enabled.

options.label: Double Gems
options.description:
Enables or disables the Double Gems item, if shop_randomization is enabled. It is advised to keep this disabled if so,
as shop logic does not account for gems received through Double Gems.

options.label: Randomize Boss Lair Requirements
options.description:
Determines the Dark Gem cost for each boss lair.

default: Each boss lair has their vanilla cost (10/20/30/40).
randomized: Randomly pick costs in the range defined by boss_lair_door_cost_min and boss_lair_door_cost_max.
shuffle: Vanilla boss lair costs are shuffled between each other (still 10/20/30/40 but in a random order).

options.label: Boss Lair Door Cost Minimum
options.description: Minimum cost for boss lairs, if set to randomized. Must be less than or equal to boss_lair_door_cost_max.

options.label: Boss Lair Door Cost Maximum
options.description: Maximum cost for boss lairs, if set to randomized.

options.label: Boss Lair Forcing
options.description:
This option decides if the generator should force boss lair(s) to have the most expensive Dark Gem costs.
Forcing takes place after costs have been decided through the above 3 options.

unchanged: Leaves boss lair costs untouched.
gnasty_gnorc/ineptune/red/mecha_red: Swaps that boss's cost with the highest cost.
automatic: Swaps all goal boss costs so that they are collectively the highest.

options.label: Randomize Light Gem Door Cost
options.description:
Determines the Light Gem cost for each Light Gem door.

default: Each door has their vanilla cost (20/45/70/95).
randomized: Randomly pick costs in the range defined by light_gem_door_cost_min and light_gem_door_cost_max.
  Randomized costs can't exceed 90 if open world mode is set to vanilla.
shuffle: Each door has their vanilla cost shuffled with the others (still 20/45/70/95 but in a random order).

options.label: Minimum Light Gem Door Cost
options.description: Minimum cost for light gem doors, if set to randomized. Must be less than or equal to light_gem_door_cost_max.

options.label: Maximum Light Gem Door Cost
options.description: Maximum cost for light gem doors, if set to randomized.

options.label: Randomize Gadget Cost
options.description:
Determines the Light Gem cost for each gadget. Listed in order of Ball Gadget -> Invincibility -> Supercharge.

default: Each gadget has their vanilla cost (8/24/40).
randomized: Randomly picks costs in the range defined by gadget_cost_min and gadget_cost_max.
  Randomized costs can't exceed 90 if open world mode is set to vanilla.
shuffle: Each gadget has their vanilla cost shuffled with the others (still 8/24/40 but in a random order).

options.label: Minimum Gadget Cost
options.description: Minimum cost for gadgets, if set to randomized. Must be less than or equal to gadget_cost_max.

options.label: Maximum Gadget Cost
options.description: Maximum cost for gadgets, if set to randomized.

options.label: Pause Menu Patch
options.description:
Decides which of 2 pause menu patches you can choose between which can help with escaping situations where you're stuck.

open_shop: pressing Y will open the shop if you are Spyro. If using non-full open_world_mode, this will auto-unlock
  your starting realm's "Depot" shop to prevent potential softlock scenarios.
teleport_to_hub: holding Y will bring you to the current realm's realm teleporter. If using non-full open_world_mode,
  this will be considered a valid alternative way to logically access a realm's hub level.

options.label: Shop Pad Proximity Activation
options.description:
When using non-full open_world_mode, shop pads only unlock via their unlock items. This can lead to situations where you
can physically reach a shop pad but be unable to teleport back to it after, adding walking time on revisits. Enabling this
allows you to teleport to any shop you've interacted with, even if you don't have its unlock item yet.

options.label: Auto Hinting
options.description:
Toggles automatic hinting for boss rewards (upon opening their lair), minigames (upon talking to NPCs), and shop
items (upon creating the save file). For each, you can enter "on", "off", or "random".

options.label: Hide Shop Item Names
options.description: Hides the name of randomized shop items (player name is still shown). Hinted shop items will display as normal.

options.label: Easy Bosses
options.description:
Bosses listed below will take triple damage, significantly shortening fights.

Valid options: ["Gnasty Gnorc", "Ineptune", "Red", "Mecha-Red"]

options.label: Time Savers
options.description:
Choose which time-saving quality of life patches are enabled. For each, enter "on", "off", or "random".
Skip Cutscenes: enables skipping most cutscenes with the Y button.
Skip Elevators: enables skipping long elevator waits with loading screen.
Teleport Across Realms: enables teleporting across realms using normal shop pads.

options.label: Cubesanity
options.description: If enabled, each destructible green cube becomes a check.

options.label: Death Link
options.description: When you die by falling out of bounds or touching red/purple blocks, everyone dies. The reverse is also true.

options.label: Death Link Amnesty
options.description: How many deaths it takes to send a Death Link.

options.label: Trap Fill Percentage
options.description: Determine the percentage of junk items in the pool to replace with traps.

options.label: Gravity Direction Trap Weight
options.description: This trap will randomize the direction of your gravity for 2 minutes or until you complete a level.

options.label: Increased Gravity Trap Weight
options.description: This trap will increase the strength of your gravity for 2 minutes or until you complete a level.

to unlock the Great Palace

Regardless of the option chosen, Keys will only be usable in their respective dungeon.

If enabled, you will be logically expected to have the Candle before going inton any caves.
This does not include the Parapa cave, as the original game expects you to traverse this cave
in the dark.

options.label: Cross Logic

If enabled, you will be logically expected to have the Cross before going to Old Kasuto
or Death Valley.

options.label: Remove Magical Key

options.label: Remove Early Boulder

options.label: Better Boots
options.description: If enabled, the water near Saria Town will be changed so that it can be walked on using the Boots.

options.label: Respawn at Palaces
options.description:
If enabled, you will respawn at the current Palace entrance if you continue,
but not if you save and reset. If disabled, this only applies to the Great Palace.

options.label: Fast Great Palace
options.description: If enabled, most of the Great Palace will be skipped.

options.label: Starting Life Level
options.description: What your starting Life level is.

options.label: Starting Magic Level
options.description: What your starting Magic level is.

options.label: Starting Attack Level
options.description: What your starting Attack level is.

options.label: Starting Lives
options.description:
How many lives you will start with upon loading the game.
This value will be permanently increased by one every time you find a
1-Up Doll.

options.label: Encounter Rate

options.label: Keep EXP

options.label: Random Palace Graphics

(ex. "Confodere = 1")

Normal: Villagers are found in their normal locations.
Shuffled: Villagers are shuffled amongst each other
Anywhere: Villagers can be found anywhere.

options.description: Which main Area you start with.

options.label: Remove Training Hall
options.description: If enabled, Training Hall will never be accessible.

options.label: Remove Large Cavern
options.description: If enabled, Large Cavern will never be accessible.

Adds the no-hit Boss chests to the check pool, except for Dracula.
If you fail to get the chest, a portal will spawn in their room that lets you refight them.

Multiplier for the amount of AP given by enemies.

The goal for your game.

Dracula: Defeat Dracula in the throne room.

How many Portraits are required to be cleared to access the underground passage
at the castle entrance.

If enabled, you will be required to fight Brauner before you can access the Throne Room,
Of course, this won't do anything if the goal is set to Brauner.

options.label: Nest of Evil State
options.description:
The state of the Nest of Evil.
Vanilla: Nest of Evil has its original rewards, the two tome pages and Greatest Five.
Randomized: The three items in the Nest of Evil are random, and added to the item pool.

and the Whip's Memory fight will grant you a random item.

Add Nest: Full, but also shuffles the Nest of Evil portrait

options.description: If enabled, all Quests will be unlocked by default.

options.label: Randomized Quests
options.description:
Specify which Quests have random items. 'Preparations' is always included, regardless of settings. Nest of Evil is never included.
You can type any quest name, as well as the following shortcuts:
Requires Item: Any Quest which requires you to turn in an item or set of items (except for Almighty and Great Sage)
Defeat Enemies: Any Quest which requires you to defeat specific enemies.
Mastery: Any Quest which requires you to Master a subweapon.
Simple: Any Quest with no specific requirement other than reaching an area or changing your status.
Grindy: Any Quest with a high grinding requirement. (Includes the Mastery quests.)
All: Enables ALL quests

options.label: Excluded Quests
options.description:
Specify Excluded randomized quests from the above option. Excluded Quests will still be randomized, but will always be your own junk items.
The same shortcuts from the above option apply.

options.label: Randomize Spell Charge Time
options.description: Randomizes the charge time of non-major spells.

options.label: Start with Call Cube
options.description: If enabled, you'll start with the Call Cube by default

options.description:
If enabled, all Boss Doors will be locked until you find its respective Key.
Key names are generally named after the room or area, and can be found on the Doc page.

options.label: Removed Boss Keys

options.label: Randomize Shop Items

Normal: SP requirements are unchanged
