options.label: Goal
options.description:
The win condition for this game.

- labyrinth_open: Open both Grey Labyrinth entrances using Radiant Projectors.
- newbucks: Accumulate a lifetime Newbucks threshold (set by Newbucks Goal Amount).
- prismacore: Complete the main story — stabilize the Prismacore.
- slimepedia: Unlock all Slimepedia entries across your enabled Slimepedia categories
  (Slimes, Resources, and/or Radiant Slimes). At least one category must be enabled.
  The goal fires when every entry in every enabled category is unlocked.
- plort_seller: Sell a set number of plorts of EACH type at the Plort Market
  (amount rolled between Plort Goal Amount Min and Max). All 25 plort types are in
  scope, including the 5 Grey Labyrinth plorts; Gold and Yolky plorts are excluded
  with Exclude RNG-Dependent Slimes, and Dervish and Tangle plorts with Exclude
  Weather-Dependent Checks.
- prisma_shard_hunt: Collect Prisma Shards scattered across the multiworld to unlock the
  Prismacore encounter, then stabilize the core. Winning still means beating the
  Prismacore — the shards only open the door. Gigi refuses to start the fight until you
  hold the required number, even when every other condition is met, and the mod satisfies
  the vanilla prerequisites (Nullifier blueprint, all five Harmonizers) on your behalf once
  you do. Set the count with Prisma Shards Required; Extra Prisma Shards (%) adds spares
  beyond that so the last one is not always the bottleneck.

options.label: Newbucks Goal Amount
options.description:
Lifetime Newbucks required to complete the Newbucks goal.
Uses lifetime total (unaffected by spending), so farming is always progress.
Only relevant when Goal is set to newbucks.

options.label: Plort Goal Amount Min
options.description:
The smallest number of plorts of each type that can be required by the plort_seller
goal. The actual per-seed amount is rolled between Min and Max (set both to the same
value for a fixed goal). If Min is higher than Max, the two values are swapped.
Only relevant when Goal is set to plort_seller.

options.label: Plort Goal Amount Max
options.description:
The largest number of plorts of each type that can be required by the plort_seller
goal. Only relevant when Goal is set to plort_seller.

options.label: Randomize Treasure Pods
options.description: Include the 113 Treasure Pods as location checks.

options.label: Randomize Gordos
options.description:
Include up to 17 static Gordo Slimes as location checks.
14 are always in scope; 3 in the Grey Labyrinth are only included for
the prismacore, prisma_shard_hunt, slimepedia, newbucks, and plort_seller goals
(every goal except labyrinth_open).

options.label: Randomize Map Nodes
options.description:
Include up to 17 Map Data Nodes as location checks.
10 are always in scope; 7 in the Grey Labyrinth are only included for
the prismacore, prisma_shard_hunt, slimepedia, newbucks, and plort_seller goals
(every goal except labyrinth_open).

options.label: Randomize Fabricator
options.description:
Controls what the 38 Fabricator upgrade crafts contain. They are location checks either
way — crafting a Vacpack upgrade sends a check rather than granting the upgrade directly,
and the upgrade arrives through the Archipelago item pool.

on:  Each craft holds a shuffled multiworld item, so an upgrade you craft may go to
     another player and yours may turn up anywhere.
off: Each craft is locked to the upgrade it grants in the vanilla game, so crafting the
     Jetpack gives you the Jetpack. The upgrades never enter the shuffled pool.

27 crafts are always in scope; 11 require Grey Labyrinth access, i.e. every goal except
labyrinth_open.

options.label: Randomize Slimepedia (Slimes)
options.description:
Include the 29 Slimepedia Slimes category entries as location checks.
A 30th entry, "Slimepedia - Radiant Slimes", lives in this category in-game but only
unlocks once you have encountered a radiant slime, so it is added by Randomize
Slimepedia (Radiant Slimes) instead of by this option.

options.label: Randomize Slimepedia (Resources)
options.description:
Include the 54 Slimepedia Resources category entries as location checks.
Covers all food types (veggies, fruits, hens/chicks), craft materials,
and special resources (Moondew Nectar, Snowball, Prisma materials).
A 55th entry, "Slimepedia: Sprinkles", is post-game Sanctuary content and is added
only when Randomize Sanctuary Content is also enabled.

options.label: Randomize Slimepedia (Radiant Slimes)
options.description:
Include the 22 Radiant Slimepedia entries as location checks, plus the
"Slimepedia - Radiant Slimes" overview entry that sits in the Slimes category (23 total).
A Radiant Slime entry is unlocked the first time the player catches a radiant
variant of that slime type. Radiant slimes are rare random world spawns;
use Radiant Spawn Rate Multiplier to increase how often they appear.

options.label: Randomize Research Drones
options.description:
Include 42 Research Drone location checks: 23 main entries (approaching each drone)
plus 19 archive pages (reading the drone's second page, unlocked by the Drone Archive Key).
Every drone has an archive except the 4 in Powderfall Bluffs, which have none.

options.label: Randomize Ghostly Drones
options.description:
Include up to 10 Ghostly Drone location checks.
7 are always in scope; 3 in the Grey Labyrinth are only included for
the prismacore, prisma_shard_hunt, slimepedia, newbucks, and plort_seller goals
(every goal except labyrinth_open).

options.label: Randomize Plort Doors
options.description:
Controls whether the 28 plort doors (PuzzleSlotLockable, lockTag='plort_door') are included
as location checks. These are the coloured plort-locked doors found throughout Ember Valley (4),
Rainbow Fields (1), Starlight Strand (12), and the Grey Labyrinth (11).

The Powderfall Bluffs region gate door is NOT included here — it is handled separately by
the Region Access Mode setting. Grey Labyrinth shadow plort doors (depositor doors) are also
NOT included — those have their own Randomize Shadow Plort Doors setting.

vanilla:   Plort doors work as normal; no location checks are sent.
locations: Filling a plort door sends an Archipelago location check. The door opens normally.

options.label: Randomize Shadow Plort Doors
options.description:
Controls the 25 Grey Labyrinth shadow plort doors (depositor doors fed with Shadow Plorts).

Only relevant when the Grey Labyrinth is in scope — that is, for every goal except
labyrinth_open. On a labyrinth_open seed this setting has no effect either way.

There is deliberately no "vanilla" mode. Several of these are dispensers rather than
doors: they hand out a blueprint, upgrade component, or spawned items on opening, and
those vanilla grants conflict with the same items being randomized into the pool. So the
mod suppresses the vanilla reward in BOTH modes, and the only question is whether the
door is an Archipelago check.

disabled:  Not location checks, and their vanilla rewards are suppressed. Opening a
           shadow door still opens it, but dispenses nothing.
locations: Opening a shadow door sends an Archipelago location check.

options.label: Randomize Plort Market
options.description:
Include up to 25 Plort Market location checks — one per sellable plort type.
The first time each plort type is deposited at the market sends a check.
20 plorts are always in scope; 5 in the Grey Labyrinth (Shadow, Sloomber, Twin,
Hyper, Prisma) are only included for the prismacore, prisma_shard_hunt, slimepedia, newbucks, and plort_seller goals
(every goal except labyrinth_open).

options.label: Randomize Polestar Provisions Shop
options.description:
Include location checks for buying items at the Polestar Provisions shop
(Conservatory — always open, Newbucks only).
A random selection of the shop's 165 items become checks, spread across the shop's
price tiers; the number of checks is rolled between Shop Check Count Min and Max.
84 items are on sale from the start of the game. The rest only appear in the shop
once something happens in-game, and carry matching logic: visiting Ember Valley (15),
Starlight Strand (8), Powderfall Bluffs (3) or the Grey Labyrinth (48), or — for 7 of
the vac palettes added in game update 1.3 — meeting a rancher, vacuuming a Yolky, or
opening the Tidepools expansion. Grey Labyrinth shop items are never selected when the
goal is Open the Grey Labyrinth.
The first purchase of a selected item sends the check instead of granting its
decoration blueprint, and that item then reads as sold out. Items that were not
selected behave completely vanilla.

options.label: Shop Check Count Min
options.description:
The smallest number of Polestar Provisions shop items that can become location checks.
Only used when Randomize Polestar Provisions Shop is enabled. If this is higher than
Shop Check Count Max, the two values are swapped. Counts above the number of eligible
items (e.g. with Grey Labyrinth shop items excluded by the goal) are clamped.

options.label: Shop Check Count Max
options.description:
The largest number of Polestar Provisions shop items that can become location checks.
Only used when Randomize Polestar Provisions Shop is enabled.

options.label: Progressive Shop Catalog
options.description:
Gate the Polestar Provisions shop checks behind Progressive Shop Catalog items.

Without this, every shop check is reachable from the start of the game — the shop is open
from minute one and Newbucks are farmable at any point, so a large Shop Check Count dumps
a hundred or more checks into sphere 1 and flattens the early multiworld.

With this on, the shop's checks are split into waves. The cheapest wave is on sale
immediately; each further wave needs one more Progressive Shop Catalog, which is shuffled
into the multiworld like any other item. Locked items are hidden in the shop, replaced by
a row saying how many are still to come.

Only affects items selected as checks. Anything the seed did not select stays fully
vanilla and remains purchasable throughout.

options.label: Shop Catalog Items
options.description:
How many Progressive Shop Catalog items to put in the pool.

The shop's checks are divided into this many waves plus one: the first is available from
the start, and each catalog item releases the next. 3 puts a quarter of the shop's checks
in sphere 1; 4 puts a fifth of them there.

Lowered automatically when there are too few shop checks to divide — each wave keeps at
least four checks, so a seed with 16 checks caps out at 3 catalog items no matter what is
set here. Only used when Progressive Shop Catalog is enabled.

options.label: Vac Palette Items
options.description:
Add the 22 vac styles from game update 1.3 to the item pool as filler.

Each one unlocks that vac style when received. They take the place of ordinary filler
(Newbucks and caches), so the total number of items does not change.

A vac style that this seed has made a Polestar Provisions shop check is left out of the
item pool, so the same palette is never both a check to buy and an item to receive.

options.label: Randomize Conservatory Expansions
options.description:
Include the 5 Conservatory expansion terminals as location checks.
The expansions unlock: The Gully, The Tidepools, The Archway, The Den, The Digsite.
Interacting with a terminal sends a check at no Newbucks cost. The expansion itself
only unlocks when the corresponding Access item is received from the item pool.

options.label: Randomize Sanctuary Content
options.description:
Include post-game Sanctuary content in the seed.
Currently adds one location: "Slimepedia: Sprinkles", which is unlocked by bringing
radiant slimes and decorations to the Sanctuary after finishing the main story.
With this off, Sprinkles is neither a check nor required by the Complete the
Slimepedia goal, so that goal can be finished without post-game content.
Requires Randomize Slimepedia (Resources) for the location to appear.

options.label: Randomize Ranch Plots
options.description:
Add the ranch's 32 plot spots to the item pool as per-area progressive unlocks
(Conservatory 8, The Gully 5, The Tidepools 5, The Archway 5, The Den 5,
The Digsite 4). Empty plots cannot be built on until enough "Ranch Plot" items
for that area have been received; each item lets you build on one more plot of
your choice in its area. Demolishing a building frees its slot again.
Starting Plots pre-grants some Conservatory plots so early ranching is possible.

options.label: Starting Plots
options.description:
How many Conservatory plot unlocks you start with when Randomize Ranch Plots is
enabled. The remaining Conservatory unlocks go into the item pool. Set to 0 for
no ranching at all until your first Ranch Plot item arrives.

options.label: Randomize Plot Buildings
options.description:
Add the 6 plot building types (Corral, Coop, Garden, Silo, Pond, Incinerator)
to the item pool as "... Plans" items. A building type cannot be constructed on
any plot until its Plans item has been received — its entry is hidden from the
plot build menu until then.

options.label: Randomize Plot Upgrades
options.description:
Add all 21 plot building upgrades (corral walls, garden sprinkler, silo storage
slots, plort collectors, ...) to the item pool. An upgrade cannot be purchased on
any plot until its item has been received — its entry is hidden from the plot
menu until then. Deluxe Coop / Deluxe Garden still also require their vanilla
prerequisites.

options.label: Region Access Mode
options.description:
Controls how region gate switches are handled.

- vanilla: Region gates work as in the base game — activating a switch opens the zone
  immediately. No region access items are added to the pool.
- locations: Gate switches become blocked location checks. The corresponding region gate
  will not open until the matching Region Access item is received from the item pool.
- bundled: Same as locations, but also grants the corresponding zone teleporter blueprint
  automatically when the Region Access item is received.

options.label: Conversation Checks
options.description:
Controls which CommStation conversations count as location checks.

- none: No conversations are location checks. All ranchers give vanilla gifts directly.
- conditional: The 10 conversations with confirmed zone or chain access conditions.
  Includes the full rancher intro-call chain (Viktor/Mochi/Ogden/Thora), Viktor's Radiant
  Projector Blueprint, Thora's Gordo Snare Advanced, Mochi's Archive Key, and BOb's intro
  call, first gift, and story call (BOb requires visiting Ember Valley and Starlight Strand).
- all: Every conversation — decorative gifts, story/lore, and deflect dialogue (~120 total).
  WARNING: Only recommended for async (asynchronous) multiworld games. Many conversations
  are gated behind real-world time delays of 1–3 in-game days each, and the full chain
  of all conversations can take many play sessions to complete. In a synchronous game
  where other players are waiting on your checks, this mode is likely to become a
  bottleneck. Use `conditional` for synchronous play.

options.label: Trap Percentage
options.description:
Percentage of filler item slots that are replaced with trap items.
Set to 0 to disable traps entirely.
Which trap types appear and how often is controlled by the individual Trap Weight options.

options.label: Tarr Spawn Trap Weight
options.description:
Relative weight of the Tarr Spawn Trap in the trap pool.
Tarr Spawn places two Tarr directly next to the player.
Set to 0 to exclude this trap type entirely.

options.label: Teleport Trap Weight
options.description:
Relative weight of the Teleport Trap in the trap pool.
Teleport sends the player to a random accessible zone entrance.
Set to 0 to exclude this trap type entirely.

options.label: Tarr Rain Trap Weight
options.description:
Relative weight of the Tarr Rain Trap in the trap pool.
Tarr Rain triggers the Slime Rain weather event, but Tarr fall from the sky instead of slimes.
Set to 0 to exclude this trap type entirely.

options.label: Vacpack Spew Trap Weight
options.description:
Relative weight of the Vacpack Spew Trap in the trap pool.
Vacpack Spew launches all items currently in the player's vacpack as physical world objects
and clears every slot — everything you were carrying flies out at once.
Set to 0 to exclude this trap type entirely.

options.label: Vacpack Fill Trap Weight
options.description:
Relative weight of the Vacpack Fill Trap in the trap pool.
Vacpack Fill fills every empty slot in the player's vacpack with Pink slimes to capacity.
Set to 0 to exclude this trap type entirely.

options.label: Disable Tarr
options.description:
When enabled, Tarr slimes (traps and checks) are removed from the randomizer entirely:
- The Slimepedia Tarr entry is excluded from the location pool (even when
  Randomize Slimepedia is on).
- Tarr Spawn Trap and Tarr Rain Trap are removed from the trap pool regardless
  of their individual weight settings.

Use this if you prefer to play without Tarr.

options.label: Exclude RNG Slimes
options.description:
When enabled, removes location checks that depend on rare slimes the player
cannot reliably control:

- Slimepedia: Gold Slime, Lucky Slime, Yolky Slime
- Radiant Slimepedia: Yolky
- Fabricator: Golden Sureshot I, II, and III (require Gold Plorts to craft)
- Plort Market: Gold Plort, Yolky Plort
- Polestar Provisions: Golden Yolky Statue (only appears in the shop after a
  Yolky discovery)

When the goal is set to slimepedia, these entries are also excluded from the
win condition — the goal fires without them being unlocked.

Useful for players who find passive-spawn-only checks frustrating or RNG-gated.

options.label: Exclude Weather Checks
options.description:
When enabled, removes location checks that depend on weather events the
player cannot control:

- Slimepedia: Tangle Slime, Dervish Slime
- Radiant Slimepedia: Tangle, Dervish
- Slimepedia Resources: Lightning Mote, Storm Glass, Drift Crystal
- Plort Market: Dervish Plort, Tangle Plort

When the goal is set to slimepedia, these entries are also excluded from the
win condition — the goal fires without them being unlocked.

Useful for players who prefer not to wait on specific weather patterns.

options.label: Tarr Instakill
options.description:
When enabled, Tarr bites always kill the player instantly regardless of current health
or the Incoming Damage Multiplier setting.
Off by default — Tarr deal their normal 20 base damage (scaled by the multiplier).

options.label: Incoming Damage Multiplier
options.description:
Multiplier applied to all incoming damage the player receives.
1 = normal damage (default).
2 = double damage.
5 = five times normal damage.
Note: a Tarr bite deals 20 base damage. At 5x this equals 100, which kills the player
at default health — but is survivable with Health Tank upgrades.

options.label: Force Heavy Weather
options.description:
When enabled, weather events always spawn at their maximum severity (Heavy tier).
Light and Medium weather phases are skipped — patterns jump directly to Heavy as
soon as they start.
Flat single-state patterns (Slime Rain, Snow) are unaffected.
On by default — ensures players can reliably farm the zone-specific resources
that only appear during severe weather (Slime Rain spawns, snow-exclusive items, etc.).

options.label: Weather Frequency Multiplier
options.description:
Multiplier applied to weather event frequency.
SR2 schedules weather events every 0.25–1.0 in-game hours by default.
This option divides that interval by the multiplier, making weather changes start more often but last for less time

1 = vanilla interval (default).
2 = weather starts twice as frequently.
4 = weather starts four times as frequently.

options.label: All Radiant Slimes
options.description:
When enabled, every slime encounter spawns as a radiant variant — the shuffle-bag
algorithm is bypassed entirely and DrawFromRadiantShuffleBag always returns true.

If this is on, Radiant Spawn Rate Multiplier has no additional effect and can be
left at its default value of 1.

Only relevant when Randomize Slimepedia (Radiant Slimes) is enabled; harmless otherwise.

options.label: Radiant Spawn Rate Multiplier
options.description:
Multiplier applied to radiant slime spawn frequency.
SR2 uses a shuffle-bag algorithm: each slime type has a bag of N encounters;
when the bag empties the next encounter with that type is guaranteed radiant.
This option divides all bag sizes by the multiplier, making radiant slimes
appear proportionally more often.

1 = vanilla rates (default). Typical bag sizes range from 25 (Yolky) to 2000 (Pink).
2 = radiant slimes appear ~2× as often.
5 = radiant slimes appear ~5× as often.
10 = radiant slimes appear ~10× as often.
50 = radiant slimes appear ~50× as often (near-guaranteed on every other encounter;
     bag sizes are floored at 2 so a radiant is never certain on every spawn).

Has no effect when All Radiant Slimes is enabled.
Only relevant when Randomize Slimepedia (Radiant Slimes) is enabled; harmless otherwise.

options.label: Gold/Lucky Spawn Rate Multiplier
options.description:
Multiplier applied to Gold and Lucky slime spawn weight.
SR2 uses a weight-based system: each DirectedActorSpawner has a SlimeSet where each
member has a Weight value. Gold and Lucky slimes have very small weights (typically 1–5)
compared to common slimes (50–200+), making them rare.
This option multiplies all Gold and Lucky member weights by the given value.

1 = vanilla weights (default).
2 = Gold/Lucky weights doubled — roughly 2× more frequent.
5 = Gold/Lucky weights ×5 — noticeably more common.
10 = Gold/Lucky weights ×10 — frequent encounters in most zones.
35 = Gold/Lucky weights ×35 — very common; note that Gold slimes drop large amounts
     of Newbucks, so high values will significantly accelerate the economy and may
     trivialize the Newbucks goal.

options.label: Gordo Feed Requirement
options.description:
Percentage of the vanilla feed count required to pop a Gordo.
Vanilla gordos require 50 slimes (most types) or 25 (some types).
This option scales that count by the given percentage.

100 = vanilla feed counts (default).
75  = 75% of vanilla — e.g. 50-slime gordos require 38.
50  = half the vanilla count — e.g. 50-slime gordos require 25.
25  = quarter of the vanilla count — e.g. 50-slime gordos require 13.
10  = minimum allowed — approximately 5 slimes for a standard gordo.
150 = 150% of vanilla — e.g. 50-slime gordos require 75.
200 = double the vanilla count — e.g. 50-slime gordos require 100.

The result is always at least 1 regardless of the percentage.
Applies to all gordos including player-placed Gordo Snares.

options.label: Newbucks Multiplier
options.description:
Percentage multiplier applied to Newbucks you earn in-game.

Scales every Newbucks payment the game itself makes — plort sales at the Market, treasure
pods, and any other in-world source. 100 is vanilla.

50  = half income; plort selling takes twice as long.
200 = double income.
500 = maximum; five times vanilla.

Newbucks from Archipelago filler items (250/500/1000 Newbucks) are NOT scaled — those are
already balanced as item-pool rewards, and multiplying them would change the value of a
check based on an economy setting. Refunds are not scaled either, so selling back a ranch
plot never returns more than it cost.

A payment that was non-zero before scaling always remains at least 1, so a low multiplier
cannot silently make small sales worthless.

Interacts with the Newbucks Milestone goal: the multiplied amount is what counts, so a high
multiplier genuinely shortens that goal. Lower Newbucks Goal Amount alongside it if you want
the same length of game.

options.label: Shadow Plort Requirement
options.description:
Percentage of the vanilla Shadow Plort count required to trigger a Grey Labyrinth
shadow plort door / dispenser.

100 = vanilla counts (default).
50  = half the vanilla count — a 6-plort door needs 3.
10  = minimum allowed.
200 = double the vanilla count.

The result is always at least 1 regardless of the percentage. Only affects depositors
that take Shadow Plorts, so ordinary coloured plort doors are untouched.

Independent of Randomize Shadow Plort Doors — the scaling applies whether or not the
doors are Archipelago checks, since it is about the cost of opening them.

options.label: Start with Resource Harvester
options.description:
When enabled, the Resource Harvester upgrade is granted at the start of the game
instead of being shuffled into the item pool.
The Resource Harvester allows the player to gather craft materials from resource nodes.
Useful for players who find early crafting progression gating frustrating.

options.label: Plort Market Mode
options.description:
Controls plort market saturation at game start.

- disabled: Vanilla behavior — market prices start at their normal levels and decrease
  as you sell plorts.
- 5_items: The market starts fully saturated (minimum prices for all plort types).
  Five Market Recovery (20%) items are added to the pool; each restores 20% of every
  plort's price. Collecting all five returns prices to their normal maximum.
- 10_items: Same as 5_items, but ten Market Recovery (10%) items are added instead —
  finer-grained price recovery at the cost of needing more items to reach full prices.

While this mode is active, selling plorts does not increase market saturation —
Market Recovery items are the only thing that changes plort prices.

options.label: Prisma Shards Required
options.description:
Number of Prisma Shards needed to unlock the Prismacore encounter.

Only used by the prisma_shard_hunt goal. Until you hold this many, Gigi will not start the
fight — no other progress substitutes for them.

options.label: Extra Prisma Shards (%)
options.description:
Percentage of ADDITIONAL Prisma Shards placed in the pool beyond the required number.

50 means half again as many: 8 required becomes 12 placed, so four are spare. Extras give
the fill algorithm slack, which stops the hunt ending in a single unavoidable bottleneck.

Shards displace filler items, so with a large requirement and few location categories
enabled there may not be room for all the extras — surplus is trimmed and noted in the
generation log. The required number is never reduced.

options.label: Item Notifications
options.description:
How prominently the mod announces items you receive from other players.

Progression and useful items use the game's major popup — the same one that appears for a
new Slimepedia entry — showing the Archipelago logo and the item name. Filler and traps,
when included, use the mod's own corner text rather than a vanilla notification.

- none: No item popups at all.
- progression: Major popup for progression items only.
- progression_useful: Major popup for progression and useful items.
- all: As above, plus corner text for filler and traps.

Popups are rate-limited, so a large batch of incoming items will not flood the screen,
and they stop entirely once you have completed your own goal.

options.label: Version
options.description: Which version of the game you want to play.

options.label: Include Jobs
options.description: Whether Jobs can contain progression or useful items.

options.label: Include Graveyard Area
options.description: Whether the Graveyard can contain progression or useful items.

options.label: Include EX Bosses
options.description: Whether EX Bosses can contain progression or useful items.

options.label: Include SP Bosses
options.description: Whether SP Bosses can contain progression or useful items.

options.label: Include Virus Battler
options.description: Whether Virus Battler Machines can contain progression or useful items.

options.label: Include Bass BX
options.description: Whether Bass BX can contain progression or useful items.

options.label: Include ProtoMan FZ
options.description: Whether ProtoMan FZ can contain progression or useful items.

options.label: Trade Quest Hinting
options.description:
Whether NPCs offering Chip Trades should show what item they provide.
None - NPCs will not provide any information on what item they will give
Partial - NPCs will state if an item is progression or not, but not the specific item
Full - NPCs will state what item they will give, providing an Archipelago Hint when doing so

options.label: Game Difficulty
options.description: Determines expected player skill. A harder difficulty means you will be expected to go further in the game with less resources.

options.label: Goal
options.description: Determines the win condition for the game. Myzand 2: Traverse Myzand's Forest, defeat him, and lock him away. Eye Chest: Open the 6-Eye Door and collect the Eye Fragment.

options.label: Shuffle Slide Puzzles
options.description: When enabled, slide puzzles and their rewards will be shuffled into the pool.

options.label: I Hate Seedling
options.description: When enabled, Blue in Lost Swamp will always give you a gun, and you will always find a spell at the Fireball location. (This may break gun/spell plando, so be warned.)

options.label: Shuffle Bug-Eating Effects
options.description: Randomizes the temporary effect gained when eating any bug other than Mushroom.

options.label: Shuffle Workshop Key
options.description: When enabled, the Workshop Key will be shuffled into the item pool, and Bins will give you a random item after defeating Xoto.

options.label: Shop Multiplier
options.description: Decreases the total cost of items in shops by a percentage. 100 = no discount, 0 = free shops. This does not impact gun upgrade costs, or buying from Supa.

options.label: Open City
options.description: When enabled, the Lost Swamp portal vine will be enabled from the beginning, allowing quick travel to City without needing to traverse through most of the early game first.

options.label: Hardcore Parkour
options.description: When enabled, the player will be expected to do more advanced or unituitive platform movement to get to some locations.

options.label: Well Light Logic
options.description: Chooses which items will be expected to be acquired for traversing the well. Glowbug for navigating dark passages, Fire Fruit Juicer for relighting the candle after Fire-Eaters, or both.

options.label: Forge the Crystal
options.description:
Bring the Adamant and Legend Sword to clear this objective.
Forces the objective reward to be the Crystal.

options.label: Conquer the Giant
options.description:
Clear the Giant of Bab-il to clear this objective.
No character will be available from the Giant with this objective.

options.label: Defeat The Fiends
options.description:
Defeat every elemental fiend to clear this objective.
Your targets are Milon, Milon Z., Kainazzo, Valvalis, Rubicant, and the Elements bosses. Good hunting.

options.label: Find The Dark Matter
options.description:
Find thirty Dark Matters and deliver them to Kory in Agart to clear this objective.
There are forty-five Dark Matters in total.

options.label: Additional Objectives
options.description:
The number of additional random objectives. Can be quests, boss fights, or character recruitments. Note that
no matter what this is set to, no more than thirty-two objectives will be set.

options.label: Max Number of Required Objectives
options.description:
The number of objectives required for victory. Note that this is ignored when no objectives are set. If this
count is greater than the total number of objectives available, then it will be reduced to match the number of
available objectives.

options.label: Objective Reward
options.description:
The reward for clearing all objectives. Note that this is ignored when no objectives are set,
and Forge the Crystal forces this to the Crystal setting.

options.label: Item Placement
options.description:
Where items can and will be placed.
Setting this to Full Shuffle will allow any items to be anywhere.
Setting this to Major Minor Split will force all non-major locations to never have progression.
In either case, major locations can only have useful or progression items.
Major locations are any MIAB or event locations.

options.label: Enable Default Priority Locations
options.description:
If set, major event locations and Monster-In-A-Box locations will be guaranteed to have
useful or progression items.

options.label: No Free Characters
options.description:
If set, characters will not be available at locations with no requirements or bosses. These locations are
Mysidia, Damcyan Watery Pass, and Mt. Ordeals.

options.label: No Earned Characters
options.description:
If set, characters will not be available at locations with requirements or bosses. These locations are Mist,
Kaipo, Mt. Hobs, Baron, the Tower of Zot, Cave Eblana, Lunar Palace, and the Giant of Bab-il.

options.label: Hero Challenge
options.description:
Enable the Hero Challenge. In Hero Challenge, your starting character is your main character and cannot be
dismissed. They will face the top of Mt. Ordeals on their own, and Kokkol will forge a weapon from FFIV Advance
for them (unless Forge the Crystal is set).

options.label: Pass In Key Item Pool
options.description: Will the Pass be included in the Key Item Pool?

options.label: Unsafe Key Item Placement
options.description:
Normally, underground access is guaranteed to be available without taking a trip to the moon.
Toggling this on disables this check.

options.label: Enable Pass in Shops
options.description: Can the pass show up in shops? This is a convenience feature and will never be required by the logic.

options.label: Allowed Characters
options.description: Pool of characters allowed to show up. Note that if Hero Challenge is enabled, your hero will still appear.

options.label: Ensure All Characters
options.description: Ensure at least one instance of each allowed character is available, if possible.

options.label: Allow Duplicate Characters
options.description: Allows multiple instances of the same character to join your party.

options.label: Restricted Characters
options.description: List of characters that can't appear in the easiest to access locations if possible.

options.label: Party Size
options.description: Maximum party size.

options.label: Characters Permanently Join
options.description: If enabled, characters may not be dismissed from the party.

options.label: Characters Permanently Die
options.description:
If enabled, characters petrified or dead at the end of battle will be removed from your party forever.
On Extreme difficulty, this also includes "cutscene" fights (Mist, Dark Elf, etc.)

options.label: MIAB Randomization
options.description:
Affects where MIABs are randomized to and their contents.
Randomized will randomize the location of MIAB chests, while Vanilla keeps them in their default location.
Vanilla Exclude acts as vanilla, but progression will never be placed in their locations.

options.label: Item Randomization
options.description: Affects item pool

options.label: Minimum Treasure Tier
options.description: The minimum tier of items that can appear in the item pool.

options.label: Maximum Treasure Tier
options.description: The maximum tier of items that can appear in the item pool.

options.label: Junk Tier
options.description: Items of this tier or below will automatically be sold for cold hard cash.

options.label: J Items
options.description:
Affects whether items not in the US release of FF4 will appear in shops or the item pool.
Does not affect enemy drops/steals.

options.label: Shop Randomization
options.description: Affects the placement of items in shops. See FE documentation for more for now.

options.label: Free Shops
options.description: Everything must go!

options.label: No Adamant Armor
options.description: Remove Adamant Armor from the item and shop pool.

options.label: Keep TrapDoor and Behemoth Fights
options.description: Should Trap Door and Behemoth Fights be enabled even when encounters are off?

options.label: No Free Bosses
options.description: Removes alternate win conditions for bosses other than good old fashioned violence.

options.label: Wacky Challenge
options.description:
Wacky challenges are not fair, balanced, stable, or even necessarily interesting.
They are, however, quite wacky. See FE documentation for more info, or pick one for a fun surprise!

choices.label: The Floor Is Made Of Lava

options.label: Starter Kit One
options.description: FE Starter Kit 1. See FE Documentation for details. Or just pick one, they can't hurt you.

options.label: Starter Kit Two
options.description: FE Starter Kit 2. See FE Documentation for details. Or just pick one, they can't hurt you.

options.label: Starter Kit Three
options.description: FE Starter Kit 3. See FE Documentation for details. Or just pick one, they can't hurt you.

options.label: Junked Items
options.description: Items that will always be sold for GP regardless of your junk tier settings.

options.label: Kept Items
options.description: Items that will never be sold for GP regardless of your junk tier settings. Takes priority over Junked Items.

options.label: Zodiac Stones in Pool
options.description:
How many Zodiac Stones will be in the item pool.
If set to less than the number required, will instead become however many are required.

options.label: Zodiac Stones Required
options.description: How many Zodiac Stones will be required to beat the game.

options.label: Zodiac Stone Locations
options.description:
Where can Zodiac Stones appear?
Vanilla limits their possible locations to those events which had one in the vanilla game.
This limits the maximum number of stones in the pool from 8-12, depending on sidequest and Altima options.
Note that with fewer stones in the pool, potential Stone locations can have other items.
Anywhere Local means stones can be at any location in your world.
Anywhere means stones can be anywhere in the multiworld.

options.label: Final Battles
options.description:
What the final goal is, located at the Murond Death City world map dot near Deep Dungeon.
Vanilla requires the completion of all six final battles in sequence at Murond Death City.
Altima Only requires only Altima at Murond Death City, and the other endgame battles will be located at Orbonne.

options.label: Sidequest Battles
options.description: Are sidequest battles (Colliery, Nelveska, Zarghidas, Deep Dungeon) in the pool of locations?

options.label: Job Unlocks
options.description: Are job unlocks in the item and location pools?

options.label: Rare Battles
options.description: Are the rare battles for each battleground in the location pool?

options.label: Poach Locations
options.description: Are poaches in the location pool? WARNING: Can be grindy and RNG-heavy.

options.label: Logical Difficulty
options.description: Affects the placement of logically required shop levels and jobs in the multiworld.

options.label: Chemist Placement
options.description:
Where Chemist is placed in the multiworld when Job Unlocks are enabled.
Starting will have you start with Chemist.
Early will ensure Chemist is one of your first items in the multiworld.
Shuffled will shuffle Chemist into the pool like other jobs.

options.label: Early Pass
options.description: Will a Pass for a neighboring region be an early item?

options.label: Starting Shop Level
options.description: The starting shop level of your game.

options.label: Randomize Poach Rewards
options.description:
Whether Fur Shop awards from poaching should be randomized.
Split will make the rare result (12% of the time) always be an item unavailable in shops,
while the common result will always be an item available in shops.

options.label: Normal Item Weight
options.description: Weight of items normally sold in shops in the filler pool.

options.label: Rare Item Weight
options.description: Weight of items not normally sold in shops in the filler pool.

options.label: Bonus Gil Item Weight
options.description: Weight of bonus items in the filler pool.

options.label: JP Boon Item Weight
options.description: Weight of JP Boon items that award JP to the team in the filler pool

options.label: Bonus Gil Item Size
options.description:
Adjusts the value of bonus gil items in the pool.
Normal is 5000/10000/40000. Frugal halves that, Expensive doubles.

options.label: JP Boon Item Size
options.description: Adjusts the value of JP Boon items. Normal is 50/100/250 JP. Frugal halves that, Expensive doubles.

options.label: Enemy Randomizer
options.description:
Randomizes enemies.
Disabled leaves enemies as vanilla.
Boss Shuffle shuffles only unique story bosses amongst each other.
Randomized randommizes all enemies per other settings in this section.
Boss Shuffle Randomized combines the above two options: bosses will be shuffled and
all other slots will be randomized per other settings.

options.label: Randomize Gariland
options.description: Whether to randomize the Gariland story fight.

options.label: Cross Enemy Randomizer
options.description: If enabled, generic jobs can randomize into special units and vice versa.

options.label: Cross Species Randomizer
options.description: If enabled, randomized humans can become monster units and vice versa.

options.label: Randomize Story Fights Only
options.description:
If enabled, only story and sidequest fights will be randomized,
and random encounters will be left alone.

options.label: Enemy Randomizer Locality
options.description:
Controls the scope of enemy randomization.
Battle randomizes enemy units of the same job differently per battle.
Region randomizes enemy units of the same job differently per region.
Global randomizes all enemy units in the game of the same job to the same randomized job.

options.label: Lucavi Randomizer
options.description:
Controls if Lucavi and Altima are included in randomization.
Disabled leaves Lucavi (Queklain, Velius, Zalera, Adramelk, Hashmalum, Elidibs) the same as vanilla.
Lucavi enables those locations and jobs to be included in randomization.
Include Altima also includes Altima 1 and 2 in the randomization. Will cause graphical glitches.

options.label: Enemy Randomizer Method
options.description:
Controls the randomization method for determining randomized units.
Shuffle will attempt to map vanilla units to new unique jobs,
such that only Squires will become Chemists, for example.
Chaos allows duplicates, such that multiple jobs could become Chemists, for example.

options.label: Move-Find Item Locations
options.description: Will Move-Find Item locations contain multiworld items? WARNING: Will be more annoying than you think.

options.label: Move-Find Item Location Logic
options.description:
Controls what is needed and used to access MFI locations.
Vanilla requires Move-Find Item to be equipped.
Chemist Innate makes Move-Find Item innate to Chemists.
Player Innate makes Move-Find Item innate to all player units.

options.label: Randomize Move-Find Item Rewards
options.description:
Should MFI tile rewards be randomized?
If Split is chosen, the rare slot (more likely with lower Brave)
will always have an item unavailable in shops while the common slot will only have shop items.

options.label: EXP Gain Multiplier
options.description: Multiplier to in-battle EXP gains.

options.label: JP Gain Multiplier
options.description: Multiplier to in-battle JP gains.

options.label: Vanilla Changes
options.description:
Controls changes from vanilla.
SwordskillUsersSwordOnly locks swordskill users like Orlandu and Beowulf to swords and knightswords.
  Most impactful for enemy randomizer.
MateriaBladeNotRequired changes Limit to require any sword, not specifically the Materia Blade.
RandomMagicHitsIncreased increases the number of hits of Truth, Un-Truth, and Holy Bracelet to ten, like in WotL/TIC.
Improved Shops adds in an early katana and spear as well as adding guns to trade cities.

options.label: Enable Transmooglifier
options.description:
Enables Transmooglifier, which gives Rad, Alicia, and Lavian new special jobs.
Check the Transmooglifier wiki page at https://github.com/Rosalie-A/Archipelago/wiki/FFT-Transmooglifier-Reference
for more info.

options.label: Transmooglifier Options
options.description: Which jobs are options for Transmooglifier. If fewer than three, the remainder will be picked at random.

options.label: Gate balancing
options.description:
Randomizes quests with weights based on gate number and quest rank.
Low rank quests have higher weights in early gates, and high rank quests have higher weights in late gates.
A value of 0 means no balancing. Higher values are more heavily weighted.

options.label: Number of quest gates
options.description:
Sets the number of quest gates. Each gate contains four quests each.
The Two Grimoires will always be the last quest.
Amount of locations per gate depends on number of item rewards

options.label: Number of gate paths
options.description:
Sets the number of branching gate paths.
How many must be completed depends on the paths_required option.
Useful for higher mission gate counts.

options.label: Number of gate paths required
options.description: Sets the number of gate paths that must be completed to unlock the final quest.

options.label: Final quest
options.description:
Sets the final questline. "The Two Grimoires" leads directly into "From The Rift".

The Ritual: You must complete "The Ritual", "The Two Grimoires", and "From the Rift" to win.
The Two Grimoires: You must complete "The Two Grimoires", and "From the Rift" to win.

options.label: Number of quest rewards
options.description: Sets the number of locations per quest.

options.label: AP gained from quests
options.description:
Sets the amount of AP gained from quests.
The amount is mulitplied by 10. Default is 5 = 50 AP.

options.label: Base exp gained from quests
options.description:
Sets the base amount of exp gained from quests.
Default is 60 exp.

options.label: Gil gained from quests
options.description:
Sets the amount of gil gained from quests.
Special values:
    Vanilla: Default value. Same as the vanilla game

options.label: Dispatch quests
options.description:
Toggle dispatch quests on or off.

Vanilla: Dispatch quests are the same as vanilla.
No Dispatch: Dispatch quests are turned turned into normal quests.

options.label: Job unlocks
options.description:
Sets job requirements.

Vanilla: Jobs require mastered abilities and certain quests (not recommended).
No Quests: Jobs require mastered abilities, but not quests.
All Unlocked: Jobs have no requirements.
All Locked: All jobs are locked. Units can only be their starting job.
Job Items: All jobs start locked. Job unlocks are checks.

options.label: Randomize starting units
options.description:
Randomizes starting units.

Disabled: Starting units will not be randomized.
Random Jobs: Starting units will have their jobs randomized.
Random Races and Jobs: Starting units will have their race and jobs randomized.
    Special units will only have their jobs randomized.
Random Races and Jobs Experimental: Starting units will have their race and jobs randomized including special units.
    Special units with randomized races may crash or freeze the game.

options.label: Starting equipment
options.description:
Sets starting unit equipment.

Basic: Units will start with basic equipment for their job.
Randomized: Units will start with random equipment.

options.label: Starting units
options.description:
Sets the starting units. Starting unit randomization overrides this except for special units.
You cannot start with more than 5 non-special units.

Format:
    ["{Name}", "{Name}", ..., "{Name}"]
    {Name} can be a special unit, or a Race and Job.
    Special units are: Adelle, Cid, Hurdy, Vaan, Penelo, Al-Cid, Montblanc, Frimelda
    Race and Job examples: Hume Archer, Nu Mou Black Mage
    No duplicates allowed.

options.label: Bazaar
options.description:
Bazaar options.

Vanilla: All loot items are in the pool. (Not recommended)
No Loot: Loot items are removed from the pool of possible checks. This makes equipment checks much more likely.
Randomized Recipes: All recipes in the bazaar are randomized.
Checks: All recipes in the bazaar are randomized and are also checks (and still unlock shop items).

options.label: Bazaar loot pool
options.description:
If recipes are randomized this is the max number of different items used of each loot type (7 types).
The amount received of a loot item from a check will be enough for all recipes that use that item.
Warning: Setting this to 14 or higher is likely to generate fill errors if path_num is set to 1 (and still possible at 3).

options.label: Difficulty Options
options.description:
Sets whether knowledge checks and/or hard tricks may be required in logic.
Standard: Requires no extra knowledge besides what is used to beat the vanilla game.
Knowledge Checks: Requires the player to know basic shortcuts, 
such as breaking hidden blocks in walls.
Hard Tricks: Everything from "knowledge checks", and also may require the player to 
perform more difficult tricks, such as jumping off of a thrown enemy in midair.

options.label: Minor Glitches
options.description:
Sets whether minor glitches may be required in logic.
Easy glitches: Simple glitches such as water walking or block clipping with flat form.
All glitches: Everything from easy glitches as well as things like wall jumps and screen wrapping.

options.label: Victory Condition
options.description:
Which condition unlocks the Rudy fight.
Music Boxes: collect enough music boxes (see Music Boxes Required).
Bosses: defeat enough bosses (see Bosses Required).
Only the selected condition is active — the other's required count
is ignored.

options.label: Music Boxes Required
options.description:
How many of the 5 music boxes Wario must collect before the
Temple opens and Rudy becomes accessible. Only active when Victory
Condition = Music Boxes. Set to 0 to make Temple always open.

options.label: Bosses Required
options.description:
Number of Bosses needed to access the Rudy fight.
Bossess include: Wormwould, Shoot, Scowler, Jamano, Anonster,
Wolfenboss, Pesce, Muddee, Doll Boy, and Yellow Belly.

options.label: Start With
options.description:
Items Wario will start with. Starting with axe or more than two random 
level starts is suggested so that early items aren't forcibly placed early.
axe: Unlocks The Peaceful Village and The Vast Plain from the start.
magnifying_glass: shows what you've collected in a level (hold B on the overworld).
both: start with both.
nothing: start with neither.

options.label: Random Level Starts
options.description: Extra random level-unlock items pre-collected (0 = off, 1-8 = that many).

options.label: Combined Items
options.description:
Controls which multi-item requirements are combined into single items.
Off:       No combining; multi-item requirements stay as-is.
Overworld: Combine items that gate level access (e.g. Blue+Green Tablet → Tablets).
In Level:  Combine items that gate chests/keys within a level (e.g. Blue+Red Chemical → Chemicals).
Both:      Combine both overworld and in-level pairs.

options.label: Key Shuffle
options.description:
Controls how the 100 level keys (4 per level × 25 levels) are handled.
Vanilla: Each key location is vanilla
Full: Keys and treasures are shuffled together across all 200 locations. (This adds 100 checks)
During syncs, it is highly recommended to couple this option with a large number of keyrings below.

options.label: Keyring Count
options.description:
Number of levels whose 4 keys are replaced by a single Keyring item.
0 = off (each key is its own item).
1-24 = that many randomly-chosen levels get a Keyring (the other levels keep individual keys).
25 = every level gets a Keyring (no individual key items in the pool).
When above 0, Key Shuffle is forced to Full so that the remaining individual
keys are still shuffled.

options.label: Transformation Shuffle
options.description:
Shuffle transformation abilities (Zombie, Vampire, Fire, etc.) as items.
When on, you must find each Form item to use that transformation via
Select+button combos; the forms are placed in logic. When off, behaves as vanilla

options.label: Rudy Hit Points
options.description:
How many hits Wario must land on Rudy
before he's defeated. Vanilla is 4.

options.label: Golf Price
options.description:
Sets the coin cost for the mini-games (golf). 
Vanilla: Tier-based cost (10 / 30 / 50 coins).
Free: FREE GOLF!
Cheap: Reduced tier-based cost (5 / 10 / 15 coins).
The Golf Building courses are always free regardless of this setting.

options.label: Golf Building
options.description:
Controls whether the Golf Building is always open or requires crayons to open.
Open: Golf Building can always be entered (always free to play).
Vanilla: the Golf Building requires all 7 crayons to open (vanilla behavior).

options.label: I Hate Golf
options.description:
Automatically win the golf mini-game as soon as it starts.
The hole is immediately cleared without having to play.
Has no effect in the Golf Building — those courses always run vanilla.

options.label: Golf Par Hints
options.description:
Hint an AP item when you clear a Golf Building hole or course at par or better.
Nothing:                       Vanilla, no hints are given.
Music Boxes (per hole/course): Hint a Music Box location — either every hole
                               cleared at par or only after clearing all 5 holes of a course at par.
Progression (per hole/course): Hint any item AP classifies as progression (keys, music boxes,
                               progression treasures, forms, abilities, etc.).
Anything    (per hole/course): Hint any unhinted, unchecked AP item.
If the chosen category has no unhinted matches left, falls back to Anything.

options.label: Reduce Flashing
options.description:
Disables flashing/blinking background palette cycling in certain rooms
(e.g. underground areas, Warped Void). Recommended for photosensitivity.
This option is automatically on if any palette shuffle is active, since palette 
cycling can be very visually jarring when combined with random palettes.

options.label: Non-Stop Chests
options.description:
Stay in the level after opening a treasure chest instead of exiting to
the overworld.

options.label: In-Game Messages
options.description:
Which in-game pop-up messages the client should display.
Everything: show every message — your own item pickups, items received from
other players, and items you sent to other players (default).
Progression: only show received items that are Progression-classified.
Items you SEND to other players still show (so you can see what they're
getting); items YOU receive show only when they're flagged Progression.
Nothing: don't display any in-game messages at all (received, own, or sent).

options.label: Big Coinsanity
options.description: Adds 200 big-coin (musical coin) locations  — 8 per level — to the pool.

options.label: Boss Defeats
options.description:
Adds 10 boss-defeat locations to the pool. This option can be used
 with "Bosses_Required" as well 
 Bosses include: Wormwould, Shoot, Scowler, Jamano,
Anonster, Wolfenboss, Pesce, Muddee, Doll Boy, Yellow Belly.

options.label: Shopsanity
options.description:
Adds 10 shop locations to the pool, purchasable with coins from
the new overworld node east of the hidden temple.
Prices scale with slot number and the shop_price_tier option.

options.label: Shop Price Tier
options.description:
Prices below are spread evenly with two towards the bottom,
two towards the top, and six prices in the middle.

cheap:     1-99 coins
normal:    25-200 coins
expensive: 50-500 coins

options.label: Enemizer
options.description:
This setting is mostly stable, but isn't guaranteed to be crash-free.
If you do run into a crash, use the command "/vanillaenemies" to revert the current room 
(or previous room if in the overworld) back to vanilla enemies."

off:    Enemies stay vanilla.
full:   Enemies are fully randomized with limited restrictions.
grouped: Enemies are randomized by type (Ground, Flying and Water-safe)

Rooms with throw blocks are guaranteed a throwable enemy in both
'full' and 'grouped' modes. Bosses always stay vanilla.

options.label: Hidden Passages Revealed
options.description:
Reveal hidden blocks and blocks that always contain color coins in-game.

- vanilla: nothing revealed or recolored (default WL3 behavior).
- hidden_blocks: hidden passages are revealed with their corresponding cracked/
  non-cracked blocks. Hidden throw/fire/yarn blocks aren't included.
- hidden_blocks_and_color_coins: same as hidden_blocks, plus blocks that
guarantee color coin drops.

options.label: Trap Fill %
options.description:
Percentage of filler items replaced with transformation traps.
When a trap is received, Wario is set on fire the next safe frame.
0 = no traps (default), 100 = every filler item is a trap.

options.label: Trap Weights
options.description:
Weighted option for traps. When a filler item is replaced with a trap, 
the chosen trap is picked from a weighted pool (i.e. 3 = 3x more).

options.label: Local Filler %
options.description:
Percentage of your filler items kept in your OWN world instead of
being shuffled into the multiworld. This helps by preventing other worlds
from being flooded with your filler items, particularly with "Big Coinsanity" on.

options.label: Death Link
options.description:
Send and receive deaths to/from other players. This will trigger the "Game Over" screen when you die, forcing you to restart the level. If Death Mode is set to "Grabs" or "Grabs and Golf", then certain enemy grabs or golf failures will also trigger deaths. You can still receive deaths from other players even if your own Death Mode is set to None.
screen from being captured by Rudy. You can include "Death Mode" below to add more
death link options locally.

options.label: Death Mode
options.description:
Controls what locally counts as a death. 
None: deaths are never triggered, unless death link is on and is from other players.
Grabs: enemy grabs that teleport you  (e.g. RoboMouse, Scowler, Rudy) 
instead trigger a Game Over death.
Grabs and Golf: same as Grabs, plus failing a golf hole par triggers a death

options.label: Music Shuffle
options.description:
Randomize the background music played in each level.
Split: Day and night music are shuffled within their own groups (day with day, night with night).
Full:  All music tracks are fully randomized regardless of day/night.

options.label: Overworld BG Palette Shuffle
options.description:
Randomize the title menu and overworld map background palettes. 
Does NOT affect key portrait colors.

options.label: Level/Room BG Palette Shuffle
options.description: Randomize level background (BG) palettes.

options.label: Enemy Palette Shuffle
options.description: Randomize enemy sprite palettes.

options.label: Wario Palette Shuffle
options.description:
Randomize Wario's color palette.
Off:       No changes.
Shirt:     Randomize the shirt/highlight color (hat and eyes too).
Overalls:  Randomize the overalls/outline color (also a few other tones).
Both:      Randomize both independently.

Any hex set under Wario Colors overrides the corresponding slot here.

options.label: Wario Colors
options.description:
Custom hex colors for Wario shirt (also hat and eyes) and
 overalls (also a few other in-game tones).
Values: hex like #RRGGBB / RRGGBB / #RGB / RGB. The closest GBC color is used.
(Example: shirt: '#daff47')

options.label: Goal

options.label: Boss Rush / Final Stage Layout
options.description:
Determines how the Boss Rush and Final Wily Stage are structured.

Vanilla:
    The Boss Rush, Wily Machine 7, and Wily Capsule remain one
    continuous stage. The configured Final Wily Stage requirement
    controls access to this stage.

Split:
    The Boss Rush becomes a separate stage unlocked by the
    Boss Rush Access Code. Completing it returns to stage select.

    The Final Wily Stage contains Wily Machine 7 and Wily Capsule
    and is unlocked by the configured Final Wily Stage requirement.

    When Wily Stages is selected as the requirement type, completing
    the Boss Rush counts as one of the four possible Wily stage clears.

Skip:
    The Boss Rush is skipped. The Final Wily Stage begins immediately
    before Wily Machine 7 and is unlocked by the configured
    Final Wily Stage requirement.

options.label: Final Wily Stage Requirement
options.description:
Determines what is required to access the Final Wily Stage,
containing Wily Machine 7 and Wily Capsule.

In Split mode, the Boss Rush is a separate stage and does not
automatically have to be completed. It can contribute toward
the Wily Stages requirement.

options.label: Wily Stages Required for Final Stage
options.description:
With the Wily Stages requirement, sets the number of completed
Wily stages required to access the Final Wily Stage.

Wily 1, Wily 2, and Wily 3 can each count toward this requirement.

In Split mode, the Boss Rush is a separate fourth Wily stage
and can also count toward this requirement. A value of 4 therefore
requires Wily 1, Wily 2, Wily 3, and the Boss Rush to be completed.

Outside Split mode, the maximum effective value is 3.
A configured value of 4 is then automatically reduced to 3.

options.label: Robot Masters Required for Final Stage
options.description:
With the Robot Masters requirement, sets the number of defeated
Robot Masters required to access the Final Wily Stage.

options.label: Weapons Required for Final Stage
options.description:
With the Weapons requirement, sets the number of Robot Master
weapons required to access the Final Wily Stage.

worlds.game: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

options.label: Logic difficulty
options.description:
Difficulty of the logic.

- **moki** (or easy): Recommended for beginners, who only played the game casually.
- **gorlek** (or medium): Harder paths that can use sword and hammer as movement options, and damage boosts.
- **kii** (or hard): Hard and precise paths that use energy weapons as movement.
- **unsafe**: Very hard and unverified paths. Warning: some paths are **extremely hard**.

options.label: Glitches
options.description:
Whether the logic includes paths with glitches. The required tricks depend on the logic difficulty.

- **Gorlek**: includes grounded sentry jumps, sentry as a fire source, breaking walls with Shuriken, and removing
  the kill plane in Feeding Grounds.
- **Kii**: glitches are not included in Kii logic yet.
- **Unsafe**: everything else.

options.label: Starting location
options.description:
Choose the starting location.

- **vanilla**: spawn in Inkwater Marsh.
- Teleporter name: spawn in this teleporter.
  Possible values: marsh, burrows, howlsden, hollow, glades, wellspring, westwoods, eastwoods,
  reach, depths, eastpools, westpools, westwastes, eastwastes, outerruins, innerruins, willow, shriek.
- **random_tp**: Spawn at a random teleporter (there are weights applied internally for this option).
- **random_loc**: Spawn at a random location (usually placed on a checkpoint).

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Set conditions for entering the final boss. Use the rando wheel (with **V**) to check goal progress.

- **trees**: All trees must be collected.
- **wisps**: All wisps must be collected.
- **quests**: All quests have to be finished.
- **relics**: Place relics in some areas, all of them must be collected.
- **one_random**: Choose one goal at random among the other selected ones.
  e.g. ['one_random', 'trees', 'wisps'] will give trees or wisps.
  If only one_random is selected, it will choose among all goals.

options.label: Relic Count
options.description: How many areas contain a relic (no effect without the relic goal).

options.label: Launch Fragments
options.description: Spilt Launch into multiple fragments.

options.label: Required Launch Fragments
options.description: Set the amount of launch fragments needed to get Launch.

options.label: Total Launch Fragments
options.description: Set the amount of launch fragments in the pool. Launch is in logic when all fragments are accessible.

options.label: Hard mode
options.description: Play the game in hard difficulty.

options.label: Free Regenerate
options.description: Ignore Regenerate in the region requirements.

options.label: Free Teleporters
options.description: Remove the requirements on teleporters for their hard lock skill (e.g. Reach TP requires Flap).

options.label: Randomize Doors
options.description:
Randomize entrances between the doors.

- **disabled** (or false): no randomization.
- **coupled** (or enabled or true): randomize doors 2 by 2 (going back will put you where you entered the door).
- **decoupled**: the entrances are fully shuffled for both entering and exiting a door.

options.label: Quality of life
options.description: Activate QOL features and gameplay improvements.

options.label: Shrines and trials hints
options.description: Display the reward for shrines and trials when activating them.

options.label: Zone hints
options.description: Lupo sells hints that indicate how many progression items are in the area.

options.label: Unpopular paths
options.description:
Enable unpopular paths for unsafe.

These involve tedious or extremely hard tricks. No effect without unsafe and glitches.

options.label: Teleporters
options.description: Add most teleporters to the item pool.

options.label: Extra teleporters
options.description: Add Ruins, West Pools and Shriek teleporters to the pool.

options.label: Bonus items
options.description: Add to the pool items specific to the randomizer.

options.label: Extra bonus items
options.description: Add to the pool powerful items specific to the randomizer.

options.label: Skill upgrades
options.description: Add to the pool upgrades to skills specific to the randomizer.

options.label: Better random spawn
options.description: Open some doors so random spawn works better.

options.label: Better Wellspring
options.description: The top door of Wellspring Glades is opened by default.

options.label: No Rain
options.description: Remove the rain in Marsh, and remove Howl.

options.label: No Combat
options.description:
Skip all combat heavy parts.

- **everything**: the same as if you include all the following
- **shrines**: Shrine have their pickup floating above them before the fight
- **arenas**: the arenas start as completed
- **demi bosses**: Demi Bosses like Howl, Beetle and Rock boss start as defeated
- **bosses**: Bosses like Kwolok, Mora and Shriek's combat phases are skipped

options.label: No Trials
options.description: Trials are already completed.

options.label: No Willow hearts
options.description: Willow hearts are already destroyed.

options.label: Quests
options.description:
Change which quests are in the location pool.

- **all**: All quests are present.
- **no_hand**: Remove the Hand-to-hand questline from the locations.
- **none**: Remove all quests that involve talking to NPCs. Main quests (e.g. wisps) or rebuilding Glades are
  still in the pool.

options.label: No Keystone doors
options.description: Open keystone doors by default (and remove keystones from the pool).

options.label: Open mode
options.description: Open most of the doors and obstacles.

options.label: Glades Done
options.description: Start with Glades rebuilt and regrown.

options.label: Spawn with Sword
options.description: Choose to have Sword at the beginning.

options.label: Spawn with Regenerate
options.description: Choose to have Regenerate at the beginning.

options.label: Vanilla shop upgrades
options.description: Weapon upgrades and shards in shops are not randomized.

options.label: Launch on Seir
options.description: Place launch on Seir (i.e. the wisp in the ruins).

options.label: DeathLink amnesty
options.description: Disable/enable death link. Set this to a non-zero integer to specify how many deaths are needed to trigger it.

options.label: Knowledge hints
options.description: Display useful hints on randomizer knowledge while playing the seed.

options.label: Shop Keywords Icons
options.description:
Have the non-local items in the shops attempt to use a keyword system to choose icons.
For example, item with 'map' in their name will have a map icon.
If no keyword fit, then the icon fall back to Classification.

options.label: Skip cutscenes
options.description: Skip most cutscenes, and makes then skippable in the pause menu.

options.label: UT Glitched Configuration
options.description:
Configuration for Universal Tracker glitched logic. This doesn't affect generation.

- **one_level**: Add the next logic level.
- **glitch**: Add glitches from the current logic level (and one above if `one_level` is also used).
- **free_region**: Remove requirements on max health and Regenerate for entering an area.
- **free_tp**: Remove skills requirements on some teleporters (same effect as `free_teleporters`).
- **max_logic**: Set the logic to unsafe + unpopular + glitches and remove region/tp requirements.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
What you need to do to beat the game.
Fireworks requires you to get the 4 flames and defeat the Manticore. The House Key is placed in its vanilla location.
Egg Hunt requires you to collect the amount of eggs you need to open the 4th Egg Door, then open the chest inside.

options.label: Eggs Required
options.description:
How many Eggs you need to open the 4th Egg Door.
The amount of Eggs you need for the other 3 doors will scale accordingly.
This is intentionally locked at 64 until we can figure it out client-side.

options.label: Key Ring
options.description:
Have one keyring which unlocks all normal key doors instead of individual key items.
Note: Due to how consumable key logic works, if this option is not enabled, you logically require all 6 keys to open any of the key doors.

options.label: Matchbox
options.description:
Have one matchbox which can light all candles instead of individual match items.
Note: Due to how consumable item logic works, if this option is not enabled, you logically require all 9 matches to light any of the candles.

options.label: Candle Checks
options.description: Lighting each of the candles sends a check.

options.label: Bunnies as Checks
options.description:
Include the secret bunnies as checks.
Exclude Tedious removes the Mural, Dream, UV, and Floor is Lava bunnies.
The Disc Spike bunny will not be a check unless you have multiple disc hops or you have both precise tricks and wheel tricks enabled.

options.label: Bunny Warps in Logic
options.description:
Include the songs that warp you to Bunny spots in logic.
If you have Bunnies as Checks enabled, this option is automatically enabled.

options.label: Fruitsanity
options.description:
All 115 fruits send a check after being eaten.
Tip: Attempting to eat a fruit 3 times will eat it even if you have full health.

options.label: Exclude Song Chests
options.description:
Exclude the Wheel chest and Office Key chests, so that you don't have to play their songs.
They will contain either filler or traps.

options.label: Randomize Final Egg
options.description:
Choose whether the 65th Egg is shuffled into the multiworld item pool or placed in its vanilla location, requiring opening the 4th Egg Door to access it.
This option is forced on if you have the egg hunt goal selected.

options.label: Tanking Damage
options.description:
Include tricks which require you to voluntarily take damage in order to perform them in logic.
You may be expected to take up to three points of damage to perform tricks enabled by this option.

options.label: Bubble Jumping
options.description:
Include using the standard Bubble Wand and chaining bubble jumps together in logic.
Short Chains means you may be expected to chain a few bubble jumps in a row.
Long Chains means you may be expected to chain an unlimited number of bubble jumps in a row.

options.label: Midair Disc Jumping
options.description:
Include jumping onto the disc without letting it bounce off of a wall first in logic.
Single means doing it once from the ground.
Multiple means having to chain them in midair.

options.label: Wheel Tricks
options.description:
Include some tricks that involve using the wheel in unconventional ways.
Simple means toggling wheel midair to "double jump", or mashing against walls to climb them.
Advanced also adds more complicated tech, such as braking on walls or climbing walls out of jumps.
Note: Tricks using wheel desyncs or wrong warps are not ever considered logical.

options.label: Ball Throwing
options.description:
Include using the ball to hit switches or buttons not "designed" for it in logic.
Off means the ball will rarely be used for anything other than breaking blocks, spikes, or guard shields.
Simple means the ball can be used to hit easy targets without any real rebound, setup, or movement. Most "yoyo chute" buttons are included here.
Advanced means hitting your target may require bouncing off a wall or moving while throwing to adjust momentum/angle.
Expert includes more complicated tricks including those that require specific setups or getting lucky.

options.label: Flute Jumps
options.description: Include sliding off of the edge of a platform while pulling out the flute so that you can jump mid-air while playing the flute.

options.label: Obscure Tricks
options.description:
Include solutions to puzzles that are obscure or hard to understand in logic.
These tricks won't be harder to perform than other tricks in logic once you know them.

options.label: Precise Tricks
options.description:
Include solutions to puzzles that are mechanically difficult to execute in logic.
These tricks may require large amounts of attempts to get right, and there may be a higher than usual cost for failure.

options.label: Home Captures Only
options.description:
Intended for players familiar with deeper mechanics of Paquerette:
Enabling this will mean only home-captures are sufficient to unlock an item.

options.label: Expert Routing
options.description: Enabling this feature may create routes that require advanced techniques or have complicating pathing.

options.label: Victory Condition
options.description:
Determines your victory condition.
For short games or new players, we recommend Credits.

- **Credits**: Reach the Credits! Beginner-friendliest choice.
- **Golden Bunny**: Find the Golden Bunny!
- **Golden Fluff**: Capture bunnies until you find all Golden Fluff!
- **Full Clear**: Capture all bunnies!

options.label: Golden Fluff
options.description:
**GOLDEN FLUFF RUNS ONLY**
Determines how much Golden Fluff will be scattered through your world!

options.label: Unlock Computer
options.description: Unlock the portable computer by default

options.label: Unlock Map
options.description: Unlock the map in the computer by default

options.label: Elevator Trap Odds
options.description: Odds of generating an Elevator trap instead of junk

options.label: Surface Trap Odds
options.description: Odds of generating a Return to Surface trap instead of junk

options.label: DeathLink
options.description: Should deathlink be enabled?

options.label: Death Link Behavior
options.description:
Deaths through Death Link will activate a trap.

- **Surface**: Returns Paquerette to the surface!
- **Elevator**: Elevator :)

options.label: Elevator Trap Depth
options.description: How long of an Elevator Ride should you have?

options.label: Elevator Trap Increment
options.description: Every time you ride, the ride gets longer!

options.label: Goal
options.description:
The victory condition for your slot.

- good_ending: reach the Good Ending (defeat the End Demon with the Magic Sword
  and the Purified Stone, then leave through the front gate).
- true_ending: reach the Good Ending after restoring the owner's soul
  (requires the 3 Soul Fragments). This is the default.
- all_endings: see all 11 endings (the demo ending is excluded).

options.label: Keep Shears
options.description:
If enabled, the Shears (secateurs) stay in their VANILLA location - the player hut -
instead of being shuffled into the multiworld. Improves early-game accessibility, since
cutting grass is the renewable source of income.

Note: with lock_player_hut on (the default), the hut itself is locked, so the vanilla
shears still sit behind the Abandoned Key.

options.label: Exclude Bridge Key
options.description:
If enabled (default), the Bridge Key stays in its vanilla location instead of
being shuffled into the multiworld.

The Bridge Key is THE first key of the game: it opens spawn (the bus stop on the
road) into the garden, and the bus blocks every other exit. When it is shuffled
(this option off), sphere 1 contains only the "Obtain BridgeKey" check itself
(plus the bus gulden if coinsanity is on) - always at least one check, so no
special generation handling is needed, but the start is extremely restricted.
Turning this off is discouraged for async play without coinsanity.

options.label: Polaroid Checks
options.description:
If enabled (default), collecting the world's polaroids sends checks.
(Ending polaroids are awarded by the endings themselves and are never shuffled.)

options.label: Ghost Checks
options.description: If enabled (default), calming the 7 ghosts scattered across the world sends checks.

options.label: Coinsanity
options.description:
If enabled, the 15 placed gulden become checks, and buying things requires
receiving "Gulden" items from the multiworld instead of cutting grass for money.

options.label: Persistent Shortcuts
options.description:
If enabled, comfort shortcuts are restored after each run reset: the Bijkeuken
shortcut, the hedge cut out of the back yard, the park's hay-bale garden and maze
accesses, the bramble burnt between the park and the road, and any lock already
opened. Read by the client mod; no logic impact.

options.label: Lock Player Hut
options.description:
Enabled by default. The player hut door is locked and requires the Abandoned Key (an
orphan key in vanilla: the v0.3 door table shows it unlocks nothing - it most likely
opened this very hut originally).

IMPORTANT - what the key really gates: the only usable BED is inside the hut (dump:
Hide_PlayerSchuur/interior/bed0; the game's only other bed is in the endgame
AtticRoom), so the key also gates SLEEPING, i.e. reaching day 2+. The logic models
this via rules.can_advance_days: the Mist ending (day 3), the Bus ending
(dayIndex >= 2), the Ferry crossing (day 2) and Calm Ghost #3 (redCar, day 2) all
require the key when this option is on [2026-07-27, playtest]. It also gates the
vanilla Shears / Toilet Key spots and the Sunday-evening hallway.

The Abandoned Key therefore becomes an early, high-value progression item - especially
interesting in multiworld, where it can come from another player's world. Turn this off
for a looser run where the hut (and sleeping) is free from the start.

options.label: Trap Percentage
options.description: Percentage of filler items that are replaced by traps.

options.label: Buff Count (per buff)
options.description:
How many copies of each progressive buff (Move Speed / Cutter Range / Cutting
Rate) are added to the item pool.

options.label: Death Link
options.description:
Death link. Every death ending you meet (any ending except Bus, Picnic and the
good/true ending) sends a DeathLink to the multiworld. Receiving a DeathLink shows
a nightmare jumpscare and resets your current run (week) - no ending is triggered
and no check is granted.

options.label: Chore Checks
options.description:
If enabled (default), finishing a maintenance job sends a check: trimming every hedge,
cutting all the grass, clearing every molehill, watering every flower and picking up all
the litter IN THE START GARDEN, plus trimming the 8 potted plants scattered around the
world.
