options.label: Include Endless Locations
options.description: Include Endless Mode loop locations in the location pool.

options.label: Include Extra Difficulty Locations
options.description: Include clear locations for difficulties above the goal (up through D8).

options.label: Death Link
options.description: When enabled, dying in a run sends a DeathLink to other players.

options.label: Unlock All Characters
options.description:
Start with every character unlock item already in your inventory.
When off (default), only the slot's starting character is free. Cinder / Lisver /
Mango / Nera each need their Archipelago unlock item if they are not that starter —
the game's own achievement unlocks are not required.

options.label: Randomize All Dice
options.description: Shuffle which dice unlock each dice-related Archipelago item grants.

options.label: Randomize All Relics
options.description: Shuffle which relic unlock each relic Archipelago item grants.

options.label: Randomize All Potions
options.description: Shuffle potion unlocks and in-run potion rewards.

options.label: Random Starting Character
options.description:
The starting character is chosen when the multiworld is generated and locked for
the whole seed. That character is playable from the start. Everyone else — including
Cinder — needs their Archipelago unlock item unless Unlock All Characters is on.

options.label: Random Starting Relic
options.description: Pick a random starting relic from the available initial relic options.

options.label: Shop Check Count
options.description:
How many general shop purchases are Archipelago checks. Each one is sent by buying
an offer in a shop, so a higher count means more of the run's shopping is checks.

options.label: Remove Cursed Relics
options.description:
Remove cursed relics from the multiworld completely. They are not placed as
items or obtain checks, never appear as rewards or shop stock, and received
cursed relic items are discarded instead of granted.

options.label: Unique Character Checks
options.description:
Duplicate progression and shop checks per playable character. Beating a boss or
buying from a shop as Cinder is a different check from doing so as Lisver, Nera, or
Mango. Obtaining a die, relic, or potion is still one shared check.

options.label: Starting Maps
options.description: Number of maps to start with unlocked

options.label: Maps to Complete
options.description:
Number of maps to complete for victory when Goal is set to Complete Maps.
Ignored when Goal is set to Goal Map.

options.label: Number of Maps
options.description: Number of maps to include in the world.

options.label: Target Week
options.description: Target week level to complete.

options.label: Max Weeks
options.description: Maximum number of weeks per map

options.label: Game Mode
options.description:
Game mode to play:
Classic: Standard Mini Metro rules.
Extreme: Lines cannot be redrawn after being placed.

options.label: Trap Chance
options.description:
Percentage of filler items replaced with traps:
Rush Hour: A station gets overcrowded.
Renovation: Your lines get removed and you must rebuild them from scratch.
Delayed: Your next week is delayed by another week.
Derailed: One of your trains gets permanently removed.

options.label: Map Shard Count Mode
options.description:
How many shards the player must collect to unlock each map.
    Static: pre-calculated from Max Weeks (max(max_weeks - 1 if max_weeks < 5 else max_weeks - 2, 1)).
    Custom: use the value of Custom Shard Count below.
In either mode the count is lowered if the shard items would not fit in the
world's locations.

options.label: Custom Shard Count
options.description:
Shards required per map when Map Shard Count Mode is set to Custom. Ignored
in Static mode. Higher values mean longer per-map gating between unlocks.
Lowered automatically if there aren't enough locations to hold every shard.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Victory condition:
Complete Maps: clear Target Week on the configured number of maps (Maps to Complete).
Goal Map: clear Target Week on a single chosen map (Goal Map below).

options.label: Victory Condition
options.description:
The condition needed to beat Glover.
Endscreen: Get to the endscreen.
Crystal Count: Get the number of crystals required to the castle cave.
Golden Garibs: Get the number of Golden Garib items required

options.label: Required Crystals
options.description: The number of crystals needed to beat Glover while Victory Condition is Crystal Count. Default 4.

options.label: Golden Garib Count
options.description: The number of Golden Garibs in the world pool while Victory Condition is Golden Garibs. Default 12.

options.label: Golden Garibs Requirement
options.description: The number of Golden Garibs required to win while Victory Condition is Golden Garibs. Default 6.

options.label: Logic Difficulty
options.description:
What tricks are allowed. Default Intended.
Intended: No clips, no skips, no glitches. Things that are reasonable for a player to do.
Easy Tricks: Jumping through the garib completion marks is expected. Things that are hard to do that don't require glitches, and minor skips are allowed.
Hard Tricks: Any glitches and clips are expected.

options.label: Starting Ball
options.description:
Set the ball you start with. Default Crystal.
Any Random and Power Ball require Power Ball Transformation to be enabled.

options.label: Garib Logic
options.description:
How the garibs are placed in logic. Default Garib Groups.
Level Garibs: Acts as vanilla Glover.
Garib Groups: Each group of garibs in a level is a check. You are sent bundles of garibs.
Garibsanity: Each garib is a check. You can be sent individual garibs.

options.label: Garib Sorting
options.description:
Where Garibs are sent to. Default In Order. Ignored if Garib Logic is Level Garibs.
By Level: Garibs sent to you are from specific levels, and all garibs from that level must be gotten to get a completion mark.
In Order: Garibs are sent to levels in world order.
Random Order: Garibs are sent to levels in a random order.

options.label: Mad Garibs
options.description: Swaps garibs with the Mad Garib variant.

options.label: Random Garib Sounds
options.description:
Makes garib sounds use random sounds instead.
Only works if garibs are not Level Garibs.

options.label: Disable Garib Items
options.description:
Replaces filler garib items with other items from the filler table.
Only works if garibs are enabled and aren't required to unlock checks.

options.label: Entrance Randomizer
options.description: Loading zones are randomized. Default on.

options.label: Entrance Overrides
Open Worlds
options.description: All the world portals start open. Default off.

options.label: Open Levels
options.description: All doors in each wayroom start open. Default off.

options.label: Open Level Bosslock
options.description:
Opens doors 1, 2 and 3 in each world and only lets you access the boss when all 3 have been completed.
Incompatable with Open Levels and Portalsanity.

options.label: Portalsanity
options.description: Goals and All Garibs in Level are checks. Portals and garib completion marks are items. Default off.

options.label: Spawn Randomizer
options.description: Spawning checkpoints are randomized. Default off.

options.label: Include Bonus Levels
options.description: Makes Bonus Levels contain checks. Default on.

options.label: Tag Link
options.description: When you transform the ball, everyone who enabled tag link changes character or the ball. Of course, the reverse is true too. Default off.

options.label: Trap Link
options.description: When you get a trap, sends a similar trap to everyone else with trap link enabled. Of course, the reverse is true too. Default off.

options.label: Randomize Jump
options.description: Start without jump. Default off.

options.label: Randomize Power Ball
options.description: Adds the Power Ball to the items. Default off.

options.label: Randomize Checkpoints
options.description: Checkpoints are checks and items. Default off.

options.label: Randomize Switches
options.description: Switches are checks and level events are items. Default on.

options.label: Mr. Tip Checks
options.description: Mr. Tips are checks. Default on.

options.label: Enemysanity
options.description: Enemies that can normally be defeated are checks.

options.label: Insectity
options.description: Defeating insects are checks.

options.label: Total Scores
options.description:
What total scores being reached will give checks.
Formatted ["Score Value A", "Score Value B"]
Example ["50000", "100000"]
Scores must be a multiple of 10000.

options.label: Easy Ball Walk
options.description: Forces the game to de-invert ball controls.

options.label: Mr. Tip Hints
options.description:
Mr. Tips give AP hints. Default 1.
Catagory only will tell you a vauge hint in regards to the quality, but not the item.

options.label: Cheat Chicken Hints
options.description: Cheat Chicken gives AP hints. Default 3.

options.label: Mr. Tip Text Display
options.description:
Sets the text of Mr. Tip Textboxes. Default Hints and Custom.
Off: Ingame Mr. Tips do not display text.
Hints and Custom: Displays hint text until there are no more hints, and then falls back to custom.
Custom Only: Only displays custom text. Multiworld hints can still be given.

options.label: Mr. Hint Scouts
options.description: Makes Mr. Tip's hints show up as multiworld hints.

options.label: Filler Duration
options.description:
On a scale from 1-5, how full the potion bottle gets when you are given a filler effect.
This also changes the duration of traps.

options.label: Bonus Garib
options.description: How many Garibs 'Extra Garibs' are worth. Only applies if Garib Sorting is not By Level.

options.label: Trap Percent
options.description: What percentage of checks that would be filler are replaced with traps. Default is 20.

options.label: Extra Garibs Weight
options.description: The weight of filler items that are Extra Garibs. Default is 0.

options.label: Chicken Sound (Nothing) Weight
options.description: The weight of filler items that play a chicken noise. That's it. Default is 10.

options.label: Life Weight
options.description: The weight of filler items that are Extra Lives. Default is 50.

options.label: Boomerang Ball Weight
options.description: The weight of filler items that are Boomerang Balls. Default is 5.

options.label: Beach Ball Weight
options.description: The weight of filler items that are Beach Balls. Default is 5.

options.label: Hercules Potion Weight
options.description: The weight of filler items that are Hercules Potions. Default is 5.

options.label: Helicopter Potion Weight
options.description: The weight of filler items that are Helicopter Potions. Default is 5.

options.label: Speed Potion Weight
options.description: The weight of filler items that are Speed Potions. Default is 5.

options.label: Frog Potion Weight
options.description: The weight of filler items that are Frog Potions. Default is 5.

options.label: Death Potion Weight
options.description: The weight of filler items that are Death Potions. Default is 5.

options.label: Sticky Potion Weight
options.description: The weight of filler items that are Sticky Potions. Default is 5.

options.label: Big Ball Weight
options.description: The weight of filler items that are Big Balls. Default is 5.

options.label: Low Gravity Weight
options.description: The weight of filler items that are Low Gravity. Default is 5.

options.label: Frog Trap Weight
options.description: The weight of traps that are Frog Traps. Default is 20.

options.label: Cursed Ball Trap Weight
options.description: The weight of traps that are Cursed Ball. Default is 20.

options.label: Instant Crystal Trap Weight
options.description: The weight of traps that are Crystal Transformations. Default is 15.

options.label: Camera Tilt Trap Weight
options.description: The weight of traps that are Camera Tilts. Default is 15.

options.label: Fish Eye Trap Weight
options.description: The weight of traps that are Fish Eyes. Default is 15.

options.label: Enemy Ball Trap Weight
options.description: The weight of traps that make your ball an enemy. Default is 10.

options.label: Control Ball Trap Weight
options.description: The weight of traps that turn you into the ball. Default is 10.

options.label: Invisiball Trap Weight
options.description: The weight of traps that make your ball vanish. Default is 5.

options.label: Tip Trap Weight
options.description:
The weight of traps that are Tips.
!! UNIMPLIMENTED !!

options.label: Generate Puml
options.description:
Generates a .puml file of the world for debugging use with the AP Logic Builder. Default off.
!! DEBUG !!

options.label: Alien Hunters DLC
options.description:
Set which locations and items from the Alien Hunters DLC are enabled.

none:                 All Alien Hunters DLC locations and items are disabled.
no_integrated_dlc:    Experimental Weapons location is disabled; for playing without the Integrated DLC option.
no_alien_rulers:      Alien Ruler locations are disabled; for avoiding tedious encounters.
all:                  All Alien Hunters DLC locations and items are enabled.

options.label: Shen's Last Gift DLC
options.description: Enable locations and items from the Shen's Last Gift DLC.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Set the goal of the seed.

alien_fortress:         Beat the Alien Fortress Assault mission. (final mission)
network_tower:          Beat the ADVENT Network Tower Assault mission. (second to last mission)
chosen_stronghold_1:    Beat any Chosen Stronghold Assault mission.
chosen_stronghold_2:    Beat any two Chosen Stronghold Assault missions.
chosen_stronghold_3:    Beat all three Chosen Stronghold Assault missions.

alien_fortress and network_tower (without extra considerations) are only recommended for async settings.
For sync settings, try chosen_stronghold_1 or chosen_stronghold_2 first and experiment from there.

options.label: Campaign Completion Requirements
options.description:
Require these objectives to be completed for the final mission to be unlocked.
Set all if you wish to experience a more vanilla XCOM 2 story progression.

'PsiGateObjective':         Require completion of the psi gate research.
'StasisSuitObjective':      Require completion of the stasis suit research.
'AvatarCorpseObjective':    Require acquisition of an avatar corpse.

options.label: Exclude Post-Goal Locations
options.description:
Exclude locations that are considered more difficult than the selected goal event.
These locations will not contain important items or items from other worlds.
Recommended when using an early goal option, e.g. in sync settings.
NOTE: This option requires enabling additional vacant locations, e.g. through Enemysanity or Itemsanity.

options.label: Enemysanity
options.description: Enable locations for the first kill of each enemy type.

options.label: Itemsanity
options.description: Enable locations for the first use of each item type.

options.label: Ranksanity
options.description:
Shuffle soldier rank-up locations and promotion items.

none:               Do not shuffle soldier promotions.
base_classes_only:  Only shuffle promotions for the four base soldier classes.
no_spark:           Only shuffle promotions for the four base soldier classes and the three faction hero classes.
no_faction_heroes:  Only shuffle promotions for the four base soldier classes and SPARKs.
all:                Shuffle promotions for all eight soldier classes.

options.label: Global Promotions
options.description:
Enable global promotions for all soldier classes, including those not covered by Ranksanity.
This adds no locations to the multiworld but rewards default promotion items for rank-up events of all classes,
meaning when one soldier reaches a certain rank, all soldiers of the same class will now have that rank going forward.
Recommended if you want insurance against DeathLink without enabling full Ranksanity (as it "saves your progress").

options.label: Chosen Huntsanity
options.description: Shuffle Chosen Hunt covert actions and their rewards, i.e. Resistance Faction influence and Chosen Stronghold missions.

options.label: Progressive Items
options.description:
Force these items to be collected in order.
Valid values: 'GunTech', 'GunTech+' (includes [Tech] Modular Weapons),
              'ArmorTech', 'ArmorTech+' (includes [Tech] Hybrid Materials),
              'SwordTech', 'GREMLINTech', 'PsionicsTech'

options.label: Split Progressive Items
options.description:
Split eligible progressive items into separate upgrade tracks.

none:       Progressive items are not split and may contain upgrades from disparate tracks.
vanilla:    Progressive items are partially split while maintaining vanilla grouping of upgrades.

Example: '[Tech] Progressive Gun' contains upgrades for all guns in an order consistent with the tech tree.
With the vanilla option, it is split into '[Tech] Progressive Rifle/Shotgun' and '[Tech] Progressive Cannon/Sniper',
inspired by the vanilla upgrades provided by individual techs.

options.label: Chosen Weapon Fragments
options.description:
Split Chosen weapons into two or three fragments each. Collect all fragments to unlock the corresponding tech.
This should decrease the likelihood of receiving Chosen weapons too early and trivializing the game.
NOTE: This option requires enabling additional vacant locations, e.g. through Enemysanity or Itemsanity.

options.label: Early Proving Ground
options.description: Force the Proving Ground to be unlockable very early (sphere 1).

options.label: Resource Share
options.description: Set the share of filler items to be resources.

options.label: Weapon Mod Share
options.description: Set the share of filler items to be weapon upgrades.

options.label: PCS Share
options.description: Set the share of filler items to be PCSs.

options.label: Staff Share
options.description: Set the share of filler items to be staff.

options.label: Trap Share
options.description: Set the share of filler items to be traps.

options.label: Active Traps
options.description:
Allow these traps to be shuffled into the item pool.
Valid values: 'DoomTrap', 'MarketTrap', 'YapTrap', 'ADVENTTrap',
              'AlienTrap', 'AmmoTrap', 'PanicTrap', 'EarthquakeTrap'

options.label: Nothing Share
options.description: Set the share of filler items to be nothing.

options.label: Enemy Rando
options.description: Enable enemy shuffle, randomizing both scripted and procedural encounters.

options.label: Enemy Plando Preset
options.description:
Override enemy plando with a preset configuration.

custom:         All enemies are shuffled by default. Edit enemy plando manually for finer control.
advent_only:    Only ADVENT enemies are shuffled.
aliens_only:    Only alien (non-ADVENT) enemies are shuffled.
separate:       ADVENT and non-ADVENT enemies are shuffled separately.

options.label: Enemy Plando
options.description:
If enemy rando is enabled, constrain enemy placements.
Define explicit shuffle groups with the 'forced' key.
Exempt enemies from shuffling with the 'fixed' key.

Example: {
    'forced': [
        [['Sectoid', 'Muton'], ['Viper', 'Archon']],
        [['Adv'], ['Adv']]
    ],
    'fixed': ['Gatekeeper', 'Sectopod']
}
Sectoids and Mutons will be replaced by Vipers and Archons randomly.
All ADVENT enemies will be replaced by random ADVENT enemies.
Gatekeepers and Sectopods will not be shuffled.
All other enemies will be shuffled among each other.

options.label: Remove Corpse Costs
options.description: Remove corpse costs from all items. Recommended if enemy rando is enabled.

options.label: Hint Research Projects
options.description:
Enable research project hints in the Avenger laboratory and shadow chamber.
Can be changed in-game via Mod Config Menu.

off:       Reveal no item info and don't create server hints.
partial:   Reveal item categories but don't create server hints.
full:      Reveal all item info and create server hints.

options.label: Skip Tedious Missions
options.description:
Automatically skip these mission types when they are spawned from a regular calendar event.
Can be changed in-game via Mod Config Menu.
Valid values: 'SupplyRaid', 'CouncilMission', 'ResistanceOp'

options.label: Disarm Covert Action Risks
options.description:
Disable these covert action risks.
Can be changed in-game via Mod Config Menu.
Valid values: 'Ambush', 'Capture'

options.label: Supply Raid Reward Base
options.description:
Set the amount of resources that are rewarded for skipped supply raids.
The base represents a percentage of set maximum values for supplies (200), alien alloys (80), elerium crystals (40) and elerium cores (3).
The error determines the range of possible values, e.g. 35-65% for default settings.
Can be changed in-game via Mod Config Menu.

options.label: Supply Raid Reward Error
options.description:
Set the amount of resources that are rewarded for skipped supply raids.
The base represents a percentage of set maximum values for supplies (200), alien alloys (80), elerium crystals (40) and elerium cores (3).
The error determines the range of possible values, e.g. 35-65% for default settings.
Can be changed in-game via Mod Config Menu.

options.label: Extra XP Gain
options.description:
Set the amount of extra XP that soldiers gain passively.
Each time an enemy dies, each soldier has the given fraction of a kill attributed to them, speeding up promotions.
Because this system is agnostic to who got the final hit, soldiers with low kill counts will benefit more from the increase.
In general, the effect will be much stronger than it seems; the default setting for example will work out to a 35% increase in XP from kills,
but something like a 140% increase in XP from assists, meaning the actual bonus lies somewhere in between.
Can be changed in-game via Mod Config Menu.

options.label: Extra Corpse Gain
options.description:
Set the amount of extra corpses that each enemy drops.
Can be changed in-game via Mod Config Menu.

options.label: DeathLink
options.description:
When one of XCOM's soldiers dies, everyone else who enabled DeathLink dies, and vice versa.
Can be changed in-game via Mod Config Menu.

options.label: DeathLink Chance
options.description:
Set the probability of a received DeathLink packet killing one of XCOM's soldiers.
Yes, it's random. That's XCOM, baby!
Can be changed in-game via Mod Config Menu.

options.label: Instant Rookie Training
options.description:
Make training rookies in the GTS instant.
Can be changed in-game via Mod Config Menu.

options.label: Instant SPARK Construction
options.description:
Make constructing SPARKs in the Proving Ground instant. No effect if Shen's Last Gift DLC is disabled.
Can be changed in-game via Mod Config Menu.

options.label: Refund SPARK Costs
options.description:
Get construction costs refunded when a SPARK is destroyed. No effect if Shen's Last Gift DLC is disabled.
Can be changed in-game via Mod Config Menu.

options.label: Replace Faction Heroes
options.description:
Gain automatic replacements for dead or missing faction heroes.
Can be changed in-game via Mod Config Menu.

options.label: Disable Day One Traps
options.description:
Disable traps received before the first day of a campaign.
Can be changed in-game via Mod Config Menu.

options.label: Disable Turn One Traps
options.description:
Disable traps received before the first turn of a mission.
Can be changed in-game via Mod Config Menu.

options.label: Active Mods
options.description:
Activate these mods from the x2wotc/mods directory.
This is only relevant when modding *the APWorld* (NOT the game), leave empty if you're unsure what that means.
Read about APWorld mods at https://github.com/Snyax/X2WOTCArchipelago/blob/main/worlds/x2wotc/docs/apworld_mods.md
List all available mods with the /mods client command.

options.label: Starting Character
options.description: Which character do you want to start with? Random will pick one for you.

options.label: Milestone Difficulty
options.description:
Scales the score required for milestones.
Easy: 50% score required.
Normal: 100% score required.
Hard: 200% score required.

options.label: Trap Weight
options.description: How many traps (Doom, Earthquake, Roulette) should be in the pool?

options.label: Points Item Value
options.description: Points granted by each '100 Points' item received.

options.label: Starter Pool
options.description: If enabled, you will start with a random assortment of coins based on rarity.

options.label: Common Starter Count
options.description: Number of Common coins to start with.

options.label: Uncommon Starter Count
options.description: Number of Uncommon coins to start with.

options.label: Rare Starter Count
options.description: Number of Rare coins to start with.

options.label: Epic Starter Count
options.description: Number of Epic coins to start with.

options.label: Core Starter Count
options.description: Number of coins with the 'Core' tag to start with.

options.label: AP Ball Spawn Mode
options.description:
How should AP prize balls spawn?
Counter: Spawns exactly every N prize balls.
Percentage: Has a % chance to replace any regular prize ball.

options.label: AP Ball Spawn Count
options.description: If using Counter mode, every Nth prize ball will be an AP ball.

options.label: AP Ball Spawn Chance
options.description: If using Percentage mode, the % chance any prize ball becomes an AP ball.

options.label: Required Victories
options.description: How many characters must clear Round 15 to trigger the Archipelago victory condition.

options.label: Checks Per Character
options.description:
How many checks each character will provide when catching their AP Prize Balls.
Lower numbers mean a faster game.

options.label: Wins Required
options.description:
The number of runs you need to win to complete your goal.

Each win must be done with a different character.

options.label: Starting Characters
options.description:
Determines your set of starting characters.

Characters omitted from "Include Characters" will not be included regardless of this option.

If a DLC option is chosen but the DLC is not enabled, an error will be raised during generation.

* Default All: Start with the default characters from the base game and all enabled DLCs.
* Random All: Start with random characters chosen from the base game and all enabled DLCs.
* Default Base Game: Start with Well Rounded, Brawler, Crazy, Ranger and Mage.
* Random Base Game: Start with random characters from the base game only.
* Default Abyssal Terrors: Start with Sailor, Curious, Builder, Captain, and Creature.
* Random Abyssal Terrors: Start with random characters from the Abyssal Terrors DLC.

options.label: Include Base Game Characters
options.description:
Which base game characters to include for checks.

Characters not listed here will not be available to play. There will be no item to unlock them, and there will be
no run or wave complete checks associated with them.

options.label: Waves Per Check
options.description:
How many waves to win to receive a check.

1 means every wave is a check, 2 means every other wave, etc.

options.label: Number of Progressive Wave Caps
options.description:
The number of caps to put on the accessible waves.

You will not be able to play beyond the maximum wave cap until you find additional
Progressive Wave Cap items.

With one cap, all waves are accessible from the start.

With two caps, waves 1-10 are accessible from the start, and waves 11-20 require one
Progressive Wave Cap.

With four caps: waves 1-5 are accessible from the start, waves 6-10 require one
Progressive Wave Cap, waves 11-15 require two, waves 16-20 require 3.

options.label: Gold Reward Mode
options.description:
Chooses how gold rewards are given.

#. One Time: Gold items are only given once, in either the current run or the next run after receiving the item.
#. All Every Time: The total amount of gold received is given to the player at the start of every run. Since gold is
   a filler item, this can lead to the game being "won" very easily early on in larger multiworlds.

options.label: XP Reward Mode
options.description:
Chooses how XP rewards are given.

#. One Time: XP items are only given once, in either the current run or the next run after receiving the item.
#. All Every Time: The total amount of XP received is given to the player at the start of every run.

options.label: Enable Enemy XP
options.description:
Sets enemies will give XP or not.

If disabled, enemies will not give XP. The only XP will be from XP items in the multiworld. Upgrades will be from
leveling up and upgrade items received.

options.label: Spawn Normal Loot Crates
options.description:
Sets whether loot crates can still spawn when connected to a multiworld.

If off, then the only consumables that spawn will be the health items and the Archipelago drop item. No regular or
legendary loot crates will spawn.

If on, then loot crates will still spawn when there are no available Archipelago drops. See 'Loot Crate Groups' for
details.

options.label: Loot Crate Locations
options.description:
Replaces the in-game loot crate drops with an Archipelago item which must be picked up to generate a check.

How the drops are made available and how many are needed to make a check are controlled by the next two settings.

options.label: Crate Pickup Step
options.description:
The number of common loot crates which need to be picked up to count as a check.

1 means every crate is a check, 2 means every other crate, etc.

options.label: Legendary Loot Crate Locations
options.description:
Replaces the in-game legendary loot crate drops with an Archipelago item which must be picked up to generate a
check.

How the drops are made available and how many are needed to make a check are controlled by the next two settings.

options.label: Legendary Loot Crate Pickup Step
options.description:
The number of legendary loot crates which need to be picked up to count as a check.

1 means every crate is a check, 2 means every other crate, etc.

options.label: Include Elites in Logic
options.description:
Sets whether to consider elites when determining game logic.

Elites appear at Danger 2 and higher, on either wave 11 or 12, or wave 14 or 15, with
the horde wave appearing in the other pair. At Danger 4, another elite appears on
wave 17 or 18.

This only affects when legendary loot crates are in logic.

* When disabled, legendary loot crates are not in logic until you can reach wave 20
  with any character and kill the boss.
* When enabled, legendary loot crates are in logic starting at wave 11. You are
  current subject to RNG on whether the elite will spawn there versus the horde.

options.label: Common Items
options.description: The weight of Common/Tier 1/White items in the pool.

options.label: Uncommon Items
options.description: The weight of Uncommon/Tier 2/Blue items in the pool.

options.label: Rare Items
options.description: The weight of Rare/Tier 3/Purple items in the pool.

options.label: Legendary Items
options.description:
The weight of Legendary/Tier 4/Red items in the pool.

Note that this is for common crate drop locations only. An additional number of legendary items is also added for
each legendary crate drop location.

options.label: Common Upgrades
options.description: The number of Common/Tier 1/White upgrades to include in the item pool.

options.label: Uncommon Upgrades
options.description: The number of Uncommon/Tier 2/Blue upgrades to include in the item pool.

options.label: Rare Upgrades
options.description: The number of Rare/Tier 3/Purple upgrades to include in the item pool.

options.label: Legendary Upgrades
options.description: The number of Legendary/Tier 4/Red upgrades to include in the item pool.

options.label: Gold Weight
options.description:
Weight of Gold items in the item pool.

The actual value of each gold item will we randomly picked from:

* 10
* 25
* 50
* 100
* 200

options.label: XP Weight
options.description:
Weight of XP items in the item pool.

The actual value of each XP item will we randomly picked from:

* 5
* 10
* 25
* 50
* 100
* 150

options.label: Starting Shop Slots
options.description: How many slot the shop begins with. Missing slots are added as items.

options.label: Starting Shop Lock Buttons
options.description:
Add the "Lock" buttons in the shop as items.

Missing buttons will be disabled until they are received as items.

The button and shop slot are different items, so it's possible to receive the button without the shop.

* All: Start with all lock buttons enabled (vanilla behavior).
* None: Start with no lock buttons enabled at start.
* Match shop slots: Start with the same number of lock buttons as shop slots.
* Custom: Choose the number to start with using "Number of Lock Buttons".

options.label: Number of Lock Buttons
options.description:
The number of "Lock" buttons in the shop to start with.

Missing buttons will not be usable until they are received as items.

The button and shop slot are different items, so it's possible to receive the button without the shop.

options.label: Enable Abyssal Terrors DLC
options.description:
Enable options which require the "Abyssal Terrors" DLC.

Currently, this only enables adding the checks for all the DLC characters.

options.label: Include Abyssal Terrors Characters
options.description:
Which characters from the "Abyssal Terrors" DLC to include for checks.

Characters not listed here will not be available to play. There will be no item to unlock them, and there will be
no run or wave complete checks associated with them.

Does nothing if "Enable Abyssal Terrors DLC" is not set.

options.label: Supervisors Required
options.description:
How many Supervisor wins are required to complete the game.
The server will randomly assign which Supervisors count toward the goal.
Value must be between 1 and 11.

options.label: Supervisors In Pool
options.description:
How many Supervisor Unlock items are placed in the multiworld item pool.
Must be >= SupervisorsRequired. Extra unlocks beyond the required count
act as safety redundancy so the player isn't forced to receive every unlock.

options.label: Starting Supervisors
options.description:
How many Supervisors the player starts with already unlocked (chosen randomly
from SV1..SV11 at generation time). Useful to ensure the player always has
something to play on immediately.

options.label: Starting Items Per Shop
options.description:
How many items the player starts with already unlocked in EACH of the
3 shops (Normal Shop, Black Market, Cafe) - chosen randomly and
independently per shop, so every shop has real starting variety instead
of only the one you happen to sample into.

options.label: Starting Perks
options.description:
How many perks the player starts with already unlocked (chosen randomly
at generation time).

options.label: Include Challenges
options.description:
If enabled, Challenge completion locations are included in the randomizer.
Challenges can be difficult; disable this for a shorter seed.

options.label: Include Nubby Trials
options.description: If enabled, Nubby Trials level completion locations are included.

options.label: Include Shop Item Checks
options.description:
If enabled, each round that hosts a shop sells exactly one Archipelago
item; once bought, that round's shop never offers another for the rest
of the game. Up to 69 checks total.

options.label: Include Perk Checks
options.description:
If enabled, "AP Perk Purchase" locations are included for all tracked
perks (sent by buying the dedicated AP Item shop slot while it
represents that location - not detected via chest pickup), for up to
27 additional checks.

options.label: Include Round Milestone Checks
options.description:
If enabled, "Reach Round N" locations are included for the first-time
completion of round 5, 10, 15, ... up to 80, for 16 additional checks.

options.label: Include Restock Milestone Checks
options.description:
If enabled, locations are included for the first time a single round's
restocks reach 1, 2, 5, 10, 50, 100, 500, 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000,
6000, 7000, 8000, 9000, or 9999 - restocks only count together if
obtained within the same round. 17 checks total.

options.label: Points Check Count
options.description:
How many "Reach N Points" locations are included. Points accumulate
from a lifetime total that persists across runs: completing a round
awards 1 point for rounds 1-5, 2 points for rounds 6-10, 3 points for
rounds 11-15, and so on, increasing by 1 every 5 rounds. Locations are
placed for reaching 1, 2, 3, ... up to this many points.

options.label: Zone-Based Shops
options.description:
If enabled, the Normal Shop's AP-tracked item pool is split as evenly
as possible into 4 groups, one per zone (Zone 1 = rounds 1-20, Zone 2 =
21-40, Zone 3 = 41-60, Zone 4 = 61-80) - only that zone's own group is
purchasable while you're in it. Zone 5 (round 81+, endless) lifts the
restriction entirely: every AP-tracked item becomes purchasable there.
This paces which items can appear based on how far into a run the shop
is, rather than the full unlocked pool being available from round 5
onward. Only affects the Normal Shop - Black Market and Cafe are
unaffected.

options.label: Lock Zones Behind Items
options.description:
If enabled, advancing past round 20/40/60 (into Zone 2/3/4) requires a
Progressive Zone Unlock item - each one received opens the next locked
zone in sequence. Progress caps at the last round of your
currently-unlocked zone until the next one arrives - you keep clearing
that round's goal (with restocks) rather than getting stuck. Zone 1
(rounds 1-20) is always accessible.

options.label: Also Lock Zone 5 (Endless)
options.description:
If enabled (requires lock_zones), Zone 5 (round 81+, endless mode) is
also gated behind the Progressive Zone Unlock sequence, as its final
step. Has no effect if lock_zones is off.

options.label: Lock Grab-A-Tron Behind Item
options.description:
If enabled, the Grab-A-Tron claw machine minigame (a random round
event) does not appear until its Unlock item is received - the round
that would have triggered it plays out as a normal round instead.

options.label: Lock Black Market Behind Item
options.description:
If enabled, the Black Market (triggered by using a found Suspicious
Key on its round event) stays inert until its Unlock item is
received - that round falls back to a normal shop instead, same as
when the player has no key at all.

options.label: Lock Cafe Nubby Behind Item
options.description:
If enabled, the Cafe door in the main room does not respond to clicks
until its Unlock item is received.

options.label: Lock Nubby Trials Behind Item
options.description:
If enabled, the Nubby Trials tile (Challenge slot 10) cannot be
entered until its Unlock item is received, on top of the game's own
5-challenges-beaten requirement.

options.label: Lock Challenges Behind Item
options.description:
If enabled, Challenge mode as a whole is locked from a fresh room
(mirrors the existing Supervisor/Tony lock mechanism - edits the
game's own obj_GAME.U_ChallengeMode save flag directly) until its
Unlock item is received.

options.label: Lock Freeze Ability Behind Item
options.description:
If enabled, the game's own shop-offer-freeze ability (drag an offer
onto the freeze button to keep it from rerolling next visit) is
disabled until its Unlock item is received.

options.label: Include Traps
options.description:
If enabled, trap items are added to the pool: deletes an item from
inventory, deletes all coins, reduces lives to 1, disables a random
item for 5 rounds, or forces a random special event next round
(delayed a round if the next round is already a special event).

options.label: Nubby Filler Percent
options.description:
What percentage of the pool's padding slots are "Filler: Nubby" -
a no-op filler item that does nothing on arrival.

options.label: Custom Final Round
options.description:
If set above 80, the final boss encounter and win condition move to
this round instead of the vanilla round 80, and round 80 itself
becomes a regular special event round instead of the boss fight.
0 (default) keeps vanilla behavior (boss/win at round 80).

options.label: Score Goal
options.description:
If set above 0, completing the game also requires accumulating this
many total points (the game's own AllPoints run score, summed across
every run played in this room) as an alternative path to victory
alongside beating the required Supervisors. 0 (default) disables this
goal entirely.

options.label: Game Mode
options.description:
Determines starting location and accessibility.
Vanilla starts you in the Docking Bay with no items.
Open Sector Hub starts you in the Sector Hub with one E-Tank and one random item. All sector elevators will be open.
Custom will apply the settings in the Custom Game Mode section.

options.label: Infant Metroids in Pool
options.description: How many Infant Metroids will be in the item pool.

options.label: Infant Metroids Required
options.description:
How many Infant Metroids will be required to beat the game.
If set to more than the number in the pool, will instead become however many are present.

options.label: Infant Metroid Locations
options.description:
Where Infant Metroids can be located.
Anywhere allows them to be anywhere in the multiworld.
Bosses Encouraged increases the chances of them being located on local boss locations.
Only Bosses means Infant Metroids can only be on your boss locations. Will limit the number of Infant Metroids
in the pool. if greater than the number of bosses.

options.label: Early Progression
options.description:
Determines if an early progression item guaranteed in one of your first locations.
Normal restricts the starting item pool to Morph Ball and Missiles.
Advanced expands the pool to Screw Attack.
If Shinespark Tricks are set to Advanced, adds Speed Booster as well
Option is in testing and may increase generation failures.

options.label: Sector Tube Shuffle
options.description:
If enabled, shuffles the tube connections between sectors.
Does not affect the non-glass tube connections.

options.label: Elevator Shuffle
options.description:
If enabled, shuffles the various elevator connections.
Sectors will shuffle the six sector elevators in the Sector Hub.
All will include all elevator connections in the game.
Note that if enabled, logical energy tank requirements will be relaxed.

options.label: Point of No Returns in Logic
options.description:
Should Point of No Return locations be in logic.
If disabled, you will never be required to enter an area without the items to exit out.

options.label: Shinespark Trick Difficulty
options.description:
What level of shinespark trick difficulty may be required to navigate around.
Note that this does not exclude items that require shinesparking in vanilla to obtain.
Use the ShinesparkLocations location group for that.

options.label: Wall Jump Trick Difficulty
options.description: What level of wall jump trick difficulty may be required to navigate around.

options.label: Combat Difficulty
options.description: What level of combat tools are logically expected for later game bosses.

options.label: Starting Location
options.description:
Your starting location.
This is a Custom Game Mode option and will only be applied if GameMode is set to Custom.

options.label: Starting Major Upgrades
options.description:
How many major upgrades you begin with.
Note that depending on your StartingLocation and EarlyProgression settings, you may receive more than specified here
in order to successfully generate the game. Upgrades are taken from the general item pool and will be replaced
by a random filler item.
These will be applied in addition to your start_inventory and start_inventory_from_pool items.
These will be sent by the client once you're connected.
This is a Custom Game Mode option and will only be applied if GameMode is set to Custom.

options.label: Starting Energy Tanks
options.description:
How many Energy Tanks you begin with.
This will be overridden by the number specified in start_inventory and start_inventory_from_pool, if applicable.
Energy tanks are taken from the general item pool and will be replaced by a random filler item.
These will be sent by the client once you're connected.
This is a Custom Game Mode option and will only be applied if GameMode is set to Custom.

options.label: Filler Items
options.description:
Which Items are used as filler when Items are removed from the pool
Whenever an item is removed from the pool by start_inventory_from_pool, StartingMajorUpgrades, StartingEnergyTanks,
or for other reasons, it will be replaced with a random item from this list.
This is a Custom Game Mode option and will only be applied if GameMode is set to Custom.

options.label: Open Sector Elevators
options.description:
Determines if the sector elevators in the Sector Hub are locked by their vanilla keycard requirements.
This is a Custom Game Mode option and will only be applied if GameMode is set to Custom.

options.label: Sector Navigation Room Hint Locks
options.description:
Determines if the Navigation Rooms at the start of each sector have their hints locked by keycard requirements.
If set, the keycard required for the hint will be one level higher than the level needed to access the sector
in vanilla. Has no effect if EnableHints is disabled.
This is a Custom Game Mode option and will only be applied if GameMode is set to Custom.

options.label: Palette Randomization
options.description: Randomize the ingame palettes.

options.label: Enable Hints
options.description: Enable ingame hints at Navigation Stations.

options.label: Nerf Geron Weaknesses
options.description: Makes Gerons only weak to their 'intended' values.

options.label: Reveal Hidden Blocks
options.description: Enables whether destructible blocks are revealed from the start.

options.label: Fast Door Transitions
options.description: Enables fast door transitions between rooms.

options.label: Missile Data Ammo
options.description: The amount of missiles provided by a Missile Data item.

options.label: Missile Tank Ammo
options.description: The amount of missiles provided by a Missile Tank item.

options.label: Power Bomb Data Ammo
options.description: The amount of power bombs provided by a Power Bomb Data item.

options.label: Power Bomb Tank Ammo
options.description: The amount of power bombs provided by a Power Bomb Tank item.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Which condition(s) are required for victory. If score or both is chosen,
will turn on Scoresanity

options.label: Scoresanity
options.description:
Earn checks for various score thresholds.

When using 'with_extra', one extra score check will be placed between checks
5-10, two extra score checks will be placed between checks 10-15, and three
extra checks will be placed between checks 15-20

options.label: Scoresanity Difficulty
options.description:
How difficult the Scoresanity checks should be.

'Normal' is equivalent to a max score of 3000.

options.label: Initial number of sizes of fruit
options.description: How many sizes of fruit to start with access to. Fewer starting fruit means fewer sphere 1 checks.

options.label: Shuffle Fruit Order
options.description:
Shuffle the fruit order. If set to 'visual', the fruit will get bigger as
you progress. If 'on', the size of the fruit is also shuffled (this makes
the early game harder but may make the late game easier)

options.label: Progressive Field Height Count
options.description:
How many Progressive Field Height items to add into the pool. When set to 0,
disables the feature. When non-zero, the field starts at 50% of its normal
height and increases linearly to its normal height with each Progressive Field
Height

options.label: Progressive Cooldown Reduction Count
options.description:
How many Progressive Cooldown Reduction items to add into the pool. When set
to 0, disables the feature. When non-zero, you start with a cooldown between
each fruit drop, which reduces linearly to zero with each Progressive
Cooldown Reduction

options.label: Starting Drop Cooldown
options.description:
How long your initial drop cooldown is, in seconds. Has no effect if
cooldown_upgrade_count is 0 (as that disables the feature entirely)

options.label: Next needs unlock
options.description: Does the ability to see the next fruit need unlocking?

options.label: Bonus Points Chance
options.description:
Chance, in percent, that any given filler item will be replaced with some
bonus points.

options.label: Trap Chance
options.description: Chance, in percent, that any given filler item will be replaced with a trap.

options.label: Instant Drop Trap weight
options.description:
The relative weight that any given trap will be an Instant Drop Trap.

Note that this is relative to the weights of other traps; if you have
Instant Drop Trap set to 50, Shuffle Trap set to 25, and all other traps set
to 0, there will be a 2/3 chance of Instant Drop trap being selected when a
trap is generated

options.label: Shuffle Trap weight
options.description:
The relative weight that any given trap will be a Shuffle Trap.

Note that this is relative to the weights of other traps; if you have
Instant Drop Trap set to 50, Shuffle Trap set to 25, and all other traps set
to 0, there will be a 2/3 chance of Instant Drop trap being selected when a
trap is generated

options.label: Impulse Trap weight
options.description:
The relative weight that any given trap will be an Impulse Trap.

Note that this is relative to the weights of other traps; if you have
Instant Drop Trap set to 50, Shuffle Trap set to 25, and all other traps set
to 0, there will be a 2/3 chance of Instant Drop trap being selected when a
trap is generated

options.label: Thanos Trap weight
options.description:
The relative weight that any given trap will be a Thanos Trap.

Note that this is relative to the weights of other traps; if you have
Instant Drop Trap set to 50, Shuffle Trap set to 25, and all other traps set
to 0, there will be a 2/3 chance of Instant Drop trap being selected when a
trap is generated

options.label: Secrecy Trap weight
options.description:
The relative weight that any given trap will be a Secrecy Trap.

Note that this is relative to the weights of other traps; if you have
Instant Drop Trap set to 50, Shuffle Trap set to 25, and all other traps set
to 0, there will be a 2/3 chance of Instant Drop trap being selected when a
trap is generated

options.label: Blindness Trap weight
options.description:
The relative weight that any given trap will be a Blindness Trap.

Note that this is relative to the weights of other traps; if you have
Instant Drop Trap set to 50, Shuffle Trap set to 25, and all other traps set
to 0, there will be a 2/3 chance of Instant Drop trap being selected when a
trap is generated

options.label: Starting Lives
options.description: Number of lives you start each puzzle with.

options.label: Starting Coins
options.description: Number of coins you start with.

options.label: Starting Hints
options.description: Number of row/column hints revealed at the start of each puzzle.

options.label: Coins Per Bundle
options.description:
Coins received from each Coin Bundle item.
low=5, normal=50 (default), high=100, custom=coins_per_bundle_custom.

options.label: Coins Per Bundle (custom)
options.description: Coins received from each Coin Bundle item when coins_per_bundle is 'custom'.

options.label: Extra Lives in Pool
options.description: Number of Extra Life items in the item pool.

options.label: Grid Count Preset
options.description:
Preset distribution of puzzles per grid size (the goal is their sum).
Choose 'custom' to set each size yourself with the puzzles_* options.
easy=10/8/5/2, normal=10/10/10/10, hard=10/15/20/20, evil=0/0/0/66,
expedition_33=0/33/33/33 (sizes 5x5/10x10/15x15/20x20).

options.label: 5x5 Puzzles (custom preset)
options.description: Number of 5x5 puzzles toward the goal (only used when grid_preset is custom).

options.label: 10x10 Puzzles (custom preset)
options.description: Number of 10x10 puzzles toward the goal (only used when grid_preset is custom).

options.label: 15x15 Puzzles (custom preset)
options.description: Number of 15x15 puzzles toward the goal (only used when grid_preset is custom).

options.label: 20x20 Puzzles (custom preset)
options.description: Number of 20x20 puzzles toward the goal (only used when grid_preset is custom).

options.label: Death Link
options.description:
How Death Link affects you when another linked player dies:
off: Death Link is disabled.
on: you lose all your lives (and your own death also sends a Death Link).
damage: you lose a single heart instead of all your lives.

options.label: Auto-X Completed Rows/Columns
options.description:
Automatically place an X on the remaining cells of a completed row/column.
Fixed by the YAML for everyone playing this Archipelago game.

options.label: Grey Out Completed Hints
options.description:
Grey out hint numbers once they have been satisfied.
Fixed by the YAML for everyone playing this Archipelago game.

options.label: Unlimited Lives
options.description:
Play without losing lives on mistakes. When disabled (default), mistakes cost a
life and Show Mistakes is forced on.

options.label: Show Mistakes in Real-Time
options.description:
Highlight incorrect cells in real-time. This is forced on and locked whenever you
play with lives (Unlimited Lives disabled); it is only freely configurable when
Unlimited Lives is enabled.

options.label: Starting Wallet Level
options.description:
Wallet level you start with (coin capacity). 0 = 49 max coins, 1 = 99,
2 = 999, 3 = 4999, 4 = 9999. Set to 4 to effectively play without a coin cap.

options.label: Wallets in Pool
options.description:
Number of progressive Wallet Upgrade items placed in the multiworld pool (0-4).
Levels added to the pool are received as multiworld items; their shop slots become
multiworld location checks instead of coin purchases.

options.label: Heart Containers in Pool
options.description:
Number of Heart Container checks placed in the shop (0-10). Their shop slots become
multiworld location checks instead of coin purchases; the max-heart increase arrives as a
Heart Container item (a quarter in Zelda Heart Mode, a whole heart otherwise). Requires
Offer Heart Containers in Shop, and is ignored under Unlimited Lives.

options.label: Require Tier Completion to Advance
options.description:
Require completing every puzzle of your current grid size before you can buy the
next difficulty in the shop. When disabled, difficulty can be bought with coins alone.

options.label: Difficulty Increase Cost
options.description:
Coin cost to increase difficulty in the shop, indexed on the size you reach.
free=0; low=30; normal=250; high=500 (flat per step);
progressive=99/999/1999 to reach 10x10/15x15/20x20. Held coins are capped by your wallet,
so expensive modes require wallet upgrades or generation rejects an unbeatable seed.

options.label: Life Restore on Clear
options.description:
How many lives are restored when you clear a puzzle (applied on the next puzzle).
none=0, one=+1, full=refill to your maximum (default), custom=+life_restore_custom.
Ignored when Unlimited Lives is on. Failing a puzzle always refills fully.

options.label: Life Restore Amount (custom)
options.description: Lives restored on clear when life_restore_on_clear is 'custom'.

options.label: Offer Healing in Shop
options.description:
Offer a 'heal one life' purchase in the shop (up to your maximum).
Ignored when Unlimited Lives is on.

options.label: Healing Cost
options.description:
Coin cost of one heal in the shop (only when shop_healing is on).
free=0, low=10, normal=30 (default), high=100,
progressive (10, +10 per heal already bought, capped at 9999), custom=healing_cost_custom.

options.label: Healing Cost (custom)
options.description: Flat coin cost of one heal when healing_cost is 'custom'.

options.label: Zelda Heart Mode (quarter hearts)
options.description:
Shop heart purchases come as quarter-heart pieces (4 = +1 max heart, Zelda-style)
instead of whole hearts. Forming a new heart fully heals you. Damage and healing always
use whole hearts. Ignored when Unlimited Lives is on.

options.label: Offer Heart Containers in Shop
options.description:
Offer max-heart expansion in the shop (buy a whole heart, or a quarter in Zelda Heart
Mode), up to 10 hearts. Ignored when Unlimited Lives is on.

options.label: Heart Cost
options.description:
Coin cost per shop heart purchase (one whole heart, or one quarter in Zelda Heart Mode).
free=0, low=30, normal=100 (default), high=300,
progressive (50, +50 per purchase, capped 9999), custom=heart_cost_custom.

options.label: Heart Cost (custom)
options.description: Flat coin cost per heart purchase when heart_cost is 'custom'.

options.label: Flawless Checks
options.description:
Send location checks for clearing puzzles without any mistakes: one per played grid size,
one for a 5-in-a-row flawless streak, and one for 10 flawless clears total. Only the checks
that are actually reachable for your configured puzzle counts are created.

options.label: Force Unique Solution
options.description:
Force each player's generated puzzles to have a single, no-guess-solvable answer. This only
affects local puzzle generation and never changes the item/location pool; players can still
toggle it in the client. Off (default) allows puzzles whose clues admit several valid grids.

options.label: Debug Mode
options.description:
Show the in-client Debug tab (slot_data simulator and debug tools) for connected players.
Off by default; turn on only when you need to debug a seed.

options.label: Starting Piece Slots
options.description: Number of piece slots (pieces shown at once) you start with.

options.label: Starting Abilities
options.description: Number of abilities (Rotate, Undo, etc.) you start with.

options.label: Rotate Abilities in Pool
options.description: Number of Rotate Ability items in the item pool.

options.label: Undo Abilities in Pool
options.description: Number of Undo Ability items in the item pool.

options.label: Remove Blocks in Pool
options.description: Number of Remove Block items in the item pool.

options.label: Hold Abilities in Pool
options.description: Number of Hold Ability items in the item pool.

options.label: Mirror Abilities in Pool
options.description: Number of Mirror Ability items in the item pool.

options.label: Shrink Abilities in Pool
options.description: Number of Shrink Ability items in the item pool.

options.label: Score Multipliers in Pool
options.description: Number of Score Multiplier items in the item pool.

options.label: Goal Score
options.description: Total score required to complete the goal.

options.label: Death Link
options.description:
When you game over, everyone with DeathLink enabled also game overs.
When you receive a DeathLink, your current game ends.

options.label: Send Checks Immediately
options.description:
Send checks as soon as the requirements are met, without waiting for the round to end.
Does not work for all checks.

options.label: Visibility Information
options.description: How much information should be displayed about what each check unlocks before it is reached.

options.label: Rebirth Blocks Death Link
options.description: Can a “Rebirth” item be used to block an incoming death link?

options.label: Space Speed Multiplier (%)
options.description: Speed up (or slow down) the “Space” game mode by reducing target scores by this factor.

options.label: Hope Stone Multiplier (%)
options.description:
Increase (or decrease) the amount of Hope Stones granted as in-game rewards.
Does not affect Hope Stones given over Archipelago.

options.label: Achievement Checks
options.description:
Which achievements are checks.
Make sure to select enough to cover all the items.

options.label: Fusions
options.description: If creating fusions are checks.

options.label: Power-Up Unlocks
options.description:
Which power-ups need to be unlocked before they can be bought.
Use this instead of “Start Inventory From Pool” to prevent issues with progressive item naming.

options.label: Power-Up Initial Levelling Items
options.description: Include initial levelling for these power-ups as items.

options.label: Cosmetic Filler (%)
options.description:
Percent of filler items that should be cosmetics.
If set to zero, or if no filler items are generated,
cosmetics are obtained in-game as they are normally.

options.label: “Standard” Distance (m)
options.description: The required distance to be achieved in “Standard” mode to reach the goal state.

options.label: “Classic” Distance (m)
options.description: The required distance to be achieved in “Classic” mode to reach the goal state.

options.label: “Baeless” Distance (m)
options.description: The required distance to be achieved in “Baeless” mode to reach the goal state.

options.label: “Gacha” Distance (m)
options.description: The required distance to be achieved in “Gacha” mode to reach the goal state.

options.label: “The Cell” Time (s)
options.description:
The required time for “The Cell” mode to be beaten in to reach the goal state.
Set to 300 to disable this requirement.

options.label: “Space” Distance (m)
options.description: The required distance to be achieved in “Space” mode to reach the goal state.

options.label: “Space” Score
options.description:
The required total score to be achieved in “Space” mode to reach the goal state.
This **is not** affected by “Space Speed Multiplier”.

options.label: Required Achievements
options.description: Which achievements are required to reach the goal state.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Determines the victory condition for the game.

Ending S: Complete all overtime missions and defeat Brock on the tank.
          This is the full game experience including overtime mode.

Ending A: Solve all of the cases and reach the helipad by 12pm on Day 4.
          Overtime scoops are removed from the pool, making for a shorter run.

Savior:   Rescue a specified number of survivors to win (see
          "Number of Survivors" below). Ending S / Ending A locations still
          exist as normal checks but are filler-only and not the goal.

options.label: Number of Survivors
options.description:
The number of survivors that must be rescued for the Savior goal. Only has
an effect when Goal is set to Savior.

The maximum (48) requires rescuing every survivor in the game — 45 from
survivor/psychopath scoops plus the 3 free survivors (Bill Brenton,
Jeff Meyer, Natalie Meyer) who arrive without a dedicated scoop.

options.label: Guaranteed Items
options.description: Guarantees that the specified items will be in the item pool

options.label: Restricted Item Mode
options.description:
When enabled, players cannot pick up items in the world unless they have been sent
to them by the Archipelago server. This creates a more challenging experience where
you must rely on items from other players or your own location checks.

Items received from AP will be shown in the Items window, and only those items
can be picked up from the ground or dispensers in the game world.

options.label: Door Randomizer
options.description:
When enabled, door connections throughout the mall are randomized.
All area keys are given to you at the start, and doors lead to unexpected locations.

The randomizer ensures all areas remain reachable and no softlocks occur.

options.label: Door Randomizer Mode
options.description:
Controls how doors are randomized when Door Randomizer is enabled.

Chaos: Doors are fully randomized. Going through door A to reach area B
       does NOT mean the door in B will take you back to A. Navigation
       requires careful attention to the door map.

Paired: Doors are randomized in pairs. If door A leads to area B, then
        a door in B will lead back to A. This creates a more intuitive
        but still randomized layout.

options.label: Randomize Rooftop/Warehouse Doors
options.description:
When enabled (and Door Randomizer is on), the doors between Rooftop and
Warehouse are included in the randomization pool.

When disabled (the default), those two doors are left vanilla even with
Door Randomizer on, so the opening sequence behaves as expected. Only
affects the Rooftop <-> Warehouse pair; all other doors still
randomize normally.

Has no effect if Door Randomizer is disabled.

options.label: ScoopSanity
options.description:
When enabled, scoops are sent to the player as items and the game time is frozen
after completing the Entrance Plaza prologue.

The order for main scoops will be randomized and the player will need
to receive the scoop item in order for the next scoop to spawn in the world.

An example:
The player's scoop order is 1. Girl Hunting, 2. Carlito's Hideout, 3. Backup for Brad.
After completing the Entrance Plaza prologue, the player will need to wait
until they receive the Girl Hunting scoop item from AP before they can do the mission.
If they receive a later mission, like Backup for Brad, they will not be able to do it until they
receive and complete the prior missions.

Players will also receive side scoops as items, which will spawn the NPCs into
the world right away.

An example:
The player receives "Lovers".  Tonya and Ross will now spawn into the world in
Wonderland plaza and are rescuable.

options.label: Exclude Levels
options.description:
When enabled, high level-up checks are prevented from having progression items.
This can be used to limit grinding and allows more control over the potential length of a run.

options.label: Exclude Levels Above
options.description:
If 'Exclude Levels' is enabled, any level-ups above the chosen value will still
exist as checks but will be prevented from having progression items.
If 'Exclude Levels' is disabled, this value can be ignored.

options.label: Enable Skill Items
options.description:
When enabled, Frank's 21 combat skills (Jump Kick, Suplex, etc.) become AP
items in the pool. They are classified as Useful — guaranteed to be in
the multiworld but not in progression logic.

Has no effect if Vanilla Progression is set to 'vanilla_only' (in that mode
the skills are granted normally on level-up and not duplicated as items).

options.label: Enable Stat Items
options.description:
When enabled, Progressive stat upgrades become AP items in the pool:
Health (+1000), Attack (+25%), Throw (+25), Item Slot (+1), Run Level (+1).
Classified as Useful.

Has no effect if Vanilla Progression is set to 'vanilla_only'.

options.label: Enable Extra Stat Buffs
options.description:
When enabled, additional stat-upgrade items push past vanilla L50 caps:
   * +4 Health (cap 16000)
   * +10 Attack (cap 500%)
   * +8 Throw (cap 400)
   * +3 Item Slot (cap 15)
   * +10 Speed Multiplier (cap 1.5x — DRAP-only category)

Useful for longer multiworld pools or harder-mode runs. Note that pushing
Attack past 250% breaks the in-game UI bar count (combat damage still
scales correctly).

options.label: Vanilla Progression
options.description:
Controls how Frank's natural level-up rewards interact with AP items.

vanilla_only:
    Engine grants skills/stats normally on level-up. AP skill/stat items
    are NOT in the pool. Use this if you only want scoop/door
    randomization without touching Frank's progression.

replace:
    Engine's level-up grants are suppressed (re-overridden each level).
    AP items are the only source of skills and stats. The default.

extra_buffs_only:
    Engine grants normally, AP items contain ONLY the over-vanilla extras
    (cap-pushing items). Best paired with Enable Extra Stat Buffs = true.

options.label: Exclude Overpowered Items
options.description:
When enabled, removes a curated set of items widely considered too
powerful from the AP item pool:

  * Book [Infinite Durability]  (weapons never break)
  * Book [Martial Arts]         (massively-boosted unarmed damage)
  * Laser Sword                 (high-damage, high-durability weapon)
  * Real Mega Buster            (high-damage ranged weapon)

Disabled by default. Players who want these items to remain in
rotation should leave it off; players who want a more balanced run
should enable it.

Note: items explicitly listed under Guaranteed Items are still added
even when this option is on, since that's an explicit user override.

options.label: Trap Percentage
options.description:
Percentage of filler-item slots that become traps. 0 = no traps,
25 = balanced default, 50 = aggressive, 100 = chaos. The selected
fraction of filler slots is dedicated to traps and round-robin
distributed across all six trap types (Stomach Ache Trap, Zombait
Trap, Slow Trap, Damage Player Trap, Hostile NPC Trap, Special
Forces Trap) so every type appears at least once before any
repeats.

options.label: Hostile NPC Count Min
options.description:
Minimum number of hostile NPCs spawned per Hostile NPC Trap.
Each trap rolls between min and max (inclusive) at fire time.

options.label: Hostile NPC Count Max
options.description:
Maximum number of hostile NPCs spawned per Hostile NPC Trap.
Capped by the trap pool's available stypes (~10 cutscene-only NPCs).

options.label: Cult Limited
options.description:
In ScoopSanity, cultists will appear after beginning either 'The Cult' or
'A Strange Group', and they will remain in the mall indefinitely.

If this option is enabled, the cult will instead disappear from the mall
after Sean is killed like they do in the regular game. However, they will
still be clustered outside the boss room in Colby's movie theater so you
can complete any cult-related checks.

This option has no effect if ScoopSanity is off.

options.label: Night Mode
options.description:
When enabled, zombies behave as if it is always night, regardless of
the in-game time. The night-side parameters of `ZombieDefinitionUserData`
(HoldMissRate, HoldBlockRate, HoldBlockFallRate) are written over the
day-side fields, and `ZombieManager.isHourNight()` is hooked to always
return true.

Effects:
  * Higher chance for grabs to land (Day 5% miss → Night 15% miss)
  * Higher chance for zombies to block counterattacks (Day 45% → Night 55%)
  * Slightly more aggressive overall behavior

The "glowing eyes" visual effect that normally accompanies night does
NOT carry over — that's tied to a separate render pass. This is purely
a difficulty modifier.

options.label: Hardcore Zombies
options.description:
When enabled, zombies become significantly more dangerous on top of
Night Mode. **Implies Night Mode** — turning this on without enabling
Night Mode auto-enables it.

Amplified parameters:
  * Bite damage: -1000 → -3000 HP per tick (3×)
  * Downed-bite damage: -3000 → -9000 HP per tick (3×)
  * Scratch damage rate: 3.5 → 7.0 (2×)
  * Player aggro radius: 9 → 25 units (much harder to sneak past)
  * General aggro radius: 13 → 35 units
  * NPC aggro radius: 10 → 25 units (zombies notice survivors faster)
  * Grab escape mash count: 15 → 30 (2× harder to escape)
  * Mash decay rate: 0.02 → 0.05 (gauge drains faster while mashing)

Recommended only for experienced players seeking a challenge run.

options.label: Random Starting Costume
options.description:
When enabled, Frank's outfit is randomized once at the start of each
play session (after the save loads or on a fresh new game). One
consistent randomized look per seed.

Randomization rules:
  * Body slot (0..42 regular costumes by default; 0..62 if DLC outfits
    are enabled below) is always picked first.
  * If the rolled Body is a regular costume (0..42), Foot / Hat /
    Glasses are also randomized to give Frank a chaotic accessorized
    outfit.
  * If the rolled Body is a DLC anchor (43..62, requires Dlc Outfits
    Enabled), it acts as a full-outfit replacement and the engine
    overrides the other slots automatically — Foot / Hat / Glasses are
    left alone since the DLC outfit dictates the whole look.

Independent of the Costume Chaos Mode option below.

options.label: Costume Chaos Mode
options.description:
When enabled, Frank's outfit is re-randomized on every area transition
(i.e. every door / loading-zone change). Frank looks different in every
area, with a fresh random outfit each time.

Uses the same Body-first randomization rules as Random Starting Costume.
Each area transition will count toward the "Change into 8 different
outfits" achievement, which may complete that location very quickly.

Compatible with Random Starting Costume. If both are on, the starting
costume picks the look at session start and chaos mode reshuffles on
every door from there.

options.label: DLC Outfits Enabled
options.description:
When enabled, the costume randomizer's Body pool includes the 20 DLC
outfit IDs (43..62) on top of the 43 regular Body costumes. DLC IDs
function as full-outfit anchors — picking one applies a complete DLC
outfit (e.g. Mega Man armor, knight set) instead of a partial body.

REQUIRES the player owns the corresponding DR-DR DLC. If the DLC is not
installed, applying these IDs is expected to fail silently (the engine
rejects the swap and Frank stays in his current outfit). Leave this
OFF if you don't own the DLC to keep the randomizer pool in the safe
range.

options.label: PP-Bonus Locations
options.description:
Adds ~57 extra AP location checks tied to PP-bonus events and key-item
pickup banners that DRAP detects via the MsgEvents watcher:

Single-fire checks:
  * Realign Servbot Head (Paradise Plaza fountain)
  * Ride the Space Rider
  * Obtain Mall Map and Transceiver (Otis bundle)
  * Obtain Maintenance Tunnel Key
  * Obtain First Aid Kit (in Seon's Food and Stuff, gated on defeating Steven)

Counted-progression checks (per-instance + ALL-X final):
  * Walk on N Treadmills (1..6, plus All Treadmills)         -- Al Fresca
  * Destroy N Sandbags (1..4, plus All Sandbags)             -- Al Fresca
  * Spin N Display Racks (1..4, plus All Display Racks)      -- Entrance
  * Break N Food Court Wall Plates (1..18, no separate "all")
  * Microwave N Items (1..9, plus Microwave All Items)
  * Heat N Pans (1..5, plus Heat All Pans)

Logic gating: each check requires the relevant region. Microwave/Heat
locations require Food Court access (the most restrictive of the regions
those events occur in). In Restricted Item Mode, microwave checks
additionally require Uncooked Pizza or Raw Meat, and stove checks
require Frying Pan.

options.label: Required Rank
options.description:
The minimum rank you must complete to win.  A run is "completed at
Rank X" when you finish the final island while accumulating at least
Rank X's worth of difficulty modifier points.

Difficulty thresholds:
  Bronze (0), Silver (1), Gold (2-3), Sapphire (4-5), Emerald (6-7),
  Ruby (8-9), Diamond (10-15), Prismatic (16+)

Higher ranks demand stacking more modifier cards before each island, so
higher requirements mean tougher runs.  Run-completion locations are
generated for this rank by default; see Extra Rank Checks to also
generate locations for higher ranks.

options.label: Run Length
options.description:
How many islands a run must complete to count as finished.  The game
cycles biomes every 28 islands, so:
  short (28): one full biome cycle
  full  (56): two full biome cycles

All island/equipment/rank locations scale with this value - a Full run
has roughly twice the location count of a Short run.

options.label: Weapons for Completion
options.description:
How many DIFFERENT weapons must be used to complete victory-rank runs
before you can win.  E.g. with this set to 5, you'll need to finish the
final island five separate times, each with a different weapon, all at
Required Rank or higher.

Only weapons in the AP pool count toward this.  Weapons you have from
the start can still generate location checks (see Equipment Check
Mode), but they never advance the goal.  Weapons in Pool is raised to
match this value when it is lower.

Capped at the total number of weapons in the game (20).

options.label: Melee for Completion
options.description:
How many DIFFERENT melee weapons must be used to complete victory-rank
runs before you can win.  Works the same as Weapons for Completion but
for melee.

Set to 0 to disable melee entirely - no melee items in the pool, no
melee location checks, and no melee requirement for victory.

options.label: Abilities for Completion
options.description:
How many DIFFERENT abilities must be used to complete victory-rank
runs before you can win.  Works the same as Weapons for Completion but
for abilities.

Set to 0 to disable abilities entirely - no ability items in the pool,
no ability location checks, and no ability requirement for victory.

options.label: Weapons in Pool
options.description:
How many weapons are randomly selected from the 20 available to be
AP items.  Pool weapons must be received via Archipelago before you can
use them.  Non-pool weapons are always available from the start.

Each pool weapon also generates its own per-island run-completion
location, so a larger pool means more checks.

Example: pool=5, for_completion=3 means 5 weapons are AP items, all 5
have location checks, but only 3 distinct ones must be used to win.

Must be >= Weapons for Completion (auto-clamped).  Set to 20 to put
every weapon in the pool - Starting Weapons is then forced to at least
1 so you always begin with something usable.

options.label: Melee in Pool
options.description:
How many melee weapons (out of 5) are randomly selected to be AP
items.  See Weapons in Pool for the full mechanic.

Must be >= Melee for Completion (auto-clamped).  Forced to 0 when
Melee for Completion is 0.  Set to 5 to put every melee weapon in the
pool - one random pool melee is then added to your starting inventory
so you always begin with something usable.

options.label: Abilities in Pool
options.description:
How many abilities (out of 7) are randomly selected to be AP items.
See Weapons in Pool for the full mechanic.

Must be >= Abilities for Completion (auto-clamped).  Forced to 0 when
Abilities for Completion is 0.  Set to 7 to put every ability in the
pool - one random pool ability is then added to your starting
inventory so you always begin with something usable.

options.label: Starting Weapons
options.description:
How many of your pool weapons you begin the game already holding.
These are randomly selected from Weapons in Pool and pre-collected, so
you can start working on equipment-run checks immediately without
waiting to receive a weapon from another player.

A weapon you start with is removed from the item pool rather than
duplicated, so its slot goes to filler instead of a second copy of
something you already hold.

Must be < Weapons in Pool (at least one weapon must still be findable
via AP).  Set to 0 to start with no pool weapons unlocked - except
when Weapons in Pool is 20, where this is forced to at least 1 because
no weapon would otherwise be available at the start.

options.label: Equipment Check Mode
options.description:
Controls whether non-pool weapons/melee/abilities have their own
run-completion location checks.  (Pool equipment ALWAYS has checks -
this option is only about non-pool items, which are available from
the start.)

These are bonus locations only.  Non-pool equipment NEVER counts
toward Weapons/Melee/Abilities for Completion, no matter which mode
is picked - otherwise the goal could be met without receiving a
single AP item.

regular:
    Non-pool equipment runs are normal location checks that can hold
    any item, including progression.  Maximum locations.
filler_only:
    Non-pool equipment runs exist as locations but are marked excluded
    - they only ever hold filler.  Adds checks for variety without
