    requiring you to use every weapon for progression.
disabled:
    Non-pool equipment run locations are not generated at all.  This
    is the default due to how many extra locations it creates.

options.label: Max Rank
options.description:
The highest rank for which any location checks are generated.  Must
be >= Required Rank (auto-clamped).

Has no effect unless Extra Rank Checks is set to something other than
"none" - without extra rank checks, only Required Rank generates
locations and Max Rank is ignored.

options.label: Extra Rank Checks
options.description:
Controls whether ranks ABOVE Required Rank generate additional
location checks.  Replaces the legacy Extra Ranked Island Checks +
Non-Progression Above Required pair with one option that captures
the meaningful combinations.

none:
    Only Required Rank produces ranked checks.  Higher ranks are
    ignored and produce no additional locations.  Smallest pool.
progression:
    Ranks above Required (up to Max Rank) add new ranked checks AND
    those locations can hold progression items.  Greatly increases
    location count and turns higher difficulty into real progression.
filler_only:
    Ranks above Required add new ranked checks but those locations
    are marked excluded - they only hold filler.  Use this to add
    more checks for variety/filler without forcing yourself to grind
    higher ranks for critical items.

Has no effect when Required Rank == Max Rank (no extra ranks exist).

options.label: Cascade Ranked Checks
options.description:
When enabled, completing an in-game check at a higher rank also
triggers the equivalent check at every lower rank.  E.g. completing
"Island 5 with Auto Rifle on Gold" also sends checks for "Island 5
with Auto Rifle on Silver" and "...on Bronze".

Convenient when playing at high ranks - you don't have to redo runs
at lower ranks for the easier checks.  Has no effect on generation
or fill, only on what the in-game client sends as you play.

options.label: Minimize Run Checks
options.description:
When enabled, drops generalized run-completion checks that are made
redundant by the most-specific equipment-and-rank check.  Pool weapons
always have these locations, so the redundant ones are always covered:

  - "Complete Island X on Rank" checks are removed
  - "Complete Island X with Weapon" checks are removed

The most specific "Complete Island X with Weapon on Rank" check is
always kept, since completing it implies completing all the dropped
variants.  Plain "Complete Island X" (unranked) is also kept.

Has no effect only in the unusual case where there are no equipment
runs at all (which currently can't happen since Weapons in Pool is
forced to >= 1).

options.label: Pickup Checks
options.description:
When enabled, picking up perks, relics, weapon mods, melee mods,
or ability mods for the FIRST TIME (per item, per multiworld) sends
a location check, e.g. "Perk: Driller" or "Relic: Time Ring".

Adds up to 305 location checks.  When disabled, these pickup
locations don't exist and the item pool focuses on island/equipment/
rank-run checks only.

See also Limit Pickup Pool / Limit Pickup Locations to scale this
down to per-run inventory caps.

options.label: Limit Pickup Pool
options.description:
When enabled, the AP item pool is limited to a randomly-selected
subset of pickups matching your per-run inventory caps:
  24 perks, 24 weapon mods, 12 ability mods, 12 melee mods, 10 relics

Items NOT in the chosen subset stay in-game and can be picked up
normally during runs, but are never sent or received via AP.

Tag-group coverage is enforced - at least one provider per pickup-tag
group is guaranteed in the subset, so tag-gated locations (like
"Relic: Time Ring") remain reachable.

Pairs naturally with Limit Pickup Locations.  Either option can be
enabled independently; both share the same chosen subset.

options.label: Limit Pickup Locations
options.description:
When enabled, pickup location checks are only generated for items
in the randomly-selected subset (see Limit Pickup Pool for the
subset sizes).  Items not in the subset still appear in-game but
produce no location check when picked up.

Pairs naturally with Limit Pickup Pool.  Either option can be
enabled independently; both share the same chosen subset when both
are on.

options.label: Progressive Inventory Slots
options.description:
When enabled, you start with fewer inventory slots than the game
normally allows, and receive additional slots as AP items.  The
in-game crystal-purchase upgrade for slots is blocked.

When disabled, you have all slots available from the start as
normal.

See Starting Perk/Weapon Mod/Ability Mod/Melee Mod Slots to control
how many slots you start with.

options.label: Starting Perk Slots
options.description:
When Progressive Inventory Slots is enabled, how many perk slots
you start with.  The remaining (24 - this value) slots are sent as
"Progressive Perk Slot" items in the AP pool.

Has no effect when Progressive Inventory Slots is disabled.

options.label: Starting Weapon Mod Slots
options.description:
When Progressive Inventory Slots is enabled, how many weapon mod
slots you start with.  The remaining (24 - this value) slots are
sent as "Progressive Weapon Mod Slot" items in the AP pool.

Has no effect when Progressive Inventory Slots is disabled.

options.label: Starting Ability Mod Slots
options.description:
When Progressive Inventory Slots is enabled, how many ability mod
slots you start with.  The remaining (12 - this value) slots are
sent as "Progressive Ability Mod Slot" items in the AP pool.

Has no effect when Progressive Inventory Slots is disabled.

options.label: Starting Melee Mod Slots
options.description:
When Progressive Inventory Slots is enabled, how many melee mod
slots you start with.  The remaining (12 - this value) slots are
sent as "Progressive Melee Mod Slot" items in the AP pool.

Has no effect when Progressive Inventory Slots is disabled.

options.label: Crystal Cache Percentage
options.description:
Percentage of "extra" item pool slots filled with Crystal Cache
(in-game currency rewards) instead of duplicate perk/mod stacks.

The pool is built by first adding required items (pool equipment,
one of each pickup, etc.).  Whatever slots remain are split between
crystal filler and extra stackable copies based on this percentage:
  0%   = all extras are duplicate perks/mods (more variety in
         received items)
  75%  = default; balanced mix
  100% = all extras are Crystal Cache (less spam of duplicates)

Crystal Cache items grant in-game currency for shops/upgrades.

options.label: Greed Item Mode
options.description:
How to handle Greed items - perks/relics/mods that can't be dropped
once picked up, making them a permanent commitment for the run.

auto:
    Greed items received from AP go directly to your inventory the
    next time you start a run, even though you can't drop them.
drop:
    Greed items received from AP spawn on the lobby floor for you
    to pick up only when you're ready to commit.
skip:
    Greed items are never granted via AP at all.  You can only
    find them naturally in-game.  Their pickup locations are also
    excluded from generation.

options.label: Guaranteed Items
options.description:
Forces specific items into the item pool regardless of other
settings.  Format is a YAML mapping of item names to copy counts:

  guaranteed_items:
    Auto Rifle: 1
    Time Bolt: 2

Useful for ensuring favorite items end up randomized.  Item names
must match exactly (case-sensitive).  Only stackable items (perks and
mods) take extra copies; relics and equipment are unique, so they get
one copy whatever the count.

worlds.game: Librarian Tidy Up the Arcane Library

options.label: Goal
options.description:
How much of the library must be tidied to win.

full    -- Complete the whole library, both floors (default).
floor_1 -- Complete Floor 1 only (1A-1N); Floor 2 leaves the pool.
floor_2 -- Complete Floor 2 only (2A-2Q); Floor 1 leaves the pool.
custom  -- Win after a number you choose. Set that number in
           custom_goal_row_count or custom_goal_book_count, whichever your
           check_mode counts in. Sections past your goal leave the seed, so you
           are not waiting on items you will never need.

individual_book_unlocks on the full goal is slow to generate and is off unless the
host allows it (allow_individual_book_unlocks in host.yaml). So is a custom goal
there that keeps more books than one floor holds (about 1600). A floor goal needs
no permission.

options.label: Custom Goal Row Count
options.description:
How many rows to finish to win, when goal = custom and check_mode = series.

Ignored otherwise: the other two check modes count books, through
custom_goal_book_count. Accepts 'random', 'random-low', 'random-high'.

options.label: Custom Goal Book Count
options.description:
How many books to shelve to win, when goal = custom and check_mode is
booksanity or count.

Ignored otherwise: check_mode series counts rows, through custom_goal_row_count.
The library holds 3072 books in 400 rows, so a number that sounds big here is a
shorter run than you might expect. The default is about half the library, which is
close to the length of a floor goal. Accepts 'random', 'random-low',
'random-high'.

options.label: Unlock Mode
options.description:
Choose how book series are unlocked.

random_series_bundles (default) -- each Series Bundle item opens a group of
    series_per_unlock series. Bundles are numbered and arrive in any order. The
    smallest item pool, and the classic setup.
individual_series_unlocks -- one unlock item per series, about 400 of them.
    Every bookcase is open from the start.
random_book_bundle -- each Progressive Book Bundle hands you the next
    books_per_bundle books of the seed's order, drawn from anywhere in the
    library, ignoring series. With check_mode: series the order is laid out so
    that a series finishes at a steady rate. numbered_book_bundles makes each
    bundle its own item instead.
individual_book_unlocks -- one unlock item per book, about 3000 of them. Every
    bookcase is open from the start. Much the biggest pool: with check_mode:
    series it is switched to booksanity, since 3000 items cannot sit in 400 row
    checks, and on the full goal, or a custom goal larger than a floor, it needs the
    host's permission (allow_individual_book_unlocks in host.yaml) because it is slow
    to generate.

options.label: Series Per Unlock
options.description:
How many series each Series Bundle holds. Lower means more
unlocks with smaller impact; higher means fewer, bigger ones. (Below 3 makes a
long unlock chain that's hard to place in tight seeds, so 3 is the minimum.)

Only applies to the random_series_bundles mode; the other three hand out series
or books directly, so they ignore it.

options.label: Books Per Bundle
options.description:
How many books arrive in each bundle. random_book_bundle only.

Higher means fewer, bigger deliveries. Raised automatically if the seed would need
more bundles than it has checks to put them in, and a little further with
check_mode: series or count so the checks stay fillable.

options.label: Numbered Book Bundles
options.description:
Give every Book Bundle its own number (Book Bundle 1, Book Bundle 2, ...) so a hint
can target the exact one. random_book_bundle only.

Off (default): bundles are copies of one item, Progressive Book Bundle, that open the
seed's book order in sequence. The tracker still tells you which bundle holds a book.
On: each bundle is its own item and they arrive in any order. This makes generation
noticeably slower with check_mode: count, so the host has to allow it
(allow_numbered_book_bundles in host.yaml).

options.label: Starting Series Count
options.description:
How many series you begin with unlocked. Always includes at least one whose
row is on the starting bookcase, so your first check is available right away.

random_series_bundles / individual_series_unlocks: that many series.
random_book_bundle: enough bundles to cover that many series, so what you
actually start with depends on books_per_bundle.
individual_book_unlocks: that many series' worth of random books -- each count
rolls a series size (3, 5, or 10 volumes), so e.g. 5 starts you with roughly
15-50 random individual books, not whole series.

options.label: Bookcase Unlocks
options.description:
How the bookcases open up.

progressive (default) -- one item per bookcase, so a section opens a few shelves
    at a time.
whole -- one item per section, opening all of its bookcases at once.
unlocked -- every bookcase is open from the start.

The two individual unlock modes are always unlocked.

options.label: Spare Book Item Percent
options.description:
Spare Series Bundle copies, as a percentage, so you do not need every one of
them to finish.

On goal: custom it sets how much of the library the seed keeps past your goal.
A goal of 200 rows and 10% spare leads to at least 220 series in the pool.
A book-counted goal of 1500 books and 10% spare has at least 1650 books in it.

options.label: Spare Shelf Items
options.description:
Spare Progressive Shelf Unlock copies, as a count per bookcase, so you do not
need every one of them to open a section.

Full and floor goals with random_series_bundles and bookcase_unlocks: progressive.
The other bookcase settings hand out whole sections or none at all, so there is
nothing for a spare copy to open. A seed with no room for the number you pick uses
fewer and says so during generation.

options.label: Check Mode
options.description:
Choose what earns you a check.

series (default) -- finishing a whole row.
booksanity -- shelving any single book correctly.
count -- every check_interval books you shelve.

One pairing cannot be built: individual_book_unlocks with series, since 3000
book items cannot sit in 400 row checks. It is switched to booksanity, and
generation says so.

options.label: Check Interval
options.description:
How many books you shelve between checks, when check_mode is count.

Lower means more checks, each worth less. A seed needs enough checks to hold all of
its items, so an interval that is too wide is brought down to fit, and the generation
log tells you what it landed on.

With random_book_bundle the two settings are tied: the interval can be at most about
books_per_bundle divided by 2.5. Five books or fewer per bundle means a check every
book; 10 per bundle allows a check every 3; 25 per bundle allows every 6 to 9,
depending on bookcase_unlocks. count_bundle_preference decides which of the two
gives way.

options.label: Count Bundle Preference
options.description:
With random_book_bundle and check_mode: count, the size of your bundles and how
often you get a check are tied together: smaller bundles need checks closer
together. If the two settings you picked cannot both be kept, this decides which
one wins.

narrow_interval (default): your bundle size stays as you set it, and checks come
    more often than you asked for.
widen_bundle: your check interval stays as you set it, and each bundle holds more
    books than you asked for.

Either way the generation log tells you the numbers it settled on. The other unlock
modes are not affected.

options.label: Magic Skills Enabled
options.description:
Which magic skills can turn up. Take out any you would rather not be given.

Dropping a skill also drops its Mastery and its Fatigue trap. What it held becomes
filler, and nothing in logic needs magic, so a shorter list only changes what you find.

options.label: Vanilla Caps
options.description:
Keep your magic skills and book capacity at the base game's maximum.

Off (default): this randomizer makes you stronger than the base game ever does. Each magic
skill can go up to five steps past its normal maximum through Mastery items (shorter cooldowns,
longer effects), and Book Capacity items let you carry up to 40 books instead of the game's 15.
On: there are no Mastery or Book Capacity items. Skills top out where the base game's do
and you carry at most 15 books. Their places go to filler; Fatigue traps stay.

options.label: Local Filler
options.description:
Keep this game's filler items in your own world.

On (default): Librarian filler fills your own locations instead of scattering
into other players' worlds; your meaningful items still circulate. Recommended,
since Librarian adds a lot of checks.
Off: filler is distributed across the multiworld like anything else.
Has no effect in a solo game.

options.label: Book Visibility
options.description:
How books from locked series look before you unlock them.

hidden -- locked books are invisible and non-grabbable; the library fills in as
          you unlock series (default).
stacks -- locked books stay visible but non-grabbable -- you walk through them.
          Pick this for a full-looking library or to avoid any hide glitches.

options.label: Only Unward Shelfable Books
options.description:
Require both the series unlock and its bookcase before a book can be picked up.

On (default): a book stays hidden until its series and its bookcase are both open,
so every book you are holding has a shelf waiting for it.

Off: a book is grabbable as soon as it is sent to you, and can go on any shelf you
have. Getting every check may then mean shelving a series, taking it back off, and
cycling another one through the same shelf.

options.label: Goal Type
options.description: Win condition for this Vault Hunters world.

options.label: Artifact Puzzle Size
options.description: Artifact puzzle size required for Artifact Puzzle and Herald goals.

options.label: Extra Artifacts
options.description: Extra Artifact items added to the item pool for Artifact and Herald goals.

options.label: Max Shop Level
options.description: Determines the amount of check shop pages. Level goals only use this when lower than the goal level.

options.label: Archipela-bits Chance
options.description: Percent chance for supported vault sources to produce Archipela-bits.

options.label: Lock Specializations
options.description: Whether ability specializations require Archipelago unlock items.

options.label: Max XP Scaling
options.description: Highest progressive XP multiplier included in the item pool.

options.label: Max Loot Scaling
options.description: Highest progressive loot multiplier included in the item pool.

options.label: Progressive Vault Time
options.description: Progressive Vault Time items included. Each item adds 5 minutes, starting from 5 minutes. Leaving this at 0 keeps the default 25 minutes

options.label: Start With Vault Kit
options.description: Start with iron gear, raw chromatic iron, vault stone, and a vault altar.

options.label: Checks Behind Skills
options.description: When enabled, learning VH skills, talents, mods, and expertises creates Archipelago location checks. Cannot be enabled with Auto Learn Skills.

options.label: Auto Learn Skills
options.description: When enabled, received VH skill, talent, mod, and expertise unlocks are automatically purchased or researched in-game. Cannot be enabled with Checks Behind Skills.

options.label: Progressive Level Cap Size
options.description: Levels unlocked by each Progressive Level Cap. -1 uses the original milestone caps.

options.label: Bounty Insanity
options.description: Completing Vault Hunters bounties sends Archipelago checks. 0 disables bounty checks.

options.label: Bounty Checks Per Progressive
options.description: Bounty checks unlocked by each Progressive Bounty item. Starts with 10 bounty checks unlocked.

options.label: Death Link
options.description: Share deaths with other DeathLink-enabled Archipelago players.

options.label: Death Link Vaults Only
options.description: Only send and receive DeathLinks while the player is inside a vault.

options.label: Death Link Vault Curse
options.description: Replace received DeathLink deaths with a curse on the current or next vault.

options.label: Enable Traps
options.description: Whether trap items are included in the item pool.

options.label: Trap Percentage
options.description: Percent of non-required item slots to reserve for traps when traps are enabled.

options.label: Mana Loss Trap Weight
options.description: Reduces the players mana to 0

options.label: Locked Out Trap Weight
options.description: Locks the next vault you enter

options.label: Buff Enemies Trap Weight
options.description: Adds enemy modifiers to the next vault

options.label: Nerf Player Trap Weight
options.description: Adds negative player modifiers to the next vault

options.label: Silenced Trap Weight
options.description: Prevents ability use for some time

options.label: Bottle Drain Trap Weight
options.description: Drains 25-50% of a vault vial, potion, mixture, or brew

options.label: Advancement Difficulty
options.description:
Sets what types of minecraft advancements that will be locations and considered for logic.
valid options for base Minecraft are ["task", "goal", "challenge"]

options.label: Activated Modules
options.description:
Sets which modules are activated.
valid options are ["Advancements", "FTBQuests", "BetterQuesting"]

options.label: FTB Quest Shapes
options.description:
Shapes of FTB quests that will be locations and considered for logic.
valid options for base FTB Quests are ["circle", "square", "rsquare", "diamond", "pentagon", "hexagon", "octagon", "heart", "gear", "none"]

options.label: Better Questing Shapes
options.description:
Shapes of Better Questing quests that will be locations and considered for logic.
valid options for base Better Questing are ["main", "other"]

options.label: Unlock Type
options.description:
Controls how locations are accessed.
Tab type gives access to a page of advancements/quests at a time.
Tree type gives access to the dependants of an advancements/quests.

options.label: End Goal
options.description:
The Goal of the Randomizer.
Use a custom advancement by using it's resource name ie. "adv minecraft:adventure/adventuring_time (Adventuring Time)"
Format: "<type> <advancement_name|quest_name> (<display_name>)"
type = one of [adv, ftb]

options.label: Advancements Give Rewards
options.description:
Whether to give a reward when getting an advancement check.
When off:
 - advancement rewards will behave as expected in vanilla.
 - only advancements that have dependants or advancement tabs will have checks associated with them.
When on:
 - advancement rewards will behave as expected in vanilla (ie. still get xp for Return to Sender).
 - advancement checks will grant a reward based on the advancement icon.
 - adds filler checks for advancements that have no dependants.

options.label: Quests Give Rewards
options.description:
Whether to give a reward when getting an ftb quests check.
When off:
 - quest rewards will behave as you would normally expect from ftb quests (granted for completing quests).
 - only quests that have dependants or quest chapters will have checks associated with them.

When on:
 - receiving a ftb quest check will grant the reward associated with the
quest instead of being able to get them by completing the quest.
 - adds filler checks for quests that have no dependants.

options.label: Are Better Questing Quest Rewards Randomized
options.description:
Whether to give a reward when getting an better questing check.
When off:
 - quest rewards will behave as you would normally expect from better questing (granted for completing quests).
 - only quests that have dependants or quest chapters will have checks associated with them.

When on:
 - receiving a better questing check will grant the reward associated with the
quest instead of being able to get them by completing the quest.
 - adds filler checks for quests that have no dependants.

options.label: Filler Items
options.description:
Items to use as filler.
Items must be in format <amount> <item_name>: <weight>
Example: 1 minecraft:iron_ingot: 1

options.label: Start With Roots
options.description:
With this set to true all checks that don't have any dependencies will be unlocked from the start.
eg. root advancements

options.label: Checks (REQUIRED, check setup guide for how to fill this in)
options.description:
Advancements and quests from the game.
This is not done manually, check the setup guide.

options.label: Start Inventory
options.description:
Start with the specified amount of these items.
Format: "<type> <item_name> (<display_name>)": 1
Example: {"adv minecraft:story/root (Minecraft)": 1, "adv minecraft:adventure/root (Adventure)": 1}
^^^ This starts you with the root of the story advancement tab and the root of the adventure advancement tab
Type one of [adv, ftb, item]

options.label: Goal
options.description: Determines which ending is required to complete the game.

options.label: Level Requirements
options.description: Determines whether level requirements use the vanilla order or are shuffled.

options.label: Goal Type
options.description:
Goals:
Key goal: Go out the door with specific key

Deadline: Beat deadline x, y amount of times

Memory Packs: Beat x amount of unique memory packs

options.label: Which key ending should be achieved
options.description:
For key ending:
Bad ending: Go out the door with skeleton key
Good ending: Go out the door with sacred key (999 + skeleton key)

options.label: What deadline to reach
options.description:
Determines what deadline should be reached to beat deadline goal
(Goal: Beat deadline x, y amount of times)
This is x

options.label: How many times should deadline goal be reached
options.description:
Determines how many of the deadlines should be beat to goal
(Goal: Beat deadline x, y amount of times)
This is y

options.label: How many cards to beat
options.description:
Determines how many memory cards should be beat to goal
(Goal: Beat x amount of unique memory packs)

options.label: Extra Checks
options.description:
[Sacred]
Adds all sacred/holy charms and calls as locations
(14 locations) - (Only recommended for ASync)

[Memory]
Adds all memory cards as locations
(19 locations) - (Only recommended for ASync)

options.label: Percetange lost from Clover Trap
options.description: How many of your clover tickets are lost when reciving a clover trap

options.label: Percetange lost from Coin Trap
options.description: How many of your coins are lost when reciving a clover trap

options.label: Trap Amount
options.description: How many clover and coin traps there will be of each

options.label: Deathlink
options.description:
Deathlink settings: (Ankh still saves you but not others)

Normal: Sends deathlink upon any death recieved besides restart

Include restart: Sends deathlinks upon any death recieved

options.label: Hard Mode
options.description: Makes the game be in hard mode

options.label: Difficulty Mode
options.description:
Sets which difficulty mode(s) will be count towards the goal.
(note: both difficulties will be available for checks regardless)

options.label: Ship Count
options.description:
How many different ship/difficulty combinations you need to win with.
(note: will be capped to 10 if Difficulty is set to Hard Only)

options.label: Starting Ship
options.description: Which ship starts unlocked

options.label: Starting Difficulty
options.description: Which difficulty starts unlocked for the chosen ship

options.label: Damage Multiplier
options.description: Adds a permanent +1% damage multiplier to your run per stack.

options.label: Projectile Size Multiplier
options.description: Adds a permanent +1% projectile size multiplier to your run per stack.

options.label: Projectile Speed Multiplier
options.description: Adds a permanent +5% projectile speed multiplier to your run per stack.

options.label: Score Multiplier
options.description:
Increase your end of run score. (Purely visual and has no impact on gameplay.)
Will be treated as enabled if no other filler items are turned on.

options.label: Game Mode
options.description:
Trophy Mode: To win, the player needs to collect one trophy apparatus from each moon (11 with no custom moons).

Collectathon: A new rare scrap is added, called the Archipelago Chest. To win, the player must collect a certain 
amount of them as well as a selection of random scrap

Credit Hunt: To win, the player needs to receive a specific amount of company credit items from the multiworld.

options.label: Collectathon Scrap Goal
options.description: The number of collectathon scrap you need to complete the collectathon goal

options.label: Collectathon Random Scrap
options.description:
Collectathon mode:
The number of random scrap required in addition to the main collectathon scrap

options.label: Credit Replacement
options.description:
Credit Hunt mode:
Replaces the specified percent of filler items with company credits

options.label: Required Credits
options.description:
Credit Hunt mode:
The percent of company credits in the pool that are required to beat the game. If there are 20 credits in the pool
and the player sets this to 75, then once 75% of the 20 credits, or 15 credits, are collected, they will win

options.label: Grade Locations Per Moon
options.description:
The total number of grade locations generated for each moon. A grade location is completed by collecting enough 
scrap in one day to obtain the minimum required grade on a moon.

options.label: Num Quotas
options.description:
The number of quota locations to create. A quota location is completed whenever the player fulfills
money_per_quota_location-worth of quota. Progress accumulates over quotas and crew wipes.

Ex: If money_per_quota_location = 70 and the first quota is 120, then 1 quota location will be completed when the 
    player fulfills their first quota. If the second quota is 200, then 3 additional quota locations will be 
    completed when the player fulfills their second quota. 320 total quota has been fulfilled at this point, so a
    total of 4 quota locations are complete.

options.label: Quota Checkpoint Every
options.description:
How many quota locations the player must complete between each checkpoint unlock event.
With the default values (num_quotas=15 and quota_checkpoint_every=3), quota locations will be grouped into five
spheres with three locations each. This helps ensure that important early items are not stuck behind late quota
locations. Set higher than num_quotas to disable checkpoints entirely and group all quota locations into a single
sphere.

options.label: Money Per Quota Location
options.description:
The total amount of quota a player must obtain to complete each quota location
For example, if money per quota location is 500, you need to reach 500 total quota for each quota location

options.label: Scrapsanity
options.description:
Enables scrapsanity, which adds locations for collecting each scrap for the first time.
Warning: adds >50 locations to the randomizer

options.label: Randomize Company Building
options.description:
Locks the company building behind an item in the multiworld, preventing the player from routing there to sell scrap until they receive 
the required item

options.label: Randomize Scanner
options.description: Locks the scanner behind an item in the multiworld, rendering the player unable to scan until they receive it

options.label: Randomize Terminal
options.description: Locks the terminal behind an item in the multiworld, preventing its use until the player receive the item

options.label: Starting Stamina Bars
options.description: The player begins with this many stamina bars, and the rest have to be unlocked.

options.label: Starting Inventory Slots
options.description: The player begins with this many inventory slots, and the rest have to be unlocked.

options.label: Grade Location Required Grade
options.description:
The end-of-day grade required to complete a grade location on a moon. This option will be ignored if 
split_moon_grades is true.

options.label: Split Moon Grades
options.description: Allows the player to customize the required grade for easy, medium, and hard moons separately.

options.label: Easy Moon Location Grade
options.description: The end-of-day grade required to complete a grade location on an easy difficulty moon

options.label: Medium Moon Location Grade
options.description: The end-of-day grade required to complete a grade location on a medium difficulty moon

options.label: Hard Moon Location Grade
options.description: The end-of-day grade required to complete a grade location on a hard difficulty moon

options.label: Minimum Scrap Spawn Chance
options.description:
Scrap will not contain important items or be required for the Collectathon goal if their spawn chance on an in-logic 
moon is less than this percentage. A value of less than 3% can significantly slow down games, while values above 6% 
exclude most scrap.

options.label: Minimum Monster Spawn Chance
options.description:
A bestiary entry will not contain important items if the monster's spawn chance on an in-logic moon is greater than or equal to this percentage. 
A value of less than 3% can significantly slow down games.

options.label: Min Money Per Money Item
options.description: The minimum amount of money that a money item can give the player.

options.label: Max Money Per Money Item
options.description:
The maximum amount of money that a money item can give the player.
This can't be less than min_money.

options.label: Modify Scrap Spawns
options.description:
Modifies the spawn rates and availability of scrap on every moon to reduce the chance of a player getting stuck for 
a long time trying to find a rare item that is blocking progression.

options.label: Exclude Killing
options.description: Guarantees that scrapsanity locations requiring the player to kill an enemy will not contain important items

options.label: Exclude Hive
options.description: Guarantees that the Hive scrapsanity location will not contain an important item

options.label: Exclude Egg
options.description: Guarantees that the Sapsucker Egg scrapsanity location will not contain an important item

options.label: Money Weight
options.description:
The weight of money items in the filler/trap pool. 
When redeemed, this item grants between min_money and max_money credits, though they don't count toward the quota.

options.label: Birthday Gift Weight
options.description:
The weight of birthday gifts in the filler/trap pool. 
When redeemed, this item sends a random store item down in the dropship.

options.label: Strength Training Weight
options.description: The total weight of strength training items. Every item received reduces the carry weight of all scrap.

options.label: Scrap Cloning Weight
options.description:
The weight of clone scrap items in the filler/trap pool. 
When redeemed, this item duplicates a random piece of scrap in the ship.

options.label: More Time Weight
options.description:
The weight of more time items in the filler/trap pool. 
When redeemed, this item adds one day to the current quota (up to 9).

options.label: Less Time Weight
options.description:
The weight of less time traps in the filler/trap pool. 
When consumed, this trap reduces the remaining time to complete the current quota by one day.

options.label: Bracken Trap Weight
options.description:
The weight of bracken traps in the filler/trap pool.
When consumed, this trap spawns a bracken on the current or next moon visited.

options.label: Haunt Trap Weight
options.description:
The weight of haunt traps in the filler/trap pool.
When consumed, this trap spawns a ghost girl on the current or next moon visited.

options.label: Death Link Scrap Loss
options.description:
The percentage of scrap lost when the last living player dies from death link. 0 means no scrap is lost, 50 means 
half of the scrap in the ship is lost, 100 means all scrap is lost. This option does not preserve scrap if the last 
player dies naturally, and does nothing if death link is disabled.

options.label: Emulator
options.description: Choose the emulator you want to use

options.label: Bell Warp
options.description: Allow sequence break using the bells.

options.label: Keep Blackjack ?
options.description: Toggle if the player starts with a starting weapon

options.label: Chick randomized ?
options.description:
Toggle wether or not the Chick should be randomized.
Enabling this means you can get blocked and have to wait until all the Chick are found in the multiworld

options.label: Furious Tornado randomized ?
options.description:
Toggle wether or not the Furious Tornado should be randomized.
Enabling this means you can get blocked and have to wait until the tornado is found in the multiworld

options.label: Optional randomized ?
options.description:
Toggle if the optional items like Pipe and Broken Vase,
which are not required to complete their respective events, should be randomized too
If this is on: Picking the item in the world will give a randomized item
If this is off: Picking the item in the world will give the original item (Pipe or Broken Vase in this example)

options.label: Bonus Chests randomized ?
options.description:
Toggle if chests containing AP Crystals or Apples, should give a random item too.
If this is on: Picking the AP Crystals/Apples from these chests will also give a randomized item too
If this is off: Picking the AP Crystals/Apples from these chests will NOT give a randomized item too.

options.label: Cleared event rewards
options.description:
Toggle if event cleared should count as a location check or not
If on: You will get random rewards when clearing event
If off: Clearing events will give you nothing

options.label: Chick amount
options.description:
Allows to control how many chick will be available
This is usefull to prevent being stuck in the first area early.
You only require 4 of those so a higher number means you're more likely
to be able to pass the count check early.
Note: This is not used if chick are not randomized

options.label: Random status alteration ?
options.description: Toggle if the player can receive status alteration as a handicap

options.label: Deathlink
options.description: Toggle to synchronize death across the multi world

options.label: No Game Over
options.description: Toggle this if you want to never run out of lifes

options.label: Entrance randomization enabled ?
options.description:
WARNING: THIS IS HIGHLY EXPERIMENTAL, IT WILL BREAK YOUR GAME
Toggle if the door should be randomized too
WARNING: THIS IS HIGHLY EXPERIMENTAL, IT WILL BREAK YOUR GAME

options.label: Faster Motocross Retry ?
options.description:
Toggle to warp back to the Motcross start after leaving the Mermaid Beach
If disabled, player will be warped to the start of the Masakari Jungle
This setting is ignored if entrance randomization is enabled

options.label: Start Level
options.description: Choose which level to start in.

options.label: Goal Level
options.description: Choose which level must be completed to finish the game.

options.label: Goal Requirement
options.description: Choose the number of levels that must be completed to unlock the goal.

options.label: Perfect Goal
options.description: Choose if the goal must be cleared with a perfect rank. Has no effect if the goal level is a secret mission.

options.label: Skipped Levels
options.description:
List as many levels as you would like to skip completing for the goal.

Skipped levels will still exist in the item pool, and can still be completed to add progress towards unlocking the goal, but will not be considered in logic.

options.label: Auto Exclude Skipped Level Locations
options.description: Choose if skipped levels should automatically have all of their locations excluded.

options.label: Auto Exclude Goal Level Locations
options.description: Choose if the goal level should automatically have all of its locations excluded.

options.label: Require Gutterman Shield Break
options.description: Forces a way to break Guttermen shields (Knuckleblaster or any Alternate Shotgun) to be required in logic.

options.label: Speedrunner Logic
options.description:
Enables various speedrunning tech in logic, such as glitches, out-of-bounds exploits, and other difficult tricks. 

Work in progress! Only implemented until the end of Layer 3.
May contain mistakes or errors! If you choose to test this, please report any issues in the Archipelago Discord server!

options.label: Level Unlock Type
options.description: Choose if levels will be unlocked one at a time, or whole layers at once.

options.label: Secret Mission Unlock Type
options.description: Choose if secret missions should be unlocked by using their secret exits, or by finding items in the multiworld.

options.label: Secret Exit Behavior
options.description:
Choose if using secret exits should count the current level as completed, or if secret exits should NOT count the 
current level as completed, and instead add rewards for using each secret exit.

Does not affect secret exits leading to prime sanctums.

options.label: Trap Item Percentage
options.description: Choose the percentage of trap items that will appear when filling the item pool with junk.

options.label: Filler Item Weights
options.description: Choose the odds of each filler item being created when filling the item pool with junk.

options.label: Trap Item Weights
options.description: Choose the odds of each trap item being created when filling the item pool with traps.

options.label: Enemy Rewards
options.description:
Adds location checks for defeating enemies and unlocking terminal entries.

Bosses: Only includes bosses at the end of each act and in Prime Sanctums.

Extra: Also includes some additional bosses that usually only appear once.

All: Includes all bosses and enemies.

options.label: Challenge Rewards
options.description: Adds location checks for completing each level's challenge, except for the goal.

options.label: P Rank Rewards
options.description: Adds location checks for completing each level with a Perfect Rank, except for the goal.

options.label: Hank Rewards
options.description: Adds location checks for giving Hank and Hank Jr. a head in 1-4 and 5-3.

options.label: Randomize Clash Mode
options.description: Randomizes the unlock for destroying all crates in 4-S.

options.label: Fish Rewards
options.description: Adds location checks for catching each fish in 5-S.

options.label: Cleaning Rewards
options.description: Adds location checks for cleaning every room in 7-S.

options.label: Chess Reward
options.description: Adds a location check for winning chess against a bot in the Developer Museum.

options.label: Rocket Race Reward
options.description: Adds a location check for winning the rocket race in the Developer Museum.

options.label: Starting Weapon Pool
options.description:
Choose a pool of possible starting weapons and their weights of being selected.

Some weapons will not be considered valid depending on other options:

If the start level is 2-3, 8-2, or 8-3, all arms will be removed from the pool.

If choosing to start with Feedbacker, it will be removed from the pool.

If choosing not to start with Feedbacker, the Whiplash, Freezeframe, and all Railcannons are removed from the pool.

If choosing to randomize secondary fire and not to start with Feedbacker, the S.R.S. Cannon and Firestarter are removed from the pool.

If choosing to randomize secondary fire, not to start with Feedbacker, and for the Nailgun to be in its Alternate form, the Overheat is removed from the pool.

options.label: Randomize Secondary Fire
options.description:
Locks the ability to use a weapon's alternate fire behind items that must be found in the multiworld.

Split: Separate items will be created for each weapon and secondary fire.

Progressive: Two items will be created for each weapon, the first item found will unlock the weapon, and the second will unlock the secondary fire.

options.label: Start with Feedbacker
options.description: Choose whether or not to start the game with the Feedbacker arm.

options.label: Starting Stamina
options.description: Choose how many bars of stamina to start with.

options.label: Starting Wall Jumps
options.description: Choose how many wall jumps to start with.

options.label: Start with Slide
options.description: Choose whether or not to start the game with the ability to slide.

options.label: Start with Slam
options.description: Choose whether or not to start the game with the ability to slam.

options.label: Revolver Form
options.description:
Choose whether the revolver should be in its standard or alternate form initially.

The Piercer, Marksman, or Sharpshooter revolver still need to be found before the revolver can be used.

The other form must be unlocked.

options.label: Shotgun Form
options.description:
Choose whether the shotgun should be in its standard or alternate form initially.

The Core Eject, Pump Charge, or Sawed-On shotgun still need to be found before the shotgun can be used.

The other form must be unlocked.

options.label: Nailgun Form
options.description:
Choose whether the nailgun should be in its standard or alternate form initially.

The Attractor, Overheat, or JumpStart nailgun still need to be found before the nailgun can be used.

The other form must be unlocked.

options.label: Randomize Skulls
options.description: Turns the red and blue skulls into items that must be found before they will appear in levels.

options.label: Randomize Limbo Switches
options.description: Randomizes the four switches in the Limbo layer.

options.label: Randomize Violence Switches
options.description: Randomizes the three switches in 7-2.

options.label: Point Multiplier
options.description: Multiplies the amount of points earned to reduce grind.

options.label: UI Color Randomizer
options.description:
Randomizes UI colors, either once at the beginning of a run, or every time a level is loaded.

Does not affect item popup colors.

This option can be changed later.

options.label: Gun Color Randomizer
options.description:
Randomizes gun colors, either once at the beginning of a run, or every time a level is loaded.

This option can be changed later.

options.label: Music Randomizer
options.description:
Randomizes the music that plays during the game.

Music can be re-randomized, or toggled on or off later.

Some music is never randomized.

options.label: Cyber Grind Hints
options.description:
Every 5 waves cleared in The Cyber Grind will unlock a hint.

This option can NOT be changed later.

options.label: Death Link
options.description:
When you die, everyone dies. The reverse is also true.

This option can be changed later.

options.label: Death Link Amnesty
options.description: Choose how many deaths must happen before a death link is sent to the multiworld.

options.label: Shuffle Chai Attacks
options.description: Shuffles Chai's attacks from the store into the multiworld.

options.label: Shuffle Peppermint Attacks
options.description: Shuffles Peppermint's attacks from the store into the multiworld.

options.label: Shuffle Macaron Attacks
options.description: Shuffles Macaron's attacks from the store into the multiworld.

options.label: Shuffle Korsica Attacks
options.description: Shuffles Korsica's attacks from the store into the multiworld.

options.label: Shuffle Special Attacks
options.description: Shuffles Chai's special attacks from the store into the multiworld.

options.label: Shuffle Store Items
options.description: Shuffles the items from the store into the multiworld.

options.label: Shuffle Chips
options.description: Shuffles the chips from the store into the multiworld.

options.label: Allow Selling in Store
options.description:
Choose if attacks and special attacks should be able to be sold after getting a location check from them.

If disabled, after purchasing something in the store that can be sold, its value will be set to 0.

Items and chips can't be sold.

options.label: Shuffle VLogs
options.description:
Shuffles the VLogs scattered around Vandelay campus into the multiworld.

VLogs in the SPECTRA Hub Room and Vandelay Gameworks areas are not randomized.

options.label: Generation Behavior
options.description:
Determines how generation should handle too many items and not enough locations.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Error: Generation will return an OptionError indicating the options to change to improve generation.
Start Inventory:  Generation will place the extra items into your starting inventory.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

options.label: Starting Weapons
options.description:
Determines which weapons you will be starting the game with,
provide a count of the weapons you want to be picked between,
two are selected to be placed on Veldin.
If Veldin skip is enabled, the weapons will be granted immediately.

options.label: Bolt and XP Multiplier
options.description:
Determines what your base bolt and xp multiplier will be set to,
recommended to use x8 if you're looking to do a sync.

options.label: Progressive Weapons
options.description:
Determines whether weapon level-ups are progressive items or not.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Disable:            Weapon leveling and exp functions like in the vanilla game.
Manual Leveling:    Weapon level caps are increased when a progressive item is collected, weapon exp past the cap
                    is disabled.
Automatic Leveling: Weapons level-up when its progressive item is collected, weapon exp is disabled.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Note: If Weapon Level Locations are enabled, Automatic Leveling will be forced to Manual Leveling instead.

options.label: Weapon Mods
options.description:
Determines whether weapon mods are items in the multiworld.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Vanilla:         Weapon mods are not added as items. Mods are unlocked like they are in the base game,
                 but can only appear on weapons that have them in the base game.
Modpack:         Weapon modpacks are added as items. Receiving a modpack unlocks all 3 mods for that weapon.
Individual Mods: Shock, Acid, and Lock-on mods are all added as separate items for each weapon in the item pool.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
If this option is not set to Vanilla, any weapon can get any weapon mod.
Even those that are not normally compatible in the base game.
Some mods might not behave as expected on weapons that they are not normally compatible with.

options.label: Armor Upgrade
options.description:
Determines how many Progressive Armor items are included in the item pool.
Set to 0 for No Armor.
Set to 4 for all vanilla Armor to be available.
Set above 4 to add extra Armor copies into the item pool.
Collecting more than 4 Progressive Armor items will do nothing.

options.label: Filler Weight
options.description:
Sets the relative weights of filler items in the item pool.
A higher value increases the likelihood of a particular filler item to appear in the item pool.
If progressive weapons are enabled, weapon xp automatically gets removed from the pool.

options.label: Enable Traps
options.description:
Determines whether trap items are included in the item pool.
------------------------------------------------------------
Disabled: No traps will be included in the item pool.
Enabled:  Traps will be included in the item pool.
------------------------------------------------------------

options.label: Trap Weight
options.description:
Sets the relative weights of trap items in the item pool.
A higher value increases the likelihood of a particular trap to appear in the item pool.
This option has no effect when traps are disabled.

options.label: Trap Magnitude
options.description:
Sets the duration/impact of trap items in the item pool.
A higher value increases the duration in seconds of a timed trap or the impact up to 100% of a non-timed trap.
This option has no effect when traps are disabled.

Min value is 1, max value is 300.

options.label: Filler Magnitude
options.description:
Sets the duration/impact of filler items in the item pool.
A higher value increases the duration in seconds of jackpot or the percentage of bolts or nanotech XP gained.
Bolts and nanotech are still capped at 200,000 and 300,000 per filler respectively,
but a higher value will increase the amount gained up to that cap.

Min value is 1, max value is 300.

options.label: Weapon Vendors
options.description:
Determines whether weapon vendors are locations in the world.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Disabled: No weapon vendors are locations.
Enabled:  Weapon vendors are added as locations.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Weapons are still randomized regardless of this setting.

options.label: Skill Points
options.description:
Determines which skill points are locations in the world.
Any Skill Points locked behind other locations such as Ranger Missions require those options to be enabled.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Simple skill point locations are the following:
- Aridia: Skillpoint: Go for hang time
- Phoenix: Skillpoint: Beat Helga's best time
- Phoenix: Skillpoint: Turn Up The Heat
- Phoenix: Skillpoint: Monkeying around
- Marcadia: Skillpoint: Reflect on how to score
- Daxx: Skillpoint: Bugs to Birds
- Annihilation Nation: Skillpoint: Lights, camera action!
- Aquatos: Skillpoint: Search for sunken treasure
- Tyhrranosis: Skillpoint: Be a Sharpshooter
- Obani Gemini: Skillpoint: Get to the belt
- Blackwater City: Skillpoint: Bash the party
- Koros: Skillpoint: You break it, you win it
- Metropolis: Skillpoint: 2002 was a good year in the city
- Crash Site: Skillpoint: Aim High
- Aridia: Skillpoint: Zap back at ya'
- Hideout: Skillpoint: Break the Dan
- Command Center: Skillpoint: Spread your germs

options.label: Trophies
options.description:
Determines which trophies are locations in the world.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None:         No trophies are locations.
Collectables: Only the collectable trophies found on various planets are locations.
All:          All special trophies are now also locations.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Note: Skill Master trophy is only included in the pool if all 30 skill points are in the world.
NG+ trophies are only included in the pool if ngplus_start is enabled, 
and the Nano Finder trophy is only included if the nanotech limitation is also set to include level 200.

options.label: Titanium Bolts
options.description:
Determines whether Titanium Bolts are locations in the world.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Disabled: No Titanium Bolts are locations.
Enabled:  Titanium Bolts are added as locations. 
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Any Titanium bolts locked behind other locations such as Ranger Missions require those options to be enabled

options.label: Rangers
options.description:
Determines whether Ranger Missions and anything that is located in or behind them is a location.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None:               Removes anything that is located in or behind a Ranger Mission from being a location.
Story Missions:     Story related Ranger Missions, and anything directly locked behind them, are added as locations.
Optional Missions:  Ranger Missions that are optional in the main game, and anything directly locked behind them,
                    are added as locations.
All:                Ranger Missions, and anything directly locked behind them, are added as locations.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Story missions include:    Marcadia, Blackwater City, and Aridia missions.
Optional missions include: Tyhrranosis: Operation ISLAND STRIKE and Metropolis: Operation URBAN STORM missions
Any Skill Points or Titanium Bolts are added if their respective setting is enabled.

options.label: Vidcomics
options.description:
Determines whether VidComics and anything that is located in or behind them is a location.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Disabled: Removes anything that is located in or behind a VidComic from being a location.
Enabled:  VidComics, and anything directly locked behind them, are added as locations.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Any Skill Points or Titanium Bolts are added if their respective setting is enabled.

options.label: VR Challenges
options.description:
Determines whether VR Challenges and anything that is located in or behind them is a location.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Disabled: Removes anything that is located in or behind a VR Challenge from being a location.
Enabled:  VR Challenges, and anything directly locked behind them, are added as locations.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Any Skill Points or Titanium Bolts are added if their respective setting is enabled.
This option also includes the VR Gadget Training Challenge before Daxx and all of its checks

options.label: Arena
options.description:
Determines whether Annihilation Nation challenges and anything that is located in or behind them is a location.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None:        Removes anything that is located in or behind an Annihilation Nation challenge from being a location.
First Only:  Annihilation Nation 1 challenges, and anything directly locked behind them, are added as locations.
Second Only: Annihilation Nation 2 challenges, and anything directly locked behind them, are added as locations.
All:         All Annihilation Nation challenges, and anything directly locked behind them, are added as locations.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Any Skill Points or Titanium Bolts are added if their respective setting is enabled.

options.label: Sewer Crystals
options.description:
Determines whether sewer crystals are locations in the world.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None:     No sewer crystals are locations.
Every 20: Makes every 20 sewer crystals locations starting from 20 sewer crystals collected.
Every 10: Makes every 10 sewer crystals locations starting from 10 sewer crystals collected.
Every 5:  Makes every 5 sewer crystals locations starting from 5 sewer crystals collected.
All:      All sewer crystals are locations.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
If set to anything other than none, this will also add the "Hit the motherload skillpoint" into the world
when skill points are set to "all".

options.label: Sewer Limitation
options.description:
Determines the upper limit of the Sewer Crystal locations in the multiworld between 1 and 101.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This option has no effect when sewer_crystals are disabled.
The locations will appear in steps the player specified in sewer_crystals.
Setting this to 100 or above will also add "Hit the motherload" into the pool if skill_points are set to "all".
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Example: If set to 40 then you only need to collect up to 40 sewer crystals. Any more won't count as checks.

options.label: Nanotech Milestones
options.description:
Determines whether nanotech milestones are locations in the world.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
None:     No nanotech milestones are locations.
Every 20: Makes every 20 nanotech milestones locations starting from nanotech level 20.
Every 10: Makes every 10 nanotech milestones locations starting from nanotech level 20.
Every 5:  Makes every 5 nanotech milestones locations starting from nanotech level 15.
All:      All nanotech milestones are locations.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

options.label: Nanotech Limitation
options.description:
Determines the upper limit of the nanotech milestone locations in the multiworld between 11 and 200.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Nanotech milestone locations start from nanotech level 11 and can go up to nanotech level 200.
The locations will appear in steps the player specified in nanotech_milestones.
This option has no effect when nanotech_milestones are disabled.
This option has no effect past 100 if ngplus_start is disabled.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Example: If set to 40 then you only need to level up to nanotech level 40 as any higher won't count as checks.

options.label: Exclude Locations
options.description: Prevent these locations from having an important item.

options.label: Ship Nose
options.description:
Cosmetic:
What Nose should you have on the ship?

options.label: Ship Wings
options.description:
Cosmetic:
What Wings should you have on the ship?

options.label: Ship Skin
options.description:
Cosmetic:
What Skin should you have on the ship?

options.label: Player Skin
options.description:
Cosmetic:
What Skin should Ratchet have?
Remember to reload your save file after starting a new game to apply the skin!
Alternatively, go to the Armor Vendor to reload the skin.

options.label: Clank Pack Options
options.description:
Determines how Clank and his packs appear in the world.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Start with:             Begin with Clank and all packs already collected.
Shuffled as one:        Clank is randomized in the pool, finding him will give access to both packs.
Shuffled Independently: Each pack is an independent item, Heli-pack is required to glide.
Shuffled Progressive:   Two Progressive packs are added, the first gives Heli-pack and the second gives Thruster.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Warning: Using this option while starting on Veldin may result in a restrictive start for solo seeds!

options.label: Ship Vendor
options.description:
Determines whether ship vendor cosmetics are locations in the world.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Disabled: No ship vendor cosmetics are locations.
Enabled:  Ship vendor cosmetics are added as locations.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Note: Each planet you have will put the next 2 items in the ship vendor in order of how they would appear in the
vanilla game.
You cannot change ship cosmetics with this option enabled.

options.label: Armor Vendor
options.description:
Determines whether armor vendor items are locations in the world.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Disabled: No armor vendor items are locations.
Enabled:  Armor vendor items are added as locations.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Visiting the planet associated with the armor will put it in the armor vendor.
Magnaplate:   Starship Phoenix
Adamantite:   Aquatos
Aegis Mark V: Zeldrin Starport
Infernox:     Koros
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Note: Disabling this option will not make armor work like in the vanilla game.
Armor is determined by the number of progressive armor items you have.

options.label: NG+ Items
options.description:
Determines how New Game Plus items appear in the multiworld.
When enabled, it puts the RY3N0 into the item pool and the mega versions of weapons in the vendor
if you have a V5 weapon.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Disabled: The RY3N0 will not appear in the multiworld, the mega versions of weapons are not purchasable.
Enabled:  The RY3N0 will appear in the multiworld, the mega versions of weapons are purchasable.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
For progressive weapons, it will instead add 3 more upgrades to the pool, up to V8.
When enabled, locations for the mega weapon vendor purchases will not be sent out, it'll provide the mega version
of the weapon only.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

options.label: NG+ Vendor
options.description:
Determines if the RY3N0 Purchase should be a location in the vendor or not.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Disabled: The RY3N0 is not a purchasable location.
Enabled:  The RY3N0 is a purchasable location.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

options.label: NG+ Start
options.description:
Determines if the game should start in New Game Plus mode.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Disabled:                Game starts in normal mode.
Enabled:                 Game starts in Challenge Mode.
Enabled with Multiplier: Game starts in Challenge Mode, and the NG+ multiplier is enabled.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WARNING:    The NG+ bolt multiplier stacks with the bolt and XP multiplier, which can lead to very high multipliers
            that trivialize everything to do with bolts. Use if you really hate grinding for bolts.

options.label: Help Desk
options.description:
Determines if the in-game help desk should be enabled/disabled from the start.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Disabled: Helpdesk is disabled when creating a new save.
Enabled:  Helpdesk is enabled when creating a new save.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

options.label: Vendor Access
options.description:
Determines if vendor items should become available after a planet is visited or once its infobot has been collected.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Visit:      Vendor items are available after visiting a planet.
Infobot:    Vendor items are available when the infobot is collected.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The Holo-shield glove is normally accessible after defeating the Noid Queen on Tyhrranosis instead of just visiting.

options.label: Weapon Level Locations
options.description:
Determines whether weapon levels should be locations or not.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
All weapon levels can be locations (including V6, V7, V8 if ngplus_items are enabled).
Only locations for the selected levels will be added. To disable weapon level locations, leave the brackets empty.
The valid keys are the following: V2, V3, V4, V5, V6, V7, V8
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Note: If progressive weapons are enabled, leveling will be forced to manual leveling instead of automatic leveling.

options.label: Bonus VidComic Health Upgrades
options.description:
Determines how many Bonus VidComic Health Upgrades are included in the item pool.
These are extra upgrades that are not normally available in the vanilla game.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Set to 0 for No extra upgrades.
Set to 3 for all extra upgrades to be available.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Note: This option has no effect if VidComics are disabled.

options.label: VidComic Health Upgrade Locations
options.description:
Determines if the VidComic Health Upgrades should be locations or not.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Disabled: The VidComic Health Upgrades are not locations.
Enabled:  The VidComic Health Upgrades are locations.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Note: This option has no effect if VidComics are disabled.

options.label: Deathlink Behavior
options.description:
Determines how the player is affected by a Deathlink.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Instant Kill: The player is killed immediately.
Nanopak Save: The Nanopak can save the player from the Deathlink.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This option has no effect if Deathlink is disabled.

options.label: Death link
options.description: WHEN THE USER DIES, EVERYONE WHO ENABLED DEATHLINK DIES. OF COURSE, THE REVERSE IS TRUE TOO.

options.label: Randomize level order
options.description:
THE NODES INSIDE OF THE PYRAMID APPEAR IN A RANODM ORDER.
NOTE THE TOP MOST LAYER WILL APPEAR IN THE SAME ORDER.

options.label: Unlock pyramid layers
options.description: THE USER WILL REQUIRE PRIVILEGE ESCALATIONS IN ORDER TO ACCESS HIGHER LAYERS IN THE PYRAMID.

options.label: Unlock weapon firing
options.description: THE USER WILL NEED FIRING CLEARNCES TO FIRE THE PISTOL, SHOTGUN, MACHINEGUN, AND SNIPERRIFLE.

options.label: Dungeons
options.description:
This controls whether dungeon locations are randomized.

This means the items found in dungeons will be randomized, not that the entrances to dungeons will be randomized.

options.label: Tingle Chests
options.description:
Tingle Chests are hidden in dungeons and must be bombed to make them appear. (2 in DRC, 1 each in FW, TotG, ET, and
WT). This controls whether they are randomized.

options.label: Dungeon Secrets
options.description:
DRC, FW, TotG, ET, and WT each contain 2-3 secret items (11 in total). This controls whether these are randomized.

The items are relatively well-hidden (they aren't in chests), so don't select this option unless you're prepared to
search each dungeon high and low!

options.label: Puzzle Secret Caves
options.description: This controls whether the rewards from puzzle-focused secret caves are randomized locations.

options.label: Combat Secret Caves
options.description:
This controls whether the rewards from combat-focused secret caves (besides Savage Labyrinth) are randomized
locations.

options.label: Savage Labyrinth
options.description: This controls whether the two locations in Savage Labyrinth are randomized.

options.label: Great Fairies
options.description: This controls whether the items given by Great Fairies are randomized.

options.label: Short Sidequests
options.description: This controls whether sidequests that can be completed quickly are randomized.

options.label: Long Sidequests
options.description: This controls whether long sidequests (e.g., Lenzo's assistant, withered trees, goron trading) are randomized.

options.label: Spoils Trading
options.description: This controls whether the items you get by trading in spoils to NPCs are randomized.

options.label: Minigames
options.description: This controls whether most minigames are randomized (auctions, mail sorting, barrel shooting, bird-man contest).

options.label: Battlesquid Minigame
options.description: This controls whether the Windfall battleship minigame is randomized.

options.label: Free Gifts
options.description: This controls whether gifts freely given by NPCs are randomized (Tott, Salvage Corp, imprisoned Tingle).

options.label: Mail
options.description: This controls whether items received from the mail are randomized.

options.label: Lookout Platforms and Rafts
options.description: This controls whether lookout platforms and rafts are randomized.

options.label: Submarines
options.description: This controls whether submarines are randomized.

options.label: Eye Reef Chests
options.description: This controls whether the chests that appear after clearing out the eye reefs are randomized.

options.label: Big Octos and Gunboats
options.description: This controls whether the items dropped by Big Octos and Gunboats are randomized.

options.label: Sunken Treasure (From Triforce Charts)
options.description: This controls whether the sunken treasure chests marked on Triforce Charts are randomized.

options.label: Sunken Treasure (From Treasure Charts)
options.description: This controls whether the sunken treasure chests marked on Treasure Charts are randomized.

options.label: Expensive Purchases
options.description:
This controls whether items that cost many Rupees are randomized (Rock Spire shop, auctions, Tingle's letter,
trading quest).

options.label: Island Puzzles
options.description: This controls whether various island puzzles are randomized (e.g., chests hidden in unusual places).

options.label: Miscellaneous
options.description:
Miscellaneous locations that don't fit into any of the above categories (outdoors chests, wind shrine, Cyclos, etc).
This controls whether these are randomized.

options.label: Randomize Maps & Compasses
options.description:
Controls how dungeon maps and compasses are randomized.

- **Start With Maps & Compasses:** You will start the game with the dungeon maps and compasses for all dungeons.
- **Vanilla Maps & Compasses:** Dungeon maps and compasses will be kept in their vanilla location (non-randomized).
- **Own Dungeon Maps & Compasses:** Dungeon maps and compasses will be randomized locally within their own dungeon.
- **Any Dungeon Maps & Compasses:** Dungeon maps and compasses will be randomized locally within any dungeon.
- **Local Maps & Compasses:** Dungeon maps and compasses will be randomized locally anywhere.
- **Key-Lunacy:** Dungeon maps and compasses can be found anywhere, without restriction.

options.label: Randomize Small Keys
options.description:
Controls how small keys are randomized.

- **Start With Small Keys:** You will start the game with the small keys for all dungeons.
- **Vanilla Small Keys:** Small keys will be kept in their vanilla location (non-randomized).
- **Own Dungeon Small Keys:** Small keys will be randomized locally within their own dungeon.
- **Any Dungeon Small Keys:** Small keys will be randomized locally within any dungeon.
- **Local Small Keys:** Small keys will be randomized locally anywhere.
- **Key-Lunacy:** Small keys can be found in any progression location, if dungeons are randomized.

options.label: Randomize Big Keys
options.description:
Controls how big keys are randomized.

- **Start With Big Keys:** You will start the game with the big keys for all dungeons.
- **Vanilla Big Keys:** Big keys will be kept in their vanilla location (non-randomized).
- **Own Dungeon Big Keys:** Big keys will be randomized locally within their own dungeon.
- **Any Dungeon Big Keys:** Big keys will be randomized locally within any dungeon.
- **Local Big Keys:** Big keys will be randomized locally anywhere.
- **Key-Lunacy:** Big keys can be found in any progression location, if dungeons are randomized.

options.label: Sword Mode
options.description:
Controls whether you start with the Hero's Sword, the Hero's Sword is randomized, or if there are no swords in the
entire game.

- **Start with Hero's Sword:** You will start the game with the basic Hero's Sword already in your inventory.
- **No Starting Sword:** You will start the game with no sword, and have to find it somewhere in the world like
  other randomized items.
- **Swords Optional:** You will start the game with no sword, but they'll still be randomized. However, they are not
  necessary to beat the game. The Hyrule Barrier will be gone, Phantom Ganon in FF is vulnerable to Skull Hammer,
  and the logic does not expect you to have a sword.
- **Swordless:** You will start the game with no sword, and won't be able to find it anywhere. You have to beat the
  entire game using other items as weapons instead of the sword. (Note that Phantom Ganon in FF becomes vulnerable
  to Skull Hammer in this mode.)

options.label: Start with random Item Slide item
options.description: Start with a random item that can item slide. This includes: Bow, Grappling Hook, Boomerang or Hookshot

options.label: Required Bosses Mode
options.description:
In this mode, you will not be allowed to beat the game until certain randomly-chosen bosses are defeated. Nothing in
dungeons for other bosses will ever be required.

You can see which islands have the required bosses on them by opening the sea chart and checking which islands have
blue quest markers.

options.label: Number of Required Bosses
options.description:
Select the number of randomly-chosen bosses that are required in Required Bosses Mode.

The door to Puppet Ganon will not unlock until you've defeated all of these bosses. Nothing in dungeons for other
bosses will ever be required.

options.label: Included Dungeons
options.description: A list of dungeons that should always be included when required bosses mode is on.

options.label: Excluded Dungeons
options.description: A list of dungeons that should always be excluded when required bosses mode is on.

options.label: Chest Type Matches Contents
options.description:
Changes the chest type to reflect its contents. A metal chest has a progress item, a wooden chest has a non-progress
item or a consumable, and a green chest has a potentially required dungeon key.

options.label: Hero Mode
options.description: In Hero Mode, you take four times more damage than normal and heart refills will not drop.

options.label: Obscure Tricks Required
options.description:
Obscure tricks are ways of obtaining items that are not obvious and may involve thinking outside the box.

This option controls the maximum difficulty of obscure tricks the randomizer will require you to do to beat the
game.

options.label: Precise Tricks Required
options.description:
Precise tricks are ways of obtaining items that involve difficult inputs such as accurate aiming or perfect timing.

This option controls the maximum difficulty of precise tricks the randomizer will require you to do to beat the
game.

options.label: Randomize Dungeons
options.description:
Shuffles around which dungeon entrances take you into which dungeons.

(No effect on Forsaken Fortress or Ganon's Tower.)

options.label: Randomize Secret Caves
options.description: Shuffles around which secret cave entrances take you into which secret caves.

options.label: Randomize Nested Minibosses
options.description:
Allows dungeon miniboss doors to act as entrances to be randomized.

If on with random dungeon entrances, dungeons may nest within each other, forming chains of connected dungeons.

options.label: Randomize Nested Bosses
options.description:
Allows dungeon boss doors to act as entrances to be randomized.

If on with random dungeon entrances, dungeons may nest within each other, forming chains of connected dungeons.
