options.label: Goal
options.description:
How you beat the game.
Deathtoll: Defeat Deathtoll.
Emblem Hunt: Collect all 8 master's emblems and turn them in at the Gem Fairy in Greenwood.

options.label: Act Progression
options.description:
Act/World progression.
Vanilla: Talk to town leaders to open the next Act/World.
Open: All worlds are open from the start of the game.

options.label: Stones Placement
options.description:
Determines the placement of the 6 stones needed to enter the World of Evil.
Vanilla: Stones are given by the town leader of each act.
Bosses: Stones are rewarded from the boss lair of each act.
Totally Random: Stones are randomized with everything else.

options.label: Stones Count
options.description: Number of Stones needed to open the World of Evil.

options.label: Open Deathtoll
options.description: Determines if Deathtoll's Palace in the World of Evil is already open.

options.label: Starting Sword
options.description:
Determines the sword you will get in the first chest.
Vanilla: You will get the Sword of Life.
<Sword Name>: You will get that sword.
Randomized: You will get a random sword.

options.label: Magician's Item
options.description:
Determines the item the Magician gives you at the start of the game.
Vanilla: The vanilla reward (Flame Ball).
Random Spell: A random castable magic spell.
Totally Random: Any reward in the item pool.

options.label: Magician's Soul
options.description:
Determines what reward you will get in place of the Magician's Soul at the start of the game.
Vanilla: You get the Soul of Magician.
Random Soul: Any progression soul. (Soul of Magician, Soul of Light, Soul of Detection)
Totally Random: Any reward in the item pool.

options.label: Text Speed
options.description:
Text Speed.
Instant: Text renders an entire window at a time.
Fast: Text renders a character at a time at the same speed as the JP version.

options.label: Release Cutscenes
options.description:
NPC Release Cutscenes.
Show: Shows NPC release cutscenes.
Skip: Skips NPC release cutscenes.

options.label: Equipment Stats
options.description:
Determines equipment power & defense.
Vanilla: No change to the way Weapons/Armor work.
Semi-progressive: Equipment strength/defense scales with the number of swords/armors obtained.
Shuffle: Shuffles the stats of all swords and armor.

options.label: Equipment Scaling
options.description:
Determines the stat progression for swords/armor.
Vanilla: Swords/Armor follow the vanilla 1/2/3/4/6/8/10/12 strength/defense progression.
Improved: Swords/Armor follow an improved 1/3/5/7/9/12/12/12 strength/defense progression.
Strong: Swords/Armor follow a strong 2/4/6/9/12/12/12/12 strength/defense progression.
Weak: Swords/Armor follow a weak 1/1/2/2/3/4/5/6 strength/defense progression.
Broken: Swords/Armor strength is set to 1/1/1/1/1/1/1/1 strength/defense progression.

options.label: Gem/Exp Pool
options.description:
Modifies the Gem/Exp rewards in the item pool.
Vanilla: The same Gem/Exp values as the vanilla game.
Improved: Gem rewards in the item pool are multiplied by 2, and Exp rewards by 10.
Random Range: Gem rewards in the pool are randomized in the range of 1-999, and Exp rewards in the range of 1-9999.

options.label: Randomize Lair Enemies
options.description: Randomize enemies spawned from lairs.

options.label: Randomize Lair Type
options.description: Randomize how lairs spawn enemies (multi-spawn, one-by-one, proximity, etc).

options.label: Randomize Lair Number of Enemies
options.description: Randomize number of enemies spawned from lairs.

options.label: Randomize Lair Spawn Rate
options.description: Randomize how fast enemies are spawned from lairs.

options.label: Randomize Pre-Spawned Enemies
options.description:
Randomize pre-spawned enemies which are already on the map.
**Not currently implemented!**

options.label: Plandomized Locations
options.description: Compatibility-only field for importing upstream settings/presets.

options.label: Logic Rules
options.description:
Set the logic used for the generator.
Glitchless: Normal gameplay. Can enable more difficult logical paths using the Logic Tricks option.
Advanced: Many powerful glitches expected, such as bomb hovering and clipping.
No Logic: No logic is used when placing items. Not recommended for most players.

options.label: Nighttime Skulltulas Expect Sun's Song
options.description: When enabled, nighttime skulltulas logically require Sun's Song.

options.label: Logic Tricks
options.description:
Set various tricks for logic in Ocarina of Time.
Format as a comma-separated list of "nice" names: ["Fewer Tunic Requirements", "Hidden Grottos without Stone of Agony"].

options.label: Advanced Allowed Tricks
options.description:
When Logic Rules is set to Advanced, choose which glitch and advanced tricks are in logic.
Format as a comma-separated list of "nice" names:
["(Glitch) Infinite Sword Glitch (ISG)", "(Glitch) Hovering with Explosives"].

options.label: Forest
options.description:
Set the state of Kokiri Forest and the path to Deku Tree.
Open: Neither the forest exit nor the path to Deku Tree is blocked.
Closed Deku: The forest exit is not blocked; the path to Deku Tree requires Kokiri Sword and Deku Shield.
Closed: Path to Deku Tree requires sword and shield. The forest exit is blocked until Deku Tree is beaten.
Closed forest will force child start, and becomes Closed Deku if interior entrances, overworld entrances, warp songs, or random spawn positions are enabled.

options.label: Kakariko Gate
options.description:
Set the state of the Kakariko Village gate for child. The gate is always open as adult.
Open: The gate starts open. Happy Mask Shop opens upon receiving Zelda's Letter.
Zelda: The gate and Mask Shop open upon receiving Zelda's Letter, without needing to show it to the guard.
Closed: Vanilla behavior; the gate and Mask Shop open upon showing Zelda's Letter to the gate guard.

options.label: Door of Time
options.description:
Set how the Door of Time is opened.
Open: The Door of Time starts opened.
Song of Time: Requires Song of Time.
OoT + Song of Time: Requires Song of Time and level 2 Ocarina progression.
3 Stones: Requires all 3 Spiritual Stones.
3 Stones + Song of Time: Requires Stones and Song of Time.
3 Stones + OoT + SoT: Requires Stones, Song of Time, and level 2 Ocarina progression.

options.label: Zora's Fountain
options.description:
Set the state of King Zora, blocking the way to Zora's Fountain.
Open: King Zora starts moved as both ages. Ruto's Letter is removed.
Adult: King Zora must be moved as child, but is always moved for adult.
Closed: Vanilla behavior; King Zora must be shown Ruto's Letter as child to move him as both ages.

options.label: Gerudo Fortress
options.description:
Set the requirements for access to Gerudo Fortress.
Normal: Vanilla behavior; all four carpenters must be rescued.
Fast: Only one carpenter must be rescued, which is the one in the bottom-left of the fortress.
Open: The Gerudo Valley bridge starts repaired. Gerudo Membership Card is given to start if not shuffled.

options.label: Rainbow Bridge Requirement
options.description:
Set the requirements for the Rainbow Bridge.
Open: The bridge is always present.
Vanilla: Bridge requires Shadow Medallion, Spirit Medallion, and Light Arrows.
Stones: Bridge requires a configurable amount of Spiritual Stones.
Medallions: Bridge requires a configurable amount of medallions.
Dungeons: Bridge requires a configurable amount of rewards (stones + medallions).
Tokens: Bridge requires a configurable amount of gold skulltula tokens.
Hearts: Bridge requires a configurable amount of hearts.

options.label: Ganon's Trials Count
options.description: Set the number of required trials in Ganon's Castle.

options.label: Starting Age
options.description: Choose which age Link will start as.

options.label: Shuffle Interior Entrances
options.description:
Shuffles interior entrances.
Simple: Houses and Great Fairies are shuffled.
All: In addition to Simple, includes Windmill, Link's House, Temple of Time, and the Kakariko potion shop.

options.label: Shuffle Grotto/Grave Entrances
options.description: Shuffles grotto and grave entrances.

options.label: Shuffle Dungeon Entrances
options.description:
Shuffles dungeon entrances. When enabled, both ages will have access to Fire Temple, Bottom of the Well, and Deku Tree.
Simple: Shuffle dungeon entrances except for Ganon's Castle.
All: Include Ganon's Castle as well.

options.label: Shuffle Overworld Entrances
options.description: Shuffles overworld loading zones.

options.label: Randomize Owl Drops
options.description: Randomizes owl drops from Lake Hylia or Death Mountain Trail as child.

options.label: Randomize Warp Songs
options.description: Randomizes warp song destinations.

options.label: Randomize Spawn Positions
options.description: Randomizes the starting position on loading a save. Consistent between savewarps.

options.label: Shuffle Boss Entrances
options.description:
Shuffles boss entrances.
Limited: Bosses will be limited to the ages that typically fight them.
Full: Bosses may be fought as different ages than usual. Child can defeat Phantom Ganon and Bongo Bongo.

options.label: Shuffle Ganon's Tower Entrance
options.description: Shuffle the entrance from Ganon's Castle Main to Ganon's Tower into the boss entrance pool.

options.label: Triforce Hunt
options.description: Gather pieces of the Triforce scattered around the world to complete the game.

options.label: Required Triforce Pieces
options.description: Number of Triforce pieces required to complete the game.

options.label: Percentage of Extra Triforce Pieces
options.description:
Percentage of additional Triforce pieces in the pool. With high numbers, you may need to randomize additional
locations to have enough items.

options.label: Add Bombchu Bag and Drops
options.description:
The first Bombchu pack found becomes a Bombchu Bag, giving the same amount of bombchus
as the original pack (e.g., finding Bombchus (5) first gives Bombchu Bag with 5 bombchus).

After finding the bag, bombchu refills drop from grass, pots, crates, and enemies.
Bombchus can be purchased from shops for 60/99/180 rupees.
Bombchus open Bombchu Bowling.

options.label: Dungeon Boss Shortcuts Mode
options.description:
Shortcuts to dungeon bosses are available without any requirements.
If enabled, this will impact the logic of dungeons where shortcuts are available.
Choice: Use the option "dungeon_shortcuts_list" to choose shortcuts.

options.label: Shortcut Dungeons
options.description: Chosen dungeons to have shortcuts.

options.label: MQ Dungeon Mode
options.description:
Choose between vanilla and Master Quest dungeon layouts.
Vanilla: All layouts are vanilla.
MQ: All layouts are Master Quest.
Specific: Use the option "mq_dungeons_list" to choose which dungeons are MQ.
Count: Use the option "mq_dungeons_count" to choose a number of random dungeons as MQ.

options.label: MQ Dungeon List
options.description: With MQ dungeons as Specific: chosen dungeons to be MQ layout.

options.label: MQ Dungeon Count
options.description: With MQ dungeons as Count: number of randomly-selected dungeons to be MQ layout.

options.label: Pre-completed Dungeons Mode
options.description:
Choose dungeons that are pre-completed. Pre-completed dungeons are filled with non-progression items.
Specific Rewards: choose rewards whose source or shuffled boss dungeon should be pre-completed.

options.label: Pre-completed Dungeon List
options.description: With pre-completed dungeons as Specific: chosen dungeons to be pre-completed.

options.label: Pre-completed Dungeon Rewards
options.description: With pre-completed dungeons as Specific Rewards: chosen rewards whose dungeons are pre-completed.

options.label: Pre-completed Dungeon Count
options.description: With pre-completed dungeons as Count: number of randomly-selected dungeons to be pre-completed.

options.label: Spiritual Stones Required for Bridge
options.description: With Stones bridge: set the number of Spiritual Stones required.

options.label: Medallions Required for Bridge
options.description: With Medallions bridge: set the number of medallions required.

options.label: Dungeon Rewards Required for Bridge
options.description: With Dungeons bridge: set the number of dungeon rewards required.

options.label: Tokens Required for Bridge
options.description: With Tokens bridge: set the number of Gold Skulltula Tokens required.

options.label: Hearts Required for Bridge
options.description: With Hearts bridge: set the number of hearts required.

options.label: Shuffle Dungeon Rewards
options.description:
Control where Medallions and Spiritual Stones can be placed.
Vanilla: Rewards appear at their vanilla locations (blue warps in their respective dungeons).
Reward: Rewards are shuffled among all nine blue-warp reward locations.
Dungeon: Each reward is shuffled within its own dungeon.
Regional: Rewards are shuffled within their region.
Overworld: Rewards are shuffled into overworld locations only.
Any Dungeon: Rewards are shuffled into any dungeon location.
Anywhere: Rewards are shuffled into any location in the pool.

options.label: Maps
options.description:
Control where to shuffle dungeon maps.
Remove: There will be no maps in the itempool.
Startwith: You start with all maps.
Vanilla: Maps remain vanilla.
Dungeon: Maps are shuffled within their original dungeon.
Regional: Maps are shuffled only in regions near the original dungeon.
Overworld: Maps are shuffled locally outside of dungeons.
Any Dungeon: Maps are shuffled locally in any dungeon.
Keysanity: Maps can be anywhere in the multiworld.

options.label: Compasses
options.description:
Control where to shuffle dungeon compasses.
Remove: There will be no compasses in the itempool.
Startwith: You start with all compasses.
Vanilla: Compasses remain vanilla.
Dungeon: Compasses are shuffled within their original dungeon.
Regional: Compasses are shuffled only in regions near the original dungeon.
Overworld: Compasses are shuffled locally outside of dungeons.
Any Dungeon: Compasses are shuffled locally in any dungeon.
Keysanity: Compasses can be anywhere in the multiworld.

options.label: Small Keys
options.description:
Control where to shuffle dungeon small keys.
Remove/"Keysy": There will be no small keys in the itempool. All small key doors are automatically unlocked.
Vanilla: Small keys remain vanilla. You may start with extra small keys in some dungeons to prevent softlocks.
Dungeon: Small keys are shuffled within their original dungeon.
Regional: Small keys are shuffled only in regions near the original dungeon.
Overworld: Small keys are shuffled locally outside of dungeons.
Any Dungeon: Small keys are shuffled locally in any dungeon.
Keysanity: Small keys can be anywhere in the multiworld.

options.label: Thieves' Hideout Keys
options.description:
Control where to shuffle the Thieves' Hideout small keys.
Vanilla: Hideout keys remain vanilla.
Regional: Hideout keys are shuffled only in the Gerudo Valley/Desert Colossus area.
Overworld: Hideout keys are shuffled locally outside of dungeons.
Any Dungeon: Hideout keys are shuffled locally in any dungeon.
Keysanity: Hideout keys can be anywhere in the multiworld.

options.label: Boss Keys
options.description:
Control where to shuffle boss keys, except the Ganon's Castle Boss Key.
Remove/"Keysy": There will be no boss keys in the itempool. All boss key doors are automatically unlocked.
Vanilla: Boss keys remain vanilla. You may start with extra small keys in some dungeons to prevent softlocks.
Dungeon: Boss keys are shuffled within their original dungeon.
Regional: Boss keys are shuffled only in regions near the original dungeon.
Overworld: Boss keys are shuffled locally outside of dungeons.
Any Dungeon: Boss keys are shuffled locally in any dungeon.
Keysanity: Boss keys can be anywhere in the multiworld.

options.label: Maps and Compasses Give Information
options.description:
Gives maps/compasses extra functionality.
map_mq: Map tells if a dungeon is vanilla or MQ.
map_dungeon_location: Map tells where a dungeon entrance leads.
compass_boss_location: Compass tells which boss is in the dungeon.
compass_reward: Compass tells what dungeon reward is in the dungeon.

options.label: Ganon's Boss Key
options.description:
Control how to shuffle the Ganon's Castle Boss Key (GCBK).
Remove: GCBK is removed, and the boss key door is automatically unlocked.
Vanilla: GCBK remains vanilla.
Dungeon: GCBK is shuffled within its original dungeon.
Regional: GCBK is shuffled only in Hyrule Field, Market, and Hyrule Castle areas.
Overworld: GCBK is shuffled locally outside of dungeons.
Any Dungeon: GCBK is shuffled locally in any dungeon.
Keysanity: GCBK can be anywhere in the multiworld.
On LACS: GCBK is on the Light Arrow Cutscene, which requires Shadow and Spirit Medallions.
Stones: GCBK will be awarded when reaching the target number of Spiritual Stones.
Medallions: GCBK will be awarded when reaching the target number of medallions.
Dungeons: GCBK will be awarded when reaching the target number of dungeon rewards.
Tokens: GCBK will be awarded when reaching the target number of Gold Skulltula Tokens.
Hearts: GCBK will be awarded when reaching the target number of hearts.

options.label: Medallions Required for Ganon's BK
options.description: With medallions GCBK: set how many medallions are required to receive GCBK.

options.label: Spiritual Stones Required for Ganon's BK
options.description: With stones GCBK: set how many Spiritual Stones are required to receive GCBK.

options.label: Dungeon Rewards Required for Ganon's BK
options.description: With dungeons GCBK: set how many dungeon rewards are required to receive GCBK.

options.label: Tokens Required for Ganon's BK
options.description: With tokens GCBK: set how many Gold Skulltula Tokens are required to receive GCBK.

options.label: Hearts Required for Ganon's BK
options.description: With hearts GCBK: set how many hearts are required to receive GCBK.

options.label: Key Rings Mode
options.description:
A key ring grants all dungeon small keys at once, rather than individually.
Choice: Use the option "key_rings_list" to choose which dungeons have key rings.
All: All dungeons have key rings instead of small keys.

options.label: Key Ring Areas
options.description: With key rings as Choice: select areas with key rings rather than individual small keys.

options.label: Silver Rupee Pouches Mode
options.description:
Silver rupee pouches grant all silver rupees for a selected puzzle at once.
Choice: Use the option "silver_rupee_pouches" to choose which puzzles use pouches.
All: All active silver rupee puzzles use pouches.

options.label: Silver Rupee Pouches
options.description: With silver rupee pouches as Choice: select puzzles that use pouches rather than individual silver rupees.
validKeys: Spirit Temple Lobby and Lower Adult

options.label: Shuffle Songs
options.description:
Set where songs can appear.
Song: Songs are shuffled into other song locations.
Dungeon: Songs are placed into end-of-dungeon locations:
- The 8 boss heart containers
- Sheik in Ice Cavern
- Lens of Truth chest in Bottom of the Well
- Ice Arrows chest in Gerudo Training Ground
- Impa at Hyrule Castle
Any: Songs can appear anywhere in the multiworld.

options.label: Randomize Ocarina Melodies
options.description:
Randomize ocarina melody assignments.
frog: Randomize the six standard songs.
warp: Randomize the six warp songs.
frogs2: Randomize the Zora's River Frogs Ocarina Game melody.

Backward compatibility:
all -> {'frog', 'warp'}

options.label: Shopsanity
options.description:
Randomizes shop contents.
Off: Shops are not randomized at all.
Fixed Number: Shop contents are shuffled, and a specific number of multiworld locations exist in each shop, controlled by the "shop_slots" option.
Random Number: Same as Fixed Number, but the number of locations per shop is random and may differ between shops.

options.label: Shuffled Shop Slots
options.description: With Shopsanity fixed number: quantity of multiworld locations per shop to be randomized.

options.label: Special Deal Prices
options.description:
Controls how prices are selected for shuffled shop special deal slots.
Vanilla: Use the vanilla price tied to each shop slot.
Betavariate: Weighted distribution across the min/max range.
Uniform: Uniform distribution across the min/max range.

options.label: Minimum Special Deal Price
options.description: Minimum rupee price for shuffled shop special deal slots.

options.label: Maximum Special Deal Price
options.description: Maximum rupee price for shuffled shop special deal slots.

options.label: Tokensanity
options.description:
Token rewards from Gold Skulltulas can be shuffled into the pool.
Dungeons: Only skulltulas in dungeons are shuffled.
Overworld: Only skulltulas on the overworld (all skulltulas not in dungeons) are shuffled.
All: Every skulltula is shuffled.

options.label: Scrub Shuffle
options.description:
Shuffle the items sold by Business Scrubs, and set the prices.
Off: Only the three business scrubs that sell one-time upgrades in vanilla will have items at their vanilla prices.
Low/"Affordable": All scrub prices are 10 rupees.
Regular/"Expensive": All scrub prices are vanilla.
Random Prices: All scrub prices are randomized between 0 and 99 rupees.

options.label: Shuffle Child Trade Item
options.description:
Select the child trade sequence items to shuffle.
To skip Child Zelda, start with Zelda's Letter and do not shuffle Zelda's Letter.

options.label: Shuffle Rupees & Hearts
options.description:
Shuffles freestanding rupees, recovery hearts, Shadow Temple Spinning Pots, and Goron Pot drops.
Dungeons: Only freestanding items in dungeons are shuffled.
Overworld: Only freestanding items in the overworld are shuffled.
All: All freestanding items are shuffled.

options.label: Shuffle Pots
options.description:
Shuffles pots and flying pots which normally contain an item.
Dungeons: Only pots in dungeons are shuffled.
Overworld: Only pots in the overworld are shuffled.
All: All pots are shuffled.

options.label: Include Empty Pots
options.description: Includes empty pots when pot shuffle is enabled.

options.label: Shuffle Crates
options.description:
Shuffles large and small crates containing an item.
Dungeons: Only crates in dungeons are shuffled.
Overworld: Only crates in the overworld are shuffled.
All: All crates are shuffled.

options.label: Include Empty Crates
options.description: Includes empty crates when crate shuffle is enabled.

options.label: Shuffle Cows
options.description: Cows give items when Epona's Song is played.

options.label: Shuffle Beehives
options.description: Beehives drop an item when destroyed by an explosion, the Hookshot, or the Boomerang.

options.label: Shuffle Wonderitems
options.description: Shuffles Wonderitems into the item pool.

options.label: Shuffle Kokiri Sword
options.description: Shuffle Kokiri Sword into the item pool.

options.label: Shuffle Ocarinas
options.description: Shuffle the Fairy Ocarina and Ocarina of Time into the item pool.

options.label: Shuffle Gerudo Card
options.description: Shuffle the Gerudo Membership Card into the item pool.

options.label: Shuffle Magic Beans
options.description: Adds a pack of 10 beans to the item pool and changes the bean salesman to sell one item for 60 rupees.

options.label: Shuffle Expensive Merchants
options.description: Shuffle the items sold by Medigoron, Granny's Potion Shop, and the Haunted Wasteland Carpet Salesman.

options.label: Shuffle Frog Song Rupees
options.description: Shuffles the purple rupees received from the Zora's River frogs.

options.label: Shuffle 100 Skulltula Rupee Reward
options.description: Shuffle the repeatable 200-rupee reward for collecting all 100 Gold Skulltulas.

options.label: Shuffle Silver Rupees
options.description:
Shuffles the Silver Rupee puzzles into the item pool.
Remove: Silver rupees are removed and puzzles are pre-solved.
Vanilla: Silver rupees remain in their vanilla locations.
Dungeon: Silver rupees are shuffled within their own dungeon.
Overworld: Silver rupees are shuffled to overworld locations only.
Any Dungeon: Silver rupees are shuffled across any dungeon.
Regional: Silver rupees are shuffled within their region.
Anywhere: Silver rupees can be anywhere in the multiworld.

options.label: Shuffle TCG Keys
options.description:
Shuffle Treasure Chest Game keys outside the minigame.
Vanilla: Keys remain in the Treasure Chest Game.
Shuffle: Keys are shuffled into the item pool.
Remove: Keys are removed and chests are unlocked.

options.label: Shuffle Individual Ocarina Notes
options.description:
Locks all Ocarina inputs and adds 5 new items (A, C-up, C-down, C-left, C-right)
that each unlock one of the 5 Ocarina notes.

options.label: TCG Requires Lens of Truth
options.description: Treasure Chest Game requires Lens of Truth to see which chests contain keys.

options.label: Shuffle Hyrule Loach Reward
options.description:
Shuffle the Hyrule Loach reward from the Fishing Pond.
Vanilla Behavior keeps the original loach spawn and sinking lure rules.
Easier Behavior always spawns the loach, makes the sinking lure available
immediately, and allows the normal fishing prizes to be won with it.

options.label: Shuffle Hideout Entrances
options.description: Shuffles the 4 interior entrances to different rooms within Gerudo Fortress.

options.label: Shuffle Gerudo Fortress Heart Piece
options.description:
Controls the child-only Heart Piece in Gerudo Fortress when Thieves' Hideout entrances are shuffled.
Remove: exclude it. Vanilla: leave it in place. Shuffle: add it to the item pool.

options.label: Shuffle Gerudo Valley River Exit
options.description: Shuffles the river exit from Gerudo Valley that drops you at Lake Hylia.

options.label: Key Rings Give Boss Keys
options.description: When enabled, obtaining a key ring also grants the corresponding boss key.

options.label: Skip Tower Escape Sequence
options.description: Skips the tower collapse sequence between the Ganondorf and Ganon fights.

options.label: Skip Child Stealth
options.description: The crawlspace into Hyrule Castle skips straight to Zelda.

options.label: Skip Epona Race
options.description: Epona can always be summoned with Epona's Song.

options.label: Skip Some Minigame Phases
options.description: Dampe Race and Horseback Archery give both rewards if the second condition is met on the first attempt.

options.label: Complete Mask Quest
options.description: All masks are immediately available to borrow from the Happy Mask Shop.

options.label: Enable Useful Cutscenes
options.description:
Reenables the Poe cutscene in Forest Temple, Darunia in Fire Temple, and Twinrova introduction. Mostly useful for
advanced logic.

options.label: Fast Chest Cutscenes
options.description: All chest animations are fast. If disabled, major items have a slow animation.

options.label: Scarecrow Song
options.description:
Set scarecrow song behavior.
Vanilla: Standard game behavior.
Fast: Shared scarecrow song behavior is simplified.
Free: Pierre can be summoned without setting the song.

options.label: Fast Bunny Hood
options.description: Bunny Hood lets you move 1.5x faster like in Majora's Mask.

options.label: Plant Magic Beans
options.description: Pre-plants all 10 magic beans in the soft soil spots.

options.label: Easier Fire Arrow Entry
options.description: Allow reducing the number of lit torches required to open Shadow Temple with Fire Arrows.

options.label: Cucco Count
options.description: Controls the number of Cuccos for Anju to give an item as child.

options.label: Big Poe Count
options.description: Number of Big Poes required for the Poe Collector's item.

options.label: Fire Arrow Entry Torch Count
options.description:
Number of lit torches required to open Shadow Temple.
Does not affect logic; use the trick Shadow Temple Entry with Fire Arrows if desired.

options.label: Fast Shadow Temple Boat
options.description: Speed up the boat ride in the Shadow Temple.

options.label: Free Reward from Rauru
options.description:
Control whether the item Rauru gives beyond the Door of Time is given as a starting item.
Not Free: Rauru gives the reward when you go beyond the Door of Time.
Free: You begin the game with the reward Rauru normally gives. If dungeon rewards are shuffled
elsewhere, the Rauru reward is shuffled along with them.
Free Forced: You begin the game with the reward Rauru normally gives, and the ToT Reward
location is forced to contain a dungeon reward even when rewards are shuffled to other pools.

options.label: Chest Appearance Matches Contents
options.description:
Changes chest textures and/or sizes to match their contents.
Off: All chests have their vanilla size/appearance.
Textures: Chest textures reflect their contents.
Both: Like Textures, but progression items and boss keys get big chests, and other items get small chests.
Classic: Old behavior of CSMC; textures distinguish keys from non-keys, and size distinguishes importance.

options.label: Chest Textures
options.description:
Select which contents use special textures when chest appearance is set to Textures or Both.
major: Major items and Archipelago progression items use gilded chests.
bosskeys: Boss keys use boss-key chests.
keys: Small keys use key chests.
tokens: Gold Skulltula tokens use spider-web chests.
hearts: Heart items use heart chests.
ap_filler: Archipelago filler items use tinted filler chests.

options.label: Stone of Agony Unlocks Chest Textures
options.description: Textures for chests will only be correct when Stone of Agony is found.

options.label: Minor Items in Big/Gold Chests
options.description:
Minor items appear in big/gold chests.
bombchus: Bombchus appear in big/gold chests.
shields: Hylian Shield and Deku Shield appear in big/gold chests.
capacity: Deku Stick and Deku Nut capacity upgrades appear in big/gold chests.

options.label: Invisible Chests
options.description: Chests visible only with Lens of Truth. Logic is not changed.

options.label: Pot, Crate, and Beehive Appearance
options.description:
Changes the appearance of pots, crates, and beehives that contain items.
Off: Vanilla appearance for all containers.
Textures (Content): Unchecked pots and crates have a texture reflecting their contents. Unchecked beehives with progression items will wiggle.
Textures (Unchecked): Unchecked pots and crates are golden. Unchecked beehives will wiggle.

options.label: Pot and Crate Textures
options.description:
Select which contents use special textures when pot and crate appearance is set to Textures (Content).
major: Major items use golden pots/crates.
bosskeys: Boss keys use boss-key pots/crates.
keys: Small keys use key pots/crates.
tokens: Gold Skulltula tokens use spider-web pots/crates.
hearts: Heart items use heart pots/crates.

options.label: Stone of Agony Unlocks Pot and Crate Textures
options.description: Textures for pots and crates will only be correct when Stone of Agony is found.

options.label: Key Appearance Matches Dungeon
options.description: Small key models match their dungeon. Requires keysanity or key ring shuffle.

options.label: Ruto Already at F1
options.description: Ruto starts at the first switch in Jabu instead of needing to be carried.

options.label: Maintain Mask Equips
options.description: Equipped masks stay equipped when using ocarina or picking up items.

options.label: Gossip Stones
options.description:
Gossip Stones can give hints about item locations.
None: Gossip Stones do not give hints.
Mask: Gossip Stones give hints with Mask of Truth.
Agony: Gossip Stones give hints wtih Stone of Agony.
Always: Gossip Stones always give hints.

options.label: Misc Hints
options.description:
Choose which miscellaneous hints are enabled.

Temple of Time Altar hints dungeon rewards, bridge info, and Ganon BK info.
Ganondorf hints the Light Arrows.
Dampe's Diary hints a local Hookshot if one exists.
Skulltula House locations hint their item at various token counts.
Frogs Ocarina Game hints the final reward.

options.label: Hint Distribution
options.description:
Choose the hint distribution to use. Affects the frequency of strong hints, which items are always hinted, etc.
Detailed documentation on hint distributions can be found on OoTRandomizer.com.
The Async hint distribution is intended for async multiworlds. It removes Way of the Hero hints to improve generation times, since they are not very useful in asyncs.

options.label: Text Shuffle
options.description:
Randomizes text in the game for comedic effect.
Except Hints: does not randomize important text such as hints, small/boss key information, and item prices.
Complete: randomizes every textbox, including the useful ones.

options.label: Damage Multiplier
options.description: Controls the amount of damage Link takes.

options.label: Bonks Do Damage
options.description: Bonking on a wall or object will hurt Link. "Normal" is a half heart of damage.

options.label: Hero Mode
options.description: Hearts will not drop from enemies or objects.

options.label: Starting Time of Day
options.description:
Change the starting time of day.
Daytime starts at Sunrise and ends at Sunset. Default is between Morning and Noon.

options.label: Blue Fire Arrows
options.description: Ice arrows can melt red ice and break the mud walls in Dodongo's Cavern.

options.label: Fix Broken Drops
options.description: Fixes two broken vanilla drops: deku shield in child Spirit Temple, and magic drop on GTG eye statue.

options.label: Start with Consumables
options.description: Start the game with full Deku Sticks and Deku Nuts.

options.label: Start with Rupees
options.description: Start with a full wallet. Wallet upgrades will also fill your wallet.

options.label: Starting Hearts
options.description: Start the game with the selected number of hearts.

options.label: Item Pool
options.description:
Changes the number of items available in the game.
Plentiful: One extra copy of every major item.
Balanced: Original item pool.
Scarce: Extra copies of major items are removed. Heart containers are removed.
Minimal: All major item upgrades not used for locations are removed. All health is removed.

options.label: Ice Traps
options.description:
Adds ice traps to the item pool.
Off: All ice traps are removed.
Normal: The vanilla quantity of ice traps are placed.
On/"Extra": There is a chance for some extra ice traps to be placed.
Mayhem: All added junk items are ice traps.
Onslaught: All junk items are replaced by ice traps, even those in the base pool.

options.label: Custom Ice Trap Percent
options.description: Percentage of junk items replaced by ice traps when Ice Traps is set to Custom (%).

options.label: Custom Ice Trap Count
options.description: Number of junk items replaced by ice traps when Ice Traps is set to Custom (count).

options.label: Trap Appearance
options.description: Changes the appearance of traps, including other games' traps, as freestanding items.

options.label: Additional Random Starting Items
options.description: Add random progression-safe starting items to start inventory.

options.label: Amount of Random Starting Items
options.description: How many additional random starting items to grant.

options.label: Exclude From Random Starting Items
options.description: Exclude item categories from random starting item selection.

options.label: Shuffle All Selected Adult Trade Items
options.description: Shuffle every selected adult trade sequence item into the item pool.

options.label: Shuffle Adult Trade Sequence Items
options.description:
Select the adult trade sequence items to shuffle.
If Shuffle All Selected Adult Trade Items is off, one selected item starts the adult trade sequence.
If Shuffle All Selected Adult Trade Items is on, every selected item is shuffled.

options.label: Default Targeting Option
options.description: Default targeting option.

options.label: Display D-Pad HUD
options.description:
Show dpad icon on HUD for quick actions (ocarina, hover boots, iron boots, mask).
On: D-Pad shown on the right side (default).
Left: D-Pad shown on the left side.
Off: D-Pad hidden.

options.label: Display D-Pad Dungeon Info
options.description: Show separated menus on the pause screen for dungeon keys, rewards, and Vanilla/MQ info.

options.label: Speed Up Music for Last Triforce Piece
options.description: In Triforce Hunt, speed up the music slightly when one piece away from the goal.

options.label: Slowdown Music When Low HP
options.description: Slow down the background music when at critically low health.

options.label: Uninvert Y-Axis in First Person Camera
options.description: Uninvert the Y-axis when in first-person camera mode (e.g. arrow aiming).

options.label: Input Viewer
options.description: Show a controller input display on screen.

options.label: Disable Battle Music
options.description: Prevent background music from being interrupted by the battle theme when near enemies.

options.label: Display Custom Song Names
options.description: When music is randomized, display the custom track name on screen.

options.label: Credits Music as BGM
options.description: Include the credits roll sequences in the background music shuffle pool.

options.label: Item Model Colors Match Cosmetics
options.description: Makes in-game models match their HUD element colors.

options.label: Background Music
options.description: Randomize or disable background music.

options.label: Fanfares
options.description: Randomize or disable item fanfares.

options.label: Ocarina Songs as Fanfares
options.description: Enable ocarina songs as fanfares. These are longer than usual fanfares. Does nothing without fanfares randomized.

options.label: Kokiri Tunic
options.description: Choose a color. "random_choice" selects a random option. "completely_random" generates a random hex code.

options.label: Goron Tunic
options.description: Choose a color. "random_choice" selects a random option. "completely_random" generates a random hex code.

options.label: Zora Tunic
options.description: Choose a color. "random_choice" selects a random option. "completely_random" generates a random hex code.

options.label: Silver Gauntlets Color
options.description: Choose a color. "random_choice" selects a random option. "completely_random" generates a random hex code.

options.label: Golden Gauntlets Color
options.description: Choose a color. "random_choice" selects a random option. "completely_random" generates a random hex code.

options.label: Mirror Shield Frame Color
options.description: Choose a color. "random_choice" selects a random option. "completely_random" generates a random hex code.

options.label: Navi Idle Inner
options.description: Choose a color. "random_choice" selects a random option. "completely_random" generates a random hex code.

options.label: Navi Idle Outer
options.description:
Choose a color. "random_choice" selects a random option. "completely_random" generates a random hex code.
"match_inner" copies the inner color for this option.

options.label: Navi Targeting Enemy Inner
options.description: Choose a color. "random_choice" selects a random option. "completely_random" generates a random hex code.

options.label: Navi Targeting Enemy Outer
options.description:
Choose a color. "random_choice" selects a random option. "completely_random" generates a random hex code.
"match_inner" copies the inner color for this option.

options.label: Navi Targeting NPC Inner
options.description: Choose a color. "random_choice" selects a random option. "completely_random" generates a random hex code.

options.label: Navi Targeting NPC Outer
options.description:
Choose a color. "random_choice" selects a random option. "completely_random" generates a random hex code.
"match_inner" copies the inner color for this option.

options.label: Navi Targeting Prop Inner
options.description: Choose a color. "random_choice" selects a random option. "completely_random" generates a random hex code.

options.label: Navi Targeting Prop Outer
options.description:
Choose a color. "random_choice" selects a random option. "completely_random" generates a random hex code.
"match_inner" copies the inner color for this option.

options.label: Sword Trail Duration
options.description: Set the duration for sword trails.

options.label: Sword Trail Inner
options.description: Choose a color. "random_choice" selects a random option. "completely_random" generates a random hex code.

options.label: Sword Trail Outer
options.description:
Choose a color. "random_choice" selects a random option. "completely_random" generates a random hex code.
"match_inner" copies the inner color for this option.

options.label: Bombchu Trail Inner
options.description: Choose a color. "random_choice" selects a random option. "completely_random" generates a random hex code.

options.label: Bombchu Trail Outer
options.description:
Choose a color. "random_choice" selects a random option. "completely_random" generates a random hex code.
"match_inner" copies the inner color for this option.

options.label: Boomerang Trail Inner
options.description: Choose a color. "random_choice" selects a random option. "completely_random" generates a random hex code.

options.label: Boomerang Trail Outer
options.description:
Choose a color. "random_choice" selects a random option. "completely_random" generates a random hex code.
"match_inner" copies the inner color for this option.

options.label: Heart Color
options.description: Choose a color. "random_choice" selects a random option. "completely_random" generates a random hex code.

options.label: Magic Color
options.description: Choose a color. "random_choice" selects a random option. "completely_random" generates a random hex code.

options.label: A Button Color
options.description: Choose a color. "random_choice" selects a random option. "completely_random" generates a random hex code.

options.label: B Button Color
options.description: Choose a color. "random_choice" selects a random option. "completely_random" generates a random hex code.

options.label: C Button Color
options.description: Choose a color. "random_choice" selects a random option. "completely_random" generates a random hex code.

options.label: Start Button Color
options.description: Choose a color. "random_choice" selects a random option. "completely_random" generates a random hex code.

options.label: Randomize All Sound Effects
options.description: Randomize all sound effects and music settings, except Link voices.

options.label: Navi Overworld
options.description:
Choose a sound effect. "random_choice" selects a random option. "random_ear_safe" selects a random safe option.
"completely_random" selects any random sound.

options.label: Navi Enemy
options.description:
Choose a sound effect. "random_choice" selects a random option. "random_ear_safe" selects a random safe option.
"completely_random" selects any random sound.

options.label: Low HP
options.description:
Choose a sound effect. "random_choice" selects a random option. "random_ear_safe" selects a random safe option.
"completely_random" selects any random sound.

options.label: Menu Cursor
options.description:
Choose a sound effect. "random_choice" selects a random option. "random_ear_safe" selects a random safe option.
"completely_random" selects any random sound.

options.label: Menu Select
options.description:
Choose a sound effect. "random_choice" selects a random option. "random_ear_safe" selects a random safe option.
"completely_random" selects any random sound.

options.label: Nightfall
options.description:
Choose a sound effect. "random_choice" selects a random option. "random_ear_safe" selects a random safe option.
"completely_random" selects any random sound.

options.label: Horse
options.description:
Choose a sound effect. "random_choice" selects a random option. "random_ear_safe" selects a random safe option.
"completely_random" selects any random sound.

options.label: Hover Boots
options.description:
Choose a sound effect. "random_choice" selects a random option. "random_ear_safe" selects a random safe option.
"completely_random" selects any random sound.

options.label: Daybreak
options.description:
Choose a sound effect. "random_choice" selects a random option. "random_ear_safe" selects a random safe option.
"completely_random" selects any random sound.

options.label: Ocarina Instrument
options.description: Change the sound of the ocarina.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Determines the victory condition.

Ending A: Reach ending A.
Ending B: Reach ending B.

options.label: Starting Skill
options.description: Determines which skill you start with.

options.label: Start With Fast Travel
options.description: Start with Fast Travel instead of shuffling it into the item pool.

options.label: Start With Healing Ward
options.description: Start with Healing Ward instead of shuffling it into the item pool.

options.label: Advanced Logic
options.description: Include Nola, No.7, Reibolg and Incomplete Gear in the logic.

options.label: Central Elevator Fix
options.description:
Determines requirements to fix the Central Stratum elevator.

Vanilla: Same as the original game.
Key: Find a key shuffled into the item pool.
Free: The elevator is already fixed.

options.label: Required Steles
options.description:
Determines the number of steles Lily requires for
'Center 4 - Faintly Glowing Aegis Curio'.

0: Only the Blighted Pupil is required.
1: Vanilla.
2+: Extra steles are required and added to the item pool.

options.label: Progressive Aptitudes
options.description:
Aptitudes are acquired in order.
Dive -> Motley's Torrent
Lars' Grip -> Lars' Swift Flight

options.label: Meta Progression
options.description:
Places progression in locations that were just unlocked, so every one you find
leads directly to the next one.

Enabling this keeps every progression item inside your own world.

options.label: Shuffle Transitions
options.description:
Shuffle area transitions and doors.
Non-door transitions between rooms of the same area are unaffected.

Off: Transitions lead where they should.
Coupled: Returning through a transition will take you from whence you came.
Decoupled: Any transition can take you to any other transition.

options.label: Chapter Scaling
options.description:
Determines how the chapter value moves between Minimum Chapter and Maximum Chapter.

Vanilla: Raises difficulty when you reach specific points.
Progress: Derived from completion, Minimum Chapter at 0% and Maximum Chapter at 100%.

options.label: Minimum Chapter
options.description: Lowest chapter value used to scale the game difficulty.

options.label: Maximum Chapter
options.description: Highest chapter value used to scale the game difficulty.

options.label: NG+ AI
options.description: Enemies use their New Game+ AI.

options.label: Relic Cost Shuffle
options.description: Shuffles the equip cost of relics.

options.label: Skill Cost Shuffle
options.description: Shuffles the materials required to upgrade skills.

options.label: Shuffle Attuner Arts
options.description: Shuffles Attuner Arts for all skills.

options.label: Allow Multiple Skills Per Spirit
options.description:
Removes the one-skill-per-spirit limit.
(Logic doesn't account for this)

options.label: Randomize Enemies
options.description: Replaces the enemies each room spawns with other enemies.

options.label: Randomize Bosses
options.description:
Replaces each boss with another boss (experimental).
(Lars phase 2 and Rooted Primordial Beast are excluded)

None: Bosses will remain in their vanilla locations.
Shuffled: Bosses will be shuffled amongst each other.
Full: Bosses will be randomized.

options.label: Shuffle BGM
options.description: Shuffles the background music tracks.

options.label: Generate Seed File
options.description: Also generate a seed file for non-archipelago play.

options.label: Artifacts Required
options.description:
How many artifacts open the last fight. Winning it is the goal. The game has 7, one per chapter's milestone.

0: the last fight is open from the start, whatever Artifact Shuffle is set to.

With Artifact Shuffle on Vanilla, the 7th artifact is the last fight's own reward, so at most 6 count: asking for
7 lowers it to 6, with a warning.

options.label: Artifact Shuffle
options.description:
Where the artifacts, the goal's items, may be placed. Each chapter's artifact scene is a location.

Vanilla: each artifact at its own scene. This World: anywhere in your game. Anywhere: anywhere in the multiworld,
another player's game included.

options.label: Shuffle Quests
options.description:
Quest rewards are locations: quests from the quest board, and side quests such as helping a lost kid.

Turned off, quests give their usual rewards and aren't part of the seed.

Checks added in this version: {count}.

options.label: Shuffle Crystal Berries
options.description:
Crystal berry spots are locations, and the berries are items. Some are well hidden.

Turned off, crystal berries stay where they are and the crystal berry shop works as usual.

Checks added in this version: {count}.

options.label: Shuffle Discoveries
options.description:
Journal discoveries are locations: recording a discovery (examining a statue, a hidden spot, arriving somewhere
new) sends a check. They give no item of their own. Off by default.

Checks added in this version: {count}.

options.label: Shuffle Hidden Items
options.description:
Items you can't see until you find them, inside grass or a bush, or inside something you hit to make them appear,
are locations: finding one sends a check. Turned off, they stay the game's own. Off by default.

Checks added in this version: {count}.

options.label: Shuffle Dig Spots
options.description:
The mounds Kabbu digs up with Beetle Dig are locations: digging one up sends a check. Turned off, they stay the
game's own. Off by default.

Checks added in this version: {count}.

options.label: Enemysanity
options.description:
Every enemy on the map is a location: winning its fight drops the check as an item to pick up. Every one stays on
its map whatever the story, so none can be missed. Bosses aren't map enemies, so they're not included. Off by
default.

Checks added in this version: {count}.

options.label: Shuffle Medal Shops
options.description:
Medals sold in shops are locations: the shelf shows what's really there, and buying it sends the check.

Turned off, shops sell their own medals as usual.

Checks added in this version: {count}.

options.label: Shuffle Item Shops
options.description:
The first purchase of each item in an item shop is a location: the shelf shows what's really there, and buying it
sends the check. After that, the shop restocks it as often as you like: its own item, or with Shuffle Shop
Inventories on (the default) the one the seed gives that slot.

Turned off, item shops sell their own items as usual (or the seed's, with Shuffle Shop Inventories).

Checks added in this version: {count}.

options.label: Shuffle Termacade
options.description:
The Termacade's prize stand, in Bugaria's commercial district: the first purchase of each prize is a location, and
its prizes (Empower+ and the other medals, the ribbons) are in the item pool. Prize locations only ever hold filler,
so no token farming is ever needed for progress.

Turned off, the stand sells its own prizes as usual.

Checks added in this version: {count}.

options.label: Minigame Prizes
options.description:
The prizes for a high score in a minigame (25 worms in Whack Farms' Wacka Worm game) can hold anything, and the
logic counts on winning them. Turned off, those locations stay but only ever hold filler. Off by default.

Locations it covers in this version: {count}.

options.label: Shop Contents
options.description:
What shop locations may hold, when shops are shuffled. Shops put many easy checks in one place, which can soak up
the important items; this keeps them spread over the world.

Anything: any item, progression included.
No Progression: no item that unlocks something (useful, filler and trap items only); those are out in the world.
Filler Only: small items only. If the whole room has too few small items to fill every shop, this seed's shops use
No Progression instead, and the generator says so.

options.label: Shuffle Shop Inventories
options.description:
What item shops restock and what respawning floor items come back with, shuffled among themselves and fixed by the
seed. It never touches an Archipelago check or location: the first purchase of each item in an item shop (Shuffle
Item Shops) and the first pickup of a respawning floor item are still checks. This only changes what they sell and
give after that, or from the start in a shop that isn't a location.

Only those items take part (food and other consumables): a shop may sell what another shop or a floor item had,
each item is still sold or found as often as before, and no shop sells the same item twice. The price is the
game's own for the item sold. No item, check or rule depends on it. On by default.

Shop slots and floor items in this version: {count}.

options.label: Entrance Randomizer (experimental)
options.description:
EXPERIMENTAL. Doors between areas lead somewhere else, and every room stays reachable. From least to most
scrambled:

Room Swap: the world keeps the game's shape. Whole rooms trade places with rooms of as many doors in their part of
the world (parts joined only by a ride or a scene stay apart), and a room's doors may turn: familiar roads,
unfamiliar rooms. Going back through a door takes you back; one-way doors stay as the game has them.
Map Shuffle: a new web of doors that still reads like a map: a door on a room's right edge leads in through another
room's left edge, up into down, so walking right keeps you going right. Going back through a door takes you back.
Doors whose two sides the game itself doesn't match (a corridor that turns, a ladder) are shuffled among
themselves, and one-way doors too.
Coupled: any door may lead to any other, a new web of doors. Going back through a door always takes you back, so
you can retrace your steps. One-way doors (the fog maze's wrong turns, drops) are shuffled among themselves.
Decoupled: as Coupled, but each way of a door is shuffled on its own: going back through a door can take you
somewhere else. The most chaotic.

The logic follows the doors and what every room needs inside, but a few doors are still to be gone through, so it
stays experimental; the pause menu's Warp gets you out of a dead end. Off by default.

Doors in this version: {count}.

options.label: Enemy Shuffle
options.description:
Changes which enemies you fight at each place, fixed by the seed. Each enemy on each map gets another fight of
the same size: a lone enemy stays a lone enemy, a group of three stays three. The enemy you see walking around
still looks like the original one for now; the fight is the shuffled one.

Off: every fight is the game's own.
Enemies Only: ordinary enemies on maps are shuffled among themselves. Bosses stay where they are.

Bosses (Bosses Only, Both, Chaos) come in a later version. Map fights shuffled in this version: {count}.

options.label: Starting Location (experimental)
options.description:
EXPERIMENTAL. Where a new file begins. Off: where the game begins, outside Bugaria. Anywhere: any room in the game,
even in the middle of a dungeon, arriving as if through one of its doors. The pause menu's Warp takes you back to
it.

The logic starts there: items are placed so the seed can be finished from where you begin. A room a seed can't
begin from (too few checks in reach with what a new file has, or no way out yet) is never picked. Off by default.

Room arrivals to start at in this version: {count}.

options.label: Starting Party Member
options.description:
Off: the story's party (Vi and Kabbu from the start, Leif after the spider in Snakemouth Den).

Vi, Kabbu or Leif: a new file starts with that one member, and the other two are items, found like any other.
Random Member: one of the three, picked by the seed. All Three: a new file starts with the whole party, and no
member is an item. With any of these, the two places where the story adds a member (the opening outside the city,
and the fall room after the spider) become locations, whoever starts.

The logic follows what each room needs. A few places still ask for all three members, more than the game does: a
few spots past the Outskirts gate, the story's own transfers, and the slots of the cranks and keys that aren't
items yet. All Three by default.

options.label: Filler Starting Checks
options.description:
The checks a new file sends by itself when the game begins (Maki and Eetl's gift, the tutorial battle, and the
opening spot where the story's second member joins, when party members are items) hold filler only: no
progression, useful or trap item, so a seed doesn't open with its good items before you've played. Nothing else
changes, the spot in the fall room after the spider included. Turn it off to plando an item there.

With the Entrance Randomizer on Coupled, Map Shuffle or Room Swap it doesn't apply, and the generator says so: the
doors can leave the start with only these spots, too few to begin a seed. On by default.

options.label: Shuffle Field Moves
options.description:
The three field attacks are items too: Vi's Beemerang Toss (the first Progressive Beemerang), Kabbu's Horn Slash and
Leif's Freeze (the first Progressive Freeze). Until one arrives, that attack does nothing but a short "can't" sound,
and each shows in the key items once it does. A move works only with its member in the party too. The abilities the
story teaches later (the Beemerang Halt, Bee Fly, the Dash and Horn Dash, Beetle Dig, the Icicle, the Shield) are
items in every seed. Without the Horn Slash, Kabbu's Dash only moves and the Horn Dash only breaks boulders.

The logic follows what each room needs. A few places still ask for all three moves, more than the game does: a few
spots past the Outskirts gate, the story's own transfers, and the slots of the cranks and keys that aren't items
yet. Off by default.

options.label: Shuffle Jump
options.description:
Jump is an item, for the whole party: until it arrives, the jump button does nothing but a short "can't" sound.
The pause menu's Warp is always there with it on, the way out of a spot you can't jump out of.

The logic is cautious: every check needs Jump except those seen reachable without it, room by room. Off by
default.

options.label: Points of No Return
options.description:
Off: wherever the logic sends you, it leaves you a way to walk back.

On: the logic may send you somewhere only the pause menu's Warp gets you out of (a drop, a one-way door, a
transfer with no way back), so items can land in more places, and you're expected to warp back to the start. The
Warp is always there with it on.

It matters wherever a room has a one-way (a drop, a door that pushes you past a lock): it counts with this on even
where getting back would take what you don't have yet, or isn't in the logic at all. Off by default.

options.label: Progressive Boat
options.description:
The Boat Ticket and the submarine (the Subaquatic Maritime Neotransport) are one progressive item, found twice: the
first copy is the Boat Ticket, the second the submarine, so the submarine always comes after the ticket. Each shows
in your key items under its own name. The submarine's docks are there only once it is yours.

Off: they are two separate items, found in any order. The Boat Ticket takes you to Metal Island on the pier's boat;
the submarine works every dock, Metal Island's included. On by default.

options.label: Extra Roadblocks
options.description:
Obstacles the game puts up later in the story, there from the start instead, each needing its ability to cross,
both ways. Without one, the way it would block stays open all game.

None yet: the Snakemouth Barrier was one until the horn tutorial was seen to move the party past it.

options.label: Music Shuffle
options.description:
Every song plays in place of another, the same way every time the seed is played: an area's music, a battle's, a
boss's. The short jingles (the victory fanfare, the game over, the chapter titles) swap among themselves. The title
screen, the wind, water, machine and breathing sounds, and the factory elevator's music stay as they are. Samira
plays the song you pick. Nothing else changes: no item, check or rule depends on it. Off by default.

options.label: Death Link
options.description:
When your party is defeated in a battle, everyone in the room with DeathLink on is too, and their deaths reach
you. This sets it for the seed when you first connect; the Archipelago panel on the main menu can still switch it
afterwards. A death DeathLink causes is never sent back.

Gates: Similar to Sonic Adventure 2 AP, levels are placed in gates with very configurable requirements to move to the next gate
Vanilla Entrance Randomizer: The world map is unlocked like in vanilla Spark 3
Level Items: You must find levels in the stages in order to progress. Levels are in their vanilla locations
Open World: All levels are unlocked from the start, effectively Gates but with only Gate 0
        - The goal level is the only exception. Progression Options denote the requirements
        - Levels are in their vanilla locations

If you have a suggestion or a question, please ask in the future game design thread

normal: The easiest option, designed for those new to the game
hard: You will need to be observant of the stage layout and know how to best utilize Spark's movement and simple tech
expert: Requires knowledge for hard difficulty as well as less simple speedrun tricks. All tricks are fair game

"Freom Mk-0" contains

Local Early: Guarantees the required combat item is in this game and early sphere
Optional Bosses: You do not need to defeat bosses in order to unlock the next gate
Start: Start with combat, takes it out of the item pool

options.label: Always On Games
options.description:
Choose which games you would like to enable.

The following games have full implementations: Barbuta, Vainger, Night Manor, Divers, and Porgy.
Party House has a more minor implementation, and counts as an implemented game.
There is a host.yaml setting that you must enable to include unimplemented games.
Unimplemented games will only have Garden, Gold, and/or Cherry checks.
The host.yaml setting is not required for the following games due to their short length:
Ninpek, Magic Garden, Velgress, and Waldorf's Journey

options.label: Random Choice Games

The number of games that will be enabled is based on the Random Choice Game Count option.

options.label: Random Choice Game Count

Choose how many Random Choice Games will be included alongside your Always On Games.
If your Random Choice Game Count is larger than the number of games in your Random Choice Games list, all of them will be enabled.

options.label: Starting Game Amount
options.description:
Choose how many games to have unlocked at the start.
At least one of the starting games will always be one of the implemented games, to avoid issues with generation and very early BK.
If this value is higher than the number of games you selected, you will start with all of them unlocked.
If you put a game in your start inventory from pool, it will count towards the amount from this option.

options.label: Goal Games
options.description: Choose which games you may have to complete to achieve your goal.

options.label: Goal Game Amount
options.description:
Choose how many games you need to goal to achieve your goal among your Goal Games.
If this number is less than the number of Goal Games you have selected, it will choose some of them at random to be your Goal Games.
If this number is greater than or equal to your number of Goal Games, then all of your games will be your Goal Games.

options.label: Cherry-Allowed Games
options.description:
Choose which games you want to include the Cherry goal in.
If the game is set as your Goal Game, then you will need to Cherry that game to complete that goal.
If the game is not set as a Goal Game, then Cherrying that game will be a check.
If the game is not selected at all, then this option will not affect it.
The defaults are ones where we believe the Cherry goal is reasonable in the context of a randomizer.

options.label: Porgy - Fuel Difficulty

Required: The Radar System is logically required for all concealed locations.

options.label: Death Link
options.description:
Shares deaths with other Death Link players.
Keep Inventory prevents Death Link deaths from dropping the players inventory.

options.label: Skill XP Multiplier
options.description: Multiplies skill experience gains by 1x - 10x.

options.label: Infinite Merchant Stock
options.description: Restocks currently available merchant offers to their normal maximum.

options.label: Core Rewards
options.description:
AP sent rewards are held by the Core until player pickup.
Access rewards by right-clicking the Core.

options.label: Merchant Sells Crown Summon
options.description: Moves Caveling Bread to the Fishing Merchant and sells the crown summon at the Cloaked Merchant.

options.label: Early Repair and Salvage
options.description: Guarantees the Salvage and Repair Station and first Furnace licenses in local starting spheres when enabled.

options.label: Prevent Progression in Optional Checks
options.description: Prefers progression items outside opt-in optional checks, allowing only required overflow.

options.label: Prevent Progression in Sanity
options.description: Prefers progression items outside opt-in sanity checks, allowing only required overflow.

options.label: Required Artifacts
options.description: Determines the number of Artifacts needed to begin the endgame sequence.

options.label: Final Boss Select
options.description:
Determines the final bosses required to beat the seed. Choose from Meta Ridley, Metroid Prime,
both, or neither.

options.label: Artifact Hints
options.description: If enabled, scanning the artifact stones in the temple will give a hint to their location. Additionally, hints may be pre-collected in the client.

options.label: Missile Launcher
options.description: If enabled, the missile launcher will be added to the item pool. This will only allow you to use missiles once the missile launcher is found (regardless of missile expansions received).

options.label: Main Power Bomb
options.description: If enabled, the main power bomb will be added to the item pool. This will only allow you to use power bombs once the main power bombs is found (regardless of power bomb expansions received).

options.label: Shuffle Scan Visor
options.description: If enabled, the Scan Visor will be shuffled into the item pool and will need to be found in order to scan dash and open certain locks.

options.label: Shuffle Unlimited Missiles
options.description: If enabled, Unlimited Missiles will be shuffled into the item pool. This is similar to Unlimited Missiles found in Metroid Prime 2 Echoes Multiplayer.

options.label: Shuffle Unlimited Power Bombs
options.description: If enabled, the Unlimited Power Bombs will be shuffled into the item pool. This is similar to Unlimited Missiles found in Metroid Prime 2 Echoes Multiplayer, but for Power Bombs.

options.label: Pre Scan Elevators
options.description: Pre scans the elevators in the game, allowing for faster transitions between regions. Makes for more interesting gameplay if disabled when the scan visor is shuffled.

options.label: Elevator Randomization
options.description: Randomizes the elevators between regions.

options.label: Door Color Randomization
options.description:
Determine if/how door colors are randomized.
None: No door colors will be randomized
Global: All door colors of a given color will be randomized to another color
Regional: Each Region will have its door colors randomized to another color

options.label: Blast Shield Randomization
options.description:
Determine if/how blast shields are randomized. Note that this will have a difficult time generating in solo worlds with no tricks enabled.
None: No blast shields will be randomized
Replace Existing: Each existing Missile Blast Shield will be replaced with a different Blast Shield type
Mix It Up: Each Region will remove all existing blast shields and instead add a specified number to new doors

options.label: Blast Shield Frequency
options.description:
If using 'Mix It Up' for blast shield randomization, how many blast shields should be added per region?
These are added using a percentage of total possible placements so exact numbers will vary by region.
Higher numbers will have more difficulty genning in solo worlds with less tricks.
Low: 10%
Medium: 30%
High: 50%

options.label: Blast Shield Available Types
options.description:
Which blast shield types are available for randomization.
All: All blast shield types are available, including beam combos, bomb, power bomb, charge beam, and super missiles
No beam combos: Flamethrower, Wavebuster, and Ice Spreader will not be included as blast shield types (Super Missiles will still be included)

options.label: Number of Locked Doors to Include
options.description:
If greater than 0, locked doors will be placed in the game (maximum of 1 per level).
These will only be placed in spots that will not prevent progression but may force alternate paths.

options.label: Include Power Beam Doors
options.description:
If enabled, Power Beam doors will be an available door color for randomization.
If the starting beam is also randomized, it will remove the new starting beam's color from the pool of available door colors.

options.label: Include Morph Ball Bomb Doors
options.description: If enabled, Morph Ball Bomb doors will be added as an available door color for door randomization.

options.label: Randomize Starting Beam
options.description: If enabled, the starting beam will be randomized to a random beam that is not the Power Beam.

options.label: Progressive Beam Upgrades
options.description: If enabled, 3 progressive beam items will be added into the item pool per beam. These unlock the beam itself, charging capabilities, and the associated missile combo.

options.label: Non-Varia Heat Damage
options.description: If enabled, the gravity suit and phazon suit will not protect against heat damage which will change the required logic of the game.

options.label: Staggered Suit Damage
options.description:
Configure how suit damage reduction is calculated.
Default: based on the strongest suit you have
Progressive: based on the number of suits you have
Additive: Individual suits provide their added damage reduction

options.label: Trick Difficulty
options.description: Determines which tricks, if any, are required to complete the seed. This will affect the logic of the game

options.label: Trick Allow List
options.description: A list of trick names to explicitly allow in logic, regardless of selected difficulty. For example, "Crashed Frigate Scan Dash" or "Alcove Escape".

options.label: Trick Deny List
options.description: A list of trick names to explicitly deny in logic, regardless of selected difficulty.  For example, "Crashed Frigate Scan Dash" or "Alcove Escape".

options.label: Flaahgra Power Bombs
options.description: If enabled, makes the sandstone block at the top of arboretum breakable with power bombs. Note that this will require you to have 4 power bombs in order to defeat Flaahgra.

options.label: Backwards Lower Mines
options.description: If enabled, allows you to progress through the lower mines in reverse by removing the locks in the PCA room.

options.label: Remove Xray Visor Requirements
options.description:
Determines the xray visor requirements.
Remove None: No xray visor requirements are removed.
Remove Most: All xray visor requirements are removed except for metroid prime, chozo ghosts (normal/minimal combat difficulty), and omega pirate.
Remove All But Omega Pirate: All xray visor requirements are removed except for omega pirate.

options.label: Remove Thermal Visor Requirements
options.description:
Determines the thermal visor requirements.
Remove None: No thermal visor requirements are removed.
Remove Most: All thermal visor requirements are removed except for metroid prime (note this means wave beam panels will be in logic without the visor to see them).
Remove All: All thermal visor requirements are removed (note this means wave beam panels will be in logic without the visor to see them).

options.label: Remove Hive Mecha
options.description:
If enabled, the trigger for the Hive Mecha boss will be removed from the game.
Can be forced on if you don't start with Power Beam and you start at Tallon Overworld - Landing Site or Chozo Ruins - Save Station 1.

options.label: Add Spring Ball
options.description:
Enables the spring ball when you receive Morph Ball Bombs or Spring Ball.
This will allow you to jump while in morph ball form by pressing up on the c stick,
reducing the complexity of double bomb jumps.
Progressive means you get Spring Ball then Bombs.

options.label: Display Non-Local Items
options.description:

None: means only local items have matching models.
Match Game: means that only Metroid Prime game have matching models.
Match Series: means that any supported Metroid games will use Metroid Prime models that matches the item from the other world.
