options.label: Death Traps
options.description: Can you receive death traps?

options.label: Easy Mode
options.description: Easy Mode gives unlimited lives

options.label: Game Over Traps
options.description: Can you receive game over traps?

options.label: Stages To Clear
options.description: Amount of stages required to reach goal.

options.label: Starting Location
options.description: Choose where you want to start the game.

options.label: Beacon Fragments in Pool
options.description: How many Prothean Beacon Fragments are shuffled into the item pool.

options.label: Beacon Fragments Required
options.description: How many Prothean Beacon Fragments unlock Ilos. Lowered to the pool size if it is larger.

options.label: Required Squad Size
options.description: How many squadmates logic expects before landing on a mission world (Eden Prime and the Citadel excepted).

options.label: Shuffle the Mako
options.description:
Shuffle the M35 Mako into the item pool. When off, the Mako is available from the start.

Most mission worlds have a Mako section, so turning this on gates nearly everything behind one item.

options.label: Kaidan and Ashley Join at the Citadel
options.description:
On: Kaidan and Ashley are not items. The first Citadel arrival recruits both as in the vanilla game, and logic
counts them once you reach the Citadel. Off: they are items like Garrus, Wrex, Tali and Liara.

options.label: Include Bring Down the Sky
options.description: Include the Bring Down the Sky content (Asteroid X57).

options.label: Codexsanity
options.description:
Codex pages are checks: unlocking a page sends it.

story: pages from the Citadel, the story planets and squadmate conversations on the Normandy (94).
full: also Normandy crew and terminals, uncharted worlds and side-assignment transmissions (119).

options.label: Journalsanity
options.description:
Journal entries are checks: each quest's first entry (Started) and its completion (Completed). A story choice can
skip a completion (a failed assignment), so completions only hold filler.

story: Citadel, story planet and squadmate quests. full: also uncharted-world assignments.

options.label: Containersanity
options.description:
Containers that need no Decryption (crates, kits, ammo packs, malfunctioning objects...) are checks: opening one
sends it. Vanilla loot stays inside.

with_drops: each container also counts once per treasure roll it makes (crates 3, kits 2, ...), all sent on open.

options.label: Aid Stations
options.description: Aid Stations (medi-gel refills) that need no Decryption are checks: using one sends it.

options.label: Unlock Containers
options.description:
Containers and Aid Stations locked behind Decryption open like plain ones (no skill, no minigame), and become
checks under Containersanity / Aid Stations (179 more).

options.label: Finished Mission Checks
options.description:
Therum and Virmire close for good once their mission is finished, so checks left behind there are lost.

filler_only: their containers and mission-only codex pages hold filler only, so nothing important can be lost.
any_item: they can hold anything; collect everything on Therum and Virmire before finishing those missions.

options.label: Shop Slots
options.description:
Archipelago Items for sale at each merchant (ten merchants: Normandy, Citadel, Noveria, Feros, Virmire), a few
hundred credits each. Buying one sends its item. The slots appear in a shop's stock the first time you visit it, so
connect the client before your first shop visit. Commander Rentola's stock on the Normandy (there only for a short
while after Virmire) holds filler only; the Virmire camp follows Finished Mission Checks.

options.label: Gear Items
options.description:
How many gear items (one manufacturer's weapon, armor, bio-amp or omni-tool line each) are drawn into the pool.

Every category is represented; about one in twenty is Spectre gear. Gear arrives at a level that climbs from I to X
as you collect it (Spectre gear is always X). Lowered to the free room in the pool.

options.label: Random Upgrades
options.description:
How many Random Upgrade items (a weapon, ammo, armor or grenade mod) are in the pool. Lowered to the free room
left after gear.

options.label: Infinite Sprint
options.description:
Sprinting (storming) never runs out of stamina. Needs the LE1APBridge ASI v11 or newer (v9 and v10 leave
Shepard out of breath).

options.label: Completion Goal
options.description:
Choose the completion goal.
Ripto - Collect enough orbs to open the arena and beat Ripto.
64 Orb - Collect 64 orbs and beat Ripto.
100 Percent - Collect all talismans, orbs, and gems and beat Ripto.
    In Open World mode, no talismans are required.
10 Tokens - Collect 8000 gems and 55 orbs to unlock the theme park
    and collect all 10 tokens in Dragon Shores.
All Skillpoints - Collect all 16 skill points in the game.
Epilogue - Unlock the full epilogue by collecting all 16 skill points
    and defeating Ripto.

options.label: Orbs to Unlock Ripto
options.description: How many orbs are required to unlock the door to Ripto.

options.label: Enable Open World
options.description:
If on, Crush and Gulp do not require talismans.
Removes talisman items from the pool.
Effectively allows early access to each homeworld,
though swim and climb may logicially lock progression.

options.label: Open World Start With Warps
options.description:
The player will start with warps to all 3 worlds.
Only has an effect in open world mode.

options.label: Start With Abilities
options.description: The player will start with swim, climb, headbash.

options.label: Winter Tundra Inner Warp
options.description:
When warping to Winter Tundra from outside Crush or Gulp,
reroutes the warp to inside the castle. Logically grants access
to inner Winter Tundra.
Represents planned vanilla functionality that was cut.
Vanilla: Warps always go to outside the castle.
Door: Warps inside the castle if you have unlocked the
    door with headbash.
Wall Orb: Warps inside the castle if you have the WT wall orb.
Always: Warps always go to inside the castle. Logic will expect
    homeworld navigation via Winter Tundra's castle warp.

options.label: Open Professor's Door
options.description:
Automatically open the Professor's door in Autumn Plains,
which normally requires 8 orbs (normally bypassable with tricks).
This door also affects the behavior of the warp from Crush to
Autumn Plains. When the door is open, this warp will bring you
next to Gulp, allowing you to skip needing climb to access the second
half of Autumn Plains. This option is intended for use with
open world with open world warps, but can be used without.

options.label: Level Locks
options.description:
Rules for unlocking each level.
Glimmer, homeworlds, and bosses always have their vanilla requirements.
If Moneybagssanity is off, sets prices to 0 to ensure beatable seeds.
Vanilla: Levels are available if you meet the vanilla requirements.
Keys: Levels are unlocked by finding "Unlock" items.
    Note: you may need to increase the number of locations (for example,
    by adding gem checks) to provide spots for the keys.

options.label: Starting Level Unlocks
options.description:
How many level unlocks the player starts with.
The player always has access to Glimmer, homeworlds, and bosses.
Only has an effect when level locks are on.

options.label: Enable 25% Gem Checks
options.description: Adds locations for getting 25% of the gems in a level

options.label: Enable 50% Gem Checks
options.description: Adds locations for getting 50% of the gems in a level

options.label: Enable 75% Gem Checks
options.description: Adds locations for getting 75% of the gems in a level

options.label: Enable 100% Gem Checks
options.description: Adds locations for getting all gems in a level

options.label: Enable Total Gem Count Checks
options.description:
Adds locations for every 500 gems you collect total.
Gems currently paid to Moneybags do not count
towards your total. Logic assumes you pay Moneybags everywhere
you can so you cannot be locked out of locations.

options.label: Max for Total Gem Count Checks
options.description:
The highest number of total gems that can be required
for Total Gem Count locations. Has no effect if
Enable Total Gem Count Checks is disabled.

options.label: Enable Skillpoint Checks
options.description: Adds locations for getting skill points

options.label: Enable Life Bottle Checks
options.description: Adds locations for getting life bottles

options.label: Enable Spirit Particle Checks
options.description:
Adds locations for getting all spirit particles in a level.
Some minigame enemies are counted as spirit particles,
like Draclets in Crystal Glacier. Some enemies only release
spirit particles while the camera is on them.

options.label: Gem Locations Added
options.description:
Adds this many individual gems as locations.
Gems are chosen at random and are not marked in game.
Trackers may help identify which gems are locations.
Gemsanity may override your choices to ensure the seed
can generate.
WARNING: Selecting an option smaller than 25 requires the host to
     edit allow_full_gemsanity in their yaml file.

options.label: Enable Gemsanity
options.description:
Adds gem items to the item pool. Touching gems in game will not
increase your total, only these items.
To ensure enough locations for these items, this may override
your settings for Gem Locations Added.
If Moneybagssanity is off, all Moneybags prices will be set to 0 in game.
Full requires the host to edit allow_full_gemsanity
    in their yaml file, as it is very disruptive.
Off: Individual gems are not checks.
Bundles: For every level with loose gems (not speedways), Gem Bundle items giving
    gems for that level will be added to the pool. Adds 10-25% more locations
    than bundles.
Full: (Almost) every gem is an item. All gems are added to the location pool.

options.label: Gemsanity Item Locations
options.description:
Should gem items be shuffled only
in your world, or spread across the entire multiworld.
Global is more disruptive to other players.

options.label: Gem Bundle Item Size
options.description:
Define the amount of gems awarded by each Gem Bundle item.
Determines how many items are added to the item pool.
Determines how many gem locations are randomly selected if
    Gemsanity is set to Partial (adds one location per bundle item).
WARNING: Selecting an option smaller than 25 requires the host to
    edit allow_full_gemsanity in their yaml file.
Default (50):adds 8 Gem Bundles per Level to the Item Pool (168 Total)
10: 40 Bundles/Level (840 Total) ,  16: 25 Bundles/level (525 Total)
20: 20 Bundles/Level (420 Total) ,  25: 16 Bundles/Level (336 Total)
40: 10 Bundles/Level (210 Total) ,  50: 8 Bundles/Level (168 Total)
80: 5 Bundles/Level (105 Total)  ,  100: 4 Bundles/Level (84 Total)

options.label: Moneybags Settings
options.description:
Settings for Moneybags unlocks.
Vanilla - Pay Moneybags to progress as usual
Moneybagssanity - You cannot pay Moneybags at all and must        find unlock items to progress. Glimmer Bridge
    is excluded to avoid issues with early game randomization.

options.label: DeathLink
options.description:
Spyro will die when a DeathLink is
received and will send them on his death.
Not every death will trigger a DeathLink,
and not every received DeathLink will kill Spyro.

options.label: Enable Extra Lives Filler
options.description: Adds extra lives to the item pool.

options.label: Enable Temporary Destructive Spyro Filler
options.description:
Adds to the item pool an item temporarily powering up
Spyro so anything destructible he touches is destroyed.
Affects enemies, strong chests, breakable walls, etc.
Warning: Behavior is not consistent while charging.

options.label: Enable Changing Spyro's Color Filler
options.description: Adds changing Spyro's color to the item pool.

options.label: Enable Big Head and Flat Spyro Filler
options.description:
Adds turning on Big Head Mode and flat Spyro Mode
to the item pool.

options.label: Enable Healing Sparx Filler
options.description:
Adds healing Sparx to the item pool.
Sparx must be alive to be healed.

options.label: Trap Percentage of Filler
options.description: The percentage of filler items that will be traps.

options.label: Enable Hurting Sparx Trap
options.description:
Adds damaging Sparx to the item pool.
Cannot directly kill Spyro.

options.label: Enable Sparxless Trap
options.description: Adds an item removing Sparx to the item pool.

options.label: Enable Invisibility Trap
options.description:
Adds turning Spyro invisible briefly to the item pool.
Duckstation must be run in Interpreter mode for this to have any effect.

options.label: Enable Lazy Sparx Trap
options.description: Adds making Sparx refuse to pick up gems for 30 seconds to the item pool.

options.label: Enable Progressive Sparx Health Upgrades
options.description:
Start the game with lower max health
and add items to the pool to increase your max health.
Off - The game behaves normally.
Blue - Your max health starts at blue Sparx.
Green - Your max health starts at green Sparx.
Sparxless - Your max health starts at no Sparx.
True Sparxless - Your max health is permanently Sparxless.

options.label: Enable Progressive Sparx Health Logic
options.description:
Certain Sparx health amounts are expected before
you are required to enter different levels.
Aquaria Towers, Crush, and Autumn Plains expects green Sparx.
Entering Skelos Badlands, Gulp, and Winter Tundra expects blue Sparx.
Entering Ripto expects gold Sparx.
This does nothing unless Enable Progressive Sparx Health Upgrades
is set to blue, green, or Sparxless,

options.label: Double Jump Ability
options.description:
Settings for the unintended double jump ability, where jumping
then pressing square without letting go of jump gains extra height.
May impact logic on harder trick settings.
Duckstation must be run in Interpreter mode for this to have any effect.
Vanilla - Double Jump behaves normally.
In Pool - Adds Double Jump to the item pool.
    The ability is disabled until you acquire the item.
Off - Double Jump is disabled.

options.label: Permanent Fireball Ability
options.description:
Settings for the Dragon Shores permanent fireball ability.
May impact logic, even on the easiest trick settings.
Vanilla - The fireball powerup in Dragon Shores behaves normally.
In Pool - Adds Permanent Fireball to the item pool.
    The Dragon Shores powerup does not work.
Off - Permanent Fireball is disabled.
    The Dragon Shores powerup does not work.
Start With - You begin the game with fireball, as in New Game Plus.

options.label: Sparx Gem Finder
options.description:
Settings for Sparx's gem finder ability.
Vanilla - Holding L1+R1+R2 has Sparx point to the nearest gem.
    Beating Ripto makes the effect permanent.
In Pool - Adds Sparx Gem Finder to the item pool.
    Behaves like Vanilla once you find the item.
Off - Removes the ability for Sparx to point to gems.

options.label: Extended Sparx Range
options.description:
Settings for Extended Sparx range.
Vanilla - Beating Ripto doubles Sparx's range.
In Pool - Adds Extended Sparx Range to the item pool.
    This item doubles Sparx's range.
    Beating Ripto has no effect on your range.

options.label: Extra Hit Point in Item Pool
options.description:
Adds an extra hit point (equivalent to the in game cheat code)
to the item pool. This does not affect progressive health logic.
Has no effect when Progressive Sparx Health Upgrades are True Sparxless.

options.label: Trick Difficulty
options.description:
Determines which tricks, if any, are in logic.
See https://github.com/Uroogla/S2AP/wiki/Tricks-and-Presets
Off: Only dev-intended strategies are expected.
Easy Tricks: Straightforward double jumps and fireball usage may be required.
Medium Tricks: Standard speedrunning tricks, including more difficult
    double jumps, may be required.
Custom: Choose exactly which tricks are in logic.

options.label: Custom Tricks
options.description:
Set various tricks for logic.
Only used if Trick Difficulty is Custom.
Format as a comma-separated list of "nice" names:
["Sunny Beach Turtle Soup without Climb", "Crystal Glacier Bridge without Moneybags"].
A full list of supported tricks can be found at:
https://github.com/Uroogla/S2AP/blob/main/apworld/spyro2/LogicTricks.py

options.label: Colossus Starting Goals
options.description: How many goals you start with in both Colossus orb challenges.

options.label: Idol Easy Fish
options.description: Red fish behave the same as other types of fish in Idol Springs.

options.label: Hurricos Easy Lightning Orbs
options.description: Lightning thieves do not steal the orbs in Hurricos.

options.label: Breeze Required Gears
options.description: How many gears you must collect to complete the trolley orb.

options.label: Scorch Bombo Settings
options.description:
Settings for the Bombo orb in Scorch.
Vanilla - Bombo behaves as normal.
First Only - Complete the first (shortest) path to complete the orb.
Attackless First Only - Complete the first (shortest) path to
    complete the orb. Bombo will not attack.

options.label: Fracture Require Headbash
options.description:
Whether Hunter requires headbash to start Earthshaper Bash.
Without headbash, this orb can be completed with fireball
or the Fracture Easy Earthshapers setting.
This changes the orb's logic.

options.label: Fracture Easy Earthshapers
options.description:
Removes the 7 earthshapers from the Alchemist area and
reduces the maximum number of spirit particles in the level.
Removes the headbash requirement from the Fracture Hills
all spirit particles check. The second orb still requires
headbash, unless Fracture Require Headbash is disabled.

options.label: Magma Spyro Starting Popcorn
options.description: How many popcorn crystals you start with in each Hunter orb challenge.

options.label: Magma Hunter Starting Popcorn
options.description: How many popcorn crystals Hunter starts with in each Hunter orb challenge.

options.label: Shady Require Headbash
options.description:
Whether Free Hippos in Shady Oasis requires headbash to start.
Without headbash, this orb can be completed with fireball.
This changes the orb's logic.

options.label: Easy Gulp
options.description: Spyro does double damage to Gulp.

options.label: Portal and Gem Collection Text Color
options.description:
Changes the color of the number that appears when gems are collected,
as well as the text on portals.

options.label: Gem Color
options.description:
Changes the color of gem types (and some other items in game).
Default: No changes.
Shuffle: Mixes up the colors of gem types.
Random Choice: Gem colors are randomly selected from a curated set of options.
True Random: Gem colors are completely random.  This probably won't look great.

options.label: Musicsanity
options.description:
Shuffles most of the music in game.
Off: No changes.
Like With Like: Music is shuffled within its type:
    Homeworld, Normal Level, Boss.
Full: Music is shuffled regardless of type.

options.label: Streamer-Friendly Music
options.description:
Streaming platforms sometimes mute VODs with the Autumn Plains
or Winter Tundrea homeworld music.
Replaces these with Summer Forest.

options.label: Completion Goal
options.description:
Lets the user choose the completion goal.
Sorceress 1 - Beat the sorceress *and* obtain the specified number of eggs.
Egg For Sale - Chase Moneybags after defeating the sorceress the first time.
Sorceress 2 - Beat the sorceress in Super Bonus Round *and*
    obtain the specified number of eggs.
All Skillpoints - Collect all 20 skill points in the game.
    Excluded locations are still required for this goal.
Epilogue - Unlock the full epilogue by collecting all 20 skill points
    and defeating the sorceress. Excluded locations are still required for this goal.
Spike - Beat Spike *and* obtain the specified number of eggs.
Scorch - Beat Scorch *and* obtain the specified number of eggs.
Egg Hunt - Find the specified number of eggs to win. Portal requirements are reduced.

options.label: Eggs to Win
options.description:
The number of eggs needed to win when goal is Sorceress 1,
Sorceress 2, Spike, Scorch, and Egg Hunt.

options.label: Percent Extra Egg Hunt Eggs
options.description:
The percentage of extra eggs in the pool for Egg Hunt.
For example, if 50 eggs are needed and there are 20% extra eggs,
60 eggs will be in the pool. The total number of available eggs
caps at 150 regardless of this option. Rounds up.

options.label: Guaranteed Items
options.description: Guarantees that the specified items will be in the item pool

options.label: Open World Mode
options.description:
Grants access to all 4 homeworlds from the start.
End of level and boss eggs are removed as checks.
This removes 18 locations from the location pool,
so you may need to enable additional locations to use this option.
If Moneybags is Vanilla, companion unlocks will be free.
Disables world keys.

options.label: Level Lock Options
options.description:
Determines the rules for entering levels.
Sparx levels, companion levels, homeworlds, Super Bonus Round, and bosses
are not affected by these settings.
At least one Sunrise level will always start unlocked.
Some settings give a free egg to ensure correct behavior.
Some settings prevent non-companion levels from out of bounds.
Vanilla: Levels have their vanilla unlock requirements.
Keys: 20 Level Unlock items are added to the item pool.
Randomize Requirements: Randomizes egg requirements for levels
    that normally require eggs to enter.
Add Requirements: Any level can have an egg requirement added.
Add Gem Requirements: Any level can have an egg OR gem requirement added.
    Only works when both Moneybagssanity and Gemsanity are on.

options.label: Number of Starting Levels
options.description:
When Level Lock Options is not Vanilla or Randomize Requirements,
determines how many non-companion levels start unlocked.
The recommended value when Keys are in use is 2 or 3.
One Sunrise level will always be unlocked.

options.label: Eggs to Open Sorceress Door
options.description:
Determines how many eggs are required to open Sorceress' Lair
in Midnight Mountain.
NOTE: This only works if Duckstation is set to interpreter mode.

options.label: Eggs to Open Super Bonus Round
options.description:
Determines how many eggs are required to open Super Bonus Round.
NOTE: This only works if Duckstation is set to interpreter mode.

options.label: Gems to Open Super Bonus Round
options.description:
Determines how many gems are required to open Super Bonus Round.
Gem requirements within Super Bonus Round are based on this number.
NOTE: This only works if Duckstation is set to interpreter mode.
In game displays may have visual glitches.

options.label: Enable 25% Gem Checks
options.description: Adds checks for getting 25% of the gems in a level

options.label: Enable 50% Gem Checks
options.description: Adds checks for getting 50% of the gems in a level

options.label: Enable 75% Gem Checks
options.description: Adds checks for getting 75% of the gems in a level

options.label: Enable 100% Gem Checks
options.description: Adds checks for getting all gems in a level

options.label: Enable Total Gem Count Checks
options.description:
Adds checks for every 500 gems you collect total.
Gems currently paid to Moneybags do not count towards your total.
Logic assumes you pay Moneybags everywhere.

options.label: Max for Total Gem Count Checks
options.description:
The highest number of total gems that can be required for Total Gem Count checks.
Has no effect if Enable Total Gem Count Checks is disabled.

options.label: Enable Gemsanity
options.description:
Adds checks for individual gems.
If Moneybagssanity is off, Moneybags unlocks become free.
WARNING: Full gemsanity requires the host to edit allow_full_gemsanity
    in their yaml file.
Off: Individual gems are not checks.
Partial: 200 random gems become checks. Adds items giving 50 or 100 gems
    for specific levels to the item pool.
Full Bundles: Every gem is a check.  Adds items giving 50 or 100 gems
    for specific levels to the item pool.  Adds many filler items.

options.label: Enable Skillpoint Checks
options.description: Adds checks for getting skill points

options.label: Enable Life Bottle Checks
options.description:
Adds checks for breaking life bottles.
Off: Life bottles are not checks.
Normal: The 26 intended life bottles become checks.
Hard: Adds the out-of-bounds life bottle in Fireworks Factory to the pool.
This does not include the 3 bottles on the impossible island in Midnight Mountain.

options.label: Sparx Power-sanity Settings
options.description:
Shuffles the Sparx abilities from completing Sparx levels into the item pool.
Sparx's ability to break baskets becomes 2 progressive items.
Having both allows atlas warp and breaking vases.

options.label: DeathLink
options.description:
Spyro will die when a DeathLink is received.
Sends DeathLinks on his death.
Some edge cases may not be handled.

options.label: Moneybags Settings
options.description:
Determines settings for Moneybags unlocks.
Moneybags dialog has small visual errors.
Defeating the Sorceress bypasses all requirements.
Vanilla - Pay Moneybags to progress as usual
Companionsanity - Unlock items replace payment for side characters.
Moneybagssanity - Unlock items replace payment for Moneybags.

options.label: Powerup Lock Settings
options.description:
Powerup gates (such as superflame) require items to use.
Does not affect the invincibility filler item.
NOTE: The Sunrise Spring early level entry tricks assume
    you do not need the superfly powerup to complete them!
Vanilla - Powerups are available at all times.
Type - Superfly, Fireball, and Invincibility Powerup items are added to the pool.
    Fireworks Factory and Super Bonus Round's combo powerups
    require both Superfly and Fireball to unlock.
Individual: Each level's powerups are unlocked by a specific item.

options.label: Enable World Keys
options.description:
Prevents moving to the next homeworld without enough World Key items.
You must still complete the vanilla requirements to go to the next homeworld.
Disabled in Open World mode.

options.label: Enable Extra Lives Filler
options.description: Enables filler items that grant extra lives

options.label: Enable Temporary Invincibility Filler
options.description: Enables filler items that grant temporary invincibility

options.label: Enable Changing Spyro's Color Filler
options.description: Enables filler items that change Spyro's color

options.label: Enable Big Head and Flat Spyro Filler
options.description: Enables filler items that turn on Big Head Mode and Flat Spyro Mode

options.label: Enable (over)healing Sparx Filler
options.description: Enables filler items that heal Sparx. Can exceed max health.

options.label: Trap Percentage of Filler
options.description: The percent chance that a filler items is a trap.

options.label: Enable Hurting Sparx Trap
options.description: Enables traps that damage Sparx. Cannot directly kill Spyro.

options.label: Enable Sparxless Trap
options.description: Enables traps that removes Sparx.

options.label: Enable Progressive Sparx Health Upgrades
options.description:
Start the game with less max health.
Add items to the pool to increase your max health.
Heal Sparx items have no effect until all items are found.
Off - The game behaves normally.
Blue - Your max health starts at blue Sparx.
Green - Your max health starts at green Sparx.
Sparxless - Your max health starts at no Sparx.
True Sparxless - Your max health is permanently Sparxless.

options.label: Enable Progressive Sparx Health Logic
options.description:
Certain Sparx health amounts are expected before
you are required to enter different levels.
Super Bonus Round, Crawdad Farm, and levels in Midday and later
logically require green Sparx.
Fireworks Factory, Charmed Ridge, and levels in Midnight and later
logically require blue Sparx.
Dino Mines and the Sorceress logically require
gold Sparx.
The Extra Health item/bonus from Starfish Reef is not considered for this logic.
Note: This does nothing unless Enable Progressive Sparx
Health Upgrades is set to blue, green, or Sparxless,

options.label: Require Sparx for Max Gems
options.description:
Determines the logic for gemsanity and 100% gem checks.
75% gem checks (100% in levels with no enemies) are always on.
Off: Sparx max health and abilities do not affect gem logic.
Green Sparx: Sparx is required.
Sparx Finder: Sparx Gem Finder is required.
NOTE: This option is ignored in True Sparxless mode,
or in Sparxless mode if Progressive Sparx Health Logic is off.

options.label: Number of Zoe Hints
options.description:
Some or all of the 13 Tutorial Zoes give hints.
Which Zoes give hints are random.
Hints include:
- Difficult or slow locations
- Progression items in your world
- Joke hints

options.label: Enable Midnight Whirlwind
options.description:
Adds a whirlwind outside the Sorceress' Lair leading to the impossible
island with 3 life bottles, once the Sorceress has been defeated.
Puts these bottles into the item pool if life bottles are enabled.

options.label: Easy Skateboarding Lizards
options.description:
The Sunny Villa lizard skateboarding challenges require only 1 lizard.
Results in minor graphical glitches.

options.label: Easy Skateboarding Points
options.description:
Point-based skateboarding challenges in Sunny Villa
and Enchanted Towers become much easier.
Includes skill points.

options.label: Easy Skateboarding Lost Fleet
options.description: Your turbo cannot run out in the Lost Fleet skateboarding challenges.

options.label: Easy Skateboarding Super Bonus Round
options.description: Your turbo cannot run out in the Super Bonus Round skateboarding challenge.

options.label: Easy Boxing
options.description: The enemy yeti in Frozen Altars boxing has only 1 health.

options.label: Easy Spooky Sheila Missions
options.description: Rocks and mushrooms never respawn in Spooky Swamp's Sheila sub-area.

options.label: Easy Tanks
options.description:
The Tanks challenges in Haunted Tomb will require only 1 tank each.
Results in minor graphical glitches.

options.label: Easy Subs
options.description:
The Lost Fleet submarine challenges require ony 1 sub.
The HUD will incorrectly display 1/1.

options.label: Easy Bluto
options.description: Bluto in Seashell Shores has only 1 health.

options.label: Easy Sleepyhead
options.description: Sleepyhead in Spooky Swamp has only 1 health.

options.label: Easy Shark Riders
options.description:
The Shark Riders challenge in Desert Ruins requires only 1 shark,
which starts to the left of the building.

options.label: Easy Whack-a-Mole
options.description: The Bentley Whack-A-Mole challenge in Crystal Islands require only 1 mole.

options.label: Easy Tunnels
options.description: Water tunnels in Seashell Shore and Dino Mines move slightly more slowly.

options.label: Convert Scorch Green Rockets to Red
options.description: Collecting a green rocket in Scorch will automatically convert to 50 red rockets instead.

options.label: Enter Sunny Villa Sheila Area Early
options.description:
Potentially require entering Sunny Villa's Sheila sub-area from out of bounds.
NOTE: Entering this area from behind may crash the game if done incorrectly.
This option only matters is Companionsanity or Moneybagssanity is turned on.

options.label: Cloud Spires Backwards
options.description:
Potentially require completing Cloud Spires backwards
without paying Moneybags or beating the Sorceress.
This option only matters if Moneybagssanity is turned on.

options.label: Enter Molten Crater Early
options.description: Potentially require entering Molten Crater from out of bounds.

options.label: Enter Molten Crater Sgt. Byrd Area Early
options.description: Potentially require entering Molten Crater's Sgt. Byrd sub-area from out of bounds

options.label: Enter Molten Crater Thieves without Moneybags
options.description:
Potentially require entering Molten Crater's Thieves sub-area from out of bounds
without paying Moneybags or beating the Sorceress.
This option only matters if Moneybagssanity is turned on.

options.label: Enter Seashell Shores Early
options.description: Potentially require entering Seashell Shores from out of bounds.

options.label: Enter Seashell Shores Sheila Area Early
options.description: Potentially require entering Seashell Shores' Sheila sub-area from out of bounds.

options.label: Enter Mushroom Speedway Early
options.description: Potentially require entering Mushroom Speedway from out of bounds.

options.label: Enter Sheila's Alp Early
options.description:
Potentially require entering Sheila's Alp from out of bounds
without paying Moneybags or beating the Sorceress.
This option only matters if Companionsanity or Moneybagssanity is turned on.

options.label: Enter Spooky Swamp Early
options.description: Potentially require entering Spooky Swamp from out of bounds.

options.label: Skip Moneybags in Spooky Swamp
options.description:
Potentially require getting to the end of Spooky Swamp
without paying Moneybags or beating the Sorceress.
This option only matters if Moneybagssanity is turned on.

options.label: Enter Bamboo Terrace Early
options.description: Potentially require entering Bamboo Terrace from out of bounds.

options.label: Enter Bamboo Terrace Bentley Area Early
options.description: Potentially require entering the Bamboo Terrace Bentley sub-area from out of bounds.

options.label: Enter Country Speedway Early
options.description: Potentially require entering Country Speedway from out of bounds.

options.label: Enter Sgt. Byrd's Base Early
options.description:
Potentially require entering Sgt. Byrd's Base from out of bounds
without paying Moneybags or beating the Sorceress.
This option only matters if Companionsanity or Moneybagssanity is turned on.

options.label: Enter Frozen Altars Bentley Area Early
options.description:
Potentially require entering the Frozen Altars Bentley sub-area from out of bounds.
This option only matters if Companionsanity or Moneybagssaniity is turned on.

options.label: Enter Frozen Altars Cat Hockey Area without Moneybags
options.description:
Potentially require entering the Frozen Altars cat hockey minigame
without paying Moneybags or beating the Sorceress.
This option only matters if Moneybagssanity is turned on.

options.label: Enter Fireworks Factory Early
options.description: Potentially require entering Fireworks Factory from out of bounds.

options.label: Enter Fireworks Factory Agent 9 Area Early
options.description:
Potentially require entering Fireworks Factory's Agent 9 sub-area
out of bounds.

options.label: Enter Charmed Ridge Early
options.description: Potentially require entering Charmed Ridge from out of bounds.

options.label: Pass Charmed Ridge Stairs without Moneybags
options.description:
Potentially require getting past the stairs in Charmed Ridge
without paying Moneybags or beating the Sorceress.
This option only matters if Moneybagssanity is turned on.

options.label: Enter Honey Speedway Early
options.description: Potentially require entering Honey Speedway from out of bounds.

options.label: Enter Bentley's Outpost Early
options.description:
Potentially require entering Bentley's Outpost
from out of bounds.
This option only matters if Companionsanity or Moneybagssanity is turned on.

options.label: Complete Crystal Islands without Moneybags
options.description:
Potentially require fully completing Crystal Islands
without paying Moneybags or beating the Sorceress.
This option only matters if Moneybagssanity is turned on.

options.label: Complete Desert Ruins without Moneybags
options.description:
Potentially require fully completing Desert Ruins
without paying Moneybags or beating the Sorceress.
This option only matters if Moneybagssanity is turned on.

options.label: Enter Dino Mines Agent 9 Area Early
options.description:
Potentially require entering the Agent 9 sub-area
of Dino Mines out of bounds.

options.label: Enter Sorceress' Lair Early
options.description:
Potentially require entering Sorceress' Lair out of bounds.
Does not change the door or goal requirements.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Choose the end goal.
Cake: Reveal all the hidden paintings and interact with the cake
Badge: Get all Badges

options.label: Logic
options.description:
Standard: Expected game logic
Glitched: Use glitches or other items to stain some paintings or access the top of the house

options.label: Damage per Filler Item
options.description: The number of coins that will be in each filler damage item.

options.label: Techsanity
options.description:
Shuffles technologies into the multiworld.
You need the real techs to research the locations corresponding to the technologies that require them.

options.label: Gate Technology Locations by Era
options.description:
Requires you to have a certain percentage of technologies in a given era before the next era's locations are in logic.
Prevents you from needing to research extremely expensive technologies early, before you have the infrastructure.
Currently requires all previous eras to reach the threshold.

options.label: GPsanity
options.description:
Turns great person bulbs into locations in the multiworld.
This also includes Great Generals and Great Spies.
Change to 0 to fully disable GPsanity.
Warning: Currently not biased towards lower numbers, so be careful with high numbers.

options.label: World Wonders
options.description:
Turns completed World Wonders into locations in the multiworld.
Warning: As wonders are still limited to one in the world, you may need to start a new game to realistically build them.

options.label: National Wonders
options.description: Turns completed National Wonders into locations in the multiworld.

options.label: Unique Units
options.description:
Adds the ability to build unique units to the item pool.
May not add every item if there aren't enough locations to fill.

options.label: Unique Buildings
options.description:
Adds the ability to build unique buildings to the item pool.
May not add every item if there aren't enough locations to fill.
Warning: Can cause in-game lag on entering city screens and breaks wit non-AP World Civilizations.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Number of character towers that must be completed
to finish the Archipelago game.

options.label: Required bosses count
options.description:
Sets the number of mini bosses required to be able to challenge phobosphere.
To unlock phobosphere this therefore requires the mini boss level unlocks
and the phobosphere level unlock

options.label: Hard mode adventure
options.description:
Allows playing the adventure in hard mode. This makes the game a little harder.
It is possible to play on normal, start on hard mode or have hard mode turned
on by a trap item and stay on permanently.

options.label: Hard Trap Count
options.description:
Specifies the amount of hard mode traps added to the item pool
when set to hard as trap.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Seed goal condition.

Currently only supports:
- All Levels Complete

options.label: Enable Level Complete checks
options.description: Enable Level Complete checks for each level.

options.label: Enable All Grain checks
options.description: Adds 'All Grain' checks (equivalent to 50/50 grains collected).

options.label: Enable Grainsanity
options.description: Adds checks for collecting grain in steps

options.label: Grainsanity step
options.description:
How many grain per Grainsanity check.
Example: 10 means checks at 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 (up to max).
It's recommended to keep this as a factor of 50 (e.g. 5, 10, 25)

options.label: Enable FLIK (all letters) checks
options.description: Adds 'FLIK Letters (All)' checks. Must collect F, L, I and K to receive this check.

options.label: Enable individual FLIK checks
options.description: Adds individual FLIK checks for each FLIK letter.

options.label: Enable 25% enemy checks
options.description: Adds checks for killing ~25% of enemies in a level.

options.label: Enable 50% enemy checks
options.description: Adds checks for killing ~50% of enemies in a level.

options.label: Enable 75% enemy checks
options.description: Adds checks for killing ~75% of enemies in a level.

options.label: Enable 100% enemy checks
options.description: Adds checks for killing ~100% of enemies in a level.

options.label: Game Version
options.description:
Choose the game version you will be playing on
 
- **sotfs:** You will be playing the scholar of the first sin version
- **vanilla:** You will be playing the vanilla version

options.label: Combat Logic
options.description:
Determines the distribution of Estus Flask Shards and Sublime Bone Dust.
Easy - Most shards/dust available fairly early on
Medium - Moderate amount of shards/dust available early in the game
Hard - There is minimal logical requirement for shards/dust to be available before the end of the game
Disabled - There is zero requirements for shards/dust anywhere; Lost Bastille is Sphere 1 in Scholar, and Sinners' Rise is Sphere 1 in vanilla.

options.label: No Weapon Requirements
options.description: Remove the requirements to wield weapons

options.label: No Spell Requirements
options.description: Remove the requirements to cast spells

options.label: No Equip Load
options.description: Disable the equip load constraint from the game.

options.label: Auto-Equip
options.description: Automatically equips any received armor, weapons or shields.

options.label: Randomize Starting Loadout
options.description: Randomizes the equipment characters begin with.

options.label: Starting Weapon Requirement
options.description: Forces starting weapons to meet the chosen requirement.

options.label: Enable NewGame+
options.description:
Include items and locations exclusive to NewGame+ cycles
NOT RECOMMENDED, WORK IN PROGRESS

options.label: Early Blacksmith
options.description: Force Lenigrast's key into an early sphere in your world or across all worlds.

options.label: Keep Infinite Lifegems
options.description: Keep Melentia's infinite supply of lifegems

options.label: Exclude Locations
options.description: Prevent these locations from having an important item.

options.label: Start Inventory
options.description: Start with these items.

options.label: Enable Crown of the Old Iron King DLC
options.description: Enable Crown of the Old Iron King DLC, randomizing items and locations within Brume Tower.

options.label: Enable Crown of the Ivory King DLC
options.description: Enable Crown of the Ivory King DLC, randomizing items and locations within Frozen Eleum Loyce.

options.label: Enable Crown of the Sunken King DLC
options.description: Enable Crown of the Sunken King DLC, randomizing items and locations within Shulva.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
The victory condition for your game.

story_star_dream: Defeat Star Dream at the end of Story Mode.
story_boss_count: Defeat a set number of Story Mode bosses (see story_boss_count).

options.label: Story Boss Count
options.description: If Goal is story_boss_count, how many Story Mode bosses must be defeated.

options.label: Stickersanity
options.description:
Stickersanity: add every normal Sticker as its own location (one per
sticker in the album).

WARNING: this adds a large number of locations and, because normal stickers
are collected passively as you play, they end up available across most of
the game at once. That can make for difficult or strange logic, since the
generator has many always-open locations to work with and the usual sense of
progression through the stickers does not apply. Turn this on only if you
want that. Rare Stickers are a separate, smaller set (see
rare_sticker_checks) and are on by default.

options.label: Rare Sticker Location Checks
options.description: Include the 35 in-stage Rare Sticker pickups as locations.

options.label: Open all stages
options.description:
Open every normal stage in an Area as soon as you can reach the Area, so
you can play them in any order. Boss doors still need their Code Cubes, and
EX stages keep their own unlock rules.

options.label: Ability Gating
options.description: Only let Kirby keep copy abilities you've received.

options.label: Armor Mode Gating
options.description: Also gate copy abilities while in the Robobot Armor.

options.label: Death Link
options.description: When you die, everyone dies. When anyone dies, you die.

options.label: Kirby Color
options.description:
Recolor Kirby's body. Cosmetic only chosen once at generation and baked
into the patched ROM. 'pink' leaves the game stock. Textures are from the
community KPR retexture pack (native Robobot format).

options.label: Death Link
options.description: When you die, everyone dies; when anyone dies, you die.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Win condition.

beat_game: reach Gamble Galaxy and claim the Strawberry Shortcake (beat the game).
chests_and_daroach: collect a set number of chests (chest_goal_count) AND beat
    Daroach, the Ice Island boss (the stage-6 boss).

options.label: Chest Goal Count
options.description: For the chests_and_daroach goal: how many chests you must collect.

options.label: Ability Acquired Checks
options.description:
Add a check for the first time you use each copy ability you've received.

Adds 23 ability-acquired locations (one per ability) and 23 more filler items
to match. Off = no ability-use checks.

options.label: Starting Spray
options.description:
Which spray paint Kirby owns from the start. Granted directly -- no location check is
consumed for it.

Pink is Kirby's default and is always available. Choose a color to also OWN that spray from
the start (it shows in your collection and you can apply / re-apply it freely from the spray
menu). 'none' = Pink only. Set this to 'random' in your YAML to have Archipelago pick one for
you -- that's handled by AP itself, so there's no explicit 'random' option here.

Unlike the old Random Starting Color, this grants the real spray instead of a cosmetic tint,
so it sticks and doesn't fight the spray menu.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
What action is required to completed to goal?
Certificate: Open the chest that gives you the certificate.
Tower: Climb the Magical Tower, and defeat Devil.
Souvenirs: Get the 7 souvenirs and give them to your mother.
gems: Get the 7 gems and open the secret door in the library.

options.label: Required Secret Stones
options.description:
How many secret stones are required to get the final exam certificate.  If zero, the ability to ascend Sage's Mountain
is all that is needed to get it.  Note that the Magical Tower requires nothing save combat experience to clear.

options.label: School Lunch
options.description:
Whether the starting 'school lunch' you have (the four Pickled Scallions) are randomized.
Vanilla: Don't touch the items.
Consumables: They are four random consumables or equipment items instead.
Anything: They can be any item.

options.label: Starting Magic
options.description:
What magic Arle should start with, out of the starting spells.
If this list is not default the other spells will be locations that send on start.

options.label: Souvenir Hunt
options.description: The shop souvenirs are shuffled, try to find them!

options.label: Starting Cookies
options.description: How many cookies you start with.

options.label: Reduced Encounters
options.description:
Halves the rate of encounters.  Helps as some places are labyrinthine and will cause a lot of encounters to happen.
Also can offset the 4x encounter rate from holding Scorpion's Wallet

options.label: Squirrel Stations
options.description: Randomizes the ability to use the squirrel station to go to certain locations.  Reaching destinations is a location.

options.label: Bestiary
options.description: Whether meeting an encounter for the first time is a location.

options.label: Skip Fairy Search
options.description:
Skips the event where the fairy at the top of Sage Mountain goes missing, so when you have the necessary secrest stones you
can immediately get the certificate.  If Bestiary is on, this removes the Owlbear location as it is not encountered.

options.label: Starting Gender
options.description: Decides the starting gender state.

options.label: Starting Area
options.description:
Which Crystal Warp platform the player starts at.  Some changes are made to assist accessibility due to
possibly being unable to reach Bewitched Bubble beforehand:
Tengoku: The honey bounce block in Large Tower Room is strengthened.
Slime Citadel: A honey bounce block is placed at Plummet to reach the top.

options.label: Shuffle Double Jump
options.description:
Shuffle the ability to double jump.
In some starting areas, you will get stuck very early without it.

options.label: Shuffle Dodge
options.description:
Shuffle the ability to dodge.
Some logic requires a dodge-jump, so it is possible to be stuck early without it.

options.label: Shuffle Chaos Pieces
options.description:
Shuffles the six Chaos Pieces in your game.
Off: All pieces are placed in their original locations.
On: All six Chaos Pieces can be found anywhere in the multiworld.
If you want to plando these, turn this on first.

options.label: Pottery Lottery
options.description: Breaking the breakables around the world sends out items.

options.label: Shopsanity
options.description: Shuffles all items normally sold in your game. Opens 29 locations.

options.label: Shop Prices
options.description: Sets, as a percentage, the price of all goods in the game.

options.label: Stat Shuffle
options.description: Shuffles all Heart and Mana Container upgrades in your game.  Adds 20 locations.

options.label: Gachapon Shuffle
options.description:
Shuffles the rewards of the gachapon rewards.
Off: All gacha coins are placed locally in their coin locations.  Gacha machines give nothing.
Coins: All gacha coins are shuffled into the multiworld.  Opens 41 locations.
All: All gacha coins and gacha prizes are shuffled into the multiworld.  Opens 82 locations.
Note that the gacha machine order is deterministic based on the seed rolled.

options.label: Quest for Sex
options.description:
Shuffles locations relevant to quest and sex experience.
Off: All quests give no reward, all quest items are vanilla, and all sex experience is tied to the sexual experience.
Sensei Minimal: Rewards for sex experience are shuffled.  Opens 14 locations.
Quests: All quests give a reward and all quest items are shuffled but the resulting cutscenes still give sex experience as normal.  Opens 79 locations.
All: All quests give a reward, and sex experience is included in the multiworld.  Cutscenes do not reward sex experience.  Opens 79 locations.

options.label: Crystal Teleports
options.description:
Shuffles the crystal teleports other than the starting warp.  Item is obtained by interacting with a teleport panel.
Chaos Castle teleport is omitted due to triviality.

options.label: Junk Hint Percent
options.description:
Percent chance an in-game hint is a junk hint.
Helps to keep in-game hints from being too useful.

options.label: I Am A Gooner
options.description: Turning this on turns the cutscenes back on.

options.label: Fuck Link
options.description:
When you get fucked, everyone gets fucked (or dies, I suppose). Of course the reverse is true too.
This is just Death Link btw.

options.label: Ending
options.description:
Choose which ending is required to complete the game.
Ending A: Reach Chamber of the Sleeper without all spells and awaken the Dreamer.
Ending B: Obtain enough Strange Coins and enter the door located in the Labyrinth of Ash.
Ending CD: Reach Chamber of the Sleeper and stare into the water pool.
Ending E: Reach Chamber of the Sleeper with all spells after watching the White VHS Tape and awaken the Dreamer.

options.label: Class
options.description:
The class you play as.
Note: The following classes are handled differently in the game:
Vampire has free access to the cattle cells and the first area, so the first vampiric symbol is unnecessary.
Custom is an advanced option.  If on a website its values will not be visible.  You know how it is smh.

options.label: Starting Area
options.description:
Where the player starts.  You will always land in the starting spot in Hollow Basin but it will be blocked off.
Demi will warp you to Wing's Rest, and the crystal will have the given starting area.
If starting area is Accursed Tomb, Clive will give you an Oil Lantern.

options.label: Entrance Randomization
options.description:
Shuffles the entrances around.  The only untouched entrances are crystal warps (including spell/item), entrance to Chamber of Fate, entrance to
Grave of the Sleeper, and the doors of Tower of Abyss.

options.label: Progressive Symbols
options.description:
Whether the Vampiric Symbols you acquire are split or progressive.  Setting to false is good on entrance randomization, otherwise
can be annoying.

options.label: Random Elements
options.description:
Randomizes the elements of almost all weapons and spells.  Guaranteed Poison ranged option.
Wand of Power is not randomized (its randomly every element and tied to its function).

options.label: Random Equipment Stats
options.description:
Determines how the stats of weapons and spells are changed.
Off: The setting is off, and all stats are vanilla.
Shuffled: The weapon stats are shuffled amongst each other.
Randomize: A random stat value given the existing stats is chosen.

options.label: Enemy Randomization
options.description:
Shuffles the in-game enemies around. Each enemy in the game is replaced by some other enemy.
THIS IS EXPERIMENTAL.  Report any weirdness or problems.

options.label: Required Strange Coins
options.description: Changes the required coins needed to open the door for Ending B.

options.label: Total Strange Coins
options.description:
The total amount of strange coins placed in the multiworld.  Matches required if lower than it.
Note: Filler will be replaced to compensate.

options.label: Shuffle Shop Items
options.description:
Choose whether the unique items Sheryl the Crow sells are locations.
Adds 9 locations.

options.label: Mob Drops
options.description:
Choose whether the items monsters drop are locations.
Off: All drops are vanilla.
Uniques: Only the unique first-drop items (weapons, spells, elixirs) are locations.  Adds 19 locations.
Randomized: Each drop is a location.  WARNING SOME DROPS ARE HORRIBLE TO GET.  Adds 143 locations.

options.label: Quenchsanity
options.description:
If a weapon can gain experience, if it is quenched, it returns a check.
Quenching a weapon now no longer upgrades the weapons, and all quench weapons are added to the pool.
Exceptions: Brittle Arming Sword repairs itself for the sake of the player, and Death Scythe is removed from the inventory as normal.

options.label: Etna's Pupil
options.description:
Become Etna's pupil!  As in, all alchemy creations are locations to check.  Cmon saying -sanity a lot is boring.
If Dropsanity: Randomized is selected, each material is force placed on drops or alchemy spots to ensure repeatability.

options.label: Bookworm
options.description:
Love reading?  Of course you do!  Every lore spot is a check.  Does not include basic signs.  All of this will be on the exam.
Adds 67 locations.

options.label: Levelsanity
options.description:
The experience you would gain instead gives you checks for every level.  Levels in the form of Deep Knowledge items are given to compensate which do give a level.
Adds up to 100 locations (amount depends on starting class).

options.label: Grasssanity
options.description: Every foliage object that normally drops something is a check.  The original drops do drop as normal for now.  Adds 502 locations.

options.label: Breakables
options.description: Every non-foliage breakable object that normally drops something is a check.  The original drops do drop as normal for now.  Adds 318 locations.

options.label: Secret Door Lock
options.description: All secret doors are locked until receiving the Dusty Crystal Orb.

options.label: Lock Switches
options.description:
All physical switches (not mirages) are locked, and cannot be flipped without their relevant item.
Note: Removes filler at random to compensate.

options.label: Lock Doors
options.description:
All physical doors leading to new zones are locked, and cannot be opened without their relevant item.
Note: Removes filler at random to compensate.

options.label: Tricks & Glitches
options.description:
Which tricks or glitches are considered in-logic.
Lightless: All light source items are not necessary for dark areas.
Rock Bridge Skip: Skipping the Vampiric Symbol doors in Castle Le Fanu with Rock Bridge is logical.
Early Surface: Removes logic for reaching the surface entrances from Wing's Rest and Hollow Basin (requires about 20 DEX only).
Barrier Skip: Skips requiring the Earth and Water Talismans.

options.label: Challenges
options.description:
These are optional challenges to make your run harder.  These may not be winnable.  If you turn these on in a public game, don't blame me, blame yourself.
No EXP: You cannot level.  This trumps Levelsanity and turns it off.
No Logic: There is no logic.  You will probably not win.  You've been warned.  But good to try and find skips.

options.label: Filler
options.description:
Lets you decide which filler are added to the game and their weights.  If the set is empty or all values are zero,
Silver and Deep Knowledge will be forced included with weights of 1. Amount received in game is a random value between 1~5, favoring 1~2.
Most filler is self-explanatory save the following:
Deep Knowledge: You get 1 level.
Weight of the Dream (Nothing): Is a nothing item.  Useful if you feel like other items make the game too easy.
Demi's Gift for a Stranger: Attempts to give a random player a random gift.  If it fails or is a solo game, does nothing.

options.label: Filler Local Percent
options.description:
How much of filler is forced local?  Helpful when you don't want to fill the multiworld with your own junk but its fine if some of it bleeds out.
Note that 0% just means none of it is *forced* to be local, not that it is all non-local.

options.label: Traps
options.description:
Lets you decide which traps are in your game and their weights.  If empty or all values are zero, same as having 0 Trap Percent.
Certain joyous traps are allowed during Christmas, otherwise are ignored.
Most traps are self-explanatory save:
Rat Gang: Spawns 5 rats, and "We're the rats" plays.
Health ViaI: It's the fake health vial item Patchouli sells you.  Drink it.  For her.
Date With Death: Sent to DETHLAND map where Death will instantly kill you if you don't teleport out fast enough.
This won't trigger unless you have Spirit Warp so you can actually have a chance to escape.
Patchouli's Gift for a Stranger: Attempts to send a random player a random trap.  If it fails or is a solo game, does nothing.
Acceptable Traps: "Bleed Trap", "Poison Trap", "Curse Trap", "Slowness Trap", "Blindness Trap", "Mana Drain Trap",
"Health ViaI", "XP Drain Trap", "Rat Gang", "Date With Death Trap", Coal, Eggnog.

options.label: Trap Percent
options.description: Percent of filler items to be converted to traps.

options.label: Custom Class
options.description:
If 'Custom' is chosen for starting class, this is used as a stand-in for that information.
If Name or Description is 'RANDOM', or any stat is -1, a random value will be supplied.
Level ranges from 1 to 10.
Stats (Strength to Resistance) range from 1 to 20.
Resistances (Normal Res to Dark Res) range from 0 to 300.

options.label: Silver Link
options.description: Silver is linked into the RingLink system.  Watch as Luigi's Mansion gets too much money and mimics beat your ass.

options.label: Victory Goals
options.description:
Which spirits, need to defeat which adversaries, at what level, to have completed the game.

Defeating an adversary at a level higher than the target level also counts as defeating them on a lower level.
Selecting multiple levels for the same spirit + adversary will have the lower values ignored.
Selecting many goals may introduce a lot of useless filler items.

options.label: Advanced Victory Goals
options.description:
Which spirits, need to defeat which adversaries, at what level, to have completed the game.

This setting replaces the settings in "Victory Goals" if present.
This setting allows you to specify the boss as an yaml in the form.
It allows you to weight spirit selection chances.
See the Game Page for examples.

options.label: Card unlocking expansions
options.description: Which expansions should be included when creating checks for playing cards

options.label: Spirit unique checks
options.description: For which spirits should playing unique cards earns you checks

options.label: Unlockable spirits & aspects
options.description:
Which spirits (and aspects) should be locked by default and unlockable through checks.

To play an aspect you must first unlock its spirit.

options.label: Starting energy offset
options.description: The starting amount energy per turn offset the spirit starts with (-1 would mean you get 1 less energy per turn. 2 Would mean you get +2 energy per turn)

options.label: Ending energy offset
options.description:
The final amount (when all +Energy checks have been gotten) energy per turn offset the spirit ends with (-1 would mean you get 1 less energy per turn. 2 Would mean you get +2 energy per turn)

This value needs to be higher than or equal to the starting energy offset

options.label: Starting cardplays offset
options.description: The starting amount energy per turn offset the spirit starts with (-1 would mean you get 1 less energy per turn. 2 Would mean you get +2 energy per turn)

options.label: Ending cardplays offset
options.description:
The final amount (when all +Cardplay checks have been gotten) cardplays per turn offset the spirit ends with (-1 would mean you get 1 less cardplay per turn. 2 Would mean you get +2 cardplays per turn)

This value needs to be higher than or equal to the starting cardplays offset

options.label: Starting blight offset
options.description: The starting amount blight offset the game starts with (-1 would mean you start with 1 fewer blight)

options.label: Ending blight offset
options.description:
The final amount blight offset when all '+ Blight' check have been collected (-1 would mean you always have at least with 1 fewer blight)

This value needs to be higher than or equal to the starting blight offset

options.label: Remove not in play cards
options.description: Remove minors and majors not selected in 'Card unlocking expansions' from the game

options.label: Spoil items on cards
options.description: Display on the powercards what item they will unlock

options.label: Prioritised Shuffle
options.description: When shuffling the power decks, put cards with unexplored locations on top

options.label: Remove cards when filling
options.description:
When the game has more locations than items, reduce the number of powercards to reduce the number of locations.

Prevents having a lot of filler items, at the cost of losing some major and minor power cards.

options.label: Spirit Shards
options.description: Divides the unlocks for spirits and aspects across that many items.

options.label: Extra copies of spirits and aspects
options.description:
Adds (up to this many) extra copies of spirit and aspect unlocking items.

Does not increase the amount of items required to unlock the spirit/aspect.

options.label: Elements Fill Ratio
options.description:
What percentage of filler items (after filling with extra spirits) should be +element.

0 means no filler items are +element.
100 means all filler items are +element.

Bonus elements last only a single turn.
Fill items that are not +element, are friendly greetings that do not have an effect on the game.

options.label: Golden Bugs
options.description:
If enabled, golden bugs will be shuffled into the itempool.
If disabled, bugs will be vanilla and agitha will not be progression

options.label: Sky Characters
options.description:
If enabled, sky characters will be shuffled into the itempool.
If disabled, sky characters will be vanilla.

options.label: Gifts from NPCs
options.description: If enabled, Gifts from NPCs can be progression items.

options.label: Shop Items
options.description: If enabled, Shop Items can be progression items.

options.label: Hidden Skills
options.description:
If enabled, golden wolfs can be progression items.
*Hidden skills will always be shuffled into item pool.

options.label: Poe Shuffled
options.description:
If enabled, Poes will be shuffled into the itempool.
If disabled, Poes will be vanilla.

options.label: Heart Pieces
options.description: If enabled, Heart Piece locations can contain progression items.

options.label: Overworld Items
options.description:
If enabled, Overworld locations can contain progression items.
Cannot be disabled if Dungeon shuffle is disabled
Note:
Disabling may lead to generation failures as the possible location count is reduced dramtically.

options.label: Dungeons Shuffled
options.description:
If enabled, Dungeons locations can contain progression items.
Cannot be disabled if Overworld shuffle is disabled

options.label: Randomize Small Keys
options.description:
Controls how small keys are randomized.

- **Start With Small Keys:** You will start the game with the small keys for all dungeons.
- **Vanilla Small Keys:** Small keys will be kept in their vanilla location (non-randomized).
- **Own Dungeon Small Keys:** Small keys will be randomized locally within their own dungeon.
- **Any Dungeon Small Keys:** Small keys will be randomized locally within any dungeon.
- **Anywhere:** Small keys can be found in any progression location, if dungeons are randomized.

Note:
Not shuffling Dungeons will overwrite this to vanilla, unless you selected start with

options.label: Randomize Big Keys
options.description:
Controls how big keys are randomized.

- **Start With Big Keys:** You will start the game with the big keys for all dungeons.
- **Vanilla Big Keys:** Big keys will be kept in their vanilla location (non-randomized).
- **Own Dungeon Big Keys:** Big keys will be randomized locally within their own dungeon.
- **Any Dungeon Big Keys:** Big keys will be randomized locally within any dungeon.
- **Anywhere:** Big keys can be found in any progression location.

Note:
Not shuffling Dungeons will overwrite this to vanilla, unless you selected start with

options.label: Randomize Maps & Compasses
options.description:
Controls how dungeon maps and compasses are randomized.

- **Start With Maps & Compasses:** You will start the game with the dungeon maps and compasses for all dungeons.
- **Vanilla Maps & Compasses:** Dungeon maps and compasses will be kept in their vanilla location (non-randomized).
- **Own Dungeon Maps & Compasses:** Dungeon maps and compasses will be randomized locally within their own dungeon.
- **Any Dungeon Maps & Compasses:** Dungeon maps and compasses will be randomized locally within any dungeon.
- **Anywhere:** Dungeon maps and compasses can be found anywhere, without restriction.

Note:
Not shuffling Dungeons will overwrite this to vanilla, unless you selected start with

options.label: Dungeon Rewards are prgression
options.description: Controls whether dungeon reward and heart containers are forced to have progression items.

options.label: Small Keys on Bosses
options.description: If disabled, Small keys cannot be placed on boss rewards

options.label: Logic Rules
options.description:
Controls what types of tricks the logic can expect you to perform.

- Glitchless: Only intended mechanics are required
- Glitched: Some glitches may be required

options.label: Castle Requirements
options.description:
NON-DEFAULT CHOICE NOT REPRESENTED IN GAME (must self enforce if changed from default)
Controls requirements for accessing Hyrule Castle.

- Open: No requirements
- Fused Shadows: Requires all Fused Shadows
- Mirror Shards: Requires all Mirror Shards
- All Dungeons: Requires completing all dungeons
- Vanilla: Beat Palace of Twilight

Note:
Choosing All Dungeons or Vanilla will force dungeons items to be in Hyrule Castle if Any Dungeon is chosen for them
    This also removes Hyrule castle from list of dungeons for other of that dungeon item to be in

options.label: Palace Requirements
options.description:
NON-DEFAULT CHOICE NOT REPRESENTED IN GAME (must self enforce if changed from default)
Controls requirements for accessing Palace of Twilight.

- Open: No requirements
- Fused Shadows: Requires all Fused Shadows
- Mirror Shards: Requires all Mirror Shards
- Vanilla: Beat City in the Sky

Note:
Choosing Vanilla will force dungeons items to be in Palace of Twilight if Any Dungeon is chosen for them
