Choose if Morph Extensions should also be included in the pool. Each Morph Extension adds 2 seconds to your morph
duration, up to a maximum of an additional 20 seconds added to your base morph duration.
Default: Disabled

options.label: Extra Channel Keys
options.description:
Determine if extra Channel Keys should be generated in addition to the minimum required to unlock all the channels.

To specify custom values, add it alongside the pre-existing options, copying their format.
Format: value : weight

options.label: Extra Shop Stocks
options.description:
If the chosen Shoppingsanity option is "Restock", this option determines if extra Shop Stocks should be generated
in addition to the minimum required to unlock all the Shop Items. This option will not have any effect otherwise.

To specify custom values, add it alongside the pre-existing options, copying their format.
Format: value : weight

options.label: Early Free Play
options.description:
Allows Free Play mode to be available without needing to fully clear a channel. Useful when wanting Camerasanity
enabled without needing to worry about Pipo Monkey actors.
default: Enabled.

options.label: Enable Monkey Mart
options.description:
Choose if Monkey Mart should be able to sell cookies, energy and pellets. Morph Stock and Lucky Ticket will
remain available

Default: Enabled

options.label: Hints from Hint Books
options.description:
Choose if the Hint Book shop items will provide hints instead of items. Shoppingsanity must be at least enabled.

Default: Disabled

options.label: Lucky Ticket Consolation Effects
options.description:
Choose if Lucky Ticket Consolation Effects should be enabled. When you get a consolation prize, get a chance to
activate a special effect that can affect the Archipelago experience.

options.label: Lucky Ticket Consolation Effects Blacklist
options.description:
When `Lucky Ticket Consolation` is enabled, this option allows you to disable certain effects from being chosen.

Highly destructive effects have override values in host.yaml that will lead to options here being ignored.
If you wish to enable these effects, please refer to the settings in your host.yaml, or contact your game host
in charge of generating the game.

options.label: Auto Save State Slot
options.description:
Choose which slot this slot session should be saved on. Useful when playing multiple instances of this game within
the same multiworld. Slots 1 - 10 are used by the PCSX2 for quick use and will not be used for this purpose.

Please refer to your host.yaml file for more AutoSave/AutoLoad State settings.

<!> WARNING: It is highly recommended to not weight this option and explicitly specify a custom value.
To specify custom values, add it alongside the pre-existing options, copying their format.
Format: value : weight

Default: 0

options.label: Emulator Preferred Port
options.description:
Specify the preferred slot to use when connecting the Archipelago Client with PCSX2
upon connection to an Archipelago Room. This should be the same slot that is specified in PCSX2
under Settings > Advanced > PINE Settings > Slot. More details about connecting the client to PCSX2
can be found in this apworld's setup guide.
Connection details can be changed anytime during play by using the client command `/pine_slot <port>`.

<!> WARNING: It is highly recommended to not weight this option and explicitly specify a custom value.
To specify custom values, add it alongside the pre-existing options, copying their format.
Format: value : weight

options.label: Emulator Linux Preferred Platform
options.description:
*For Linux Players only
Specify which PCSX2 installation to prioritize searching and connecting to upon connection to an Archipelago Room.
Connection details can be changed anytime during play by using the client command `/pine_platform <option>`.

<!> WARNING: It is highly recommended to not weight this option.

> auto - Automatically search for any running PCSX2 installation and connect to the first one detected.
> standard - Prioritize connecting to a normal installation of PCSX2, either from a traditional package manager,
the official appimage, or others. Even if multiple sources of this type are present,
they are all detected as a singular instance, and cannot be individually connected to.
> flatpak - Prioritize connecting to the Flatpak installation of PCSX2.

options.label: Fill With Determination
options.description:
Either fills the rat with determination, or does nothing. Perhaps both.

This option was added early on for technical reasons. It does not directly affect the game.

options.label: Victory Location
options.description:
Optionally moves the final victory location earlier to reduce the number of locations in the multiworld.

- **Snakes on a Planet (default):** The game goes all the way to "Moon, The". This gives the longest game.
- **Secret Cache:** The game stops at the end of Cool World. This gives the middlest-length game.
- **Captured Goldfish:** The game stops at the end of The Sewers. This gives the shortest game.

options.label: Enabled Buffs
options.description:
Enables various buffs that affect how the rat behaves. All are enabled by default.

- **Well Fed:** Gets more done
- **Lucky:** One free success
- **Energized:** Moves faster
- **Stylish:** Better RNG
- **Confident:** Ignore a trap
- **Smart:** Next check is progression

options.label: Enabled Traps
options.description:
Enables various traps that affect how the rat behaves. All are enabled by default.

- **Upset Tummy:** Gets less done
- **Unlucky:** Worse RNG
- **Sluggish:** Moves slower
- **Distracted:** Skip a "step"
- **Startled:** Run towards start
- **Conspiratorial:** Next check is trap
- **Poison:** Dies

options.label: Messages - Changed Target
options.description:
What messages the rat can say when a buff or trap is added to the queue of location checks to send before resuming its normal logic.

Specify the message itself, or with an optional weight to have that message appear more often (default weight is 1).

The text {LOCATION} will be replaced with the name of the actual location.

If you want to disable rat chat, then you're in the wrong place. Do that from the settings menu in the game client itself.

options.label: Messages - Go Mode
options.description:
What messages the rat can say when it first realizes that it can complete its goal.

Specify the message itself, or with an optional weight to have that message appear more often (default weight is 1).

If you want to disable rat chat, then you're in the wrong place. Do that from the settings menu in the game client itself.

options.label: Messages - Enter BK Mode
options.description:
What messages the rat can say when it first sees that no further location checks are in logic.

Specify the message itself, or with an optional weight to have that message appear more often (default weight is 1).

If you want to disable rat chat, then you're in the wrong place. Do that from the settings menu in the game client itself.

options.label: Messages - Still BK
options.description:
What messages the rat can say to occasionally remind the players that it has no further location checks in logic.

Specify the message itself, or with an optional weight to have that message appear more often (default weight is 1).

If you want to disable rat chat, then you're in the wrong place. Do that from the settings menu in the game client itself.

options.label: Messages - Exit BK
options.description:
What messages the rat can say after one or more location checks become in logic.

Specify the message itself, or with an optional weight to have that message appear more often (default weight is 1).

If you want to disable rat chat, then you're in the wrong place. Do that from the settings menu in the game client itself.

options.label: Messages - Victory
options.description:
What messages the rat can say to celebrate victory.

Specify the message itself, or with an optional weight to have that message appear more often (default weight is 1).

If you want to disable rat chat, then you're in the wrong place. Do that from the settings menu in the game client itself.

options.label: Messages - Impending Doom
options.description:
What messages the rat can say when it's about to die.

Specify the message itself, or with an optional weight to have that message appear more often (default weight is 1).

If you want to disable rat chat, then you're in the wrong place. Do that from the settings menu in the game client itself.

options.label: Lactose Intolerant Mode
options.description: Replaces all references to lactose-containing products with less offensive ones.

options.label: Death Link
options.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

options.label: Death Link Delay
options.description:
Has no effect if "Poison" traps are disabled. Otherwise:

Sets the delay (in seconds) from a death trigger to when the rat actually "dies".

Default: 5 (seconds)

options.label: Death Item Replacement %
options.description:
Has no effect if "Poison" traps are disabled. Otherwise:

Controls what percentage of trap items added to the pool should be replaced by "poison" items. The percentage is
taken from the items that are INTENDED to be traps, so you can disable all other traps and still get the same number
of "poison" items as you would otherwise have.

Specifically, items with "poison" auras are held back, and then this configured percentage of random trap items are
replaced by copies of the items that were held back.

Whole numbers only.

Default: 2 (percent).

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Sets the goal in order to beat the game.

- Complete Skedar Ruins: The game ends after completing Skedar Ruins.
- Complete Missions: Complete missions until you get the set amount of mission stars.
- Complete Challenges: Complete challenges until you get the set amount of challenge stars.
- Complete Both: Complete both missions and challenges until you get the set amount of stars.

options.label: Skedar Ruins Requirements
options.description:
Sets the requirements to unlock Skedar Ruins.
This option only matters if goal is set to Complete Skedar Ruins.

- Item: You can get Skedar Ruins as an item which could make the run shorter.
- Collect Mission Stars: Unlocks after you collect enough mission stars.
- Collect Challenge Stars: Unlocks after you collect enough challenge stars.
- Collect Both Stars: Unlocks after you collect enough mission and challenge stars.

options.label: Place Stars Anywhere
options.description:
Choose if you want mission stars and challenge stars to be placed in any location. 
This option only matters if you need to collect stars for the goal.

- False: Mission stars and challenge stars can only be acquired 
         from completing missions and challenges in your game.

- True: Mission stars and challenge stars can be found in anyone's game.

options.label: Mission Logic
options.description:
Choose how hard the logic will be for the missions. 
This will also affect cheats as they share the same logic.

- Normal: The logic expects you to have the starting weapon in missions.
- Veteran: The logic is the same as Normal but it expects you to use hidden items.
- Hard: The logic expects you to do missions without certain items.
- Perfect: The logic expects you to complete missions with less items than hard.

Note: Hard and Perfect includes the hidden items in logic

options.label: Include Agent
options.description:
Determines whether Agent sends location checks.
You must have one of the difficulties enabled if you have 
to do missions for the goal or Skedar Ruins requirements.

options.label: Required Agent Mission Stars
options.description:
Sets the required amount of Agent mission stars to beat the game.
This option only matters if you have to collect mission stars and Agent is enabled.
If you are playing more than one difficulty, then the number of mission stars 
you must collect for the goal is combined from each enabled difficulty.

The max is 20 if the goal is set to Complete Skedar Ruins.

options.label: Include Special Agent
options.description:
Determines whether Special Agent sends location checks.
You must have one of the difficulties enabled if you have 
to do missions for the goal or Skedar Ruins requirements.

options.label: Required Special Agent Mission Stars
options.description:
Sets the required amount of Special Agent mission stars to beat the game.
This option only matters if you have to collect mission stars and Special Agent is enabled.
If you are playing more than one difficulty, then the number of mission stars 
you must collect for the goal is combined from each enabled difficulty.

The max is 20 if the goal is set to Complete Skedar Ruins.

options.label: Include Perfect Agent
options.description:
Determines whether Perfect Agent sends location checks.
You must have one of the difficulties enabled if you have 
to do missions for the goal or Skedar Ruins requirements.

If Perfect Agent is too difficult, you can use Perfect Dark mode
to lower enemies' health, damage, and accuracy to make it easier.
Note: Lowering enemy health will also lower your ally's health. 
      Keep this in mind when playing missions with allies you need to keep alive.

options.label: Required Perfect Agent Mission Stars
options.description:
Sets the required amount of Perfect Agent mission stars to beat the game.
This option only matters if you have to collect mission stars and Perfect Agent is enabled.
If you are playing more than one difficulty, then the number of mission stars 
you must collect for the goal is combined from each enabled difficulty.

The max is 20 if the goal is set to Complete Skedar Ruins.

options.label: Start with a Mission
options.description: Start with a random mission in your inventory.

options.label: Weapon Progression
options.description:
Choose how weapon progression will work in your game.

- Normal:
    Every weapon, except for the classic weapons, is its own item in the itempool.
    You start a mission with the weapons that you normally would once you unlock them.
    You can only pick up unlocked weapons and use them.
    Pick this for the most vanilla experience.

- All Guns:
    Every weapon in the game is its own item in the itempool.
    Every weapon you unlocked will be in your inventory at the start of a mission.
    This allows you to use weapons in missions they normally don't appear in.

- Progressive Weapon:
    You will progress through weapons from weakest to strongest. 
    Every weapon you progress through will be in your inventory at the start of a mission.
    Some weapons required for mission objectives are in the itempool so that some locations can be done earlier.

- Progressive One Gun:
    You progress through the weapons in the same order, but you will only have
    the current progressive weapon in your inventory at the start of a mission.
    You are given infinite ammo on some weapons and a laser on some missions to prevent softlocks.
    Only recommended for people who are looking for a challenging run.

- Progressive Types:
    This splits the progressive weapon into five types:
    Pistols, SMGs, Rifles, Explosives, and Other.
    Your inventory will only be filled with the current
    progressive weapon for each type at the start of a mission.

options.label: Progressive Weapons In Challenges
options.description:
Allows you to use progressive weapons in challenges.
This option only works if challenges are enabled 
and weapon progression is not set to normal.

- False: You will not have any weapons in your inventory
         and must pick up weapons that you have unlocked.

- True: Your progressive weapons will be in your inventory.

options.label: Start with a Weapon
options.description:
Start with a weapon in your inventory.

- Normal and All Guns: You will start with a random weapon.
- Progressive Weapon and One Gun: You will start with the first progressive weapon.
- Progressive Types: You will start with a random weapon type.

options.label: Master Key
options.description:
Combines any key cards into one item for the mission area.
Any missions that only have one key card will just use that item.
You will still need to pick up the key card in the mission to use it.

options.label: Challenges
options.description:
Adds the combat simulator challenges as checks.
Each challenge is an item you need to find in order to play it.

options.label: Required Challenge Stars
options.description:
Sets the required amount of challenge stars to beat the game.
This option only matters if you are required to collect challenge stars for the goal.

If you exclude any challenges and set the required amount of challenge stars to a number
greater than you can earn, then it automatically sets this to the maximum you can earn.

options.label: Challenge Logic
options.description:
Choose how hard the logic will be for the challenges. 

- Strict: The logic expects you to have every weapon and device in the weapon set.
- Normal: The logic expects you to have some weapons in the weapon set.
- Hard: The logic expects you to have one of the weapons in the weapon set.

options.label: Challenges in Item Pool
options.description:
Adds each challenge to the item pool.
You cannot start a challenge until you find it.
This option only matters if challenges are enabled.
Recommend disabling this if there are not enough locations in your multiworld.

options.label: Excluded Challenges
options.description:
Sets which challenges will not appear in the run,
allowing you to leave out any difficult ones. 
Valid challenges are Challenge 1 through Challenge 30.
Ex: ['Challenge 1', 'Challenge 5', 'Challenge 26']

options.label: Shorter Challenges
options.description: Shortens each challenge's time limit and score limit.

options.label: Weapon Training
options.description:
Adds the 96 firing range medals as checks.
Recommend enabling this if you are doing a solo world.

options.label: Device Training
options.description: Adds the 10 device training as checks.

options.label: Holotraining
options.description:
Adds the 7 holotraining as checks.
Recommend enabling this so you have checks at the start.

options.label: Completion Cheat Unlocks
options.description:
Adds the 17 cheat unlocks that require you to
complete a mission on any difficulty as checks.

options.label: Timed Cheat Unlocks
options.description:
Adds the 17 cheat unlocks that require you to 
complete a mission within a time limit as checks.
Some checks require certain difficulties.

options.label: Weapon Cheat Unlocks
options.description:
Adds the 8 cheat unlocks that require you to
get gold medals in the firing range as checks.

options.label: Cheats in the Item Pool
options.description:
Adds the cheats to the item pool.

- False: Cheats will not be sent to you. They can be unlocked the normal way.
- True: Cheats will be sent to you. They cannot be unlocked the normal way.

options.label: NPCs in the Item Pool
options.description:
Adds important NPCs to the item pool.
They are Carrington, Cassandra, Dr. Caroll, Jonathan, Elvis, and the President.
You will not be able to do certain objectives and some missions if they are missing.

options.label: Multiplayer Unlocks
options.description:
Adds 65 checks for getting the multiplayer unlockables
by completing a number of challenges.
This option only works if you have challenges enabled.

options.label: Alternate Exits
options.description:
Adds checks for the different exits you can take on
G5 Building, A51 Escape, and Air Base in order to complete the mission.
You must have any of the difficulties enabled for this to work.

- Disabled: There will not be a check on any exit.
- One: One of the exits is randomly picked to have a check.
- All: Each exit will have a check.

options.label: Pickupsanity
options.description:
Adds checks for picking up ammo crates, shields, and hidden items in missions.
You must have any of the difficulties enabled for this to work.
Some checks are only in certain difficulties.

options.label: Trap Chance
options.description:
Sets the percentage of filler that is replaced by a trap.
Types of traps:
    - DK Mode Trap: turns on DK Mode
    - Small Jo Trap: turns the player small
    - Small Characters Trap: turns everyone else small
    - Slow Motion Trap: slows down the game
    - Enemy Rockets Trap: gives enemies a Rocket Launcher
    - Perfect Darkness Trap: turns the map dark
    - Fast Animations Trap: makes enemies move fast
    - Skedar Trap: spawns Skedars on the map
    - N-Bomb Trap: spawns an N-Bomb on the player

options.label: Excluded Traps
options.description:
Sets which traps will not appear in the item pool. 
Valid traps are:
    - DK Mode Trap
    - Small Jo Trap
    - Small Characters Trap
    - Slow Motion Trap
    - Enemy Rockets Trap
    - Perfect Darkness Trap
    - Fast Animations Trap
    - Skedar Trap
    - N-Bomb Trap
Ex: ['DK Mode Trap', 'Slow Motion Trap', 'Skedar Trap']

options.label: Death Link
options.description:
Enables death link in your game, making you die at the same time as other players.
You can send and receive death links during single player missions.
You can receive death links in combat simulator but can't send it.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
The completion condition for the slot
One Hard Travel: Your victory condition will be a trip at maximum distance and maximum speed (chosen from the other settings)
Allsanity: Obtain every check
Short MacGuffin: The slot will contain items that are the letters for "Ap-Go!". Collecting all 6 is victory
Long MacGuffin: The slot will contain items that are the letters for "Archipela-Go!". Collecting all 13 is victory

options.label: Number of Checks
options.description:
The number of checks to generate in the world.
Most items in this game are flexible, so the more checks you have, the more of each item you will get, but each will be less powerful.
If you pick a MacGuffin goal, you need at least enough checks to fit the goal items. If not, they will be placed in your start_inventory

options.label: Minimum Distance
options.description:
The minimum distance in meters you will be expected to go to for a check.
Keep in mind that you might have to travel twice that to come back home afterwards.
Even Distance reduction items will not make distances cross this threshold

options.label: Maximum Distance
options.description:
The maximum distance in meters you will be expected to go to for a check.
Keep in mind that you might have to travel twice that to come back home afterwards.
Some checks can appear outside of this range at first, but will only be in-logic after distance has been reduced below this threshold
The generator does not know in advance about hills in your area, so make sure you consider them in your distance commitment

options.label: Speed Requirement
options.description:
[Not currently implemented]
Every check will generate a random minimum speed in km/h you must travel at in order to be allowed to get it.
This setting will be an upper bound for this speed requirement. The lower bound will scale with the choice as well.
If you reach the check too slowly, you will need to go back home and try again.
The generator does not know in advance about hills in your area, so make sure you consider them in your speed commitment.

options.label: NumberOfLocks
options.description:
This will place "keys" in the item pools, and some checks will start out locked behind a random number of keys
If there are not enough checks to hold all the keys you need, this option will be reduced by force

options.label: Enable Distance Reductions
options.description:
[Not currently implemented in the app]
Whether some checks will spawn further than the maximum distance, and distance reduction items are in the pool

options.label: Enable Scouting Distance Bonuses
options.description:
[Not currently implemented]
Whether the item pool can contain permanent bonuses to scouting distance

options.label: Enable Collection Distance Bonuses
options.description:
[Not currently implemented]
Whether the item pool can contain permanent bonuses to collection distance

options.label: Trap Rate
options.description: What percentage of the remaining item pool should be traps. Some traps may be honor-system based and rely on the player to execute them

options.label: Deathlink
options.description: Link all player deaths together. If you die, all other players in the session (with Deathlink enabled) also die. This works the same the other way around.

options.label: Open Springleaf Path
options.description:
Remove Demon Strings and Wind Barriers in Springleaf Path to enable entering other areas before getting Awakened Sacred Leaf/Sacred Anemone.
Other areas with Demon Strings will still require Awakened Sacred Leaf to open them.

options.label: Bell Hover Generation
options.description:
Consider Bell Hover as a possible strat for world generation.
Bell Hover is done by using the Healing Bell (at most 3 times) when reaching the peak of a jump to gain extra height.
This strat is used to access certain areas without having the correct skill (i.e. Demon Frontier without Wall Jump)

options.label: Lunar Crystal Branch Shuffle
options.description: Add the Lunar Crystal Branches (the white things that give you money when destroyed) as item location checks.

options.label: Randomize Key items
options.description:
Add Key Items needed for progression to the randomization pool and as location checks.
These items are: Gold Moonlit Dust, Silver Moonlit Dust and Windmill Key.

options.label: Add Oracle Sigil
options.description:
Add the Oracle Sigil to the item pool and as a location check.
The Oracle location check requires to free all 30 Lumen Fairies.

options.label: Berrysanity
options.description: Add all berry types as item location checks, as well as adding progressive health, magic, stamina and black berry upgrades to the itempool.

options.label: Lilysanity
options.description: Add the Heavenly Lilies as item location checks, as well as adding progressive damage upgrade to the itempool.

options.label: Fairysanity
options.description:
Add the Lumen Fairies as item location checks, as well as adding progressive Lumen Fairies to the itempool
You need a total of 30 Lumen Fairies to unlock the Oracle Sigil item or location check.

options.label: Companionsanity
options.description:
Add Companions to the item pool and as item location checks.
Note: Dora and Lineth companions are not locations checks or part of the itempool (coding jank).

options.label: Progressive Selin Door Keys
options.description:
Add 4 progressive keys required to open the door to the Selin boss fight to the randomization pool. 
With this enabled, it's not required to defeat all four of Selin's Shades to unlock the door.

options.label: Victory Condition
options.description: Choose which boss must be defeated to be considered as having completed the game.

options.label: Include Iron Rig DLC
options.description: Include the Iron Rig DLC (Iron Rig DLC required for this)

options.label: Include Pale Reach DLC
options.description: Include the Pale Reach DLC (Pale Reach DLC required for this)

options.label: Require Boat Performance
options.description:
Set logic to require a fast enough, well lit boat to reach further areas, counting only engines and lights that
fit in the hull together.

Gale Cliffs, Stellar Basin, Twisted Strand and Devil's Spine: 50 knots and 1800 lumens
Open Ocean dredging, fishing and pickups, and the Iron Rig: 50 knots and 2100 lumens
The Pale Reach: 60 knots and 2100 lumens

options.label: Logical Nets
options.description:
If enabled, logic may expect players to use nets as the only method of catching fish that are also catchable with a
rod. This includes passive net catches in specific regions.

If disabled, logic will only consider rod-based access for such fish, ensuring checks are reachable through active
fishing.

Recommended: disabled for players who prefer reliable, targeted fishing.

options.label: Include Aberrations
options.description: If enabled, checks for fish aberrations may contain progression items.

options.label: Add Fishing Licenses
options.description: If enabled, adds a required item to be able to catch each region's fish.

options.label: Add Passage Items
options.description:
If enabled, adds required items to be able to traverse each zone.
The Windward Litany = Gale Cliffs
The Astral Testament = Stellar Basin
The Mangrove Canticle = Twisted Strand
The Cinder Gospel = Devil's Spine
The Pelagic Psalm = Open Ocean
The Rimebound Chronicle = Pale Reach

options.label: Include Messages in Bottles
options.description: If enabled, picking up each of the 10 messages in a bottle is a check.

options.label: Include Research Checks
options.description:
If enabled, researching each piece of equipment at the research station is a check. Research costs nothing in an
AP save, so these are free checks once the research tree lets you reach them. Research Parts are never in the pool.

options.label: Progressive Aberration Chance Items
options.description:
How many Progressive Aberration Chance items to add. Each raises the minimum chance of catching an aberration by
an equal share, so having all of them makes every catch an aberration. 0 adds none.

Logic expects at least half of them (or the Guaranteed Aberrations item) before any aberration, or anything that
needs one, is in logic. With neither item in the pool, aberrations are left to the normal chance.

The boost can be switched off in game with "ap aberrations off" or in the mod settings.

options.label: Guaranteed Aberrations Item
options.description:
Adds a Guaranteed Aberrations item that makes every catch an aberration as soon as it's received.
Once received, every aberration is in logic.

The boost can be switched off in game with "ap aberrations off" or in the mod settings.

options.label: Trap Percentage
options.description: The percentage of filler items replaced with traps. 0 adds no traps.

options.label: Enabled Traps
options.description:
Which traps can replace filler.

Damaging Event Trap: a monster that can damage your boat appears
Scary Event Trap: something unsettling but harmless happens
Money Loss Trap: lose 10% of your money
Teleport Trap: get pulled back to where the Manifest ability takes you
Panic Trap: your panic rises sharply
Hull Damage Trap: your boat takes a hit
Engine Damage Trap: an engine takes damage
Nightfall Trap: time skips ahead to nightfall
Rot Trap: a fish in your cargo rots
Slow Trap: your boat slows down for a short while
Lights Out Trap: your lights go out for a short while
Cargo Scramble Trap: your cargo gets rearranged
Reverse Controls Trap: your steering and throttle are reversed for a short while

options.label: Death Link
options.description: Enables deathlink

options.label: More Slugcats Expansion?
options.description: Whether More Slugcats Expansion (Downpour) is enabled, regardless of which campaign you plan to play.

options.label: The Watcher?
options.description: Whether The Watcher is enabled, regardless of which campaign you plan to play.

options.label: Campaign
options.description: Which slugcat's campaign you will play.

options.label: Passage progress without Survivor
options.description:
How The Survivor affects earning other passages.

**Disabled**: Only The Martyr, The Mother, and The Pilgrim can be earned before The Survivor.

**Enabled**: The Dragon Slayer, The Friend, and The Wanderer can additionally be earned before The Survivor.

**Bypassed**: Every passage can be earned before The Survivor.

This will override the actual value of the corresponding setting in the Rain World Remix menu.

options.label: Victory condition
options.description:
What the victory condition should be.
**Ascension** is the default, and **Story** is the slugcat specific ending.
**Echoes** requires meeting enough Echoes to satisfy the Pilgrim passage.
**Food Quest** requires eating every edible food in order to fill out the tracker.
This includes expanded food quest, if it is enabled.

The **Story** victory condition depends on the selected gamestate:

**Vanilla**, **Saint**, or **Sofanthiel**: No alternate.

**Monk** and **Survivor**: Reach Journey's End in Outer Expanse.

**Hunter**: Use the green neuron on Looks to the Moon in Shoreline.

**Gourmand**: Receive the Mark in order to reach Outer Expanse, and subsequently reach Journey's End.

**Artificer**: Receive the Mark and the Citizen ID drone in order to reach Metropolis and kill the Chieftain Scavenger.

**Rivulet**: Receive the Rarefaction Cell and deliver it to Submerged Superstructure,
then meet Looks to the Moon.

**Spearmaster**: Receive the SM pearl and Moon's message, then deliver it to Communications Array in Sky Islands.

When playing as the Watcher, these options are different:
**Ascension** / **Spinning Top**: Complete the Spinning Top ending.
**Story** / **Prince**: Complete the Prince ending.
**Echoes** / **Weaver**: Complete the Weaver ending.
**True Ending**: Complete the True ending. If this is chosen on a non-Watcher slugcat, it will be interpreted as ascension.

options.label: Gate behavior
options.description:
**Key only**: A key for each accessible gate is placed into the pool.
These keys are required to use karma gates, and karma is not.

**Key and Karma**: Keys are required *and* gates have karma requirements.

**Key or Karma**: Either keys or karma are sufficient to use a gate.

**Karma only**: Unrandomized behavior.  Keys are not placed into the pool.

Gates will have Monk-style behavior if you choose a setting other than **Key only**.

options.label: Sparse Gates
options.description:
When enabled, the world will only generate exactly as many gates / warps needed to reach every region.
Only applies when Gate Behavior is set to require keys.

options.label: Randomize Starting Region
options.description:
Whether the starting region should be randomized.

**Default Start**: Do not randomize the starting region.

**Weighted Choice**: Refer to "Possible Starting Regions" option to decide what starting regions can be chosen.

**Any Valid**: The starting region is chosen among every accessible region in the selected game state.

options.label: Debug Output
options.description: Whether to log extra information about the world and slot for debugging.

options.label: The Monk difficulty
options.description:
The number of different types of non-meats that must be available before The Monk can be logically required.
Higher numbers are easier.

options.label: The Hunter difficulty
options.description:
The number of different types of meats that must be available before The Hunter can be logically required.
Higher numbers are easier.

options.label: The Outlaw difficulty
options.description:
The number of different types of creatures that must be available before The Outlaw can be logically required.
Higher numbers are easier.

options.label: The Nomad difficulty
options.description:
The number of regions that must be accessible before The Nomad can be logically required.
Higher numbers are easier.

options.label: The Chieftain requires toll
options.description:
Whether a Scavenger toll must be accessible before The Chieftain can be logically required.
If disabled, Chieftain becomes accessible whenever any Scavengers are accessible.

options.label: Glow required for dark places
options.description:
Whether the neuron glow is logically required for Shaded Citadel,
parts of lower Pipeyard, and Filtration System.

options.label: Extreme threats
options.description:
Whether eliminating an extreme threat could be required (such as for a food quest check).
This includes Daddy Long Legs (and variants), Red Lizards, King Vultures, Miros Vultures,
Miros Birds, Aquapedes, and Red Centipedes.

options.label: Late Submerged
options.description:
Changes the logical requirement for entering Submerged Superstructure.

If off, Submerged has no additional requirement to enter.

If set to aquatic, access to Submerged will expect you to have longer breath time from the Aquatic perk
or to be playing as Rivulet. If the Aquatic perk is not in the item pool, this acts the same as "off".

If set to longer cycles, Rivulet will not be expected to enter Submerged until the Longer Cycles item is obtained.

options.label: Low-karma echo appearance
options.description:
How echo apperances work below 5 max karma.
Does not affect the echoes in Subterranean and The Exterior, which can always be visited.

**Unaltered**: Vanilla behavior.  Artificer needs a karma flower and other slugcats do not.

**Never**: Echoes cannot appear below 5 karma.

**With Karma Flower**: Echoes may appear below 5 karma
if karma flower reinforcement is active and current karma equals max karma.
This is the normal behavior for Artificer.

**Without Karma Flower**: Echoes may appear if current karma equals max karma.

options.label: Expedition Perks
options.description:
Choose which Expedition perks will be added to the item pool.
If an ability in this list is given to a slugcat that innately has it, there is no effect.
Requires MSC.

Valid Perks: Back Spear Perk, Dual Wielding Perk, Blast Resistance Perk, Explosive Parry Perk,
Explosive Jump Perk, Crafting Perk, Aquatic Perk, Agility Perk

options.label: Trap percentage
options.description: The percentage of filler items that will be traps.  Set to 0 to remove traps entirely.

options.label: Filler weight jitter
options.description:
Each non-zero filler weight receives a random number, up to this jitter value, added to it.
The lower the setting, the less likely it is that items with small weights appear in the pool at all.
The higher the setting, the lower the influence of the item weights altogether.

options.label: Extra karma cap increases
options.description:
Number of extra karma cap increases in the pool beyond the minimum required for ascension.
For Watcher, this option will also apply to Ripple.

options.label: Spear damage increases
options.description:
Add an amount of items to the pool that permanently increase the damage of thrown spears.
Each progressive upgrade adds 10% damage on top of the slugcat's base damage.

options.label: Broadcasts
options.description: Which slugcats broadcasts should be available to.  Requires MSC.

options.label: Food quest
options.description: Which slugcats the food quest should be available to.  Requires MSC.

options.label: Expanded food quest
options.description:
Whether the food quest should be expanded to include most creatures.
Specific food quest checks may be disabled by excluding the locations,
and some slugcats will not be required to kill and eat extreme threats if that setting is enabled.
Requires MSC.

options.label: Priority Passages
options.description:
Number of Passages that are randomly marked as priority checks,
increasing the chance that they will contain progression items.
These are in addition to any manually-prioritized Passages,
and will not override any manually-excluded Passages.

options.label: All tokens and pearls
options.description: Whether all tokens and pearls should be visible to all slugcats.

options.label: Sheltersanity
options.description: Whether each shelter is a check.

options.label: Include Submerged
options.description:
Whether Submerged Superstructure has any checks.
If only aquatic is chosen, checks will only be generated
if playing Rivulet or the Aquatic perk is in the item pool.

options.label: Karma Flowers
options.description: Whether each static karma flower spawn is a check.

options.label: Dev tokens
options.description: Whether dev commentary tokens should be checks.  Requires MSC.

options.label: Permarotted accessibility
options.description:
Controls the generation of Crumbling Fringes, Corrupted Factories, Decaying Tunnels, and Infested Wastes.

**None**: There will be no checks in rotted vanilla regions, and bad warping will not be required to reach Outer Rim.

**Passthrough**: There will be no checks in rotted vanilla regions, but you may still have to bad warp to reach Outer Rim.

**Full**: Checks will be present in rotted vanilla regions

options.label: Min Ripple target
options.description:
The lowest that your *minimum* Ripple can be before Ripplespace is logically accessible.
The default, 5, matches the actual game behavior.

options.label: Rotted region target
options.description:
The number of regions that must be rotted for the Rot ending.
The default, 21, matches the unaltered game behavior.

options.label: Randomize Weaver ability
options.description:
Adds 4 progressive Weaver ability items to the item pool instead of gaining the ability naturally through Weaver encounters.
For related ending only, the endings in question are Weaver or True Ending.
The Weaver cannot be randomized if the Prince ending is chosen.

options.label: Rot spread checks
options.description:
Whether spreading the Rot to new regions are checks.
This option will be force-disabled if "Randomize Weaver Ability" is set to true, or Weaver / True Ending is chosen.
For related ending only, the ending in question is the Prince ending.

options.label: Weaver encounter checks
options.description:
Whether each of the 4 Weaver encounters are checks.
This is separate from whether the ability itself is randomized.
For related ending only, the endings in question are Weaver or True Ending.

options.label: Spinning Top keys
options.description: Whether keys are required to travel through Spinning Top warps.

options.label: Daemon keys
options.description: Whether keys are required to travel through Daemon warps.

options.label: Priority Throne
options.description: Whether Prince checks should be normal, priority, or excluded locations.

options.label: Use Watcher Passages
options.description:
Whether passage tokens will be added to the item pool when playing as Watcher.
You will need the mod "Watcher Region Art" enabled in order to use passage tokens in-game.
The mod can be found on the Steam workshop: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3660768308
