options.label: Bunny Hopping
options.description: Locations which require preservation of momentum through bunny hopping will be considered in logic

options.label: Hard Combat
options.description: Locations which require more proficiency in combat to access will be considered in logic

options.label: Shop Item Cost Discount
options.description: Discount percentage to apply to shop prices to reduce money farming requirement. 0 is normal price, 50 is half price

options.label: Starting Weapon
options.description: Weapon you start with.

options.label: Characters
options.description:
Enter the list of characters to play as.  Valid characters are:
'Ironclad'
'Silent'
'Defect'
'Regent'
'Necrobinder'

options.label: Modded Characters
options.description:
Modded characters to include when Advanced Characters is disabled. Enter each character's
internal ID or a predefined display name, such as Watcher, Guardian, or Tectonic.
The list of predefined display names will probably be pinned somewhere on Discord.
At most 20 modded characters can be present in the generated character set.
Duplicate aliases and IDs are removed, keeping the first occurrence. Predefined characters use their
display names; other selected characters are numbered consecutively in YAML order.
A larger candidate list is allowed when Pick Number of Characters selects a subset.

If using a modded character:
Predefined display names and internal IDs are matched case-insensitively.
Unrecognised characters still require their full internal ID.

If you don't know the exact ID to enter with the mod installed go to
`Archipelago Settings -> Archipelago` to view a list of installed modded character IDs.

Every configured character must be installed with the matching internal ID. The client
rejects the AP connection if a configured character cannot be loaded.

options.label: Lock Characters
options.description:
Whether characters must be unlocked by "Unlock [Char]" items in a multi-character run.
unlocked makes every character available from the start.
locked_random starts you with one random character; the others are unlock items.
locked_fixed starts you with unlocked_character; the others are unlock items.

options.label: Unlocked Character
options.description:
Which character you start with when lock_characters is set to locked_fixed.
It must be one of your configured characters, and is always kept when Pick Number of
Characters selects a subset. Leave it empty ("") to start with a random character.
Can also enter a predefined display name or full internal ID for modded characters.
The list of predefined display names will probably be pinned somewhere on Discord.

options.label: Ascension
options.description:
Logic assumes Ascension 1 is enabled for relic checks. A single number N enables Ascensions 1 through N.
When multiple values are supplied, each number enables only that numbered Ascension. You can also provide
names which are shown below. Names are case-sensitive.

 The ascension names are as follows:
 - 'SwarmingElites'
 - 'WearyTraveler'
 - 'Poverty'
 - 'TightBelt'
 - 'AscendersBane'
 - 'Inflation'
 - 'Scarcity'
 - 'ToughEnemies'
 - 'DeadlyEnemies'
 - 'DoubleBoss'

options.label: Ascension Down
options.description:
Ascension Down items to add for each character.
Only enabled Ascensions can receive a corresponding Ascension Down.

A single number N selects the highest N enabled Ascensions. When multiple values are supplied, each
number selects only that numbered Ascension. Names are case-sensitive.
Supports both numbers and names.

- 'SwarmingElites'
- 'WearyTraveler'
- 'Poverty'
- 'TightBelt'
- 'AscendersBane'
- 'Inflation'
- 'Scarcity'
- 'ToughEnemies'
- 'DeadlyEnemies'
- 'DoubleBoss'

Logic does not account for receiving these items.

options.label: Use New Logic
options.description:
Use the new logic. Disable to use the previous 1.1.X and below logic.
New logic allows more random item order—for example, Extra relics and cards can help supplement missing ancients or rests.
One example is that old logic required your progressive starter card+relic to beat your 1st elite but new logic
no longer requires this as 'Power' can be made up with extra cards/relics. Similar cases for ancients/smiths/rests.

Old logic is used automatically (regardless of this option) when floor, gold, and potion checks
 are all disabled to reduce failed generations.

options.label: Ancient Relic Location
options.description:
Controls when Progressive Ancient relic choices are offered.

Start Of Act presents them through the normal Ancient encounter. Anytime presents
them as linked choices in the Archipelago reward menu as soon as they are received.

options.label: Ancient Relic Pool
options.description:
Controls which Ancient relics can appear in each three-choice reward.

Balanced uses the natural Ancient rolled for that act. Chaos can use relics from
any Ancient in the appropriate act. True Chaos combines the Act 2 and Act 3 pools for the
Act 2 and Act 3 Progressive Ancient rewards. Neow's reward always uses Neow's Act 1 pool.

options.label: Relic Rewards Available Anytime
options.description:
How many AP Relic items can be claimed via the AP Menu without fighting elites or visiting chests.
Later AP Relic Items can only be 'claimed' by beating Elites or opening treasure chests.
i.e. A value of 2 here and receiving 3 relics from AP means you get 2 relics in your AP menu and the 3rd 
requires beating one elite or visiting one chest. 
tldr; fight elites and go to chests to get more relics. Lower value = elites matter more so don't skip them

options.label: Progressive Starter Card
options.description:
Enables progressive special starter cards by default for every configured character.
Advanced Characters can override this per character with progressive_starter_card.

Requires Include Floor Checks. Each character gets two Progressive Starter Card items, which
replace two floor-check filler items. With none received, the character
starts without the special starter card that Archaic Tooth would transform (Bash, Neutralize, a compatible modded equivalent etc).
The first item restores the normal card; the second applies its Archaic Tooth transformation.

Characters without an Archaic Tooth transformation are left unchanged, although their two
Progressive Starter Card items are still present in the multiworld.

WARNING: This can make the early game significantly harder for some characters.

options.label: Progressive Starter Relic
options.description:
Enables progressive starter relics by default for every configured character.
Advanced Characters can override this per character with progressive_starter_relic.

Requires Include Floor Checks. Each character gets two Progressive Starter Relic items, which
replace two floor-check filler items. With none received, the character
starts without the starter relic that Touch of Orobas would refine (such as Burning Blood, or a
compatible modded equivalent).

The first item restores the normal relic; the second applies its Touch of Orobas refinement.

Characters without a Touch of Orobas refinement are left unchanged, although their two
Progressive Starter Relic items are still present in the multiworld.

WARNING: This can make the early game significantly harder for characters whose starting relic
is central to their early power.

options.label: Shuffle All Card Rewards
options.description: Whether every card reward is shuffled.  If false, then every other card reward is shuffled

options.label: Bonus Items
options.description:
Add a number of Bonus Items to the item pool.
These items make the game easier to complete, and are not accounted for in logic.

Each ordered entry creates one character-agnostic bonus item and must provide either
a non-empty list of value Pools or one specific Value. For example:

    bonus_items:
        - WAX_RELIC:
            Pools: [Common, Uncommon]
        - WAX_RELIC:
            Value: Orichalcum


Generation fails if more bonus items are configured than there are filler slots.

It's HIGHLY recommended to use the YAML Builder on our website to easily generate this option, which you can find at https://sts2ap.net

options.label: Include Floor Checks
options.description:
Add locations for reaching new floors and fill the corresponding item-pool space with
configurable filler. Ascension Down and Progressive Starter options require these locations.

options.label: Neow Sanity
options.description:
Adds Neow's starting Ancient Relic as a Progressive Ancient reward.

With Anytime mode, Neow's relic choices appear in the Archipelago reward menu.

options.label: Campfire Sanity
options.description:
Whether to shuffle being able to rest and smith at each campsite per act.  Also adds
new locations at campsites per act.

options.label: Gold Sanity
options.description: Whether to replace combat, elite, and boss gold rewards with AP locations. Adds 22 locations per character.

options.label: Potion Sanity
options.description: Whether to replace potion rewards with AP locations. Adds 9 locations per character.

options.label: Shop Sanity
options.description:
Move the configured shop slots to a separate AP shop page as purchasable location checks and
shuffle items that progressively restore the corresponding slots on the normal shop page.

options.label: Shop Card Slots
options.description: When shop_sanity is enabled, the number of colored card slots to shuffle.

options.label: Shop Neutral Card Slots
options.description: When shop_sanity is enabled, the number of neutral card slots to shuffle.

options.label: Shop Relic Slots
options.description: When shop_sanity is enabled, the number of relic slots to shuffle.

options.label: Shop Potion Slots
options.description: When shop_sanity is enabled, the number of potion slots to shuffle

options.label: Shop Remove Slots
options.description:
When shop_sanity is enabled, whether to shuffle the ability to remove cards at the shop.
Progressive based on Act; i.e. you'll gain the ability to remove cards per Act, starting from Act 1.
Act 4 will be treated as Act 3.

options.label: Shop Sanity Costs
options.description:
Controls the price paid for location checks on the AP shop page. Normal shop-item prices are
unaffected. Tiered modes first calculate a vanilla-style baseline for the AP card, relic, or potion.

Fixed: 15 gold per AP check.
Super Discount Tiered: 20 percent of the calculated baseline.
Discount Tiered: 50 percent of the calculated baseline.
Tiered: the full calculated baseline.

Generation logic does not account for these prices.

options.label: Death Link
options.description:
Share deaths with other Death Link players. Dying sends a Death Link. Receiving one while in
a run damages the current character by Death Link Damage Percent of maximum health and can add a
Death Fragment if the character survives. Local client settings can override these slot settings.

options.label: Enable Death Fragments
Death Link Damage Percent
options.description:
If Death Link is enabled, this setting determines how much damage you take when you receive a Death Link, 
as a percentage of your max health. 
If you do not want to take any damage, set this to 0. 
If you want to be killed whenever you receive a Death Link, set this to 100.

options.label: Release Checks On Victory
options.description: Release the winning character's remaining checks when their goal is recorded.

options.label: Seeded Run
options.description: Whether each character should have a fixed seed to climb the spire with or not.

options.label: Advanced Characters
options.description:
Whether to use the advanced characters feature. The normal options for character, ascension, etc. are ignored.
Global progressive starter options remain defaults unless overridden for a character.
See the "advanced_characters" option.

options.label: Advanced Characters
options.description:
The configuration for advanced characters.  Each character's options can be configured
independently of each other.  No validation is done on the character name, so use carefully.
Format is:
    <char name>:
        ascension:
            - <string or number>
        ascension_down:
            - <string or number>
        progressive_starter_card: <true or false>
        progressive_starter_relic: <true or false>

Omitted progressive starter options inherit their global settings. Explicit true/false
values override them for that character. Both still require Include Floor Checks.

If using a modded character:
Enter its full internal ID or a predefined display name, such as Watcher.
The list of predefined display names will probably be pinned somewhere on Discord.
Do not include both an alias and its full ID as separate entries.

If you don't know the exact ID to enter with the mod installed go to
`Archipelago Settings -> Archipelago` to view a list of installed modded character IDs.

Every configured character must be installed with the matching internal ID. The client
rejects the AP connection if a configured character cannot be loaded.

options.label: One Gold Filler Weight
options.description:
Weight for One Gold filler items. Grants one gold to its associated character. If every filler weight is None, the generator
uses that character's One Gold as the required safe fallback.

options.label: Five Gold Filler Weight
options.description: Weight for Five Gold filler items. Grants five gold to its associated character.

options.label: Free Attack Filler Weight
options.description: Weight for Free Attack filler items. At the start of the next player combat turn, makes the next Attack played cost zero energy.

options.label: Free Power Filler Weight
options.description: Weight for Free Power filler items. At the start of the next player combat turn, makes the next Power played cost zero energy.

options.label: Free Skill Filler Weight
options.description: Weight for Free Skill filler items. At the start of the next player combat turn, makes the next Skill played cost zero energy.

options.label: Vigor Filler Weight
options.description: Weight for Vigor filler items. Applies Vigor at the start of the next player combat turn.

options.label: Artifact Filler Weight
options.description: Weight for Artifact filler items. Applies Artifact at the start of the next player combat turn.

options.label: Thorns Filler Weight
options.description: Weight for Thorns filler items. Applies Thorns at the start of the next player combat turn.

options.label: Buffer Filler Weight
options.description: Weight for Buffer filler items. Applies Buffer at the start of the next player combat turn.

options.label: Dexterity Filler Weight
options.description: Weight for Dexterity filler items. Applies Dexterity at the start of the next player combat turn.

options.label: Strength Filler Weight
options.description: Weight for Strength filler items. Applies Strength at the start of the next player combat turn.

options.label: Plating Filler Weight
options.description: Weight for Plating filler items. Applies Plating at the start of the next player combat turn.

options.label: Friendship Filler Weight
options.description: Weight for Friendship filler items. Applies Friendship at the start of the next player combat turn, raising maximum energy by one.

options.label: Post-Combat Card Upgrade Filler Weight
options.description: Weight for Post-Combat Card Upgrade filler items. At the start of the next player combat turn, applies a buff that upgrades a random deck card after combat.

options.label: Post-Combat Card Removal Filler Weight
options.description: Weight for Post-Combat Card Removal filler items. At the start of the next player combat turn, applies a buff that lets you remove a deck card after combat.

options.label: Additional Card Reward Filler Weight
options.description: Weight for Additional Card Reward filler items. At the start of the next player combat turn, applies a buff that adds a card reward after combat.

options.label: Trap Chance
options.description: Chance for filler item to be replaced by a trap.

options.label: Weak Trap Weight
options.description: Applies 1 Weak, reducing damage dealt by the player for 1 turn.

options.label: Frail Trap Weight
options.description: Applies 1 Frail, reducing Block gained for one turn.

options.label: Vulnerable Trap Weight
options.description: Applies 1 Vulnerable, increasing attack damage taken for one turn.

options.label: No Draw Trap Weight
options.description: Blocks extra card draws for the turn

options.label: Tangled Trap Weight
options.description: Attack cards cost 1 more energy for the turn.

options.label: Vakuu Trap Weight
options.description: Vakuu plays your hand on one additional turn, no earlier than turn two.

options.label: Confused Trap Weight
options.description: Randomizes card energy costs when drawn for the rest of combat.

options.label: Sloth Trap Weight
options.description: Applies a six-card limit per turn for the rest of combat.

options.label: Dazed Trap Weight
options.description: Shuffles two Dazed into your combat draw pile.

worlds.game: Age Of Empires II: Definitive Edition

options.label: Scenario Branching
Shuffle Buildings
options.description:
Determines which buildings to shuffle.
Economy: Shuffle houses, TC, market, resource buildings, farms. Includes dock.
Tech: Shuffle blacksmith, university, monastery.
Military: Shuffle military buildings. Includes dock and castle.
Defense: Shuffle defensive buildings. Includes castle.
Unique: Shuffle unique buildings, if applicable civilizations are in the pool. Other options apply to these buildings, e.g. if economy isn't shuffled, neither is folwark.
Wonder: The wonder, the wonder, the... NO!

options.label: Enabled Campaigns
options.description: Determines which vanilla campaigns will be unlocked for the player.

options.label: Enabled Campaigns
options.description: Determines which vanilla campaigns will start unlocked for the player.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Goal for this playthrough.
Win Selected Campaigns: Finish each campaign selected for victory.

options.label: Dexsanity
options.description:
If enabled, each Pokemon has its own location check ('Guess {Pokemon}').
Access is gated by whichever lock options are active (Type Keys, Region Passes,
Route Keys, Line Unlocks, Gym Badges, etc.).
Disabling removes all per-Pokemon locations, leaving only milestone-based checks.
Automatically enabled when Route Locks or Line Locks is on.

options.label: Enable Type Locks
options.description:
If enabled, guessing a Pokemon requires all Type Keys matching its elemental types
(e.g. Bulbasaur needs both Grass Type Key and Poison Type Key).

Generation cost: adds one progression item per active type (up to 18).
Pokemon of a type can only be caught with that Type Key, so most Type Keys
must go in non-type-gated locations (starting slots + "Guessed N" milestones
+ dexsanity "Guess X" locations). Disabling Dexsanity removes the per-Pokemon
locations and can squeeze Type Key placement on small regions -- see the
Hisui-only case in the backlog history and the Line Locks perf note below.

options.label: Region Locks
options.description:
If enabled, non-starting regions require a Region Pass item to access.
Disabling this makes all selected regions freely accessible from the start.

options.label: Regions
options.description:
Which game regions to include. Each region adds its Pokemon to the pool.

Provide a YAML list of region names, for example:
    regions:
      - Kanto
      - Johto
      - Hoenn
(Inline form also works: regions: [Kanto, Johto, Hoenn].)

At least one region is always active (defaults to Kanto if the list is empty).
This manual list is honored by default. It is ONLY ignored if you set
'random_region_count' to a non-zero value, which randomizes the regions instead.
Valid regions: Kanto, Johto, Hoenn, Sinnoh, Unova, Kalos, Alola, Galar, Hisui, Paldea.

KNOWN CORNER, Hisui on its own: Hisui has only 7 Pokemon, where every other region has
72 or more. It supplies roughly 37 locations and nearly all of them sit behind the very
keys that need placing. So 'regions: [Hisui]' with nothing else AND two or more lock
options (type + line + route + legendary + badge + the category locks) is rejected at
the start of generation with a clear error naming the fix, instead of dying mid-fill
with a cryptic 'FillError: No more spots to place N items'. The world never silently
disables a lock you chose. The fix is to add a second region (Galar is the natural
partner for Hisui) or to turn some lock options off. Random selection will never hand
you a lone Hisui by accident, so you only reach this by asking for it here. Hisui
together with any other region is perfectly safe.

options.label: Random Region Count
options.description:
Override the manual Regions list with a random selection.
Set to 0 (or disabled) to use the manual Regions list above (THIS IS THE DEFAULT,
so your 'regions:' list is honored unless you change this).
Set to 1-10 to ignore the manual list and randomly pick that many regions
(or generations if grouping is on).
Set to random to also randomize how many are picked.
When 'Group Hisui & Galar' is enabled, this picks from 9 generation units
(Gen 8 = Galar + Hisui together) instead of 10 individual regions.
One guard rail: when the roll comes out to a single unit, regions with fewer than 20
Pokemon are left out of that draw, because a lone 7-Pokemon Hisui cannot hold a heavy
lock stack's keys and would crash generation. Hisui stays fully available in every roll
of two or more regions, and your lock choices are never touched. If you actually want a
solo micro-region, ask for it directly with the manual 'regions' list; note that a solo
micro-region combined with two or more lock options is rejected at generation start
(see the Regions option's known-corner note).

options.label: Group Hisui & Galar
options.description:
When enabled, Galar and Hisui are treated as a single 'Gen 8' unit
for random region selection. Picking Gen 8 always includes both regions.
When disabled, Galar and Hisui are independent picks.
Only affects random_region_count; the manual Regions list is unaffected.
Leaving this on is the friendliest setting for Hisui, since it guarantees Hisui always
arrives with Galar's 89 Pokemon behind it. With it off, Hisui can still be rolled in any
multi-region set; it just can never be rolled as the only region (see
'random_region_count').

options.label: Starter Region
options.description:
Which game region your adventure starts in.
Determines which Pokemon starters are available and which Type Keys begin pre-collected.
'any': a random active region is chosen each seed.
Specific region: must also be included in the Regions option.
If the chosen region is not active, falls back to a random active region.

options.label: Starter Pokemon
options.description:
Which starter Pokemon to begin with.
'any': a random starter from the starting region's list.
'first'/'second'/'third': by position in the starting region's list.
'random_starter': picks randomly from ALL regional starters across active regions.
'random_any': picks from ALL active base-form Pokemon (fully random).
Starter Count controls how many starters are chosen (1-3) for random modes.

options.label: Starter Count
options.description:
How many starter Pokemon to begin with (1-3).
Each starter pre-collects its Type Keys, Route Key, Line Unlock, and
Region Pass (if the starter is in a non-starting region).
More starters = more open early game with wider type/route/line coverage.
Only used when Starter Pokemon is set to 'random_starter' or 'random_any'.

options.label: Prefer Lab Starters
options.description:
When Starter Pokemon is 'random', prefer traditional starters
(Bulbasaur, Charmander, Squirtle, Chikorita, etc.) over wild Pokemon.
Gives a 5x weight to Professor's Lab Pokemon in the random selection.

options.label: Starting Location Count
options.description:
Number of free 'Oak's Lab' starting locations to include (0-8).
These are immediately accessible checks (Oak's Parcel Delivery, Pokedex Received, etc.)
that kickstart your adventure. Set to 0 to disable them entirely.

options.label: Route Locks
options.description:
Require Route Key items to access Pokemon by game area.
Routes are grouped into meaningful areas (e.g. Melemele Island, Wild Area
North, Hoenn Early Routes). Each area adds one Route Key to the item pool.
A Pokemon is accessible if you have ANY area key for a route it appears on.
Forces Dexsanity ON if it isn't already (needed for enough locations to
hold all Route Keys); a logging.warning fires when that mutation happens.
Route Locks and Line Locks compose independently and no longer auto-disable
each other -- the two gating axes are orthogonal (they gate by different
things: where a Pokemon is found vs. its evolution family).

YAML key: route_locks_enabled (NOT route_locks). The dataclass attribute
in PokepelagoOptions uses the _enabled suffix; AP silently ignores unknown
keys, so a YAML with `route_locks: true` will generate with this option
set to its default (0) and the setting will appear to have no effect.

options.label: Line Locks
options.description:
Require a Line Unlock item for each evolution family.
Every active evolution family adds one Line Unlock to the item pool.
Required for ALL members of the family (base forms and evolutions).
Evolution-only Pokemon inherit route access from their base form.
Forces Dexsanity ON if it isn't already (needed for enough locations to
hold all Line Unlocks); a logging.warning fires when that mutation happens.
Composes independently with Route Locks (no longer auto-disabled when
Route Locks is also on). When the active region pool is too small for
the number of progression items Line Locks would create, generation only
*warns* about the estimated progression-to-location ratio -- it never
silently disables the option (see the -- GENERATION PERFORMANCE -- note
below for the heuristic and its threshold).

-- GENERATION PERFORMANCE -------------------------------------------------
Line Locks is the single biggest cost on generation time, because it adds
one progression item per evolution family across every active region
(~50-100 per region, 300+ across many regions). Stacking Line Locks with:

  - 5+ active regions, AND
  - Type Locks + Region Locks + Badge Level Gating, AND
  - 3+ of {legendary, trade, baby, fossil, paradox, stone, ultra_beast} locks

...pushes the progression-item count into the 700-900 range. `fill_restrictive`
complexity scales with progression-items x locations, so these configs can
take 30-60s to generate on modest hardware (vs. <5s for typical configs).
The heuristic at `__init__.py:90-108` only WARNS (via logging.warning) when the
estimated progression-to-location ratio exceeds 55% -- it no longer disables
Line Locks. This flags likely FillError risk but not slow-but-completes
generation. If you want all-locks-on with many regions, be prepared to
wait on generation.

options.label: Badge Level Gating
options.description:
Gate Pokemon behind Gym Badges based on their encounter level.
Higher-level Pokemon require more badges (Lv1-10: 0 badges, Lv11-20: 1, etc.).
When combined with Legendary Locks, uses the higher requirement of the two.
Requires Gym Badges in the item pool (enabled automatically).

options.label: Legendary Locks
options.description:
Gate legendary Pokemon behind Gym Badge items.
Collect 6 Badges for sub-legendaries (trios, regis, tapus, etc.),
7 Badges for box legendaries (version mascots), and
8 Badges for mythics (event-only Pokemon like Mew, Celebi, Arceus).
When Badge Level Gating is also on, uses the higher badge requirement.
8 Gym Badge items are added to the item pool when enabled.

options.label: Trade Evolution Lock
options.description:
Require a Link Cable item before guessing trade-evolved Pokemon
(Alakazam, Machamp, Golem, Gengar, Scizor, Steelix, Conkeldurr, etc.).

options.label: Baby Pokemon Lock
options.description:
Require Daycare item(s) before guessing baby Pokemon
(Pichu, Cleffa, Igglybuff, Togepi, Tyrogue, Smoochum, Elekid, Magby, etc.).

options.label: Daycare Items Required
options.description:
Number of Daycare items required to unlock baby Pokemon.
Only used when Baby Pokemon Lock is enabled.
Set higher for a more gradual unlock; all copies must be received.

options.label: Fossil Lock
options.description:
Require a Fossil Restorer item before guessing fossil-revived Pokemon
(Omanyte, Omastar, Kabuto, Kabutops, Aerodactyl, Lileep, Cranidos, etc.).

options.label: Ultra Beast Lock
options.description:
Require an Ultra Wormhole item before guessing Ultra Beasts
(Nihilego through Blacephalon, plus Necrozma which also originates from Ultra Space).

options.label: Paradox Lock
options.description:
Require a Time Rift item before guessing Paradox Pokemon
(Great Tusk, Roaring Moon, Iron Valiant, etc., plus Koraidon and Miraidon).
Only relevant when Paldea is active.

options.label: Stone Evolution Lock
options.description:
Require the matching evolutionary stone item before guessing stone-only evolutions.
Each stone type that gates at least one active Pokemon adds one stone item to the pool.
Examples: Fire Stone -> Arcanine/Ninetales/Flareon, Water Stone -> Starmie/Vaporeon/Cloyster.

options.label: Master Ball Bypasses Gates
options.description:
If enabled, Master Balls can catch any Pokemon regardless of lock gates.
If disabled, Master Balls can only be used on Pokemon you could normally guess.

options.label: Pokedex/Pokegear as Filler
options.description:
Classify Pokedex and Pokegear as filler instead of useful items.
They behave identically in-game (reveal a Pokemon's type/identity); this only
lowers their fill priority so they stop crowding the useful-item tier when you
end up with a large surplus. Master Ball is unaffected.
Off by default (Pokedex and Pokegear remain 'useful').

options.label: Include Shiny Charms
options.description:
Add Shiny Charm filler items to the item pool.
Receiving a Shiny Charm makes a random Pokemon in your caught list display
its shiny sprite. Purely cosmetic -- no gameplay effect.

options.label: Goal Type
options.description:
How the goal is defined.
Percentage: guess a percentage of the active Pokemon pool (see 'Goal Percentage').
Count: guess a fixed number of Pokemon (see 'Goal Count').

options.label: Goal Percentage
options.description:
Percentage of the active Pokemon pool that must be guessed to complete the game.
Only used when 'Goal Type' is set to 'percentage'.
For example, 80 with 386 active Pokemon means guessing 309 to win.

options.label: Goal Count
options.description:
Fixed number of Pokemon that must be guessed to complete the game.
Only used when 'Goal Type' is set to 'count'.
Automatically capped to the total active Pokemon across selected regions.

options.label: Stop Auto-submit After Goal
options.description:
Default for the client's 'stop auto-submit after goal' toggle.
When on, once your goal is reached the client stops auto-submitting remaining
guesses. This only sets the client's initial preference -- players can still
override it locally. Off by default (auto-submit keeps running after goal).
Has no effect on generation or logic.

options.label: Hide Spoilers (Dex Numbers)
options.description:
If on, every per-Pokemon location name is shown as its National Dex number
instead of the Pokemon name ('Guess Bulbasaur' becomes 'Guess Pokemon 1').
This stops hints and tracker location lists from giving away which Pokemon
are available to guess. It is cosmetic only: location ids, logic, checks and
item names are unchanged, so generation and completion are identical either way.
Useful for streams or shared screens. Off by default.

options.label: Trap Chance
options.description:
Percentage chance (0-100) that a filler item slot will be replaced by a trap item.
0 means no traps; 100 means all filler items will be traps.

options.label: Local Filler Percent
options.description:
Percentage of this world's own filler items to force into this world's own
locations before the multiworld fill runs, keeping them out of other players'
games. Only filler is localized (Pokedex, Pokegear, Master Ball, Shiny Charm,
traps, and the splash filler); progression and useful gate items are never
localized, so the seed stays completable and cross-game progression is
unaffected. Higher values keep more of Pokepelago's large Dexsanity filler pool
out of an async/multiworld.

Dexsanity can create up to ~1025 'Guess {Pokemon}' locations, which forces an
equally large filler pool; without this, most of that filler floods other games.
'off' (0) keeps the classic behavior. 'auto' (-1, the default) scales a forced
minimum by how inflated the pool is: 0 when Dexsanity is off, otherwise 50% for
one region and +10% per additional region, capped at 90% so some filler still
travels to the rest of the multiworld.

options.label: Include Kanto (deprecated)
options.description: Deprecated -- use the 'regions' option instead.

options.label: Include Johto (deprecated)
options.description: Deprecated -- use the 'regions' option instead.

options.label: Include Hoenn (deprecated)
options.description: Deprecated -- use the 'regions' option instead.

options.label: Include Sinnoh (deprecated)
options.description: Deprecated -- use the 'regions' option instead.

options.label: Include Unova (deprecated)
options.description: Deprecated -- use the 'regions' option instead.

options.label: Include Kalos (deprecated)
options.description: Deprecated -- use the 'regions' option instead.

options.label: Include Alola (deprecated)
options.description: Deprecated -- use the 'regions' option instead.
