options.label: Starting Weapons
options.description:
Randomize what two weapons you start the game with.
Vanilla: Start with the Lancer and Gravity Bomb.
Balanced: Start with two random weapons that are relatively balanced.
Non-Broken: Start with two random weapons besides RYNO II and Zodiac.
Unrestricted: Start with any two non-upgraded weapons.

options.label: Randomize Megacorp Vendor
options.description:
Randomize what items appear at the Megacorp vendor. New items will get added as you visit more planets.
When enabled, you can switch between buying items and buying ammo by pressing up/down when in the vendor.

options.label: Randomize Gadgetron Vendor
options.description: Randomize what items appear at the Gadgetron vendor on Barlow.

options.label: Exclude Very Expensive Items
options.description:
Exclude RYNO II and Zodiac from the randomization leaving them at their vanilla locations.
This will only take effect if the corresponding vendors are randomized

options.label: Skip Wupash Nebula
options.description: Skips the Wupash Nebula ship section that appears when first traveling to Maktar Nebula.

options.label: Enable Bolt Multiplier
options.description: Enables the bolt multiplier feature without being in New Game+.

options.label: Remove Revisit Rewards Change
options.description:
In the vanilla game, rewards given when killing enemies change when you come back to a previously visited planet
(bolts & experience). Enabling this option removes this behavior, making the experience and bolts obtained more
stable throughout the seed.

options.label: Remove Kill Rewards Degradation
options.description:
In the vanilla game, rewards given by a specific enemy decrease each time you kill it (bolts & experience).
Enabling this option removes this behavior, making the experience and bolts obtained more stable throughout
the seed.

options.label: Free Challenge Selection
options.description:
Makes all hoverbike and spaceship challenges selectable right away, which means you don't have to win a
challenge to access the next one.

options.label: Nanotech XP Multiplier
options.description: A multiplier applied to experience gained for Nanotech levels, in percent.

options.label: Weapon XP Multiplier
options.description: A multiplier applied to experience gained for weapon levels, in percent.

options.label: Extra Spaceship Challenge Locations
options.description:
In the vanilla game, only the first challenge and the race challenge completed perfectly give an item as a
reward. If enabled, this option makes all spaceship challenges reward an item on first completion.

options.label: Extended Weapon Progression
options.description:
If enabled, make all weapon tiers obtainable through weapon experience. This means LV2 (orange) weapons can
upgrade into LV3 (yellow) weapons, which can then upgrade into LV4 (blue) weapons.
This effectively makes all weapons that are usually restricted to NG+ available with enough grinding.

options.label: First Person Mode Glitch In Logic
options.description:
Determines if logic should take first person mode glitches into account when evaluating which locations are
reachable. Various difficulty levels can be picked:
- Easy: simple climbs (e.g. getting the Platinum Bolt near Oozla scientist)
- Medium: harder climbs and basic lateral movement (e.g. Getting to the Notak Worker Bots without the Heli-pack nor the Thermanator)
- Hard: full navigation following walls (e.g. Getting to the Mutated Protopet only with the Infiltrator)

options.label: Opened NO4 Backdoor
options.description:
Determines the behavior for the back door from Entrance to Underground Cavern
closed: The door will be closed as in vanilla
open: The door will be open after reaching Alchemy Laboratory, ensuring the Death cutscene
open_early: The door will be open from the start, allowing you to break the Death cutscene

Locations that require a higher score than the target are removed.

Enable DeeDee to randomly spawn in the night like in vanilla UCN.
If enabled, DeeDee repels will also be added to the filler item pool.

options.label: Excluded Animatronics
options.description:
Exclude these animatronics from the item pool.
Incompatible with hard_logic
NOTE: When excluding animatronics, abilities that are only used by excluded animatronics also get removed.

(Example: When excluding Chica, it will also remove the Change Music item from the item pool, but won't remove the
Global Music Box, because Lefty and the Marionette also need it. If you remove them alongside Chica however,
the GMB will be excluded as well.)

options.label: Death Link Amnesty
options.description: The number of times you have to die to send a death link to everyone.

options.label: Start With Vertical Scale Blocks
options.description: Choose to start with or without Vertical Scale Blocks. This will probably break generation if you turn it off.

options.label: Start With Chains Door
options.description: Choose to start with or without the Chains Door. This will probably break generation if you turn it off.

options.label: Start With Place Indicators
options.description: Choose to start with or without Place Indicators. This will probably break generation if you turn it off.

options.label: Death Link Amnesty
options.description: How many deaths or restarts it takes to trigger a DeathLink

options.label: Victory Condition
options.description:
What the victory condition for the overall game is. 
Clear X Levels: You must clear X total levels to goal the game.
Beat X Par Times: You must beat the target time on X total levels.
Beat X Crystal Targets: You must beat the crystal target on X total levels.
Coordinate Hunt: You must find X "Transporter Coordinates" items to gain access to Rocky Horror, which you must then clear to win the game.

options.label: Target Level Count
options.description:
Sets the value of X for the chosen Victory Condition. Does not affect Coordinate Hunt. 
If a target number higher than the number of available levels is given, target will automatically cap at 'all levels'.

options.label: Locked Coordinate Locations
options.description:
Only relevant if Victory Condition is set to "Coordinate Hunt". 
If true, then clearing each level unlocks one "Transporter Coordinates" item. 
If false, then the "Transporter Coordinates" can be anywhere in the multiworld. An extra location is still added to each level.

options.label: Coordinates Required
options.description:
Sets the number of Transporter Coordinate items required for Coordinate Hunt.
If higher than the number in the pool, will be automatically lowered.
"0" is a special case that means "every".

options.label: Coordinates In Pool
options.description:
Sets the number of Transporter Coordinates items shuffled into the item pool, if Locked Coordinates are disabled. 
Does not have an effect otherwise - there will still be exactly one Transporter Coordinate on every level.
"0" is a special case that means "1 per level".

options.label: Available Levels
options.description:
How many levels are available to play, selected randomly from the chosen campaigns.
If a number higher than the number of selected campaign levels is given, all selected levels will be available.

options.label: Available Levels At Start
options.description: How many levels are available initially to the player.

options.label: Sphere 1 Levels At Start
options.description: How many of your initially available levels are guaranteed to be beatable before receiving items.

options.label: Target Times Are Locations
options.description: Whether target times for levels are Locations.

options.label: Target Time Difficulty
options.description:
How difficult the target times are per level. 
Caution is strongly advised when using Rock Hard targets in a multiplayer game - they are very difficult.

options.label: Crystal Targets Are Locations
options.description: Whether target crystal counts for levels are Locations.

options.label: Crystal Target Percentage
options.description:
The percentage of the total possible crystals required to clear the extra Location.
Has no effect if Crystal Targets Are Locations is disabled.

options.label: Buildings Are Items
options.description: Whether Buildings must be found in the multiworld to be unlocked.

options.label: Items Are Items
options.description: Whether Items (Electric Fences and Dynamite) must be found in the multiworld to be unlocked.

options.label: Vehicles Are Items
options.description: Whether Vehicles must be found in the multiworld to be unlocked.

options.label: Progressive Items
options.description:
Affects behaviour of unlockable Buildings/Items/Vehicles.
'Normal' puts a single unlockable copy into the itempool. Finding the unlock item allows you build as many copies of that unlockable as you like.
'Duplicates' adds a second copy of certain unlock items, to increase the chances of finding one sooner. Receiving the second copy has no effect.
'Progressive' adds split copies of several unlock items, where getting the first item allows you to build a single copy of the unlockable, and further copies of the unlock items increase that limit. 
NB: Small Digger and Small Mobile Laser Cutter instead increment by +2 each time. 
'Progressive And Duplicate' will act like 'Progressive', but also attempt to add some duplicates of certain non-progressive items into the pool, to increase their chances of being found. This will depend on the number of items vs number of locations your other settings allow.

options.label: No Infinite STT
options.description:
If using Progressive Items, this turns off the 'infinite build allowed' for Small Transport Truck, that normally comes when you have enough progressive items. 
Filler copies of Progressive Small Transport Truck will be added to the pool, with a low chance.

options.label: Miner Cap
options.description: Adds a limit to the number of miners you can have at once, increasable by items in the multiworld.

options.label: Miner Cap Base Level
options.description:
If Miner Cap is enabled, sets the base level of miners you start with. 
Does not affect the amount of increases in the multiworld. 
(For now, logic all assumes this is set to 5.)

options.label: Chief's Favourite Truck
options.description: Whether to include a bonus starting Small Transport Truck in the Item pool.

options.label: Useful Filler Only
options.description: If enabled, only gameplay-affecting filler will be included, instead of 'empty' items. Can affect game balance slightly.

options.label: Breathing Always In Logic
options.description:
Whether the ability to build a Support Station is logically required for all levels with limited air.
When enabled, some levels that can be comfortably beaten before the air runs out will remain out of logic. 
Has no effect if Buildings Are Items is disabled.

options.label: Faster Blasting Always In Logic
options.description:
The Small Mobile Laser Cutter and Small Digger are often in logic for their ability to get through hard rock walls, but both are quite slow at it. The Upgrade Station allows some improvement. 
When this setting is enabled, any time that the Small Digger or SMLC is required by logic, so is the Upgrade Station.

options.label: Electric Fences In Logic
options.description: Puts the Electric Fence in logic for certain levels with heavy monster issues.

options.label: Enable Bonus Locations For Clearing Levels
options.description: When enabled, clearing a level will award 2-5 Locations instead of 1. Harder levels are worth more.

options.label: Include 'Standard' Campaign Levels
options.description:
Whether your game will include the Standard campaign levels.
If no campaigns are selected, this one will automatically enable.

options.label: Include 'Remastered' Campaign Levels
options.description: Whether your game will include the Remastered campaign levels.

options.label: Include 'Classic' Campaign Levels
options.description: Whether your game will include the Classic campaign levels.

options.label: Include 'Baz's Mod' Campaign Levels
options.description: Whether your game will include the Baz's Mod campaign levels.

options.label: No Duplicate Levels
options.description:
If this is enabled, instead of all selected levels, you will have only one of each, selected randomly from the enabled campaigns. 
For example, you will have a random Rocky Horror, but only one.
You are guaranteed to start with Driller Night.

options.label: Include Baz-unique Levels
options.description:
When using No Duplicate Levels and Baz's Mod, whether to include the Baz-unique levels. Has no effect if not using both of these options.
If disabled, only the original 25 levels will be shuffled. 
If enabled, all 33 levels will be shuffled, which means the Baz-unique 8 will always be present.

Vanilla: The Citizen's Card is obtained normally.
Randomized: Shuffles the Citizen's Card and location into the pool.
Open: The Citizen's Card does nothing and the doors to the city are always open.

options.label: Shuffle Class B License
options.description:
The Class B License controls access to the Underground Ruins.
Vanilla: The Class B License is obtained normally.
Randomized: Shuffles the Class B License and location into the pool.
Open: The Class B License does nothing and the doors to the Underground Ruins are always open.

options.label: Shuffle Class A License
options.description:
The Class A License controls access to the three Sub-Gates.
Vanilla: The Class A License is obtained normally.
Randomized: Shuffles the Class A License and location into the pool.
Open: The Class A License does nothing and the doors to the Sub-Gates are always open.

options.label: Shuffle Main Gate Unlock

Vanilla: Access to the Main Gate is obtained normally.
Randomized: Shuffles a Main Gate Unlock item and location into the pool.
Open: The doors to the Main Gate are always open.

options.label: Shuffle Sub-Cities Unlock
options.description:
Vanilla: Access to the Sub-Cities is obtained normally.
Randomized: Shuffles a Sub-Cities Unlock item and location into the pool.
Open: The doors to the Sub-Cities are always open.

options.label: Shuffle Starting Special Weapon
options.description: Shuffles the Mine Parts Kit into the item pool and randomizes the first special weapon received.

options.label: Shuffle Starting Special Weapon Options
options.description:
If 'Shuffle Starting Special Weapon' is enabled, this option will determine the special weapon pool to shuffle from.
If none are selected, the logic will default to the Splash Arm.

options.label: Shuffle Buster Max
options.description: Shuffles the Buster Max buster part into the item pool.

options.label: Teleporter Start
options.description:
Start with a teleporter 
if you don't do this, give another item or start with StD or FtC you will start off BKed and generation will fail in singleplayer

worlds.game: Black Market of Bulletphilia ~ 100th Black Market

options.label: Anti-Grinding Item Toggle
options.description: Toggles whether generation logic should consider anti-grinding placements.

options.label: Anti-Grinding Item Placements
options.description:
Which items should be prioritized for placement during early game to reduce grinding as much as possible.
Four cards and 1000 Funds are on the list by default, but you can choose to remove them.

options.label: Starting Market
options.description:
Choose which stage to have unlocked at the start of the game.

If Progressive Markets is enabled:
- Unlock items for stages preceding the Starting Market will not appear.
- Any stages preceding the Starting Market will be unlocked.

options.label: Progressive Market
options.description: Stages will be unlocked in order as the game progresses.

options.label: Itemize Equipment Upgrades
options.description:
Whether starting card slots and equip cost will be upgraded according to the number of bosses defeated or via items received.
The game begins with 1 starting card slot and 100% equip cost.

1. Disabled - Slots and cost will be unlocked according to the number of bosses defeated (vanilla).
2. Simultaneous - Both slots and cost will be upgraded at the same time.
3. Separate - Slots and cost will only be upgraded with the appropriate items received.

options.label: Simultaneous - Equipment Upgrades Count
options.description:
Only used if "Itemize Equipment Upgrades" is set to Simultaneous.
This will determine how many of them will be in the item pool.
Minimum of +6 items because of one of the Achievements.
Can technically go up to +33, but it is recommended to only go up to +15 at most.

options.label: Separate - Starting Card Slot Upgrades Count
options.description:
Only used if "Itemize Equipment Upgrades" is set to Separate.
This determines how many starting card slot upgrades will be in the item pool.
Minimum of +6 slots because of one of the Achievements.
Can technically go up to +33, but it is recommended to only go up to +15 at most.

options.label: Separate - Equip Cost Upgrades Count
options.description:
Only used if "Itemize Equipment Upgrades" is set to Separate.
This will determine how many equip cost upgrades will be in the item pool.
Equip cost maxes out at +900%, and each upgrade is worth 50%.

options.label: Boss and Stage Locations
options.description: Whether boss encounters and defeats will count as locations, and whether stage clears will count as locations.

options.label: Lock Challenge Market in Logic
options.description:
Generation logic will consider Challenge Market inaccessible if all other stages have not been unlocked yet.
Disable this option to turn off the above handicap.

options.label: Completion Goal
options.description:
A goal to reach.

1. Full Story Clear - Defeat Chimata Tenkyuu, Nitori Kawashiro, Takane Yamashiro.
2. Minimum Story Clear - Defeat Takane Yamashiro.
3. All Ability Cards Owned.
4. All Bosses Defeated - Challenge Market does not count.
5. Challenge Market Clear.
6. Clear everything except Challenge Market.
7. Clear everything.
8. Dragon Gem Hunt - Collect a certain number of Dragon Gem items randomly placed throughout the game.

options.label: Trap Chance
options.description: Percentage chance that any given filler Item will be replaced by a trap item.

options.label: Trap Blacklist
options.description:
Which Trap items will not be generated if Trap Chance is higher than 0.
Remove any of these entries if you want those traps to appear.

options.label: Recommended Loadout in Logic
options.description:
Whether the generation logic should include certain Ability Cards as compulsory before challenging late-game stages.

0. Disabled.
1. Stage 4 requires only 2 of them, stage 5 requires 4, etc.
2. All late-game stages logically require all cards below.

* 4th-6th Market + Challenge Market:
Life Explosion Elixir, Princess Kaguya's Secret Stash, Soot-covered Uchiwa,
Esteemed Authority, Gluttonous Centipede, and Money Is The Best Lawyer In Hell.
* End of Market:
Life Explosion Elixir, Esteemed Authority
* Takane: + Lucky Cat with Good Business Skills
* Nitori: + 1 card loadout slot progression

options.label: Recommended Equipment Upgrades in Logic
options.description:
Whether generation logic should also consider placing itemized equipment upgrades before late-game stages.
This only works if "Itemize Equipment Upgrades" and "Recommended Loadout in Logic" are enabled.
This will scale based on "Recommended Loadout in Logic".

options.label: Include Non-Money Filler
options.description:
Whether filler items that are not Funds or Bullet Money will appear during generation.
Also affects Traps.

options.label: Dragon Gems Required
options.description:
Only effective if the Completion Type is set to Dragon Gem Hunt.
This will determine how many Dragon Gem items are required for goal.
If there are not enough locations for the required count, the count will be adjusted accordingly.

options.label: Dragon Gems in Pool
options.description:
Only effective if the Completion Type is set to Dragon Gem Hunt.
This will determine how many Dragon Gem items would be in the item pool.
If this number is less than the victory condition number,
the number in the item pool will be randomized with a minimum the same as the victory condition.

options.label: Death Link Trigger
options.description:
Determines when a Death Link would be sent. Only takes effect if Death Link is enabled.
Can be temporarily changed during gameplay.

0. Upon losing a life. This means Life Explosion Elixir will also trigger Death Link.
1. Upon failing a stage attempt. All lives must be lost before this triggers.

options.label: Anti-Death Link Invincibility
options.description: Determines whether invincibility can protect against incoming Death Links.

options.label: Energy Link
options.description:
Allows usage of the EnergyLink pool.
Funds can be deposited and withdrawn at a certain exchange rate.
However, undeposited and withdrawn Funds will not be automatically saved.

options.label: Energy Link Bullet Money Exchanges
options.description:
If enabled, EnergyLink exchanges permit exchanging energy for Bullet Money as well.
Conversion rates for Bullet Money differ from that for Funds.
Bullet Money cannot be deposited nor withdrawn outside of stages.

options.label: Enable Music Room Checks
options.description: Whether soundtrack unlocks in the Music Room also counts as checks.

options.label: Enable Achievement Checks
options.description: Whether Achievements also counts as checks.

options.label: Allow Permanent Player Upgrades
options.description:
Whether items for permanently upgrading player initial stats (starting lives, starting shot attack, etc.) will appear.
These permanent upgrades were never part of the original game, and will not be required for progression.
However, they will be prioritized for filler before other filler items can be placed (e.g. Funds filler, one-time Shot Attack bonuses).

options.label: Starting Upgrades: Lives
options.description:
How many upgrades for additional starting lives? Cannot exceed 3 upgrades (4 starting lives).
Note that you begin with 1 life by default in every stage.

options.label: Starting Upgrades: Bullet Money (70 Bullet Money/upgrade)
options.description:
How many upgrades for additional starting Bullet Money? Each upgrade is worth 70 Bullet Money.
Note that you begin with 0 Bullet Money by default in every stage.

options.label: Starting Upgrades: Power
options.description:
How many upgrades for additional starting Power? Cannot exceed 3 upgrades (4 starting Power).
Note that you begin with 1 Power by default in every stage.

options.label: Starting Upgrades: Shot Attack (5%/upgrade)
options.description:
How many upgrades for additional starting shot attack? Each upgrade is worth 5%.
Note that you begin with 100% shot attack by default in every stage.

options.label: Starting Upgrades: Magic Circle Attack (5%/upgrade)
options.description:
How many upgrades for additional starting magic circle strength? Each upgrade is worth 5%.
Note that you begin with 100% magic circle strength by default in every stage.

options.label: Packs or Sets
options.description:
Packs contain cards that are randomized upon receipt at the lua script level
Sets are static card sets (i.e. You received Card Set Lady Luck 4-6)

options.label: Starting Packs
options.description: If Packs are enabled, sets how many you start with

options.label: Zeroes
options.description: Toggle whether 0 value card's should be included in the item pool.  Innefective if you are using card packs

options.label: Cure
options.description: Toggle whether Cure cards should be included in the item pool.  Innefective if you are using card packs

options.label: Early Cure
options.description: Toggles whether one of the starting locations should contain Cure 4-6?

options.label: Enemy Cards
options.description: Toggles whether enemy cards should be shuffled into the item pool.

options.label: Starting Worlds
options.description: Number of random world cards to start with in addition to Traverse Town, which is always available.

options.label: Excluded Enemy Cards

options.label: Exclude Sleights
options.description: Detmerines which sleights should be excluded from the pool, if any.

options.label: Character
options.description:
Determines the expected player character.
0: Ventus
1: Aqua
2: Terra

options.label: Starting Worlds
options.description: Number of random worlds to start with.

options.label: Final Terra Xehanort II
options.description:
Determines if Aqua will need to defeat Final Terra Xehanort II to complete her seed.
Does nothing if the player chooses a character other than Aqua

options.label: Mirage Arena Battles
options.description: Determines if Mirage Arena battle locations should be included.

options.label: Command Board
options.description: Determines if Mirage Arena Command Board locations should be included.

options.label: Super Bosses
options.description: Determines if Super Boss locations should be included.

options.label: Max HP Increases
options.description: Number of Max HP Increases are in the item pool.

options.label: Randomize Keyblade Stats
options.description: Determines if Keyblade stats should be randomized

options.label: Keyblade Minimum STR Bonus
options.description: Determines the minimum Strength bonus a keyblade can have.

options.label: Keyblade Maximum STR Bonus
options.description: Determines the maximum Strength bonus a keyblade can have.

options.label: Keyblade Minimum MP Bonus
options.description: Determines the minimum Magic bonus a keyblade can have.

options.label: Keyblade Maximum MP Bonus
options.description: Determines the maximum Magic bonus a keyblade can have.

options.label: Realm of Darkness
options.description: If your character is Aqua, determines if Realm of Darkness is included as a world.

options.label: Advanced Logic
options.description: If enabled, using commands for tricky movement and precise jumps will be required to reach many locations

options.label: Minigames
options.description: Determines whether to include locations for the Disney Town minigames and the racing minigames in Mirage Arena

options.label: Mirage Arena Medals
options.description: Determines if there should be locations for Mirage Arena medal collecting. Currently these have no logic or shortcuts beyond having Mirage Arena.

options.label: Mirage Arena Global Locations
options.description:
Determines if there should be locations for the Mirage Arena missions that require beating the game with each character
Also enables Combined Threat and Monster of the Deep without their respective worlds
If playing on a fresh save leave this off or you'll have unreachable locations!

options.label: Block Size
options.description:
The size of a single block (and the width/height of each board). A standard Sudoku is 9.
Smaller sizes are easier, larger sizes are more difficult.

options.label: Boards per Cluster
options.description:
How many boards to put in each cluster of overlapping boards.
1 creates individual boards without clusters, 100 puts all boards into a
single big cluster.

options.label: Number of Boards
options.description:
How many boards to generate. Maximum depend on block size:
- 4-9: 100 boards
- 12: 64 boards
- 16: 36 boards

options.label: Difficulty
options.description:
The overall difficulty level. Solving techniques required:
- Beginner: Naked/hidden singles.
- Easy: Pointing pairs, box line reduction.
- Medium: Naked pairs/triples.
- Hard: Hidden pairs/triples.
- Very Hard: X-Wing, Swordfish, Y-Wing.

options.label: Block Unlocks
options.description:
How blocks are unlocked during the game.
- Fixed: Blocks are unlocked by progressive block items in a fixed order. Smoother progression.
- Shuffled: Blocks are unlocked by specific block items. More chaotic progression.

options.label: Bundle Size
options.description:
How many blocks a single progression item unlocks at once.
- A value of 1 disables bundling.
- The value is clamped to the block size, so a bundle never unlocks more than a whole
  board's worth of blocks.
- For Fixed progression each "Progressive Block" is worth this many unlocks.
- For Shuffled progression each bundle is a "Block Bundle" item unlocking this many blocks.

options.label: Additional Starting Blocks
options.description:
How many additional blocks beyond the regular starting board that start unlocked.
This removes that many blocks from the item pool, replacing them with filler items.

options.label: Duplicate Progression Items
options.description:
Percent of progression items that should be duplicated.
- For Fixed progression higher values may lead to progression being too fast and as such a
  lower value is recommended.
- For Shuffled progression this can safely be set to 100% to make progression a bit faster.
  The blocks to duplicate are chosen randomly if not 100%, though each block can only be duplicated once.

options.label: Disabled Locations
options.description:
Location types to remove entirely, reducing the number of locations and filler items. Valid
values: blocks, rows, columns, boards. If disabling the requested types would leave too few
locations for the progression items, some types are automatically re-enabled (a warning is
logged). Higher bundle sizes allow disabling more, since they reduce the number of progression
items.

options.label: Location Scouting
options.description:
How scouting of locations is handled.
- Auto: Locations are scouted automatically when fully revealed.
- Manual: Locations can be scouted manually.
- Disabled: Locations cannot be scouted.

options.label: Filler Ratio: Solve Selected Cell
options.description: Ratio of Solve Selected Cell filler items to number of boards, in percent.

options.label: Filler Ratio: Solve Random Cell
options.description: Ratio of Solve Random Cell filler items to number of boards, in percent.

options.label: Filler Ratio: Remove Random Candidate
options.description: Ratio of Remove Random Candidate filler items to number of boards, in percent.

options.label: Filler Ratio: Emoji Trap
options.description:
Ratio of Emoji Trap filler items to number of boards, in percent.
When received your numbers will be replaced with emojis for a time.

options.label: Filler Ratio: Disco Trap
options.description:
Ratio of Disco Trap filler items to number of boards, in percent.
When received all cells will shift colors for a time.

options.label: Filler Ratio: Tunnel Vision Trap
options.description:
Ratio of Tunnel Vision Trap filler items to number of boards, in percent.
When received you will only be able to see a small area of the board for a time.

options.label: Pre-fill Nothings Percentage
options.description:
Percentage of Nothing items that should be pre-filled, forcing them to be placed in
an Archipeladoku game and thus excluding them from other games.
Caution: This reduces the number of filler items in the item pool. Having few fillers can lead
to increased generation times or even generation failures. As long as you don't remove other
filler items this shouldn't be an issue though, even at 100%.

options.label: Death Link
options.description:
Enable Death Link. When a player with death link enabled dies all other players that also
enabled it die as well. Archipeladoku can only receive death links, not send them. When a death
link is received all non-given numbers will be cleared. This can also be toggled in the client
from the Debug menu.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Choose the victory condition for this world.

gnasty: Defeat Gnasty Gnorc
loot: Reach the vortex at the end of Gnasty's Loot

options.label: Starting Homeworld
options.description:
Choose which homeworld to start in.

Options are:
artisans
peace_keepers
magic_crafters
beast_makers
dream_weavers

options.label: Portal Shuffle
options.description: If enabled, where a portal leads to is shuffled.

options.label: Global Gem Threshold Percentage
options.description:
A percentage multiplier for the every 500 gem total threshold locations. 50, for example, will mean that getting
50% of the gems in every accessible level will logically be expected at any given point. Accepts a range between
1 and 100.

options.label: Maximum Per-Area Gem Threshold
options.description:
The maximum gem threshold locations to include for each level/hub. Corresponds to the maximum percentage of gems
per area to create locations for. Useful for reducing amount of filler relative to useful items for this game.

options.label: Story Arcs
options.description:
Which story ladders are played. With one arc, the Singles/Doubles choosers are skipped and only that arc's
checks exist.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
island_open: win the Island Open final (of each arc played).
dream_match: win the Dream Match at Peach's Castle (of each arc played).
completionist: check every location.

options.label: Mini-Games
options.description:
progressive: each of the 9 Mario mini-games is a progressive item; its copies open the grid cell and levels 2 and 3.
vanilla: each mini-game is one item opening its cell; levels unlock by clearing, as in the game.
excluded: every cell is open and mini-game clears are not locations.

options.label: Story Match Sets
options.description: Sets in every story match (best of). Vanilla keeps each match's own length.

options.label: Story Match Games
options.description: Games per set in every story match. Vanilla keeps each match's own length.

options.label: Skip Intro
options.description: A new story game skips the opening tour and starts in the Dorm Room.

options.label: Skip Awards Ceremony
options.description:
Winning an Island Open final goes straight from the bracket to the congratulations artwork and credits,
skipping the fireworks and the Awards Ceremony.

options.label: Default Text Speed
options.description: The message speed a new story file starts with. It can still be changed in the game's Options.

options.label: Default Camera Mode
options.description:
The match camera a new story file starts with: normal, or player (the court turned so you are always on the near
side). It can still be changed from the match pause menu.

options.label: Item Messages
options.description:
Shows a message in the overworld for each item you find, send or receive. Turned off, items still arrive as
normal, just silently.

options.label: Nerf Swing Contest
options.description: Lowers the swing contest's thresholds from 100 and 150 swings to 60 and 90.

options.label: Nerf Two-on-One
options.description: Bowser's mini-game, Two-on-One, plays 2 games per set instead of 6.

options.label: Experience Modifier
options.description:
Multiplies every EXP award: story, exhibition and linked matches, drills, and EXP Bundles. A single award is
capped at 65535 and never drops to 0.

options.label: Dream Match Difficulty
options.description:
How hard Mario plays in Peach's first Dream Match offer (Intense in the original game). After a win she lets
you pick any of the three, as usual.

options.label: Shot Items
options.description:
Your shots are items: topspin, slice and the flat shot (the second copy of each adds its power shot, or the
smash), the lob and drop shot, and the topspin, slice and flat serves (the second copy adds the nice serve).
You start with one random stroke and one random serve; a locked shot plays the first stroke or serve you own.

options.label: Remote Items
options.description:
Every item, this world's own and the starting inventory included, comes from the server. Needed for co-op or
playing one slot on two carts; nothing is granted while disconnected.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Select one or more goals. All selected goals must be completed to win.

- Elite Four: Defeat the Champion and enter the Hall of Fame
- Red: Defeat Red in Mt. Silver
- Diploma: Catch all logically available Pokemon and receive the diploma in Celadon City
- Rival: Win all possible rival battles
- Defeat Team Rocket: Vanquish Team Rocket in Slowpoke Well, Mahogany Town, Radio Tower and defeat the grunt
   on Route 24 (if Kanto is accessible)
- Unown Hunt: Catch all 26 Unown forms that are attached to signs across the region(s) and show the completed Unown dex
   to the scientist in Ruins of Alph. In order to encounter the Unown you'll need to solve their corresponding tile puzzle.
   Each puzzle requires 16 pieces which must be found first.
- Battle Tower: Beat all 10 Battle Tower tiers (7 trainers each).

options.label: Vanilla Event Chains
options.description:
Restores the selected vanilla event chains instead of the streamlined Archipelago behaviour.

Misty: Misty is not in her gym at the start. You must meet the Power Plant manager, witness the Rocket
 flee the Cerulean Gym, then find Misty on her date on Route 25 before she returns to her gym. The Cerulean Gym
 Machine Part cannot be picked up until the Power Plant manager step.

Clair: Clair refuses to give you the Rising Badge until you prove your worth to the Elders in the
 Dragon's Den Shrine, which requires Whirlpool to access.

Jasmine: the Cianwood Pharmacy only hands over the SecretPotion after you've visited Jasmine tending
 her sick Amphy atop the Olivine Lighthouse. (Curing Amphy to bring Jasmine back to her gym is always
 required; this just gates the SecretPotion behind meeting her first.)

Copycat: the guy in the Vermilion Pokemon Fan Club only gives you the Lost Item after you've spoken to
 the Copycat in Saffron and learned she lost it.

- _All includes all event chains
- _Random has a 50% chance to include each event chain that is not already included

options.label: Johto Only
options.description:
Excludes Kanto and disables Kanto access. Include Silver Cave keeps Silver Cave and Mt. Silver available.

- The Diploma goal is removed; the Red goal is also removed unless Silver Cave is included
  (Elite Four is used if no goals remain)
- Gym count requirements are capped at 8 (7 for Radio Tower)
- Badge count requirements are capped at 8 (7 for Radio Tower and Route 44) unless badges are completely
  random, in which case extra Kanto badges are added to the pool

options.label: Victory Road Requirement
options.description: Sets the requirement to pass the Victory Road badge check

options.label: Victory Road Count
options.description:
Sets the number of badges/gyms required to pass the Victory Road badge check

This will be limited to 8 if the requirement is Johto Badges

options.label: Elite Four Requirement
options.description: Sets the requirement go between Indigo Pokecenter 1F and Will's room

options.label: Elite Four Count
options.description:
Sets the number of badges/gyms required to go between Indigo Pokecenter 1F and Will's room

This will be limited to 8 if the requirement is Johto Badges

options.label: Red Requirement
options.description: Sets the requirement to battle Red

options.label: Red Count
options.description: Number of badges/gyms required to battle Red

options.label: Mt. Silver Requirement
options.description: Sets the requirement to access Mt. Silver and Silver Cave

options.label: Mt. Silver Count
options.description: Number of badges/gyms required to access Mt. Silver and Silver Cave

options.label: Radio Tower Requirement
options.description: Sets the requirement for Team Rocket to take over the Goldenrod Radio Tower

options.label: Radio Tower Count
options.description: Number of badges/gyms at which Team Rocket takes over the Goldenrod Radio Tower

options.label: Route 44 Access Requirement
options.description: Sets the requirement to pass between Mahogany Town and Route 44

options.label: Route 44 Access Count
options.description: Sets the number of badges/gyms required to pass between Mahogany Town and Route 44

options.label: Magnet Train Access
options.description:
Sets the requirement to ride the Magnet Train

- Pass requires only the Pass
- Pass and Power requires the Pass and restoring power to Kanto by returning the Machine Part

options.label: Route 23 Restored
options.description:
Inserts a restored Route 23 (the cut Kanto area) between Victory Road's
southern exit and Victory Road Gate. Adds new wild encounters, a berry
tree, and two hidden items.

options.label: Flooded Mine
options.description:
Adds the Flooded Mine, a small cave connecting Cherrygrove City and
Route 32, with new wild encounters, three hidden items, and a TM.

options.label: Randomize Starting Town
options.description:
Randomly chooses a town to start in.
Any Pokemon Center except Indigo Plateau, Cinnabar Island and Silver Cave can be chosen. The Pokemon Centers at Union Cave and Rock Tunnel can also be chosen.
Lake of Rage will start you at its flypoint and cannot be chosen if gate entrances are randomized. Pallet Town will start you in front of Red's House.
When Pokemon Center entrances are randomized, the Pokemon Centers of Cherrygrove City, Viridian City, and Mahogany Town will be vanilla when the starting town is New Bark Town, Pallet Town, or Lake of Rage respectively.

Other settings may additionally restrict which Pokemon Centers can be chosen.

WARNING: Some starting towns without level scaling may produce difficult starts.

options.label: Starting Town Blocklist
options.description:
Specify places which cannot be chosen as a starting town. If you block every valid option, this list will do nothing.
Indigo Plateau, Cinnabar Island and Silver Cave cannot be chosen as starting towns and are not valid options.
"_Johto" and "_Kanto" are shortcuts for all Johto and Kanto towns respectively.
"Union Cave" and "Rock Tunnel" are valid starting towns.

options.label: Randomize Badges
options.description:
Shuffles gym badge locations into the pool
- Vanilla: Does not randomize gym badges
- Shuffle: Randomizes gym badges between gym leaders
- Completely Random: Randomizes badges with all other items

options.label: Randomize Hidden Items
options.description: Shuffles hidden item locations into the pool

options.label: Battle Tower Sanity
options.description:
Adds locations in the Battle Tower.

- off: no Battle Tower locations.
- tiers: 10 locations, one for completing each tier.
- tiers_and_trainers: the 10 tier locations plus one location per Battle Tower trainer (70 extra).

Tier N is logically gated behind access to N of the following: gyms, E4 and Red. Trainer locations share the gate
of whichever tier they are shuffled into for the seed.

WARNING: The Battle Tower is legit. Your team will be levelled down to match your tier, if needed. You cannot
use items from your bag, held items must all be different and the trainers have the best possible AI. Bringing in Pokemon with >= 600 BST requires the Battle Tower
Uber Pass, which will be shuffled into the item pool.

options.label: Battle Tower Progressive Tier Unlocks
options.description:
Locks Battle Tower tiers behind progressive unlock items.
Each item received unlocks the next tier in order; without them, all tiers
are immediately accessible. Only takes effect when battle_tower_sanity is on
or the Battle Tower goal is selected.

options.label: Require Itemfinder
options.description:
Hidden items require Itemfinder in logic

- Not Required: Hidden items do not require the Itemfinder at all
- Logically Required: Hidden items will expect you to have Itemfinder for logic but can be picked up without it
- Hard Required: Hidden items cannot be picked up without the Itemfinder

options.label: Item Pool Fill
options.description:
Changes the weight of non-progression items in the pool.

- Vanilla: weighted similarly to vanilla.
- Balanced: all weighted equally.
- Youngster: weighted to reflect a young trainer (weak items).
- Cooltrainer: weighted to reflect a cooltrainer (strong items).
- Shuckle: weighted to reflect a Shuckle (🐢).

options.label: Add Missing Useful Items
options.description: Adds useful items which are unobtainable to the pool, these replace filler

options.label: Route 32 Access Condition
options.description:
Sets the condition required to pass between the north and south parts of Route 32
- Egg from aide: Collect the Egg from the aide in the Violet City Pokemon Center after beating Falkner
- Any badge: Obtain any badge
- Any gym: Beat any gym
- Zephyr Badge: Obtain the Zephyr Badge
- None: No requirement

options.label: Dark Areas
options.description:
Sets which areas are dark until Flash is used

- _All includes all areas
- _Random has a 50% chance to include each area that is not already included

options.label: Victory Road Strength
options.description: If enabled, Strength is required to pass through Victory Road to Indigo Plateau.

options.label: Route 22 Access Requirement
options.description:
Sets the requirement to pass between Victory Road gate and Kanto
- Wake Snorlax: Wake the Snorlax outside of Diglett's Cave
- Badges: Requires the number of badges specified by route_22_access_count
- Gyms: Requires beating the number of gyms specified by route_22_access_count
- Become Champion: Defeat Lance and enter the Hall of Fame

This setting does nothing if Johto Only is enabled

options.label: Route 22 Access Count
options.description:
Sets the number of badges/gyms required to pass between Victory Road gate and Kanto
Only applies if Route 22 Access Requirement is set to badges or gyms

options.label: Red Gyarados Access
options.description:
Sets the access requirement for the red Gyarados
- Vanilla requires Surf
- Whirlpool requires Surf and Whirlpool
- Shore requires nothing

options.label: Route 2 Access
options.description:
Sets the roadblock for moving between the west of Route 2 and Diglett's cave
- Vanilla: Cut is required
- Ledge: A ledge is added north of Diglett's cave allowing east -> west access without Cut
- Open: No requirement

options.label: Route 3 Access
options.description:
Sets the roadblock for moving between Pewter City and Route 3
- Vanilla: No requirement
- Boulder Badge: The Boulder Badge is required to pass

options.label: Blackthorn Dark Cave Access
options.description:
Sets the roadblock for travelling from Route 31 to Blackthorn City through Dark Cave
- Vanilla: Traversal is not possible
- Waterfall: A waterfall is added to the Violet side of Dark Cave and a ledge is removed on the Blackthorn side,
allowing passage with Flash, Surf and Waterfall

options.label: National Park Access
options.description:
Sets the requirement to enter National Park
- Vanilla: No requirement
- Bicycle: The Bicycle is required

options.label: Route 42 Access
options.description:
Sets the requirement to traverse the water on Route 42
- Vanilla: Route 42 can be traversed with Surf
- Whirlpool: Access to Central Route 42 is blocked by a whirlpool
- Blocked: Access to Central Route 42 is completely blocked, requiring going through Mount Mortar instead.
Mount Mortar 1F gets an extra map connection between the Inside and Central Outside
- Whirlpool Open Mortar: Route 42 has whirlpools and Mount Mortar 1F has the extra map connection.

options.label: Mount Mortar Access
options.description:
Sets the requirement to pass through Mount Mortar east <> west
- Vanilla: No requirement
- Rock Smash: Rock Smash is required

options.label: Route 12 Access
options.description:
Sets the requirement to pass between the north and south parts of Route 12
- Vanilla: No requirement
- Weird Tree: Requires Squirtbottle, but can be bypassed with Surf
- Weird Tree Surf Block: Requires Squirtbottle and adds boulders to prevent surfing around

The roadblock is north of the path to Route 11

options.label: S.S. Aqua Access
options.description:
Sets the requirement to sail on the S.S. Aqua
- Vanilla: S.S. Ticket is required
- Lighthouse and Ticket: Healing Amphy in the Olivine lighthouse and the S.S Ticket are required

options.label: Route 30 Access
options.description:
Sets the requirement to end the Pokemon battle on Route 30
- Mr. Pokemon: Visit Mr. Pokemon in his house
- Mystery Egg: Return the Mystery Egg to Professor Elm

options.label: Route 30 Battle
options.description: Sets which directions the battle on Route 30 blocks

options.label: South Kanto Access
options.description:
Sets where the landslide that is normally south of Fuchsia City is located

Both can only be used if the condition is power restored.

options.label: South Kanto Condition
options.description: Sets the condition which clears the south Kanto landslide

options.label: Rematchsanity
options.description:
Adds the phone-trainer rematch fights as checks.

Rematches unlock in order as you hit story milestones (visiting Goldenrod / Olivine /
etc., clearing the Radio Tower, beating the Elite Four, restoring power to Kanto).
All rematches need the Pokegear and a Phone Card.

Picnicker Tiffany's rematches only count if Randomize Pokemon Requests is also on.

Joey's HP Up is given after his last rematch.

options.label: Kinda Early Surf
options.description:
Adds Surf as a logical requirement for: the Magnet Train, going east of Mahogany,
fighting Jasmine, the Rocket takeover of the Radio Tower, entering Tin Tower,
waking Snorlax, and entering the Kanto Gyms. Forced off if Randomize Starting Town,
Johto Only, or Entrance Randomization is enabled.

options.label: Randomize Wilds
options.description:
Randomizes species of wild Pokemon

- Base Forms: Ensures that at least every Pokemon that cannot be obtained through evolution is available in the wild
- Evolution Lines: Ensures that at least one Pokemon from each evolutionary line can be obtained in the wild
- Catch 'em All: Ensures that every Pokemon will be obtainable in the wild

If this setting is anything other than vanilla, bug catching contest encounters will be completely random.

options.label: Shared Wild Encounters
options.description:
Requires Wild Match Mode to be None, and has no effect otherwise or if wild Pokemon are not randomized.

Wild and bug catching contest encounters are generated from the multiworld seed instead of your own slot,
so every player who enables this will have identical wild encounters.

For identical tables, players must also match on: Randomize Wilds, Wild Encounter Blocklist, Encounter Grouping,
Time of Day Encounters, Encounter Slot Distribution and Dexsanity Starters,
and all must have or lack the Unown Hunt goal.
Unique Static Pokemon must be disabled, and type shortcuts in the blocklist require Randomize Types to be off.
Pokemon required by a player's own logic (for example trade requests or Ditto) may still differ.

options.label: Dexsanity
options.description:
Adds checks for catching Pokemon
Pokemon that cannot be logically obtained will never be included

options.label: Dexsanity Starters
options.description:
Controls how Dexsanity treats starter Pokemon

- Allow: Starter Pokemon will be allowed as Dexsanity checks
- Block: Starter Pokemon will not be allowed as Dexsanity Checks
- Available Early: Starter Pokemon will all be obtainable in the wild immediately, unless there is nowhere to obtain
wild Pokemon immediately

options.label: Dexsanity Logic
options.description:
Restricts which encounter sources may provide Pokemon for Dexsanity and Dexcountsanity locations.

Only applies when Dexsanity or Dexcountsanity is enabled.
Selected sources are further restricted by their own logic settings (e.g. Wild Encounter Methods Required).
If no Pokemon are available from the selected sources, falls back to the full logically available pool.

_Random has a 50% chance to include types which are not already included
_All will include all types

options.label: Dexcountsanity
options.description:
Adds checks for completing Pokedex milestones
This setting specifies number of caught Pokemon on which you'll get your last check

options.label: Dexcountsanity Step
options.description:
If Dexcountsanity is enabled, specifies the step interval at which your checks are placed.
For example, if you have Dexcountsanity 50 and Dexcountsanity Step 10, you will have checks at
10, 20, 30, 40 and 50 total Pokemon caught.

options.label: Dexcountsanity Leniency
options.description:
If Dexcountsanity is enabled, specifies the logic leniency for checks.
For example, if you set Dexcountsanity Leniency to 5 and have a Dexcountsanity check at 10, you will not be
logically required to obtain this check until you can obtain 15 Pokemon

Checks that would go over the total number of logically available Pokemon will be clamped to that limit

options.label: Wild Encounter Methods Required
options.description:
Sets which wild encounter types may be logically required

- Land: Pokemon encountered in grass and caves
- Surfing: Pokemon encountered while surfing
- Fishing: Pokemon encountered with any rod
- Headbutt: Pokemon encountered by headbutting trees
- Rock Smash: Pokemon encountered by smashing rocks
- Bug Catching Contest: Pokemon encountered in the National Park contest
- Swarm: Pokemon encountered during a swarm

_Random has a 50% chance to include types which are not already included
_All will include all types

Swarm encounters require Randomize Phone Calls to be enabled.
Roamers are NEVER in logic.

options.label: Enforce Wild Encounter Methods Logic
options.description:
Sets whether the game will prevent capture of Pokemon found through disabled wild encounter methods
Statics, roamers and contest encounters can always be caught

You can always re-catch Pokemon you have already caught

options.label: Trades Required
options.description: Specifies if in-game trades may be logically required

options.label: Randomize Lucky Number Show
options.description:
Adds the Radio Tower Lucky Number Show as three locations.

Three in-game trades are chosen at random; obtaining each traded Pokemon wins the
matching prize (1st/2nd/3rd).

options.label: Static Pokemon Required
options.description: Sets whether static Pokemon may be logically required

options.label: Evolution Methods Required
options.description:
Sets which types of evolutions may be logically required

_Random has a 50% chance to include types which are not already included
_All will include all types

options.label: Evolution Gym Levels
options.description:
Sets how many levels each accessible gym puts into logic for level (and Tyrogue) evolutions

For example, if you set this to 4 and have access to 5 gyms, evolutions up to level 20 would be in logic.

If Johto only is enabled the minimum for this setting is 8.

options.label: Breeding Method Required
options.description: Specifies which breeding methods may be logically required.

options.label: Enforce Breeding Methods Logic
options.description: Sets whether the game will prevent the breeding of Pokemon that do not match the selected breeding logic

options.label: Shopsanity
options.description:
Adds shop purchases as locations, items in shops are added to the item pool
- Johto Marts: Adds Johto Poke Marts, including the Goldenrod Dept. Store.
- Kanto Marts: Adds Kanto Poke Marts, including the Celadon Dept. Store.
- Blue Card: Adds the Blue Card prize shop, accessing this shop requires the Blue Card and buying items requires
points. Five Blue Card Points are added to the item pool. Points are not spent when purchasing.
- Game Corners: The Game Corner TM shops are added.
- Apricorns: Kurt's Apricorn Ball shop is added, each slot requires a different Apricorn. Apricorns are progression.
- _All: Includes all valid options.
- _Random: Each option that is not included has a 50% chance to be additionally included.

IMPORTANT NOTE: There is a non-randomized shop on Pokecenter 2F, you can always buy Poke Balls and Escape Ropes there.

options.label: Shopsanity Prices
options.description:
Sets how shop item prices are determined when Shopsanity is enabled
- Vanilla: Shop prices are unchanged
- Item Price: Shop prices are determined by the value of the item being sold
- Spheres: Shop prices are determined by sphere access
- Classification: Shop prices are determined by item classifications (Progression, Useful, Filler/Trap)
- Spheres and Classifications: Shop prices are determined by both sphere access and item classifications
- Completely Random: Shop prices will be completely random

options.label: Minimum Shopsanity Price
options.description: Sets the minimum cost of shop items when Shopsanity is enabled

options.label: Maximum Shopsanity Price
options.description: Sets the maximum cost of shop items when Shopsanity is enabled

options.label: Provide Shop Hints
options.description: Sends out hints when a randomized shop is accessed

options.label: Shopsanity Restrict Rare Candies
options.description: Makes Rare Candies in shops only purchasable once

options.label: Shopsanity X Items
options.description:
Determines how Shopsanity treats X Items
- Anywhere: X Items will be shuffled into the multiworld pool
- Any Shop: At least one of each X Item will be available for purchase in a local shop

NOTE: You cannot purchase any shop item repeatedly when Remote Items is active

options.label: Randomize Pokegear
options.description: Shuffles the Pokegear and cards into the pool

options.label: Randomize Berry Trees
options.description: Shuffles berry tree locations into the pool

options.label: Randomize Pokedex
options.description:
Sets whether the Pokedex is shuffled into the pool

The Pokedex is required for Dexsanity, Dexcountsanity, trades and Pokemon request locations.

options.label: Randomize Pokemon Requests
options.description:
Shuffles the items given by Bill's Grandpa after showing him specific Pokemon into the pool, as well as the reward
for showing a Magikarp to the fisher in the house at Lake of Rage

Optionally also randomizes the requested Pokemon, except the Magikarp

Trainers which need you to show them a Pokemon to get their phone number require both this option and Randomize Phone Call Items to be enabled.

options.label: Pokemon Request Logic
options.description:
Restricts which encounter sources may provide Pokemon for randomized requests and trades
(Bill's Grandpa, phone call trainers, in-game trades, etc.)

Only applies when Pokemon requests or trades are randomized.
Selected sources are further restricted by their own logic settings (e.g. Wild Encounter Methods Required).
If no Pokemon are available from the selected sources, falls back to the full logically available pool.

_Random has a 50% chance to include types which are not already included
_All will include all types

options.label: Randomize Phone Call Items
options.description:
Shuffles gift items from phone trainers into the item pool.

You need the Pokegear to register phone numbers and the Phone Card to make and receive calls.

Trainers that ask to see a Pokemon to exchange numbers are only included if Randomize Pokemon Requests is also on.

options.label: Momsanity
options.description:
Adds 10 locations for the items Mom buys you at different money thresholds
while she's saving your money.

Logically requires access to Mom, and either giving the Mystery Egg to Elm or
reaching Route 31 (where Mom calls you). Each item logically requires an
increasing number of accessible gyms, starting at zero.

Items that go in your bag will be deposited into the PC. Items which do not go
in your bag will be in the BANK OF MOM collection box in the PC.

You can deposit money into the BANK OF MOM by talking to Mom after giving Elm
the Mystery Egg or her having called you on Route 31.

options.label: Phone Call Mode
options.description:
Controls how in-game phone calls work.

- Vanilla: Calling a trainer only does something useful at the right day and time of day.
  Trainers calling you is random. WARNING: triggering specific phone calls this way can
  require resetting the clock, toggling DST, and a lot of patience.

- Simple: Calling any trainer always does something useful if available. Trainers calling
  you skip the random roll and offer their action directly.

options.label: Randomize Fly Unlocks
options.description: Shuffles Fly destination unlocks into the pool

options.label: Randomize Bug Catching Contest
options.description:
Shuffles the bug catching contest prizes into the pool
- All: shuffles all prizes into the pool. WARNING: It can be very difficult to get second or third place.
- Combine second and third: Combines second and third place into a single prize. Shuffles 1st, 2nd+3rd and 4th.
- Participate: Shuffles a single participation award into the pool, which is obtained by completing the contest.

options.label: Randomize Starters
options.description: Randomizes species of starter Pokemon

options.label: Starter Blocklist
options.description:
These Pokemon will not be chosen as starter Pokemon
Does nothing if starter Pokemon are not randomized
Blocklists are best effort, other constraints may cause them to be ignored

options.label: Starter BST Range
options.description: If you chose Base Stat Mode for your starters, what is the average base stat total you want your available starters to be?

options.label: Wild Encounter Blocklist
options.description:
These Pokemon will not appear in the wild
Does nothing if wild Pokemon are not randomized
Blocklists are best effort, other constraints may cause them to be ignored
This setting also applies to bug catching contest encounters

options.label: Wild Match Mode
options.description:
Controls how randomized wild Pokemon are matched to the vanilla encounters they replace.

- None: Wild Pokemon are replaced with no regard for the encounter they replace
- Match Types: Wild Pokemon are replaced with Pokemon of the same type
- Match Base Stats: Wild Pokemon are replaced with Pokemon of similar base stat totals
- Match Types and Base Stats: Wild Pokemon are replaced with Pokemon of the same type and similar base stat totals

This setting has no effect if wild Pokemon are not randomized.

options.label: Encounter Grouping
options.description:
Determines how randomized wild Pokemon are grouped in encounter tables.

- All Split: Each encounter area will have each slot randomized separately. For example, grass areas will have seven
  randomized encounter slots.
- One to One: Each encounter area will retain its vanilla slot grouping. For example, if an area has two encounters
  in vanilla, it will be randomized as two slots.
- One per Method: Each encounter method on a route will be treated as a single slot. For example, the grass on a route
  will contain only a single encounter. Each rod is a separate encounter.

This setting has no effect if wild Pokemon are not randomized.
This setting does not affect the bug catching contest.

options.label: Time of Day Encounters
options.description:
When enabled, land encounters vary by time of day (morning/day/night), and
fishing encounters that vary by time of day in vanilla vary by day/night.
Each time period is randomized independently.

When disabled, all time periods use the same encounters.

options.label: Unlockable Time of Day
options.description:
When enabled, the player must find Morn, Day and Nite items to access
land and fishing encounters for those time periods. You start with one of these at random.

Requires Time of Day Encounters to be enabled.

Time of day can be adjusted using the Pokegear.

options.label: Force Fully Evolved
options.description:
When an opponent uses a Pokemon of the specified level or higher, restricts the species to only fully evolved Pokemon.

Evolution Level instead evolves each opponent Pokemon into the species it would naturally have become at its level,
so a species is never used at or above the level it would evolve at. Species that do not evolve by level are
unaffected.

Only applies when trainer parties are randomized.

options.label: Encounter Slot Distribution
options.description:
Sets how the Pokemon encounter slots in an area are distributed.

Remove 1%'s modifies grass/cave encounters to 30%/25%/20%/10%/5%/5%/5% and does not modify any others.
Balanced sets the following:
    Grass/Cave: 20%/20%/15%/15%/10%/10%/10%
    Surf (unchanged): 60%/30%/10%
    Headbutt:  20%/20%/20%/15%/15%/10%
    Rock Smash: 70%/30%
    Fishing (unchanged):
        Old Rod: 70%/15%/15%
        Good Rod: 35%/35%/20%/10%
        Super Rod: 40%/30%/20%/10%
    Bug Catching Contest (unchanged): 20%/20%/10%/10%/10%/10%/5%/5%/5%/5%
Equal sets all encounter slots to have (almost) equal probability.

options.label: Randomize Static Pokemon
options.description:
Randomizes species of static Pokemon encounters
This includes overworld Pokemon, gift Pokemon and gift egg Pokemon

Match Types: Pokemon are replaced with Pokemon of the same type
Match Base Stats: Pokemon are replaced with Pokemon of similar base stat totals
Match Types and Base Stats: Pokemon are replaced with Pokemon of the same type and similar base stat totals
Completely Random: Pokemon are replaced with completely random Pokemon

NOTE: If this setting is disabled, the Odd Egg will still be fixed to a single possible Pokemon

options.label: Static Blocklist
options.description:
These Pokemon will not appear as static overworld encounters, gift eggs, gift Pokemon or received trade Pokemon
Only applies to static Pokemon or received trade Pokemon that are randomized
Blocklists are best effort, other constraints may cause them to be ignored

options.label: Unique Static Pokemon
options.description:
Makes static encounter species globally unique. A species rolled into a static slot will not
appear in another static slot, and will be excluded from wild encounters. If evolution methods
are logically required, pre-evolutions of the static species (along logically-required evolution
paths) are also excluded from wilds. If breeding methods are logically required, any Pokemon
whose egg produces a static species is also excluded from wilds.

Only applies to static slots that are in logic. Does nothing if static Pokemon are not randomized or not required.

- Legendaries Only: only applies to the four legendary static slots (Suicune, Lugia, Ho-Oh, Celebi)
- Legendaries and Uniques: the legendary slots plus the unique overworld encounters
(Sudowoodo, Red Gyarados, Snorlax, Lapras)
- All: applies to every static slot

options.label: Level Scaling
options.description:
Sets whether Trainer, Wild Pokemon and Static Pokemon levels are scaled based on sphere access.

- Off: Vanilla levels are used.
- Spheres: Levels are scaled based on sphere access only.
- Spheres and Distance: Levels are scaled based on both sphere access and distance from starting town.

options.label: Level Curve
options.description:
When level scaling is enabled, use a custom level curve instead of deriving levels from vanilla data.
The curve distributes levels from min to max across all scaled levels (trainers, statics, and wild encounters).

- Vanilla: Use vanilla levels as the basis for scaling.
- Linear: Levels increase at a constant rate from min to max.
- Sqrt: Levels rise quickly early then taper off. Harder early game, compressed late game.
- Quadratic: Levels stay low early then rise steeply. Easier early game, rapid late-game growth.
- S Curve: Slow start, fast middle, slow finish.

options.label: Level Curve Min Level
options.description: The starting level for the custom level curve. Only used when Level Curve is not vanilla.

options.label: Level Curve Max Level
options.description:
The ending level for the custom level curve. Only used when Level Curve is not vanilla.

Red will be scaled so his lowest level matches this value. Wilds and statics will be scaled up to 2/3 of this value.

NOTE: Trainers are scaled based on their lowest level party member, so they can have levels above this value.

options.label: Lock Kanto Gyms
options.description:
Logically lock entering all Kanto gyms, Mt. Moon and Trainer House behind access to a high level Pokemon, included locations:
- Snorlax
- Ho-oh
- Lugia
- Suicune
- Silver Cave entrance
- Victory Road

You can still enter gyms, Mt. Moon and Trainer House without access to any of these.

NOTE: This option is automatically disabled when Level Scaling is enabled.

options.label: Randomize Trades
options.description:
Randomizes species of in-game trades
Received species respect the Static Blocklist

options.label: Randomize Trainer Parties
options.description:
Randomizes Pokemon in enemy trainer parties

- Match Types: Pokemon are replaced with Pokemon of the same type
- Match Base Stats: Pokemon are replaced with Pokemon of similar base stat totals
- Match Types and Base Stats: Pokemon are replaced with Pokemon of the same type and similar base stat totals
- Completely Random: Pokemon are replaced with completely random Pokemon

options.label: Trainer Party Blocklist
options.description:
These Pokemon will not appear in enemy trainer parties
Does nothing if trainer parties are not randomized
Blocklists are best effort, other constraints may cause them to be ignored

options.label: Boost Trainer Pokemon Levels
options.description:
Boost levels of every trainer's Pokemon. There are 2 different boost modes:
Percentage Boost: Increases every trainer Pokemon's level by the boost percentage.
Set Min Level: Trainer Pokemon will be the specified level or higher.

options.label: Trainer Level Boost Value
options.description:
This Value only works if Boost Trainer Pokemon Levels is being used.
The meaning of this value depends on Trainer Boost Mode.

Percentage Boost: This value represents the boost amount percentage
Set Min Level: Trainer Pokemon will never be lower than this level

options.label: Randomize Learnsets
options.description:
- Vanilla: Vanilla learnsets
- Randomize: Random learnsets
- Start With Four Moves: Random learnsets with 4 starting moves

options.label: Metronome Only
options.description:
Only Metronome is usable in battle, PP is infinite
You can still teach HMs and useful TMs

options.label: Move Learnset Type Bias
options.description:
This option will have an effect only if Randomize Learnset option is enabled.

Percentage chance of each move in a Pokemon's learnset to match one of its types.
Default value is none (-1). This means there will be no bias.
The lowest possible type matching value is 0. This means there will be no STAB moves in a Pokemon's learnset.
If set to 100 all moves that a Pokemon will learn by levelling up will match one of its types.

options.label: Randomize Moves
options.description:
Randomizes the properties of moves.

The following options can be provided:
- Power Restricted: Multiplies the power of each move by a random number between 0.5 and 1.5
- PP Restricted: Adds or subtracts 0, 5 or 10 from original move PP. Base PP is limited to 5-40.
- Power Full: Randomizes the power of each move in the range 20-150.
  Multi hit moves have their power divided by average hit count.
- PP Full: Randomizes the PP of each move in the range 5-40.
- Accuracy: Randomizes the accuracy of each move. Accuracy has a 70% chance to be 100% for each move,
  otherwise it is linearly distributed in the range 30-100.
- Type: Randomizes the type of each move.
- _All includes all options.
- _Random has a 50% chance to include each option that is not already included.
- _RandomExcludingAccuracy has a 50% chance to include each option except Accuracy.

Full options override Restricted options.

options.label: Randomize Type Chart
options.description:
Randomizes the type matchup chart
- Vanilla: Type matchups are unchanged
- Shuffle: Shuffles type matchups around, keeping the same number of each possible matchup
- Completely Random: Generates a random matchup for each type pair. WARNING: This can result in a lot of immunities

options.label: Physical/Special Split
options.description:
Sets how moves are determined to be Physical or Special
- Vanilla: Determined by move type, for example: all Fire moves are Special
- Modern: Determined by the move, for example: Flame Wheel is Physical and Ember is Special
- Random by type: Vanilla, but shuffled randomly for each type
- Random by move: Modern, but shuffled randomly for each move

options.label: Randomize TM Moves
options.description: Randomizes the moves available as TMs

options.label: TM Plando
options.description:
Specify what move a TM will contain.
TMs 02 and 08 can never be plandoed. This also means Headbutt and Rock Smash cannot be plandoed onto other TMs.
If Dexsanity or Dexcountsanity are enabled, and Sweet Scent hasn't been plandoed, it will be forced to TM12.
This option takes priority over the TM Blocklist and vanilla TMs, and is ignored in Metronome Only mode.

A single move or a weighted dict of moves can be provided per TM:
tm_plando:
  1: Dynamicpunch
  3: Curse
  10:
    Ice Beam: 50
    Blizzard: 50

options.label: TM Same Type Compatibility
options.description:
Percent chance for Pokemon to be compatible with each TM whose move type matches one of the Pokemon's types.
Headbutt and Rock Smash are considered HMs when applying compatibility.

options.label: TM Other Type Compatibility
options.description:
Percent chance for Pokemon to be compatible with each TM whose move type does not match any of the Pokemon's types.
Headbutt and Rock Smash are considered HMs when applying compatibility.

options.label: HM Same Type Compatibility
options.description:
Percent chance for Pokemon to be compatible with each HM whose move type matches one of the Pokemon's types.
Headbutt and Rock Smash are considered HMs when applying compatibility.

You can look up HM compatible Pokemon in the Pokedex using the search function.

options.label: HM Other Type Compatibility
options.description:
Percent chance for Pokemon to be compatible with each HM whose move type does not match any of the Pokemon's types.
Headbutt and Rock Smash are considered HMs when applying compatibility.

You can look up HM compatible Pokemon in the Pokedex using the search function.

options.label: HM Compatibility Override
options.description:
Allows overriding compatibility percentage for specific HMs

Uses the following format:
hm_compatibility_override:
  Headbutt: 10
  Fly: 100
  Flash: 0

Headbutt and Rock Smash are considered HMs for this setting.

options.label: HM Power Cap
options.description:
Lowers the power of damaging HM moves that exceed the set power down to match it.
Headbutt and Rock Smash are considered HMs for this setting.

options.label: Field Moves Always Usable
options.description:
Decouples TM/HM Compatibility for Battle Moves and Field Moves.
If enabled, Field Moves will always be considered usable, regardless of TM or HM compatibility. Badge requirements still apply.

options.label: Randomize Base Stats
options.description:
- Vanilla: Vanilla base stats
- Keep BST: Random base stats, but base stat total is preserved
- Completely Random: Base stats and BST are completely random

options.label: Make Random Base Stats Multiples of 5
options.description:
When randomizing base stats, aim to make the new base stats multiples of 5.
When using Keep BST, any remainder will be added to one stat.

options.label: Base Stats Evolution Mode
options.description:
- Independent: Base stats are randomized separately for every Pokemon, so evolving can be a downgrade
- Follow Evolutions: Pokemon inherit their pre-evolution's stat spread, and evolving always increases BST

Has no effect when Randomize Evolution is enabled, as random evolutions already increase base stat total.

options.label: Randomize Types
options.description:
- Vanilla: Vanilla Pokemon types
- Follow Evolutions: Types are randomized but preserved when evolved
- Completely Random: Types are completely random

options.label: Shared Primary Type
options.description: If types are randomized, all Pokemon will share this type

options.label: Randomize Evolution
options.description:
- Vanilla: Pokemon evolve into the same Pokemon they do in vanilla
- Match a Type: Pokemon evolve into a random Pokemon with a higher base stat total, that shares at least one type with it.
- Increase BST: Pokemon evolve into a random Pokemon with a higher base stat total.

Note: If random BST, random types, or the evolution blocklist cause a Pokemon to have no valid evolution within
your chosen setting here, it will evolve into the closest available thing to a valid evolution.

Note: All Pokemon will be standardized to the medium-fast EXP curve when any evolution randomization is enabled.

options.label: Convergent Evolution
options.description:
Random evolution can cause multiple Pokemon to evolve into the same Pokemon.
- Avoid: Each Pokemon can only evolve from one Pokemon.
- Allow: Multiple Pokemon can evolve into the same Pokemon.

options.label: Evolution Blocklist
options.description:
No Pokemon will evolve into these Pokemon. Does nothing if evolution is not randomized.
Blocklists are best effort, other constraints may cause them to be ignored.

options.label: Maximum Evolution Level
options.description: Reduces all level-based evolution levels to at most the specified level.

options.label: Randomize Breeding
options.description:
- Vanilla: Breeding is unchanged
- Random Line Base: Each Pokemon will produce eggs for a random base Pokemon that evolves into it
- Random Any Base: Each Pokemon will produce eggs for a random base Pokemon
- Random Lower BST: Each Pokemon will produce eggs for a random Pokemon with equal or lower BST
- Completely Random: Each Pokemon will produce eggs for a random Pokemon

options.label: Breeding Blocklist
options.description:
No Pokemon will produce eggs containing these Pokemon.
Blocklists are best effort, other constraints may cause them to be ignored.

options.label: Modify Palettes
options.description:
- Vanilla: Vanilla Pokemon color palettes
- Match Types: Color palettes match Pokemon Type
- Randomize: Color palettes are completely random
- Swap Shiny: Regular Pokemon use shiny palettes and vice versa
- Gold and Silver: For the Pokemon whose palettes changed between Gold/Silver and Crystal, restores their old palette

options.label: Randomize Music
options.description:
Randomize all music
- Shuffle will map each music track to a new track
- Completely Random will map each music area to a new track

options.label: Move Blocklist
options.description:
Pokemon won't learn these moves via learnsets.
Moves should be provided in the form: "Ice Beam"
Does not apply to vanilla learnsets

options.label: TM Blocklist
options.description:
No TM will contain these moves.
Moves should be provided in the form: "Ice Beam"
Does not apply to vanilla TMs

options.label: Free Fly Location
options.description:
- Free Fly: Unlocks a random Fly destination when Fly is obtained.
- Free Fly and Map Card: Additionally unlocks a random Fly destination after obtaining both the Pokegear and Map Card.
- Map Card: Unlocks a single random Fly destination only after obtaining both the Pokegear and Map card.

options.label: Fly Location Blocklist
options.description:
These locations won't be given to you as fly locations, either as your free one or from receiving the map card.
Locations should be provided in the form: "Ecruteak City"
If you blocklist enough locations that there aren't enough locations left for your total number of free fly locations, the blocklist will simply do nothing
"_Johto" and "_Kanto" are shortcuts for all Johto and Kanto towns respectively

options.label: Early Fly
options.description:
HM02 Fly will be placed early in the game
If this option is enabled, you will be able to Fly before being forced to use an item to progress
Early Fly is a best effort setting, if Fly and its badge cannot be placed early, then they will be placed
    randomly

options.label: Require Flash
options.description:
Determines if the ability to use Flash is required to traverse dark areas

- Not Required: Dark areas do not require Flash at all
- Logically Required: Dark areas will expect you to be able to use Flash for logic, but you can traverse them without
- Hard Required: You will not be able to traverse dark areas without the ability to use Flash there

options.label: HM Badge Requirements
options.description:
- Vanilla: HMs require their vanilla badges
- No Badges: HMs do not require a badge to use
