options.label: Include Fight Club
options.description: Whether to include both Fight Club instances with each level as an individual location check.

options.label: Include FUZZ
options.description: Whether to include both FUZZ instances with each level as an individual location check.

options.label: Include Insurance Fraud
options.description: Whether to include both Insurance Fraud instances with each level as an individual location check.

options.label: Include Heli Assault
options.description: Whether to include both Heli Assault instances with each level as an individual location check.

options.label: Include Hitman Lists
options.description: Whether to include all Hitman lists with each target as an individual location check.

options.label: Include Mayhem
options.description: Whether to include both Mayhem instances with each level as an individual location check.

options.label: Include Septic Avenger
options.description: Whether to include both Septic Avenger instances with each level as an individual location check.

options.label: Include Snatch
options.description: Whether to include both Snatch instances with each level as an individual location check.

options.label: Include Trail Blazing
options.description: Whether to include both Trail Blazing instances with each level as an individual location check.

options.label: Include CDs
options.description: Whether to include all 50 CDs as individual location checks.

options.label: Includes Races
options.description:
Whether to include all races as individual location checks.

Each race will include a location for the Bronze, Silver and Gold medal.

options.label: Include Tags
options.description: Whether to include all 50 tags as individual location checks.

options.label: Trap Chance
options.description: Percentage chance that you'll drop a trap item.

options.label: Bonus Respect Percentage
options.description:
Percentage of bonus respect points to add to the item pool.

Very useful to make it easier to find more respect to progress.

options.label: Style Level Location Count
options.description: Amount of player style level locations to include.

options.label: Allow progression items on high Style Level locations
options.description:
Allow progression items on high Style Level locations.

NOTE: Getting to Style Level 9 and 10 requires A LOT of money! Keep that in mind when enabling this option!

options.label: Money Filler Item Weight
options.description: The weights of a money filler item to be included in the item pool.

options.label: Weapon Filler Item Weight
options.description: The weights of a weapon filler item to be included in the item pool.

options.label: Vehicle Filler Item Weight
options.description: The weights of a vehicle filler item to be included in the item pool.

options.label: Misc. Filler Item Weight
options.description: The weights of a misc. filler item to be included in the item pool.

options.label: Include notoriety trap items
options.description: Whether to include notoriety traps in the item pool.

options.label: Include weather trap items
options.description: Whether to include permanent weather traps in the item pool.

worlds.game: Sly Cooper and the Thievius Raccoonus

options.label: Unlock Clockwerk
options.description: What you need to do to unlock Cold Heart of Hate to defeat Clockwerk

options.label: Fast Clockwerk
options.description: If enabled, unlocking Cold Heart of Hate will give you access directly to the Clockwerk boss fight skipping all the previous levels.

options.label: Requiredbosses
options.description:
How many members of the Fiendish Five you need to defeat before Cold Heart of Hate is unlocked.
Only used if boss victories is selected as the Unlock Clockwerk option.

options.label: Maxpages
options.description:
How many pages are available to collect in the multiworld.
These pages are NOT the same as the normal pages that give you thief moves.
Only used if page hunt is selected as the Unlock Clockwerk option.
Note that this option requires more locations than usual. Cluesanity is recommended.

options.label: Requiredpages
options.description:
How many pages of the Thievius Raccoonus you need to collect before Cold Heart of Hate is unlocked.
These pages are NOT the same as the normal pages that give you thief moves.
Only used if page hunt is selected as the Unlock Clockwerk option.

options.label: Starting Episode
options.description:
Determines which episode you will start in. You will be able to do the initial level for it, but
will only be able to continue if you receive a key for that episode (or unlock a different episode)
from a location within it. Avoid Early BK is suggested if you want to avoid early stuck points.

options.label: Include Hourglasses
options.description: If enabled, Hourglasses are included in the locations.

options.label: Hourglasses Require Roll
options.description:
Some Hourglasses are tough without the Roll move.
If enabled, at least one Progressive Roll will logically be required for Hourglasses.

options.label: Avoid Early BK
options.description:
Determines if you will start with 1 key for your chosen starting episode.
If all is selected, you are given 1 key for a random episode.

options.label: Exclude Minigames
options.description:
Choose which minigames types you want to exclude as locations.
Crabs: Treasure in the Depths
Races: At the Dog Track, A Desperate Race
Turrets: Murray's Big Gamble, The King of the Hill
Hover Blasters: A Ghastly Voyage, Rapid Fire Assault
Chicken Killing: Down Home Cooking
Swamp Skiff: Piranha Lake

options.label: Minigame Caches
options.description:
Determines how many additional "minigame cache" checks that minigame levels send when completed.
Minigame levels will still have a key location even if this is set to 0.
This is ignored for any minigame levels excluded above. Allows a range from 0-10.

options.label: Location Cluesanity Bundle Size
options.description:
Determines how many bottles you need to collect for each check.
Set to 0 to disable. Allows a range between 0 and 5.

options.label: Item Cluesanity Bundle Size
options.description:
Determines how many bottles you will receive for a given level.
Set to 0 to disable. Allows a range between 0 and 5.

options.label: Enable Tricks
options.description:
This option allows you to enable alternative forms of logic to access parts of the game via tricks.
Intended for use by people who know speedrun tricks already, but if you would like to learn, watch an
Any% run of the game for reference on how to do the below tricks.

Tide of Terror supports tot_second_half_early and tot_raleigh_early.
Sunset Snake Eyes supports sse_second_half_early and sse_muggshot_early.
Vicious Voodoo only supports vv_second_half early as Mz. Ruby does not have known methods of early access.
Fire in the Sky supports fits_second_half_early and fits_panda_early.
Additionally, an 8th trick unseen_foe_invis_skip is supported which puts all Unseen Foe locations into logic
without requiring any progressive invisibility items.

Including any of the tricks below will potentially require you to do those tricks to progress, depending
on the randomization.

options.label: Cutscene Skip
options.description:
Automatically skips dialogue and FMV cutscenes if enabled.
Dialogue can be skipped with the R2 button whether this option is on or off.

options.label: Include Traps
options.description:
Determines the chance for a filler item to become a trap.
Set it to 0 for no traps.

options.label: Ice Physics Trap Weight
options.description:
The weight of ice physics traps in the trap pool.
Ice physics traps turn on the low friction cheat code for 10 seconds.

options.label: Speed Change Trap Weight
options.description:
The weight of speed change traps in the trap pool.
Speed change traps change the game speed for 10 seconds.

options.label: Invisibility Trap Weight
options.description:
The weight of invisibility traps in the trap pool.
Invisibility traps turn Sly completely invisible for 10 seconds.

options.label: Ball Trap Weight
options.description:
The weight of ball traps in the trap pool.
Ball traps force Sly to stay in the roll form for 10 seconds.

options.label: Keysanity
options.description: If disabled, keys that are used within dungeons can only be found in their respective dungeons.

options.label: Include Hidden Panels
options.description:
Hidden panels can have any item; the star pieces normally hidden under them are added to the item pool. To flip
hidden panels, you need Super Boots or Ultra Hammer.

options.label: Gear Shuffle
options.description:
Vanilla: Gear (Boots and Hammers) appear in their vanilla locations
Gear Location Shuffle: Gear is shuffled amongst the upgrade chests and the bush in Jr. Troopa's playground
Full Shuffle: Gear can be anywhere.

options.label: Include Trading Event Rewards
options.description:
Adds the 3 rewards obtained for doing the Trading Toad quests (started via Koopa Village's radio) into the item
pool. These checks are available with 1, 3, and 5 star spirits saved.

options.label: Koopa Koot Favors
options.description:
Koopa Koot's Favors unlock after ridding the village of the Fuzzies, and three more are unlocked per star spirit
saved up to 6 star spirits.
Vanilla: Koopa Koot Favor rewards and quest items are unshuffled.
Shuffle rewards: Shuffle the favor rewards, but not the key items for his quests.
Full Shuffle: Shuffle the rewards AND the quest key items.

options.label: Shuffle Favor Coins
options.description:
Coins from Koopa Koot's favor rewards are included in the item pool.
Only has an effect when Koopa Koot's rewards are shuffled.

options.label: Shuffle Overworld Coins
options.description: Overworld coins are included in the item pool

options.label: Shuffle Foliage Coins
options.description:
Coins from bushes and trees are included in the item pool.
It's recommended to turn on 'Foliage Item Hints' with this setting.

options.label: Shuffle Coin Blocks
options.description: Single coin blocks are included in the item pool

options.label: Shopsanity
options.description:
Shop items are included in the item pool.
This includes regular item shops, Rowf's badge shop, and Merlow's star piece trade

options.label: Dojo Rewards
options.description:
Number of Dojo fights with randomized rewards. The logic can only expect you to do the 2nd fight with 1 star
spirit saved. The three Master fights are only in logic after you have 3, 4, and 5 star spirits saved.

options.label: Partner Upgrades
options.description:
Vanilla: Partners are upgraded through super blocks as usual.
Super Block Locations: Super blocks are replaced by item blocks that give partner specific upgrade items.
Full Shuffle: Super blocks are replaced with item blocks and specific partner upgrades are added as
items in the pool.

options.label: Letter Delivery Rewards
options.description:
Vanilla: Letter rewards remain unshuffled.
Vanilla Letter Chain: Shuffle delivery rewards, but don't shuffle anything in the long letter chain.
Final Letter Chain Reward: Shuffle letter delivery rewards and the final reward of the long letter chain.
Full shuffle: Every letter delivery reward is shuffled, effectively removing the letter
chain as each letter in the chain is shuffled.

options.label: Shuffle Super/Multicoin Blocks
options.description:
Off: Super Blocks and Multicoin blocks appear in their usual locations
Shuffle: Shuffles the locations of the Super Blocks and Multicoin Brick Blocks together
Anywhere: Multi coin blocks can be shuffled into non-block locations, which turns them into 'Coin Bag' items that
grant you 10 coins.

options.label: Rowf Items in Logic
options.description:
Determines how many sets of items sold by Rowf are candidates for progression items.
He sells 4 items initially, and 3 more for each Star Spirit up to saved 4 Spirits, up to 16 total items.
Note: You can talk to him and request he change his offerings.

options.label: Merlow Items in Logic
options.description:
Determines whether Merlow's Star Piece rewards can be required for progression. The items that you buy directly
are never progression items. This is specifically for the rewards which are granted after spending X Star Pieces.

options.label: Rip Cheato Items In Logic
options.description:
Number of items sold by Rip Cheato that can be required by logic.
Items in logic will always be sold by him before the out of logic ones.

options.label: Local Consumables Percentage
options.description:
A percentage of consumable items will remain in the player's world instead of being shuffled into the multiworld.
This can prevent other people from getting too many of your filler items, as well as make it easier to restock your
inventory without farming items from enemies or using a potentially limited variety of consumables.

options.label: Shuffle Partners
options.description: Partners become items in the item pool, and you get an item where you would normally get a partner.

options.label: Partners Always Usable
options.description: All partner field abilities are available to use even before you have unlocked them.

options.label: Start With Random Partners
options.description: Start with a random set of partners.

options.label: Number of Starting Partners
options.description: Number of random partners you start with, from 1 to 8

options.label: Start With Goombario
options.description: Have Goombario as a starting partner. You must have at least one partner selected or be given a random one.

options.label: Start With Kooper
options.description: Have Kooper as a starting partner. You must have at least one partner selected or be given a random one.

options.label: Start With Bombette
options.description: Have Bombette as a starting partner. You must have at least one partner selected or be given a random one.

options.label: Start With Parakarry
options.description: Have Parakarry as a starting partner. You must have at least one partner selected or be given a random one.

options.label: Start With Bow
options.description: Have Bow as a starting partner. You must have at least one partner selected or be given a random one.

options.label: Start With Watt
options.description: Have Watt as a starting partner. You must have at least one partner selected or be given a random one.

options.label: Start With Sushie
options.description: Have Sushie as a starting partner. You must have at least one partner selected or be given a random one.

options.label: Start With Lakilester
options.description: Have Lakilester as a starting partner. You must have at least one partner selected or be given a random one.

options.label: Badges BP
options.description:
Vanilla: Badges have their original Badge Point (BP) costs.
Balanced Random: Random BP costs 1-8, but weighted so most are +/-2 from vanilla.
Shuffled: Original BP costs are shuffled together.
Fully Random: Random BP costs from 1-6, unweighted.

options.label: Badges FP
options.description:
Vanilla: Abilities granted by badges have their original Flower Point (FP) costs.
Shuffled: Original FP costs are shuffled together.
Balanced Random: Random FP costs 1-7, but weighted so most are +/-2 from vanilla.
Fully Random: Random FP costs from 1-7, unweighted.

options.label: Partners FP
options.description:
Vanilla: Partner special attacks have their original Flower Point (FP) costs.
Shuffled: Original FP values are shuffled together.
Balanced Random: Random FP values 1-8, but weighted so most are +/-2 from vanilla.
Fully Random: Random FP values from 1-8, unweighted.

options.label: SP Costs
options.description:
Vanilla: Star Spirit abilities have their original Star Power (SP) costs.
Shuffled: Original SP costs are shuffled together.
Balanced Random: Random SP costs 1-3, but weighted so most are +/-1 from vanilla.
Fully Random: Random SP costs from 1-3, unweighted.

options.label: Mystery
options.description:
Vanilla: Mystery will pull from the vanilla item pool (one of six basic items).
Random Pick: Mystery will be a random item for the full playthrough.
Random Per Use: Mystery will be a random item on every use.

options.label: Shuffle Battle Formations
options.description:
Shuffles which enemies you encounter and in what number.
Enemies are limited to those that normally appear in the area.

options.label: Randomize Puzzles
options.description:
Randomizes most of the game's puzzles.
See https://github.com/icebound777/PMR-SeedGenerator/wiki/Random-Puzzles for a full list.

options.label: Shuffle Bosses
options.description:
Shuffles end of chapter bosses. While enabled, Mario can run on the first turn of a boss battle.
Note: This is not yet implemented and will fail to generate if set to True.

options.label: Blooper Damage Requirements
options.description:
There are 3 Blooper fights. Regardless of what order you visit the fight locations, you always fight Blooper,
then Electro Blooper, then Super Blooper. This setting can add logic such that you are able to deal enough damage
per turn with jump and partner attacks to comfortably defeat all 3 Bloopers before needing to defeat any of them.
Note that damage is calculated only by partners and boot upgrades, not badges or partner upgrades/abilities.
None: No logical requirements to defeat Bloopers
Low: 3 damage per turn required
Medium: 6 damage per turn required
High: 9 damage per turn required

options.label: Enemy Difficulty
options.description:
Vanilla: Original enemy stats.
Shuffle Chapter Difficulty: Each chapter is assigned a new number, enemies are scaled accordingly.
Progressive Scaling: Enemies scale as Mario gains more progression items and partners.

options.label: Enemy Difficulty
options.description: Increases the damage done by enemy attacks.

options.label: Cap Enemy XP
options.description: Limits the amount of XP per defeated enemy to 5.

options.label: XP Multiplier
options.description:
Increase or decrease the star points gained from enemies. Double the desired value for this setting.
ex: if you want double XP, set this to 4; for vanilla XP, set this to 2

options.label: No Save Blocks
options.description: Remove save blocks from the game. You can still save at the end of each chapter.

options.label: No Heart Blocks
options.description: Remove heart blocks from the game

options.label: No Healing Items
options.description: HP/FP restoring items will have no effect.

options.label: One Hit KO
options.description: Mario will die instantly from an enemy attack if a block action command is failed

options.label: Drop Star Points
options.description:
Mario will drop star points when running away from battle.
Equipping the Runaway Pay badge will prevent him from dropping star points.

options.label: No Healing Items
options.description: Increases Mario's attack power with boots or hammer attacks the more badges of similar type he wears.

options.label: Merlow Rewards Pricing
options.description:
Cheap: Rewards every 5 star pieces spent, up to 30 total.
Normal: Rewards every 10 star pieces spent, up to 60 total.

options.label: Chet Rippo Available
options.description: Determines if Chet Rippo, the shady NPC who you can pay to reallocate Mario's stats, appears in Toad Town.

options.label: Bowser Door Quiz
options.description:
Quiz: The second Bowser door in Bowser's castle has a quiz. Pass it or be forced to fight the anti-guy unit.
Anti Guys Unit: The second Bowser door in Bowser's castle has no quiz; you must fight the anti guys unit.
Skip: The second Bowser door in Bowser's castle is open as though the quiz has already been completed.

options.label: Kent C. Koopa
options.description:
Blocks Pleasant Path: You must pay 50 coins or defeat him to get into Pleasant Path.
Must Defeat: You must defeat him to get into Pleasant Path. Expects two chapters completed and a way to flip him.
Already Paid: Stands on the side of Pleasant Path as if already paid.
Already Defeated: Removed from Pleasant Path as if already defeated.

options.label: Seed Goal
options.description:
Defeat Bowser: The game is complete once you've defeated Bowser to take back the Star Rod.
Open Star Way: The game is complete once you've fulfilled the requirements to open Star Way

options.label: Power Star Hunt
options.description:
Adds power stars into the item pool. You must collect a certain amount and give them to Eldstar at
Shooting Star Summit to open up Star Way.

options.label: Required Spirits
options.description:
Determines if specific spirits are needed to open star way.
Any: Any spirits can open Star Way.
Specific: A set of specific spirits open Star Way. You can find which are required by visiting Shooting Star Summit.
Specific and Limit Chapter Logic: Progression items will be limited to prologue, common areas, and areas in required
chapters.

options.label: Spirits Required for Star Way
options.description:
Number of star spirits required to open up Star Way and access Chapter 8.
Access requirements will also include power stars if Power Star Hunt is turned on.

options.label: Power Stars Required for Star Way
options.description: Number of power stars required to open up Star Way and access Chapter 8.

options.label: Shuffle Star Beam
options.description:
Star Beam becomes an item shuffled in the item pool. Another random item will replace Star Beam in Star Haven.
Upon reaching the first Bowser fight in Peach's Castle, he will tell you where Star Beam is.

options.label: Spirits Required for Star Beam
options.description:
Number of star spirits required to obtain the item in the Star Beam location in Star Sanctuary.
Forced to 0 when Limit Chapter Logic is active.

options.label: Power Stars Required for Star Beam
options.description: Number of power stars required to be gifted the Star Beam in Star Sanctuary

options.label: Total Power Stars
options.description:
Number of power stars placed in the game world. Must be more than the "Required Power Stars".
It's recommended that this is around 1.5 times the number of required stars.

options.label: Starting Boots
options.description:
Level of the boots that Mario will start the game with.
Note: While jumpless, you can still climb up some places with Parakarry.
You can also hit floating blocks by using Kooper's ability beneath them.

options.label: Starting Hammer
options.description:
Level of the hammer that Mario will start the game with.
Note: Without hammer, you can still hit trees and break yellow blocks using Bombette's ability.

options.label: Starting Coins
options.description:
Amount of coins Mario will start the game with.
Note: You will need to pay 50 coins to get past Kent C Koopa on the way to Koopa Village. It's recommended that you
don't spend all your coins before paying him off.

options.label: Starting HP
options.description:
Amount of Health Points Mario will start the game with
Note: Mario must have at least one starting stat raised past its initial value (5 for HP and FP, 3 for BP)

options.label: Starting BP
options.description:
Amount of Badge Points Mario will start the game with
Note: Mario must have at least one starting stat raised past its initial value (5 for HP and FP, 3 for BP)

options.label: Starting FP
options.description:
Amount of Flower Points Mario will start the game with
Note: Mario must have at least one starting stat raised past its initial value (5 for HP and FP, 3 for BP)

options.label: Starting SP
options.description:
Amount of Star Power Mario will start the game with.
Starting with SP allows Mario to use star powers, which will be cast by Twink until star spirits are saved.

options.label: Random Starting Items
options.description: Number of random items you want to start with.

options.label: Random Starting Stats
options.description:
Instead of choosing starting stats, you can have them randomized based on a chosen starting level.
Setting this to true will overwrite the starting BP, HP, and FP stat settings
Base stats are 5 HP, 5 FP, and 3 BP, with each level raising one of these at random

options.label: Random Starting Stats Level
options.description:
When random starting stats is true, this changes what level (1-27) Mario starts at.
Starting stats will be randomly distributed and will overwrite the starting HP, FP, and BP stat settings

options.label: Consumable Item Pool
options.description:
Vanilla: Original consumable items.
Mystery Only: All consumables are replaced by Mystery.
Fully Random: Consumables are completely random.
Balanced Random: Consumables are randomized and balanced according to Balanced Random Item Quality.

options.label: Consumable Item Quality (%)
options.description:
Sets how powerful consumable items should be on average, where a higher % means better items.
100% is the strength of the vanilla item pool.

options.label: Item Traps
options.description: Replaces some items with fakes that deal 2 damage upon contact.

options.label: Add Item Pouches
options.description:
Adds 5 item pouches into the item pool. Every pouch found increases Mario's inventory size by 2.
This increases total inventory size from 10 items up to a maximum of 20.

options.label: Add Unused Badge Duplicates
options.description: Adds unused duplicates of badges that can stack into the item pool.

options.label: Add Beta Items
options.description: Adds unused beta badges and consumable items into the item pool.

options.label: Progressive Badges
options.description:
Badges that come in different power levels are changed to progressive badges.
This affects jump/hammer charge, power and mega jump/hammer, and quake hammer.
Intermediate beta badges are included for the involved badge families even if beta badges are turned off.

options.label: Badge Pool Limit
options.description: Sets the max amount of badges that can be in the item pool. There are 80 badges in vanilla.

options.label: Starting Location
options.description:
Sets the town/village where the game starts.
This is also where the Homeward Shroom warps Mario.
You may use the warp shroom from the key items menu in the overworld.

options.label: Open Prologue
options.description:
When enabled, Goomba King starts off defeated and the bridge to reach Goomba Village will be open from the start.
When starting from anywhere other than Goomba Village, this will mean having to reach the village via sewers.

options.label: Open Mt. Rugged
options.description:
When enabled, the boulder blocking the train from going to Mt. Rugged will be gone from the start.
When disabled, you will have to use Bombette to blow up the boulder.

options.label: Open Forest
options.description:
When enabled, Oakley allows you through Forever Forest with no requirements.
When disabled, Oakley only allows you through once you have a Forest Pass (added randomizer item), and Fice T's
cutscene will have an item check.

options.label: Magical Seeds Required
options.description:
The amount of Magical Seeds required to open the gate to Flower Fields. Changing this does not remove the
Bub-ulb checks.

options.label: Open Toy Box
options.description:
When enabled, you can open the door to enter Shy Guy's Toy Box from the start.
When disabled, you will have to use Bow to hide from the Shy Guy to enter Shy Guy's Toy Box for the first time.

options.label: Open Whale
options.description:
When enabled, you can ride the whale to Lavalava Island from the start.
When disabled, you will have to use Watt to catch and defeat Fuzzipede in order to ride the whale.

options.label: Open Blue House
options.description:
When enabled, the door to the Blue House in Toad Town's Southern District is unlocked from the start
and the Odd Key is removed from the item pool.
When disabled, you will have to use the Odd Key to open the Blue House door.

options.label: Ch.7 Bridge Visible
options.description:
When enabled, blocks leading to Shiver City are visible and can be hit from above with Super Boots.
When disabled, they will be invisible and you will have to hit them from below with Ultra Boots.

options.label: Mirror Mode
options.description:
Off: The overworld is never mirrored.
Always On: The overworld is always mirrored.
Random On Every Load: Whether the overworld is mirrored or not is random with every screen transition.
Static Random: Some overworld screens are mirrored, some are not, but they won't change within a playthrough.
Note: The Static Random option is not yet implemented and will fail to generate.

options.label: Bowser's Castle Mode
options.description:
Vanilla: Mario will need to go through the entire castle, requiring 5 keys and most partner abilities.
Shortened: Multiple sections of Bowser's Castle will be skipped. No keys or partner abilities will be required.
Boss Rush: The entire castle will be skipped until the hallway where you fight the Duplighosts.

options.label: Dungeon Entrance Shuffle
options.description:
Shuffles the main entrance of every chapter dungeon. You can also choose to include Bowser's Castle's entrance.
Note: This is not yet implemented and will fail to generate if set to True.

options.label: Hidden Block Mode
options.description:
Vanilla: Hidden blocks are only visible while using Watt's ability.
Watt Out: Hidden blocks are visible when Watt is your active partner, even without using her ability.
Watt Obtained: Hidden blocks are always visible after you have obtained Watt as a partner.
Always Visible: Hidden blocks are always visible.

options.label: Prevent OOB/LZS Tricks
options.description:
When enabled, prevents out of bound and loading zone storage tricks. This setting does NOT affect logic.
Warning: in some cases, attempting OOB exploits with this enabled can cause softlocks since the game fails to
properly reset Mario's position.

options.label: Skip Quiz
options.description: When enabled, quiz rewards will be handed out without having to answer questions.

options.label: Quizmo Always Appears
options.description: When enabled, Chuck Quizmo always appears somewhere in town until his location questions have been answered.

options.label: Visible Hidden Panels
options.description:
When enabled, hidden panels will have an altered appearance to make identifying them easier.
Recommended for players not familiar with every single hidden panel locations when shuffling hidden panels.

options.label: Always Speedy Spin
options.description:
When enabled, Mario will always spin fast when pressing Z without needing to equip the Speedy Spin badge.
The Speedy Spin badge is also removed from the item pool.

options.label: Always Peekaboo
options.description:
When enabled, you will always be able to see enemy's HP bars without needing to equip the Peekaboo badge.
The Peekaboo badge is also removed from the item pool.

options.label: Always I Spy
options.description:
When enabled, you will always get an indicator if you enter a room with a hidden panel without needing to equip
the I Spy badge. The sound effect is removed, so it is only a visual cue.
The I Spy badge is also removed from the item pool.
Recommended for players not familiar with every single hidden panel locations when shuffling hidden panels.

options.label: I Spy Panel Hints
options.description:
Off: Don't show panel hints.
Vague: Display a generic item sprite based on the type of item inside the panel (e.g. badge, star piece, key item).
Concrete: Display the exact sprite of the item inside the panel.

options.label: Foliage Item Hints
options.description: When enabled, bushes and trees will emit a glow when they are hiding something.

options.label: Cook Without Frying Pan
options.description:
When enabled, allows Tayce T. to cook for you without first finding the frying pan.
When disabled, you will have to find the frying pan before Tayce T. can cook anything for you.

options.label: Cutscene Mode
options.description:
Vanilla: Cutscenes from the original game are preserved.
Shortened: Cutscenes are quicker but preserved with some condensed dialogue.
Minimal: Most cutscenes and dialogues are removed.

options.label: Skip Epilogue
options.description: When enabled, the game will skip directly to credits once you have acquired the Star Rod.

options.label: Mario's Color Palette
options.description: Changes the way the sprite looks in-game.

options.label: Goombario's Color Palette
options.description: Changes the way the sprite looks in-game.

options.label: Kooper's Color Palette
options.description: Changes the way the sprite looks in-game.

options.label: Bombette's Color Palette
options.description: Changes the way the sprite looks in-game.

options.label: Parakarry's Color Palette
options.description: Changes the way the sprite looks in-game.

options.label: Bow's Color Palette
options.description: Changes the way the sprite looks in-game.

options.label: Watt's Color Palette
options.description: Changes the way the sprite looks in-game.

options.label: Sushie's Color Palette
options.description: Changes the way the sprite looks in-game.

options.label: Lakilester's Color Palette
options.description: Changes the way the sprite looks in-game.

options.label: Bosses Color Palettes
options.description: Changes the way the sprites look in-game.

options.label: NPC Color Palettes
options.description: Changes the way the sprites look in-game.

options.label: Enemy Color Palettes
options.description: Changes the way the sprites look in-game.

options.label: Hammer Color Palette
options.description: Changes the way the sprite looks in-game.

options.label: Status Menu Color Palette
options.description: Changes the way the status menu at the top of the screen looks in-game.

options.label: Coin Color Palette
options.description: Changes the way the sprites look in-game.

options.label: Random Text
options.description: When enabled, all text in the game will be randomized.

options.label: Roman Numerals
options.description: When enabled, enemy HP bars will use roman numerals.

options.label: Shuffle Music
options.description:
Shuffles the different songs in the game.
Shuffle By Mood: Songs will be shuffled within groups of similar moods such as relaxed, upbeat, battle.
Shuffle By Type: Songs will be shuffled within groups of similar types such as overworld, battle, event.
Full Shuffle: Any song can play anywhere in the game.

options.label: Shuffle Jingles
options.description: When enabled, shuffles the different short music jingles in the game.

options.label: Random Pitch
options.description: When enabled, randomizes the pitch of the game's music and sounds.

options.label: Mute Danger Beeps
options.description: When enabled, mutes the sound effect that plays when Mario is in danger.

options.label: Game Mode
options.description:
How would you like to experience Taz Wanted?

Open Mode has all of the levels at your disposal at the very start. Find
the level unlocks to gain access to them!

Linear Mode has you playing the game in order. In this mode you have to
fight every boss.

options.label: Random Costumes
options.description:
Shuffle which costume each level's phone booth gives you.

Off keeps the game as it shipped: each level gives its own costume.

1 for 1 shuffles them so that every costume still appears exactly once,
and no level keeps its own. You still find all eleven, they are just
somewhere else.

Completely Random picks each level's costume independently. A costume can
turn up at two booths, or not appear in the seed at all, and a level can
keep its own by chance.

Beating a catcher costs Taz whatever he is wearing, so a level's catchers
need that level's costume either way -- shuffling changes which item that
is, not how many checks there are.

The costumes are put on the disc when you patch it, so they are simply
part of the game -- no loading, no stutter, and nothing built while you
play. Whatever you pick here, you patch your own dump the same way; this
only decides what the patch writes.

options.label: Starting Levels
options.description:
NOTE: This does nothing if you didn't select Open Mode.

How many levels would you like to start your game with?

At least one: with none, every location is inside a level you cannot
enter, so there is nowhere for the generator to place anything.

options.label: Goal Conditions
options.description:
NOTE: This does nothing if you didn't select Open Mode.

What you have to do to open The Hindenbird and win.

This is one setting rather than three switches because a goal has to
require SOMETHING -- with separate toggles it was possible to turn all
three off and generate a seed that was already finished.

Wanted Posters uses your Wanted Posters Goal. Defeated Bosses uses your
Defeated Bosses Goal, and gives every boss a second check holding a
Hindenbird Ticket. Level Unlock puts The Hindenbird Unlock in the item
pool -- and if you do NOT pick it, that item does not exist in the seed at
all, because then the goal itself is the only thing standing between you
and the last fight.

options.label: Wanted Posters Pool - Open
options.description:
NOTE: This does nothing if you didn't select Open Mode, or if Wanted
Posters are not part of your Goal Conditions.

Determines how many Wanted Posters are in the item Pool. Setting this
above your Wanted Posters Goal is fine, and often better -- a pool of 70
for a goal of 50 means finding any 50 of them, anywhere.

If your goal does not include Wanted Posters then nothing in the seed
requires one, so none are added at all and those slots become filler
instead.

options.label: Wanted Posters Goal
options.description:
NOTE: This does nothing if you didn't select Open Mode.

Determines how many Wanted Posters are needed to reach your goal.

options.label: Defeated Bosses
options.description:
NOTE: This does nothing if you didn't select it as your game mode or
goal condition.

Determines how many bosses you have to defeat to reach your goal.

options.label: Wanted Posters Pool - Linear
options.description:
NOTE: This does nothing if you didn't select Linear Mode.

Determines how many Wanted Posters are in the item Pool.

options.label: Elephant Pong Wanted Posters Gate
options.description:
NOTE: This does nothing if you didn't select Linear Mode.

Determines how many Wanted Posters are needed to enter Elephant Pong.

options.label: Gladiatoons Wanted Posters Gate
options.description:
NOTE: This does nothing if you didn't select Linear Mode.

Determines how many Wanted Posters are needed to enter Gladiatoons.

options.label: Dodge City Wanted Posters Gate
options.description:
NOTE: This does nothing if you didn't select Linear Mode.

Determines how many Wanted Posters are needed to enter Dodge City.

options.label: Disco Volcano & Hindenbird Wanted Posters Gate
options.description:
NOTE: This does nothing if you didn't select Linear Mode.

Determines how many Wanted Posters are needed to enter Disco Volcano which
leads into The Hindenbird.

options.label: Sandwich Checks Unlock
options.description:
Do the sandwiches have to be unlocked before they are there to collect?

Start Unlocked is the game as it has always been: every sandwich is lying
where it always was, from the first level you walk into.

Sandwich Part Hitlist gives you a shopping list. Somewhere in the
multiworld are the parts of a sandwich, and until you are holding every
one your list asks for, NO level has any sandwiches in it at all. Find the
last one and all ten levels fill up at once. Which parts are on your list
is rolled per seed -- your client's Sandwich Hitlist tab tells you exactly
what to look for, and what is a decoy.

Sandwich Level Unlocks scatters ten "<Level> - Sandwich Unlock" items
instead. Each one spawns the sandwiches in its own level and nowhere else.

Either way the sandwiches are genuinely GONE until then -- not merely out
of logic. If you unlock a level's sandwiches while you are standing in it,
leave and come back and they will be there.

options.label: Sandwich Part Hitlist Pool
options.description:
NOTE: This does nothing unless Sandwich Checks Unlock is set to
Sandwich Part Hitlist.

How many of the twenty sandwich parts exist in the seed at all.

Anything above your Requirement becomes a decoy: a real item that really
travels the multiworld and does absolutely nothing when it arrives. A pool
of 20 with a requirement of 10 means ten parts matter and ten are there to
keep everybody else guessing.

options.label: Sandwich Part Hitlist Requirement
options.description:
NOTE: This does nothing unless Sandwich Checks Unlock is set to
Sandwich Part Hitlist.

How many of the parts in the pool you actually have to find.

Which ones is rolled per seed. Setting this equal to the Pool means every
part in the seed is on your list and there are no decoys; setting it above
the Pool would ask you for parts the seed does not contain, so it refuses
to generate rather than roll a seed nobody can finish.

options.label: Starting Sandwiches
options.description: Collecting 100 Sandwiches sends a check. This gets you there sooner.

options.label: Sandwich Checks
options.description:
By default, you'll receive an item for getting 100 sandwiches. This
allows you to get more checks based on which value you set it to. For
example, if you start with 0 and set your Checks to 5, each level will have
20 sandwich checks in it. If you set it to 0, no checks will be sent for
sandwiches.

1 makes every single sandwich a check: 100 per level, 1000 in the seed.
The tracker shows those as one counter per level rather than a thousand
separate pins.

options.label: Starting Daffy-culty
options.description:
YOU MUST SELECT THIS IN GAME BEFORE STARTING!

Changing this makes various things in the game harder, but for AP checks,
it determines when a Destruction Bonus should trigger.

Standard=50%  Advanced=75%  Expert=100%

options.label: Destruction Checks
options.description:
How often destroying a level sends a check, as a percentage of it.

Your Daffy-culty sets the target: 50% on Standard, 75% on Advanced, 100%
on Expert. A check fires at every multiple of this value up to that
target, and the target itself ALWAYS pays out -- so when the value does
not divide the target evenly, the remainder is a check of its own.

On Expert, checks every 75% is two checks: one at 75% and one at 100%.
On Advanced, checks every 50% is two: 50% and 75%. On Standard, checks
every 5% is ten, 5% through 50%.

0% means no destruction checks at all. 1% makes every whole percent a
check -- up to 100 per level on Expert -- which the tracker shows as one
counter per level rather than as a hundred pins.

75% needs Advanced or Expert and 100% needs Expert, since a value above
the target could never be reached. Choosing one the Daffy-culty cannot
reach refuses to generate, rather than quietly building a seed with no
destruction checks in it.

options.label: Raised Bounty Filler Weight
options.description: Does Nothing, but Makes Sam mad!

options.label: Chili Pepper Filler Weight
options.description: HOT HOT HOT!

options.label: Burp Can Filler Weight
options.description: That tasted great!

options.label: Invisibility Filler Weight
options.description: Now you see me, now you don't!

options.label: Bubble Gum Filler Weight
options.description: Sticky...

options.label: Filler Replaced With Traps
options.description:
Determines the percentage of filler items that will be replaced with
traps.

options.label: Dynamite Trap Weight
options.description: Taz no feel so good...

options.label: Squash Trap Weight
options.description: Like a pancake...

options.label: Electrocute Trap Weight
options.description: Shocking... Isn't it...

options.label: Hiccup Trap Weight
options.description: That caught me off guard!

options.label: No Spinning Trap Weight
options.description: Finally, I was getting Dizzy

options.label: Costume Strip Trap Weight
options.description: hey! I was wearing that!

options.label: Slippery Trap Weight
options.description: Whoa! Taz no good on ice!

options.label: In Game Text Client
options.description:
Announce received items in the game's own subtitle box.

Off shows nothing. Progression Only shows items Archipelago has
classified as progression -- posters, costumes, unlocks, tickets -- and
stays quiet for filler and traps. All Items shows everything.

Messages wait until the player actually has control, so nothing appears
over a loading screen, a cutscene or the pause menu; they queue and
arrive once Taz is playable again.

The player can also cycle this in game by holding both bumpers and both
triggers together. That change lasts for the session and does not alter
the yaml.

options.label: Local Filler
options.description:
Keep your own filler items in your own game instead of sending them out.

Every sandwich or every percent of destruction as a check means up to two
thousand locations in one slot, and almost all of them hold filler. Sent
into a multiworld that is a flood: everyone else spends the seed opening
your Chili Peppers.

With this on, your filler is placed in your own world before the fill
begins, so you find it yourself. Traps are not affected and still travel
normally -- a trap that cannot reach anyone else is not a trap.

Some of it still goes out. Enough of your locations are deliberately left
free for progression to have somewhere to land, and on a small seed -- no
sandwich or destruction checks -- there is no spare filler to keep, so
this does nothing at all.

options.label: Death Link
options.description:
If Taz dies you kill everyone else that has Death Link on and vice
versa. The way it works in Taz Wanted, is Taz is teleported to the start
of the level, unless he's in a boss fight, then he just loses.

options.label: What Sends a Death Link
options.description:
Which of your deaths kill everyone else.

NOTE: Does nothing if Death Link is turned off.

Captures is a catcher grabbing you. Void Outs is dying any other ordinary
way -- drowning, falling, being crushed, or wrecking a rollercoaster.
Boss Losses is losing a boss fight.

There is no "nothing" here on purpose: turning Death Link on and sending
none of your own deaths is not a way to play, it is a setting somebody
forgot to finish. If you want to be left alone, turn Death Link off.

options.label: Void Out Amnesty
options.description:
How many Void Out deaths before a death link is sent. This setting does
nothing if void out deaths weren't selected.

options.label: Game Mode
options.description:
How would you like to experience Toy Story 2?
Open Mode has all of the levels at your disposal at the very start.
Find the level unlocks to gain access to them!
Linear Mode has you playing the game in order. Each area is fully
unlocked after defeating a boss to allow you more options and to keep
you from getting stuck. In this mode you have to fight every boss.

options.label: Skips
options.description:
Determines the logic for certain checks.
Easy is incredibly easy skips that anyone can do. They may require trial and error,
but you won't have to try for too long.
Hard is for the glitch hunters and rule breakers out there.
Insane is for the most demanding tricks, on top of all Easy and Hard skips.

options.label: Missing Toy Bundle Size
options.description:
How the missing toys are RECEIVED. 1 = each toy arrives individually (five
separate "Sheep" / "Soldier" / etc. items per level, the original behaviour).
5 = each level's toys arrive together as a single item (e.g. one "5 Sheep")
that grants all five at once. The in-level toy CHECK locations are identical
either way; only the received items change.

options.label: Missing Toy Reward Hint
options.description:
The character who wants the missing toys tells you what you will get.

Every seed already replaces the "pizza planet token" in their dialog with
who the reward is for and what KIND of thing it is -- "progressive item",
"useful item", "filler item" -- so it is always worth knowing whether the
five toys are worth chasing yet.

Turn this on and they name the item outright instead of its class, and
talking to them hints it for the whole multiworld, exactly as Hamm does with
his shop under Shopsanity. Off, the reward stays a surprise and nothing is
hinted.

As in the shop, a trap always claims to be a "progressive item".

options.label: Pizza Planet Token Pool
options.description:
Determines how many Pizza Planet Tokens are in the item pool.
Highly recommend adding more sanities the more tokens you add.

options.label: Starting Levels
options.description:
NOTE: This does nothing if you didn't select Open Mode.
How many levels would you like to start your game with?

options.label: Omit Airport Infiltration From Pool
options.description:
NOTE: This does nothing if you didn't select Open Mode.
Airport Infiltration has nothing going for it if you don't have Stomp.
This makes it so you won't get it as a starting level.

options.label: Movesanity
options.description:
Movesanity shuffles every single thing Buzz can do into the item pool,
which means you START WITH NO MOVES and must find them as checks -- including
Double Jump, Ledge Grab, and Pole Climb.
Because almost every location needs those basic moves, you MUST pair this with
other sanities (lifesanity, batterysanity, green_laser_sanity, rexsanity,
hint_block_sanity, coinsanity) and/or more starting_levels so there are enough
no-move locations at the start to place your first moves. If your settings are
too sparse (e.g. Movesanity with no other sanities and a single starting level),
generation will stop and tell you to enable more sanities or pick a LITE option.
Movesanity LITE (Weapons) only shuffles Buzz's attack abilities:
Laser, Spin, Stomp, and Visor. You still start with all movement moves.
Movesanity LITE (Traversal) only shuffles Buzz's movement abilities:
Double Jump, Pole Climb, Ledge Grab, Pole Vault, Push, and Rope Sliding.
You still start with all attack abilities.

options.label: Coinsanity
options.description:
Coins send checks! They aren't individually id'd, it's based on the
amount you gather in one go through a level. Keep that in mind when
selecting your bundle amounts. You'll be gathering the same coins a lot.
Your coins are also items that are sent to you based on your Coinsanity
Received Bundle Size as well. Make Hamm proud and get him some coins!

Note: enemies automatically drop coins, and those coins are automatically
collected for you - you don't need to pick them up yourself.

options.label: Coinsanity Checks Bundle Size
options.description:
If Coinsanity is not turned on, this does nothing.

Choose the amount coins needed per level to send checks.

options.label: Coinsanity Received Bundle Size
options.description:
If Coinsanity is not turned on, this does nothing.

Choose the amount coins received.

This is the setting that decides how many Coin Bundle ITEMS exist: a level
worth 99 coins sends 99 of them at size 1, but only 20 at size 5. Those items
have to fit in your check locations alongside everything else, so a small
size here is the most common reason a coin-heavy yaml fails to generate.

With Hamm Checks set to Shopsanity, size 1 has a second cost: a shop slot
priced at 40 coins needs 40 bundles in hand, so nearly every Coin Bundle
becomes progression and generation slows to a crawl. 5 or higher is strongly
recommended with a shop.

options.label: Coin Total Per Level
options.description:
If Coinsanity is not turned on, this does nothing.

How many coins each level is worth as far as Archipelago is concerned.

Vanilla - each level is worth what it actually holds: 63 in Elevator Hop,
99 in Andy's Neighborhood, and everything in between. Levels are uneven,
which is faithful but means a small level's shop is a cheap shop.
(Alleys and Gullies physically holds 103, but the coin counter is two
digits, so it counts as 99 like everything else at the top.)

Uniform 99 - every level is worth 99, whatever it physically contains. That
evens out how much money each level is worth and puts every shop on the same
footing.

Uniform 99 ADDS items to the pool, because a level that holds 63 coins still
has to be sent 99 coins' worth of bundles. How many depends on your received
bundle size: at size 5 it is 200 Coin Bundle items instead of 168, which is
nothing - but at size 1 it is 990 instead of 818, and those 172 extra items
have to displace something. If generation complains it has nowhere to put
them, raise the received bundle size first; that is far and away the biggest
lever.

Only the coins SENT to you change. The coins lying around in the level are
the ones the game shipped with, so the "collect N coins" checks are still
counted against what is really there - which is also why this does nothing
without Coinsanity: with it off there is no way to hand you a coin that the
level does not contain.

options.label: Hamm Checks
options.description:
What Hamm does with your coins.

Off - Hamm takes no coins and sends no checks. Nothing gates on coins any
more, so every Coin Bundle item becomes pure filler.

Vanilla - the original behaviour. Handing Hamm 50 coins in a level sends
that level's "Hamm's 50 Coins Token" check. Ten checks in all.

Shopsanity - Hamm opens a shop instead. Each slot is its own check, so a coin
level is worth up to ten checks, and coins turn from a one-time toll into a
ladder of thresholds.

A PRICE IS WHAT YOU MUST BE HOLDING, NOT WHAT YOU HAND OVER. Nothing is
bought and nothing is spent. Talk to Hamm and he counts your coins, hands you
everything you already qualify for, and you keep every one of them. So no
slot can ever cost you another, there is no order to get wrong, and once you
can reach a number every slot at or under it is yours.

Claimed slots leave the page, so what you are reading is always what is left.

Shopsanity works with or without Coinsanity. With Coinsanity on it counts
the coins AP sends you; with it off it counts the coins you pick up in the
level, which are kept between visits and cannot be farmed again.

Shopsanity replaces the 50-coin token entirely - you cannot have both.

options.label: Hamm's Shop Items
options.description:
If Hamm Checks is not set to Shopsanity, this does nothing.

How many items Hamm stocks per coin level - so ten times this many checks
in total.

options.label: Hamm's Shop Price Pressure
options.description:
If Hamm Checks is not set to Shopsanity, this does nothing.

How high the DEAREST slot in a level asks you to climb, as a percentage of
that level's coins. At 70% the most expensive item wants about seven tenths
of everything the level holds and the other slots sit below that; at 100%
one slot asks for every coin in the level. A level's coins means its real
total - 63 in Elevator Hop, 99 in Andy's Neighborhood - so each shop is
priced to the level it sits in.

Since prices are thresholds you are never asked to hand over, this sets how
much of a level you have to comb rather than how much you have to give up.
No price is ever set above what the level can actually yield.

options.label: Hamm's Shop Price Spread
options.description:
If Hamm Checks is not set to Shopsanity, this does nothing.

How the slots sit underneath the price pressure.

Escalating - an even staircase up to the ceiling, slot 1 cheapest. Hands you
items steadily as you comb the level and turns the last one into a goal.
Shuffled - thresholds rolled with the seed and dealt out at random. The
dearest slot is still at the ceiling, but you will not know which it is
until you look.

With a large Coinsanity Received Bundle Size there are only a few bundles
per level to climb with, so several slots open together and the spread
matters less.

options.label: Hamm's Shop Hints
options.description:
If Hamm Checks is not set to Shopsanity, this does nothing.

Off (the default) keeps his stock private. The page shows each slot's CLASS
instead of its name - "progressive item", "useful item", "filler item" -
which is still enough to judge whether a slot is worth combing the level for,
without telling you what it is.

Turn it on and talking to Hamm for the first time in a level hints everything
he is holding there, so the whole multiworld can see it and not just the
player standing in front of him.

The recipient is shown either way, so you can see whose item a slot is
holding even when you cannot see what it is.

options.label: Lifesanity
options.description:
All lives are checks now! That means lives will no longer grant you a
life, but a check instead! They also don't respawn so play carefully!

options.label: Batterysanity
options.description:
All batteries are checks now! Batteries will still give health, but
they won't respawn.

options.label: Green Laser Sanity
options.description:
Green Lasers are checks now! But just like the other sanities, these
won't respawn. Use them wisely!

options.label: Rexsanity
options.description: Hey Buzz! Need a hint? Talking to Rex now gives checks!

options.label: Hint Block Sanity
options.description: Hints? Who needs them? I'd rather get a useful item! This turns all hint blocks into checks!

options.label: Filler Replaced With Traps
options.description:
Determines the percentage of filler items that will be replaced
with traps.

options.label: Cutscene Trap Weight
options.description: Hope you like Toy Story 2, because you're gonna be watching it a lot!

options.label: Narrow Vision Trap Weight
options.description: I can't see! I can't see!

options.label: Damage Buzz Trap Weight
options.description: Ouch!

options.label: Freeze Buzz Trap Weight
options.description: Buzz must have run out of batteries!

options.label: Invincible Enemies Trap Weight
options.description: I swear I hit him!

options.label: Dizzy Buzz Trap Weight
options.description: I don't feel so good...

options.label: 1 Life Filler Weight
options.description: How often 1 Life appears among the filler items.

options.label: Extra Battery Filler Weight
options.description: How often Extra Battery appears among the filler items.

options.label: Invincible Buzz Filler Weight
options.description:
How often Invincible Buzz appears among the filler items.
Grants Buzz 15 seconds of invincibility. Can't touch this!

options.label: Determination to Save Woody Filler Weight
options.description:
How often "Determination to Save Woody" appears among the filler items.
It does absolutely nothing when received — pure flavor filler. Set to 'off'
if you'd rather never see it. Defaults high so seeds heavy on useful filler
get diluted with something that gives no advantage.

options.label: Local Filler
options.description:
Force THIS slot's own dynamic filler (1 Life, Extra Battery, Invincible
Buzz, Determination to Save Woody) to be placed in your own world instead of
being sent to other players. Handy when this game produces a lot of filler and
you'd rather find more of it yourself, or when sharing a multiworld with games
that have far fewer locations. Traps are unaffected and still travel normally.

options.label: Skip Cutscenes
options.description:
Sets all the cutscene flags to 'watched' when starting the game.
This does not bypass the Cutscene Trap.

options.label: Quick Loads
options.description:
Fast-forwards the loading screens into and out of every level, pressing
X for you where the game waits for it. After a boss win it also skips the
victory screen and answers the save screen with "don't save". Sound is
muted while it fast-forwards. The final fight's ending and cutscenes always
play at normal speed, and your own emulator speed and sound come back as
soon as the load is done.

You can turn it on or off at any time while playing by typing /speedup in
the Toy Story 2 Client ("/speedup on" or "/speedup off" also work). The
client says which state it is in each time.

options.label: Disc Launcher Pick Ups Fill Pockets
options.description:
When you pick up Disc Launchers they will
now go to the maximum you can hold!

options.label: On-Screen Item Feed
options.description:
Show Archipelago item activity on-screen (top-left) in BizHawk.
Off shows nothing. Sent shows checks you send out. Received shows items you
get. Both shows everything. Pressing Select will cycle this feature's modes.

options.label: Disable Falling Animation
options.description: Makes it so Buzz always lands on his feet!

options.label: Start Every Level With Full Health
options.description: I feel like this should have been in the vanilla game!

options.label: Never Game Over
options.description:
No longer forces the game to reset on game over. Instead if you're one
hit away with no lives, you're booted back to the map with 5 lives. Highly
recommended for Coinsanity!

options.label: Music Randomizer Mode
options.description:
Normal: Randomizes the game's music one to one! Note, minigame,
miniboss, title screen, and map aren't randomized.
Chaos: You never know what you're going to get! You could be listening
to the Game Over music on loop for all I know!
Oops All Bangers: What's your favorite song? What if you heard that for
every single level in the game?

options.label: Oops All Bangers Song
options.description: Better choose wisely, you're gonna be hearing this for a while.

choices.label: Youve Got A Friend In Me

options.label: Skip Song
options.description:
Man this song sucks. Wouldn't it be nice if you could skip it?
Well now you can! If you're in a level, you can hold Triangle and press
L2 and R2 to change the song! Unless you're in Oops All Bangers Mode.
You dug your grave and now you have to lay in it.

options.label: Death Link
options.description:
If Buzz dies you kill everyone else that has Death Link on and vice
versa. Highly recommended to turn on Never Game Over if you play with
Death Link.

options.label: Puzzle Count
options.description: Number of puzzles to randomly generate.

options.label: Starting Puzzles
options.description:
Number of puzzles to randomly add to the starting inventory. These will be
removed from the item pool.

options.label: Target Completion Percentage
options.description:
Percent of puzzles which must be completed to finish the world, rounding up.

If you set this to a low value, it is HIGHLY RECOMMENDED to disable release on world completion.

options.label: Min Difficulty
options.description:
Minimum difficulty to select generated presets from. Note that not all genres have presets at "Hard" difficulty,
so they will never appear if the minimum difficulty is set to Hard (unless you specify custom presets for them).

options.label: Max Difficulty
options.description:
Maximum difficulty to select generated presets from. Takes priority over the Minimum Difficulty option if it is lower.

Puzzles on "Ridiculous" difficulty are either very big or not actually randomized. Use this difficulty at your own risk.

options.label: Genre Weights
options.description:
Relative chance for each genre to be selected as a random preset. Set a genre's
weight to 0 or remove it from this list to disable it.

options.label: Genre Min Difficulty
options.description: Minimum difficulty for each genre. Use 0 for easy, 1 for normal, 2 for hard, and 3 for ridiculous.

options.label: Genre Max Difficulty
options.description: Maximum difficulty for each genre. Use 0 for easy, 1 for normal, 2 for hard, and 3 for ridiculous.

options.label: Preset Overrides
options.description:
List of presets to use for a given genre. Replaces the default presets for
that puzzle if specified.

For example, to make Net puzzles always use wrapping grids, add:
net: [5x5w, 7x7w, 9x9w, 11x11w]

options.label: Fixed Puzzles
options.description:
List of additional puzzles to include. These puzzles will be placed at the start of the list.
The remaining list (up to puzzle_count) will be filled according to genre_weights.

You can specify by genre (net), parameter string (net:2x2), seed (net:2x2#12345), or ID (net:2x2:c494).
