options.label: Goal
options.description:
The victory condition for this run.

duna_return            -- Return a vessel (or crew) from Duna.
eeloo_return           -- Return a vessel (or crew) from Eeloo.
flag_every_body        -- Plant a flag on all 15 landable bodies (crewed).
standard_returns       -- Return from 11 bodies (excl. Eve, Tylo, Laythe).
standard_sample_returns -- Crewed sample return from the same 11 bodies.
complete_tech_tree     -- Purchase all 62 tech tree nodes with science.
mun_flag               -- Plant a flag on the Mun.
mun_sample_return      -- Crewed sample return from the Mun.
jool_moons_return      -- Return from each Jool moon (Laythe, Vall, Tylo,
                          Bop, Pol).  Home is filtered out, so a Laythe
                          start gives a tight 4-target Jool-system goal.
random_contracts       -- No destination goal: complete X of your available
                          contracts, then plant a flag at home to win. Only
                          valid with goal_contract_mode = count or
                          progressive_unlock.
custom                 -- Build a goal from the body-list options below.

options.label: Starting Body
options.description:
The celestial body whose surface the player launches from.  Mun /
Minmus / Laythe / etc. are landable bodies that the Selector mod
can spawn KSC at.  Jool and Kerbol are excluded — gas giant and
star, no surface.

Most existing goals still work from non-Kerbin homes (returns,
flag plants, sample returns are filtered for the new home).
Goals whose only target *is* the home body become unwinnable and
generation aborts with OptionError — e.g. ``mun_flag`` with
``home = mun`` is rejected at gen time.

``eve`` launches from the 6,140 m mesa pad (~8,996 m/s ascent);
heavy departures are lifted across up to three launches and docked
in Eve orbit (multi-launch assembly).  The deepest casual-margin
Return/Sample Return targets stay out of logic and route through the
proxy; comfortable/expert are fully in logic.  Expect the hardest
seeds in the game.

Default ``kerbin`` preserves the existing single-home behaviour.

Pool keys (resolved to a concrete body at generation time using the
seed RNG) are quick picks for randomized starts:

atmospheric -- Kerbin, Duna, Laythe.
standard    -- Kerbin, Duna, Laythe, Moho, Eeloo.
planets     -- Moho, Kerbin, Duna, Dres, Eeloo (planets only).
all         -- Every landable body except Eve (Eve is opt-in only via
               the explicit ``eve`` key).  Includes Tylo and Laythe;
               expect punishing seeds.

For custom weights, use the standard AP weighted-random YAML form
over the concrete body keys, e.g. ``kerbin: 40, duna: 20,
laythe: 40``.  Pool keys can be weighted the same way.

options.label: Difficulty
options.description:
Sets pacing defaults: Tech Slots Per Node, Starting Inventory Count,
Science Safety Factor, and contract pacing — each overridable independently.

Delta-V margins and hardware strictness are NOT set here — those are the
Physics Difficulty option (which defaults to follow this).

casual  -- 20 starts, 4 tech slots/node, 50% science; physics 'generous'.
normal  -- 15 starts, 4 tech slots/node, 70% science; physics 'comfortable'.
expert  -- 10 starts, 3 tech slots/node, 85% science; physics 'small'.

options.label: Tech Slots Per Node
options.description:
Number of AP location slots created per tech tree node (62 nodes total).

More slots = larger location pool, looser fill.  Fewer slots = tighter
item pool tension and faster progression pacing.

WARNING: Lowering this shrinks the location pool and can cause fill
failures on long goals (e.g. standard_sample_returns, flag_every_body).
If generation fails: reroll with a new seed, or raise this value, or
raise Starting Inventory Count to give the fill algorithm more room.
Short goals (mun_flag, duna_return) are unaffected.

auto -- Derived from Difficulty (casual/normal=4, expert=3).
1..4 -- Explicit override.

options.label: Starting Inventory Count
options.description:
Number of zero-requirement bootstrap locations available at run start.

These auto-check on connect — the AP fill algorithm uses them to seed
your initial parts kit.  Higher = easier bootstrap, more wide-open
early game.  Lower = scarcer starts, tighter pacing.

The Progressive Launch Pad bonus (+3, capped at 20) still applies on
top of this when enabled.

WARNING: Lowering this shrinks the location pool and can cause fill
failures on long goals (e.g. standard_sample_returns, flag_every_body).
If generation fails: reroll with a new seed, or raise this value, or
raise Tech Slots Per Node to give the fill algorithm more room.
Short goals (mun_flag, duna_return) are unaffected.

auto  -- Derived from Difficulty (20/15/10).
0..20 -- Explicit override.

options.label: Science Safety Factor
options.description:
Percentage of estimated accessible science counted toward tech tree gates.

The capability system estimates how much science the player could earn
from reachable bodies; this factor scales that estimate.  Lower = stricter
(tech tiers unlock later, more bodies must be reachable first).  Higher =
more permissive.  This is the single most impactful knob for tech tree
progression pacing.

Does NOT affect fill success — only tech tree gating.  Safe to tune.

auto    -- Derived from Difficulty (casual=50, normal=70, expert=85).
0..100  -- Explicit percentage override.

options.label: Physics Difficulty
options.description:
Delta-V margins and hardware strictness used by the capability model.

This is the physics axis only — it does NOT touch tech-slot, starting-
inventory, science, or contract pacing (those follow Difficulty).  The
levels are hand-curated profiles, not a numeric dial: margins shrink while
other knobs (e.g. drag credit) move the other way, so there's no meaningful
value "between" two levels.

auto        -- Follow Difficulty (casual->generous, normal->comfortable,
               expert->small).  The default.
generous    -- Largest margins; most forgiving (casual physics).
comfortable -- Default margins (normal physics).
small       -- Tight margins (expert physics).
zero        -- No margin at all: every dv budget must close exactly, no
               plane-change cushion, lowest TWR floors.  "Fly it perfectly."
               Maps to no Difficulty — opt in deliberately.

options.label: Start With Launch Clamps
options.description:
Start the run with Launch Clamps already collected.

Launch Clamps stabilize tall rockets on the pad.  They are not required
for any mission — the capability system never gates on them — but
enabling this gives the player access to one from the start of the run
instead of waiting for the part item.

options.label: Guarantee Science Rover
options.description:
Internal starting-convenience floor (not a player-facing option).

Precollects a complete science-capable kit — a control source (a probe or
a capsule, rolled per seed), a wheel, a power source, and a science
instrument — so the KSC-biome science and splashdown checks are doable from
the moment you connect, regardless of what your ascent parts rolled or where
the multiworld scattered them.  The location rules stay real physics and
generation is solvable without it; it exists so tests can build a genuinely
empty starting state to verify those rules in isolation.

options.label: Accessibility
options.description:
Set rules for reachability of locations.

KSP1 defaults to **minimal**: only locations on the path to your goal need
to be reachable. Useful items (parts) may end up at locations the player
can't reach — they're not required to win, just collectibles. This avoids
`inaccessible_location_rules` filler-only marking that caused fill failures
when only ~91 of ~530 locations were initially reachable from sphere-0.

See bug 074 for the full rationale.

options.label: Exclude Locations
options.description:
Locations that are excluded from containing progression items by default.

Empty by default: missions the dv model can't verify from the active
home at the seed's difficulty (e.g. Eve surface returns) are gated via
the "all progression items collected" proxy rule (see
``MODEL_INFEASIBLE_BASE`` in ``data/feasibility.py``).
That mechanism already prevents fill failures without taking the
locations out of the progression pool.

The previous Kerbin-shaped hardcoded default (Eve / Tylo / Laythe
returns) made non-Kerbin home configs trip over their own goal — a
Laythe-home ``jool_moons_return`` seed needs Tylo Return as a goal
target, but the default excluded it.  Failing early at gen time on
that mismatch (see ``_validate_goal_not_excluded`` in ``world.py``)
catches user errors more clearly than the previous fill-failure
symptom.

options.label: Exclude Late Tech Tree
options.description:
Exclude tier-8 tech tree locations from containing progression items.

Tier-8 nodes require massive amounts of science to unlock.  Enabling this
prevents late-game science grind from being required to complete the seed.
Disable for Complete Tech Tree goal or challenge runs.

options.label: Progressive Launch Pad
options.description:
Gate buildable rocket launch mass through Progressive Launch Pad items.

Mirrors KSP career mode launch pad upgrades. The pool gets 3 copies and
collecting them raises the launch-mass cap through tiers
(100 → 200 → 500 → unlimited tonnes by default — see
PROGRESSIVE_LAUNCH_PAD_CAPS).

Creates a real progression gate on broad goals like Standard Sample
Returns — you can have all the parts but still need a bigger launch
pad before tackling Vall / Duna / heavy missions.

Disabling this option can result in more wide-open seeds where you can
sometimes reach all bodies at once after a small bootstrap kit. Leave
enabled if you want a sequential progression journey; disable if you
find the mass cap annoying.

options.label: Buildings In Logic
options.description:
Gate capability-driving KSP facilities as in-logic progression.

When on (default), the curated facilities start at level 0 and the player
upgrades them by collecting building progressives.  When off, all facilities
are maxed similar to science sandbox, no facility gates anything:

  - **Astronaut Complex** gates EVA.  Until upgraded, planting a flag and EVA
    in orbit are out of logic on EVERY body incl. home, as are rescues and
    surface samples away from home; only plain home-surface EVA works at
    level 0.
  - **Research & Development** gates surface samples (needs the R&D facility
    even on the home body) *and* the science-cost cap — how expensive a tech
    node you may buy.  Its level rides the Progressive R&D count on a
    ``(2, 4)`` schedule (samples + mid cap at the 2nd copy, max at the 4th),
    placed so the cap never binds before the tech band does.
  - **Tracking Station** gates the Deep Space Network comms range (a weaker
    DSN needs a stronger antenna, so far uncrewed missions and far science
    transmission require upgrading it) *and* patched conics (L2), a
    prerequisite for navigation.
  - **Mission Control** gates maneuver nodes (L2) — with conics, this is what
    lets you plan rendezvous and transfers.  Rendezvous (rescue, docking) and
    interplanetary transfers need both; home-system (moon) transfers scale
    with difficulty (see ``HomeSystemConics`` / ``HomeSystemNodes``).

The VAB/SPH buildable limits are wired end-to-end but ship maxed this
release; their part-count gate is a follow-up.

options.label: Home System Conics
options.description:
Whether home-system (moon) transfers require patched conics.

Patched conics (Tracking Station L2) let you see an encounter before you
commit the burn.  Interplanetary transfers and rendezvous always need them;
this option only covers transfers to the home body's own moons, which a
skilled pilot can eyeball.  Only matters when ``buildings_in_logic`` is on.

auto         -- follow Difficulty (casual: required, normal: required,
                expert: not required).  The default.
required     -- home-system transfers always need conics.
not_required -- home-system transfers never need conics.

options.label: Home System Nodes
options.description:
Whether home-system (moon) transfers require maneuver nodes.

Maneuver nodes (Mission Control L2, plus conics) let you plan a precise burn.
Interplanetary transfers and rendezvous always need them; this option only
covers transfers to the home body's own moons.  Only matters when
``buildings_in_logic`` is on.

auto         -- follow Difficulty (casual: required, normal: not required,
                expert: not required).  The default.
required     -- home-system transfers always need nodes (and conics).
not_required -- home-system transfers never need nodes.

options.label: Contract Type Weights
options.description:
Relative weight of each contract mission type in the non-goal contract pool.

Contracts are paced into the run as items; completing one (a native KSP
contract injected by the client) checks an AP location. A weight of 0
disables that type entirely. Weights are relative — {"mine_ore": 2} alone
behaves the same as {"mine_ore": 1}; mixing types biases the random pick.

Only ever-achievable (type, body) combinations are placed.

options.label: Contracts Available
options.description:
Total number of ordinary (non-goal) contracts placed into the seed.
Independent of the goal; goal contracts are separate.

Capped at the number of ever-achievable (enabled-type, body) combinations
available in the seed, so a high value may yield fewer in practice.

options.label: Contracts Required For Goal
options.description:
Completed non-goal contracts (X) required before the goal contract item(s)
are awarded. Read only by goal_contract_mode = count / progressive_unlock;
ignored by findable / starting.

auto  -- ceil(0.8 * contracts actually generated).
0..40 -- Explicit. Must not exceed Contracts Available; clamped down to the
         number of contracts actually generated this seed.

options.label: Goal Contract Mode
options.description:
How the goal contract item(s) reach the player.

findable           -- goal contract item is in the multiworld item pool,
                      found like any other item.
starting           -- goal contract item(s) are precollected as EXTRA
                      starting items; you are limited only by physics, parts,
                      and buildings.
count              -- (default) complete X of your Y available contracts; on
                      hitting X all goal contract items are awarded at once.
progressive_unlock -- complete contracts to unlock the goal contract items
                      one at a time (easiest goal mission first), the last
                      at X.

options.label: Allow Missions Harder Than Goal
options.description:
Allow contracts whose mission is harder than your goal mission.

On (default): the full ever-achievable contract range is eligible, so a
contract can be significantly harder than the goal and (once goals are
contracts) can even end up gating your goal. Off: contracts are capped at
the goal's difficulty — e.g. a Duna-return goal won't hand you a Tylo mining
contract. Difficulty is compared by intrinsic mission delta-v.

Independent of the home-system-local invariant: a home-local goal (e.g.
Mun flag) never gets out-of-system contracts regardless of this setting.

options.label: Allow Eve On Expert
options.description:
Allow Eve surface return / sample-return missions as goals and contracts.

Off (default): Eve return and sample-return are excluded everywhere as a
deliberate curation choice — they're physically achievable but tedious to
fly, so they never become a goal target or a contract. On: they become
available, but ONLY when base Difficulty is expert — independent of Physics
Difficulty (so a 'zero' physics run on a casual/normal base never surfaces
Eve).

options.label: Home Contract Floor
options.description:
Minimum number of home-body contracts guaranteed in the seed, regardless of
the ordinary contract selection.

Home-body contracts are the earliest-reachable locations in a run, so this
floor guarantees the item fill always has enough early slots to assemble a
deep goal's kit. Without it, far-home / broad-goal seeds can rarely run out
of reachable early slots and strand a progression item (an unsolvable seed).
The floor draws from whatever home-safe contract types are available — so it
stays generic as new contract types are added — and picks them randomly each
seed, so it adds slack without making starts samey.

0 = off (no guarantee). Counts toward the contract pool; does not raise the
per-contract reward-slot count.

options.label: Body Visibility Mode
options.description:
Which celestial bodies start HIDDEN, revealed only as you receive
"Discover <Body>" items (ResearchBodies-style).

auto         -- (default) pick a sane mode from the goal: a goal confined to
                your home system hides EVEN the home system (home_only, so
                you discover your own neighbourhood progressively); any wider
                goal hides everything OUTSIDE the home system (home_system).
all_visible  -- feature off: every body visible from the start, exactly as
                before. No Discover items are added.
home_system  -- your home body and the rest of its local system are visible;
                every other body is hidden until discovered.
home_only    -- only your home body is visible; everything else — including
                the rest of your home system — is hidden until discovered.

A hidden body's missions/contracts require its Discover item (logic-gated in
both AllowUndiscoveredBodies settings). Parent planets are discovered before
their moons. Your home body and the Sun are never hidden.

options.label: Allow Undiscovered Bodies
options.description:
Whether an undiscovered body's sphere still physically exists in-game.

On (default): a hidden body renders but is uninteractable — no map label,
not clickable, not Tab-selectable. You can still fly a probe there out of
logic; arriving reveals it locally. Off: a hidden body is fully invisible
(its sphere is removed); flying into its SOI destroys the craft, so you can
only reach what you have discovered.

Only meaningful when Body Visibility Mode is not all_visible; the generation
logic requires the Discover item either way.

options.label: Flag Bodies
options.description: Bodies to plant flags on (custom goal). Leave empty for preset goals.

options.label: Return Bodies
options.description: Bodies to return from (custom goal). Leave empty for preset goals.

options.label: Sample Return Bodies
options.description: Bodies to sample-return from (custom goal). Leave empty for preset goals.

options.label: Orbit Bodies
options.description: Bodies to reach orbit around (custom goal). Leave empty for preset goals.

options.label: Flyby Bodies
options.description: Bodies to perform a flyby of (custom goal). Leave empty for preset goals.

options.label: Enabled Part Packs
options.description:
Optional part packs to include in the seed. Stock parts are always
available; enable the DLC/expansion packs you own here (disable a pack to
leave its parts out of the run). Defaults to every shipped optional pack.

options.label: Trap Density
options.description:
How much of the filler item pool is replaced by trap items.

Traps are quirky client-actuated hazards (random staging, gravity
anomalies, a kerbal deciding to step outside, ...) that fire in flight
some time after being received.  Which traps appear is controlled by
Trap Type Weights.

none     -- No traps.
light    -- ~10% of filler items become traps.  The default.
moderate -- ~25% of filler.
heavy    -- ~50% of filler.
hell     -- Every filler item is a trap.

options.label: Trap Type Weights
options.description:
Relative weight of each trap type in the trap pool.  A weight of 0
disables that trap entirely; weights are relative, mirroring Contract
Type Weights.  All traps enabled and equally likely by default.

staging       -- Stage Fright: a 5-second klaxon, then your next stage fires.
gravity       -- Gravity Storm: local gravity runs 20-50% off for a while.
spin          -- Spin Cycle: the craft is thrown into a random tumble.
comms_outage  -- Radio Silence: every antenna goes dead for a while.
power_drain   -- Short Circuit: charge drains rapidly for a few seconds.
overheat      -- Thermal Runaway: one part heats toward (not past) failure.
part_failure  -- Loose Bolts: one peripheral part falls off.  Permanently.
surprise_eva  -- Mandatory Spacewalk: a kerbal steps outside.  Right now.
timewarp      -- Time Slip: time warp changes on its own.
throttle      -- Sticky Throttle: the throttle jumps to a random setting.
deployables   -- Minor Kraken Attack: panels, gear and antennas toggle.

options.label: Buff Density
options.description:
How many buff items are added to the filler pool.

Buffs are the upside twin of traps: the client mod applies each one
permanently for the rest of the run, and copies stack additively (three
+1% copies is +3%).  Each buff type ships as a three-rung ladder --
I is +1%, II is +3%, III is +5% -- so the density sets both how many
buffs you find and how high a single type can stack.  Structural
Integrity is the exception: it runs a steeper 5/15/25 ladder, because
the stats it scales are small enough in absolute terms that 1/3/5
would be imperceptible.

Buffs are drawn from the same pool as science packs, so a higher density
means fewer science packs.  They are invisible to logic: a buff can never
make an out-of-logic mission reachable, only make an in-logic one easier.

This also sets how many CONSUMABLE buffs you find -- one-shot charges you
spend from the mod menu whenever you want, rather than permanent boosts.
They have no I/II/III ladder, so the density is just a charge count.

Ceilings below are for the standard ladder; Structural Integrity's is
five times higher (+20% / +70% / +120% respectively).

none   -- No buffs.  No charges either.
light  -- 1 x I + 1 x II per type; a type can reach +4%.  1 charge per consumable type.
normal -- 3 x I + 2 x II + 1 x III per type; a type can reach +14%.  3 charges.  The default.
heavy  -- 5 x I + 3 x II + 2 x III per type; a type can reach +24%.  5 charges.

options.label: Buff Types
options.description:
Which buff categories can appear.  Omitting a name disables it entirely;
all of them are enabled by default.  Every enabled type is stocked equally.
The last entry is a consumable -- a one-shot charge you spend when you
choose -- and can be switched off exactly like the permanent boosts.

isp            -- Engine Efficiency: engines burn fuel more efficiently (more delta-v).
thrust         -- Engine Thrust: liquid engines push harder (better TWR).  Not SRBs.
heat_tolerance -- Heat Tolerance: every part survives a higher temperature.
structural     -- Structural Integrity: parts survive harder impacts and more stress.
control        -- Control Authority: stronger reaction wheels and wider engine gimbals.
power          -- Power Generation: solar panels, RTGs and fuel cells produce more charge.
refuel         -- Mid-Air Refuel (consumable): refills the active craft's fuel tanks in flight.

options.label: Death Link On Revert
options.description:
Also broadcast a death when you Revert a flight, so you can't save-scum a
failure away without the rest of the multiworld paying for it.  Requires
Death Link; ignored on its own.

Reverting a craft that never actually launched -- still clamped on the pad,
or on the runway before you taxi -- is always free, so checking a design or
fixing a misclick costs nothing.  A flight that already broadcast a death
(you crashed, or an incoming Death Link destroyed your craft) never sends a
second one when you revert it.

options.label: Level Order
options.description:
Determines which levels are unlocked with beacons. Each beacon will still unlock the same number of levels.
Vanilla: Each beacon will unlock its normal levels. Note that beacon locations may still be shuffled to random locations with Shuffle Beacons.
Faramore_Start_Shuffle: Each beacon will unlock 2 or 3 random levels, but Faramore Town is guaranteed to be one of your 2 starting levels to grant access to the shop.
Shuffle: Each beacon will unlock 2 or 3 random levels. Be careful that activating this might lock the store away for a while, and force the player to farm bags to get power stones.
Using Level Order = Faramore_Start_Shuffle or Shuffle without enabling Shuffle Beacons will make it hard to get a successful generation.

options.label: Shuffle Barrier Types
options.description:
When enabled, will randomize the barrier types. All barriers of a certain type will be changed to another.
If enabled, then Shuffle Coins or Tricky Jumps needs to be enabled as well, or else the Crypts Coin would be unreachable.

options.label: Shuffle NPCs
options.description: Include NPCs in the item and location pools. NPCs will stay in your local game.

options.label: Shuffle Bags
options.description: Include bags in the item and location pools.

options.label: Shuffle Keys
options.description:
Include all keys in the item and location pools.
This does not include quest items like the Fort Findula Dungeon Key.
This does also not include the Key in Lichen Hills' Music Shrine.

options.label: Shuffle Hills Key
options.description:
Add the Lichen Hills key and its Music Shrine location to the pool.
If spawned in your local game, this key is invisible until the Fatal Flute is played near it, making it difficult to find otherwise.
One would need to know every location check in the game, and play the Flute next to them if they are empty.
The only other empty location would be the Shield Ring if you already collected the Reflecting Ring.

options.label: Shuffle Candles
options.description: Include all candles in the item and location pools.

options.label: Shuffle Coins
options.description: Include all secret coins in the item and location pools.

options.label: Shuffle Rocks
options.description: Include all four colored rocks in the item and location pools.

options.label: Shuffle Plants
options.description: Include all three of the Cypress' quest's plants in the item and location poolsl.

options.label: Shuffle Upgrades
options.description: Include all the capacity upgrades in the item and location pools. This includes Infinite Soulfire.

options.label: Shuffle Life-Ups
options.description: Include all Life-Ups (extra hearts) in the item and location pools.

options.label: Shuffle Bonus Scrolls
options.description:
Include Bonus Scrolls in the item and location pools.
Bonus Scrolls will stay in your local game, and cannot spawn from other items.

options.label: Shuffle Bonus Scroll Rewards
options.description:
Include the Rubies rewards from the bonus minigame scrolls in the item and location pools.
Note that Faramore, Volcano and Castle Bonus do not have any rewards.

options.label: Shuffle Race Rewards
options.description: Include the 100 Rubies rewards from the Rudy races in the item and location pools.

options.label: Shuffle Beacons
options.description:
Include the Sacred Beacons in the item and location pools.
Sacred Beacons will stay in your local game, cannot spawn from other items, and will still unlock levels when hit.
Not to be confused with Level Order, which decides which level is unlocked by hitting the beacon.

options.label: Shuffle Jewel Shards
options.description: Include the Faramore Jewel shards in the item and location pools. Beating the five bosses will now grant random items.

options.label: Trading Sequence
options.description:
Determine how the Chainsword trading sequence is randomized:
Vanilla: All items except the Dungeon Key will be in their vanilla locations, including the Chainsword. In other words, talking to Alven once will give you random item. Finding the Fort Findula Dungeon Key will kickstart the trading sequence, which will always lead to the Chainsword in the end.
Random_Start: One random item of the trading sequence will be shuffled, and the rest of the sequence from that item will be in their vanilla locations, including the Chainsword. The start of the trade quest will be avoided entirely, including Zazie's Soul Upgrade if it doesn't start with the Sacred Oil.
Excluded: The Dungeon Key, the Sacred Oil & Refined Chains, and the Chainsword items will be shuffled, as well as the locations for the Dungeon Key, the Sacred Oil and the Chainsword. The rest of the trade quest will be avoided entirely, including Zazie's Soul Upgrade. In other words, talking to Alven once will give you random item, talking to Alven with the Sacred Oil and Refined Chains will give you a random item, and going to the end of the Fort Findula Dungeon will give you a random item. Every other NPC interaction in the sequence will ask for an item that you cannot obtain.
Shuffle: Every item in the Chainsword trading sequence is added to the item and location pools. The game has been modified so you can hold multiple items of the trading sequence at the same time, but they might not show up in the inventory.

options.label: Tricky Jumps
options.description: When enabled, some jumps and movement techniques that are much more difficult than usual may be considered in logic. See documentation for more information.

options.label: No Lantern
options.description: When enabled, you may be expected to navigate dark areas without the lantern.

options.label: Damage Boosting
options.description: When enabled, you may be expected to damage boost to an extent that will be possible in casual mode with health drops. When disabled, you can collect everything logically without taking damage.

options.label: Goal Type
options.description:
Determines what is required to unlock The Rainbow Cloud where Mew (the Goal Condtion) lives.
Note: If significantly lowering requirements, we recommend disabling the # pokemon and score cehcks
- signs: What is used in Vanilla Pokemon Snap - spread accross the multiworlds. Can be adjusted.
- pokemon_pictures: A number of Pokemon Pictures spread accross the multiworlds.  Can be adjusted.

options.label: 'Good Technique' Mew Required
options.description:
Determines if submitting a "Good Technique" photo of Mew is required to win.
Does nothing if "Good Technique" photos are disabled

options.label: Signs Required
options.description:
Determines the number of Sign Pictures required to unlock the Rainbow Cloud.
Only matters if Goal Type is set to "Signs"

options.label: Extra Sign Pictures
options.description:
Determines how many extra Sign Pictures to add to the pool.
Only matters if Goal Type is set to "Signs"

options.label: Pokemon Required
options.description:
Determines the number of Pokemon Pictures required to unlock the Rainbow Cloud.
Only matters if Goal Type is set to "Pokemon"

options.label: Extra Pokemon Pictures
options.description:
Determines how many extra Pokemon Pictures to add to the pool.
Only matters if Goal Type is set to "Pokemon"

options.label: Picture Names
options.description:
Determines how the goal items are named.

Generic: All goal items will be called "Pokemon Picture"/"Sign Picture"
Specific: Items will be labeled to specific locations, e.g. "Pokemon Picture: Charmander"/"Sign Picture: Kingler Rock"

options.label: Photo Scoring
options.description:
Determines how the photo score bonuses, "Good Technique" and "Multiple PKMN", are unlocked.
- vanilla: Photo score bonuses are available from the start. "Multiple PKMN" score requires "Good Technique."
- separate: Photo score bonuses are available from the start. "Multiple PKMN" can be scored *without* "Good Technique."
- progressive_unlocks: Adds "Progressive Scoring" items that unlock "Good Technique" then "Multiple PKMN."
- separate_unlocks: Adds items that unlock "Good Technique" and "Multiple PKMN" scoring separately.

options.label: Extra 'Photo Score Bonus' Items
options.description:
Adds the specified number of extra scoring bonus items to the pool, making it more likely
to unlock "Good Technique" and "Multiple PKMN" bonuses earlier.

If `photo_scoring` is set to `vanilla` or `separate`, this does nothing.

options.label: Starting Film
options.description: Sets the amount of film available at the start of the game.

options.label: Maximum Film
options.description:
Sets the maximum amount of film available.
Making this number very small will increase the length of your playthrough.

options.label: Film Upgrade Amount
options.description: Sets the amount of film granted by each "Film Capacity Upgrade" item.

options.label: Extra Film Capacity Upgrades
options.description: Adds the specified number of extra "Film Capacity Upgrade" items to the item pool.

options.label: Map Fragments
options.description:
Determines the number of items required to unlock a course.

Examples:
- If set to 1, finding the "Beach" item will unlock the Beach course.
- If set to 2+, you will need that many "Beach: Map Fragment" items to unlock the Beach course.

options.label: Per-Course Item Unlocks
options.description: Unlock the Apple, Pester Ball, and PokeFlute for each level separately, rather than every level at once.

options.label: Filler Item Names
options.description:
Determines how filler items are named. 

Simple: all filler items will be called "Bad Picture"
Flavorful: filler items will have flavorful names, e.g. "Faded Photo of Blastoise"

options.label: 'Apple-shaped Pokemon Food' Item Name
options.description: Determines what the "Apple-Shaped Pokemon Food" unlock is called in the AP world. Has no impact on gameplay.

options.label: Include photo bonuses
options.description:
Determines which photo bonuses to include as checks.
- technique_and_multiple: adds "Good Technique" and "Multiple Pokemon" photos as checks 
- technique_only: adds "Good Technique" photos as checks
- none: only normal photos are checks

options.label: Include special poses
options.description:
Include the 11 "Special Pose" photos as checks. The special poses are:
- Beach:   Surfing Pikachu, Pikachu on a Stump, Gust-Using Pidgey
- Tunnel:  Pikachu on a Ball
- Volcano: Fighting Magmar
- River:   Speed Pikachu
- Cave:    Balloon Pikachu, Flying Pikachu, Jigglypuff on Stage, Jigglypuff Trio on Stage
- Valley:  Graveler's Group Dance

options.label: Include pokemon signs
options.description: Include the 6 Pokemon Sign photos as checks (requires Pokemon Sign Detector).

options.label: Include secret exits
options.description: Include taking each of the 3 Secret Exits (Tunnel, River, and Valley) as checks.

options.label: PKMN Report Photo Rewards
options.description:
Include the three photo count rewards from Professor Oak as checks. 
They are rewarded for having 6, 22, and 40 pictures in your PKMN Report.

options.label: PKMN Report Score Rewards
options.description:
Include the three PKMN Report score checkpoint rewards from Professor Oak as checks. 
They are rewarded for having a score of 24,000, 72,500, and 130,000 in your PKMN Report.

options.label: Include random checks
options.description:
Include the luck-heavy photos as checks. They are:
- [Volcano] Arcanine: Multiple
- [  River] Cloyster: Multiple and Psyduck: Multiple
- [ Valley] Magikarp (Valley): Multiple and Dratini: Multiple

options.label: Include hard checks
options.description:
Include the hard photos as checks. They are:
- [ River] Pikachu (River): Good Technique
- [  Cave] Zubat (Cave): Multiple, Magikarp (Cave): Wonderful, Balloon Pikachu, and Flying Pikachu
- [Valley] Staryu: Multiple, Starmie: Multiple, and Goldeen: Good Technique

options.label: Hard logic
options.description:
Enable hard logic.

This puts more checks in-logic earlier, with potentially much more difficult requirements. 
Only enable this option if you are experienced and want a challenge.

options.label: Start with Dash Engine
options.description:
Start with the Dash Engine.

This makes up to six more checks available from the beginning.

options.label: Press L to start/stop
options.description:
Adds the ability to start/stop the Zero-One by pressing L.
- start_with: start the game with this ability
- in_item_pool: add the ability to the item pool
- disabled: default

options.label: Press L to start/stop (deprecated)
options.description: Deprecated. Use the new option `left_bumper_to_start_stop` instead.

options.label: Camera Inversion
options.description: Choose if the camera controls are Normal or Inverted.

options.label: Death Link
options.description:
When somebody dies the level will be reloaded.
Can be toggled with '/deathlink' in-game

options.label: Death Link Amnesty
options.description: How many water/scissor touches it takes to send a DeathLink

options.label: Trap Link
options.description:
Traps with other TrapLink players are shared.
Can be toggled with '/traplink' in-game

options.label: Shuffle Kiosk Reward
options.description:
Choose whether to shuffle the Kiosk to NOT give the next Ticket but instead something else.
Compatible with 'Start with Ticket'.
Check the in-game Tracker for Kiosk Cost and if you bought it.

options.label: Start with Ticket
options.description: You'll start with a random Ticket. Highly recommended as there are only 3 checks at Home!

options.label: Enable Achievements
options.description:
Enables if Achievements should be a location.
Frog Fan only needs 10 bumps & Volley Dreams only needs a highscore of 5 in every level.

options.label: Shuffle Handsome Frog
options.description: Enables if talking to Handsome Frog should be a location.

options.label: Shuffle Gary's Garden
options.description: Choose whether Gary's Garden should have locations.

options.label: Gary's Garden Access
options.description:
Changes when Gary's Garden is accessible.
Tadpole HQ: Gary's Garden will be accessible when Tadpole HQ is accessible.
-----------------------------------------------------------
Tadpole HQ & Gary's Garden: Gary's Garden won't be accessible until Tadpole HQ Ticket & Gary's Garden Ticket are obtained.
-----------------------------------------------------------
Gary's Garden: Gary's Garden will be accessible in 'Home' when Gary's Garden Ticket has been obtained.

options.label: Level Specific Keys
options.description:
If this option is enabled, Keys will be specific to the level.
Hairball City Keys only open Hairball City Locks, Turbine Town Keys only open Turbine Town Locks etc.

options.label: Cassette Logic
options.description:
This changes how Mitch & Mai work

LevelBased: Cassettes have been split up into level specific variants.
So you need 'Hairball City Cassette' 5x/10x to trade with Mitch/Mai in Hairball City.
-----------------------------------------------------------
Progressive: Mitch and Mai require increasing numbers of cassettes to unlock their locations.
Unlock order is fixed: The number of cassettes needed progresses incrementally -> 5 -> 10 -> 15 -> 20 -> 25.
The in-game Cassette Tracker shows from left to right your progress.
When you buy the first progressive unlock, the first Mitch/Mai icon will be marked as purchased.
If Gary's Garden is shuffled -> The tracker starts at Gary's Garden. If not shuffled -> The tracker starts at Hairball City.
-----------------------------------------------------------
Scattered: Prices are randomly shuffled between all Mitch & Mai Locations.

options.label: Extra Cassettes in Item Pool
options.description:
This option will try to add extra 'Cassettes' to the Item Pool.
If there are not enough locations, it will add as many as it can!

options.label: Progressive Contact List
options.description: If this option is enabled, the Contact Lists will not be separate, so you cannot get Contact List 2 before Contact List 1.

options.label: Snail Shop
options.description: When enabled the clothes shop from the Tamagotchi Snail will contain AP Items.

options.label: Speed Boost in Item Pool
options.description: Determines how many 'Speed Boost' are in the pool.

options.label: Completion Goal
options.description:
Set your Completion Goal.
Hired: Reach Pepper's Interview and get hired!
Employee: Get 76 Coins and be the Employee Of The Month!
Custom: Get a custom amount of coins to complete the game!
Garden: Restore Gary's Garden to its former glory!
Friend: Be everyone's best friend by helping Mitch, Mai, Little Gabi, Fischer, Moomy and co. (This will enable Fishsanity, Seedsanity, Flowersanity and Bonesanity)

options.label: Minimum Kiosk Cost
options.description:
Determines the lowest possible cost for a Kiosk.
Disabled if 'Shuffle Kiosk Reward' is false

options.label: Maximum Kiosk Cost
options.description:
Determines the highest possible cost for a Kiosk.
Disabled if 'Shuffle Kiosk Reward' is false

options.label: Minimum Elevator Repair Cost
options.description: Determines the lowest possible cost for the elevator

options.label: Maximum Elevator Repair Cost
options.description: Determines the highest possible cost for the elevator

options.label: Minimum Custom Goal Cost
options.description: Determines the lowest possible cost the custom goal.

options.label: Maximum Custom Goal Cost
options.description: Determines the highest possible cost the custom goal.

options.label: Safety Helmet
options.description: When enabled, a 'Safety Helmet' is required to break breakable blocks.

options.label: Bug net
options.description: When enabled, a 'Bug Net' is required to catch bugs.

options.label: Soda Cans
options.description:
When enabled, soda cannons are broken, the item 'Soda Repair' will make the frog engineers repair them.
DOESN'T INCLUDE THE ELEVATOR!

options.label: Parasols
options.description: When enabled, Parasols are broken, the item 'Parasol Repair' will make the frog engineers repair them.

options.label: Swimming
options.description: When enabled, a 'Swim Course' is required to swim in water.

options.label: Precise Jumps
options.description:
Only available when Swimming is enabled.
When this option is enabled, the logic will expect you to reach locations that require precise jumps

options.label: Textbox
options.description:
Want to have a break talking with NPCs?
Vanilla: Normal Here Comes Niko! behaviour
-----------------------------------------------------------
Global: The item 'Textbox' is required to interact with anything that uses the textbox
-----------------------------------------------------------
Level: Every level requires its own textbox item to interact with anything that uses the textbox, so Hairball City needs 'Hairball City Textbox'

options.label: Air Conditioners
options.description: When enabled, ACs are broken, the item 'AC Repair' will make the frog engineers repair them.

options.label: Apple Basket
options.description: When enabled, Apples cannot be picked up until you have the item 'Apple Basket' to store them in.

options.label: Fishsanity
options.description:
Need more checks or are you just insane?
Vanilla: Normal Here Comes Niko! behaviour
-----------------------------------------------------------
Location: Every single fish you can fish with Fischer is a unique location
-----------------------------------------------------------
Insanity: Same as location with the change that Fischer won't give you the 'Fish with Fischer' item until you have all 5 fish for that level obtained.
So you need the item 'Hairball City Fish' 5x before being able to obtain Fischer's reward in Hairball City.
Check the in-game menu, to see if you have enough fish and obtained the reward from Fischer.

options.label: Seedsanity
options.description:
Need more checks or are you just insane?
Vanilla: Normal Here Comes Niko! behaviour
-----------------------------------------------------------
Location: Every single seed you can collect with the hamster ball is a unique location
-----------------------------------------------------------
Insanity: Same as location with the change that Moomy won't give you the reward for collecting all seeds until you have been sent all 10 seeds for that level.
So you need the item 'Hairball City Seed' 10x before being able to obtain Moomy's reward in Hairball City.
Check the in-game menu, to see if you have enough seeds and obtained the reward from Moomy.

options.label: Flowersanity
options.description:
Need more checks or are you just insane?
Vanilla: Normal Here Comes Niko! behaviour
-----------------------------------------------------------
Location: Every single flower bed is a unique location
-----------------------------------------------------------
Insanity: Same as location with the change that Little Gabi won't give you the reward for completing all flower beds until you have been sent all flowers for that level.
So you need the item 'Hairball City Flower' 3x before being able to obtain Little Gabi's reward in Hairball City.
Check the in-game menu, to see if you have enough flowers and obtained the reward from Little Gabi.

options.label: Bonesanity
options.description:
Need more checks or are you just insane?
Vanilla: Normal Here Comes Niko! behaviour
-----------------------------------------------------------
Location: Every single bone is a unique location
-----------------------------------------------------------
Insanity: Same as location with the change that Bone Dog won't give you the reward for collecting all bones until you have been sent all bones for that level.
So you need the item 'Hairball City Bone' 5x before being able to obtain Bone Dog's reward in Hairball City.
Check the in-game menu, to see if you have enough bones and obtained the reward from Bone Dog.

options.label: Applesanity
options.description:
Need more checks or are you just insane?
When enabled, freestanding apples will be randomized.
This adds ~290 locations.

options.label: Bugsanity
options.description:
Need more checks or are you just insane?
When enabled, bugs will be randomized.
This adds 349 locations.

options.label: Chatsanity
options.description:
Need more checks or are you just insane?
Vanilla: Normal Here Comes Niko! behaviour
-----------------------------------------------------------
Level Based: Every single NPC you can talk to is a unique location in every level
-----------------------------------------------------------
Global: Every single NPC you can talk to is a unique location, but only once, regardless of level

options.label: Thoughtsanity
options.description:
Chatsanity Part 2
When enabled, Niko's thoughts will send a unique location similar to Chatsanity
Niko's thought are found at places with a magnifying glass

options.label: Trap Chance
options.description: The chance for any junk item in the pool to be replaced by a trap.

options.label: Freeze Trap Weight
options.description:
The weight of Freeze Traps in the trap pool.
Freeze Traps will temporarily make Niko unable to move.

options.label: Iron Boots Trap Weight
options.description:
The weight of Iron Boots Traps in the trap pool.
Iron Boots Traps will make Niko slow & heavy.

options.label: Whoops! Trap Weight
options.description:
The weight of Whoops! Traps in the trap pool.
Whoops! Traps will send Niko way up in the sky.

options.label: My Turn! Trap Weight
options.description:
The weight of My Turn! Traps in the trap pool.
My Turn! Traps will make Niko jump, dive and move in random directions.

options.label: Gravity Trap Weight
options.description:
The weight of Gravity Traps in the trap pool.
Gravity Traps will temporarily remove gravity.

options.label: Home Trap Weight
options.description:
The weight of Home Traps in the trap pool.
Home Traps will send Niko back to Home.

options.label: W I D E Trap Weight
options.description:
The weight of W I D E Traps in the trap pool.
W I D E Traps will make Niko very wide.

options.label: Phone Trap Weight
options.description:
The weight of Phone Traps in the trap pool.
Phone Traps will force Niko to receive an unskippable phone call.

options.label: Tiny Trap Weight
options.description:
The weight of Tiny Traps in the trap pool.
Tiny Traps will make Niko very tiny.

options.label: Jumping Jacks Trap Weight
options.description:
The weight of Jumping Jacks Traps in the trap pool.
Jumping Jacks Traps will make Niko jump continuously.

options.label: Camera Stuck Trap Weight
options.description:
The weight of Camera Stuck Traps in the trap pool.
Camera Stuck Traps will stop the camera from turning.

options.label: Inverted Camera Trap Weight
options.description:
The weight of Inverted Camera Traps in the trap pool.
Inverted Camera Traps will invert the cameras X and Y controls.

options.label: There Goes Niko Trap Weight
options.description:
The weight of There Goes Niko Traps in the trap pool.
There Goes Niko Traps will make the camera stop in place.

options.label: Goal
options.description: Select the victory condition used for this seed.

options.label: Triple Pagie Medal Goal
options.description: Number of Triple Pagie Medals required for Triple Pagie Medal Hunt.

options.label: Golden Pagie Goal
options.description: Number of Golden Pagies required for Golden Pagie Hunt.

options.label: Golden Pagie Pool
options.description: Number of Golden Pagies placed in the item pool for Golden Pagie Hunt.

options.label: Capital Key Pool
options.description: Number of Capital Keys placed in the item pool for Defeat Capital B.

options.label: Capital Key Goal
options.description: Number of Capital Keys required to unlock Capital B for Defeat Capital B.

options.label: Quillsanity
options.description: Include all 750 individual Quill checks as Archipelago locations as well as 30 Trowzer shop locations + 5 checks for having all 150 quills. Adds 785 locations to the game

options.label: Final Round Tickets Required
options.description: Number of Final Round Tickets required before a final-round win can complete the goal.

options.label: Final Round Tickets In Pool
options.description: Number of Final Round Tickets in the item pool. Must be at least the ticket goal.

options.label: Team Round Checks
options.description: Include the thirteen team round checks and one Teamwork Crown progression item.

options.label: Final Rounds Checks
options.description: Include qualification checks for the selected final maps.

options.label: Final Round Maps
options.description: Final maps to include when Final Rounds Checks is enabled. Remove names to disable specific maps.

options.label: DeathLink
options.description:
Share local eliminations. Received DeathLinks block checks until the next map loads.
Override during play with /deathlink on or /deathlink off.

options.label: Qualifysanity
options.description:
Add sequential qualification checks and 18 Progressive Qualify Cap items.
Start at 10% capacity; each item unlocks another 5%. Qualifications at the cap are discarded.

options.label: Qualifysanity Checks
options.description: Total sequential qualification checks. Fractional capacities round down to whole checks.

options.label: Itchy and Scratchy Ticket Requirement
options.description:
Goal is watching the Itchy and Scratchy film in the Lobby.
You'll receive the Ticket when you complete the requirements chosen.

options.label: Required Wasp Amount
options.description: Number of Wasps additionally required to gain the Itchy and Scratchy ticket. There are 20 per level.

options.label: Required Card Amount
options.description: Number of Cards additionally required to gain the Itchy and Scratchy ticket. There are 7 per level.

options.label: Required Mission Levels
options.description:
If the ticket requires missions, choose which level's missions are required.
Missions in other levels may still unlock required items.
Has no effect if the ticket doesn't require missions.
Valid options are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, or All.

options.label: Bonus Mission Required
options.description: Choose whether bonus missions from required levels are required to goal.

options.label: Race Mission Required
options.description: Choose whether race missions from required levels are required to goal.

options.label: Required Car Amount
options.description: If the ticket requires cars collected, choose the amount of cars required.

options.label: Lock Levels
options.description: If enabled, levels are will be inaccessible to Free Roam until you receive their respective Level item.

options.label: Early Level Item
options.description: If enabled, attempt to place at least one of your required levels in an early location.

options.label: Shuffle Levels
options.description:
Choose how you want Levels to be received.
If shuffled, 6 Level X items will be shuffled into the item pool which will allow access to that level's missions
Otherwise, 6 Progressive Level items will be shuffled into the item pool, allowing you to access levels in the vanilla order.
Regardless of your choice, missions can be played in any order on an unlocked level.

options.label: Shuffle Starting Car
options.description:
Choose whether to shuffle starting car between available cars from your starting level.
If disabled, you'll always start with your starting level's default car.

options.label: Shuffle Attack
options.description:
Choose whether to add Attack to the pool for each character.
Valid options are Homer, Bart, Lisa, Marge, Apu, All, or None.

options.label: Shuffle Jump
options.description:
Choose whether to add Jump to the pool for each character.
Valid options are Homer, Bart, Lisa, Marge, Apu, All, or None.

options.label: Starting Jump Level
options.description:
Choose how many Progressive Jump items to start with for each character.
Characters who aren't included in ShuffleJump will start with Progressive Jump Level 2.

options.label: Shuffle Gagfinder
options.description:
Choose whether to add a Gagfinder to the pool for each Character that will be required to
unlock gags as that character. Valid options are Homer, Bart, Lisa, Marge, Apu, All, or None.
If None, gags will instead be locked until you receive their Level.

options.label: Shuffle Checkered Flags
options.description:
Choose whether to add a Checkered Flag to the pool for each Character that will be required to
unlock races as that character. Valid options are Homer, Bart, Lisa, Marge, Apu, All, or None.
If None, races will instead be locked until you receive their Level.

options.label: Shuffle E-Brake
options.description:
Choose whether to shuffle ability to use the E-Brake for each character into the item pool.
Characters not chosen will always be able to use the E-Brake.
Valid options are Homer, Bart, Lisa, Marge, Apu, All, or None.

options.label: Shuffle Bumpers
options.description:
Choose whether to shuffle Frink-o-Matic Wasp Bumpers into the item pool.
Characters not chosen won't have a Wasp Bumper in the item pool and *WILL NOT* be able to break wasps with cars.
Valid options are Homer, Bart, Lisa, Marge, Apu, All, or None.

options.label: Start With Bumpers
options.description:
If true, add all enabled Wasp Bumpers to the start inventory.
If you want more granular control of this, use the generic start inventory.

options.label: Shuffle Forward
options.description:
Choose whether to shuffle the ability to move forward or drive forward for each character into the item pool.
Characters not chosen won't have a forward in the item pool and will always be able to move forward.
Valid options are Homer, Bart, Lisa, Marge, Apu, All, or None.
**THIS COULD CREATE VERY DIFFICULT SEEDS**

options.label: Early Forward
options.description:
If enabled and forward is shuffled, try to place each specified character's Forward item early.
Valid options are Homer, Bart, Lisa, Marge, Apu, All, or None. Does nothing if the character's forward isn't shuffled.

options.label: Shuffle Cards
options.description:
Randomize card locations. This option adds several possible locations for
cards. There will still be 49 total cards with 7 in each level.

options.label: Mission Locks
options.description: Add car requirements to a percentage of missions

options.label: Adjust Mission Timers
options.description:
Increase mission timers by the chosen percentage.
For example, if a mission has a timer of 1:00 and the chosen value is 50, then the mission will have a timer of 1:30

options.label: Min Shop Price
options.description: The minimum cost of any item in Gil's Shop. If this is greater than the max shop price, then the max will be used instead.

options.label: Max Shop Price
options.description: The maximum cost of any item in Gil's Shop.

options.label: Shop Price Level Scale Multiplier
options.description:
The multiplier for shop costs per levels. For each level after L1, min and max will be multiplied by level number and this multiplier.
L2 = Min/Max * Mod * 2, L3 = Min/Max * Mod * 3, etc.

options.label: Starting Wallet Level
options.description:
Choose how many Progressive Wallet Levels to start with.
Level 1 shops are in logic with 1 level, level 2 with 2, etc.
Your coin cap = MaxShopPrice * WalletLevel * ShopScaleMod and is unlimited at Wallet Level 7

options.label: Shop Hint Policy
options.description:
Choose the level of hints sent when speaking to Gil for the first time on a level
All: Hint all items in Gil's shop
OnlyProg: Only hint progression items in Gil's shop
None: No shop hints will be created

options.label: Extra Hint Policy
options.description: Place extra hints in various places.

options.label: Filler Wrench Efficiency
options.description: Percentage damage a filler wrench item will repair your cars.

options.label: Filler Hit N Run Reset Efficiency
options.description: Percentage a filler Hit N Run Reset item will lower your Hit N Run meter.

options.label: Shuffle Traffic
options.description: Randomize traffic per level. Cars that are usually used as traffic in that level plus the starting car of the next level are unable to be chosen for their level.

options.label: Traffic Blacklist
options.description:
Block cars from appearing as traffic. There must be at least 35 cars available to shuffle.
If there are less than 5 cars available for any level after applying the blacklist, then traffic will not be shuffled.

options.label: Filler Traps
options.description:
How many fillers will be replaced with traps. 0 means no additional traps, 100 means all fillers are traps.
These traps are IN ADDITION to any enabled traps above, though it won't add trap types that have been disabled.

options.label: Enable Eject Traps
options.description: Whether to include Eject traps in the item pool.

options.label: Enable Duff Traps
options.description: Whether to include Duff traps in the item pool.

options.label: Enable Launch Traps
options.description: Whether to include Launch traps in the item pool.

options.label: Enable Hit N Run Traps
options.description: Whether to include Hit N Run traps in the item pool.

options.label: Enable Traffic Traps
options.description: Whether to include Traffic traps in the item pool.

options.label: End Goal
options.description:
The end goal required to beat the game.

**X-0 - Helping Hands:**
Clear all other bosses (1-X, 2-X, 3-X, 3-DOG, 1-XN, 5-X, 6-X, 7-X, 7-X2) to unlock X-0 - Helping Hands.
Then, clear X-0 to beat the game!

**B Rank All Levels:**
Clear all levels with a B rank or higher to beat the game!

**A Rank All Levels:**
Clear all levels with an A rank or higher to beat the game!

**Perfect All Levels:**
Clear all levels with an S/Perfect rank to beat the game!

options.label: Boss Unlock Requirement
options.description:
The requirements to unlock the boss level for an act.

**B Rank:**
The number of levels in their respective act are required to be cleared with a B rank or higher to unlock the act's boss.

**A Rank:**
The number of levels in their respective act are required to be cleared with an A rank or higher to unlock the act's boss.

**Perfect:**
The number of levels in their respective act are required to be cleared with an S/Perfect rank to unlock the act's boss.

options.label: Act 1 Boss Unlock Requirement
options.description:
The number of levels required to be cleared (with the rank set in Boss Unlock Requirement) to unlock '1-X - Battleworn Insomniac'.

This includes '1-BOO - theme of really spooky bird' and '1-CNY - Chinese New Year'.

options.label: Act 2 Boss Unlock Requirement
options.description:
The number of levels required to be cleared (with the rank set in Boss Unlock Requirement) to unlock '2-X - All The Times'.

This includes '2-B1 - Beans Hopper', but **does not** include '2-XN - Bitter Times'.

options.label: Act 3 Boss Unlock Requirement
options.description: The number of levels required to be cleared (with the rank set in Boss Unlock Requirement) to unlock '3-X - One Shift More'.

options.label: Act 4 Boss Unlock Requirement
options.description: The number of levels required to be cleared (with the rank set in Boss Unlock Requirement) to unlock '1-XN - Super Battleworn Insomniac'.

options.label: Act 5 Boss Unlock Requirement
options.description:
The number of levels required to be cleared (with the rank set in Boss Unlock Requirement) to unlock 5-X - Dreams Don't Stop.

This includes '5-3 - Seventh-Inning Stretch', but **does not** include '5-B1 - Rhythm Weightlifter'.

options.label: Act 6 Boss Unlock Requirement
options.description: The number of levels required to be cleared (with the rank set in Boss Unlock Requirement) to unlock '6-X - Boss Fight'.

options.label: Act 7 Boss Unlock Requirement
options.description:
The number of levels required to be cleared (with the rank set in Boss Unlock Requirement) to unlock the Abandoned Ward and '7-X - Miracle Defibrillator', '7-X2 - Miracle Defibrillator (Cole's Song)'.

This includes '2-XN - Bitter Times'.

options.label: Perfect Rank Locations
options.description: Determines if Perfect/S rank locations should be placed in the world.

options.label: Trap Chance
options.description:
Determines the percent likeliness of a **filler item becoming a trap**.
**The sum of Trap Chance and Powerup Chance cannot be over 100%.**

options.label: Enable Fragile Heart Traps
options.description: Determines if **increased mistake weight traps** should be in the item pool.

options.label: Enable Character Scramble Traps
options.description: Determines if **randomized characters traps** should be in the item pool.

options.label: Enable Beatsound Scramble Traps
options.description: Determines if **randomized beatsound traps** should be in the item pool.

options.label: Enable Hitsound Scramble Traps
options.description: Determines if **randomized hitsound traps** should be in the item pool.

options.label: Enable Hard Difficulty Traps
options.description: Determines if **hard difficulty traps** should be in the item pool.

options.label: Enable Chilli Speed Traps
options.description: Determines if **🌶️ chilli speed traps** should be in the item pool.

options.label: Enable Ghost Tap Traps
options.description: Determines if **ghost tap traps** (make a mistake on ghost tap) should be in the item pool.

options.label: Sticky Traps
options.description: Determines the **set of traps that should be applied wherever possible**.

options.label: Powerup Chance
options.description:
Determines the percent likeliness of a **filler item becoming a powerup**.
**The sum of Trap Chance and Powerup Chance cannot be over 100%.**

options.label: Enable Easy Difficulty Powerups
options.description: Determines if **easy difficulty powerups** should be in the item pool.

options.label: Enable Strong Heart Powerups
options.description: Determines if **decreased mistake weight powerups** should be in the item pool.

options.label: Enable Ice Speed Powerups
options.description: Determines if **🧊 ice speed powerups** should be in the item pool.

options.label: Death Link
options.description:
When you die (a patient's heart breaks), everyone dies. The reverse is also true.

This can be changed in-game, using the Archipelago page in the pause menu.

options.label: Number of Chests
options.description: How many chests there are.

options.label: Number of Locked Chests
options.description:
How many of the chests are locked.
If a chest is locked, it will require its respective key to open.
This number must be at least 1 less than the total number of chests. If it isn't, this number will be changed automatically.

options.label: Number of Required Chests
options.description:
How many chests must be opened in order to goal.
This number must be no greater than the total number of chests. If it isn't, this number will be changed automatically.

options.label: Required Level
options.description: Choose what level is required to beat the game.

options.label: Victory Condition
options.description:
Choose what the victory condition of your run is:
'Any%' - You must defeat the Queen of Karst Castle
'True Ending' - You must get game's True Ending
'100%' - You must colelct every single randomized location and then beat the final boss

options.label: Fast Kill
options.description:
If this is enabled, any damage taken will instantly kill you, regardless of hp.
Can be on/off all the time or else only enabled during boss fights.

options.label: Include Ivory Bugs
options.description: If this is enabled, Ivory Bug locations will be included as checks.

options.label: Include Vitality Fragments
options.description: If this is enabled, Vitality Fragment locations will be included as checks.

options.label: HARD MODE
options.description:
Makes item logic less strict. You will have to do speedrun tech to progress.
Specifically, no-hit boss drops and garden key skip are in logic.

options.label: Death Link
options.description:
If enabled, dying will kill all other deathlink players, and vice versa.
Can be on/off all the time or else only enabled during boss fights.

options.label: Death Link Amount
options.description: How many deaths will it take to trigger a deathlink. (Ignored if Deathlink=never)

options.label: Character
options.description:
The character you play as during the run.
The game will force the character picked here to be your character in-game.
That means you don't need to unlock Scorpion/Sub-Zero first in order to play as them.
The VS mode exclusive characters are also available, but due to how they work they always start with fully upgraded
 special moves except for R2, so that means there will be no special move upgrade items in the multiworld except R2,
You can still purchase upgrades in the menu like with other characters.

options.label: Red Koin goal percent
options.description:
There are 60 Red Koins in the item pool.
Choose what percent of the 60 Red Koins are needed for goal.

0 - the goal will be beating the boss goal only, will turn Red Koins to filler.
80 (default) - get at least 80% of all Red Koins AND beat the boss goal to win.
100 - get ALL 60 Red Koins AND beat the boss goal.

There is a tracker in the pause menu that shows: current amount / needed for goal / total in the multiworld.

options.label: Boss Goal
options.description:
What bosses are needed for goal.
The goal also includes getting enough Red Koins, set in the red_koin_need_percent option.

no_bosses - no bosses at all are needed, the goal is Red Koins only.
shao_kahn_only (default) - only the final boss of the game is needed for the goal.
main_bosses - all main bosses (Kitana, Reptile, Baraka, Goro and Scorpion) and the final boss.
main_and_secret_bosses - all previously mentioned bosses and all secret bosses (Ermac, Mileena and Kano).

Setting this to no_bosses requires red_koin_need_percent to be above 0.

options.label: Fatalitysanity
options.description: If on, adds checks for performing all of your character's different fatalities, multalities and brutality

options.label: Shopsanity
options.description:
If on, adds checks for purchasing special move upgrades and combos
Logic expects you to be able to reach a different amount of regions in the game before buying tiers of upgrades
and to buy upgrades in order or price, so buy the cheap upgrades first then go up.
If off, buying special move upgrades acts like the vanilla game.

options.label: Wu-Shi Academy start
options.description:
If on, when pressing new game in the main menu, the game will start in Wu-Shi instead of Goro's Lair.
You can get to Goro's Lair from Wu-Shi after getting the fist of ruin ability.
This option allows for faster starts and more varied seeds.

options.label: Skip Tutorial
options.description:
Turn this option on to skip the turotials in Goro's Lair.
Irrelevant when Wu-Shi start is on.

options.label: Randomize tournament victories
options.description:
If on, shuffles 5 tournament victories in the item pool, all 5 are required to open the door to the foundry.
when off, beating all 5 main bosses is required to open the foundry door.

options.label: Mana Upgrades
options.description:
If on, shuffles 4 mana upgrades to the item pool.
the upgrades increase your maximum mana by 25% each time, doubling your mana after all upgrades

options.label: Friendsanity
options.description:
Add checks for befriending each character.
Each multiple of 10 friendship points is a check.

options.label: Datesanity
options.description: Add checks for dating each character.

options.label: Ending
options.description: Which endings should be considered a goal?

options.label: Perksanity
options.description:
Add checks for getting each skill perk.
Will disable your ability to level past each perk and shuffle perks into the pool

options.label: Building Randomization
options.description: Should buildings be randomized with each other?

options.label: Character Randomization
options.description: Should characters be randomized with each other?

options.label: Force Card Battles
options.description: Should card battles be forced on?

options.label: Element amount
options.description: How many elements are received from Archipelago?

options.label: Filler amount
options.description: How many items are to be produced extra for filler in Archipelago?

options.label: Intermediate amount
options.description: How many items do you want that aren't included in archipelago directly?

options.label: Compounds can be ingredients
options.description: Can Compounds (locations) be used as ingredients in recipes as well?

options.label: Required Levels
options.description:
How many levels must be completed to finish the game.
Levels are chosen randomly from the included collections.
If more levels are chosen that the maximumem available the levels get capped at the maximum available.
The required number of levels can be tracked on the level select screen. These are shown as hints on the bottom of the screen. 
Max: 55 (with all collections included)
Default: All levels in chosen collections.

options.label: Required S Ranks
options.description:
How many S Ranks must be achieved on any level to finish the game.
If more levels are chosen that the maximumem available the levels get capped at the maximum available.
The required number of S ranks can be tracked on the level select screen. These are shown as hints on the bottom of the screen. 
Max: 52 (with all collections included)
Default: 0

options.label: Required Bonus Objectives
options.description:
How many Bonus Objectives must be completed on any level to finish the game.
If more Bonus Objectives are chosen that the maximumem available the objectives get capped at the maximum available.
The required number of Bonus Objectives can be tracked on the level select screen. These are shown as hints on the bottom of the screen.
Max: 104 (with all collections included)
Default: 0

options.label: Include Story Levels
options.description:
Include all Story levels.
In total this adds 27 levels.
If no collections are chosen, Story levels are included by default.

options.label: Include Non-Gameplay Levels
options.description:
Include non-gameplay levels, such as the tutorial and Story levels that are mostly cutscenes.
Only applies if the Story collection is included.
In total this includes 3 levels: Story Level 1, 25 & 27.
These levels add one check and pose no challenge.

options.label: Include Horde Levels
options.description:
Remove all Horde Levels from the active level pool.
In total this includes 5 levels accros 3 collections: Story Level 8, 15 & 26, Challenge Level 8, Support Group Level 9.

options.label: Include Story S Rank Locations
options.description:
Include S Rank locations for Story levels.
Each Story level will have an additional check for achieving an S Rank.

options.label: Include Story Bonus Objectives
options.description:
Include two Bonus Objectives for Story levels. 
Adds 2 extra location for each level.

options.label: Include Challenge Levels
options.description:
Include all Challenge levels.
In total this adds 12 levels.
If no collections are chosen, Story levels are included by default.

options.label: Include Challenge S Rank Locations
options.description:
Include S Rank locations for Challenge levels.
Each Challenge level will have an additional check for achieving an S Rank.

options.label: Include Challenge Bonus Objectives
options.description:
Include two Bonus Objectives for Challenge levels. 
Adds 2 extra location for each level.

options.label: Include Support Levels
options.description:
Include all Support Group levels.
In total this adds 9 levels.
If no collections are chosen, Story levels are included by default.

options.label: Include Support Group S Rank Locations
options.description:
Include S Rank locations for Support Group levels.
Each Support Group level will have an additional check for achieving an S Rank.

options.label: Include Support Group Bonus Objectives
options.description:
Include two Bonus Objectives for Support Group levels. 
Adds 2 extra location for each level.

options.label: Include Cold Sweat Levels
options.description:
Include all Cold Sweat levels.
In total this adds 7 levels.
Cold Sweat is intended to be the most challenging collection in I Am Your Beast.
It is possible you will not be able to finish one or more levels.
If no collections are chosen, Story levels are included by default.
If Weapons unlocks are enabled, you are not able to choose ONLY Cold Sweat levels.

options.label: Include Cold Sweat S Rank Locations
options.description:
Include S Rank locations for Cold Sweat levels.
Each Cold Sweat level will have an additional check for achieving an S Rank.
Cold Sweat levels are already very challenging, so S Ranks may be extremely difficult.

options.label: Include Cold Sweat Bonus Objectives
options.description:
Include two Bonus Objectives for Cold Sweat levels. 
Adds 2 extra location for each level.

options.label: Include Snowmen
options.description:
Include Destroying the secret Snowman on each of the included levels as a location.
In total this can add 51 checks to the game.

options.label: Pickup Locations
options.description:
This option makes all heal and armor items location in each of the levels. The items still give their normal effects.
Yellow highlighted pickups have not yet been collected.
None - Option is turned off.
Individual - Every pickup is its own location. Each one sends a check on first use.
Grouped - Pickups are grouped by levels. A check is sent when you pick up all of them in a level. Has to be done in one try.

options.label: Minimap Type
options.description:
This option changes the minimap to also show armor type pickups on the minimal.
Default - Game default minimap, only shows health pickups.
Armor (No Color) - Armor pickups are shown on the minimap with the health pickup icon, but they are the same color.
Armor (Color) - Armor pickups are shown on the minimap with the health pickup icon, but they are green or blue.

options.label: Make Kick an Unlockable Item
options.description: Makes the Kick an unlockable item and shuffles it into the item pool.

options.label: Make Weapons and Equipment Unlockable Items
options.description: Makes weapons and equipment unlockable items and shuffles them into the item pool. You will only have the Tree Bark unlocked at the start of the game.

options.label: Minimal Conditions
options.description:
NOT YET AVAILABLE — this option is always disabled.
Only parts of it are done, will be added in a future update.

Hard mode option for the levels. Each levels S rank and on harder levels completion logic will assume you only need the minimal required weapons to complete the checks.
Standard logic is base game logic, meaning you need most of the weapons on a level to be able to achieve an S rank. Only matters if weapons are randomized.

options.label: Glitched Logic
options.description:
NOT YET AVAILABLE — this option is always disabled.
Only parts of it are done, will be added in a future update.

Includes out of bounds skips and item duplications in the logic. Only matters if weapons are randomized.

options.label: Include Traps
options.description:
Include trap items in the filler item pool.
Traps are negative effects sent to other players, such as bleeding, being disarmed, or being immobilized.

options.label: Death link
options.description: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

options.label: Deathlink Amnesty
options.description:
The number of deaths needed to send out a deathlink event
Deathlink can be disabled entirely.

options.label: Trap Chance
options.description:
The percentage chance that a filler item rolled for the item pool becomes a trap instead of a regular filler item.
Only applies if Include Traps is enabled.

options.label: Addition Randomization
options.description:
Controls how character Additions are unlocked.

Force up to two early-game progression items (Soil Sword, Watering Can,
Fertilizer) to be in sphere 1 locally.

options.label: Logic Level
options.description:
The overall difficulty of the logic, used to determine the requirements to access locations and regions.

Normal: Suitable for anyone who has beaten the game. Requires backflips and knowing where everything is.
Hard: Requires some easier movement tricks such as cling climbing and backwards ultras using solar wind,
      and more nuanced movement like turning during an air kick.
Expert: Requires more difficult movement tricks such as ultrahops and reverse wallkicks, and obscure knowledge.
Lunatic: Requires extremely difficult jumps and creative thinking. No holds barred. You have been warned.

options.label: Obscure Logic
options.description:
Enables logic for obscure knowledge and creative pathing that isn't difficult to execute
but may not be obvious or commonly known.
This option is forced on if logic level is set to Expert or Lunatic.

options.label: Ultra Cap
options.description:
Determines how the ultra height cap behaves. This only matters for Expert+ logic.

Vanilla: Ultras have the lower blue cap unless Solar Wind has been obtained and is active.
Full Gold: Ultras always have the higher gold cap.

options.label: Progressive Dream Breaker

options.label: Progressive Slide

options.label: Split Sun Greaves
options.description: Replaces Sun Greaves and Heliacal Power with four individual Air Kicks.

options.label: Split Cling Gem

options.label: Start With Breaker
options.description: Places Dream Breaker (or one Progressive Dream Breaker) in the starting inventory.

options.label: Start With Map

If turned off, the time trials will not have items and the outfits are placed in the starting inventory.

Adds goatlings as locations. Talk to the goatling to get the item.
