For each location added, an essentially useless filler item is also added to the item pool.

options.label: Randomize Chairs
options.description:
Adds places Sybil can sit as locations. Sit down to get the item.
This option adds 16 locations.
For each location added, an essentially useless filler item is also added to the item pool.

options.label: Randomize Books
options.description:
Adds books in the library as locations. Read the book to get the item.
This option adds 13 locations.
For each location added, an essentially useless filler item is also added to the item pool.

options.label: Randomize Notes

Adds notes as locations. Read the note to get the item.

options.label: Combat Difficulty

options.label: Include Unreasonable Advancements
options.description: Enables the extremely difficult advancements "How Did We Get Here?" and "Adventuring Time."

options.label: Include Postgame Advancements

options.label: Bee Trap Percentage
options.description:
Replaces a percentage of junk items with bee traps, which spawn multiple angered bees around every player when
received.

options.label: Send Defeated Mobs

options.label: Immediate Respawn
options.description: Choose whether to respawn immediately on death, or to be put into the game over screen.

options.label: Starting Items
options.description:
Start with these items. Each entry should be of this format: {item: "item_name", amount: #}
`item` can include components, and should be in an identical format to a `/give` command with
`"` escaped for json reasons.

`amount` is optional and will default to 1 if omitted.

example:
```
starting_items: [
    { "item": "minecraft:stick[minecraft:custom_name="{'text':'pointy stick'}"]" },
    { "item": "minecraft:arrow[minecraft:rarity=epic]", amount: 64 }
]
```

options.label: Goal
options.description:
What you need to do to finish. With several goals, all are required.
Once all goals are done, listen to K.K. Slider on Saturday night (8pm-12am) to finish.
- Statue: pay off every house loan so Tom Nook builds your statue.
- Museum: receive "Museum Goal Percent" of the museum donation items (needs Museumsanity).
- Froggy Chair: get the froggy chair into your catalog, any way you can (never a Catalogsanity item).
- Catalog: get "Catalog Goal Percent" of the Catalogsanity items into your catalog (needs Catalogsanity).
- Furniture Set: every piece of the Furniture Set placed somewhere in your house. 
  Each piece is an item mailed to you from AP and is unobtainable through normal means.
- Chess Set: a full chess board's pieces somewhere in your house.
  Per color: 8 pawns, 2 rooks, 2 knights, 2 bishops, 1 queen, 1 king.
  Only one item of each kind is sent through AP, after which you can order the rest
  from the catalog.
Chess and furniture goals need the basement built and an open shop time unlocked.

no store available, so this setting cannot be changed later in-game.

as the only way to get ants without spoiled turnips is candy, which
is sold in October. This setting can't be changed later in-game.

Villagers in this list will never move in, show up at the start, be a summer
camper, etc. "Personality: Cranky" (or Normal, Peppy, Lazy, Jock, Snooty)
blacklists all villagers with that personality. At least 6 villagers must stay allowed.

options.label: Starting Villagers
options.description:
Can force starting villagers. If more than 6, will be chosen randomly.
"Personality: Cranky" (or Normal, Peppy, Lazy, Jock, Snooty) adds
every villager with it. Blacklisted villagers are skipped.

options.label: Starting Loan
options.description: Loan amount for your starting house. Vanilla: 17,400.

options.label: Medium House Loan
options.description: Loan amount for the first house upgrade (bigger main floor). Vanilla: 148,000.

options.label: Basement Loan
options.description: Loan amount for the basement (second upgrade). Vanilla: 49,800.

options.label: Large House Loan
options.description:
Loan amount for the third house upgrade (biggest main floor). Vanilla: 398,000
.

options.label: Upper Floor Loan
options.description: Loan amount for the upper floor (the last upgrade). Vanilla: 798,000.

options.label: Loan Credit Percent
options.description:
The main filler in this game: credits applied to your house loan, or to your
savings if your loans are paid off. Setting is the percentage of your total
loan; setting to 100 means filler will be enough to completely pay your loan.
Bell credits reduce interruptions and menuing, and are the recommended filler.

options.label: Extra Bells (x10,000)
options.description:
Extra Bells in the pool, sent directly to you in the mail. Value is x10,000,
so 6 = 60,000. A mix of 10k and 30k bags. If there's not enough filler items,
you may not get the full amount or the exact amount. In the extreme case, can
completely remove the credit filler, but this is unusual.

options.label: Favorsanity
options.description:
Villager favors send checks. This is the "give me work!" dialog option when
talking to villagers. Favors are gated by pools to deepen progression/spheres.
First pool always open from start. ANY favor from any Villager counts.

options.label: Favor Pools
options.description:
With Favorsanity, the number of pools to gate favors. Each pool has "Favors Per Pool"
amount of favors in it. "Favor Pools" x "Favors per Pool" is at most 100.

options.label: Favors per Pool
options.description: Favor checks in each Favor Pool.

options.label: Shellsanity
options.description:
Archipelago items sometimes wash up on the beach in place of a shell.
Like shells, they stay forever until picked up. To get more shells to
spawn, pick up existing ones (including non-AP shells) and move to a new day.

options.label: Beach Checks per Month
options.description: With Shellsanity, the beach checks per month (3 makes 36).

options.label: Treesanity
options.description:
Fruit trees drop AP items, up to the given amount per fruit tree type.
Fruit is now progressive and in the pool, and is unobtainable through
normal means in-game. Note that once fruit is received, Tom Nook will
sell it in his store, should you lose it.

options.label: Tree Checks per Fruit
Loansanity
options.description:
Paying of loans sends a configurable amount of checks. Next loan gated by
Progressive House items in AP pool. Turning this off sets loan behavior
to vanilla, except for your configured loan amounts.
Required for "Statue" goal.

options.label: Fossil Loans
options.description:
All loans after the first have logic to require the shovel and one dinosaur
fossil set, IF those are set to be AP items. This ensures you have a consistent
way to make money if early game is stacked with Progressive Houses. Note that
this gives less varied seeds, as you'll almost always get early shovel.

options.label: Total Loan Checks
options.description:
Number of checks spread over the five loans in total, split by each loan's
share of the total debt. Each loan gets at LEAST one check. Paying a loan
releases ALL checks associated with that loan at once.

options.label: Timesanity
options.description:
The clock stops fully. Each month and each time slot (Morning 4-8, Day 9-15, Evening 16-20, Night 21-3)
is an item. You set the date and hour from the pause menu, to any month and slot you own.

options.label: Starting Month
options.description:
With timesanity, the month you start with. The game starts on the 1st of
the month.

options.label: Starting Time
options.description:
With timesanity, the time slot you start with. The game starts on the
first hour of the time slot.

options.label: Catalogsanity
options.description:
Reserve a section of the catalog for AP. Sections are gated by Progressive
Catalog Pool. Registering an item sends a check. Items in the Catalogsanity
pool only come from registered sources (see "Catalog Sources").
Must be on for the Catalog goal.

options.label: Catalog Pools
options.description:
Catalog is split into pools, each one requiring a Progressive Catalog Pool
unlock (none open at the start). Pools x Pool Size = total catalog checks,
at most 575 (furniture, clothes, carpets and wallpaper only)

options.label: Catalog Pool Size
options.description:
Catalog items unlocked per Progressive Catalog Pool. Items are picked at
random, with every pool getting a similar mix of furniture, clothes,
carpets and wallpaper.

options.label: Catalog Sources
options.description:
What can give you items from the reserved Catalogsanity catalog.
Nook's shop is always a source and will eventually sell everything, so this
never changes what is reachable, only how easy it is to get items outside Nook.
- Favors: villager favor rewards.
- Trades: villagers trading or selling in a chat.
- Lost and Found: the daily item.
- Dump: the daily items.
- Letters: villager reply presents and letter-quality rewards.
- Trees: furniture from shaking trees.
- Presents: from trees and balloons.
- Grab Bags: Nook's sale day bags.
- Wisp: his reward.

options.label: Museumsanity
options.description:
Catching, digging up or donating things sends checks (see the options below).
Required for the Museum Goal, which replaces museum donations with AP items.

options.label: Bug Checks
options.description:
With Museumsanity, what sends a check for each bug.
- Off: no bug checks or AP items
- Journal: catching it for the first time. With the Museum goal, Blathers never takes bugs.
- Museum: donating it. With the Museum goal, Blathers takes it while its check isn't sent.
- Both: catching and donating are separate checks. Doubles bug checks

options.label: Fish Checks
options.description:
With Museumsanity, what sends a check for each fish.
- Off: no fish checks.
- Journal: catching it for the first time. With the Museum goal, Blathers never takes fish.
- Museum: donating it. With the Museum goal, Blathers takes it while its check isn't sent.
- Both: catching and donating are separate checks. Doubles fish checks

options.label: Fossil Checks
options.description:
With Museumsanity, what sends a check for each fossil.
- Off: no fossil checks.
- Instant: fossils come out of the ground already appraised; digging one up sends its check.
- Vanilla: mail the fossil to the museum for appraisal, then donating it sends the check.
- Instant Donate: dig up as Instant, plus a second check for donating it. Doubles fossil checks

options.label: Painting Checks
options.description: With Museumsanity, what sends a check for each painting. Not available yet.

options.label: Bug Availability
options.description:
Which bugs can spawn.
- All: every bug.
- Progressive: a bug only spawns once you have its item:
  - "Tree Bugs" (cicadas, Bagworm, Spider, Purple Butterfly, Bee)
  - "Beetles"
  - "Flower Bugs" (butterflies, ladybugs, Mantis, Snail)
  - "Ground Bugs" (crickets, Grasshopper, locusts, Mole Cricket, Pill Bug, Ant, Cockroach)
  - "Flying Bugs" (dragonflies, Mosquito, Firefly, Pond Skater)
Needs Bug Checks (with Museumsanity); without them this is All.

options.label: Fish Availability
options.description:
Which fish can spawn.
- All: every fish.
- Progressive: a fish only spawns once you have one of its items:
  - "Small River Fish"
  - "Medium River Fish"
  - "Large River Fish"
  - "Pond Fish" (includes the lake)
  - "Sea Fish"
The fishing tourney needs the river items for the basses. Needs Fish Checks (with Museumsanity); without them this is All.

options.label: Fossil Availability
options.description:
Which fossils can come out of the ground. Works without Museumsanity too.
- All: every fossil.
- Season Locked: each fossil only comes out in one season:
  - Spring: March-May
  - Summer: June-August
  - Autumn: September-November
  - Winter: December-February
- Progressive: each dinosaur series requires an item before it spawns, adds 8 progressive items to pool.
No fossils are buried until you have one of these items. Needs Fossil Checks (with
Museumsanity); without them this is All.

options.label: Nook Store Upgrades
options.description:
How Tom Nook upgrades his store. Regardless of setting, Nookington's never
needs a visitor to upgrade, unlike vanilla.
- Progressive: three Progressive Nook Store items in the pool, one upgrade each.
- Sales: total Bells spent at the store reaches the Nook Store Sales amounts (Vanilla behavior).
- Catalog: the number of entries in your catalog reaches the Nook Store Catalog counts (any, not just Catalogsanity).

options.label: Nook 'n' Go Sales
options.description: Sales Upgrades only: total Bells spent for Nook 'n' Go. Vanilla: 25,000.

options.label: Nookway Sales
options.description: Sales Upgrades only: total Bells spent for Nookway. Vanilla: 90,000.

options.label: Nookington's Sales
options.description: Sales Upgrades only: total Bells spent for Nookington's. Vanilla: 240,000.

options.label: Nook 'n' Go Catalog
options.description: Catalog Upgrades only: catalog entries (of the current player) for Nook 'n' Go.

options.label: Nookway Catalog
options.description: Catalog Upgrades only: catalog entries (of the current player) for Nookway.

options.label: Nookington's Catalog
options.description: Catalog Upgrades only: catalog entries (of the current player) for Nookington's.

options.label: No Cockroaches
options.description:
Cockroaches never appear in your house, even if you're away for a while.
This can later be changed in-game under Settings > AP.

options.label: No Weeds
options.description:
Weeds never grow in your town.
This can later be changed in-game under Settings > AP.

options.label: More Favors
options.description:
Villagers will almost always give you a job when you talk to them.
This can later be changed in-game under Settings > AP.

options.label: Villagers Don't Leave
options.description:
Villagers never move out, and nobody talks about moving. Once your town has
15 villagers, nobody new moves in either.
This can later be changed in-game under Settings > AP.

options.label: Villagers Never Sleep
options.description:
Villagers never go to sleep: when they would, they stay awake at home,
so you can always visit them (handy for favors when you only have
early-morning or night hours).
This can later be changed in-game under Settings > AP.

options.label: No Falling Stalks
options.description:
The stalk market never rolls the falling pattern (prices only go down all week).
This can later be changed in-game under Settings > AP.

options.label: No Fishing Trash
options.description:
Fishing never hooks an empty can, boot or old tire.
This can later be changed in-game under Settings > AP.

options.label: Easier Critter Catch
options.description:
Fish can't get scared from running, and give you one whole additional second
when biting the bobber. Tools can still be used to manually scare fish. Sea
fish (attempt to) face the beach like in newer games. Bugs take longer to
flee with walking or running (but still can). Bees chase at half speed,
and Purple butterflies fly low to the ground.
This can later be changed in-game under Settings > AP.

options.label: Hidden Bug Hints
options.description:
Normally hidden bugs now show a visible sign for where they are.
Dirt pops up near rocks with pill bugs or mole crickets underground,
and trees with spiders or bagworms shake.
This can later be changed in-game under Settings > AP.

options.label: Hidden Item Hints
options.description:
Money rocks and trees with furniture, a present, or the golden shovel now sparkle.
With Catalogsanity, goods in Nook's shop that would send a catalog check sparkle too.
This can later be changed in-game under Settings > AP.

options.label: Skip HRA Talk
options.description:
Tom Nook never stops you in his shop to talk about the Happy Room Academy.
The Academy starts judging your house the day after you move in.
This can later be changed in-game under Settings > AP.

options.label: Short Shop Talk
options.description:
Tom Nook keeps it short when you buy something in his shop: just the item, the
price and "would you like it?". He still gives you raffle tickets, he just
doesn't talk about them. Catalog orders skip the small talk too.
This can later be changed in-game under Settings > AP.

options.label: Shop Never Sells Out
options.description:
Things you buy in Tom Nook's shop stay on the shelf, so you can buy them again.
Grab bags still sell out.
This can later be changed in-game under Settings > AP.

options.label: Coconuts Wash Up
options.description:
Coconuts sometimes wash up on the town beach in place of a shell.
This can later be changed in-game under Settings > AP.

options.label: Normalized Time Travel
options.description:
Time travel always counts as one day forward, no matter how far forward
or back you actually travel. Setting this to false uses vanilla logic:
backwards travel has penalties, and forward travel brings weeds and
villager move-outs, etc.
This can later be changed in-game under Settings > AP.

options.label: Critter Odds
options.description:
How likely each bug and fish is. Works without Museumsanity too.
- Vanilla: the game's odds.
- Normalized: every bug and fish spawn is equally likely.
- Dynamic: like Normalized, but bugs and fish whose check isn't sent yet (or have not been found)
  are 6 times as likely.
Normalized and Dynamic force unique region fish (waterfall, lake) to take up a greater
share of the fish in that region over river fish. Bugs also spawn more frequently in
acres, which helps with winter sparseness.
This can later be changed in-game under Settings > AP.

options.label: Fossil Odds
options.description:
How likely each available fossil is. Works without Museumsanity too.
- Vanilla: the game's original odds (not in your favor)
- Normalized: every available fossil equally likely.
- Dynamic: like Normalized, but fossils whose check isn't sent yet (or which have not been found) are 6 times as likely.
This can later be changed in-game under Settings > AP.

options.label: New Item Chance
options.description:
How often a random item you get from Catalogsanity sources is new
(Nook's shop, favors, balloon presents, ...)
This can later be changed in-game under Settings > AP.

options.label: Shellsanity Item Chance
options.description:
With Shellsanity, percent chance that a generated shell is an Archipelago item.
The beach can hold at most 20 of any shell, including AP items.
This can later be changed in-game under Settings > AP.

options.label: Specific Keys
options.description: Normal keys are specific to a dungeon. The key count for each dungeon may be found in extra pages in the pause menu. Turn off to make normal keys act like in vanilla. If off, you may need to buy keys from Zaegul.

options.label: Colors Required
options.description: Number of colors out of 5 needed to enter the Lighthouse.

options.label: Blessings Required
options.description: Number of blessings out of 5 needed to access Enlightenment or to get the Hero's Rest ending.

options.label: Crest Fragments Required
options.description: Number of crest fragments out of 5 needed to get past the door in Castle Vann.

options.label: Coins of Crowl Required
options.description: Number of Coins of Crowl out of 13 needed to get past the underwater door.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
The goal of the game.
var: Defeat Var.
rest: Revive Torran.
shadow: Defeat Shadow Oran.
torran: Defeat Torran.
any: Defeat any of the three.

options.label: Color Locations
options.description:
Choose where your colors can be found.
dungeon_prizes: Colors can be found on dungeon prizes (Vulture, Tidal Frog, Water Blessing, Rat Potion, Wren, Yhote, Spirit of Vann, Ram Wraith, Loomagnos, Earth Blessing, Color Correction, Light Spirit, Stindle, Frozen Heart, Killer, Siska, Mechanized Slot Machine, Inkwell).
local: Colors can be found anywhere in your own world.
any: Colors can be found in any world.

options.label: Blessing Locations
options.description:
Choose where your blessings can be found.
dungeon_prizes: Blessings can be found on dungeon prizes (Vulture, Tidal Frog, Water Blessing, Rat Potion, Wren, Yhote, Spirit of Vann, Ram Wraith, Loomagnos, Earth Blessing, Color Correction, Light Spirit, Stindle, Frozen Heart, Killer, Siska, Mechanized Slot Machine, Inkwell).
local: Blessings can be found anywhere in your own world.
any: Blessings can be found in any world.

options.label: Lighthouse Key
options.description:
Choose where your lighthouse key can be found. (Only applies if Specific Keys is on)
blessings: The lighthouse key is obtained when you return the blessings and get the Hero's Soul.
coins: The lighthouse key is found underwater behind the door requiring coins of Crowl.
materials: The lighthouse key is given to you by Bolivar when you give him the four materials.
local: The lighthouse key may be found anywhere in your own world.
any: The lighthouse key may be found in any world.

options.label: Trading Quest
options.description:
How to handle the trading quest.
vanilla: The Lost Shipment and Ulni checks are randomized. The entire trading quest must be completed as in vanilla to get Ulni's check.
skip: The Lost Shipment location and Anchor Greaves are randomized. The Lost Shipment itself is not randomized, and Ulni is not a check.
shuffle: All items in the trading quest are randomized, and each of the corresponding NPCs is a check.

options.label: Shuffle Grelin Drops
options.description: Grelin randomly drop four Archipelago items, and the Holy Relic, Wedding Ring, Silver Mirror, and Painting are added to the pool.

options.label: Shuffle Hidden Items
options.description: Include hidden overworld items in the pool.

options.label: Shuffle Bjerg Castle
options.description: Include Bjerg Castle (Mariana's marriage dungeon) in the pool. A sailor near the arena will take you there.

options.label: Shuffle Daemon's Dive
options.description: Include Daemon's Dive in the pool.

options.label: Shuffle Enlightenment
options.description: Include Enlightenment in the pool.

options.label: Shuffle Secret Shop
options.description: Include Zaegul's Secret Shop in the pool.

options.label: Skips In Logic
options.description: The seed may require skips such as side hits, two-tile flare jumps outside of Enlightenment, deleting objects with the Empowered Hand, and interacting with objects from a tile away.

options.label: Start With Spiced Ham
options.description: Start with a buff that lets you run.

options.label: Start With Winged Boots
options.description: Start with Winged Boots.

options.label: Skip One Small Favor
options.description: Tara gives you an item directly instead of requiring you to go on a fetch quest.

options.label: Fake Dread Hand
options.description: Allow using teleport statues without having the dread hand.

options.label: Fast Fishing
options.description: Only 100 points are required in the fishing minigame to get the item from Keaton and to get free fish.

options.label: Altar to Var
options.description: Defile the altar to Var. Receive double damage.

options.label: Altar to Zolei
options.description: Defile the altar to Zolei. Item drops are reduced in frequency, and you must fight Zolei alongside Var.

options.label: Altar to Raem
options.description: Defile the altar to Raem. Raem will attack you with beams of light, and you cannot gain extra HP through prayer.

options.label: Altar to Hate
options.description: Defile the altar to Hate. Heart ores do not increase your maximum HP.

options.label: Curse of Frailty
options.description: Accept the curse of frailty. You die in one hit.

options.label: Curse of Famine
options.description: Accept the curse of famine. You cannot buy buffs.

options.label: Curse of Rust
options.description: Accept the curse of rust. The pick cannot be upgraded, and boots and rings do not work, except for the Winged Boots and Wedding Rings.

options.label: Curse of Wind
options.description: Accept the curse of wind. Doubles the speed of projectiles.

options.label: Curse of Blooms
options.description: Accept the curse of blooms. Enemies drop bombs when they die.

options.label: Curse of Crowns
options.description: Accept the curse of crowns. You cannot marry anyone.

options.label: Curse of Horns
options.description: Accept the curse of horns. All junk items, such as gold, are replaced by traps. Note that if no trap options are selected then all traps will be enabled.

options.label: Curse of Flames
options.description: Accept the curse of flames. Flames appear behind you as you move through dungeons.

options.label: Trap Chance
options.description: Percentage chance of an added filler item being a trap. Items in the base pool are not affected. Has no effect if Curse of Horns is active.

options.label: Enable All Traps
options.description: Enabling this overrides the individual trap settings and enables all types of traps.

options.label: Slowness Traps
options.description: Enable slowness traps, which prevent you from running for 20 seconds.

options.label: Rust Traps
options.description: Enable rust traps, which disable boots and rings for 20 seconds.

options.label: Confusion Traps
options.description: Enable confusion traps, which reverse your movement for 20 seconds.

options.label: Disarming Traps
options.description: Enable disarming traps, which prevent use of the pick for 20 seconds.

options.label: Light Traps
options.description: Enable light traps, which attack you with beams of light for 20 seconds.

options.label: Glitch Traps
options.description: Enable glitch traps, which cause graphical glitches for 20 seconds.

options.label: Zombie Traps
options.description: Enable zombie traps, which spawn zombies around you.

options.label: Shadow Traps
options.description: Enable shadow traps, which warp you as though you used the Dread Hand.

options.label: Logic Mode
options.description:
Logic to use for item placement.
normal: Standard gameplay, no tricky item use or glitches. If unsure, choose this.
hard: Adds tricks that aren't technically glitches. Lamp + Net considered as weapons. No glitches.
glitched: Includes the above plus a selection of easy-to-learn glitches.
adv_glitched: Includes the above plus "advanced" glitches that may be a challenge to master.
hell: Includes every known RTA-viable glitch. Don't choose this.

options.label: Randomize Dungeon Prizes
options.description: This shuffles all Sage Portraits and Pendants among themselves.

options.label: Progression Bosses
options.description: Place progression items on all dungeon bosses.

options.label: Lorule Castle Requirement
options.description: Choose how many Portraits are needed to enter Lorule Castle and fight Yuganon.

options.label: Pedestal Requirement
options.description:
Choose which Pendants are required to reach the Master Sword Pedestal.
vanilla: Only the Pendants of Power and Wisdom are required.
standard: All Pendants are required.

options.label: Nice Items
options.description:
Choose how to handle Nice Items.
vanilla: Nice Items are obtained as upgrades from Mother Maiamai.
shuffled: Freely shuffles two progressive copies of each Ravio Item.
off: Removes Nice Items from the game.
upgrades: Shuffles upgrades for each Ravio item, which upgrade your item once you get it.

options.label: Super Items
options.description:
Choose how to handle Super Items.
shuffled: Shuffles a second progressive copy of the Lamp and Net into the general item pool.
off: Removes Super Items from the game.
upgrades: Shuffles upgrades for the Lamp and Net, which upgrade your item once you get it.

options.label: Shuffle Maiamai Rewards
options.description:
Choose whether to put items on Mother Maiamai. Has no effect if `nice_items` is set to vanilla.
Instead of trading Maiamai for items, Mother Maiamai gives you an item once you have the
required Ravio item and a certain number of Maiamai, controlled by `maiamai_limit`.

options.label: Maiamai Limit
options.description:
When Mother Maiamai rewards are shuffled, this controls the maximum number of Maiamai
that can be required to get items from Mother Maiamai.

options.label: Small Keys
options.description:
Choose how to randomize small keys.
own_dungeons: Small keys are found in their own dungeons.
anywhere: (Keyos) Small keys can be found in any world.
remove: (Keysy) Small keys and the doors they lock are removed from the game.

options.label: Big Keys
options.description:
Choose how to randomize big keys.
own_dungeons: Big keys are found in their own dungeons.
anywhere: (Keyos) Big keys can be found in any world.
remove: (Keysy) Big keys and the doors they lock are removed from the game.

options.label: Compasses
options.description:
Choose how to randomize compasses.
own_dungeons: Compasses are found in their own dungeons.
anywhere: Compasses can be found in any world.
startwith: Start with the compass to every dungeon.

options.label: Key Rings
options.description: Replace all the small keys for a dungeon with a single Key Ring for that dungeon that opens all the locked doors.

options.label: Lamp and Net as Weapons
options.description:
Treat the base Lamp and Net as damage-dealing weapons?
- The red base Lamp and Net each deal 1/2 the damage of the Forgotten Sword (i.e. they're VERY BAD weapons).
- The blue Super Lamp and Super Net each deal 4 damage (same as MS Lv3) and are always considered weapons, regardless of this setting.

options.label: No Progression Enemies
options.description:
Removes Enemies from dungeons that are themselves Progression (e.g.: Bawbs, the bomb enemy).
Logic will be adjusted to require the player's items instead.

options.label: Assured Weapon
options.description: If enabled at least one weapon is guaranteed to be placed in Ravio's Shop.

options.label: Maiamai Mayhem
options.description: This shuffles Maiamai into the pool, adding 100 more locations.

options.label: Initial Crack State
options.description:
Choose the initial Crack state:
closed: All Cracks except the Hyrule Castle Crack (and its pair) remain closed until the Quake Item is found.
open: All Cracks are open from the start of the game, and the Quake Item is not in the item pool.
progressive: All Cracks except the Hyrule Castle Crack are closed, but the Quake Item and the Bracelets are not in the item pool.
  Instead, there are two Progressive Merge items. The first one you get allows you to merge, while the second one opens the cracks.

options.label: Crack Shuffle
options.description:
Choose how to shuffle Cracks:
off: Cracks are not shuffled.
cross_world_pairs: Cracks are shuffled, but remain in Hyrule/Lorule pairs.
any_world_pairs: Cracks are shuffled freely, and can lead to the same or opposite world.
mirrored_cross_world_pairs: Same as Cross World Pairs, but each pair's vanilla counterparts will be in a matching pair.
mirrored_any_world_pairs: Same as Any World Pairs, but each pair's vanilla counterparts will be in a matching pair.

options.label: Minigames Excluded
options.description: Excludes the following: Octoball Derby, Dodge the Cuccos, Hyrule Hotfoot, Treacherous Tower, and both Rupee Rushes.

options.label: Skip Big Bomb Flower
options.description:
Skips the Big Bomb Flower by removing the 5 Big Rocks in Lorule Field.
(Does not affect Lorule Castle Bomb Trial)

options.label: Trials Required
options.description: Choose the number of (randomly selected) trials required to open the Lorule Castle Trials Door.

options.label: Open Trials Door
options.description:
Makes the Lorule Castle Trials Door automatically open from both sides.
This may require entering Lorule Castle early via the crack.
If turned on, this overrides the Trials Required setting.

options.label: Bow of Light in Castle
options.description: Limits the Bow of Light's placement to somewhere in Lorule Castle (including possibly Zelda).

options.label: Weather Vanes
options.description:
Choose Weather Vanes behavior. Logic may require using them to progress.
standard: Start with only the standard complimentary Weather Vanes (Link's House & Vacant House)
shuffled: Weather Vane destinations are shuffled into random pairs
convenient: Start with convenient Weather Vanes that don't affect logic
hyrule: Start with the 9 Hyrule Weather Vanes (and Vacant House)
lorule: Start with the 13 Lorule Weather Vanes (and Link's House)
all: Start with all 22 Weather Vanes

options.label: Dark Rooms Lampless
options.description:
If enabled the logic may expect players to cross Dark Rooms without the Lamp.
Not for beginners and those who like being able to see things.

options.label: Swordless Mode
options.description:
Removes *ALL* Swords from the game.
The Bug Net becomes a required item to play Dead Man's Volley against Yuga Ganon.

options.label: Hint Ghosts
options.description:
Choose the behavior of the Hint Ghosts. (Hint Ghosts in dungeons never appear.)
off: Hint Ghosts do not appear.
always: Hint Ghosts always appear.

options.label: Skill Shuffler
options.description:
Randomize player class's skills. Player class skills are divided into groups and the skill groups are shuffled among themselves.
Therefore active skills are shuffled amoung themselves, passive skills which reserve mana are shuffled among themselves, etc.
There is no guaranteed usability between skills and modifiers shuffled this way, for example a modifier which increases projectile
damage will likely have no effect on Horn of Gandarr.

options.label: Skill Balance Randomizer
options.description:
Randomize all numerical values in player class skills and passives, including but not limited to
damage values, action speeds, mana costs, cooldown times, projectile count, and pet summons.

options.label: Devotion Balance Randomizer
options.description:
Randomize all numerical values in player devotion skills in the constellation tree, including but not limited to
damage values, action speeds, mana costs, cooldown times, projectile count, and pet summons.
Only the skills are randomized, not the passive nodes leading up to them.

options.label: Skill Balance Range
options.description:
The range which skill balance randomizer can affect skill values. Has no effect if Skill/Devotion Balance Randomizer is disabled.
micro - Random range between 0.9x and 1.1x
small - Random range between 0.75x and 1.25x
medium - Random range between 0.66x and 1.5x
large - Random range between 0.5x and 2x
extreme - Random range between 0.2x and 3x
mayhem - Random range between 0.1x and 10x. This is just for fun as this setting completely breaks game balance.

options.label: Skill Balance Weight
options.description:
The weight that affects a skill's randomized value to be buffed or nerfed. Has no effect if Skill/Devotion Balance Randomizer is disabled.
only_nerfs - 100% chance for values to roll a nerf
mostly_nerfs - 75% chance for values to roll a nerf
balanced - 50/50 chance for values to roll a buff or nerf
mostly_buffs - 75% chance for values to roll a buff
only_buffs - 100% chance for values to roll a buff

options.label: Skill Balance Preserve Damage
options.description:
If enabled, prevents base damage and damage multiplier values from being randomized.
Has no effect if Skill/Devotion Balance Randomizer is disabled.

options.label: Skill Balance Preserve Area
options.description:
If enabled, prevents area, distance, and target values from being randomized.
Has no effect if Skill/Devotion Balance Randomizer is disabled.

options.label: Skill Balance Preserve Duration
options.description:
If enabled, prevents effect duration and summon lifetime values from being randomized.
Has no effect if Skill/Devotion Balance Randomizer is disabled.

options.label: Skill Balance Preserve Mana
options.description:
If enabled, prevents mana cost and mana reservation values from being randomized.
Has no effect if Skill/Devotion Balance Randomizer is disabled.

options.label: Skill Balance Preserve Projectiles
options.description:

Has no effect if Skill/Devotion Balance Randomizer is disabled.

options.label: Skill Balance Preserve Cooldown

Has no effect if Skill/Devotion Balance Randomizer is disabled.

options.label: Skill Balance Preserve Chance

options.label: Skill Balance Preserve Defense

options.label: Skill Balance Preserve Summon

options.label: Skill Balance Preserve Speed

options.label: Duelist Progression
options.description:
Whenever you receive a "Progressive Duelist" item, the next duelist or group of duelists will be unlocked. This
setting controls what those duelist groups are.

"Thematic" places duelists in large groups based on theme. You will start with all of Egypt 1 unlocked, then unlock
all of World Tournament, then all of Egypt 2, then Final 6 one at a time.

"Campaign" unlocks duelists roughly the same way as in Campaign mode: you will start with all of Egypt 1 unlocked
except Seto 1, then unlock Seto 1, then each of the World Tournament duelists one at a time, then Mage Soldier and
the Jono and Teana refights all together, then 2 random low mage and high mage pairs at the same time, then
Labryinth Mage, then Seto 2, then the rest of Egypt 2 all at once, then Final 6.

"Singular" unlocks every duelist one at a time in the same order they're encountered in the campaign up until the
mages, then unlocks mages one at a time at random without respecting low and high mage pairs.

Regardless of your choice, you will always have Simon Muran and Duel Master K unlocked, and Heishin 1 is always
excluded until Heishin 2 is unlocked.

options.label: Randomize Duelist Unlock Order
options.description:
If enabled, the order of the groups of duelists you unlock up until Final 6 will be randomized. Your starting
group of duelists remains unchanged.

For "Campaign" and "Singular" progression choices, you are guaranteed to unlock all of the Egypt 1 and
World Tournament duelists before unlocking any Egypt 2 duelists.

options.label: Item Mode
options.description:
Selects what type of items to place at checks in addition to the required Progressive Duelist items.

"Starchips" places a value of starchips behind checks.

"Cards" splits the pool of accessible checks in half, reserving one half as reward items, and the other half as
check locations. The reward cards are used to fill the check locations instead of starchips. Using a tracker is
highly recommended for this setting since there's no other way to determine which cards are randomly selected to be
the check locations.

options.label: Local Starchip Bias
options.description:
If enabled, 75% of your starchip items will be local to your world.

Has no effect unless "Starchips" is selected for Item Mode.

options.label: Unobtainable Cards As Items
options.description:
When using the "Cards" Item Mode, normally only cards that would be eligible as checks under your settings can be
selected as reward items. If this setting is enabled, any card can be selected as a reward, including cards that
cannot be otherwise obtained by the player like Black Luster Soldier.

Note that enabling this setting may trivialize the game if cards such as Blue-Eyes Ultimate Dragon or Gate Guardian
are rolled as item rewards.

Has no effect unless "Cards" is selected for Item Mode.

options.label: Final 6 Progression
options.description:
"Fixed": The check you receive for defeating a member of Final 6 is guaranteed to unlock the next Final 6 duelist.
This means you will have Go Mode as soon as the first Final 6 duelist is unlocked.

"Shuffled": The Progressive Duelist items to unlock each Final 6 duelist are shuffled into the item pool.

options.label: Final 6 Sequence
options.description:
"Vanilla": You will always unlock the Final 6 duelists in this order: Guardian Sebek, Guardian Neku, Heishin 2, Seto
3, DarkNite, Nitemare.

"First 5 Shuffled": The order you unlock the Final 6 duelists is randomized, except Nitemare will always be last.

"All 6 Shuffled": The order you unlock the Final 6 duelists is completely randomized, and you'll reach your goal
when you defeat the last one. Depending on your other settings, "All 6 Shuffled" could put Nitemare ATecs into logic
in the lategame.

options.label: Extra Progressive Duelist Items
options.description:
Adds extra Progressive Duelist items into the item pool. Note that this setting can allow all but the final Final 6
member to be skipped.

options.label: Weakest Trap for ATecs
options.description:
The weakest (i.e. lowest mox Attack Point activation) trap card with which you can be expected to ATec a duelist.
ATecs will be in logic as soon as you have access to a duelist who drops this card or a stronger trap card,
excluding their SATec drop pool. Your other ATec settings are still respected.

Note that Fake Trap puts ATecs in logic right from the start since it drops off of Simon Muran and Simon Muran is
always unlocked.

options.label: Exclusion Drop Rate
options.description:
Prohibits progression items from being placed behind cards with a drop rate at or below the specified value (out of
2048). This logic takes your duelist progression into account, such that if the duelists you logically have access
to drop at or below this rate, the card will be excluded until you have access to a duelist with a higher rate if
one exists, or forever excluded otherwise.

Single: No dependencies
Diamonds: Several grid graphs (4/9/16 nodes each)
Pyramids: Several top halves of diamonds (6/10/15 nodes each)
Funnels: Several bottom halves of diamonds (6/10/15 nodes each)
Trees: Several trees
Choices: A single balanced binary tree

options.label: Minimum Science Pack Cost
options.description: The cheapest a Technology can be in Science Packs.

options.label: Maximum Science Pack Cost
options.description: The most expensive a Technology can be in Science Packs.

options.label: Tech Cost Distribution
options.description:
Random distribution of costs of the Science Packs.
Even: any number between min and max is equally likely.
Low: low costs, near the minimum, are more likely.
Middle: medium costs, near the average, are more likely.
High: high costs, near the maximum, are more likely.

options.label: Science Pack Cost Mix
options.description:
Percent chance that a preceding Science Pack is also required.
Chance is rolled per preceding pack.

options.label: Ramping Tech Costs
options.description:
Forces the amount of Science Packs required to ramp up with the highest involved Pack. Average is preserved.
For example:
off: Automation (red)/Logistics (green) sciences can range from 1 to 1000 Science Packs,
on: Automation (red) ranges to ~500 packs and Logistics (green) from ~500 to 1000 Science Packs

options.description: When randomizing ingredients, increase the estimated difficulty of each successive science pack ingredient pool by this percentage.

options.description:
World Generation settings. Overview of options at https://wiki.factorio.com/Map_generator,
with in-depth documentation at https://lua-api.factorio.com/latest/Concepts.html#MapGenSettings

options.label: Free Power
options.description: Harness the power of free, high-voltage atmospheric electricity.  Warning: Electricity will be provided whether you want it or not.

options.label: Progressive Technologies
options.description:
Merges together Technologies like "automation-1" to "automation-3" into 3 copies of "Progressive Automation",
which awards them in order.

options.label: Teleport Traps
options.description: Trap items that when received trigger a random teleport.

options.label: Grenade Traps
options.description: Trap items that when received trigger a grenade explosion on each player.

options.label: Cluster Grenade Traps
options.description: Trap items that when received trigger a cluster grenade explosion on each player.

options.label: Artillery Traps
options.description: Trap items that when received trigger an artillery shell on each player.

options.label: Atomic Rocket Traps
options.description:
Trap items that when received trigger an atomic rocket explosion on each player.
Warning: there is no warning. The launch is instantaneous.

options.label: Atomic Cliff Remover Traps
options.description:
Trap items that when received trigger an atomic rocket explosion on a random cliff.
Warning: there is no warning. The launch is instantaneous.

options.label: Inventory Spill Traps
options.description: Trap items that when received trigger dropping your main inventory and trash inventory onto the ground.

options.label: Quality Traps
options.description: Trap items that when received hide a Quality Module in one of your machines.

options.label: Attack Traps
options.description: Trap items that when received trigger an attack on your base.

options.label: Evolution Traps
options.description: Trap items that when received increase the enemy evolution.

options.label: Evolution Trap % Effect
options.description:
How much an Evolution Trap increases the enemy evolution.
Increases scale down proportionally to the session's current evolution factor
(40 increase at 0.50 will add 0.20... 40 increase at 0.75 will add 0.10...)

options.label: EnergyLink
options.description: Allow sending energy to other worlds. 25% of the energy is lost in the transfer.

options.label: Sword Progression
options.description: Adds four sword upgrades to the item pool that will progressively grant stronger melee weapons, including two new swords with increased range and attack power.

options.label: Start With Sword
options.description: Start with a sword in the player's inventory. Does not count towards Sword Progression.

options.label: Keys Behind Bosses
options.description:
Places the three hexagon keys behind their respective boss fight in your world.
If playing Hexagon Quest, it will place three gold hexagons at the boss locations.

options.label: Shuffle Abilities
options.description:
Locks the usage of Prayer, Holy Cross*, and the Icebolt combo until the relevant pages of the manual have been found.
If playing Hexagon Quest, abilities are instead randomly unlocked after obtaining 25%, 50%, and 75% of the required
Hexagon goal amount, unless the option is set to have them unlock via pages instead.
* Certain Holy Cross usages are still allowed, such as the free bomb codes, the seeking spell, and other player-facing codes.

options.label: Fool Traps
options.description: Replaces low-to-medium value money rewards in the item pool with fool traps, which cause random negative effects to the player.

options.label: Laurels Location
options.description:
Force the Hero's Laurels to be placed at a location in your world.
For if you want to avoid or specify early or late Laurels.

options.label: Hexagon Quest
options.description: An alternate goal that shuffles Gold "Questagon" items into the item pool and allows the game to be completed after collecting the required number of them.

options.label: Gold Hexagons Required
options.description: How many Gold Questagons are required to complete the game on Hexagon Quest.

options.label: Percentage of Extra Gold Hexagons
options.description:
How many extra Gold Questagons are shuffled into the item pool, taken as a percentage of the goal amount.
The max number of Gold Questagons that can be in the item pool is 100, so this option may be overridden and/or
reduced if the Hexagon Goal amount is greater than 50.

options.label: Hexagon Quest Ability Unlocks
options.description:
Determines how abilities are unlocked when playing Hexagon Quest with Shuffled Abilities enabled.

Hexagons: A new ability is randomly unlocked after obtaining 25%, 50%, and 75% of the required Hexagon goal amount. Requires at least 3 Gold Hexagons in the item pool, or 15 if Keys Behind Bosses is enabled.
Pages: Abilities are unlocked by finding specific pages in the manual.

This option does nothing if Shuffled Abilities is not enabled.

options.label: Shuffle Ladders
options.description:
Turns several ladders in the game into items that must be found before they can be climbed on.
Adds more layers of progression to the game by blocking access to many areas early on.
"Ladders were a mistake."
—Andrew Shouldice

options.label: Shuffle Fuses
options.description:
Praying at a fuse will reward a check instead of turning on the power.
The power from each fuse gets turned into an item that must be found in order to restore power for that part of the path.

options.label: Shuffle Bells
options.description:
The East and West bells are shuffled into the item pool and must be found in order to unlock the Sealed Temple.
Ringing the bells will instead now reward a check.

options.label: Breakable Shuffle
options.description: Turns approximately 250 breakable objects in the game into checks.

options.label: Shuffle Enemy Drops
options.description:
Every individual enemy and boss drops a check when defeated (excluding The Heir).
On: Adds about ~600 locations.
Extra: Includes nighttime and New Game+ enemy spawns for an additional ~90 checks. (Note: These enemies will appear alongside the normal enemy pool, since nighttime is not in the randomizer.)

options.label: Shuffle Enemy Souls
options.description:
Enemies do not appear until their corresponding "Soul" item is found. There are about 30 Enemy Soul items in total, including one for The Heir that is required to beat the game.
This option has no effect if you do not have Shuffle Enemy Drops enabled.

options.label: Grass Randomizer
options.description: Turns over 6,000 blades of grass and bushes in the game into checks.

options.label: Local Fill Percent
options.description:
Choose the percentage of your filler/trap items that will be kept local or distributed to other TUNIC players with this option enabled.
The default value for this option will be higher or lower depending on what combination of options you have enabled:
- Grass Randomizer + Breakable Shuffle or Shuffled Enemy Drops = 96%
- Grass Randomizer = 95%
- Shuffled Enemy Drops + Breakable Shuffle = 73%
- Shuffled Enemy Drops = 65%
- Breakable Shuffle = 40%
If you have any of the following options enabled, this option must be set greater than or equal to the corresponding value to avoid flooding the item pool:
- Grass Randomizer: >= 95%
- Shuffled Enemy Drops + Breakable Shuffle: >= 40%
- Shuffled Enemy Drops: >= 30%
The host can remove the above restriction by turning off the limit_local_fill setting in host.yaml.
This option ignores items placed in your local_items or non_local_items.
This option does nothing in single player games.

options.label: Entrance Rando
options.description:
Randomize the connections between scenes.
A small, very lost fox on a big adventure.

If you set this option's value to a string, it will be used as a custom seed.
Every player who uses the same custom seed will have the same entrances, choosing the most restrictive settings among these players for the purpose of pairing entrances.

options.label: Entrance Layout
options.description:
Decide how the Entrance Randomizer chooses how to pair the entrances.
Standard: Entrances are randomly connected. There are 6 shops in the pool with this option.
Fixed Shop: Forces the Windmill entrance to lead to a shop, and removes the other shops from the pool.
Adds another entrance in Rooted Ziggurat Lower to keep an even number of entrances.
Direction Pairs: Entrances facing opposite directions are paired together. There are 8 shops in the pool with this option.
Note: For seed groups, if one player in a group chooses Fixed Shop and another chooses Direction Pairs, it will error out.
Either of these options will override Standard within a seed group.

options.label: Decoupled Entrances
options.description:
Decouple the entrances, so that when you go from one entrance to another, the return trip won't necessarily bring you back to the same place.
Note: For seed groups, all players in the group must have this option enabled or disabled.

options.label: More Combat Logic
options.description:
If enabled, the player will logically require a combination of stat upgrade items and equipment to get some checks or navigate to some areas, with a goal of matching the vanilla combat difficulty.
The player may still be expected to run past enemies, reset aggro (by using a checkpoint or doing a scene transition), or find sneaky paths to checks.
This option marks many more items as progression and may force weapons much earlier than normal.
Bosses Only makes it so that additional combat logic is only added to the boss fights and the Gauntlet.
If disabled, the standard, looser logic is used. The standard logic does not include stat upgrades, just minimal weapon requirements, such as requiring a Sword or Magic Wand for Quarry, or not requiring a weapon for Swamp.

options.label: Lanternless
options.description:
When enabled, you may be required to navigate dark areas without the Lantern.
The Lantern is marked as Useful instead of Progression.

options.label: Maskless
options.description:
When enabled, you may be required to traverse Lower Quarry without the Scavenger's Mask.
The Scavenger's Mask is marked as Useful instead of Progression.

options.label: Laurels Zips Logic
options.description:
Choose whether to include using the Hero's Laurels to zip through gates, doors, and tricky spots.
Notable inclusions are the Monastery gate, Ruined Passage door, Old House gate, Forest Grave Path gate, and getting from the Back of Swamp to the Middle of Swamp.

options.label: Ice Grapple Logic
options.description:
Choose whether grappling frozen enemies is in logic.
Easy includes ice grappling enemies that are in range without luring them. May include clips through terrain.
Medium includes using ice grapples to push enemies through doors or off ledges without luring them. Also includes bringing an enemy over to the Temple Door to grapple through it.
Hard includes luring or grappling enemies to get to where you want to go.
Enabling any of these difficulty options will give the player the Torch to return to the Overworld checkpoint to avoid softlocks. Using the Torch is considered in logic.
Note: You will still be expected to ice grapple to the slime in East Forest from below with this option off.

options.label: Ladder Storage Logic
options.description:
Choose whether Ladder Storage is in logic.
Easy includes uses of Ladder Storage to get to open doors over a long distance without too much difficulty. May include convenient elevation changes (going up Mountain stairs, stairs in front of Special Shop, etc.).
Medium includes the above as well as changing your elevation using the environment and getting knocked down by melee enemies mid-LS.
Hard includes the above as well as going behind the map to enter closed doors from behind, shooting a fuse with the magic wand to knock yourself down at close range, and getting into the Cathedral Secret Legend room mid-LS.
Enabling any of these difficulty options will give the player the Torch to return to the Overworld checkpoint to avoid softlocks. Using the Torch is considered in logic.
Opening individual chests while doing ladder storage is excluded due to tedium.
Knocking yourself out of LS with a bomb is excluded due to the problematic nature of consumables in logic.

options.label: Ladder Storage without Items
options.description:
If disabled, you logically require Stick, Sword, Magic Orb, or Shield to perform Ladder Storage.
If enabled, you will be expected to perform Ladder Storage without progression items.
This can be done with the plushie code, a Golden Coin, Prayer, and many other options.

This option has no effect if you do not have Ladder Storage Logic enabled.

options.label: All Random Debug
options.description:
Sets all options that can be random to random.
For test gens.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Determines what your goal(s) are required to beat the game.
If none are selected, the goal becomes Escape.

Escape - Complete Land of Confusion

Captain - Beat Ianthe and become a ranger captain

options.label: Song Part Count
options.description:
How many Song Parts are in the item pool.
Game normally has 9, requires 4, and expects 8
Extra Song Parts do nothing.

options.label: Final Battle Friend Count
options.description:
How many companions the game expects you to have
  unlock and reached friendship level 1 with in
  order to fight the final battle
You will be able to fight the battle with fewer
  companions, but it will be outside of logic

options.label: Archangel Hunt Count
options.description:
How many Archangels must be defeated to achieve the
  Archangel Hunt goal
Without the Pier of the Unknown DLC, the max number
  is 13

options.label: Exclude Postgame
options.description: Force postgame locations to be filler

options.label: Experience Multiplier
options.description:
Multiplies the amount of experience gain by a percentage
100 = default
50  = half
200 = double
etc.

options.label: Friendship Multiplier
options.description:
Multiplies the amount of friendship gain by a percentage
100 = default
50  = half
200 = double
etc.

options.label: Battle Loot Multiplier
options.description:
Multiplies the amount of battle loot gain by a percentage
100 = default
50  = half
200 = double
etc.

options.label: Bootleg Multiplier
options.description:
Multiplies the odds that an overworld monster will be a bootleg.
1000 = 100% Bootleg chance
10   = 1%

options.label: Use Pier of the Unknown
options.description: Adds the Pier of the Unknown locations and items

options.label: Shuffle Chest Loot Tables
options.description:
Shuffles the randomized loot table pulls that chests
  give into the item pool

Most chests will gain a second location, replacing
  their randomized loot

options.label: Traps
options.description:
Adds trap items to the item pool before filler items

None - No traps

Few - About 5% of unfilled items become traps

Some - About 20% of unfilled items become traps

Many - About half of unfilled items become with traps

options.label: Shopsanity
options.description:
Put Archipelago items in the Town Hall shop
  and Fused Shards in the item pool

options.label: Trainersanity
options.description:
Make defeating optional trainers into locations
  and put their loot into the item pool

options.label: Tapesanity
options.description:
Adds recording tapes as locations
  and blank tapes to the item pool

None - No tapes are locations

Specific - Each tape has its own location

Percentage - Getting a total number of unique tapes up
  to a certain percentage are locations

options.label: Tapesanity Percentage
options.description:
The percentage of tapes that must be recorded to
  obtain all items

options.label: Tapesanity Percentage Item Count
options.description:
The number of Tapesanity locations for percentage

If the number of tapes to record is less then the
  number of locations, then the item count will be
  reduced so that one tapes give one item

options.label: Add Bootleg Tapes
options.description:
Adds custom tapes that always record and turn
  the recorded monster into a specific bootleg.

At least one of each will be added to the item pool.

options.label: Bootlegsanity
options.description:
Adds recording bootleg tapes as locations
  and bootleg related items to the item pool

None - No bootlegs are locations

Per Tape - Each tape has one location for any bootleg

Specific - Each tape has 14 locations, one for each
  bootleg, yes tapes can be bootlegs of their
  original type

Percentage Tape - Getting a total number of unique
  tapes that are bootleg to a certain percentage
  are location

Percentage All - Getting a total number of different
  bootlegs of unique tapes are locations

options.label: Bootlegsanity Percentage
options.description:
The percentage of bootleg tapes that must be recorded to
  obtain all items

options.label: Bootlegsanity Percentage Item Count
options.description:
The number of Bootlegsanity locations for percentage

If the number of tapes to record is less then the
  number of locations, then the item count will be
  reduced so that one tape gives one item

options.label: Fusionsanity
options.description:
Adds encountering or fusing into fusions as locations

Many Pear Fusilli will be added to the item pool

options.label: Fusionsanity Amount
options.description:
The number of fusions that must be seen or fused
  into to obtain all items
Without the Pier of the Unknown dlc, the max
  amount is 17689

options.label: Fusionsanity Item Count
options.description:
The number of Fusionsanity locations

If the number of fusions seen is less then the
  number of locations, then the item count will be
  reduced so that one fusion gives one item

options.label: Special Monsters
options.description: Add the secret monster to applicable locations.

options.label: Goal
options.description: The achievement that completes the slot.

options.label: Total Win Goal
options.description: Number of credited victories required for the total-wins goal.

options.label: Wins Per Goal Civilization
options.description: Numbered victories required with every selected goal civilization.

options.label: Goal Civilizations
options.description: Civilizations unlocked and required when the goal is civilization wins. Civilization pool is then ignored.

options.label: Target Rank
options.description: Rank which must be observed for the selected ranked goal. Rank completion is permanent.

options.label: Civilization Pool
options.description: Civilizations unlocked for total-wins and rank goals. Ignored by the civilization-wins goal.

options.label: Starting Civilization
options.description: A guaranteed starting unlock. Random uses the active goal-dependent civilization pool.

options.label: Starting Civilizations
options.description: Number of deterministic random civilizations to start unlocked, from 1 to 5.

options.label: Starting Civilization List
options.description: Exact starting civilizations. When non-empty, this overrides the other starting civilization options.

options.label: Eligible Match Modes
options.description: Standard queues which can produce wins, losses, checks, and DeathLinks.

options.label: Civilization Sanity
options.description: Add configured win checks per pool civilization for total-win/rank goals. Civilization-win goals ignore this.

options.label: Civilization Sanity Win Count
options.description: Number of numbered win checks per civilization when civilization sanity is enabled.

options.label: Win Check Interval
options.description: Credited victories between progressive total-win checks. Civilization-win goals ignore this.

options.label: Win Check Count
options.description: Number of total-win milestone checks. Ignored by civilization-win goals.

options.label: Include Custom Games
options.description: Count completed custom games when the client has a session-only AOE4World API key.

options.label: Death Link
options.description: Send a DeathLink on eligible losses and suppress one eligible match after a received DeathLink.

options.label: Use DLC Content
options.description: Adds supported The Ancient Gods equipment and gameplay content to the randomizer, including the Sentinel Hammer and Support Runes. Mission inclusion is controlled by Mission Pool.

options.label: Mission Pool
options.description:
Choose the set of missions available for this seed.

Base — 13 Base Campaign missions (The Dark Lord disabled).
Full Saga — All 19 normal missions across Base, TAG1, and TAG2 plus The Dark Lord.
DLC Only — The 6 missions of The Ancient Gods Parts One and Two plus The Dark Lord.
Custom — Explicitly select candidate missions and whether The Dark Lord is eligible.

options.label: Custom Missions
options.description: Missions included when Mission Pool is set to Custom.

options.label: Custom Dark Lord
options.description: Include The Dark Lord when Mission Pool is set to Custom.

options.label: Mission Count
options.description:
Number of normal missions to include in Random Mission Order or Mission Access as Items.

All [default] — Includes all candidate normal missions from the selected Mission Pool.
3..19 — Selects a random active subset of this size (The Dark Lord is independent).
Ignored in Vanilla Order (Vanilla Order always uses all candidate missions in chronological order).

options.label: Mission Order
options.description:
Choose chronological progression, a fixed seeded sequence, or individual Access items.

Enabled missions follow chronological order in Vanilla Order; the selected goal mission is played last.

Every completed stage remains replayable; travel returns through the Fortress.
Access and sequence availability do not guarantee immediate logical completion.

options.label: Campaign Difficulty
options.description: Gameplay difficulty fixed for this generated room, including Base, TAG1 and TAG2.

options.label: Starting Missions
options.description: Number of stages initially available in Mission Access as Items. Other modes start with one.

options.label: Full Saga Final Boss
options.description: Reserve the final Full Saga encounter. Vanilla Order always ends at Davoth.

options.label: Goal Mission as Item
options.description:
In Access mode, place the selected boss stage's concrete Access item.

Receipt bypasses ordinary completion gating, but not selected victory objectives.
Has no effect for Acquire the Unmaykr, which ends in the Fortress.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Choose the main objective that wins your Archipelago world.

Acquire the Unmaykr — Complete the six Base Campaign Slayer Gates and claim the Unmaykr from its case in the Fortress of Doom.

Kill the Icon of Sin — Progress through the Base Campaign and defeat the Icon of Sin.

Kill the Dark Lord — Progress through The Ancient Gods Part Two and defeat the Dark Lord.

Complete the Full Saga — Use the unified Base/TAG campaign and defeat its selected final boss. Selected additional objectives remain required. Goal Mission as Item can bypass the ordinary mission-completion gate.

options.label: Additional Victory Requirements
options.description: Choose extra objectives that must also be completed before your Goal counts as victory. Hover an objective to see exactly what it requires.

options.label: Special Weapon
options.description: Choose a three-stage Crucible-to-Hammer progression, a two-stage Sentinel Hammer progression, or one standalone Crucible stage.

options.label: DeathLink Mode
options.description: Choose how a received DeathLink is fulfilled. Soft applies one death to you, but can be mitigated by Extra Lives or Saving Throw. Hardcore applies one death and cannot be mitigated.

options.label: Enhanced Melee Damage
options.description: Increase the damage of normal punches, making melee a more useful close-range fallback.

options.label: Randomize Chainsaw
options.description:
Randomize the Chainsaw. If false, the Chainsaw will always be found at its
vanilla location in Hell on Earth.

options.label: Randomize Dash
options.description:
Shuffle the Dash pickup into the item pool.

Warning: routes before finding Dash can require advanced movement such as
bunny hopping (bhop) or Ballista boosting. Enable this only if you are
comfortable playing without Dash until you find it.

options.label: Include Slayer Gates
options.description: Include Slayer Gate completion checks and their keys in the item pool. Acquire the Unmaykr requires this option.

options.label: Include Secret Encounters
options.description: Include Secret Encounter completion checks.

options.label: Include Weapon Mastery Challenges
options.description: Include the 13 Weapon Mastery Challenge locations.

options.label: Reveal AP Locations on Automap
options.description: Show Archipelago pickup locations on the DOOM Eternal Automap, making checks easier to find while exploring or replaying missions.

options.label: Starting Weapon
options.description: Choose the weapon you start with. Random selects one eligible weapon when the seed is generated. That weapon belongs to your starting inventory.

options.label: Trap Percentage
options.description: Percentage of filler padding replaced by enabled traps.

options.label: Enabled Traps
options.description: Trap types eligible for filler-padding replacement.

traps: Exultia - Extra Life - Inside Electric Trap

options.label: Starting Vehicle Type
options.description:
Which vehicle type you start with.
'random' picks randomly from all transport types.
For all options, Starting Vehicle Count controls how many vehicles you receive.

options.label: Starting Vehicle Count
options.description:
How many starting vehicles to receive.
For 'random', vehicles are drawn from all transport types.
For a specific type, all vehicles come from that type.

options.label: Win Difficulty
options.description:
Overall win difficulty. Sets ALL six victory targets at once.
You must meet EVERY target simultaneously to win.

Casual:    Very forgiving — great for first-time players or short sessions.
Easy:      A relaxed challenge. Takes a few hours of play.
Normal:    The balanced default experience. Moderate effort required.
Medium:    Noticeably harder. Requires solid network planning.
Hard:      Serious challenge. Efficient routes and smart vehicle use needed.
Very Hard: Expert level. Requires optimised play throughout.
Extreme:   Near-maximum challenge. Marginal error tolerance.
Insane:    Almost nothing forgiven. For veteran players only.
Nutcase:   Maximum standard difficulty. Near-impossible on default map size.
Madness:   Absurd targets. Only for challenge runs with custom settings.
Custom:    Use the sliders below to set your own targets.

options.label: Custom: Target Company Value (GBP)
options.description: [Custom only] Target company value in pounds.

options.label: Custom: Target Town Population
options.description:
[Custom only] Target total world population across all towns.
The game clamps this to 10,000 per town on the actual map, so a target
larger than the map can hold is reduced rather than left unreachable.

options.label: Custom: Target Vehicle Count
options.description: [Custom only] Target number of active vehicles you own simultaneously.

options.label: Custom: Target Cargo Delivered (tons)
options.description: [Custom only] Total cumulative tons of cargo to deliver this session.

options.label: Custom: Target Yearly Profit (GBP)
options.description:
[Custom only] YEARLY net profit target in pounds — the net over the last
four completed quarters. The YAML key keeps its historical monthly name so
existing settings files stay valid; the number it sets is a yearly figure.

options.label: Custom: Target Missions Completed
options.description: [Custom only] Number of AP missions (location checks) that must be completed.

options.label: Enable Sphere Progression
options.description:
Enable sphere-based progression. When ON, all unlock items (rail directions,
road directions, signals, bridges, tunnels, airports, terraform, wagons, trees,
town actions) are locked at session start and must be found as Archipelago items.
This creates proper progression spheres:

Sphere 0: Starting vehicles + precollected infra → Easy missions
Sphere 1: More vehicles + basic infra (rail/road/airports) → Medium missions
Sphere 2: Even more vehicles + crossing infra (bridge/tunnel) → Hard missions
Sphere 3: Full fleet + terraform → Extreme missions

When OFF, all infrastructure is available from the start (flat progression).
This is a master toggle — it enables ALL unlock categories at once.

options.label: Mission Tier Unlock Count
options.description:
How many missions of the previous tier must be completed before the next tier unlocks.
Example: setting 5 means you need 5 easy missions done before any medium missions are evaluated.
Set to 0 to disable tier gating entirely (all tiers always available).

options.label: Mission Difficulty
options.description:
Scales the target amounts in all generated missions up or down.
Does not affect vehicle/town/station counts — only monetary and cargo targets.

Very Easy: amounts × 0.25  — great for first-timers or short sessions
Easy:      amounts × 0.5
Normal:    amounts × 1.0  — the balanced default experience
Hard:      amounts × 2.0
Very Hard: amounts × 4.0  — for veteran players who want a serious challenge

options.label: Victory Vehicle Requirement (Logic)
options.description:
Minimum number of vehicles the logic requires before Victory is reachable.

The Archipelago logic uses this to determine which sphere Victory falls in.
Higher values push Victory into later spheres (more items needed first).
Lower values allow Victory to appear earlier in the spoiler log.

The actual in-game win condition is set by Win Difficulty — this only
affects the logical SPHERE placement. If you set this too low, Victory
may appear reachable in sphere 2-3 which means other players' items
could be locked behind your early completion.

Default 15 ensures Victory sits comfortably in sphere 4+.
If you have many NewGRFs enabled, consider raising this.

options.label: Hard Tier Vehicle Multiplier
options.description:
Vehicle count multiplier for Hard mission access rules.

The number of vehicles needed to access Hard missions is calculated as:
Mission Tier Unlock Count × this multiplier.

Default 2 means if Tier Unlock Count is 5, you need 10 vehicles for Hard.
Set higher to make Hard missions require a larger fleet.
Set to 1 to make Hard missions accessible with fewer vehicles.

Note: If this results in fewer than 1, the minimum is always 1.

options.label: Extreme Tier Vehicle Multiplier
options.description:
Vehicle count multiplier for Extreme mission access rules.

The number of vehicles needed to access Extreme missions is calculated as:
Mission Tier Unlock Count × this multiplier.

Default 3 means if Tier Unlock Count is 5, you need 15 vehicles for Extreme.
Set higher for a longer grind before endgame content.
Set to 1 to make Extreme missions accessible much earlier.

Note: If this results in fewer than 1, the minimum is always 1.

options.label: Utility Count
options.description:
How many utility items (cash injections, loan reductions, boosts) to include.
The remainder of the item pool is filled with vehicles for your landscape.

options.label: Speed Boost Count
options.description:
How many Speed Boost items to place in the multiworld pool.
Each Speed Boost gives +10% fast-forward speed, from 100% up to 300%.
20 items reaches that maximum. Anything beyond 20 is a dead item: the
game caps the speed and says so out loud when the 21st arrives.
Raise this only to pad the pool; use Utility Count for that instead.

options.label: Shop Price Tier
options.description:
How expensive shop purchases are. Seven tiers from cheapest to most expensive.
Prices are drawn at random inside the chosen tier and then sorted, so the
shop opens with its cheapest slots and works up to its most expensive.

Tier 1: £10,000 – £500,000
Tier 2: £50,000 – £1,000,000
Tier 3: £100,000 – £5,000,000
Tier 4: £500,000 – £15,000,000
Tier 5: £1,000,000 – £50,000,000
Tier 6: £5,000,000 – £150,000,000
Tier 7: £10,000,000 – £500,000,000

options.label: Starting Cash Bonus
options.description:
Extra cash given to your company at the start of a session,
on top of whatever loan you take. Helps new players build their
first routes without going bankrupt.
None:        £0          (default — no bonus)
Small:       £50,000
Medium:      £200,000
Large:       £500,000
Very Large:  £2,000,000

options.label: Enable Wagon Unlocks
options.group: Manual Unlock Toggles (IGNORED when Sphere Progression is ON)
options.description:
Lock wagons at session start — they must be received as Archipelago items.
Without this, all wagons are available from the start.
NOTE: Ignored when Sphere Progression is ON (auto-enabled).

options.label: Enable Rail Direction Unlocks
options.group: Manual Unlock Toggles (IGNORED when Sphere Progression is ON)
options.description:
Lock rail track directions (Normal, Electrified, Monorail, Maglev x 6 dirs each = 24 items).
You must find direction unlocks before you can build track in that orientation.
NOTE: Ignored when Sphere Progression is ON (auto-enabled).

options.label: Enable Road Direction Unlocks
options.group: Manual Unlock Toggles (IGNORED when Sphere Progression is ON)
options.description:
Lock road directions (NE-SW, NW-SE). You must find direction unlocks before
you can build roads in that orientation.
NOTE: Ignored when Sphere Progression is ON (auto-enabled).

options.label: Enable Signal Unlocks
options.group: Manual Unlock Toggles (IGNORED when Sphere Progression is ON)
options.description:
Lock signal types (Block, Entry, Exit, Combo, Path, One-Way Path).
You must find signal unlocks before you can place them.
NOTE: Ignored when Sphere Progression is ON (auto-enabled).

options.label: Enable Bridge Unlocks
options.group: Manual Unlock Toggles (IGNORED when Sphere Progression is ON)
options.description:
Lock bridge types (Wooden through Tubular Silicon = 13 items).
You must find bridge unlocks before you can build them.
NOTE: Ignored when Sphere Progression is ON (auto-enabled).

options.label: Enable Tunnel Unlocks
options.group: Manual Unlock Toggles (IGNORED when Sphere Progression is ON)
options.description:
Lock tunnel construction. You must find the Tunnel Construction item
before you can dig tunnels.
NOTE: Ignored when Sphere Progression is ON (auto-enabled).

options.label: Enable Airport Unlocks
options.group: Manual Unlock Toggles (IGNORED when Sphere Progression is ON)
options.description:
Lock airport types (Large, Heliport, Metropolitan, International, Commuter,
Helidepot, Intercontinental, Helistation = 8 items). Small Airport is always free.
NOTE: Ignored when Sphere Progression is ON (auto-enabled).

options.label: Enable Tree Unlocks
options.group: Manual Unlock Toggles (IGNORED when Sphere Progression is ON)
options.description:
Lock tree planting — 10 tree packs (3 per climate + Toyland) must be
received as items before you can plant those tree types.
NOTE: Ignored when Sphere Progression is ON (auto-enabled).

options.label: Enable Terraform Unlocks
options.group: Manual Unlock Toggles (IGNORED when Sphere Progression is ON)
options.description:
Lock terraform abilities (Raise Land, Lower Land). You must find terraform
unlocks before you can modify terrain height.
NOTE: Ignored when Sphere Progression is ON (auto-enabled).

options.label: Enable Town Action Unlocks
options.group: Manual Unlock Toggles (IGNORED when Sphere Progression is ON)
options.description:
Lock town authority actions (advertise, bribe, fund buildings, etc. = 8 items).
You must find action unlocks before you can use them.
NOTE: Ignored when Sphere Progression is ON (auto-enabled).

options.label: Ruin Pool Size
options.description:
Total number of ruins that will spawn over the course of the game.
Ruins appear on the map and require cargo delivery to clear them.
Clearing a ruin sends a check (items come from the shop pool).
Set to 0 to disable ruins entirely.

options.label: Max Active Ruins
options.description:
Maximum number of ruins that can exist on the map at the same time.
New ruins spawn after existing ones are cleared (with a cooldown).

options.label: Ruin Cargo Types (Min)
options.description:
Minimum number of different cargo types each ruin requires.
Includes all cargo types for the landscape (passengers, mail, goods, coal, etc.).

options.label: Ruin Cargo Types (Max)
options.description:
Maximum number of different cargo types each ruin requires.
The actual number is randomly picked between min and max for each ruin.

options.label: Enable Stars
options.description:
Enable star collectibles scattered across the map.
Small star outlines are hidden in open fields. Click one to collect it
and send an Archipelago check. Stars never spawn near buildings.

options.label: Star Pool Size
options.description:
Internal — kept for option compatibility but hidden.
Star count is computed dynamically (50/50 split with shop).

options.label: Enable Traps
options.description: Whether trap items can be sent to you by other players.

options.label: Trap Count
options.description:
How many trap items to include in the item pool.
