options.label: Require Stage
options.description:
Add Stage items to the pool that blocks maps of the type
Does nothing unless on map grouping

options.label: Divine Teleporter on Stage 5
options.description: Only allow access to teleport to final stage if on stage 5, like RoR2

options.label: Strict Map Requirements
options.description:
Require both the prior stage and any corresponding map before having access to later stages
Ex. You won't be able to access Stage 3 until you have Stage 2 and either Stage 2 map

options.label: Teleporter Fragments Required
options.description: Percentage of teleporter fragments required to access the final stage

options.label: Teleporter Fragments Available
options.description: Percentage of filler items to be replaced with teleporter fragments

options.label: Item Pickup Step
options.description:
Number of items to pick up before an AP Check is completed.
Setting to 1 means every other pickup.
Setting to 2 means every third pickup. So on...

options.label: Enable Trap Items
options.description: Allows Trap items in the item pool.

options.label: Common Items

Weight of common items in the item pool.

(Ignored unless Item Weight Presets is 'No')

Weight of uncommon items in the item pool.

(Ignored unless Item Weight Presets is 'No')

Weight of legendary items in the item pool.

Weight of boss items in the item pool.

Weight of equipment items in the item pool.

(Ignored unless Item Weight Presets is 'No')

Weight of money items in the item pool.

Weight of 1000 exp items in the item pool.

(Ignored unless Item Weight Presets is 'No')

options.label: Time Warp Trap

Weight of time warp trap items in the item pool.

options.label: Combat Trap

Weight of combat trap items in the item pool.

options.label: Meteor Trap

Weight of meteor trap items in the item pool.

(Ignored unless Item Weight Presets is 'No')

options.label: DLC Packs
options.description:
Choose which DLC Packs will be included in the pool of chooseable songs.
Both individual songs and dlc pack names work.

Current DLC Pack Groups: ["All", "Celeste", "Pizza Tower", "Hatsune Miku", "Hololive", "Everhood", "Monstercat", "Shovel Knight", 
                          "Friday Night Funkin'", "VA-11 HALL-A", "Undertale", "Volume 2", "K/DA", "Omega Strikers", "Hatsune Miku 2"]

options.label: Starting Song Count
options.description: The number of songs that will be unlocked from the start

options.label: Additional Song Count
options.description:
The total number of songs that will be placed in the randomization pool.
- This does not count any starting songs or the goal song.
- The final song count may be lower due to other settings.

options.label: Duplicate Song Percentage
options.description:
Percentage of duplicate songs to place in remaining filler slots.
Duplicate songs are considered Useful and thus out of logic.

options.label: Include Remix Mode
options.description: Adds remix mode songs as separate items and locations. When off, both normal and remix mode unlocks are the same.

options.label: Include Minigames
options.description:
Adds minigames to the song pool.
Split allows medium and hard variants to be shuffled separately.

options.label: Include Boss Battles
options.description:
Add boss battles to the song pool
Split allows medium and hard variants to be shuffled separately.

options.label: Difficulty Selection
options.description:
Determines what difficulties to be selected for song filtering (Rhythm Rifts only)
This setting will not force you to play on any of the selected difficulties and intened to be used with the following intensity settings

options.label: Minimum Intensity
options.description:
Ensures chosen rhythm rift will have a chart with an intensity value higher than this value (Rhythm Rifts only)
Note: Highest intensity song in vanilla is 30

options.label: Maximum Intensity
options.description:
Ensures chosen rhythm rift will have a chart with an intensity value lower than this value (Rhythm Rifts only)
Note: Highest intensity song in vanilla is 30

options.label: Grade Needed
options.description: Minimum Grade required on song completion to send a check

options.label: Full Combo Needed
options.description: Requires a full combo on song completion to send a check

options.label: Diamond Percentage
options.description: Percentage of filler item to be replaced with diamonds.

options.label: Diamonds Needed to Win
options.description: The percentage of diamonds in the item pool that are needed to unlock the winning song.

options.label: Include Songs Percentage
options.description: Percentage chance for songs in the included list to be chosen.

options.label: Include Songs
options.description:
These songs will be guaranteed* to show up within the seed.
- You must have the DLC or respective game mode enabled for these songs to actually be picked.
- Difficulty options will affect these songs.
- *Changing Include Songs Percentage from 100% will make it no longer guarenteed.

options.label: Exclude Songs
options.description:
These songs will be guaranteed to not show up within the seed.

Note: Does not affect songs within the "Include Songs" list.

options.label: Goal Song Pool
options.description:
Songs listed here will randomly chosen to be the final song.
If empty, the goal song will be chosen randomly from all included songs.

options.label: Enable Deathlink
options.description: Includes Deathlink

options.label: Goal Condition
options.description:
Set the goal condition

- **Gwyn:** Default option -Beat Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
- **Bosses:** Defeat all bosses
- **Ornstein and Smough:** Kill Ornstein and Smough

options.label: Guaranteed Items
options.description: Guarantees that the specified items will be in the item pool

options.label: Excluded Locations Behavior
options.description:
How to choose items for excluded locations in DSR.

- **Forbid Useful:** Neither progression items nor useful items can be placed in excluded
  locations.
- **Do Not Randomize:** Excluded locations always contain the same item as in vanilla
  Dark Souls: Remastered.

options.label: Can Warp Without Lordvessel
options.description: Gain the ability to warp as soon as you have rested at any warpable bonfire.

options.label: Warp To All Bonfires
options.description:
Makes all bonfires eligible to be warped to via the in-game menu.
No matter your settings, you will still need to actually rest at the warpable points to be able to warp to them.

As a side-effect, this will also make warping set your destination as your "return" point upon next death, homeward, etc.
Warpable bonfires are synced between all saves on the slot, regardless of your choice.

options.label: Ghost Difficulty
options.description:
How to manage difficulty for ghosts.

- **Normal:** Ghost's behavior is unchanged and no mitigations are made to make them easier to deal with.
- **Ghosts Are Not Ghostly:** Ghosts can be damaged by all weapons and items.
  Similar to having a transient curse always active.
- **Rickert Sells Curses:** Rickert, the blacksmith/shopkeeper in the safe part of New Londo, 
  will sell unlimited transient curse items, 1500 souls apiece.

options.label: Soul Multiplier - Base Percentage
options.description:
Base value for a multiplier applied to enemy & boss soul drops, expressed as a percentage.
100 is vanilla.

options.label: Soul Multiplier - Maximum Percentage
options.description:
Maximum (final) value for a multiplier applied to enemy & boss soul drops, expressed as a percentage.

Only takes effect if not equal to soul_multiplier_base, and soul_multiplier_steps is non-zero.

options.label: Soul Multiplier Steps
options.description:
Number of steps from the base to the maximum multiplier. 
This is how many "Progressive Soul Multiplier" items will be added to the item pool.

Upon receiving one, the soul multiplier will increase (1/(this value)) * (the distance from max to base).
As an example, if your soul_multiplier_base is 100, soul_multiplier_max is 200, and this is set to 4, then the
first such item will set the soul drop multiplier to 125%, 2nd to 150%, and so on.

Progressive Soul Multiplier update will only take effect when enemies are reloaded or respawned.

Has no effect if the soul_multiplier_base and soul_multiplier_max are equal.

If zero, soul_multiplier_base is applied as a static multiplier.

options.label: Weight Multiplier - Base Percentage
options.description:
Base value for a multiplier applied to weight of weapons, shields, and armors, expressed as a percentage.
100 is vanilla weight.
50 is half weight.
0 is no weight.

options.label: Weight Multiplier - Minimum Percentage
options.description:
Minimum (final) value for a multiplier applied to weight of weapons, shields, and armors, expressed as a percentage.

Only takes effect if not equal to weight_multiplier_base, and weight_multiplier_steps is non-zero.

options.label: Weight Multiplier Steps
options.description:
Number of steps from the base to the minimum multiplier. 
This is how many "Progressive Weight Reducer" items will be added to the item pool.

Upon receiving one, the weight multiplier will decrease (1/(this value)) * (the distance from base to min).
As an example, if your weight_multiplier_base is 100, weight_multiplier_min is 20, and this is set to 4, then the
first such item will set the weight multiplier to 80%, 2nd to 60%, and so on.

Has no effect if the weight_multiplier_base and weight_multiplier_min are equal.

If zero, weight_multiplier_base is applied as a static multiplier.

If you want to turn off weapon and armor weight entirely, set weight_multiplier_base and this value both to 0.

options.label: Fogwall Sanity
options.description:
Makes area fog walls uninteractable until you receive their items from the item pool. 
Fog walls will also give checks when you pass through them.
The Undead Asylum fog wall will not be locked, to avoid super-early BK.
Recommended to turn this on.

options.label: Boss Fogwall Sanity
options.description:
Makes boss fog walls uninteractable until you receive their items from the item pool.
Boss fog walls will also give checks when you pass through them.
The following will be neither locations nor checks as they all do not have fog walls
upon your first entry into their arena:
  Asylum Demon (first encounter),
  Sif,
  Seath (2nd encounter), and
  Kalameet.

options.label: Boss Soul Shuffle
options.description:
Makes boss soul drops be shuffled into the multiworld item pool.
Does not affect the Lord Souls, which are always shuffled in.

options.label: Boss Humanity Shuffle
options.description: Makes boss humanity and twin humanity drops be shuffled into the multiworld item pool.

options.label: Boss Bone Shuffle
options.description: Makes boss homeward bone drops be shuffled into the multiworld item pool.

options.label: Black Knight Weapon Shuffle
options.description:
Makes Black Knight weapon drop locations guaranteed, and adds their weapons to the multiworld item pool.
This only applies to the 7 non-respawning Black Knights in the game.
With this off, their Titanite Chunk drops are still added to the pool, and the weapon drops are left to chance.

These weapons are quite powerful, and this option adds 2 Swords, 2 Halberds, 1 Greataxe, 1 Greatsword, and 1 Shield to the pool.

options.label: Crystal Lizard Shuffle
options.description:
Adds Crystal Lizard drop locations to the multiworld item pool.
This adds 2 locations per lizard: 1 for their Twinkling Titanite, and 1 for an additional drop - which is made guaranteed.

There are 25 total crystal lizards, 10 of which are in the Great Hollow, and 5 of which are in the DLC.
If one escapes, you can quit out and reload to respawn it.
Great Hollow lizards are forced to spawn on every load instead of their vanilla 1/3 chance per load.

options.label: Unlimited Shop Item Shuffle
options.description:
Shuffles unlimited quantity consumable and arrow shop slots from unmissable shopkeepers.

Shops Shuffled by this option include all those on the Limited shuffle option below, plus Ingward.

options.label: Limited Shop Item Shuffle
options.description:
Adds limited quantity shop slots from unmissable shopkeepers as locations, and shuffles their items into the multiworld.
This treats Weapon and Armor slots as limited quantity slots, adding 1 of each to the pool.
Missable shopkeepers, who can be made unavailable based on progression or dialogue options, will not have their shops shuffled into the multiworld.
Shuffled Shops' keepers will be made immune to player attacks to make them unmissable, and their drops added as shuffled locations to their shop.

Shops Shuffled by this option:
Andre of Astora
Big Hat Logan
Crestfallen Merchant
Domhnall of Zena (including post-boss equipment)
Female Undead Merchant
Giant Blacksmith
Griggs of Vinheim
Hawkeye Gough
Laurentius of the Great Swamp - The client will prevent him from moving on to Blighttown until you have bought out his shop.
Male Undead Merchant
Marvelous Chester
Oswald of Carim
Petrus of Thorolund
Rickert of Vinheim
Vamos

options.label: Shop Hints
options.description: When Shop items are shuffled, this options control what types of Archipelago Hints will be created upon talking to the relevant merchant (with the shop slots unlocked).

options.label: Logic Requirement to Access Firelink Altar
options.description:
Firelink Altar logical Access requirement.
 Before the chosen condition, Firelink Altar will be considered "out of logic".
 This will also restrict logical access to areas behind golden fog walls, since Firelink Altar access is required for placing the lordvessel.
 This will not actually prevent you from accessing the Altar from either Serpent.

- **Either:** As soon as you can reach either Serpent (Kaathe or Frampt), Firelink Altar in-logic. It is left up to chance (the generate process) which one is expected by the logic.
- **Both:** Only when both Serpents are accessible is Firelink Altar considered in-logic. This is the "safest" option.
- **Frampt:** (default) Frampt being accessible puts Firelink Altar in-logic (both bells can be rung)
- **Kaathe:** Kaathe being accessible puts Firelink Altar in-logic (via defeating the Four Kings in the Abyss under New Londo).

If you accidentally dismiss or anger Kaathe, and this option is "Either" or "Kaathe", thus making you unable to get to the altar, you can use the /warp FA command in the client to warp to the altar.

options.label: Logic Requirement to Access Catacombs
options.description:
Artificial logic for The Catacombs access. 
 Before the chosen condition, The Catacombs will be considered "out of logic"

- **no_logic:** (not recommended) Catacombs is in-logic as soon as you get to Firelink Shrine.
- **undead_merchant:** Access to Undead Merchant in the Upper Undead Burg puts Catacombs in-logic.
- **andre:** Access to Andre puts Catacombs in-logic.
- **andre_or_undead_merchant:** Access to either Andre or Undead Merchant puts Catacombs in-logic.
- **ornstein_and_smough:** (Default) Access to Ornstein and Smough puts Catcombs in-logic.

options.label: Logic Requirement to Access Tomb of the Giants
options.description:
Artificial logic for Tomb of the Giants (TotG) access.
 Before the chosen condition, TotG will be considered "out of logic".

- **no_logic:** TotG is in-logic as soon as you defeat Pinwheel.
- **skull_lantern:** Receiving a Skull Lantern as an AP item puts TotG in-logic.
- **sunlight_maggot:** Receiving a Sunlight Maggot as an AP item puts TotG in-logic.

options.label: Randomize Starting Loadout
options.description:
Randomize each class's starting weapons, shields, and armors.
This will also replace the thief's master key, which would break logic.
Shields will always be 1-handed-wieldable with starting stats.
Weapons will always be at least 2-handed-wieldable with starting stats.
You can see what weapons/shield/item each class starts with in their description.
Starting spells are randomized separately.

options.label: Randomize Starting Gifts
options.description:
Randomize the starting gift options to a subset of a custom item pool.
This pool includes many additional consumable options, and some rings.
This pool also includes most of the default gifts, except Master key, which breaks logic.

options.label: Require One Handed Starting Weapons
options.description:
If randomize_starting_loadouts is on, this option determines if each class's weapons can be wielded with one hand with their starting stats.
Ignored if no_weapon_requirements is true.

options.label: Extra Starting Weapon For Melee Classes
options.description: If randomize_starting_loadouts is on, this option determines if melee classes will get a second melee weapon.

options.label: Extra Starting Shield For All Classes
options.description: If randomize_starting_loadouts is on, this option determines if all classes will get a second starting shield.

options.label: Starting Sorcery
options.description:
How to randomize starting sorceries.
Limited to spells the sorcerer can cast with their starting stats, unless "remove_spell_stat_requirements" is on.

- **Soul Arrow:** Default option - vanilla starting sorcery
- **Any:** Any sorcery
- **Attack:** Any attack sorcery

options.label: Starting Miracle
options.description:
How to randomize starting miracles.
Limited to spells the cleric can cast with their starting stats, unless "remove_spell_stat_requirements" is on.

- **Heal:** Default option - vanilla starting miracle
- **Any:** Any miracle
- **Healing:** Any healing miracle

options.label: Starting Pyromancy
options.description:
How to randomize starting pyromancies.

- **Fireball:** Default option - vanilla starting pyromancy
- **Any:** Any pyromancy
- **Attack:** Any attack pyromancy

options.label: No Weapon Stat Requirements
options.description: Removes weapon and shield stat requirements.

options.label: No Spell Stat Requirements
options.description: Removes stat requirements for casting all miracles and sorceries.

options.label: No Miracle Covenant Requirements
options.description: Removes covenant requirements for casting certain miracles.

options.label: Upgraded Weapons Percentage
options.description:
Percentage of weapons (including shields) in the pool that will be replaced with upgraded versions, if possible.
Does not affect starting equipment.
Choose a higher value for an easier time.

options.label: Upgraded Weapons - Allowed Infusions
options.description:
Which infusions are allowed if UpgradedWeapons.
Available infusion types are Normal, Raw, Magic, Fire, Divine, Chaos, Enchanted, Occult, Crystal, and Lightning.
If "Normal" is removed, all upgraded weapons will have a different, available infusion.

options.label: Upgraded Weapons - Adjust Ranges
options.description:
For upgraded weapons added to the pool, Whether to 'adjust' weapon levels for applying the ranges.
When true, the min/max levels will apply to an calculated "level" of an infused weapon adjusted by:
 +5 for Raw/Magic/Fire/Divine
 +10 for Chaos/Enchanted/Occult/Crystal/Lightning 
When false, the min/max levels will not be adjusted.

options.label: Upgraded Weapons - Minimum Level
options.description:
Minimum upgrade value on upgraded weapons in the pool.
This can exclude certain infusions if their calculated level cannot be at the minimum level.

options.label: Upgraded Weapons - Maximum Level
options.description: Maximum upgrade plus value on upgraded weapons in the pool.

traps: DE: Soul of a Nameless Soldier - Ooze Trap

options.label: Max Number of Easter Eggs
options.description:
The maximum number of Easter Eggs that will be in the item pool.
If fewer available locations exist in the pool than this number, random potions will be removed to make space.
By default, 26 eggs can be placed before potions are removed;
with all locations enabled, there is space for 57 eggs.
Required Percentage of Easter Eggs will be calculated based off of this number.

options.label: Required Percentage of Easter Eggs
options.description:
What percentage of Easter Eggs are required to beat the game. Note that you will receive
the Rainbow Shot after 5 eggs no matter how many eggs are required.

options.label: Encourage Eggs In Late Spheres
options.description:
If set to true, the randomizer logic will attempt to place eggs in later spheres
resulting in harder to get to eggs.

options.label: Apply Beginner Mod
options.description:
If set to true, applies an accessibility mod for new players.
This mod shows hidden paths and reveals breakable blocks.
Additionally, the mod fixes a few areas to prevent softlocks.

options.label: Attack Mode
options.description:
Normal attack mode starts you with 0 attack ups.
Super attack mode starts you with 20 attack ups.
Hyper attack mode starts you with 30 attack ups.

This gives you a lot more damage, which is especially useful because you often don't get
the hammer early in randomizer games. (Ribbon does about 20 damage per shot in super attack mode)

options.label: Knowledge
options.description:
Knowledge can be Basic, Intermediate, Advanced, or Obscure.

There are many tricks in the game that requires advanced knowledge of how the game works to perform.
Knowledge levels (mostly) align with the tricks explained on each section of the Platforming Tricks Tutorial custom map.
Obscure contains tricks that require incredibly specific game knowledge and may be scarcely documented, if at all.

options.label: Trick Difficulty
options.description:
Difficulty can be Normal, Hard, Very Hard, Extreme, or Stupid.

Some tricks in Rabi-Ribi can be very difficult to execute. This flag determines the minimum execution ability required to complete the seed.

Normal is recommended for most players. Any tricks in normal should be only as hard as what is expected in a Low Item% playthrough.
Hard involves some tricks that are tight and can be difficult to execute for newer players.
Very Hard involves some tricks that are very tight and can be difficult to execute even for experienced players.
Extreme involves tricks that can be quite unreasonable to be expected to execute.
Stupid refers to tricks that no one wants to do, ever. This often refers to tricks that have only been performed successfully once, just to prove that it is possible.

options.label: Block Clips Required
options.description:
Block clips are performed by quick-dropping onto the top of a one-tile block to obtain the item inside the block.
Turning off this flag removes the need for block clips.

options.label: Semi Solid Clips Required
options.description:
Semisolid Clips refers to clipping through semisolid
(one-way) platforms via a specific glitch. If this flag is turned on,
reaching some of the items may require semisolid clips to be performed.
If turned off, all the required items can be obtained without the need
for semisolid clips.

options.label: Zips Required
options.description:
Zips are glitches that allow you to clip through terrain.
The main types of zips are slide zips and hammer roll zips.
If this flag is turned on, reaching some of the items may require
zips to be performed. If turned off, all the required items can be
obtained without the need for zips.

options.label: Bunstrike Zips Required
options.description:
A bunstrike zip is an obscure zip method performed by using Bunny Strike.
If this flag is turned on, reaching some of the items may require
bunstrike zips to be performed. If turned off, all the required items
can be obtained without the need for bunstrike zips.

options.label: Boring Tricks Required
options.description:
If this flag is true, some of the items may require performing tricks
considered too boring or tedious to normally be included in logic.
Note that most of these tricks are still considered to be at least
Advanced knowledge and Very Hard difficulty at minimum.

options.label: Darkness Without Light Orb
options.description:
If this flag is true, the game might expect you to go into dark areas,
even if you don’t have the Light Orb.

options.label: Underwater Without Water Orb
options.description:
If this flag is true, the game might expect you to go into underwater areas,
even if you don’t have the Water Orb.

options.label: Carrot Shooter In Logic
options.description:
If set to false, Carrot Shooter will not be required to bomb locations.
These locations will be locked behind Carrot Bomb instead.

options.label: Rainbow Egg In Logic
options.description:
If set to false, Rainbow Egg will not be considered as a collectable magic type
to enable the item menu.

options.label: Event Warps in Logic
options.description:
If this flag is true, events that warp the player to another location are considered in logic.
While some of these events can only be reached once normally, the randomizer adds doors that
allow these events to be accessed multiple times.

options.label: IncludePlurkwood
options.description: If this flag is true, the game might expect you to go into Plurkwood.

options.label: Include Warp Destination
options.description:
If this flag is true, locations in the warp destination area are included in the pool.
Note that some of these locations may require beating the game to reach again if missed.

options.label: Include Post Game
options.description: If this flag is true, locations only reachable in the post game are included in the pool.

options.label: Include Post Irisu
options.description: If this flag is true, locations only reachable after beating Irisu are included in the pool.

options.label: Include Halloween DLC
options.description:
If this flag is true, the Halloween DLC locations are included in the pool.
Requires the "Cinini's Halloween!" DLC.

options.label: Number of Map Constraint Changes
options.description:
Sets the total number of map constraint changes to be added.

A map constraint is an predefined edit to the map to restrict access to parts of Rabi Rabi Island with various obstacles.
By restricting access to certain areas of the map, the amount of checks opened per sphere is kept more uniform, allowing for better game flow.

These constraints are enabled by default, as not only can the main game of Rabi-Ribi be completed without any items,
but over half of the item locations can be reached without items as well.

options.label: Required Constraints
options.description: Sets the map constraints that should be forced when selecting which constraints to place.

options.label: Exclude Constraints
options.description: Sets the map constraints that should be excluded when selecting which constraints to place.

options.label: Shuffle Map Transitions
options.description: If this flag is true, the randomizer will shuffle the entrances between maps.

options.label: Shuffle Start Location
options.description:
If this flag is true, the randomizer will start the player at one of several locations
around Rabi Rabi Island.

options.label: Shuffle Music
options.description: If this flag is true, the randomizer will shuffle the music tracks played in each area.

options.label: Shuffle Backgrounds
options.description:
If this flag is true, the randomizer will shuffle the room backgrounds in each area.
By default, some backgrounds that introduce lag or make tricks difficult to perform are disabled.

options.label: Allow Laggy Backgrounds
options.description:
If this flag is true, the randomizer will add backgrounds that introduce lag
to the pool of backgrounds to choose from when shuffling backgrounds.

options.label: Allow Difficult Backgrounds
options.description:
If this flag is true, the randomizer will add backgrounds that can make tricks difficult to perform
to the pool of backgrounds to choose from when shuffling backgrounds.

with all locations enabled, there is space for 57 eggs.
Required Percentage of Easter Eggs will be calculated based off of this number.

If this flag is true, events that warp the player to another location are considered in logic.
While some of these events can only be reached once normally, the randomizer adds doors that
allow these events to be accessed multiple times.

options.label: IncludePlurkwood
options.description: If this flag is true, the game might expect you to go into Plurkwood.

options.label: Include Warp Destination
options.description:
If this flag is true, locations in the warp destination area are included in the pool.
Note that some of these locations may require beating the game to reach again if missed.

options.label: Include Post Game
options.description: If this flag is true, locations only reachable in the post game are included in the pool.

options.label: Include Post Irisu
options.description: If this flag is true, locations only reachable after beating Irisu are included in the pool.

options.label: Include Halloween DLC
options.description:
If this flag is true, the Halloween DLC locations are included in the pool.
Requires the "Cinini's Halloween!" DLC.

options.label: Number of Map Constraint Changes
options.description:
Sets the total number of map constraint changes to be added.

A map constraint is an predefined edit to the map to restrict access to parts of Rabi Rabi Island with various obstacles.
By restricting access to certain areas of the map, the amount of checks opened per sphere is kept more uniform, allowing for better game flow.

These constraints are enabled by default, as not only can the main game of Rabi-Ribi be completed without any items,
but over half of the item locations can be reached without items as well.

options.label: Required Constraints
options.description: Sets the map constraints that should be forced when selecting which constraints to place.

options.label: Exclude Constraints
options.description: Sets the map constraints that should be excluded when selecting which constraints to place.

options.label: Shuffle Map Transitions
options.description: If this flag is true, the randomizer will shuffle the entrances between maps.

options.label: Shuffle Start Location
options.description:
If this flag is true, the randomizer will start the player at one of several locations
around Rabi Rabi Island.

options.label: Shuffle Music
options.description: If this flag is true, the randomizer will shuffle the music tracks played in each area.

options.label: Shuffle Backgrounds
options.description:
If this flag is true, the randomizer will shuffle the room backgrounds in each area.
By default, some backgrounds that introduce lag or make tricks difficult to perform are disabled.

options.label: Allow Laggy Backgrounds
options.description:
If this flag is true, the randomizer will add backgrounds that introduce lag
to the pool of backgrounds to choose from when shuffling backgrounds.

options.label: Allow Difficult Backgrounds
options.description:
If this flag is true, the randomizer will add backgrounds that can make tricks difficult to perform
to the pool of backgrounds to choose from when shuffling backgrounds.

options.label: Progression Balancing
options.description:
ATTEMPTS TO BALANCE THE PROGRESSION OF YOUR ITEMS.

SETTING THE VALUE LOWER WILL RESULT IN MORE WAITING TO RECIEVE ITEMS.

SETTING THE VALUE HIGHER WILL RESULT IN LESS WAITING TO RECIEVE ITEMS.

options.description:
SETS THE RULES FOR THE ABILITY TO REACH ALL ITEMS.

- **Full** *GUARANTEES THAT ALL ITEMS CAN BE OBTAINED.*

- **Minimal** *GUARANTEES ONLY WHAT IS NECESSARY, BUT NO MORE.*

CHOOSE THE ROUTE THAT YOU PREFER.

- **Weird Route** *Proceed through the "Weird Route" storyline. Can we rename this to Side B yet*

WILL GAINING RECRUITS COUNT AS LOCATIONS?

options.label: Lose recruits Sanity

WILL LOSING RECRUITS COUNT AS LOCATIONS?

options.label: Randomize Secret Bosses

LOCATIONS GIVEN BY SHADOW CRYSTAL BOSSES WILL BE RANDOMIZED OR EVEN REQUIRED.

*Secret bosses are: Jevil, Spamton Neo, Chapter 3 Knight, Hammer of Justice, Pink*

- **Randomized** *Chapters are unlocked through getting items. You'll be expected to move in-between chapters a lot.*

achieve your goal. By default, only "Final Boss" and "DLC Final Boss" is
selected.

options.label: Key Item Shards

Which key items should be broken up into shards and how many
shards are required to use them.

**KeyItem**Shards:
- Req: (1-10) *required shards*
- Max: (1-10) *maximum shards*

Requiring about half of the maximum shards allows for more
flexibility to not get blocked at major required gates.

options.label: Exclude Mini Dungeon Bosses

options.label: World Logic

World Logic options

**Region Lock:** Each region will require a 'Special item'.
**Open World:** No region locking. This can create a huge sphere 1, so this setting
is disallowed in multiworlds unless force_region_lock is disabled in host.yaml.

options.label: Separate Progression

options.description:
Guarantee that you don't need to enter the DLC until later in the run. 
This just changes how early you can get Mohgwyn Palace access so you'll still need to find the region_lock items if it's on.

- **Early:** 'Pureblood Knight Medal' will spawn in an early sphere, unless MissableLocationBehaviorOption

- **Late:** You won't have Mohgwyn Palace access until after getting to Snowfield.

options.label: DLC Abyssal Torrent
options.description: Prevent Torrent from getting frightened.

options.label: Randomize Spiritspring Stones
options.description: Randomize Spiritspring Stones into the item pool.

options.label: Enemy Randomizer
options.description:
Randomizes the enemies.
You can change the enemy preset in the static randomizer itself before you randomize the game.

options.label: Merge All Bosses
options.description:
Merge all boss categories into the same pool.
    
When off: major bosses, minidungeon bosses, world minibosses, evergaol bosses, night bosses,

options.label: Restrictive Boss Placement

Give Serpent-Hunter on encounter with Rykard/Serpent in boss arenas.
If off Serpent-Hunter will be randomized and be required for whatever Rykard/Serpent blocks.

options.label: Boss HP/Damage Scaling Percent
options.description:
Scales HP and damage for enemies placed into boss slots.

100 keeps the current static randomizer scaling. 90 means 90% of the boss
location's HP and damage scaling, while 120 means 120%.

options.label: Disable Damage Tick in Valiant Gargoyles' Poison Cloud
options.description: Disable the damage tick in Valiant Gargoyles' poison cloud while leaving poison buildup intact.

options.label: Night Bosses
options.description:
Normal: Bosses spawn at night.
Always On: Bosses will always spawn.

options.label: Dungeon Sweep
options.description: After killing the boss of a mini dungeon collect all remaining items within that dungeon automatically.

options.label: Random Enemy Preset
options.description:
The YAML preset for the static enemy randomizer.

See the online enemy randomization documentation for available options.
Include this as nested YAML. For example:

  random_enemy_preset:
    RemoveSource: Basilisk; Fingercreeper
    DontRandomize: Tree Sentinel

Elden Ring uses class-based enemy pools. To let major bosses, minor bosses,
world minibosses, night minibosses, dragon minibosses, and evergaol bosses
draw from one combined boss pool:

  random_enemy_preset:
    DontRandomize: DLCAllEnemies
    Classes:
      Boss:
        Pools:
        - Weight: 100
          Pool: AllBosses

To keep only DLC hostile NPCs and invasions at their vanilla placements while
still shuffling base game hostile NPCs:

  random_enemy_preset:
    DontRandomize: DLCHostileNPC

options.label: Material Randomizer
options.description: Randomizes the indefinitely spawning materials.

options.label: DeathLink Amnesty
options.description: How many deaths before you send a deathlink to the multiworld.

options.label: Total Trap Count
options.description:
Total amount of traps in the world.
    
This can be capped to total filler your world has or 1000 if you're crazy.
    
A quarter of added traps are split evenly between enabled trap types and the rest are divided based on trap chances.
    
This does nothing if no traps are enabled.

options.description: **NG+ Trap:** Sets the game to random NG+ level until the player dies.

options.label: Status Trap Chance
options.description: **Status Trap:** Applies a random status to the player, with a low chance of deathblight when receiving multiple in close succession.

options.label: Blindness Trap Chance

options.label: Blizzard Trap Chance
options.description: **Blizzard Trap:** Spawns a blizzard that heavily limits visibility as long as you're outside, lasting for a while or until death.

options.label: Randomize Starting Loadout

options.label: Randomize Starting Keepsakes

options.label: Require One-Handed Starting Weapons

options.label: Remove All Weapon and Spell Requirements
