options.label: Auto-Equip
options.description: Automatically equips any received armor or left/right weapons.

options.label: Auto-Upgrade
options.description: Automatically upgrades any received weapons to highest upgraded level.

options.label: Crafting Kit Behavior
options.description:
Choose how the Crafting Kit is handled.

- **Randomize:** Can be anywhere.
- **Early:** Make it anywhere before Altus and not in Caelid, if DLC Only it'll be in Gravesite Plain.
- **Do Not Randomize:** Leave it at its normal spot, if DLC Only is on it'll be in Roundtable Twin Maiden Shop.

options.label: Flask of Wondrous Physick Behavior
options.description:
Choose how the Flask of Wondrous Physick is handled.

- **Randomize:** Can be anywhere.
- **Early:** Make it anywhere before Altus and not in Caelid, if DLC Only it'll be in Gravesite Plain.
- **Do Not Randomize:** Leave it at its normal spot, if DLC Only is on it'll be in Roundtable Twin Maiden Shop.

options.label: Map Behavior
options.description:
Choose how maps are handled.

- **Randomize:** Can be anywhere.
- **Give:** Add to starting inventory.
- **Do Not Randomize:** Leave them at their normal spots.

options.label: Smithing Bell Bearing Behavior
options.description:
Choose how smithing stone bell bearings are handled.
This doesn't work with dlc only, add them to starting inventory or they get randomized.

- **Randomize:** Can be anywhere.
- **Progression Randomize:** Make them a progression item, and be required for the area after they would normally be in and for DLC.
- **Do Not Randomize:** Leave them at their normal spots.

options.label: Smooth Upgrade Items
options.description:
Smooth Upgrade Items.
The smoothing is fuzzy, so you should see stones 1-4 in early spheres and 6-dragon in ending spheres.

options.label: Smooth Rune Items
options.description:
Smooth Rune Items.
The smoothing is fuzzy, so you'll see lower tier (200-10k) runes in early spheres and high tier (35k-80k) runes in ending spheres.

options.label: Spell Shop Spells Only
options.description: Spell Shops only have spells.

options.label: Stormveil and Raya Lucaria Early
options.description: Access to Stormveil and Raya Lucaria will be early.

options.label: Priority Location Groups
options.description:
Prevent these location types from having an unimportant items.
    
    If you add more priority locations then progression items, random priority locations will contain normal items.
    Otherwise your world would contain a lot of other worlds progression.
    
    Base Game
    - **Achievement Boss**: Base game Achievement bosses.
    - **Boss Reward**: Base game bosses. *Use exclude_locations: 'Dungeon' for overworld bosses only.*
    - **Key Items**: Base game Key items.
    - **Shop**: Base game unmissable shops.
    - **Map**: Base game Map pillars.
    - **Chest**: Base game Chests.
    - **Scarab**: Base game Scarabs.
    - **Seedtree**: Golden Seed trees.
    - **Church**: Sacred Tears.
    - **Basin**: Basins that contain tears.
    
DLC
    - **DLC Remembrance Boss**: DLC Remembrance bosses.
    - **DLC Boss Reward**: DLC bosses. *Use exclude_locations: 'Dungeon' for overworld bosses only.*
    - **DLC Key Items**: DLC Key items.
    - **DLC Shop**: DLC unmissable shops.
    - **DLC Map**: DLC Map pillars.
    - **DLC Chest**: DLC Chests.
    - **DLC Scarab**: DLC Scarabs.
    - **Cross**: All cross items.
    - **Fragment**: Scadu Fragments. *Includes enemy dropped ones.*
    - **Revered**: Revered Spirit Ashes.
    - **Spiritspring Stones**: Spiritspring Stone if spiritspring_stones is on.

options.label: Important at Priority Only
options.description:
Should important items be only at priority locations.

Creates extra locations at priority locations to contain all important items.
If there are no priority locations in the starting region one will be added.
Base: "LG/(SG): Finger Severer - beside grace"
DLC: "GP/TPC: Scadutree Fragment - by cross"

Generator likes to fail if there is to little priority locations, add more if it fails.

options.label: Important At Priority Early
options.description:
Needs Important at Priority Only On.
Does nothing if there are tons of Priority Locations.

Make extra generated locations appear more early game (Limgrave, Weeping, Liurnia, Stormveil and Raya Lucaria).
If starting in DLC (Gravesite, Belurat, Dragon Pit and Ensis).

1: Normal.
2+: Multiplied odds of early game locations.

Example: Setting this to 3 will make early locations 3 times more likely to have extra locations.

options.label: Other World Useful At Priority
options.description:
Should other worlds useful items place only at priority locations.
You probaly don't want this off, but also can cause gen fails due to lots of item rules.

options.label: Flask Upgrades at Priority
options.description: Should flask upgrades be randomized to important locations.

options.label: Whetblades at Priority
options.description: Should whetblades be randomized to important locations.

options.label: Scadutree Fragments at Priority
options.description: Should scadu fragments be randomized to important locations.

options.label: Talisman Pouches at Priority
options.description: Should talisman pouches be randomized to important locations.

options.label: Crystal Tears at Priority
options.description: Should Wondrous Physick tears be randomized to important locations.

options.label: Memory Stones at Priority
options.description: Should memory stones be randomized to important locations.

options.label: Remembrances at Priority
options.description: Should remembrances be randomized to important locations.

options.label: Local Item Only
options.description:
Which categories should be local only, useful and progression excluded.

- [Est Items] **Item Group**    *done on full game*
- [472] **Weapons**: All Weapons and Ammo.
- [423] **Armor**: All Armors.
- [160] **Accessories**: All Talismans.
- [105] **Ash of war**: All Ashes of War.
- [3250] **Goods**: The two below
- [1000] **Filler**: All Crafting Mats, and some craftables.
- [2200] **Non-Filler**: Below and Key Items which don't get made local.
  - [650] **Runes**: All Rune items.
  - [585] **Smithing Stones**: Smithing Stones and Somber Stones.
  - [220] **Spells**: Incantations and Sorceries.
  - [86] **Gloveworts**: Grave and Ghost Gloveworts.
  - [82] **Ashes**: Spirit Ashes.

*host.yaml can force categories local, by default Filler, Ash of war, Gloveworts and Ashes are forced local.*

options.label: Exclude Locations
options.description:
Prevent these locations from having an important item.
- **DLC**: If you want DLC items but dont wanna do DLC.
- **Hidden**: Hard to find locations.
- **Blizzard**: The hard to see area of snowfield.
- **Scarab**: Scarabs that drop items.
- **Furnace Golem**: DLC Furnace Golems.
- **Out of the Way**: Locations that take a bit to get.
- **Drop**: One time drop items from enemies.
- **Dungeon**: All locations in mini dungeons. *Caves, Catas, Tunnels, ect..*

- **Post Leyndell**: Used for great rune hunt, excludes everything after Leyndell. *-untested*

options.label: Excluded Locations Behavior
options.description:
How to choose items for excluded locations in ER.

- **Allow Useful:** Excluded locations can't have progression items, but they can have useful items.
- **Forbid Useful:** Neither progression items nor useful items can be placed in excluded locations.
- **Do Not Randomize:** Excluded locations always contain the same item as in vanilla.
- **Omit:** This location won't count as a check (if the item is filler) and contains the same item as in vanilla.

A "progression item" is anything that's required to unlock another location in some game.
A "useful item" is something each game defines individually, usually items that are quite
desirable but not strictly necessary.

options.label: Missable Locations Behavior
options.description:
Which items can be placed in locations that can be permanently missed.

- **Allow Useful:** Missable locations can't have progression items, but they can have useful items.
- **Forbid Useful:** Neither progression items nor useful items can be placed in missable locations.
- **Do Not Randomize:** Missable locations always contain the same item as in vanilla.
- **Omit:** This location won't count as a check (if the item is filler) and contains the same item as in vanilla.

A "progression item" is anything that's required to unlock another location in some game.
A "useful item" is something each game defines individually, usually items that are quite
desirable but not strictly necessary.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Goal required to complete the game.

space science: Research victory with 4 science packs: automation, logistic, chemical, space (red, green, blue, white).
any other planet science: (default) Research victory with 5 science packs: automation, logistic, chemical, space, and one of metallurgic, agricultural, or electromagnetic. If you start on another planet, then that science doesn't count.
aquilo orbit: Reach Aquilo orbit with a space platform. planet-discovery-aquilo is shuffled into the multiworld.
aquilo orbit 10 science: Reach Aquilo orbit after researching the unrandomized planet-discovery-aquilo, which requires 10 science packs (everything except cryogenic and promethium).
solar system edge: Reach the solar system edge with a space platform. stellar-discovery-solar-system-edge is shuffled into the multiworld.
solar system edge 11 science: Reach the solar system edge after researching the unrandomized stellar-discovery-solar-system-edge, which requires all 11 non-promethium science packs.

Note that technology_prerequisites adds extra steps to unlocking unrandomized technology locations related to the goal.

For shorter games, consider also setting production_and_utility_science: removed.

If starting_planet is aquilo_orbit, then goal: aquilo_orbit automatically gets extended to goal: solar_system_edge,
aquilo_orbit_10_science is extended to solar_system_edge_11_science,
and goal: space_science additionally requires cryogenic science pack from Aquilo's surface.
The space_technology_level option is ignored when starting_planet is aquilo_orbit.

options.label: Starting Planet
options.description:
Start on another planet.
To randomly select a planet, use advanced option randomization to specify weights.
Sometimes requires _CodeGreen's Any Planet Start mod: https://mods.factorio.com/mod/any-planet-start
Sometimes requires my Aquilo Orbit Start mod: https://mods.factorio.com/mod/aquilo-orbit-start

WARNING: starting on Gleba with enemies enabled is very difficult. See also pentapod_killers and gleba_coal.

WARNING: starting in Aquilo Orbit is a very different experience from the other options.
You may want to read the Aquilo Orbit Start mod's documentation before decciding to try it out.
See also aquilo_orbit_start_settings.
See also goal.

options.label: Allow Imported Blueprints
options.description: Allow blueprints imported from outside the current game.

options.label: World Gen
options.description:
buffed_resources: (the default value for this YAML option) All resource patches cranked to the max, cliffs disabled, oceans reduced, Fulgoran islands max size.
custom: use the map_exchange_string for most settings, but the seed is randomized. If world_gen_enemies is set to false, then that setting is applied as well.
custom_verbatim: use the map_exchange_string exactly as is.
default (or vanilla): The vanilla Default settings. (Not the default selection for this YAML option.)
rich_resources, marathon, death_world, etc.: The builtin presets of the same name.

options.label: World Gen Enemies
options.description:
Enable enemies. Turning this off checks the 'No enemies' mode during world gen and disables pollution.
Ignored when world_gen is set to custom_verbatim.

options.label: Technology Prerequisites
options.description:
Researching a technology location requires researching the prerequisite locations first,
the connections in the technology graph.
vanilla: Imitate the vanilla tech tree connections.
removed: No prerequisites. All technology locations can be researched simply by meeting the individual requirements.

Note that with prerequisites removed, the technology GUI lists all the trigger techs for planets you haven't visited yet
before the research techs that you're actually looking for, which can be a little annoying.
However, with prerequisites included, triggers can block large swaths of other techs, such as pumping oil and mining uranium.

options.label: Progressive Technologies
options.description:
Group technologies together as progressive item chains.
For example, there are 3 copies of 'progressive-speed-module' in the multiworld item pool,
the first one you receive gives the recipe for speed module 1, the second gives speed module 2, and so on.
See https://github.com/thejoshwolfe/Archipelago/blob/space-age/worlds/factorio_space_age/data/ap_data.py for the full definitions of these.

only_related: Technologies with similar names will be grouped together in a progress chain.
This requires several specific items to progress, such as oil-gathering, oil-processing, plastics, and advanced-circuit all as individual items.
large_groups: Loosely-related technologies will be grouped together with more critical recipes near the start and less critical bonuses near the end.
This allows many more ways to get critical technologies, for example 2/9+ progressive-oil and 2/9+ progressive-circuit to get the same set of recipes listed in the previous example.
Additional copies of progressive-circuit can be added to the pool with filler_processing_unit_productivity_weight, and similarly with other infinite technologies as filler items.

See also this community-maintained info sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/e/2PACX-1vQEF0W46I7aHX6mgmaiVfVMI_SWJIhQyNpzkelunmdCHO8VloBntOKRI1Hg7j0y-LwcOmiVbS-dLqba/pubhtml#gid=1921791348

options.label: Infinite Technologies
options.description:
How to handle infinitely researchable technologies, e.g. steel-plate-productivity.
vanilla: They are not randomized, e.g. research productivity always requires promethium science packs.
shuffled: The cost and prerequisites of the infinite techs are shuffled, e.g. research productivity might require only red, greend, blue, and purple science (the location of the steel-plate-productivity technology).
removed: Infinite technologies are removed.

options.label: Intermediate Technologies
options.description:
How to handle technologies that only unlock recipes for items that are not directly useful, e.g. advanced-circuit.

shuffled: the technologies are shuffled into the multiworld as items just like other technologies.
unlocked: (default) intermediate recipes are unlocked from the start and their technologies are removed. This makes multiworld items received more impactful and function less like fragments of something useable. For the full list of technologies unlocked by this option, see https://github.com/thejoshwolfe/Archipelago/blob/space-age/worlds/factorio_space_age/data/ap_data.py . You do not get free samples for the unlocked recipes.

Unlocking intermediates is recommended to enable Factorio: Space Age advancement keep pace with other games in the multiworld.
Particularly these milestones need fewer advancement items: chemical-science-pack (5 fewer), utility-science-pack (11 fewer), launching rockets (9 fewer).

Shuffling intermediates is recommended for a more authentic Factorio experience, but makes the early game much longer.

options.label: Production And Utility Science
options.description:
Should production and utility science (purple and yellow) be removed from the game?

included: (default)
removed: remove the production and utility science pack components from all research objectives. This allows smaller factories and quicker games. The crafting recipes for these science packs will never unlock.

options.label: Technology Tree Information
options.description:
How much information should be displayed in the tech tree.
None: No indication of what a research unlocks.
Advancement: Indicates if it's a logical advancement for the recipient.
Recipient: Reveals who the recipient is.
Recipient Advancement: Says both who it's for and whether it's an advancement.
Full: Reveals exact names and recipients of unlocked items; all researches are prefilled into the !hint command.

options.label: Quick Start
options.description:
Start with power armor, some personal bots, some bot speed upgrades,
and a chunk of materials to help get through the early game.

options.label: Skip Starting Trigger Techs
options.description:
Instead of needing to craft iron plates, copper plates, and a lab at the start of the run,
start with the recipes for steam power, labs, and automation science pack already unlocked.
The set of technologies changes with the starting_planet setting, and it's recommended particularly on Vulcanus and Gleba.
The free_samples setting gives items from the early triggers, so on Vulcanus, you can start with foundries straight away without setting up a lubricant build,
and on Gleba, you can start with biochambers without looting egg rafts.

options.label: Starting Items
options.description: Mapping of Factorio internal item-name to amount granted on start.

options.label: Free Samples
options.description:
Get free items with your recipe unlocks.
These are not considered by logic.

options.label: Free Samples Quality
options.description: If free samples are on, determine the quality of the granted items.

options.label: Free Sample Blacklist
options.description:
Recipes that when unlocked should never grant Free Samples of their products.
Fluids, barreling/unbarreling, and biter eggs are always excluded.

options.label: Tech Cost Divisor
options.description:
Reduce the cost of research technologies by dividing by this number.
1 = Vanilla. 10 = All technologies require 1/10th as much science.
This is applied before tech_cost_max_count, and does not apply to infinite technologies.

options.label: Tech Cost Max Count
options.description:
Cap the number of units a research technology can require. Vanilla technologies max out at 5000 (e.g. mech-armor).
This limit is applied after tech_cost_divisor, and does not apply to infinite technologies.
If a technology price multiplier is included in a map_exchange_string, that is applied last.
The order is: tech_cost_divisor -> tech_cost_max_count -> map_exchange_string.technology_price_multiplier

options.label: Space Technology Level
options.description:
WARNING: This option is in danger of getting deprecated. If you try it out and like it,
please advocate for its existence on Discord or here: https://github.com/thejoshwolfe/Archipelago/issues/39 .
Until then, I don't recommend changing this option from it's default: vanilla.

Downgrade space-related crafting ingredients to make space travel accessible earlier in the game:
vanilla               -> mid game         -> early game;
processing unit       -> advanced circuit -> electronic circuit;
low density structure -> plastic bar      -> copper plate;
rocket fuel           -> sulfur           -> coal;
electric engine unit  -> engine unit      -> iron gear wheel;
steel plate           -> steel plate      -> iron plate;
concrete              -> concrete         -> stone brick;

Changes apply to these recipes: rocket-silo, rocket-part, space-platform-foundation,
space-platform-starter-pack, cargo-landing-pad, cargo-bay, asteroid-collector, crusher,
thruster, chemical-plant, solar-panel.

If require_self_sufficient_space_platform is enabled and not starting on Vulcans, then electric-furnace will also be included in the list.
The early_game setting unlocks chemical plants as part of space-platform-thruster so you can melt ice and make fuel.

This setting also reduces small and medium asteroid health.

To get the most out of this option, you might be interested in these other changes:
  technology_prerequisites: removed
  progressive_technologies: only_related # TODO: make a better option for this mode.
  energy_link_recipe: early_game
And if you really want to go straight into space at the start of the multiworld:
  start_inventory_from_pool:
    rocket-silo: 1
    space-platform: 1
    advanced-material-processing-2: 1  # if you want furnaces in space
    space-platform-thruster: 1
    gun-turret: 1
    # One of these:
    solar-energy: 1
    ap-energy-link-bridge: 1

When starting_planet is set to vulcanus, gleba, or fulgora, then this option's behavior changes accordingly.
When starting_planet is set to aquilo_orbit, this option is ignored.

options.label: Vulcanus Rocks
options.description:
When starting on Vulcanus, multiply all drops from hand-mining rocks.
This is your only source of iron, copper, and stone until you make foundries (which are not randomized).
Hand-mined rocks are your only source of tungsten ore to make more foundries until big mining drills,
and until you can kill demolishers, if enabled.
Hand-mining rocks never satisfies the logical requirements for automating metallurgic science.

options.label: Gleba Coal
options.description:
When starting on Gleba, how should coal be acquired or obviated?
Coal is normally required for military science and may be used for defense against Gleba enemies.

vanilla: 20 spoilage -> 1 coal through burnt spoilage and carbon synthesis.
buffed_ratio: 1 spoilage -> 1 coal through burnt spoilage and carbon synthesis.
buffed_speed: burnt spoilage recipe sped up from 12s to 1s.
alternate_explosives: add alternate recipes for explosives and grenades to avoid the need for coal on Gleba.

options.label: Aquilo Orbit Start Settings
options.description:
Balance settings for the aquilo-orbit-start mod.
Ignored when starting_planet is not aquilo_orbit.

The default values for this Archipelago randomizer buff the "sky block" recipes by 5x relative to the aquilo-orbit-start mod's own default settings.
This is recommended to help Factorio: Spage Age players get advacement items at the pace generally expected in Archipelago.

The settings for aquilo-orbit-start not listed here are locked to their easier settings for technical logic-related reasons.

options.label: Require Electric Mining Drill
options.description:
Logically require electric mining drills for logistic science pack automation (green science).
Otherwise, you may need to use burner mining drills for automation until Vulcanus or uranium is required.

When starting_planet is aquilo_orbit, the requirement is for agricultural and electromagnetic sciences instead.

options.label: Require Logistics
options.description: Logically require underground belts and splitters for logistic science pack automation (green science).

options.label: Require Self Sufficient Space Platform
options.description:
Logically require either electric furnaces or both foundries and advanced asteroid processing for space science pack automation and for traveling space.
Otherwise, you may need to supply space platforms with metal plates shipped up via rocket.

options.label: Require Ice Melting
options.description:
Logically require ice melting for traveling space.
Otherwise, you may need to supply space platforms with water barrels shipped up via rocket.

options.label: Require Gun Turret
options.description:
Logically require gun turrets for destroying medium asteroids.
Otherwise, you may need to use walls and speed regulation to survive space travel.
(Large and huge asteroids always logically require rocket turrets and railgun turrets respectively.)

options.label: Require Gun Turret Upgrades
options.description:
When require_gun_turret is enabled, how many levels of weapon-shooting-speed and physical-projectile-damage
should also be logically required for destroying medium asteroids?

easy: (default) 6 damage, 6 speed.
medium: 4 damage, 4 speed.
hard: 2 damage, 2 speed.
none: no logically required bonuses.

When space_technology_level is mid_game or early_game,
These numbers are reduced by 1/2 or 1/4 (rounded down) respectively,
because that option also reduces asteroid HP.

options.label: Require Lightning Rod
options.description:
Logically require lightning rods for setting up mining drills on Fulgora.
Otherwise, you may need to solve the lightning problem some other way.
NOTE: This option does nothing, because the requirements for landing on Fulgora include all the requirements for crafting lightning rods.

options.label: Require Medium Electric Pole
options.description:
Logically require medium electric poles for automating metallurgic and electromagnetic science packs.
Otherwise, you may need to ship in wood to make electric poles.

options.label: Require Gleba For Spoilage
options.description:
Logically require Gleba for access to spoilage.
Otherwise, you may need to wait >2 hours (configurable) for fish to spoil on Nauvis to get nutrient-triggered technology.

options.label: Require Seed Disposal
options.description: Logically require either heating towers or recyclers to automate agricultural science pack.

options.label: Require Dark Power
options.description:
Logically require nuclear power to reach Aquilo.
Otherwise, you may need to rely on poorly performing solar panels in dark space.

options.label: Require Fast Inserter
options.description: Logically require fast inserters to automate advanced circuits.

options.label: Require Assembling Machine 2
options.description: Logically require assembling machine 2 to automate advanced circuits.

options.label: Require Fluid Handling
options.description: Logically require pumps and storage tanks for advanced oil processing.

options.label: Require Construction Robots
options.description: Logically require construction robots before automating production or utility science (purple/yellow) or traveling to another planet.

options.label: Require Logistic Robots
options.description: Logically require requester chests and logistic robots before traveling to another planet.

options.label: Require Asteroid Processing
options.description: Logically require asteroid reprocessing and advanced asteroid processing to reach Aquilo.

options.label: Require Heating Tower
options.description:
Logically require heating towers to heat buildings on Aquilo.
Otherwise, you may need to ship in nuclear fuel cells.

options.label: Demolisher Killers
options.description:
What should the logic consider viable methods for killing small demolishers?
When enemies are enabled (according to `world_gen_enemies` and/or `map_exchange_string`),
killing small demolishers is logically required for automating tungsten ore.
WARNING: military bonuses for damage, weapon speed, etc. are not considered by the logic.

options.label: Pentapod Killers
options.description:
What should the logic consider viable methods for killing Gleba enemies and defending your base against their attacks?
When enemies are enabled (according to `world_gen_enemies` and/or `map_exchange_string`),
killing Gleba enemies is logically required for automating agricultural science,
and if starting on Gelba, also required for automating chemical science.
WARNING: military bonuses for damage, weapon speed, etc. are not considered by the logic.

For backward compatibility with apworld versions prior to 2.2.0, "land mine" is accepted as an alias for "land mine and construction robot".

options.label: Energy Link
options.description:
Allow sending and receiving energy to/from a shared pool in the multiworld.
The Archipelago EnergyLink Bridge item is craftable in-game and functions like an accumulator for sending and receiving energy.
25% of the energy is lost during sending.

All EnergyLink-enabled games in the multiworld use the same pool.
Unit conversions between Factorio (Joules), Mega Man (HP), Roller Coaster Tycoon (USD),
Donkey Kong Country (Bananas), etc. is left to the apworld developers.

EnergyLink can also be used to transport energy between planets in Factorio: Space Age or to/from space platforms.

options.label: Energy Link Recipe
options.description:
The recipe to craft an Archipelago EnergyLink Bridge.
early game: Made from iron plates and copper plates.
mid game: Made from accumulator and radar (requires oil, acid, and battery).
fulgora: Made from supercapacitor and radar.

options.label: Energy Link Technology
options.description:
Should the Archipelago EnergyLink Bridge recipe be unlocked by a technology, which is an item in the multiworld?
Note that this interacts with the free samples option.

options.label: Require Energy Link
options.description:
Logically require Archipelago EnergyLink Bridges for the following, depending on the setting of energy_link_recipe:
early_game: logistic science pack automation (green science).
mid_game: chemical science pack automation (blue science).
fulgora: electromagnetic science pack automation.

options.label: Energy Link Satisfies Requirements
options.description:
Allow Archipelago EnergyLink Bridges to satisfy the logical requirement for generating power in space, including in dark space.
This may make solar panels unnecessary.

options.label: Filler Count
options.description:
How many filler items should there be?
The actual number of filler items may be higher than the number specified for various reasons.

The settings below can be used to specify the weighted chance that filler items are helpful, harmful, or nothing.

New locations, if needed, are generated by creating copies of random existing (finite, non-trigger) research objectives.

With progressive_technologies: large_groups, many of the filler items configurable below will provide meaningful advancement.

options.label: Filler Nothing Weight
options.description:
Weighted chance that a filler item does literally nothing.
The name of a nothing item is chosen randomly from: laser, flammables, modules.

options.label: Filler Artillery Shell Damage Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is progressive-artillery-shell-damage

options.label: Filler Artillery Shell Range Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is progressive-artillery-shell-range

options.label: Filler Artillery Shell Speed Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is progressive-artillery-shell-speed

options.label: Filler Asteroid Productivity Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is progressive-asteroid-productivity

options.label: Filler Electric Weapons Damage Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is progressive-electric-weapons-damage

options.label: Filler Follower Robot Count Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is progressive-follower-robot-count

options.label: Filler Health Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is progressive-health

options.label: Filler Laser Weapons Damage Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is progressive-laser-weapons-damage

options.label: Filler Low Density Structure Productivity Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is progressive-low-density-structure-productivity

options.label: Filler Mining Productivity Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is progressive-mining-productivity

options.label: Filler Physical Projectile Damage Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is progressive-physical-projectile-damage

options.label: Filler Plastic Bar Productivity Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is progressive-plastic-bar-productivity

options.label: Filler Processing Unit Productivity Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is progressive-processing-unit-productivity

options.label: Filler Railgun Damage Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is progressive-railgun-damage

options.label: Filler Railgun Shooting Speed Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is progressive-railgun-shooting-speed

options.label: Filler Refined Flammables Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is progressive-refined-flammables

options.label: Filler Research Productivity Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is progressive-research-productivity

options.label: Filler Rocket Fuel Productivity Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is progressive-rocket-fuel-productivity

options.label: Filler Rocket Part Productivity Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is progressive-rocket-part-productivity

options.label: Filler Scrap Recycling Productivity Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is progressive-scrap-recycling-productivity

options.label: Filler Steel Plate Productivity Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is progressive-steel-plate-productivity

options.label: Filler Stronger Explosives Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is progressive-stronger-explosives

options.label: Filler Worker Robots Speed Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is progressive-worker-robots-speed

options.label: Teleport Trap Weight
options.description:
DEPRECATED: this option has been removed due to bugs.
See https://github.com/thejoshwolfe/Archipelago/issues/18 if you'd like to contribute a fix so that it can be re-enabled.

options.label: Grenade Trap Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is a trap that when received triggers a grenade explosion on each player.

options.label: Cluster Grenade Trap Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is a trap that when received triggers a cluster grenade explosion on each player.

options.label: Artillery Trap Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is a trap that when received triggers an artillery shell on each player.

options.label: Atomic Rocket Trap Weight
options.description:
Weighted chance that a filler item is a trap that when received triggers an atomic rocket explosion on each player.
Warning: there is no warning. The launch is instantaneous.

options.label: Atomic Cliff Remover Trap Weight
options.description:
Weighted chance that a filler item is a trap that when received triggers an atomic rocket explosion on a random cliff.
Warning: there is no warning. The launch is instantaneous.

options.label: Inventory Spill Trap Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is a trap that when received triggers dropping your main inventory and trash inventory onto the ground.

options.label: Attack Trap Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is a trap that when received triggers an attack on your base.

options.label: Evolution Trap Weight
options.description: Weighted chance that a filler item is a trap that when received increase the enemy evolution.

options.label: Evolution Trap % Effect
options.description:
How much an Evolution Trap increases the enemy evolution.
Increases scale down proportionally to the session's current evolution factor
(40 increase at 0.50 will add 0.20... 40 increase at 0.75 will add 0.10...)

options.label: Logic
options.description:
Affects where items are allowed to be placed.

**Normal:** Playable without using any tricks or glitches. Can require
knowledge from a vanilla playthrough, such as how to open Color Dungeon.

**Hard:** More advanced techniques may be required, but glitches are not.
Examples include tricky jumps, killing enemies with only pots.

**Glitched:** Advanced glitches and techniques may be required, but
extremely difficult or tedious tricks are not required. Examples include
Bomb Triggers, Super Jumps and Jesus Jumps.

**Hell:** Obscure knowledge and hard techniques may be required. Examples
include featherless jumping with boots and/or hookshot, sequential pit
buffers and unclipped superjumps. Things in here can be extremely hard to do
or very time consuming.

options.label: Trade Quest
options.description:
Trade quest items are randomized. Each NPC takes its normal trade quest
item and gives a randomized item in return.

options.label: Rooster
options.description:
Adds the rooster to the item pool. If disabled, the overworld will be
modified so that any location requiring the rooster is accessible by other
means.

options.label: Entrance Rules
options.description:
Sets how doors work when shuffled.

**Normal:** Doors function normally.

**Wild:** Connections can go from overworld to overworld, or inside to inside.

**Chaos:** Entrances and exits are decoupled.

**Insane:** Combines chaos and wild.

**Madness:** Insane, but multiple entrances can lead to the same location.

This does nothing unless other settings are enabled to select entrances to shuffle.

options.label: Random Start Location
options.description:
Randomizes where your starting house is located.

**Limited:** Your start location will be selected from a curated list of overworld locations.

**Global:** Your start location is shuffled into the global entrance pool.

options.label: Shuffle Dungeons
options.description:
Randomizes where dungeon entrances lead to.

**Limited:** They are shuffled with each other.

**Global:** They are shuffled into the global entrance pool.

options.label: Shuffle Basic
options.description:
Randomizes where caves/houses with one entrance and an item lead to.

**Limited:** They are shuffled with each other.

**Global:** They are shuffled into the global entrance pool.

options.label: Shuffle Junk
options.description:
Randomizes where caves/houses with one entrance and no items lead to.

**Limited:** They are shuffled with each other.

**Global:** They are shuffled into the global entrance pool.

options.label: Shuffle Connectors
options.description:
Randomizes where caves/houses with two entrances lead to.

**Limited:** They are shuffled with each other.

**Global:** They are shuffled into the global entrance pool.

options.label: Shuffle Water
options.description:
Randomizes water entrances lead to (Manbo and Damp Cave).

**Limited:** They are shuffled with each other.

**Global:** They are shuffled into the global entrance pool.

Use the warp-to-home from the Save & Quit menu if you get stuck (hold A+B+Start+Select until it works).

options.label: Shuffle Annoying
options.description:
Randomizes where a few very annoying entrances lead to (Mamu and the Raft House). 

**Limited:** They are shuffled with each other.

**Global:** They are shuffled into the global entrance pool.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
The Goal of the game.

**Instruments:** The Wind Fish's Egg will only open if you have the required
number of Instruments of the Sirens, and play the Ballad of the Wind Fish.

**Seashells:** The Egg will open when you bring 20 seashells. The Ballad and
Ocarina are not needed.

**Open:** The Egg will start pre-opened.

    **Specific:** The Wind Fish's Egg will open with specific instruments, check the sign at the egg to see which.

options.label: Instrument Count
options.description: Sets the number of instruments required to open the Egg.

options.label: Link's Palette
options.description:
Sets Link's palette.

A-D are color palettes usually used during the damage animation and can
change based on where you are.

options.label: Warps
options.description:
**Improved:** Adds remake style warp screen to the game. Choose your warp
destination on the map after jumping in a portal and press *B* to select.

**Improved Additional:** Improved warps, and adds a warp point at Crazy
Tracy's house (the Mambo teleport spot) and Eagle's Tower.

options.label: Trendy Game
options.description:
**Easy:** All of the items hold still for you.

**Normal:** The vanilla behavior.

**Hard:** The trade item also moves.

**Harder:** The items move faster.

**Hardest:** The items move diagonally.

**Impossible:** The items move impossibly fast, may scroll on and off the
screen.

options.label: Palette
options.description:
Sets the palette for the game.

Note: A few places aren't patched, such as the menu and a few color dungeon
tiles.

**Normal:** The vanilla palette.

**1-Bit:** One bit of color per channel.

**2-Bit:** Two bits of color per channel.

**Greyscale:** Shades of grey.

**Pink:** Aesthetic.

**Inverted:** Inverted.

options.label: Foreign Item Icons
options.description:
Choose how to display foreign items.

**Guess By Name:** Foreign items can look like any Link's Awakening item.

**Indicate Progression:** Foreign items are either a Piece of Power
(progression) or Guardian Acorn (non-progression).

options.label: Shuffle Nightmare Keys
options.description:
**Original Dungeon:** The item will be within its original dungeon.

**Own Dungeons:** The item will be within a dungeon in your world.

**Own World:** The item will be somewhere in your world.

**Any World:** The item could be anywhere.

**Different World:** The item will be somewhere in another world.

options.label: Shuffle Small Keys
options.description:
**Original Dungeon:** The item will be within its original dungeon.

**Own Dungeons:** The item will be within a dungeon in your world.

**Own World:** The item will be somewhere in your world.

**Any World:** The item could be anywhere.

**Different World:** The item will be somewhere in another world.

options.label: Shuffle Maps
options.description:
**Original Dungeon:** The item will be within its original dungeon.

**Own Dungeons:** The item will be within a dungeon in your world.

**Own World:** The item will be somewhere in your world.

**Any World:** The item could be anywhere.

**Different World:** The item will be somewhere in another world.

options.label: Shuffle Compasses
options.description:
**Original Dungeon:** The item will be within its original dungeon.

**Own Dungeons:** The item will be within a dungeon in your world.

**Own World:** The item will be somewhere in your world.

**Any World:** The item could be anywhere.

**Different World:** The item will be somewhere in another world.

options.label: Shuffle Stone Beaks
options.description:
**Original Dungeon:** The item will be within its original dungeon.

**Own Dungeons:** The item will be within a dungeon in your world.

**Own World:** The item will be somewhere in your world.

**Any World:** The item could be anywhere.

**Different World:** The item will be somewhere in another world.

options.label: Music
options.description:
**Vanilla:** Regular Music

**Shuffled:** Shuffled Music

**Off:** No music

options.label: Shuffle Instruments
options.description:
**Original Dungeon:** The item will be within its original dungeon.

**Own Dungeons:** The item will be within a dungeon in your world.

**Own World:** The item will be somewhere in your world.

**Any World:** The item could be anywhere.

**Different World:** The item will be somewhere in another world.

**Vanilla:** The item will be in its vanilla location in your world.

options.label: Music Change Condition
options.description:
Controls how the music changes.

**Sword:** When you pick up a sword, the music changes.

**Always:** You always have the post-sword music.

options.label: AP Title Screen
options.description: Enables AP specific title screen and disables the intro cutscene.

options.label: Boots Controls
options.description:
Adds an additional button to activate Pegasus Boots (does nothing if you
haven't picked up your boots!)

**Vanilla:** Nothing changes, you have to equip the boots to use them.

**Bracelet:** Holding down the button for the bracelet also activates boots
(somewhat like Link to the Past).

**Press A:** Holding down A activates boots.

**Press B:** Holding down B activates boots.

options.label: Stealing
options.description: Puts stealing from the shop in logic if the player has a sword.

options.label: Quickswap
options.description: Instead of opening the map, the *SELECT* button swaps the top item of your inventory on to your *A* or *B* button.

options.label: Hard Mode
options.description:
**Oracle:** Less iframes and health from drops. Bombs damage yourself. Water
damages you without flippers. No pieces of power or acorns.

**Hero:** Switch version hero mode, double damage, no heart/fairy drops.

**OHKO:** You die on a single hit, always.

options.label: Low HP Beep
options.description: Slows or disables the low health beeping sound.

options.label: Text Mode
options.description: **Fast:** Makes text appear twice as fast.

options.label: No Flash
options.description:
Remove the flashing light effects from Mamu, shopkeeper and MadBatter.
Useful for capture cards and people that are sensitive to these things.

options.label: In-Game Hint Count
options.description:
Determines how many owl statues and library books will indicate the location
of your items in the multiworld. All others will give junk hints that reveal
nothing.

There are:
- 10 overworld owl statues
- 21 dungeon owl statues
- 7 hint books in the library

options.label: In-Game Hint Excluded Items
options.description: Indicated items will not be used for in-game hints.

options.label: In-Game Hint Priority Items
options.description: Indicated items will be prioritized for in-game hints.

options.label: Overworld
options.description:
**Open Mabe:** Replaces rock on the east side of Mabe Village with bushes,
allowing access to Ukuku Prairie without Power Bracelet.

options.label: More Filler
options.description: Removes some rupees from the vanilla item pool to make more room for filler.

options.label: Filler Pool
options.description: Sets which items can be added to the item pool to replace removed items.

options.label: Expand Start
options.description:
Starting from Tarin's Gift, locally place progression items until the target
number of locations or more can be reached. Does nothing if set to *1*.
When set to *2* it will only ever place an item on Tarin's Gift.
May interfere with plando.

options.label: Follower
options.description: Gives you a pet follower in the game.

options.label: Entrance Plando
options.description: Define some or all entrance connections.

options.label: Entrance Shuffle Seed
options.description:
Specify seed number for entrance shuffle.
Everybody with the same seed will get the same entrance shuffle result
as long as their entrance shuffle and logic settings are the same.
At zero, no seed is used.

options.label: Goal Condition
options.description:
Your Goal Condition for your game

ender_dragon - Goal when the Ender Dragon is defeated
wither - Goal when the Wither is defeated
both_bosses - Goal when the Ender Dragon and Wither is defeated
advancements_only - Goal when you collect a certain amount of Advancements and/or Items
ruby_hunt - Goal when a certain amount of rubies are collected (McGuffin hunt)

options.label: Advancements to Goal
options.description:
Determines the number of advancements needed in order to beat the game! These Advancements are required for goaling
in addition to your regular goal. If this is set to zero, no advancements will be required to goal.

If fewer available advancements exist than this number, the number of available advancements will be used instead.

options.label: Excluded Locations
options.description:
Determines Blacklisted Locations in the Randomizer
If a Location Category is given here, Checks won't appear in locations categorized under it

This Wiki Page details all locations that're blacklisted via these settings:
https://modded.wiki/w/Fabric_Archipelago_Mod:Optional_Locations

Options:
    "Hard" - Disables Locations that're Hard
    "Exploration" - Disables Locations that might require Exploration
    "Unreasonable" - Disables Location's that're EXTREMELY Hard

options.label: Ruby Percentage Needed
options.description:
The Percentage of Rubies that need to be collected to Goal for Ruby Hunt.
(Only Takes Effect when going for the Ruby Hunt Goal)

options.label: Total Rubies In Game
options.description:
Maximum possible number of Rubies that will be in the item pool

If fewer available locations exist in the pool than this number, the number of available locations will be used instead.

Required Percentage of Rubies will be calculated based off of that number.

(Only Takes Effect when going for the Ruby Hunt Goal)

options.label: Itemsanity
options.description: Enables "Itemsanity" which causes items obtainable in Survival to be checks

options.label: Items to Goal
options.description:
Determines the number of Items needed in order to beat the game! You will need to gather this many unique items in
addition to your regular goal. If this is set to zero, no items will be required to goal.

If fewer available items exist than this number, the number of available items will be used instead.

This Option only takes effect if Itemsanity is enabled, it is highly recommended to set this number high (~200) in
order to prevent fast goals

options.label: Itemsanity Local Fill
options.description:
The Percentage of Itemsanity Checks that should only contain items from your world
(Highly recommend setting this to a high value to prevent everyone's items from being in your game)

options.label: Excluded From Itemsanity
options.description:
Determines certain Items that shouldn't appear in Itemsanity
Useful for blacklisting tedious items, or cutting down the amount of Itemsanity checks in a game

Options:
    Discs - Music Discs
    Dyed Items - Items that are Dyed (Concretes, Wools, Terracottas, etc.)
    Flowers - Flowers (all flowers except Wither Rose)
    Rare Ores - Ores that are extremely rare (such as Deepslate Emerald)
    Mob Heads - Mob Heads that're only dropped from Charged Creeper Explosions
    Netherite Gear - Netherite Tools, Armor, and Netherite Smithing Template
    Trims - Smithing Templates that're used for Trims (Doesn't include Upgrade Templates)
    Sherds - Pottery Sherds
    Slabs - Slabs (such as Oak Slabs, Stone Slabs, etc.)
    Stairs - Stairs (such as Oak Stairs, Stone Stairs, etc.)
    Walls - Walls, Fences, and Fence Gates (Oak Fence, Stone Wall, etc.)

options.label: Empty Fill Percentage
options.description:
Replaces a certain amount of Non-Trap Junk Items with Items that do nothing.
This option is primarily for preventing massive amounts of inventory clutter when Itemsanity is Enabled

options.label: Required Before Nether
options.description:
Makes it so certain Items are required in Logic before Nether Access

Used to help make the Randomizer Easier or Harder

Available Items
    "Iron Weapons"
    "Iron Armor"
    "Bow"
    "Jump"
    "Sprint"
    "Beds"

options.label: Required Before Wither or Dragon
options.description:
Makes it so certain Items are required in Logic before you need
to fight the Ender Dragon or Wither

Used to help make the Randomizer Easier or Harder

Available Items
    "Iron Weapons"
    "Iron Armor"
    "Bow"
    "Jump"
    "Sprint"
    "Beds"

options.label: Required Before Raids
options.description:
Makes it so certain Items are required in Logic before you need
to fight a Raid

Used to help make the Randomizer Easier or Harder

Available Items
    "Iron Weapons"
    "Iron Armor"
    "Bow"
    "Jump"
    "Sprint"
    "Beds"

options.label: Keep Inventory
options.description: Prevents you from dropping your items when you die!

options.label: Ability Shuffle
options.description:
Determines which abilities and items will be added as items in the item pool
If an ability is not present in the list they will be treated as unlocked from the start

Some abilities (such as Jump) don't gate any content, and are meant mainly for the challenge

Lockable Abilities:
    "Chests" - Removes the ability to craft and use chests (and similar storage containers), and adds Chests to the Item pool.
    "Jump" - Removes the ability to jump, and adds Jumping to the Item pool.
    "Sprint" - Removes the ability to run, and adds Sprint to the Item pool.
    "Swim" - Removes the ability to enter water, and adds Swim to the Item pool.

options.label: Time Saving Options
options.description:
Decrease Wait times or Increase likelihood for various events that can occur in the game

Options:
    "Wither Skulls" - Increases the 2.5% Chance for Wither Skulls to drop to 50%
    "Rabbits Foot" - Increases the 10% Chance for Rabbit's Foot to drop to 50%
    "Drowned Items" - Increases the Chance for a Drowned to drop the items they're holding to 100%
    "Copper Oxidation" - Increases the Chance for Copper Blocks to attempt to Oxidize from 5% to 55%

options.label: Logic Difficulty Options
options.description:
Changes the logical requirements of certain locations to make progression easier

Options:
    "Natures Compass Logic" - Locks exploration checks that depend on rare biomes behind the ability
    to locate that biome with Nature's Compass (Requires Nature's Compass Mod)
    "Explorers Compass Logic" - Locks exploration checks that depend on rare structures behind the ability
    to locate that structure with Explorer's Compass (Requires Explorer's Compass Mod)
    "Movement Before Exploration" - Requires Jump, Sprint, Swim for checks that require exploration
    "Sleeping Before Exploration" - Requires Sleeping for checks that require exploration
    "Meteorology" - Requires the Totem of Meteorology (a custom item that allows manual weather setting) for
    checks that require thunder

options.label: Trap Fill Percentage
options.description: Replace a percentage of junk items in the item pool with random traps

options.label: Reverse Controls Trap Weight
options.description: Likelihood of a receiving a trap which causes WASD, Shift, Jump, Break, and Place to Swap for a short duration

options.label: Inverted Mouse Trap Weight
options.description: Likelihood of a receiving a trap which causes the Mouse to Invert for a short duration

options.label: Ice Trap Weight
options.description: Likelihood of a receiving a trap which causes all blocks to become slippery for a short duration

options.label: Random Status Effect Trap Weight
options.description: Likelihood of a receiving a trap which applies a random Negative Status Effect

options.label: Stun Trap Weight
options.description: Likelihood of a receiving a trap that temporarily stops movement of the player

options.label: TNT Trap Weight
options.description: Likelihood of a receiving a trap that spawns a block of lit TNT on the player's position

options.label: Teleport Trap Weight
options.description: Likelihood of a receiving a trap that Teleports the player similar to Chorus Fruit

options.label: Bee Trap Weight
options.description: Likelihood of a receiving a trap that Spawns 6 angry bees near the player

options.label: Literature Trap Weight
options.description: Likelihood of a receiving a trap that Opens Literature Pop-Ups

options.label: DeathLink
options.description: Enable DeathLink

options.label: TrapLink
options.description: Enable TrapLink

options.label: Enabled Mods
options.description:
WARNING: Fabric Archipelago's Mod support is still in a very early stage, so do keep in mind that playing with mods can lead to unbeatable games!

This option allows other mods to be integrated into the randomizer if they are supported.
You can add a mod by putting its Mod ID here.

For a list of supported Mods, refer to here: https://modded.wiki/w/Fabric_Archipelago_Mod:Mod_Support

options.label: Goal Condition
options.description:
Your Goal Condition for your game

ender_dragon - Goal when the Ender Dragon (Tethlaen) is defeated
closure - Goal when entering the Drehmal credits room
tower_hunt - Goal when Terminus Tower completion reaches a certain percentage

options.label: Tower Percentage Needed
options.description:
The Percentage of Towers that need to be collected to Goal for Tower Hunt.
(Only Takes Effect when going for the Tower Hunt Goal)

options.label: Excluded Locations
options.description:
Determines Blacklisted advancements in the Randomizer

Options:
    "Normal" - Disables regular advancements
    "Hard" - Disables advancements that are hard or tedious
    "Exploration" - Disables advancements that are given for discovering a location
    "Unreasonable" - Disables advancements that are EXTREMELY hard or tedious

options.label: Ability Shuffle
options.description:
Determines which abilities and recipes/interactions will be added as items in the item pool
If an ability is not present in the list they will be treated as unlocked from the start

Valid options: "Chests", "Jump", "Sprint", "Swim", "Spawn_Point", "Wither_Summoning", "Trading",
"Bartering", "Brewing", "Enchanting", "Smithing", "Misc_Stations", "Bucket", "Igniter", 
"Minecarts", "Brush", "Spyglass", "Shears", "Ender_Eye", "Fishing", "Bottles", "Compacting",
"Shield", "Bundles", "TNT", "Tools", "Weapons", "Archery", "Armor", "Smelting", "Dyes"

options.label: Randomize Mythicals
options.description: Adds Drehmal's Mythical weapons to the item and location pool.

options.label: Randomize Legendaries
options.description: Adds Drehmal's Legendary items to the item and location pool.

options.label: Randomize Terminus Towers
options.description:
Adds Drehmal's fast travel Terminus towers to the item and location pool. 
If option region_locks is selected, you will not be able to enter a region until you have obtained its corresponding Terminus tower.
(Capital Valley tower will always be unlocked to prevent softlocks.)

options.label: Randomize Quest Items
options.description:
Adds miscellaneous quest items from Drehmal to the item and location pool.
Fervor Stones, Frenzy Fragments, Left and Right Blade Fragments, 
Nihilist's Notes, Yavhlix Overrides, Foundry Levers

options.label: Randomize Relics
options.description: Adds all four stages of each of the 11 relics to the item and location pool.

options.label: Automatic Scouting
options.description:
Automatically sends hints for tedious locations, including devotion relics,
items locked behind clearing the Foundry, and boss rewards

options.label: Trap Fill Percentage
options.description: Replace a percentage of junk items in the item pool with random traps

options.description: Likelihood of a receiving a trap which causes WASD, Shift, Jump, Break, and Place to Swap for a short duration

options.label: Random Status Effect Trap Weight
options.description: Likelihood of a receiving a trap which applies a random Negative Status Effect

options.label: Stun Trap Weight
options.description: Likelihood of a receiving a trap that temporarily stops movement of the player

options.label: TNT Trap Weight
options.description: Likelihood of a receiving a trap that spawns a block of lit TNT on the player's position

options.label: Teleport Trap Weight
options.description: Likelihood of a receiving a trap that repeatedly teleports the player similar to Chorus Fruit

options.label: Bee Trap Weight
options.description: Likelihood of a receiving a trap that Spawns 6 angry bees near the player

options.label: Literature Trap Weight
options.description: Likelihood of a receiving a trap that Opens Literature Pop-Ups

options.label: Music Randomizer
options.description: Enable Music Randomizer

options.label: Starting Money
options.description: Amount of money to start with

options.label: Species Unlocked
options.description: Number of species unlocked at start

options.label: Barriers Unlocked
options.description: What barrier level should be start with

options.label: Filler Cash Amount
options.description: How much money per Medium Cash inject amounts: Small will half value, Large will double

options.label: Filler Conservation Amount
options.description: How much money per Medium Conservation point inject amounts: Small will half value, Large will double

options.label: Objective
options.description:
**Kill the Creator:** Get to the final boss (the Creator) and beat all it's forms.

**Obtain secrets and kill the Creator:** like the "Kill the Creator", but need to find all three secret memories
before getting to the Creator.

**Killing the four gods:**, Beat all four enemy gods ("Fallen God", "Mithalan God", "Drunian God", "Lumerean God").

**Gods and Creator:** like "Killing the four gods" but you also have to beat the creator.

choices.label: Obtain Secrets And Kill The Creator

options.label: Minibosses to beat
options.description:
The number of minibosses to beat before having access to the goal.

The minibosses are "Nautilus Prime", "Blaster Peg Prime", "Mergog", "Mithalan priests", "Octopus Prime",
"Crabbius Maximus", "Mantis Shrimp Prime" and "King Jellyfish God Prime".

Note that the "Energy Statue" and "Simon Says" are not minibosses.

Also note that if the objective is "killing the four enemy gods" or "Gods and creator", it might be needed to go in the abyss and
bubble cave to kill "King Jellyfish God Prime" and "Mantis Shrimp Prime".

options.label: Big bosses to beat
options.description:
The number of big bosses to beat before having access to the creator (the final boss).

The big bosses are "Fallen God", "Mithalan God", "Drunian God", "Lumerean God" and "The Golem".

Has no effect if the objective is "killing the four gods" or "Gods and Creator".

options.label: Turtle Randomizer
options.description:
Randomize the transportation turtle.

If the objective is "killing the four gods" or "Gods and Creator", the abyss and body turtle will not be randomized.

options.label: Early Energy form
options.description:
Force the Energy form to be in a location early in the multiworld (or directly in your world if Early and Local is
selected).

options.label: Early Bind song
options.description:
Force the Bind song to be in a location early in the multiworld (or directly in your world if Early and Local is
selected).

options.label: Light needed to get to dark places
options.description:
Make sure that the sun form or the dumbo pet can be acquired before getting to dark places.

Be aware that navigating in dark places without light is extremely difficult.

You can also force the sun form to be accessible by using the "sun form" option.

options.label: Bind song needed to get sing bulbs under rocks
options.description: Make sure that the bind song can be acquired before having to obtain sing bulbs under rocks.

options.label: Unconfine Home Waters Area
options.description:
Open the way out of the Home Waters area so that Naija can go to open water and beyond without the bind song.

**Via energy door:** Open the energy door between the home waters and the open waters

**Via transturtle:** Remove the rock blocking the home water transturtle.

Note that if you turn this option off, it is recommended to turn on the Early Energy form and Early Bind Song
options.

options.label: Randomize Ingredients
options.description:
Select if the simple ingredients (that do not have a recipe) should be randomized.

If "Common Ingredients" is selected, the randomization will exclude the "Red Bulb", "Special Bulb" and "Rukh Egg".

options.label: Dish Randomizer
options.description: Randomize the drop of Dishes (Ingredients with recipe).

options.label: Translate Aquarian
options.description: Translate the Aquarian scripture in the game into English.

options.label: Skip Naija's first vision
options.description: Skip the first vision in the game, where Naija transforms into Energy Form and gets flooded by enemies.

options.label: Hide the goal's requirements
options.description:
Hide the goal's requirements from the help page so that you don't know what is needed to goal.

Note that when you get to the final boss door (or you beat the last gods when the "Killing the four gods"
is selected) you can then see the requirements in the help page.

options.label: Infinite Hot Soup
options.description:
As soon as a "hot soup" is received, the user will never run out of this dish.

This option is recommended if using Ingredient randomization since "hot soup" ingredients may become hard to get
and the "hot soup" is necessary to get to some locations.

options.label: Maximum ingredient amount
options.description: The maximum number of the same ingredients that can be stacked on the ingredient inventory.

options.label: Skip final boss third form
options.description:
The Final boss third form (the hide and seek form) can be easy and quite long. So, this option can be used
to skip this form.

Note that you will still need to deliver the final blow to the 3rd form in order to activate the 4th form animation.

options.label: Save heal Naija
options.description:
When you save, Naija is healed back to full health. If disabled, saving won't heal Naija.

Note that Naija can still heal by sleeping in some beds in the game (including in her home).

options.label: Throne as a location
options.description:
If enabled, sitting on the Mithalas City Castle throne (with the seal on it) will be a location and opening the
door to the Mithalas Cathedral will be an item.

options.label: Golem as a location
options.description:
If enabled, beating the golem in Sunken City will be a location and opening the
body's tongue will be an item.

options.label: Enable traps
options.description: If enabled, trap may be added in the item pool.

options.label: Progressive Recipes
options.description:
If enabled, the recipe will be learned progressively.
For example, hen you learn a soup, you will always learn the hot soup first, then the hearty soup, etc.

options.label: Far away sing bulb
Use Fish Form to go around rocks
options.description:
Using Fish Form, you can sometime go around rocks.

Easier place to go around rocks with Fish Form are:
"Home Waters, rock to access the Transportation turtle",
"Home Waters, rock to access the bottom left path",
"Home Waters, rock to access the Nautilus Lair",
"Energy temple first area, rock bellow the save room exit",
"Veil bottom area, rock to access the Verse Egg",
"The Veil top left area, Rock blocking a bulb close to the right exit".

Harder place are:
"Home Waters, rock to access the Energy temple",
"Song Cave, rock to access the Verse Egg",
"Turtle Cave, rocks to access the Turtle Egg",

options.label: Using Nature Form jump to climb Sun Temple cliffs
options.description:
If enabled, the randomizer logic will consider it possible to climb the
Sun Temple boss path cliffs using the Nature Form jump glitch

options.label: Sun Temple save cristal glitch
options.description:
If enabled, the randomizer logic will consider it possible to pass from
the Sun Temple left area to the Sun Temple right area by crossing the wall using the
save crystal.

Note: You will have to cross the big dark room without light.

options.label: Mithalas Dark Jelly glitch
options.description:
If enabled, the randomizer logic will consider it possible to go through the
Mithalas top area current using a Dark Jelly.

options.label: Trident Head with Fish Form Glitch
options.description:
If enabled, the randomizer logic will consider it possible to go through the
stream to get the trident head using the fish form.

options.label: Bind and Rock to get Urchin Costume
options.description:
If enabled, the randomizer logic will consider it possible to get to the Urchin Costume
by jumping on a binded rock.

options.label: No progression in hard or hidden locations
options.description:
Make sure that there are no progression items at hard-to-reach or hard-to-find locations.

Those locations are very High locations (that need beast form, soup and skill to get), every location in the
bubble cave, locations where need you to cross a false wall without any indication, the Arnassi race,
bosses and minibosses.

Useful for those that want a more casual run.

options.label: No progression in Simon says area
options.description: Make sure that there are no progression items in the says area.

options.label: No progression in Kelp Forest
options.description:
Make sure that there are no progression items in Kelp Forest (excluding Simon says area).

Can be useful to get smaller runs.

options.label: No progression in the Veil
options.description:
Make sure that there are no progression items in the Veil.

Can be useful to get smaller runs.

options.label: No progression in Mithalas
options.description:
Make sure that there are no progression items in the Mithalas (city, castle and cathedral).

Can be useful to get smaller runs.

options.label: No progression in the Energy Temple
options.description:
Make sure that there are no progression items in the Energy Temple.

Can be useful to get smaller runs.

options.label: No progression in Arnassi Ruins
options.description:
Make sure that there are no progression items in the Arnassi Ruins.

Can be useful to get smaller runs.

Note that if the Transportation turtle are not randomize, this include Simon Says area.

options.label: No progression in the Frozen Veil
options.description:
Make sure that there are no progression items in the Frozen Veil (including Ice Cavern and Bubble Cave).

Can be useful to get smaller runs.

options.label: No progression in the Abyss
options.description:
Make sure that there are no progression items in the Abyss.

Can be useful to get smaller runs.

Has no effect if the objective is "killing the four gods".

options.label: No progression in the Sunken City
options.description:
Make sure that there are no progression items in the Sunken City.

Can be useful to get smaller runs.

Has no effect if the objective is "killing the four gods".

options.label: No progression in the Body
options.description:
Make sure that there are no progression items in the Body (including the before-boss transturtle room
and the boss location).

Can be useful to get smaller runs.

Has no effect if the objective is "killing the four gods".

options.label: Kingdom Sanity
options.description: Kingdoms must be found before they can be visited

options.label: Run Type
options.description:
Determines which kingdoms can be visited during a run
Kingdom: Only base kingdoms will be visited
Extra: Only extra kingdoms will be visited
Either: Any kingdom can be visited determined by the starting route
Combined: Any kingdom can be visited

options.label: All Kingdoms
options.description:
How many kingdoms you visit before heading to the pale keep or Reflecting Pool.
If progressive regions and/or kingdom sanity is on,
your run ends in a failure if you are not allowed to visit enough kingdoms.

options.label: Progressive Regions
options.description:
Introduces items that increases the amount regions you are currently allowed to visit in a run.
Includes Pale Keep/Looping Hallway and Moonlit Pinnacle/Reflecting Pool.
Outskirts or Geode is always accessible.

options.label: Excluded Kingdoms
options.description:
What kingdoms, if any, should not be added to the pool of locations.
There will always be a generic location that any class can obtain.
Available Options: [ "Scholar's Nest", "King's Arsenal", "Red Darkhouse", "Churchmouse Streets", "Emerald Lakeside",
                    "Darkhouse Depths", "Atelier Aurum", "Subterra Sanctum"]
Additionally you can exclude one of Kingdom Outskirts/Crack In The Geode, The Pale Keep/Looping Hallway,
and Moonlit Pinnacle/Reflecting Pool depending on your RunType

options.label: Enforce Kingdom Order With Kingdom Sanity
options.description:
Introduces another requirement to reaching a kingdom rather than just receiving the item.
You also need to have at least one kingdom from all the previous orders.
Kingdom Order is always used if you have Progressive Regions but not Kingdom Sanity,
so you can't access all kingdoms after receiving one progressive region.

options.label: Class Sanity
options.description: Classes must be found before they can be played

options.label: Exclude Class
options.description:
What class, if any, should not be accounted for in logic.
Throughout the run you will not be able to play that class at all.
Available Options: ["Wizard", "Assassin", "Heavyblade", "Dancer", "Druid", "Spellsword", "Sniper", "Bruiser",
                    "Defender", "Ancient", "Hammermaid", "Pyromancer", "Grenadier", "Shadow"]

options.label: Checks Per Class
options.description:
What classes should have locations associated with them.
There will always be a generic location that any class can obtain.
Available Options: ["Wizard", "Assassin", "Heavyblade", "Dancer", "Druid", "Spellsword", "Sniper", "Bruiser",
                    "Defender", "Ancient","Hammermaid", "Pyromancer", "Grenadier", "Shadow"]
_ALL can be used to put checks on all classes

options.label: Random Include Classes For Checks Per Class
options.description:
How many classes to randomly add to checks per class.
Will not choose from classes that have been excluded, or already included.

options.label: Item Sanity
options.description:
What is required to have an item appear in a non AP treasuresphere
None: Any item is always available
Itemset: Receiving the itemset unlocks all the items in the itemset
Full: Need to get each individual item unlocked

options.label: Checks Per Item In Chest
options.description:
Each item in a standard chest is an archipelago item.
Shuffles treasurespheres into the item pool, which will contain the non AP items.
Does not add one check per class if 'Checks Per Class' is on

options.label: Upgrade Sanity
options.description:
What is required to have an upgrade appear in a shop, will randomly be chosen between available options still
None: Any upgrade is always available
Simple: Just need to get 'Ruby' item to unlock all the Ruby upgrades
Full: Need to get 'Ruby Primary' item to unlock the ruby upgrade for the primary

options.label: Potion Sanity
options.description:
How the top shelf of the shop appears
None: Default behavior
Locked: Hp and level will be in their position when their item is found, and potions are added to the pool as they are found
Roulette: Randomly fills the slots with unlocked 'potions', meaning hp and level are not guaranteed

options.label: Goal Condition
options.description:
Set your Goal Condition.
Shira: Defeat Shira x number of times, which is configured below

options.label: Required Shira Kills
options.description: How many unique classes must defeat Shira to goal if included in goal

options.label: Required Witch Kills
options.description: How many unique classes must defeat Witch to goal if included in goal

options.label: Shop Sanity
options.description:
Shops contain ap items to purchase, ap item is required to purchase before you can purchase the normal shop item in that slot
None: Shops do not carry ap items
Global: Shops carry the same ap items, and only need to be purchased once to unblock that slot
Regional: Each kingdom contains their own ap items that need to be purchased

options.label: Death Link Amnesty
options.description: How many times you need to fall of the track to trigger a DeathLink death. (1 = every fall, 2 = every other fall, etc. Only applies when DeathLink is on.)

options.label: DeathLink Respawn Time
options.description:
How long Lakitu takes to pick you up after a received DeathLink, in tenths
of a second. 25 is the vanilla 2.5 seconds. Only applies when DeathLink is on.
Deaths you cause by falling off the track keep the vanilla pickup time.

options.label: Enabled CCs
options.description: Which engine classes (CCs) generate location checks. (options: 50cc, 100cc, 150cc, Mirror)

options.label: Enabled Cup Check Tiers
options.description: Which difficulty tiers generate cup completion checks. (options: 3rd_place, 2nd_place, 1st_place, 1_star, 2_star, 3_star)

options.label: Include Race Checks
options.description: Include individual race 1st place checks in addition to cup checks.

options.label: Cups Required for Goal
options.description: Number of cups that must be completed at goal difficulty/CC to win.

options.label: Goal Difficulty
options.description: Difficulty tier required for goal cups.

options.label: Goal CC
options.description: Engine class required for goal cups.

options.label: Lock Default Characters
options.description:
Add default characters (unlocked in vanilla) to the item pool and
require them to be found. Two starting characters of different weight
classes are still granted at the start.
When disabled, all default characters are available from the start.

options.label: Lock Default Vehicles
options.description:
Add default karts and bikes (unlocked in vanilla) to the item pool
and require them to be found. A starting kart and starting bike are
still granted at the start, in weight classes that match the starting
characters (or two random classes if characters aren't locked).
When disabled, all default vehicles are available from the start.

options.label: Enable Item Randomization
options.description:
Enable mid-race item randomization. When enabled, items from item boxes
are replaced with AP-pool items, and filler/powerup items from the multiworld
are injected into the item slot during races.

options.label: Starting Items
options.description:
Which items are available from the start before any Powerup items are
unlocked. These are the only items that can appear from item boxes at the
beginning of the game.
(options: Green Shell, Red Shell, Banana, Fake Item Box, Mushroom,
Triple Mushrooms, Bob-omb, Blue Shell, Lightning, Star, Golden Mushroom,
Mega Mushroom, Blooper, POW Block, Bullet Bill, Triple Green Shells,
Triple Red Shells, Triple Bananas)

options.label: Random Item Mode
options.description:
How 'Filler: Random Item' is resolved during a race.
placement_weighted: weighted by GP placement odds for current position.
uniform: uniform random from all unlocked items.

options.label: Enable Traps
options.description:
Allow trap items to appear in the item pool.
Requires Enable Item Randomization. Trap weights below control which traps
appear and how often.
DISABLE FOR NOW! NO TRAPS ARE IMPLEMENTED YET!!!

options.label: Trap Percentage
options.description: Percentage of filler items that will be traps (0-100).

options.label: Trap Weight: Brake
options.description: Weight for Brake Trap. Set to 0 to disable.

options.label: Trap Weight: Gas
options.description: Weight for Gas Trap. Set to 0 to disable.

options.label: Trap Weight: Boost
options.description: Weight for Boost Trap. Set to 0 to disable.

options.label: Trap Weight: Cloud
options.description: Weight for Cloud Trap. Set to 0 to disable.

options.label: Trap Weight: POW
options.description: Weight for POW Trap. Set to 0 to disable.

options.label: Trap Weight: Lightning
options.description: Weight for Lightning Trap. Set to 0 to disable.

options.label: Filler Item Queue Cap
options.description: Maximum filler items that can be queued per race. 0 = unlimited.

options.label: Filler Weight: Random Item
options.description: Weight for Random Item filler.

options.label: Filler Weight: Mushroom
options.description: Weight for Mushroom filler.

options.label: Filler Weight: Triple Mushroom
options.description: Weight for Triple Mushroom filler.

options.label: Filler Weight: Golden Mushroom
options.description: Weight for Golden Mushroom filler.

options.label: Filler Weight: Star
options.description: Weight for Star filler.

options.label: Filler Weight: Bullet Bill
options.description: Weight for Bullet Bill filler.

options.label: Filler Weight: Mega Mushroom
options.description: Weight for Mega Mushroom filler.

options.label: Filler Weight: Blue Shell
options.description: Weight for Blue Shell filler.

options.label: Filler Weight: Red Shell
options.description: Weight for Red Shell filler.

options.label: Filler Weight: Triple Red Shell
options.description: Weight for Triple Red Shell filler.

options.label: Filler Weight: Bob-omb
options.description: Weight for Bob-omb filler.

options.label: Filler Weight: Lightning
options.description: Weight for Lightning filler (not trap).

options.label: Filler Weight: Blooper
options.description: Weight for Blooper filler.

options.label: Filler Weight: POW Block
