options.description: Weight for POW Block filler.

options.label: Victory Condition
options.description:
This selects the victory condition from the following:
Entropy - Collect seven party members and beat Entropy.
Omni - Reach Omni and defeat them using any strategy.
Memory Emblem - Find and collect enough Memory Emblems.
Chaos Emblem - Defeat bosses holding Chaos Emblems.

options.label: Memory Emblem Requirement
options.description:
How many Memory Emblems are required to beat the game?
(Only affected if your goal is Memory Emblems)

options.label: Memory Emblem Pool
options.description:
How many Memory Emblems are added to the item pool?
(Only affected if your goal is Memory Emblems)

options.label: Chaos Chip Requirement
options.description:
How many Chaos Chips are required to beat the game?
(Only affected if your goal is Chaos Chips)

Chaos Chips will only spawn on bosses dictated by your
settings.

options.label: Chaos Chip Pool
options.description:
How many Chaos Chips are added to the item pool?
(Only affected if your goal is Chaos Chips)

options.label: Hint Chaos Chips
options.description: Toggle on to hint the location of Chaos Chips at the beginning.

options.label: Easy Logic
options.description:
This creates an easier path for the player which prevents logic requiring the use of the multicolored doors found
in other zones.

options.label: Omni Level Scaling
options.description: This toggles whether Omni scales the party's level down to 50 when fought.

options.label: Disable Enemy Level Slider
options.description:
This toggles whether the Enemy Levels slider in the options is available to be edited.
WARNING: This could cause required grinding for some seeds.

options.label: Enable Miniboss Drops
options.description:
This toggles whether minibosses drops are included in the multiworld.
NOTE: You may still need to defeat minibosses if they are blocking your path to progression

options.label: Enable Warden Drops
options.description:
This toggles whether Wardens drops are included in the multiworld.
NOTE: This only includes normal Wardens, Chaos Wardens are a different option

options.label: Chaos Warden Drops
options.description:
This toggles whether Chaos Wardens drops are included in the multiworld.
NOTE: This only includes Chaos Wardens, normal Wardens are a different option

options.label: Omni Drops
options.description:
This toggles whether Omni drops are included in the multiworld.
Note! Disabling this could prevent Omni from being beatable.

options.label: Enable Shops
options.description: This toggles whether shops are included in the multiworld.

options.label: Enable ReCollections
options.description: This toggles whether ReCollections are included in the multiworld.

options.label: Enable Starstuds
options.description: This toggles whether Starstuds are included in the multiworld.

options.label: Character
options.description: Choose your character!

options.label: Toppin Count
options.description:
Number of toppins shuffled into the item pool.

May be less than expected if the item pool is too small.

options.label: Floor 1 Boss Toppins
options.description: Percentage of Toppins required to fight the Floor 1 Boss.

options.label: Floor 2 Boss Toppins
options.description: Percentage of Toppins required to fight the Floor 2 Boss.

options.label: Floor 3 Boss Toppins
options.description: Percentage of Toppins required to fight the Floor 3 Boss.

options.label: Floor 4 Boss Toppins
options.description: Percentage of Toppins required to fight the Floor 4 Boss.

options.label: Floor 5 Boss Toppins
options.description: Percentage of Toppins required to fight the Floor 5 Boss.

options.label: Treasures Award Checks
options.description: Adds the game's 19 Treasures to the pool as locations.

options.label: Secrets Award Checks
options.description: Adds the game's 57 Secrets to the pool as locations.

options.label: S Ranks Award Checks
options.description:
Adds the game's 24 S Ranks to the pool as locations.

Obtaining a P Rank in a level will also check its corresponding S Rank location.

options.label: P Ranks Award Checks
options.description: Adds the game's 24 P Ranks to the pool as locations.

options.label: Chef Tasks Award Checks
options.description:
Adds the game's 72 Chef Tasks (achievements) to the pool as locations.

If S/P Rank checks are disabled, the no-hit boss Chef Tasks as well as S/P Ranked floor Chef Tasks will set to Excluded.
If Pumpkin checks are enabled, this will also add the 2 pumpkin-related Chef Tasks as checks.

options.label: Shuffle Boss Keys
options.description:
On: Shuffle Boss Keys into the item pool.

Off: Keep Boss Keys in their normal spots.

options.label: Shuffle Level Gates
options.description: Shuffle level entrances around the Hub.

options.label: Shuffle Boss Gates
options.description: Shuffle bosses (except Pizzaface) between floors.

options.label: Shuffle Secrets
options.description: Shuffle Secrets between levels.

options.label: Open World
options.description:
Unlock all floors immediately, making more levels accessible from the start.

If active, boss keys will be removed from the item pool.

options.label: Bonus Ladders
options.description:
Add bonus ladders to Hub to make accessing levels easier.

Floors up to and including the selected floor number are affected.

Set to 0 to disable bonus ladders.

options.label: Trap Percentage
options.description: Set a percentage of how many filler items are replaced with traps here.

options.label: Fairly Random
options.description:
On: The first two levels will have at least two accessible locations each, and the first boss will not require a grab to defeat.

Off: The first two levels and first boss can be anything.

Only applies when Shuffle Level Gates and/or Shuffle Boss Gates are enabled.

options.label: Difficulty
options.description:
Determines how strict the randomizer logic will be, and as a result, how difficult your run may be.

Normal: Stricter logic for new players or those looking for a quick, simple run. The randomizer will never expect you to do anything too technical or creative.

Expert: Relaxed logic for those looking for a challenge. The randomizer may expect you to know obscure mechanics, perform precise tricks, or use glitches or other unintended behavior.

options.label: Randomize Moves
options.description: Determines whether your moves will be randomized. If disabled, only Toppins, Boss Keys, and filler will appear in the item pool.

options.label: Randomize These Moves
options.description: If "Randomize Moves" is enabled, any move indicated here will be shuffled into the item pool, and any move not indicated here will be useable from the start.

options.label: Randomize Transformations
options.description:
Determines whether any level-specific Transformations will be shuffled into the item pool.
Enabling this setting in combination with moveset randomization will place 2 movement abilities at the beginning of your world to prevent a restrictive start.

options.label: Randomize These Transformations
options.description: If "Randomize Transformations" is enabled, any Transformation indicated here will be shuffled into the item pool, and any not indicated here will be useable from the start.

options.label: Ring Link
options.description:
Links your in-level point gain/loss with other players.
Point gain is only linked when coming from pizza toppings, pizzasonas, clocks and bells.

options.label: Shuffle Clothes
options.description: Determines whether outfits will be shuffled into the item pool.

options.label: Shuffle Lap 2 Portals
options.description:
On: Shuffles an item into the pool that enables all lap 2 portals

Off: Enables all lap 2 portals from the start

options.label: Pumpkin Checks
options.description: Adds the game's 30 pumpkins to the pool as locations.

options.label: Pumpkin Count
options.description:
Number of Pumpkins shuffled into the item pool if pumpkin checks is turned on.

May be less than expected if the item pool is too small.

options.label: Tricky Treat Door Pumpkins
options.description: Percentage of Pumpkins required to access Tricky Treat.

options.label: Randomize Music
options.description: Determines whether in-game music should be randomized.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Determines your goal in this run.
CTOP: Defeat Pizzaface and complete the Crumbling Tower of Pizza.
Snotty: Kill Snotty. Only levels below Snotty's home floor will be accessible.

options.label: Snotty's Home Floor
options.description: Determines which floor Snotty will show up on.

options.label: Randomize Enemies
options.description: Determines whether an enemy is replaced with a random other enemy.

options.label: Post Game Required
options.description: If enabled, Post Game Dungeons may hold key progression items.

options.label: Randomized Start Character
options.description: If enabled, starting character is randomized.

options.label: Randomized Quest Rewards
options.description:
If enabled, Quest are included as Checks.
Increases the average clear time by 3-5 hours.

options.label: Include Monster Tokens
options.description: Include Monster Tokens as AP Locations/Items

options.label: Include Keys
options.description: Include Keys as AP Locations/Items

options.label: Include Warp Gates
options.description:
Include Warp Gates as AP Locations/Items
Additionally, to offset issues with snack gates, you will start with 400 Scooby Snacks

options.label: Include Snacks
options.description: Include Snacks as AP Locations/Items

options.label: Completion Goal
options.description:
Select which completion goal you want for this world:
0 = Vanilla/Beat Mastermind
1 = Bosses
2 = Monster Tokens
3 = Bosses/Tokens
4 = Scooby Snacks
5 = Snacks/Bosses
6 = Snacks/Tokens
7 = Bosses/Tokens/Snacks
For Non-Vanilla options, Mastermind still needs to be defeated - you just can't fight him
until the goal has been met Snack Clear Conditions will only work with Snacksanity Enabled

options.label: Boss Kills Count
options.description: Sets the number of bosses needed if Boss Completion Goal is being used

options.label: Token Count
options.description: Sets the number of tokens needed if Token Completion Goal is being used

options.label: Snack Count
options.description: Sets the number of Scooby Snacks needed if Snack Completion Goal is being used

options.label: Advanced Logic
options.description: Changes generation to expect certain tricks to be performed, intended for experienced players

options.label: Expert Logic
options.description: Changes generation to expect certain tricks to be performed, intended for even MORE experienced players

options.label: Creepy Early
options.description:
Changes generation to expect certain tricks to be performed (CREEPY EARLY [GCN]),
intended for less sane players

options.label: Speedster
options.description: For Fun Setting, permanently makes scooby move at mach speed

options.label: Entrance Randomisation
options.description:
Determine logic for entrance randomisation

Off - Do not randomise entrances

Quests Only - Randomise every quest

Quests and Rooms Separate - Randomise every quest and every room

Everything - Randomise every quest and room together

options.label: Randomise Tower Entrance
options.description: Determine whether the tower is affected by your entrance randomisation setting. Does not have any effect if entrance randomisation does not randomise rooms

options.label: Randomise X Potion
options.description: Determine whether the X Potion is affected by your entrance randomisation setting. Does not have any effect if entrance randomisation does not randomise quests

options.label: Starting Weapon
options.description:
Select the weapon that you will start the game with.

Progressive Weapons will give you the next weapon in the sequence each time you get it.

options.label: Progressive Jump
options.description: Obtain the Pogo Stick, the Desert Bird Feather and the Rocket Boots in that order

options.label: Candy Production Multiplier
options.description: The number of candies generated per second will be multiplied by this number.

options.label: Candy Drop Multiplier
options.description: The number of candies dropped in quests will be multiplied by this number.

options.label: Lollipop Production Multiplier
options.description: The number of lollipops generated per second will be multiplied by this number.

options.label: Candy Merchant's Hat Price (x1000)
options.description: The price (in thousands of candies) required to buy the Candy Merchant's Hat.

options.label: Sorceress' Hat Price (x1000)
options.description: The price (in thousands of lollipops) required to buy the Sorceress' Hat.

options.label: Teapot Boss HP
options.description: The teapot boss's total HP.

options.label: Randomise HP Bar
options.description: Whether the HP Bar must be an item found elsewhere

options.label: Brew X Potions
options.description:
Determine whether you can brew more than one X potion at a time

One at a time - You can only brew one X potion at a time

Simultaneously - You can brew multiple X potions at a time, provided you have enough resources to brew them all at once.

options.label: Enable The Computer
options.description: Whether to enable The Computer. Once you have cleared the game, The Computer can be used to cheat items.

options.label: Spells
options.description:
Select how spells will be itemised

Individual Grimoires - The item pool will be filled with Beginner's Grimoire, Advanced Grimoire and Black Magic Grimoire

Progressive Grimoires - The item pool will have three Progressive Grimoires

Individual Spells - The item pool will contain each spell individually. Buying the Beginner's Grimoire will send three checks. Obtaining the other grimoires will send two checks.

options.label: Pains au Chocolat Count
options.description: The number of available Pains au Chocolat.

options.label: Energy Link
options.description: Allow sending energy to other worlds. Candy and lollipops can be converted to energy. 25% of the energy is lost in the transfer.

options.label: Gifting
options.description:
Do you want to enable gifting items to and from other Archipelago slots?
Items can only be sent to games that also support gifting

options.label: Create Hints
options.description: Do you want to create hints when you first enter a shop?

options.label: Font Traps
options.description: The number of font traps made available in the item pool

options.label: Game Version
options.description: Select FireRed or LeafGreen version.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Sets what your goal is to consider the game beaten.

- Champion: Defeat the Champion
- Champion Rematch: Defeat the Champion Rematch

options.label: Skip Intro
options.description:
Set whether the vanilla intro sequence where you get your starter Pokemon from Oak's Lab should be skipped or not.
If the intro is skipped then you will be prompted to select your starter Pokemon during Oak's initial speech.

This setting is forced on if Random Starting Town or any type of Entrance Randomization is on.

options.label: Skip Elite Four
options.description: Set whether to skip the Elite Four fights and go straight to the Champion fight when entering the Pokemon League.

options.label: Kanto Only
options.description:
Excludes all the Sevii Island locations. Navel Rock and Birth Island are still included.
HM06 Rock Smash, HM07 Waterfall, and the Sun Stone will still be in the item pool.
The Move Reminder will be moved from Two Island to the Move Deleter's House in Fuchsia City.

options.label: Random Starting Town
options.description: Randomizes the town that you start in. This includes any area that has a Pokemon Center except for Indigo Plateau.

options.label: Starting Town Blacklist
options.description:
Prevents certain towns from being chosen as your random starting town.

Has no effect if the starting town is not randomized.

options.label: Shuffle Pokemon Center Entrances
options.description:
Shuffles the Pokemon Center entrances amongst each other.

The Player's House is included in this pool but will never be shuffled as your starting town's Pokemon Center.

options.label: Shuffle Gym Entrances
options.description: Shuffles the gym entrances amongst each other.

options.label: Shuffle Mart Entrances
options.description:
Shuffles the Poke Mart entrances amongst each other.

This does not include the Celadon Department Store entrances.

options.label: Shuffle Harbor Entrances
options.description: Shuffles the harbor entrances amongst each other.

options.label: Shuffle Building Entrances
options.description:
Shuffles the building entrances amongst each other.

The Celadon Department Store entrances are included in this pool.

A building is considered a multi entrance building if the two entrances are normally connected inside the building.
For instance, the Celadon Condominium is not considered a multi entrance building and the Route 16 Gate counts as
two separate multi entrance buildings.

- Off: Building entrances are not shuffled
- Simple: Single entrance buildings and multi entrance buildings are shuffled separately from each other. Both entrances for multi entrance buildings will connect to the same building
- Restricted: Single entrance buildings and multi entrance buildings are shuffled separately from each other. Both entrances for multi entrance buildings do not need to lead to the same building
- Full: All building entrances are shuffled together

options.label: Shuffle Dungeon Entrances
options.description:
Shuffles the dungeon entrances amongst each other.

- Off: Dungeon entrances are not shuffled
- Seafoam: Swaps the two Seafoam Island entrances.
- Simple: Single entrance dungeons and multi entrance dungeons are shuffled separately from each other. Both entrances for multi entrance dungeons will connect to the same dungeon
- Restricted: Single entrance dungeons and multi entrance dungeons are shuffled separately from each other. Both entrances for multi entrance dungeons do not need to lead to the same dungeon
- Full: All dungeon entrances are shuffled together

options.label: Shuffle Interior Warps
options.description:
Shuffles the interior warps of buildings and dungeons amongst each other.

The Safari Zone will behave like a normal dungeon when interiors are shuffled.

The elevator warps in the Celadon Department Store, Rocket Hideout, and Silph Co. are not shuffled.

The Safari Zone Entrance <-> Safari Zone Center warp is not shuffled.

The only warps in Lost Cave that are shuffled are the two ladders.

options.label: Shuffle Warp Tiles
options.description:
Shuffles the warp tiles in buildings and dungeons amongst each other.

- Off: Warp tiles are not shuffled
- Simple: All warp tiles in a building or dungeon are shuffled amongst each other, but they will never lead to another building or dungeon
- Full: All warp tiles are shuffled together

options.label: Shuffle Dropdowns
options.description:
Shuffles the dropdowns in dungeons amongst each other.

The incorrect dropdowns in Dotted Hole are not shuffled.

- Off: Dropdowns are not shuffled
- Simple: All dropdowns of a dungeon are shuffled amongst each other, but they will never lead to another dungeon
- Full: All dropdowns are shuffled together

options.label: Mix Entrance/Warp Pools
options.description:
Shuffle the selected entrances/warps into a mixed pool instead of separate ones. Has no effect on pools whose
entrances/warps aren't shuffled. Entrances/warps can only be mixed with other entrance/warps that have the same
restrictions. Can specify "All" as a shortcut for adding in all entrances/warps that can be mixed.

Your starting town's Pokemon Center entrance (Player's House entrance if starting in Pallet Town) is guaranteed to go to a Pokemon Center.

Dropdowns are only added to the mixed pool if entrances/warps are decoupled.

The avaialble pools that can be mixed are:
- Pokemon Centers
- Gyms
- Marts
- Harbors
- Buildings
- Dungeons
- Interiors
- Warp Tiles
- Dropdowns

options.label: Decouple Entrances/Warps
options.description:
Decouple entrances/warps when shuffling them. This means that you are no longer guaranteed to end up back where you
came from when you go back through an entrance/warp.

Simple Building/Dungeon shuffle are not compatible with this option and will be changed to Restricted shuffle.

options.label: Randomize Fly Destinations
options.description:
Randomizes where each fly point takes you. The new fly destinations can be almost any outdoor warp point in the
game with a few exceptions (Cycling Road Gates for example).

- Off: Fly destinations are not randomized
- Area: Fly destinations will be randomized to a location in the same area as its original location (e.g. Vermilion Fly Destination would go to either Vermilion City, Route 6, or Route 11)
- Map: Fly destinations will be randomized to a location on the same map as its original location (e.g. One Island Fly Destination would go to either One Island, Two Island, or Three Island)
- Region: Fly destinations will be randomized to a location in the same region as its original location (e.g. Sevii fly destinations would go to another location on the Sevii Islands)
- Completely Random: Fly destinations are completely random

options.label: Fly Destination Plando
options.description:
Plando what warp certain fly unlocks will take you to.

For example "Pallet Town Fly Destination": "Player's House" will make it so that unlocking the Pallet Town fly
point will let you fly to in front of the Player's House.

A full list of supported warps can be found at:
https://github.com/vyneras/Archipelago/blob/frlg-stable/worlds/pokemon_frlg/docs/fly_plando.md

Has no effect if fly destinations aren't randomized.

options.label: Shuffle Badges
options.description: Shuffle Gym Badges into the general item pool. If turned off, Badges will be shuffled among themselves.

options.label: Shuffle Hidden Items
options.description:
Shuffle Hidden Items into the general item pool.

- Off: Hidden Items are not shuffled
- Nonrecurring: Nonrecurring Hidden Items are shuffled
- All: All Hidden Items are shuffled. Recurring Hidden Items will always appear and will not regenerate

options.label: Extra Key Items
options.description:
Adds key items that are required to access the Rocket Hideout, Safari Zone, Pokemon Mansion, and Power Plant.

Adds four new locations:
- Item in the Celadon Rocket House
- Item given by a Worker in the Fuchsia Safari Office
- Item given by the Scientist in the Cinnabar Pokemon Lab Research Room
- Hidden Item in the Cerulean Gym (requires Surf & Itemfinder)

options.label: Shopsanity
options.description:
Shuffles shop items into the general item pool. The Celadon Department Store 4F Held Items Shop is not shuffled.

IMPORTANT NOTE: There is a non-randomized shop on the Pokecenter 2F where you can always buy Poke Balls, Potions, etc.

options.label: Vending Machines
options.description:
Shuffles the Celadon Department Store vending machine items into the general item pool.

At least one Fresh Water, Soda Pop, and Lemonade are guaranteed to be placed in a shop location.

options.label: Prizesanity
options.description: Shuffles the Celadon Game Corner Prize Room items and TMs into the general item pool.

options.label: Shop Slots
options.description:
Sets the number of slots per shop that can have progression items when shopsanity is on. Shop slots that cannot be
progression items will be filled with a random normal shop item from your world.

options.label: Shop Prices
options.description:
Sets how shop item's prices are randomized.

- Vanilla: Items cost their base price
- Cheap: Items cost 50% of their base price
- Affordable: Items cost between 50% - 100% of their base price
- Standard: Items cost 50% - 150% of their base price
- Expensive: Items cost 100% - 150% of their base price

options.label: Consistent Shop Prices
options.description:
Sets whether all instances of an item will cost the same price in every shop (e.g. if a Potion's price in a shop is
200 then all Potions in shops will cost 200).

options.label: Kanto Trainersanity
options.description:
Beating a Kanto trainer gives you an item.

You can specify how many Trainers should be a check between 0 and 357. Trainers that have checks will periodically
have an exclamation mark appear above their head in game.

Trainers are no longer missable. Each trainer will add a random filler item into the pool.

options.label: Sevii Trainersanity
options.description:
Beating a Sevii trainer gives you an item.

You can specify how many Trainers should be a check between 0 and 99. Trainers that have checks will periodically
have an exclamation mark appear above their head in game.

Trainers are no longer missable. Each trainer will add a random filler item into the pool.

options.label: Rematchsanity
options.description:
Beating each of a trainer's rematches gives you an item. Only the rematches for trainers who have a trainersanity
item will give an item for rematchsanity.

Each trainer rematch will add a random filler item into the pool.

options.label: Rematch Requirements
options.description:
Sets the requirement for being able to battle trainer's rematches.

- Badges: Obtain some number of Badges
- Gyms: Beat some number of Gyms

options.label: Dexsanity
options.description:
Adding a "caught" Pokedex entry gives you an item (catching, evolving, trading, etc.).

You can specify how many Pokedex entries should be a check between 0 and 386. Depending on your settings for
randomizing wild Pokemon, there might not actually be as many locations as you specify. Pokemon that have checks
will have a black silhouette of a pokeball in the Pokedex and in the battle HUD if you have seen them already.

Defeating Gym Leaders provides seen Pokedex info, allowing you to see on the map where a Pokemon can be found in
the wild.

Each entry will add a random filler item into the pool.

options.label: Famesanity
options.description:
Unlocking entries in the Fame Checker gives you an item.

Each entry will add a random filler item into the pool.

options.label: Shuffle Fly Unlocks
options.description:
Shuffles the ability to fly to Pokemon Centers into the pool. Entering the map that normally would unlock the
fly point on the map gives a random item.

- Off: Fly Unlocks are not shuffled
- Exclude Indigo: Fly Unlocks are shuffled. Indigo Plateau Fly Unlock is vanilla
- All: Fly Unlocks are shuffled

options.label: Pokemon Request Locations
options.description:
Shuffle the locations that require you to show a specific Pokemon to an NPC. If turned on, the Pokemon that are
required will be found somewhere in the wild. Talking to the NPC that wants to see the Pokemon will provide you with
the Pokedex info for where to find it as well as tell you the item they'll give.

options.label: Shuffle Pokedex
options.description:
Shuffle the Pokedex into the item pool, or start with it.

The Pokedex is hard required for any of the Oak's Aide or Dexsanity locations and is logically required for any of
the Pokemon Request Locations and In-Game Trades.

options.label: Shuffle Running Shoes
options.description: Shuffle the running shoes into the item pool, or start with it.

options.label: Shuffle Berry Pouch
options.description: Shuffles the berry pouch into the item pool. If not shuffled then you will start with it.

options.label: Shuffle TM Case
options.description: Shuffles the TM case into the item pool. If not shuffled then you will start with it.

options.label: Shuffle Jumping Shoes
options.description:
Shuffles the Jumping Shoes into the item pool. If not shuffled then you will start with it.

The Jumping Shoes are a new item that grants you the ability to jump down ledges.

options.label: Post Goal Locations
options.description:
Shuffles locations into the item pool that are only accessible after your goal is completed.

If Cerulean Cave access is locked by your goal then Cerulean Cave won't be included in Shuffled Dungeons.

options.label: Silph Co. Card Key
options.description:
Sets how the card key that unlocks the doors in Silph Co. is handled. If Split or Progressive, nine new locations
will be added to Silph Co. in the form of item balls on floors 2 through 11 (except for floor five).

- Vanilla: There is one Card Key in the pool that unlocks every door in Silph Co.
- Split: The Card Key is split into ten items, one for each floor of Silph Co. that has doors
- Progressive: The Card Key is split into ten items, and you will always obtain them in order from 2F to 11F

options.label: Sevii Island Passes
options.description:
Sets how the passes that allow you to travel to the Sevii Islands are handled. If Split or Progressive, five new
locations will be added to events related to the Sevii Islands.

- Vanilla: The Tri Pass and Rainbow Pass are two separate items in the pool and can be found in any order
- Progressive: There are two Progressive Passes in the pool. You will always obtain the Tri Pass before the Rainbow Pass
- Split: The Tri Pass and Rainbow Pass are split into seven items, one for each island
- Progressive Split: The Tri Pass and Rainbow Pass are split into seven items, and you will always obtain the Passes in order from the First Pass to the Seventh Pass

options.label: Fishing Rods
options.description:
Sets how the fishing rods are handled.

- Vanilla: The fishing rods are all separate items in the pool and can be found in any order
- Progressive: There are three Progressive Rods in the pool, and you will always obtain them in order from Old Rod to Super Rod

options.label: Split Teas
options.description:
Splits the Tea item into four different items. Each guard to Saffron City will require a different Tea to pass.
Brock, Misty, and Erika will appear in the Celadon Condominiums after beating them and give you a randomized item.

The Tea required to get past each guard are as follows:
- Route 5: Blue Tea
- Route 6: Red Tea
- Route 7: Green Tea
- Route 8: Purple Tea

options.label: Gym Keys
options.description:
Adds keys that are needed to enter each of the gyms similar to the Secret Key. Renames the Secret Key to the
Cinnabar Key.

Adds seven new locations:
- Item in the Pewter Museum 2F
- Item from Man on a Date at Route 25
- Item in Diglett's Cave B1F
- Item in the Celadon Hotel
- Item in the Safari Zone East Rest House
- Item in the Saffron Dojo
- Item from the Old Man near Viridian Gym

options.label: Item Appearance Matches Contents
options.description:
Changes the color of item balls to match their contents. Green balls contain progression items, blue balls contain
useful items, and red balls contain filler items. Traps will be a random color between the three.

The following item balls are not affected by this setting and will always be a red ball:
- Rocket Hideout B4F - Team Rocket Grunt Item
- Rocket Hideout B4F - Giovanni Item
- Dotted Hole 1F - Dropped Item
- Tanoby Ruins - Island Item

options.label: Itemfinder Required
options.description:
Sets whether the Itemfinder if required for Hidden Items. Some items cannot be picked up without using the
Itemfinder regardless of this setting (e.g. the Leftovers under Snorlax on Route 12 & 16).

- Off: The Itemfinder is not required to pickup Hidden Items
- Logic: The Itemfinder is logically required to pickup Hidden Items
- Required: The Itemfinder is required to pickup Hidden Items

options.label: Flash Required
options.description:
Sets whether HM05 Flash is logically required to navigate dark caves.

- Off: Flash is not required to navigate dark caves
- Logic: Flash is logically required to navigate dark caves
- Required: Flash is required to navigate dark caves

options.label: Fame Checker Required
options.description:
Sets whether it is required to have the Fame Checker in order to unlock entries.

All Fame Checker entries that are one time occurences have been changed so that you can trigger them repeatedly.

options.label: Bicycle Requires Jumping Shoes
options.description: Sets whether the Bicycle requires you to have the Jumping Shoes in order to jump down ledges while on the Bicycle.

options.label: Acrobatic Bicycle
options.description:
Sets whether the Bicycle is able to jump up ledges in addition to jumping down ledges. If the Bicycle Requires
Jumping Shoes setting is on then the Jumping Shoes is necessary in order to jump up ledges as well.

options.label: Evolutions Required
options.description: Sets which types of locations and/or access rules that evolutions may be logically required for.

options.label: Evolution Methods Required
options.description: Sets which types of evolutions may be logically required.

options.label: Viridian City Roadblock
options.description:
Sets the requirement for passing the Old Man in Viridian City.

- Vanilla: The Old Man moves out of the way after delivering Oak's Parcel
- Early Parcel: Same as Vanilla but Oak's Parcel will be available at the beginning of your game. This option will have no effect and be treated as Vanilla if Random Starting Town is on
- Open: The Old Man is moved out of the way at the start of the game

options.label: Pewter City Roadblock
options.description:
Sets the requirement for moving between Pewter City and Route 3.

- Open: The boy will not stop you from moving between Pewter City and Route 3
- Brock: The boy will stop you from moving between Pewter City and Route 3 until you defeat Brock
- Any Gym Leader: The boy will stop you from moving between Pewter City and Route 3 until you defeat any Gym Leader
- Boulder Badge: The boy will stop you from moving between Pewter City and Route 3 until you have the Boulder Badge
- Any Badge: The boy will stop you from moving between Pewter City and Route 3 until you have a Badge

options.label: Digletts Cave Roadblock
options.description:
Sets the roadblock for accessing Diglett's Cave from Pewter City.

- Vanilla: A cut tree will block your access to Diglett's Cave
- Rock Smash: A smashable rock will block the access to Diglett's Cave

options.label: Remove Cerulean City Roadblocks
options.description: Moves the Policeman and Slowpoke that are blocking the exits of Cerulean City without needing to save Bill.

options.label: Block Underground Paths
options.description: Blocks the entrances to the underground paths with smashable rocks.

options.label: Route 9 Roadblock
options.description:
Sets the roadblock for moving between Cerulean City and Route 9.

- Vanilla: A cut tree will block you from moving between Cerulean City and Route 9
- Rock Smash: A smashable rock will block you from moving between Cerulean City and Route 9

options.label: Route 10 Waterfall
options.description: Adds a waterfall to Route 10 that connects the north and south sides

options.label: Block Pokemon Tower
options.description: Moves the forced ghost battle in Pokemon Tower to be in front of the 1F stairs.

options.label: Route 12 Boulders
options.description: Adds boulders to Route 12 that block the exits to Lavender Town, Route 11, and Route 13.

options.label: Route 12 Rocks
options.description: Adds impassable rocks to Route 12 that prevent surfing around Snorlax.

options.label: Route 16 Rock
options.description: Adds a smashable rock to Route 16 that allows you to bypass the Snorlax.

options.label: Open Silph Co.
options.description:
The Team Rocket Grunt that blocks the entrance to Silph Co. will be moved out of the way without needing to rescue
Mr. Fuji.

options.label: Remove Saffron Rockets
options.description: Removes the Team Rocket Grunts from Saffron City without needing to liberate Silph Co.

options.label: Route 23 Trees
options.description: Adds cuttable trees to Route 23 under the sixth checkpoint.

options.label: Route 23 Waterfall
options.description: Adds a waterfall to Route 23 at the end of the water section.

options.label: Victory Road Rocks
options.description: Adds smashable rocks to Victory Road that block the floor switches.

options.label: Block Vermilion Sailing
options.description: Prevents you from sailing to Vermilion City on the Seagallop until you have gotten the S.S. Ticket.

options.label: Total Darkness
options.description: Changes dark caves to be completely black and provide no vision without Flash.

options.label: Early Gossipers
options.description: Removes the requirement to have entered the Hall of Fame from various Famesanity locations.

options.label: Elevator's Condition
options.description:
Sets the conditions the Celadon Department Store and Silph Co. elevators are in. Has no logical implications unless
interior warps are shuffled.

- Open: The elevators can be used normally
- Locked: The elevators will require the Lift Key before they can be used
- Disabled: The elevators are completely unusable

options.label: Additional Dark Caves
options.description:
Set additional caves to be dark caves, potentially requiring Flash to navigate them.

The caves that can be turned into dark caves are:
- Mt. Moon
- Diglett's Cave
- Victory Road

options.label: Remove Badge Requirement
options.description:
Removes the badge requirement to use any of the HMs listed.

HMs need to be listed by the move name (e.g. Cut, Fly, Surf, etc.).

options.label: Oak's Aide Route 2
options.description:
Sets the number of Pokemon that need to be registered in the Pokedex to receive the item from Professor Oak's Aide
on Route 2. Vanilla is 10.

options.label: Oak's Aide Route 10
options.description:
Sets the number of Pokemon that need to be registered in the Pokedex to receive the item from Professor Oak's Aide
on Route 10. Vanilla is 20.

options.label: Oak's Aide Route 11
options.description:
Sets the number of Pokemon that need to be registered in the Pokedex to receive the item from Professor Oak's Aide
on Route 11. Vanilla is 30.

options.label: Oak's Aide Route 16
options.description:
Sets the number of Pokemon that need to be registered in the Pokedex to receive the item from Professor Oak's Aide
on Route 16. Vanilla is 40.

options.label: Oak's Aide Route 15
options.description:
Sets the number of Pokemon that need to be registered in the Pokedex to receive the item from Professor Oak's Aide
on Route 15. Vanilla is 50.

options.label: Pokemon Lab Fossil Count
options.description: Sets the number of fossils you need to revive at the Pokemon Lab in order to obtain the second fossil.

options.label: Viridian Gym Requirement
options.description:
Sets the requirement for opening the Viridian Gym.

- Badges: Obtain some number of Badges
- Gyms: Beat some number of Gyms

options.label: Viridian Gym Count
options.description: Sets the number of Badges/Gyms required to open the Viridian Gym.

options.label: Route 22 Gate Requirement
options.description:
Sets the requirement for passing through the Route 22 Gate.

- Badges: Obtain some number of Badges
- Gyms: Beat some number of Gyms

options.label: Route 22 Gate Count
options.description: Sets the number of Badges/Gyms required to pass through the Route 22 Gate.

options.label: Route 23 Guard Requirement
options.description:
Sets the requirement for passing the Route 23 Guard.

- Badges: Obtain some number of Badges
- Gyms: Beat some number of Gyms

options.label: Route 23 Guard Count
options.description: Sets the number of Badges/Gyms required to pass the Route 23 Guard.

options.label: Elite Four Requirement
options.description:
Sets the requirement for challenging the Elite Four.

- Badges: Obtain some number of Badges
- Gyms: Beat some number of Gyms

options.label: Elite Four Count
options.description: Sets the number of Badges/Gyms required to challenge the Elite Four.

options.label: Elite Four Rematch Requirement
options.description:
Sets the requirement for challenging the Elite Four Rematch.

- Badges: Obtain some number of Badges
- Gyms: Beat some number of Gyms

options.label: Elite Four Rematch Count
options.description: Sets the number of Badges/Gyms required to challenge the Elite Four Rematch.

options.label: Cerulean Cave Requirement
options.description:
Sets the requirement for being able to enter Cerulean Cave.

- Vanilla: Become the Champion and restore the Network Machine on the Sevii Islands
- Champion: Become the Champion
- Network Machine: Restore the Network Machine on the Sevii Islands
- Badges: Obtain some number of Badges
- Gyms: Beat some number of Gyms

options.label: Cerulean Cave Count
options.description:
Sets the number of Badges/Gyms required to enter Cerulean Cave. This setting only matters if the Cerulean Cave
Requirement is set to either Badges or Gyms.

options.label: Level Scaling
options.description:
Sets whether encounter levels are scaled by sphere access.

- Off: Vanilla levels are used
- Spheres: Levels are scaled based on sphere access
- Spheres and Distance: Levels are scaled based on sphere access and the distance they are from your starting town

options.label: Modify Trainer Levels
options.description: Modifies the level of all Trainer's Pokemon by the specified percentage.

options.label: Force Fully Evolved
options.description:
Forces opponent's Pokemon to be fully evolved if they are greater than or equal to the specified level.

If set to "species" will force opponent's Pokemon to be evolved based on the level the species would normally
evolve. For species that don't evolve based on levels, the level they will be evolved at is determined by their BST.

Only applies when trainer parties are randomized.

options.label: Randomize Wild Pokemon
options.description:
Randomizes wild Pokemon encounters (grass, caves, water, fishing)

- Vanilla: Wild Pokemon are unchanged
- Match Base Stats: Wild Pokemon are replaced with species with approximately the same BST
- Match Type: Wild Pokemon are replaced with species that share a type with the original
- Match Base Stats and Type: Apply both Match Base Stats and Match Type
- Completely Random: There are no restrictions

options.label: Wild Pokemon Groups
options.description:
If wild Pokemon are not vanilla, they will be randomized according to the grouping specified.

- None: Pokemon are not randomized together based on any groupings
- Dungeons: All Pokemon of the same species in a dungeon are randomized together
- Species: All Pokemon of the same species are randomized together

options.label: Wild Pokemon Blacklist
options.description:
Prevents listed species from appearing in the wild when wild Pokemon are randomized.

May be overridden if enforcing other restrictions in combination with this blacklist is impossible.

Use "Legendaries" as a shortcut for all legendary Pokemon.

options.label: Randomize Starters
options.description:
Randomizes the starter Pokemon in Professor Oak's Lab.

- Vanilla: Starters are unchanged
- Match Base Stats: Starters are replaced with species with approximately the same BST
- Match Type: Starters are replaced with species that share a type with the original
- Match Base Stats and Type: Apply both Match Base Stats and Match Type
- Completely Random: There are no restrictions

options.label: Starter Blacklist
options.description:
Prevents listed species from appearing as a starter when starters are randomized.

May be overridden if enforcing other restrictions in combination with this blacklist is impossible.

Use "Legendaries" as a shortcut for all legendary Pokemon.

options.label: Randomize Trainer Parties
options.description:
Randomizes the Pokemon in all trainer's parties.

- Vanilla: Parties are unchanged
- Match Base Stats: Trainer Pokemon are replaced with species with approximately the same BST
- Match Type: Trainer Pokemon are replaced with species that share a type with the original
- Match Base Stats and Type: Apply both Match Base Stats and Match Type
- Completely Random: There are no restrictions

options.label: Trainer Party Blacklist
options.description:
Prevents listed species from appearing in trainer's parties when trainer's parties are randomized.

May be overridden if enforcing other restrictions in combination with this blacklist is impossible.

Use "Legendaries" as a shortcut for all legendary Pokemon.

options.label: Randomize Legendary Pokemon
options.description:
Randomizes legendary Pokemon (Mewtwo, Zapdos, Deoxys, etc.). Does not randomize the roamer.

- Vanilla: Legendary encounters are unchanged
- Legendaries: Legendary encounters are replaced with another legendary Pokemon
- Match Base Stats: Legendary encounters are replaced with species with approximately the same BST
- Match Type: Legendary encounters are replaced with species that share a type with the original
- Match Base Stats and Type: Apply both Match Base Stats and Match Type
- Completely Random: There are no restrictions

options.label: Legendary Pokemon Blacklist
options.description:
Prevents the listed species from appearing as a legenary Pokemon when legendary Pokemon are randomized.

May be overridden if enforcing other restrictions in combination with this blacklist is impossible.

Use "Legendaries" as a shortcut for all legendary Pokemon.

options.label: Randomize Misc Pokemon
options.description:
Randomizes misc Pokemon. This includes non-legendary static encounters, gift Pokemon, and trade Pokemon.

- Vanilla: Species are unchanged
- Match Base Stats: Species are replaced with species with approximately the same bst
- Match Type: Species are replaced with species that share a type with the original
- Match Base Stats and Type: Apply both Match Base Stats and Match Type
- Completely Random: There are no restrictions

options.label: Misc Pokemon Blacklist
options.description:
Prevents the listed species from appearing as a miscellaneous Pokemon when miscellaneous Pokemon are randomized.

May be overridden if enforcing other restrictions in combination with this blacklist is impossible.

Use "Legendaries" as a shortcut for all legendary Pokemon.

options.label: Randomize Types
options.description:
Randomizes the type(s) of every Pokemon. Each species will have the same number of types.

- Vanilla: Types are unchanged
- Shuffle: Types are shuffled globally for all species (e.g. every Water-type Pokemon becomes Fire-type)
- Completely Random: Each species has its type(s) randomized
- Follow Evolutions: Types are randomized per evolution line instead of per species

options.label: Randomize Abilities
options.description:
Randomizes abilities of every species. Each species will have the same number of abilities.

- Vanilla: Abilities are unchanged
- Completely Random: Each species has its abilities randomized
- Follow Evolutions: Abilities are randomized, but evolutions that normally retain abilities will still do so

options.label: Ability Blacklist
options.description:
Prevent species from being given these abilities.

Has no effect if abilities are not randomized.

options.label: Randomize Moves
options.description:
Randomizes the moves a Pokemon learns through leveling.
Your starter is guaranteed to have a usable damaging move.

- Vanilla: Learnset is unchanged
- Randomized: Moves are randomized
- Start with Four Moves: Moves are randomized and all Pokemon know 4 moves at level 1

options.label: Move Match Type Bias
options.description:
Sets the probability that a learned move will be forced to match one of the types of a Pokemon.

If a move is not forced to match type, it will roll for Normal type bias.

options.label: Move Normal Type Bias
options.description:
Sets the probability that a learned move will be forced to be a Normal type move.

If a move is not forced to be Normal, it will be completely random.

options.label: Move Blacklist
options.description:
Prevents species from learning these moves via learnsets.

Has no effect if moves are not randomized.

options.label: Randomize Base Stats
options.description:
Randomize the base stats for every species.

- Vanilla: Base stats are unchanged
- Shuffle: Base stats are shuffled amongst each other
- Keep BST: Random base stats, but base stat total is preserved
- Completely Random: Random base stats and base stat total

options.label: Physical/Special Split
options.description:
Changes the damage category that moves use to match the categories since the Gen IV physical/special split instead
of the damage category being determined by the move's type.

options.label: Randomize Move Types
options.description:
Randomizes the type for each move.

- Vanilla: Move types are unchanged
- Shuffle: Move types are shuffled globally for all moves (e.g. every Water-type Move becomes Fire-type)
- Completely Random: Each move has its type randomized

options.label: Randomize Damage Categories
options.description:
Randomizes the damage category for each move/type. Will randomized the damage category of the moves individually or
by each type depending on if the Physical/Special Split option is on.

- Vanilla: Damage Categories are unchanged
- Shuffle: Damage Categories for moves/types are shuffled so the amount of physical and special moves/types will remain the same
- Completely Random: Each moves/types damage category is chosen at random with no regard to maintaining the same amount of physical and special moves/types

options.label: HM Compatibility
options.description:
Sets the percent chance that a given HM is compatible with a species.

If you have seen a Pokemon already, the HMs it can use are listed in the Pokedex.

options.label: TM/Tutor Compatibility
options.description: Sets the percent chance that a given TM or move tutor is compatible with a species.

options.label: Randomize TM/Tutor Moves
options.description:
Randomizes the moves taught by TMs and move tutors.

Some opponents like gym leaders are allowed to use TMs. This option can affect the moves they know.

options.label: TM/Tutor Moves Blacklist
options.description:
Prevents TMs and move tutors from teaching these moves.

Has no effect if TM and tutor moves are not randomized.

options.label: Reusable TMs/Move Tutors
options.description: Sets TMs to not break after use (they remain sellable). Allows Move Tutors to be used infinitely.

options.label: Minimum Catch Rate
options.description:
Sets the minimum catch rate a Pokemon can have. It will raise any Pokemon's catch rate to this value if its normal
catch rate is lower than the chosen value.

options.label: All Pokemon Seen
options.description:
Start will all Pokemon seen in your Pokedex.
This allows you to see where the Pokemon can be encountered in the wild.

options.label: Starting Money
options.description: Sets the amount of money that you start with.

options.label: Better Shops
options.description:
Most Pokemarts will sell all normal Pokemart items. The exceptions are the following:

- Celadon Department Store 2F TM Pokemart
- Celadon Department Store 4F Evo Stone Pokemart
- Celadon Department Store 4F Held Items Pokemart
- Celadon Department Store 5F Vitamin Pokemart
- Two Island Market Stall

options.label: Cheaper Coins
options.description: Reduces the cost of buying coins from the Celadon Game Corner by 90%.

options.label: Free Fly Location
options.description: Enables flying to one random location (excluding cities reachable with no items).

options.label: Free Fly Blacklist
options.description: Prevents certain towns from being chosen as your free fly location.

options.label: Town Map Fly Location
options.description:
Enables flying to one random location once the town map has been obtained (excluding cities reachable with no
items).

options.label: Town Map Fly Blacklist
options.description: Prevents certain towns from being chosen as your town map fly location.

options.label: Remote Items
options.description:
Instead of placing your own items directly into the ROM, all items are received from the server, including items you find for yourself.

This enables co-op of a single slot and recovering more items after a lost save file (if you're so unlucky).

But it changes pickup behavior slightly and requires connection to the server to receive any items.

options.label: Randomize Music
options.description: Shuffles music played in any situation where it loops.

options.label: Randomize Fanfares
options.description: Shuffles fanfares for item pickups, healing at the Pokecenter, etc.

options.label: Game Options
options.description:
Allows you to preset the in game options.
The available options and their allowed values are the following:

- Text Speed: Slow, Mid, Fast, Instant - Sets the speed at which text advances
- Turbo Button: Off, A, B, A/B - Sets which buttons auto advance text when held
- Auto Run: Off, On - Sets whether run activates automatically, if 'On' you can hold B to walk
- Button Mode: Help, L/R, L=A - Sets how the L/R buttons behave
    - Help: The L/R buttons open the help menu
    - L/R: The L/R buttons switch between certain screens such as bag pockets
    - L=A: The L button maps to the same functionality as the A button, the R button does nothing
- Frame: 1-10 - Sets the window frame for menus and textboxes
- Battle Scene: Off, On - Sets whether battle animations play
- Battle Style: Shift, Set - Sets whether you are asked to switch between trainer Pokemon
- Show Effectiveness: Off, On - Sets whether a moves effectiveness is shown in the additional move info box in battle
- Experience Multiplier: 0-1000 in increments of 10 (0, 10, 20, etc.) - Sets the Exp multiplier from battles
- Experience Distribution: Gen III, Gen VI, Gen VIII - Sets how Exp is distributed when fainting a Pokemon
    - Gen III: Exp is split evenly among battle participants, Exp. Share splits evenly between participants and non-participants
    - Gen VI: Battle participants earn 100% Exp, non-participants earn 50% of Exp when Exp. Share is enabled
    - Gen VIII: Battle participants earn 100% Exp, non-participants earn 100% of Exp when Exp. Share is enabled
- Sound: Mono, Stereo - Sets the sound mode
- Low HP Beep: Off, On - Sets whether the low HP beep plays
- Skip Fanfares: Off, On - Sets whether you can skip fanfares with the B button
- Bike Music: Off, On - Sets whether the bike music will play
- Surf Music: Off, On - Sets whether the surf music will play
- Guaranteed Catch: Off, On - Sets whether balls have a 100% success rate
- Guaranteed Run: Off, On - Sets whether running has a 100% success rate
- Encounter Rates: Vanilla, Normalized - Sets how encounter rates are determined
    - Vanilla: Encounter rates are unchanged from the vanilla game
    - Normalized: Every encounter slot has roughly the same chance of being chosen (this does not mean each Pokemon has the same chance of appearing)
- Encounter Mode: Random, Boost, Rotate - Sets what method is used for determining wild encounters
    - Random: Encounters are chosen randomly based on the encounter rates
    - Boost: Encounters are chosen based on the encounter rates with a higher chance for Pokemon that haven't already been caught
    - Rotate: Encounters are chosen by rotating through the encounter slots in an area (multiple slots in a row can be the same Pokemon)
- Blind Trainers: Off, On - Sets whether trainers will see you without you directly talking to them
- Skip Nicknames: Off, On - Sets whether the game will ask you to nickname Pokemon upon receiving them
- Item Messages: All, Progression, None - Sets what items will display a message when received from another game in the multiworld

options.label: Provide Hints
options.description:
Provides an Archipelago Hint for locations that tell you what item they give once you've gotten the in game hint.

This includes the Oak's Aides, Bicycle Shop, Shops, and Pokemon Request Locations.

options.label: Progressive Parts
options.description: Pod racer parts will always be the next level upgrade

options.label: No Traction Upgrades
options.description: Removes Traction parts from the item pool

options.label: Course Unlock Mode
options.description:
Sets how courses should unlock
Full Shuffle: All course unlocks are fully shuffled. Recommended for moderate to longer games and asyncs.
Circuits: Access to entire circuits is shuffled. Recommended for a shorter game.
Progressive Circuits: Access to entire circuits is shuffled, and you will always unlock them in order. Recommended for a shorter game.

options.label: Randomize Starting Racers
options.description: Changes which racers are available to use at the beginning

options.label: Number of Starting Racers
options.description:
How many random racers to start with
This option is only used if 'Randomize Starting Racers' is enabled

options.label: Starting Racers Plando
options.description:
List of specific racers with which to start
This option is only used if 'Randomize Starting Racers' is enabled

options.label: Max Additional Racers
options.description: How many racers can be added to the pool (excluding the starting racers)

options.label: Mirrored Tracks
options.description: How many tracks should be mirrored

options.label: Disable Part Damage
options.description:
Prevents parts from being damaged and removes pit droids from the item pool
This does not remove the pit droid shop checks, just the pit droids themselves
Extra money will be added to the pool to compensate

options.label: AI Scaling
options.description:
Affects AI speed
Vanilla: Courses use their default scaling, which may result in tough races early on
Circuits: AI is scaled according to the current circuit
Parts: AI is dynamically scaled according to the quality of your parts

options.label: Additional AI Multiplier
options.description:
Applies additional scaling to AI
1000 = 1.000

options.label: Enable Multiplier Control
options.description: Allows the player to change the additional AI multiplier in-game

options.label: 1-Lap Mode
options.description: Races only require 1 lap to complete

options.label: Auto-Hint Shop
options.description: Automatically hints shop items as they unlock

options.label: Shop Costs
options.description:
Sets the cost of items at Watto's shop
Vanilla: Prices are unchanged. Some may require grinding truguts to afford
Normalized: Prices are much closer together, with some categories being slightly more expensive than others
Tiered: Each tier of any part type is an identical cost to that of other parts. This is the cheapest option

options.label: Shop Cost Multiplier
options.description: Additional multiplier for shop costs

options.label: Course Plando
options.description:
Sets specific courses
For mirrored, append ' (Mirrored)' to any course name
Repeated courses will cause errors

options.label: Death Link Amnesty
options.description: Amount of times you can crash your pod before sending a DeathLink to the server

options.label: Shuffle Gear Shops
options.description: Shuffle the content of all Weapon Shops together, and do the same for Armor Shops.

options.label: Shuffle Spells
options.description: Shuffle Spells amongst their own School.

options.label: Job Promotion
options.description:
Set how Promotion Jobs are handled.

Bahamut: Giving the Rat's Tail to Bahamut promote all Characters.

Promote All Item: A Promote All Item is added to the Item Pool, when found all Characters promote.
Bahamut becomes a Location.

Job Item: All six Promotion Jobs become an individual Item added to the Item Pool.
When acquired, all characters of the corresponding base Job promote. Bahamut becomes a Location.

options.label: Lute Tablatures
options.description:
Playing the Lute requires a fixed number of Tablatures; 40 are shuffled in the Item Pool.
This sets the number required to play the Lute and open the path in the Temple of Fiends.
Set to 0 to disable this feature.
If the required number is higher than 0, the Lute is in your starting inventory.
The Item description will reveal the required number.

options.label: Crystals Required
options.description:
Set the number of Crystals that must be restored so the Black Orb can be destroyed.
Talking to the Black Orb will reveal the required number.

options.label: Nerf Chaos
options.description: Halve Chaos' HP and reduce his Intelligence and Attack Power by 25%.

options.label: Boss Minions
options.description:
Add Minions to Bosses and Extend some Minibosses party.
None: Original Parties are maintained.
Weak Minions: Add relatively weak minions to Bosses and extend Minibosses by 1-2 members.
Strong Minions: Add relatively strong minions to Bosses and extend Minibosses by 2-3 members.
Weak-Strong Minions: Minions can be weak or strong.

options.label: Monster Parties
options.description:
Randomize Monster Parties.
Standard: Original Monster Parties are maintained.
No Variance: Monsters will be replaced by Monsters of roughly the same power.
Low Variance: Monsters can be replaced by slightly weaker or slightly stronger Monsters.
High Variance: Monsters can be replaced by much weaker or much stronger Monsters.

options.label: Variance Cap
options.description:
If Monster Parties are randomized, bound Power Variance.
This option doesn't do anything for Standard and No Variance choices.
None: Variance is unbounded, Randomized Monster Parties can be weaker or stronger.
Upper Bound: Randomized Monsters cannot be more powerful than the replaced Monsters, but they can be weaker.
Lower Bound: Randomized Monsters cannot be weaker than the replaced Monsters, but they can be more powerful.

options.label: Dungeon Encounter Rate
options.description:
Modify the Encounter Rate in dungeons by the multiplier selected.
NOTE: This option doesn't affect the Boost setting to disable/enable encounters.

options.label: Overworld Encounter Rate
options.description:
Modify the Encounter Rate on the Overworld by the multiplier selected.
NOTE: This option doesn't affect the Boost setting to disable/enable encounters.

options.label: Shuffle Trials' Maze
options.description: Shuffle the Pillars Maze on floor 2F of the Citadel of Trials.

options.label: Shuffle Overworld
options.description:
Shuffle all Overworld entrances, except the Towns.

NOTE: The Princess won't teleport you to Cornelia Castle when this is enabled.

options.label: Shuffle Entrances
options.description:
Shuffle all non-Overworld entrances.

No Shuffle: Entrances stay the same.
Dungeon Internal: Only shuffle the Dungeons' entrances, and keep them inside their respective dungeon.
Dungeon Mixed: Only shuffle the Dungeons' entrances amongst all dungeons.
All: Shuffle all locations' entrances except Towns.

options.label: Shuffle Towns
options.description:
Shuffle all Town entrances, except Cornelia; if Early Progression is set to Bikke's Ship, Pravoka is also excluded.
No Shuffle: Entrances stay the same.
Between Towns: Towns are shuffled only amongst themselves.
Shallow Shuffle: If Overworld or Entrances are shuffled, Towns will be included with them, but will always be
on the first floor of any location.
Deep Shuffle: If Overworld or Entrances are shuffled, Towns will be included with them and can end up
at any floor inside a location.

options.label: Early Progression
options.description:
Set how the world is opened at the start of the game.

Bikke's Ship: The Bridge is built from the start and Bikke will always give the Ship.

Marsh Cave Path: Open a path to the West of Cornelia that allows you to reach the Marsh Cave area by foot.
The Bridge is never built. The Ship is shuffled with other items and Bikke is a Location.

options.label: Northern Docks
options.description: Add docks to the Onrac Continent and the Mirage Desert Continent to make them accessible by Ship.

options.label: Experience Boost
options.description: Set the default Experience Boost multiplier. This can still be modified in the Boost menu.

options.label: Gil Boost
options.description: Set the default Gil Boost multiplier. This can still be modified in the Boost menu.

options.label: Boost Menu
options.description: Enable/Disable the in-game Boost menu. This will lock you to your current XP, Gil and Encounter Rate options.

options.label: Difficulty
options.description:
Considers the ability to perform various movement tech in logic.
Beginner: No difficult tech required. May still require unexpected use of map geometry.
Intermediate: Involves some tricky movement that may require a small amount of practice and fast inputs.
Hard: Involves very particular movement that may require highly strict timing or a large amount of setup.

options.label: Start Location
options.description:
Where Fynn should start their adventure.

NOTE: Not all start locations are made equally. In some particular cases,
Fynn will be given additional items to start with in order to minimize the
chances of BK (or to make the seed playable).

options.label: Entrance Rando
options.description: Whether or not to randomize entrances.

options.label: Shroomsanity
options.description: Shuffles all shrooms into the pool.

options.label: Eventsanity
options.description: Shuffles events into the pool. For example, healing the Giant is a location with a check.

options.label: Gratitudesanity
options.description:
How to treat Gratitude, the resource you gain from taking care of your family.

Disable (default): Gratitude is obtained by feeding hatched fellas, as in the original game.
Enable: Shuffles gratitude into the pool. Feeding hatched fellas is now a location.
Split: Shuffles gratitude and the Sun Cavern teleports into the pool separately.

options.label: Carryablesanity
options.description:
How to treat carryable items, like the apples in Lostleaf Lake, Jester
Boots its various locations, and so on.

Disable (default): Leave them in their usual spots.
Kind: Shuffle them into the pool. Entering doorways will cause you to drop
your carryable, ensuring short pathways.
Mean: Shuffle them into the pool without mercy. An example scenario is that
you may have to carry Shelnert's Fish from Shelwart's tombstone through
Lostleaf Lake, into Sun Cavern, then through Moon Cavern, Gallery Lobby,
the Foyer, and finally into the Earth Lobby to toss into the painting.

options.label: Shuffle Abilities
options.description: Shuffles the abilities the Sage gives you into the pool.

options.label: Shuffle High Jump
options.description: Shuffles the ability to High Jump into the pool.

options.label: Shuffle Climb
options.description: Shuffles the ability to climb into the pool.

options.label: Shuffle Carry
options.description: Shuffles the ability to pick up and carry throwables into the pool.

options.label: Shuffle Roll
options.description: Shuffles the ability to roll into the pool.

options.label: Shuffle Sprint
options.description: Shuffles the ability to build momentum into the pool.

options.label: Shuffle Swim
options.description:
Shuffles the ability to swim into the pool. If you touch water without the
ability to swim, you die.

options.label: Include Double Jump
options.description: Shuffles a brand new ability to double jump into the pool.

options.label: Exclude Flight
options.description: Removes Flight from the pool. Highly recommended.

options.label: Exclude Wings
options.description: Removes Wings from the pool. For the brave and bold.

options.label: Split Tail
options.description:
Splits the Tail into grounded and aerial versions, requiring you to obtain both
to have the full power of the Tail Whip.

options.label: Super Bounce
options.description:
How to treat super bounce, a tech that enables gaining significant height using an aerial tailwhip while rolling.

Disable (default): Prevents the use of super bounce.
Enable: Allows the use of super bounce, considering its use in logic.
Shuffle: Shuffles super bounce into the pool, considering its use in logic.

options.label: Super Bubble Jump
options.description:
How to treat super bubble jump, a tech that enables gaining significant height using bubble shots while rolling.

Disable (default): Prevents the use of super bubble jump.
Enable: Allows the use of super bubble jump, considering its use in logic.
Shuffle: Shuffles super bubble jump into the pool, considering its use in logic.

options.label: Air Swim
options.description:
How to treat air swim, a tech that enables free movement in the air.

Disable (default): Prevents the use of air swim.
Enable: Allows the use of air swim, considering its use in logic.
Shuffle: Shuffles air swim into the pool, considering its use in logic.

options.label: Ejection Launch
options.description:
Consider use of ejection launches in logic.

An example of an ejection launch is clipping into the Pom to launch yourself
out of the Jester Boots area in Prismic Palace.

options.label: Z Target
options.description:
Consider obscure use of z-targeting in logic.

An example is using z-targeting to simultaneously move backwards and fire
Bubbles to build significant speed in the air.

options.label: Momentum Cancel
options.description:
Consider pausing to cancel momentum in logic.

An example is repeatedly pausing while using Wings to gain more distance.

options.label: Ability Toggle
options.description:
Consider toggling abilities in logic.

An example is hovering with the Wings, then enabling Double Jump to gain extra height.

options.label: Out Of Bounds
options.description:
Consider out of bounds movement in logic.

An example is clipping out of the lake using the tombstone fish in Lostleaf Lake.

options.label: Wing Jump
options.description:
Consider advanced use of the Wings in logic.

Examples include jumping and immediately activating the Wings to gain more distance, and riding along slopes to gain height.

options.label: Wing Storage
options.description:
Consider Wing storage in logic.

Sliding from an unwalkable slope onto walkable terrain while the Wings are activated makes your next airtime trigger Wings without an additional jump press, enabling a significant boost to height and distance.

options.label: Bubble Jump
options.description:
Consider use of Bubble for movement in logic.

Disable (default): Don't include in logic.
Enable: Consider floating by holding Bubble in logic.
With Recoil: Also consider firing Bubbles to launch yourself backwards in logic.

options.label: Roll Disjoint
options.description:
Consider use of roll disjoints in logic.

Roll disjoints involve canceling roll after attempting to trigger another
animation, like a Tail Whip, in order to disjoint Fynn's hitbox to touch
loading zones through walls.

options.label: Damage Boost
options.description: Consider use of damage boosts in logic.

options.label: Ground Tail Jump
options.description:
Consider use of grounded Tail Whip jumps in logic.

If you Tail Whip on the ground and then jump, you are able to jump again once
the animation ends.

options.label: Air Tail Jump
options.description:
Consider use of aerial Tail Whip jumps in logic.

If you land while attempting a Tail Whip in the air, you launch yourself
forward, and are able to jump for a short period of time, gaining a small
amount of extra height compared to a standard jump.

options.label: Jester Boots Slope Movement
options.description:
Allows use of the Jester Boots to climb normally unwalkable slopes in
logic.

Some slopes can uniquely be climbed while wearing the Jester Boots. For
example, you can grab the Deep Woods egg location by simply walking up the
wall with the Jester Boots.

options.label: Carry Through Doors
options.description:
Allows Fynn to carry temporary items through doorways.

When disabled, Fynn drops anything they're carrying as they move to a new
area. Forces Carryablesanity to Kind.

options.label: Allow Fun
options.description:
Allows making use of some combinations of abilities that are out-of-logic.

When disabled, the Jester Boots have a distaste for Fynn carrying items,
and will refuse to allow Fynn to pick items up unless they are taken off
first. They're only fine with the idea if you are within the boundaries of
the Deep Woods.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Determines the goal of the seed

Final Mixtape: Complete the Final Mixtape

options.label: Required Rank
options.description:
The rank required to receive a check on a level.

Cool: Any passing rank will reward a check

Amazing: Better than Cool, while still allowing a few misses

Perfect: Requires perfection. WARNING: THIS WILL CAUSE CHECKS TO BE EXTREMELY DIFFICULT!

options.label: Required Level Completions
options.description: The number of total levels that need to be completed to unlock the Final Mixtape

options.label: Required 16RPM Completions
options.description: The number of 16RPM completions required to unlock Final Mixtape

options.label: Excluded 16RPM Levels
options.description: Choose which 16 RPM levels should not have required items

options.label: Required 45RPM Completions
options.description: The number of 45RPM completions required to unlock Final Mixtape

options.label: Excluded 45RPM Levels
options.description: Choose which 45 RPM levels should not have required items

options.label: Required 78RPM Completions
options.description: The number of 78RPM completions required to unlock Final Mixtape

options.label: Excluded 78RPM Levels
options.description: Choose which 78 RPM levels should not have required items

options.label: Badgesanity
options.description: Determines whether badges provide a check when collected (some more difficult badges will be de-prioritized)

options.label: Excluded Badges
options.description: Sets which badges should not have required items

options.label: Story Missions For Goal
options.description: How many story missions (missions played as Ty) do you need to unlock the airship that leads to Quinking?

options.label: Bunyip Missions For Goal
options.description: How many Bunyip missions do you need to unlock the airship that leads to Quinking?

options.label: Gunyip Missions For Goal
options.description: How many Gunyip missions do you need to unlock the airship that leads to Quinking?

options.label: Missions For Goal
options.description: How many race missions do you need to unlock the airship that leads to Quinking?

options.label: Checks Require Ultra
options.description:
Determines whether the generator considers checks using invisible objects logically require an Ultra Stone

This also affects Frame Sanity

options.label: Start With Maps
options.description: Determines if you begin with the collectible maps

options.label: Frame Sanity
options.description: Determines if collecting Picture Frames grants checks

options.label: Steve Sanity
options.description: Determines if talking to Steve grants checks

options.label: Stone Sanity
options.description: Determines if finding Rang Stones grants checks

options.label: Starting Heads Chance
options.description: The initial chance for the coin to land on heads without any upgrades

options.label: AutoFlip
options.description: Adds autoflip upgrades to the pool and enables the autoflip button in game

options.label: Trap Fill Percentage
options.description: The percentage of filler that will be replaced by traps

options.label: Flip Difficulty
options.description: How many flips logic expects you to do to buy an item in the shop

options.label: Death Link Chance
options.description: Percentage chance to send a death on breaking a streak of heads

options.label: Limit Stars
options.description: Prevents required items from being placed on the third star check of each level.

options.label: Require Red Stars
options.description: Determines if red stars (hard mode) are required for checks to send.

options.label: Require Level Completions
options.description: Determines if all levels in each zone must be completed to unlock the final level of the zone.

options.label: Maximum Star Check
options.description: Determines the maximum star threshold which sends a check.

options.label: Include Hard Mode
options.description: Determines if hard mode versions of dreams send checks.

options.label: Required Star Percent
options.description:
Percentage of stars added to the pool required for goal (roughly).

This affects every level's star cost.

options.label: Include Overtime
options.description:
Adds items and level completion checks for the Overtime missions.
WARNING: On gold threshold, these level completion checks are very hard.

options.label: Include Tournament
options.description:
Adds challenmges and level completion checks for the Telepost Tournament DLC.
ALL PLAYERS MUST OWN THE DLC

options.label: Required Level Completions
options.description:
Number of unique level completions required to unlock Stand Your Post (Winter 12)
Compatible with required levels per week.

options.label: Required Level Completions Per Week
options.description:
Number of unique level completions per week required to unlock Stand Your Post (Winter 12)
Compatible with required levels.
Winter - Week 3 will only ever require maximum 3 (does not include Stand Your Post).

options.label: Required Collectibles
options.description: Number of hidden collectibles required to unlock Stand Your Post (Winter 12)

options.label: Required Collectible Checks
options.description: Number of hidden collectible checks required to unlock Stand Your Post (Winter 12)

options.label: Required Overtime Completions
options.description:
Number of overtime shift completions required to unlock Stand Your Post (Winter 12)
MUST HAVE "INCLUDE OVERTIME" ON

options.label: Required Overtime Completions
options.description:
Number of Telepost Tournament completions required to unlock Stand Your Post (Winter 12)
MUST HAVE "INCLUDE TOURNAMENT" ON

options.label: Starting Week
options.description: Choose which week will initially be unlocked.

options.label: Level Completion Threshold
options.description: Minimum required rank required on level completion to send the level completion check.

options.label: Challengesanity
options.description: Determines whether completing level challenges sends checks.

options.label: Goal
options.description:
Determines the goal of the seed

Final Battle: Beat Boss Cass in Final Battle and rescue your parents from The Dreaming

options.label: Goal Requires Bosses
options.description: Determines if beating all bosses is a requirement to go to Final Battle

options.label: Logic Difficulty
options.description:
What set of logic to use

Standard: The logic assumes elemental rangs are required to enter hubs

Advanced: Assumes hubs may be entered early and elemental rangs are optional

Doom: Assumes checks can be completed with the bare-minimum of items. WARNING: MAY CAUSE SUFFERING!

options.label: Progressive Elemental Rangs
options.description: Determines if elemental rangs are a progressive check

options.label: Thunder Egg Gating
options.description:
If bosses are unlocked via hub Thunder Egg counts, required count per hub can be set here
This also sets the required Thunder Egg count to receive the elemental attribute check after completing bosses

options.label: Extra Thunder Eggs
options.description:
Sets number of additional thunder eggs of each type to add to the pool
WARNING - Setting this value high without sanity is likely to lead to generation failures

options.label: Cog Gating
options.description: Cog requirement count for each attribute check in Julius' lab

options.label: Extra Cogs
options.description:
Sets number of additional golden cogs to add to the pool per attribute check
WARNING - Setting this value high without sanity is likely to lead to generation failures

options.label: Gate Time Attacks
options.description:
If true, adds Stopwatch items to the pool which unlock the time attacks for each level
If false, time attacks are unlocked by completing the main objective thunder egg check for the level (vanilla)
Also adds checks for beating specific times in the time attacks

options.label: Level Shuffle
options.description: Determines whether the levels that portals lead to will be shuffled

options.label: Level Unlock Style
options.description:
Determines how levels are unlocked

Vanilla: All levels are unlocked from the start of the world

Checks: The first level is unlocked from the start but all other levels are unlocked via checks
